pulls.title: fix: handle CRLF line endings in edit_file and stage-4 schematic check
pulls.body:
<!--
Fill in the sections that apply and delete the rest, including this comment.
Keep prose em-dash-free (use colons, commas, or parentheses).
Reference files as clickable relative links, e.g. [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts).
-->

## What

This PR fixes multiline `edit_file` anchor failures and Stage 4 schematic completion check rejections on Windows by normalizing CRLF line endings.

## Why

Closes #376. Git checkouts on Windows with `core.autocrlf=true` write working tree files with CRLF. Since the AI models and the deterministic drafting engine strictly emit LF, this line-ending mismatch caused exact-string anchor lookups to fail and byte-for-byte equality checks to reject valid schematic drafts.

## Design

In [filetools.ts](src/agent/filetools.ts), `toolEditFile` dynamically detects if the target file on disk uses CRLF. If so, it normalizes the AI-provided search anchor and replacement strings to use CRLF. This allows `indexOf` to match successfully while preserving the file's original line endings upon writing.
In [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts), the Stage 4 `isComplete` check now normalizes both the drafted `dry.text` and the existing file contents to LF before asserting strict equality.

pulls.title: fix(codex): refresh working directory mtime on each turn
pulls.body:
## What

Refreshes the \mtime\ of \CodexProvider\'s owned temporary working directory on every turn using \utimes\.

## Why

In \CodexProvider\ (\src/agent/providers/codex.ts\), an owned temporary working directory was allocated once upon the first turn and never had its \mtime\ refreshed on subsequent turns.
In contrast, \ClaudeCodeProvider\ and \CursorProvider\ touch their scratch directories via \utimes\ on every turn so that a concurrent \create\ run's startup sweep (\sweepStaleTempDirs\, 2-hour age gate) does not delete the live process's scratch directory during multi-hour runs. Without this refresh, a long Codex run exceeding 2 hours had its owned working directory eligible for deletion by a concurrent startup sweep.

## Design

- In \CodexProvider.ensureWorkingDirectory()\, when \	his.ownsWorkingDirectory\ is true, touch \	his.workingDirectory\ with the current timestamp via \utimes(..., now, now).catch(() => {})\.
- Best-effort and non-blocking, matching the pattern in \ClaudeCodeProvider\ and \CursorProvider\.

pulls.title: redact secrets in CLI error output and compat error messages
pulls.body:
## What

A compat provider endpoint that embeds its credential in the URL (Gemini's compat endpoint does this with `?key=...`) could leak that credential into CLI error output.

## Why

`makeProvider`'s bare-`compat` error in [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts) interpolated the configured `baseURL` raw. [cli.ts](src/cli.ts) then printed every caught error's `.message` straight to stderr with no redaction anywhere in that path. SECURITY.md names this directly: "an API key appearing unredacted in ... terminal output" is a vulnerability. Transcripts and summaries already redact at write time (AC-4.1); the CLI's own error output was the one surface that did not.

[doctor.ts](src/commands/doctor.ts) already had the right fix for its own display path: it strips query and userinfo rather than pattern-matching, since a URL-embedded credential is not reliably one of the known key shapes. `loop.ts`'s throw site was missed when that was written. `cli.ts` never redacted at all. This is distinct from #84 and #130, which added key-shape patterns and fixed `doctor.ts`'s display. Neither touched this throw site or the stderr boundary.

## Design

The fix moves the URL-sanitizing logic `doctor.ts` already had for its display path into a shared `sanitizeEndpoint()` in [redact.ts](src/util/redact.ts). `doctor.ts` switches to it as a pure refactor. `loop.ts` uses it at the actual leak site: that is the real fix. A new helper, `formatCliError()` in [cli-error.ts](src/util/cli-error.ts), runs `redactSecrets` on any caught error before it is printed. Every `console.error((err as Error).message)` call in `cli.ts` now goes through it instead. That closes the stderr boundary generally: a future key-shaped leak anywhere in the CLI gets caught too, not just this one bug.

No spec-level behavior changed.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1039 passed, 45 failed, 75 skipped |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | not run, no API key in this environment | skip |

This PR adds 7 new tests, all passing, in `test/safety.test.ts` (unit tests for `sanitizeEndpoint` and `formatCliError`) and `test/openai-compat.test.ts` (confirms `makeProvider` no longer leaks a query-string credential; reverting the one-line fix locally reproduces the leak and fails this test).

The 45 failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this change. Unmodified `main` fails the same 45 in this environment: a missing local `kicad-cli`; a CRLF-vs-LF comparison; a `chmod 0o000` check that does not hold under Windows' permission model. The branch passes 1039 against `main`'s 1032 with the same 45 failures either way. The difference is exactly the 7 new tests. This PR does not make the full suite pass; it adds passing coverage without changing the pre-existing failure count.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `edit`
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ ./manual-tests/setup.sh edit
sandbox ready: manual-tests/runs/edit

$ COPPERHEAD_KICAD_CLI=<stub printing "10.0.4"> npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit init
created docs/SPEC.md ... created .git/hooks/pre-commit

$ git -C manual-tests/runs/edit commit -m "scaffold docs" --no-verify
(the pre-commit hook shells out to a globally installed copperhead binary,
not present in this environment; --no-verify only skips it for this
throwaway sandbox commit)

# Before the fix (confirmed by temporarily reverting the one-line change):
$ COPPERHEAD_BASE_URL=https://example.com/v1?key=shouldNotLeakThisSecretValue123 \
  COPPERHEAD_KICAD_CLI=<stub> npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit do "test request" --model compat
compat requires a model id; use "compat:<model-id>" (endpoint https://example.com/v1?key=shouldNotLeakThisSecretValue123 is configured, but has no default model)

# After the fix:
$ COPPERHEAD_BASE_URL=https://example.com/v1?key=shouldNotLeakThisSecretValue123 \
```

## Docs

fix(create): require ownership marker before recursive temp cleanup (#359)
pulls.body:
## What

Requires a positive ownership marker (\.copperhead-owned-temp\) and symlink-free directory verification before recursively deleting stale scratch directories during startup cleanup, ensuring unrelated user projects and disposable worktrees whose names begin with \copperhead-\ are preserved.

## Why

Fixes #359.

During startup of \copperhead create\, \sweepStaleTempDirs\ recursively deleted any directory directly below \os.tmpdir()\ whose basename began with \copperhead-\ and whose directory \mtime\ was at least 2 hours old. Prefix and age alone were treated as sufficient authorization for recursive deletion, causing silent data loss of unrelated user projects, disposable worktrees, and test fixtures.

## Design

1. **Ownership Marker**: Added \createCopperheadTempDir()\ in [tmp.ts](src/util/tmp.ts) which creates directories under the temp root and immediately writes \.copperhead-owned-temp\ with exact content \copperhead-owned-temp\nv1\n\. If marker creation fails, the directory is immediately cleaned up and the error re-thrown.
2. **Safe Sweep Authorization**: Updated \sweepStaleTempDirs()\ in [tmp.ts](src/util/tmp.ts) to:
   - Use \lstat()\ instead of \stat()\ so symlinks matching the prefix are never followed.
   - Verify that the candidate directory contains \.copperhead-owned-temp\ with exact expected contents before calling \m(..., { recursive: true, force: true })\.
   - Leave unmarked directories, symlinks, and lookalikes untouched regardless of age.
3. **Migrated Production Producers**: Migrated all production scratch directory creation sites to \createCopperheadTempDir()\:
   - KiCad check, load error, unrouted count, and netlist export in [cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts)
   - Board population validation in [populate.ts](src/kicad/populate.ts)
   - Failed-run backup directory in [git.ts](src/util/git.ts)
   - Provider scratch working directories in [claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts), [codex.ts](src/agent/providers/codex.ts), and [cursor.ts](src/agent/providers/cursor.ts).

pulls.title: fix: refuse the unborn-HEAD case before any scaffold write (#322)
pulls.body:
## What

the documented quickstart (`git init && copperhead create`) refuses before stage 1 does any work, because `create` requires at least one commit. the refusal itself is correct and well explained, but it fires too late: `stage spec-seed: running` already printed, and `.copperhead/config.json` was already written, so a fresh folder that followed the docs exactly ends up with a confusing "it started, then failed" message and a non-empty folder to clean up.

## Why

closes #322.

`gitPreflight` (the unborn-HEAD check in `src/util/git.ts`) only runs inside `runAgentLoop`, which the `create` command reaches only after `openspecInit` and `markCreateOrigin` have already written to the repo, and after the first stage's "running" line has already printed. the check itself was never wrong, it was just in the wrong place for `create` specifically (every other command reaches it before writing anything).

## Design

moved the identical check (`gitPreflight(opts.repoRoot, { allowDirty: true })`, matching the `allowDirty: true` every stage's own call already uses, since `create`'s stages intentionally build on each other's uncommitted state) to the top of `runCreate`, before the brief is even read. no new check, no behavior change for the allowed cases, just earlier placement so the refusal (when it does fire) is the only thing that happens.

also added the missing `git commit --allow-empty` step to the quickstart snippet in [examples/README.md](examples/README.md), so following the docs exactly succeeds on the first try instead of needing this fix to even discover the requirement.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Markdownlint (changed doc) | `npx markdownlint-cli2 examples/README.md` | pass |
| Unit + offline (targeted) | `npx vitest run test/create-footprints.test.ts test/create-layout-draft.test.ts test/create-resilience.test.ts test/create-stage-turns.test.ts test/preflight.test.ts` | 28 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped |

The 1 failure (`create-footprints.test.ts`, an uninstalled-footprint resume case) and a second suite-level failure in `create-layout-draft.test.ts` are pre-existing: identical failures reproduce on `main` with the same local setup (no real KiCad library install on this machine, only a stub `kicad-cli` that answers `version`), unrelated to this change. Confirmed by running the same 5 files against `main` before applying this patch.

I didn't run the full `npm test` here since many unrelated suites (drafting, layout, ERC scoring) need a real KiCad install to produce real geometry, which this machine doesn't have; I scoped to the files that actually exercise `runCreate`/`gitPreflight`/the create pipeline instead, and checked both for determinism (ran twice) and against `main` (same failures, so no regression).

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `create`, but via the raw documented quickstart commands rather than `manual-tests/setup.sh create` directly, since that script's own `create` variant commits before handing off (so it never hits the bug this PR fixes). Ran with a stub `kicad-cli` (no real KiCad on this machine) and `--model claude-code`, outside the repo (Windows: the real home directory is itself a git worktree, so `TMPDIR` needs to point elsewhere or `git` preflight checks misbehave).

```text
$ mkdir my-board && cd my-board && git init
$ copperhead --repo my-board create --brief examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md --model claude-code
repository has no commits; copperhead requires at least one commit for snapshots and rollback

why it failed: the pre-run snapshot is the current HEAD commit; with an unborn HEAD there is nothing to roll back to if verification fails
to fix:
  1. git add -A && git commit -m "initial commit"
  2. rerun the same copperhead command
$ ls my-board
# (empty except .git — no stray config.json, no misleading "running" line)

$ git -C my-board commit --allow-empty -m "initial commit"
$ copperhead --repo my-board create --brief examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md --model claude-code
stage spec-seed: running
copperhead v0.11.0 · kicad-cli 10.0.4 · node v24.19.0
create · stage spec-seed (1/8) · model claude-code ...
# (stage 1 actually starts now; run then hit an unrelated local auth error,
# expected since this machine has no real Claude Code login)
```

Also confirmed the same no-commit case reproduces exactly as described in #322 (misleading "running" line + leftover `.copperhead/config.json`) when run against unpatched `main`, and does not reproduce with this patch applied.

## Docs

updated the quickstart snippet in [examples/README.md](examples/README.md) with the missing initial-commit step and a one-line pointer to `gitPreflight`.

---

- [ ] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: N/A, doesn't touch `src/commands/check`.
- [ ] **No sexp serialization**: N/A, doesn't touch `src/kicad/`.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, doesn't touch the ledger.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A, no secret-handling code touched.

pulls.title: fix(search): bound regex evaluation against ReDoS
pulls.body:
## Why

Fixes #366 by addressing a potential ReDoS vulnerability in `toolSearch()`.

Previously, regular expressions were evaluated synchronously against file contents. A carefully crafted pattern could trigger catastrophic backtracking, consume excessive CPU time, and block the main thread.

This change bounds search execution by moving the work to a separate worker thread and enforcing a time limit.

## Summary

The fix is intentionally scoped to regex search execution and aims to preserve existing search behavior while preventing expensive patterns from blocking the application.

## What changed

- Moved file searching and regex evaluation into a separate worker thread.
- Added a default **2,000 ms execution budget** and a **1,000-character pattern limit**.
- Added explicit error handling for invalid patterns, timeouts, aborted searches, and worker failures.
- Improved cleanup of worker resources, timers, and abort listeners.
- Routed search errors through the existing error-handling path without triggering automatic retries.
- Added regression tests for normal searches, glob matching, invalid and oversized patterns, timeouts, cancellation, cleanup, and error handling.
- Updated the main OpenSpec specification and its corresponding change proposal to document the bounded-search requirement.

## Testing

The following checks passed:

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`

pulls.title: feat(cli): add versioned capability handshake
pulls.body:
## What

Adds `copperhead capabilities --json`, returning a versioned capability descriptor (`protocol: "copperhead-run/1"`, CLI version, sorted top-level primary command inventory, truthful feature list, and installed tool versions). Non-interactive runners and automation hosts can discover runtime boundaries deterministically before launching an agent run.

## Why

Non-interactive consumers, hosted orchestrators, and CI harnesses currently have no stable machine-readable handshake to discover what runtime capabilities and protocol versions a given Copperhead installation supports. Without a handshake, consumers must rely on heuristic command parsing, version assumptions, or fragile error matching during execution. Issue #258 outlines the phased run protocol: Phase 0 establishes the offline capability discovery contract.

## Design

- **Protocol versioning**: Identifies the protocol as `copperhead-run/1`. Breaking protocol changes require incrementing the major version. Consumers can reject unsupported major versions before initiating execution using the pure helper `isProtocolCompatible`. Additive fields in the report payload are ignored safely by forward-compatible consumers.
- **Capability discovery vs health checking**: While [doctor.ts](src/commands/doctor.ts) evaluates execution readiness (and fails if dependencies or API keys are missing), [capabilities.ts](src/commands/capabilities.ts) discovers supported protocol and runtime capabilities. It exits with code 0 without requiring a Git repository, KiCad project, API credentials, or network access.
- **Truthful feature advertisement**: The `features` array is strictly empty (`[]`) in this build. Phase 1-4 capabilities (such as event streams and result documents) are omitted until their wire implementations land. Structural CLI assertions confirm unknown options like `--event-stream` and `--result` are rejected.
- **Dynamic command inventory**: [extractPublicCommands](src/commands/capabilities.ts) extracts top-level primary commands dynamically from Commander program registrations, filters out internal helpers and help, and sorts them lexicographically. The static catalog array was removed; parity is validated against independently observed CLI help registrations.
- **Fault-isolated tool probing with process-tree cleanup**: External tool probes (`kicadCli`, `git`, `openspec`) enforce bounded subprocess execution (configurable, default 5000 ms). KiCad and OpenSpec probes route through `execKicadProcess` in [cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts), which enforces process-tree termination on Windows (`taskkill /F /T /PID <pid>`) upon deadline expiration to prevent `.cmd` batch wrappers from leaking orphaned descendant processes or keeping inherited stdio pipes open. Linux and macOS signals are preserved via standard `AbortController`. Failures, timeouts, or missing binaries degrade safely to `null` without throwing or leaking host filepaths or diagnostics.
- **Hermetic test isolation**: Unit tests inject stubbed tool probes rather than invoking host binaries, keeping test execution fast and deterministic.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- OpenSpec Change: `add-run-protocol-handshake` (validated with `openspec validate add-run-protocol-handshake`)
  - Proposal: [proposal.md](openspec/changes/add-run-protocol-handshake/proposal.md)
  - Design: [design.md](openspec/changes/add-run-protocol-handshake/design.md)
  - Tasks: [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-run-protocol-handshake/tasks.md)
  - Delta spec: [run-protocol-handshake/spec.md](openspec/changes/add-run-protocol-handshake/specs/run-protocol-handshake/spec.md)
  - Delta spec: [cli-surface/spec.md](openspec/changes/add-run-protocol-handshake/specs/cli-surface/spec.md)
- Authoritative Spec Update: Section 3 and Section 9 (AC-17: AC-17.1 through AC-17.5) updated in [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md).

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (0 errors) |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass (clean dist emission) |
| Markdown Lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass (markdown files scanned, 0 issues) |
| OpenSpec Validation | `npx openspec validate add-run-protocol-handshake` | pass (valid change) |
| Capability Suite | `npx vitest run test/capabilities.test.ts` | pass (38/38 passed, including process-tree termination and deadline bounds) |
| Doctor Suite | `npx vitest run test/doctor.test.ts` | pass (43/43 passed) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 57 test files passed, 22 failed, 2 skipped (1066 passed, 46 failed, 75 skipped; all 46 failures match pre-existing failures on upstream main e26be94 due to missing host kicad-cli binary/footprints and Windows-specific path/CRLF assertions; 0 introduced regressions) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | skip (Phase 0 is entirely offline; live provider tests not executed) |

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `manual-tests/runs/edit` (initialized via `manual-tests/setup.sh edit --fresh`)
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node dist/cli.js capabilities --json
{

  "cli": "0.11.0",
  "commands": [
    "capabilities",
    "check",

    "demo",
```

- [x] **Secrets**: Verified. No secret or environment variables exposed in capability report; `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/` remain gitignored; probe failures redact all subprocess output.

pulls.title: Fix observed create pipeline gates and export validation
pulls.body:
## What

Align create completion with verified artifacts and fix part-selection feedback, installed firmware-build evidence, and independent final development-plan review. Publish the genuine medium eight-stage run and the final software-validation evidence.

## Why

Related to [#66](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/issues/66). Real runs exposed an ambiguous MPN field contract, a missing executable firmware-build capability despite an installed SDK, and a prewritten DEVPLAN that could skip final review; the stage gates must require current evidence before completion.

## Design

### Latest published version

Current head: [2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/commit/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49), a normal fast-forward from `5e1fa72d424ba8b45fab24d6060a5f642dce68c7`. Its Git tree is `1c44b4cb153c9e16c5a8c2e91ada72e89454eb9d`, identical to the locally verified final publication tree.

This update fixes three failures observed in a genuine medium-complexity programmable `create` run:

1. **Part-selection field feedback:** require the selected identity in MPN and put qualification in Rationale. Check the existing selection predicate at finish, so an `UNVERIFIED` prefix receives actionable feedback before committing an incomplete stage.
2. **Explicit installed firmware toolchain:** opt-in CLI settings expose an existing ESP-IDF build capability, run builds in isolated source copies, retain real logs and source/binary hashes, and require current successful evidence at finish/resume. Explicit reproducibility compares two independent ELF/bin sets; compiler intermediates are handled without fabricating a successful build.
3. **Independent final development-plan review:** a DEVPLAN written during firmware no longer completes Stage 8 by content alone. Resume requires matching final-stage file-changing commit evidence; finish requires a change from the stage-entry document. The normal Stage 8 agent reviews and improves the preserved candidate.

See [design and contracts](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/changes/fix-create-stage-evidence/design.md), [create stage gates](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/src/commands/create.ts), and [explicit firmware build](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/src/commands/firmware-build.ts). The update also retains opt-in conservative populated-reference clearance. Subsequent publication review fixes exclude identified mechanical/DNP ordering rows without accepting other missing MPNs, recognize observed KiCad-save power-symbol defaults without accepting counterfeit geometry, and consolidate duplicate normative deltas. These follow-ups were validated after the preserved live run; they are not relabeled as its original runtime version.

## Testing

### Automated test status

The [published check index and source/test hash bindings](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/results.json) records these independently executed results:

| Check | Result on the final publication source |
| --- | --- |
| Native KiCad 9.0.9 full offline suite | 1,396 passed, 0 failed, 23 skipped; exit 0 |
| Native KiCad 10.0.6 full offline suite | 1,396 passed, 0 failed, 23 skipped; exit 0 |
| Explicit KiCad 9 recorded integration and controls | 5/5 passed; unchanged 29 recorded responses; exit 0 |
| Typecheck / build | Both exit 0 |
| Scoped `fix-create-stage-evidence` OpenSpec strict validation | 1 valid change, zero issues |
| Final authored-document Markdown lint | 231 files, zero issues; exit 0 |

Links: [KiCad 9 suite](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/full-kicad9.filtered.log), [KiCad 10 suite](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/full-kicad10.filtered.log), [recorded job](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/recorded-kicad9.filtered.log), [lint](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/lint.filtered.log), and [scoped OpenSpec validation](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/openspec-strict.filtered.log). The final lint record uses the installed Markdown CLI directly with the package's arguments/configuration; no automatic fix was applied.

The separate replay is sequential recorded-response regression with real tools, gates, KiCad and Git activity; it is not fresh inference or historical request/tool-result matching. These totals are separate checks and must not be added together. [Skipped-case scope](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/checks/skipped-tests.json) remains explicit. The preserved medium runtime's earlier offline count was 1,392/23; the 1,396/23 results describe the subsequent publication source. No new live model run was performed merely to publish this version, and these local logs do not claim a remote CI pass.

### Genuine medium create evidence

The new [medium evidence overview](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/README.md) records a 39-part, six-subsystem ESP32-C3 temperature/humidity display design: protected USB-C input, 3.3 V regulation, reset/UART, SHT40, external I2C OLED and RF/mechanics. It used the ordinary create CLI and real `gpt-6.1-sol/medium` through the installed Codex SDK/CLI.

[Eight independent stage commits and all completed predicates](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/stage-commits.json), final CLI exit 0, [failed attempts and successful resumes](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/attempts.json), 13 retained summaries, and [85 actual provider calls](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/provider-call-index.json) are published with [source provenance](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/source-provenance.json). The real Stage 8-only resume completed the final development-plan review; it skipped the earlier seven completed stages rather than rerunning them. Resume is allowed by [issue #66](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/issues/66).

[Two isolated real firmware builds](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/firmware/receipt.filtered.json) used ESP-IDF 5.5.3 / GCC 14.2.0 for ESP32-C3 and produced matching ELF/bin hashes with exit 0. [Project sources](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/tree/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/design), [export inventory](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/export-manifest.json), and [final hash checks](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/checks/final-hash-recheck.json) retain source/export/build bindings. Compiler binaries, generated plots, SDK caches, private provider payloads and full design Git objects are withheld; the bounded public subset cannot independently reconstruct the full historical Git chain or rehash withheld binaries. The model run demonstrates this one provider/sample, not provider parity or physical acceptance.

### DRC results: distinct designs

| Evidence set | Native raw result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New medium ESP32-C3 sample, KiCad 9.0.9 | Exit 5; **0 violations, 93 unconnected items**, zero schematic-parity findings | Draft ratsnest is allowed by the product's draft-stage contract; routing remains incomplete |
| Historical 500 mA USB-C prototype, KiCad 9.0.2 | Exit 5; **4 error-severity J1 hole-clearance findings, 0 unconnected items** | Those original raw errors remain in the preserved historical records |

The medium [raw DRC](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/checks/final-native-drc.json) and [execution record](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/checks/final-native-drc-execution.json) retain exit 5 explicitly. The historical [500 mA evidence receipt](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/native-500ma-evidence-receipt.md) and [provenance inventory](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/evidence/native-500ma-20261009/README.md) retain its failures and qualifications. The new sample does not repair or replace the historical board's four errors. Neither result establishes fabrication readiness, physical qualification, zone-fill correctness or manufacturer acceptance.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `edit`, through the repository's actual setup script.
- Commands and outcomes are retained in the six publication logs; the executed deterministic sequence was:

```text
bash manual-tests/setup.sh edit
exit 0: sandbox prepared

node dist/cli.js --repo manual-tests/runs/edit init
exit 0: documentation and real pre-commit hook created

git -C manual-tests/runs/edit add -A
exit 0

git -C manual-tests/runs/edit commit -m "scaffold docs"
exit 0: real hook ran; legibility findings remained visible

node dist/cli.js --repo manual-tests/runs/edit check
exit 0: ERC, normalized DRC and drift passed
legibility: 1 error, 5 advisory findings; score 40/100

node dist/cli.js --repo manual-tests/runs/edit export bom --supplier jlcpcb
exit 0: 0 parts included, 3 missing-MPN rows excluded
```

The real edit-sandbox setup, init, staging, real-hook commit, check and supplier-BOM export all exited 0, as indexed in the publication checks. The [manual check log](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/manual-command-5.log) still reports **1 legibility error, 5 advisory findings, score 40/100**. ERC, normalized DRC and drift passed; legibility did not become all-zero. The [supplier export](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/pipeline-run-logs/medium-create-20261011/publication-checks/manual-command-6.log) included zero parts and excluded three missing-MPN rows. That is honest exclusion, not an orderable BOM. No optional live `do`, hardware flash or bench test is claimed.

## Spec / OpenSpec

### Scope and existing behavior

Related to [#66](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/issues/66). The earlier patches align create completion with artifact evidence: spec-seed checks before commit, strict evidence-backed firmware N/A, complete generated-power definitions, fresh actual export inventories, generic outputs by default, and an explicit bounded KiCad 9 JLC profile. Full Stage 6 still requires current source/file hashes, complete exports and a valid archive; old manifests and profile switches require re-export. Generic settings/fill and manufacturer acceptance remain unverified.

The earlier [mutation-probe repair](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/mutation-probe-fix.md) registers writes and invalidates cached checks before attempting restoration after an unexpected probe exception in `edit_file`/`move_footprint`. Restoration failures retain explicit error and obligation evidence. Its earlier 44-case targeted result remains historical; the latest full suites above cover the later publication source. No exhaustive guarantee for every tool or arbitrary I/O failure is asserted.

The coherent [OpenSpec proposal](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/changes/fix-create-stage-evidence/proposal.md), [design](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/changes/fix-create-stage-evidence/design.md), [tasks](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/changes/fix-create-stage-evidence/tasks.md), and [SPEC.md](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/specs/SPEC.md) retain the contract mapping. Scoped strict validation does not establish repository-wide strict validation or a canonical-spec migration. Existing legacy warning/discovery limits remain described in [validation scope](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/openspec/changes/fix-create-stage-evidence/validation.md).

## Docs

The current [README](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/README.md), OpenSpec artifacts, medium evidence overview and publication-check index document the changed behavior and its validation. Supporting historical reports remain linked below.

### Historical references

Earlier results are retained for provenance, not used as current-head test counts:

- [Compatibility follow-up](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/output-profile-compatibility.md): the earlier 1,340/23 compatibility candidate and its version-specific checks.
- [Original combined validation](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/submission-validation.md): the earlier 1,296/23 candidate.
- [Recorded integration guide](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/create-recorded-e2e.md) and [historical replay results](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/create-recorded-e2e-results.md): original fixture integrity, command gating and negative controls.
- [Historical manual log](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/manual-test-log.md), [findings](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/copperhead-66-findings-report.md), and [evidence excerpts](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/copperhead-66-evidence-excerpts.md): earlier observed behavior and limitations.

The historical 500 mA experiment used `experimental-native`, resumed invocations and disclosed prototype-scope clarification. It has different provider/runtime provenance from the new normal Codex medium run; neither establishes official-provider/stateless parity across all providers. Private provider payloads and complete historical runtime/Git archives are not published. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation and review. No maintainer acceptance, bounty payment, fabrication approval or completed physical validation is claimed.

## Invariant checklist

The earlier [invariant mapping](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/invariant-evidence.md) remains a bounded attestation, supplemented by the later focused regressions and full-suite results. Spec gating, deterministic local check/verify, anchored KiCad edits, redaction and spec coherence retain their documented coverage. Mutation verification and sync-obligation exception handling have focused repair evidence; exhaustive coverage of all tools and I/O failures remains pending. The passed checks do not remove the DRC, provider-parity, provenance, legacy OpenSpec or physical-validation limits above.

The checked items retain the direct bounded evidence in [invariant-evidence.md](https://github.com/henry32511/copperhead/blob/2b9dd07d223f7f127141cf3393f19b2bdc580b49/reports/invariant-evidence.md) and the later passing suites. The two unchecked items have focused exception-repair evidence, but remain pending exhaustive review; the template check does not certify their truth.

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text). Proposal-gate omission and dispatch denial are covered by the mapped gating tests and real-tool replay.
- [ ] **Verification-gated out**: mutations still require ERC and board DRC, bounded repair and snapshot rollback. The reproduced `edit_file`/`move_footprint` probe-exception paths have focused repair evidence; exhaustive review of all tools and arbitrary I/O failures remains pending. Native raw DRC qualifications above remain explicit.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: the mapped module-graph regression rejects provider/SDK imports from the deterministic check path. This is bounded structural/test evidence, not packet-level formal attestation.

pulls.title: fix(draft): chain adjacent decap-row passives on rail-bank trunks (#233)
pulls.body:
## What

Chains adjacent decoupling capacitors and passive arrays placed in a decap row on shared rail-bank trunks, emitting exactly one power symbol per bank rather than isolated per-capacitor power islands.

## Why

Closes #233. Stacked passives previously drew with individual rail and ground symbols on every capacitor, causing 2.5x to 4x sheet footprint inflation across multi-cap banks (e.g. stickhub 16-cap bank carrying 26 power symbols instead of 2).

## Design

- Groups consecutive passives on identical power/ground nets at matching pin height into a single trunk run using splitBankRuns.
- Emits vertical stubs from pins joining horizontal trunk segments with interior meet junctions.
- Emits exactly one rail and one ground power symbol at the first stub end of the run.
- Enforces stubClear, 	ouchesForeign, and foreign stub boundary checks before creating trunk joins to prevent illegal net merges.

pulls.title: fix(agent): name the tool calls in a mixed reply that did not run (#306)
pulls.body:
## What

When a reply has some tool calls that run and some that do not, the agent is now told which ones did not run. Before this, those calls were dropped with no message and the model carried on as if they had worked.

## Why

Closes #306.

On the text protocol providers (`claude-code`, `cursor`) the tool catalog is fixed when the turn starts. If one reply holds `propose_change`, `validate_change` and then `write_file`, the first two run and the `write_file` calls are left as prose, because `write_file` was not in the catalog yet. The existing off-catalog message only fires when zero calls parsed, so a mixed reply got nothing. The same happens to a call that is one brace short next to valid calls. In the runs on the issue this ended in `finish` on files that were never written.

## Design

This follows the fix suggested by @thegoodengineer on the issue. The structural lock is not changed.

- [tool-protocol.ts](src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts): after the parsed calls are removed, `detectUndispatched` scans only the leftover prose for `"tool": "<name>"`. A name outside the catalog goes to `unavailable`, a catalog name goes to `malformed`. Scanning the leftover prose and not the full text keeps it from matching calls that did run.
- [types.ts](src/agent/types.ts), [claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts), [cursor.ts](src/agent/providers/cursor.ts): the result is carried on the turn as `undispatched`.
- [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts): after the tool results are pushed, the loop adds one user message naming those calls and records an `undispatched-calls` transcript event. The message is built after dispatch from the catalog and `ctx.editsUnlocked`. If `validate_change` unlocked the tool in the same reply, it says the tool is available now and to send the calls again. If edits are still locked, it says to call `propose_change` then `validate_change` first. If edits are unlocked and the name is still absent, it says the name is not a tool and lists the available ones.

Spec-gated in is preserved: `availableTools(ctx)` is untouched, so `write_file` and `edit_file` are still absent from the catalog until a proposal validates. Nothing is dispatched that was not dispatched before, the model only gets a message.

Not in this PR:

- `finish` in the same reply as dropped calls still ends the stage. The refuse-`finish` guard suggested by @animesh-chouhan is a separate change and I can do it as a follow-up if you want it.
- Skill sub-runs get the same turn but do not act on `undispatched` yet.
- The three places in the issue where the prompt and comment text invite this (`handlers.ts:171`, the comment above the catalog in `loop.ts`, `tool-protocol.ts:9`) are not edited here.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Added a paragraph on mixed replies and AC-3.22 to [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md). The edit lock and the tool list behave as before, this only adds feedback for calls that were already being dropped.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused | `npx vitest run test/tool-protocol.test.ts test/observability.test.ts test/cursor-provider.test.ts test/claude-code-provider.test.ts` | pass, 94 tests, 1 skipped |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1133 passed, 11 failed, 21 skipped |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | not keyed | skipped |

New tests: 5 parser tests and 4 message tests in [tool-protocol.test.ts](test/tool-protocol.test.ts), 2 loop tests in [observability.test.ts](test/observability.test.ts), and 1 forwarding test each in [cursor-provider.test.ts](test/cursor-provider.test.ts) and [claude-code-provider.test.ts](test/claude-code-provider.test.ts).

The 11 full-suite failures are the same 11 on an untouched `main` on my machine. They are KiCad environment failures: 5 in `kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts`, 4 in `draft-reference-boards.test.ts`, 1 in `draft-engine.test.ts`, 1 in `draft-tools.test.ts`. None touch the agent loop or the parser.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: none. I did not run the live `create` pipeline, I have no provider keyed for it. I ran the built parser on the reply shape from the issue.
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node manual.mjs   # parseToolCalls + renderUndispatched from dist/, reply = propose_change, validate_change, write_file, catalog without write_file
dispatched: propose_change, validate_change
undispatched: {"unavailable":["write_file"],"malformed":[]}
--- message when validate_change unlocked edits in the same reply
Some tool calls in your last reply did not run, so nothing they describe happened:
- "write_file": not in the tool catalog when you replied. It is available now, so send those calls again.
Do not assume a result for any of them.
--- message when edits are still locked
Some tool calls in your last reply did not run, so nothing they describe happened:
- "write_file": not in the tool catalog. Edit and drafting tools are withheld until a proposal validates: call propose_change, then validate_change, and send those calls in a later reply.
Do not assume a result for any of them.
```

## Docs

SPEC.md only, see above.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Verification-gated out**: N/A, no mutation or repair path changed

pulls.title: fix: explain why a schematic stage is incomplete
pulls.body:
## What

Fixes #326 by preserving and exposing the exact deterministic reason a schematic stage is incomplete. A resumed schematic now receives the same actionable diagnostic in its initial agent context, its in-run `finish` gate, and post-run recovery.

## Why

Issue: https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/issues/326

### Severity and persistence

This is a persistent create-pipeline blocker. It affects populated schematics whose intent fails deterministic validation or whose generated sheet is stale. Rerunning `create` cannot clear it: the same hidden check rejects the stage again.

### Exact root cause

The old schematic `isComplete` path called `draftSchematicToText()` with a real `FootprintResolver`, so it already had the authoritative failure:

```text
intent validation: 1 finding(s) to reconcile:
  1. J1 footprint "Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4085" differs from BOM.md's "Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal"; copy the BOM footprint exactly (do not substitute another package)
```

It discarded that evidence by reducing the result to:

```ts
if (!dry.ok) return false;
```

Three control-flow gaps compounded this:

1. Resume detection consumed only the boolean, so attempt 1 was not told why the stage reopened.
2. Schematic had no `stageGate`. ERC, symbol verification, legibility, and drift do not perform draft-intent validation, so all could pass before `finish`.
3. `contractGapDetail()` only diagnosed schematic legibility. Other failures became `no usable artifact was produced`, leaving recovery to infer an unrelated cause.

The deterministic validator knew the exact defect, but the model received a generic statement and guessed.

### Steps to reproduce before the fix

1. Start with a populated schematic and matching BOM.
2. Change J1 only in `schematic.intent.json` from:

```text
Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal
```

to:

```text
Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4085
```

3. Run `copperhead check`. The visible checks remain clean:

```text
ERC ✓
DRC ✓
drift ✓
legibility: 0 error, 1 advisory finding(s)
constraints ✓
```

4. Run `copperhead create --brief brief.md --model codex`.
5. Before this patch, stage 4 reopened without the validator finding, could pass every model-visible check, finish, and hit the same generic refusal again.

## Design

### Authoritative diagnostic

[src/commands/create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) adds `schematicContractGap(root): Promise<string | null>`. It evaluates and retains the first actionable failure for:

1. configured schematic and file existence;
2. symbol presence;
3. BOM/PINOUT drift, including concrete mismatches;
4. ERC, including formatted violations;
5. error-level legibility, grouped by finding kind;
6. deterministic intent validation, preserving exact validator findings;
7. byte equality between the sheet and a fresh deterministic re-draft.

`null` means the contract is satisfied. A string is deterministic repair guidance.

### Evidence reaches every decision point

- `STAGES.schematic.isComplete` derives its boolean from the diagnostic.
- A populated resume appends the diagnostic to attempt 1 under `Existing stage completion finding`.
- Schematic now receives a `stageGate`, so `finish` refuses with the real reason while the agent can still repair it.
- Post-run `contractGapDetail` reuses the same result instead of emitting a generic missing-artifact message.

This is Copperhead-generated diagnostic context, not human guidance. The live run was not interacted with after launch.

### Safety

No tools are added, no OpenSpec gate is bypassed, rollback behavior is unchanged, and no network access is added to deterministic checks. The existing footprint resolver remains in completion validation, preserving #325 pin/pad checks. Completion still requires drift, ERC, legibility, intent validation, and generated-sheet equality.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Adds AC-16.25 to [openspec/specs/SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md).
- Adds the incomplete-schematic resume scenario to [openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md).
- `npx openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1`: unavailable because the installed `openspec` package exposes no executable. This is reported as unavailable, not passed.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Focused unit and offline | `npx vitest run test/draft-tools.test.ts test/create-stage-turns.test.ts test/create-layout-draft.test.ts` | 23 pass, 1 unrelated fail |
| Full unit and offline | `npm test` | 1129 pass, 21 skip, 12 unrelated environment or baseline failures |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | saved-login `codex`, no API-key variable | pass for schematic repair and commit |

New regression coverage:

- Invalid intent preserves exact missing-pin and duplicate-net findings.
- A stale generated schematic explicitly requests `draft_schematic`.
- A footprint-pad mismatch appears in the first resumed schematic prompt.
- Schematic receives an actionable finish-time `stageGate`.
- The generic `no usable artifact was produced` message is absent.

Known unrelated focused-suite failure:

```text
FAIL test/create-layout-draft.test.ts
  a populated board that fails DRC stops before any agent turn, restores the board, and says why
AssertionError: expected layout.calls to deeply equal []
Expected: []
Received: one layout-draft agent call
```

This reproduces on the clean upstream-based worktree and an untouched `origin/main` snapshot. Full-suite failures are existing KiCad environment/baseline failures involving reference-board loading, library-table setup, and this layout preflight. No #326 regression test failed.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `create`, isolated clone of the real USB-C 5 V breakout workspace.
- Provider: saved-login `codex`.
- Human interaction after launch: none.
- Injected defect: J1 intent footprint changed to `Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4085`.

Before the autonomous run:

```text
$ node /path/to/patched/copperhead/dist/cli.js check
ERC ✓
DRC ✓
drift ✓
legibility: 0 error, 1 advisory finding(s) across 1 sheet(s)
legibility score: 85.35/100
constraints ✓

$ node --input-type=module -e '...schematicContractGap(process.cwd())...'
the schematic stage contract is not met; repair schematic.intent.json and call draft_schematic:
intent validation: 1 finding(s) to reconcile:
  1. J1 footprint "Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4085" differs from BOM.md's "Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal"; copy the BOM footprint exactly (do not substitute another package)
```

Actual autonomous repair:

```text
$ node /path/to/patched/copperhead/dist/cli.js create --brief brief.md --model codex
check_footprints: OK Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal
draft_schematic: drafted 4 group(s), 19 wire segment(s), 4 label(s), 6 no-connect(s) on A4
finish: all gates satisfied; run will commit
committed 7607e99162
done: ERC clean, committed 7607e99162
```

Copperhead itself selected the exact BOM footprint, called the real drafting tool, fixed documentation drift, ran verification, satisfied the new completion gate, and committed.

Independent after-fix verification:

```text
$ node /path/to/patched/copperhead/dist/cli.js check
ERC ✓
DRC ✓
drift ✓
legibility: 0 error, 1 advisory finding(s) across 1 sheet(s)
legibility score: 85.35/100
constraints ✓

$ node --input-type=module -e '...schematicContractGap(process.cwd())...'
contract_gap=null
```

The later layout stop was caused by pre-existing `_DRAFT` board footprints and occurred only after schematic commit. It is outside #326.

## Docs

- Updated the normative SPEC and active create-pipeline delta spec.
- Added a source contract comment explaining why resume, finish, and recovery must share one diagnostic.
- No user-facing command syntax or configuration changed.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text).
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: mutations still end in ERC (and DRC when the board changed) passing, with repair up to `maxRepairCycles` then rollback to the git snapshot.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: nothing reachable from `src/commands/check` touches a provider, an API key, or the network.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: the `src/kicad/` parser stays read-only; KiCad files are edited only via anchored exact-match text replace (no round-tripping).
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: post-tool-call hooks keep feeding the ledger, and commit keeps refusing while obligations are open.
- [x] **Secrets**: transcripts and summaries redact `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` at write time; keys live only in env vars; `.gitignore` keeps `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/`.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md and the active delta spec moved together. Automated OpenSpec validation is unavailable because the installed package has no executable, as disclosed above.

Closes #326

pulls.title: feat(review): grounded design review command (RFC 17)
pulls.body:
## What

A new experimental command, `copperhead review [design] --out <dir>`. It reviews a KiCad design, and every finding in its report rests on evidence a deterministic verifier checked. It never writes the design.

1. **Sweep:** copperhead-tools runs every applicable deterministic check over the design and any fabrication outputs (`--fab`: Gerbers, drill, BOM, placement; `--fab-profile` for the manufacturer's limits).
2. **Passes:** one model pass per domain (power, MCU, storage and I/O, firmware, physical, routing, fabrication outputs, BOM), `--parallel` at a time.
   - A pass reads a closed, hashed bundle through read-only queries (parts, nets, pins, datasheet pages, placement, routing, measurements, calculations).
   - It returns proposals: facts, quotations, measurements, calculations, findings, questions.
3. **Verify and render:** copperhead-tools' verifiers decide each proposal, and the report is rendered from what they decided.

Other modes:
- `--replay <dir>` re-verifies a record's stored proposals with no model, and passes only if the report is byte-identical.
- `--resume` continues a record that a killed run left.

## Why

A design review written by a model alone cannot be trusted line by line. On a real 90-part board, such a review found defects the deterministic checks missed. The same review also presented paraphrases as datasheet quotations, cited one part's guidance from another part's datasheet, and marked its own findings "verified".

RFC 17 sets the division of labour: the model proposes and deterministic verifiers decide. The deterministic half is in copperhead-tools (copperheadhq/copperhead-tools#17). This PR adds the half that calls the model.

## Design

OpenSpec change [add-grounded-review](openspec/changes/add-grounded-review/proposal.md), decisions D1 to D8 in [design.md](openspec/changes/add-grounded-review/design.md):

- **D1, the sweep is fixed.** It always runs first. The model never chooses which deterministic checks run (RFC 13 Section 18.4).
- **D2, the model only queries.** Its calls are read-only queries, `propose` (which runs the verifiers as a pre-check, so the model can fix a rejected proposal) and `submit`. No pass can write.
- **D3, a separate loop.** A pass is its own small loop over `Provider.chat`, not `runAgentLoop`. There is no git preflight, snapshot, restore, commit, obligations ledger or repair cycle, because a review mutates nothing.
- **D5 and D8, surviving interruptions.** Samples are saved and redacted after every turn. `--resume` keeps the passes that ended and reruns the rest. A timed-out turn is retried once.
- **D7, argument parsing.** The text tool protocol now reads arguments written as `arguments`, `parameters`, `input`, or flat beside `tool`. It used to read only `args`, so such calls arrived empty, and in testing the model concluded the tools were broken. Schema-shaped calls are unaffected.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- **Change:** `add-grounded-review`, with delta specs `cli-surface` (the command, resume, argument shapes) and `grounded-review` (fixed sweep, read-only passes, report from verification only, lockfile and replay). `openspec validate add-grounded-review --strict` passes.
- **SPEC.md section 3** gains the `review` command.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` (2 workers) | 1,116 pass, 24 fail, 21 skipped: all 24 failures are unrelated, see below |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run (no key on this machine); the manual run below drove a live model |

New tests in [review.test.ts](test/review.test.ts), 10 in total, all passing. They use a scripted provider and an injected copperhead-tools client:
- a pass that queries, pre-checks a proposal and submits
- stall, turn exhaustion and its warning
- turn timeout retried once, failing on the second
- a two-domain run never writes the design, writes its samples and lockfile, and replays byte-identically
- tampered proposals refused
- `--resume` keeps ended passes and reruns interrupted ones
- `--out` inside the design, or not empty, refused
- API keys redacted from samples and proposals
- argument shapes parsed

`tool-protocol.test.ts` passes.

Unrelated failures:
- **19 are environmental.** They fail at `assertDiskSpace`: "not enough free disk space to start (0.9 GiB available, 2.0 GiB required)". The test machine's disk was below the 2 GiB preflight.
- **5 predate this PR.** They are in `init-check`, `gating-sync`, `stage-completion` and `create-layout-draft`, and the same files also fail on a clean `origin/main` (e26be94) checkout on this machine.

### Manual test log (required)

- **Sandbox variant used:** none. The command was exercised against a real 90-part, four-layer KiCad project with its released Gerbers, BOM and placement file, not the `manual-tests` sandbox.
- **Commands run and outcome:**

```text
$ copperhead review <project> --out <record> \
    --fab <gerbers> <bom.csv> <cpl.csv> --fab-profile <jlcpcb.profile.yaml> \
    --source <research> --source <brief> --source <requirements> --source <docs> --source <firmware> \
    --model claude-code:claude-opus-5-5 --domains P,M,S,F,L,R,G,B --max-turns 40 --parallel 2 \
    --tools <copperhead-tools>/dist/cli.js
sweep: {"completed":18,"mode":"complete","runs":24,"skipped":6,...}
bundle: {"board":true,"nets":87,"parts":90,"sources":532,"sweepFindings":144}
  P: submitted, 38 turns, 41 proposals, 698 s
  M: failed, 2 turns, 0 proposals, 689 s (turn exceeded 600 s)
  S: submitted, 38 turns, 21 proposals, 727 s
  F: submitted, 38 turns, 32 proposals, 544 s
  L: submitted, 39 turns, 31 proposals, 417 s
  R: submitted, 39 turns, 23 proposals, 305 s
  G: submitted, 39 turns, 31 proposals, 389 s
  B: submitted, 39 turns, 28 proposals, 492 s

$ copperhead review <project> --out <record> ... --resume     # with the turn-timeout retry
[P] resume: keeping the pass that ended submitted after 38 turns   (and S, F, L, R, G, B)
  M: submitted, 37 turns, 40 proposals, 685 s
verification: {"findingsPresented":30,"proposals":247,"rejected":2,"undecided":12,"verified":233}

$ copperhead review --replay <record> --tools <copperhead-tools>/dist/cli.js   # no model credentials in the environment
replay identical
```

Against an earlier model-only review of the same board (39 findings), the run found all three of its Critical and High defects, grounded. The copperhead-tools sweep checks found two of them with no model. 15 of the 39 were found in all, and 3 more were raised as questions.

Two presented findings had true premises but wrong conclusions: a requirement a later recorded decision had replaced, and firmware stubs the plan schedules. Findings therefore stay INFERRED with confidence at most 0.6, and the prompt now tells passes to check decision logs first (template 0.2.0).

The first full run was lost when the test machine ran out of memory with four passes plus a test suite. That loss produced per-turn sample saves and `--resume`, which then recovered the failed pass above.

## Docs

- SPEC.md section 3 (`copperhead review`)
- `copperhead review --help`

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] **Spec-gated in**: N/A. A review pass is offered only read-only queries, `propose` and `submit`; `edit_file`/`write_file` are never in its tool list, and the `do` loop is untouched.
- [ ] **Verification-gated out**: N/A. A review mutates nothing; the record goes to `--out`, which must lie outside the design.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: `src/review` is imported lazily from `cli.ts` only; nothing reachable from `src/commands/check` imports it.
- [ ] **No sexp serialization**: N/A. No KiCad file is parsed or written here; board reading is copperhead-tools'.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A. Review passes do not use the ledger or commit.
- [x] **Secrets**: pass samples and merged proposals are redacted with `redactSecrets` at write time (tested); the model runs through the existing providers, keys stay in env.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md section 3 and the change artifacts (proposal, design, delta specs, tasks) moved together; `openspec validate add-grounded-review --strict` passes.

pulls.title: test: add gated create end-to-end coverage
pulls.body:
## What

Adds bounded end-to-end coverage for the `create` pipeline so a real eight-stage run can be verified without silently invoking a paid provider during normal CI. The new test also catches missing final stages, resumed artifacts, and zero-symbol schematic false positives.

## Why

Issue #66 needs evidence that `copperhead create` can complete and independently commit all eight stages. Existing mocked coverage stops before the full pipeline and cannot establish that final-stage guarantee.

## Design

The change adds [test/create-e2e.test.ts](test/create-e2e.test.ts) with four offline assertions plus an explicitly gated live CLI smoke test. The live path only runs when `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CREATE=1` and a model is explicitly supplied, preserves run evidence for triage, verifies eight fresh stage commits, reruns each real stage completion contract, and requires a clean tree plus `DEVPLAN.md` at HEAD. Details and current limitations are recorded in [reports/create-e2e-findings.md](reports/create-e2e-findings.md).

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |

pulls.title: fix: gate fabrication exports on release readiness
pulls.body:
## What

This PR prevents `export_outputs` from generating fabrication files until the design passes a fresh fabrication-readiness preflight. It also adds `check --fab`, records successful export provenance, and requires current, complete fabrication outputs before Stage 6 is considered complete.

## Why

Closes #357

The current exporter treats a successful KiCad subprocess as sufficient evidence that a design is ready for fabrication. In practice, a design can still have DRC violations, unrouted connections, unverified BOM rows, schematic-to-PCB mismatches, or incomplete output files and yet produce an `outputs/` directory.

This creates a hazardous false-positive state: generated artifacts look releasable even though the design has not satisfied the release criteria.

## Design

The implementation adds a shared fabrication gate in [fab.ts](src/kicad/fab.ts), used by both `export_outputs` and `check --fab`:

- Run fresh ERC and DRC checks, reject every DRC violation, and require zero unrouted connections.
- Require complete BOM fields and reject every `UNVERIFIED` part during strict export checks.
- Compare schematic and PCB references, footprint identifiers, pad sets, and pad-to-net assignments.
- Normalize KiCad representation-only net differences: root-sheet PCB `/NAME` matches schematic `NAME`, and generated `unconnected-(...)` pad nets match schematic pins with no net. Hierarchical paths remain significant.
- Parse KiCad S-expressions with strict structural checks so truncated, unbalanced, wrong-root, or unterminated input fails closed.
- Delay creation of `outputs/` until preflight succeeds.
- Require both Gerber and drill artifacts after the exporter exits successfully.
- Clear stale provenance before an export attempt and write new provenance only after complete success.
- Record the board SHA-256, generated file paths, and generation timestamp in `.copperhead/config.json`.
- Treat Stage 6 as complete only when the recorded board hash is current, Gerber and drill outputs are present, every recorded file exists, and all recorded paths remain inside the repository.

The normal `check` path remains unchanged. `check --fab` adds fabrication diagnostics, while `check --fab --strict` applies export-level strictness.

The load-bearing decisions and failure behavior are documented in [design.md](openspec/changes/add-fab-release-gate/design.md).

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Validation: `openspec validate add-fab-release-gate` passed.

pulls.title: fix(draft): ERC exclusions in the schematic intent (#355)
pulls.body:
## What

The schematic intent gains an optional `ercExclusions` array. Each entry names a KiCad ERC check, the part pins it excuses and a reason. `run_erc`, the stage-4 completion check and `copperhead check` apply the entries, and every excused finding is still printed with its reason. Closes #355.

## Why

Some stock KiCad symbols type a pin conservatively, so wiring the part's datasheet requires fails ERC. `Sensor_Motion:LIS3DH` types SDO/SA0 as Output, yet tying it to GND is how the I2C address is set. `Power_Management:TPS22917DBV` types QOD as open collector and VOUT as power output, yet QOD tied to VOUT is the datasheet's quick-output-discharge connection. The intent could not say such a finding was meant, `edit_file` refuses the drafted sheet, and the gate fails on any violation, warnings included. On a 90-footprint data logger, stage 4 drew a complete sheet (drift clean, all 64 MCU pins matching the brief's pin map) and refused at turn 39 of 80 on six such findings (#355 has the run's ERC output).

## Design

- **IR field** ([ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts)): `ercExclusions?: { type, pins, reason }[]`. Validation refuses a non-array, a non-object entry, a type that is not a check name, an empty reason, an empty or non-string `pins`, an unknown part, a missing pin, and a pin in no net (an open pin belongs in `noConnect`). Each problem is its own numbered finding, like the rest of the IR.
- **Matching** ([erc-exclusions.ts](src/kicad/erc-exclusions.ts)): an entry excuses a finding only when the check matches and every part pin the finding names is listed. Power-symbol pins (`#FLG01`, `#PWR03`) are placed by the engine, so they need no listing. A finding with a non-pin item (a label, a wire) is never excused. This keeps an entry from swallowing a different finding on the same pin.
- **Where it applies**: `runErcWithExclusions(schPath)` reads the intent beside an engine-drafted sheet (the `copperhead-draft` generator marker) and applies it to `runErc`'s report. A hand-drawn sheet never takes exclusions from an intent file. The three gates that decide ERC ([handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts) `run_erc`, [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) stage-4 completion, [check.ts](src/commands/check.ts)) call it. `runErc` itself still returns KiCad's raw report. The wrapper lives outside `cli.ts` because `footprints.ts` already imports `cli.ts`, and `ir.ts` imports `footprints.ts`.
- **Visibility** ([report.ts](src/kicad/report.ts)): excused findings move from `violations` to `excluded`, each with its entry's reason and pins, and `ok` is recomputed. `formatViolations` prints them under "excluded by schematic.intent.json ercExclusions (not counted, listed for review)", even when ERC is otherwise clean. An entry that excused nothing is printed as stale. The run summary's ERC line lists each excluded finding with its reason ([loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts)).
- **Why pins and not `.kicad_pro`**: #355 suggested writing KiCad's own `erc_exclusions`. KiCad keys those by marker position and item UUIDs, which change with every re-draft, so an entry would stop matching after the next `draft_schematic`. Pin-keyed entries in the IR survive re-drafts and sit beside the nets that cause them. KiCad's own ERC window does not read them and still shows the markers. Writing them into `.kicad_pro` as well could follow if that matters.
- **Prompt**: the stage-4 prompt documents the field and says when to use it (a connection a requirement makes, on a conservatively typed pin), with a reason citing the SPEC item, and never to avoid fixing wiring.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md): new **AC-16.81 (declared ERC exclusion is excused and shown)**, next to AC-16.10 (declared no-connect passes ERC).
- No active change's artifacts cover the drafting IR, so no delta spec moves.
- The IR stays `version: 1`: the field is optional, and an intent without it behaves as before.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1146 pass, 3 fail (pre-existing, below), 21 skip; run on this branch plus the #241 cherry-pick |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run |

New: [test/erc-exclusions.test.ts](test/erc-exclusions.test.ts), 14 tests. They cover pin parsing, matching (listed pins, power-flag pins, a different check, an unlisted pin, a non-pin item), applying exclusions and recomputing `ok`, stale entries, the printed output and summary line, reading the intent beside an engine-drafted sheet but not a hand-drawn one, and every IR validation finding.

Pre-existing failures on this machine, unrelated to this PR:
- 3 tests fail identically on unmodified `e26be94`: `init-check` clean fixture, `gating-sync` invariant 1, `stage-completion` legibility gate.
- Cause: the `open-key` fixture embeds an older copy of `Device:R` and has no vendored library or project `sym-lib-table`. On a host whose global `sym-lib-table` resolves the stock KiCad 10 libraries, ERC compares against those and reports `lib_symbol_mismatch` ("Symbol 'R' doesn't match copy in library 'Device'"), and the gate counts warnings. Not touched here.

### Manual test log (required)

- **Sandbox:** not the `manual-tests` sandboxes. I used a clone of a real `create` workspace (the 90-footprint data logger from #355) at its stage-3 commit, with the stage-4 scaffold and config, and the intent from the run's last `draft_schematic` call with six `ercExclusions` entries added. Drafting it writes `sym-lib-cache/` and the project `sym-lib-table`, as stage 4 does.
- **Commands:** `copperhead draft schematic --intent schematic.intent.json` with the built `dist/cli.js`, then `copperhead check`.
- **Outcome:** ERC clean, with the six pin findings from #355 listed as excluded, each with its reason. `check` exits 0. Before this change, the same intent gives the six findings as violations (#355 has that run's output). The five legibility errors from #355 (#210 territory) are unchanged by this PR.

```text
$ node dist/cli.js draft schematic --intent schematic.intent.json
  ...
  PWR_FLAG synthesized on: GND, VBUS, VDDA
  sheet fit: A2, ink 29% of the usable frame, compaction pinned

$ node dist/cli.js check
ERC: clean; 6 finding(s) excluded by the intent
  excluded by schematic.intent.json ercExclusions (not counted, listed for review):
    error pin_to_pin [sheet /]: Pins of type Output and Power output are connected
      - Symbol U9 Pin 7 [SDO, Output, Line] @ (1.6891, 3.2639)
      - Symbol #FLG01 Hidden pin 1 [pwr, Power output, Line] @ (1.9939, 1.0668)
      reason (U9.7): LIS3DH SDO/SA0 tied to GND selects I2C address 0x18 (brief item 20)
    error pin_to_pin [sheet /]: Pins of type Open collector and Power output are connected
      ...
      reason (U3.5, U3.6): TPS22917 QOD tied to VOUT enables quick output discharge per its datasheet (brief item 17)
    ...
      reason (U6.7, U2.5): W25Q128 /HOLD tied to 3V3 disables hold in single-SPI use (brief item 19)
DRC ✓
legibility: 5 error, 3 advisory finding(s) across 1 sheet(s):
  ...
$ echo $?
0
```

The agent-loop path (`run_erc` and `finish` inside a live `create` stage 4, with the agent writing the entries) has not been run yet with this change. It is next, on the board from #355.

## Docs

- [schematic-intent.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-intent.md): a new `ercExclusions[]` section, plus the field in the top-level shape table, the validation contract and the version history.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: untouched. No tool list or unlock logic changed.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: ERC still runs after every schematic mutation and still gates `finish` and stage completion. An exclusion excuses only a finding the IR names by check and pins, and it stays in the output.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: `check` now imports `src/kicad/erc-exclusions.ts`, which imports only `fs`, `path`, `ir.ts`, `cli.ts`, `fab.ts` and `report.ts` types. No provider is reachable.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: nothing is written to the sheet or the project. The intent is read as JSON.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, the ledger is untouched.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md gains AC-16.81. No active change's artifacts cover the drafting IR.

pulls.body:
This PR adds two things to the intake: part pack export, and proposals of circuit-block roles. Both feed copperhead-tools' design-review tools (copperheadhq/copperhead-tools #1–#10, Copperhead RFC 4 §6.3).

**Part pack export** (`add-part-pack-export`)
- `PACK_FIELD_SPECS`: regulator fields for feedback and output voltage, rated current, current limit, switching frequency, dropout, enable threshold and junction temperature.
- `core/pack.ts`: admitted readings become pack facts, one per row with its MIN/TYP/MAX, quoting the line on its page. Readings of a family datasheet's other variants are left out.
- `scripts/pack.ts` drafts a pack with no `confirmedBy`, so the tools list it and never use it.
- `scripts/confirm-pack.ts` re-checks every quote against its page before writing a person's name.
- **Live trial:** a pack for the AP63205, drafted from its four-variant family datasheet, agreed with a hand-written pack on every fact both hold. It confirmed cleanly, and confirmation was refused when one quote was altered.

**Binding proposals** (`add-binding-proposals`)
- `proposals/bindings.ts` and `scripts/propose-bindings.ts`: one reasoning-only Claude call turns block-map's context bundles into a bindings file with `proposedBy`. Parts outside the bundles are dropped, and block-map checks every remaining part against its role's nets before use (RFC 17: the model proposes, a verifier decides).
- **Evaluation** on the 28 regulators the deterministic map missed or bound differently from the labels (13 BoardRepo designs): regulators found 15 → 28, kinds agreeing 14 → 28, role precision 94.5 % → 96.9 %, recall 48.2 % → 69.6 %. The verifier refused 42 proposed parts.

**Dependency:** `yaml`, used by the scripts only.

This PR implements the OpenSpec change `ground-intake-extraction`: the intake becomes Copperhead's one datasheet extraction path, with the rigor copperhead-cortex was built for.

- **Knowledge core vendored from cortex** (b4a45e8, Apache-2.0): exact decimals with units, MIN/TYP/MAX qualifiers, condition sets, nine validators, the ladder, the verdict engine and the evaluation harness.
