pulls.title: fix: resolve pipeline blockers and false-greens for bounty 66
pulls.body:
## What
Fixes pipeline blocks, missing DRC enforcement, and false-green completion checks for Bounty #66. Adds a full end-to-end integration test.

## Why
Required to meet the bounty specifications, ensuring the copperhead create pipeline completes all 8 stages cleanly and exits 0 natively without manual artifact intervention.

## Testing
Tested via itest run test/create-e2e.test.ts ensuring clean execution of all 8 pipeline stages.

## Invariants
- [ ] I have read the CONTRIBUTING.md document.
- [ ] Code compiles and passes all tests locally.

## Findings Report
# Copperhead Pipeline Findings Report

## BLOCKER
**Where**: `src/commands/create.ts` (outputs and spec-seed stages)
**Symptom**: Uncommitted files. The `emitJlcpcbAfterOutputs` and `writeBriefHash` functions generate tracking artifacts (`BOM.csv` and `BRIEF.sha256`) outside of the `runAgentLoop`'s commit boundary. These files are grouped into the subsequent stage's commit, breaking the "independent stage commit" requirement.
**Suggested**: Check if the working tree `isDirty` after generating pipeline artifacts, and immediately `commitAll` the generated files.
**Status**: Fixed
**Priority**: P0

## DEFECT
**Where**: `src/commands/create.ts` (`layout-draft` stage `isComplete` check)
**Symptom**: DRC False-Green. The stage completion check does not execute the Design Rules Check (`runDrc`), even though the stage prompt strictly requires all routed nets to pass DRC.
**Suggested**: Invoke `runDrc(p)` during `isComplete` and ensure it returns an `ok` result before allowing the stage to pass.
**Status**: Fixed
**Priority**: P0

## DEFECT
**Where**: `src/commands/create.ts` (`layout-draft` stage `isComplete` check)
**Symptom**: Content False-Green. The stage is considered complete as long as the board contains a footprint and `LAYOUT.md` includes the heading `## Draft quality`. Since the `init` script scaffolds `LAYOUT.md` with this exact heading, the agent can bypass drafting the actual quality documentation by just adding a footprint.
**Suggested**: Use regex and string manipulation to isolate the content *beneath* the `## Draft quality` heading and verify it contains at least one non-empty line of text.
**Status**: Fixed
**Priority**: P1

## NOTE
**Where**: `test/create-e2e.test.ts`
**Symptom**: Missing end-to-end coverage for the complete pipeline.
**Suggested**: Added a deterministic end-to-end integration test mocking the agent loop to successfully produce passing artifacts for all 8 stages, asserting `res.ok` and all 8 stages run to completion.
**Status**: Fixed
**Priority**: P1

pulls.body:
## What

`parseBomTable` now skips any Refdes-headed table that has no Value column, instead of reading that table's second cell as the part value. A supporting table in BOM.md (for example a symbol availability audit) can no longer inject a phantom row that overrides a real part's value. Refdes, Footprint and MPN keep their positional fallbacks; Value alone has none.

## Why

Closes #321. `parseBomTable` fell back to column index 1 when it could not find a Value header, so any Refdes-headed table without one had its second cell read as the value.

I hit this in a fresh `create` run on a 4-diode AC-to-DC brief. Stage 3 wrote a "Symbol availability audit" table (`Refdes | Symbol lib_id | Symbol exists? | Pins read back...`) into docs/BOM.md. The parser read `Device:C_Polarized` as the value of C1, next to the real `4700uF`. The stage-4 BOM/IR cross-check then blocked with: C1 value "4700uF" differs from BOM.md's "Device:C_Polarized". The schematic stage ended after three attempts (one turn-budget exhaustion, two refusals) with zero symbols placed. #321 reports the same mechanism with different tables (J1's value became "0 mA").

## Design

One change in src/memory/bom-table.ts: `parseBomTable` resolves the Value column by header name only, and skips a table that has no Value header. Refdes (0), Footprint (2) and MPN (3) still resolve by header name with a fallback to the canonical index. Value is the only column with no fallback, because Value is what separates a BOM row from a supporting-table row.

Behavior:

- A Refdes-headed table with no Value column now yields zero rows.
- A real BOM table that is missing its Value header is no longer parsed as a BOM.
- Not addressed: a supporting table that does have a Value header and repeats a refdes is still read as a BOM table. This fix keys on the Value header and does not pick a single canonical table among several. That is a separate follow-up.
- `isHeader` is unchanged because pin-headed tables still need it.
- `export bom` is not touched. #99 is a separate issue.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec change.

## Testing

New tests in test/bom-table.test.ts:

- ignores a Refdes-headed table with no Value column and keeps the real row
- does not let a quiescent-current or lib_id table override a real value (the repro from #321)
- still parses a normal Refdes | Value | Footprint | MPN | Rationale BOM unchanged
- parses a BOM with extra appended columns (Manufacturer, LCSC)
- ignores a pin-headed table

Results: `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass. `npm test`: 1133 passed, 3 failed. The same 3 tests (test/init-check.test.ts, test/gating-sync.test.ts, test/stage-completion.test.ts) fail on the v0.11.0 tag without this change. On my machine KiCad 10.0.6 ERC emits `lib_symbol_mismatch` warnings on the test fixture, and the code treats warnings as errors.

Manual test: I re-ran the same brief with `create --model compat:deepseek-chat` (Linux, KiCad 10.0.6, Node 20.20.2) on this branch. The stage-4 cross-check no longer blocks. Stages 1 to 6 completed (spec-seed, architecture, part-selection, schematic, layout-draft, outputs). Stage 7 (firmware) refused because the board has no MCU and the run exited 1, which is unrelated to this change. Before the fix, the same brief stopped at stage 4.

## Docs

No README, config or changelog changes. The JSDoc on `parseBomTable` states the Value rule.

pulls.title: fix(kicad): cache library pad sets per process, rank variant hints by family; close the #344 review findings
pulls.body:
## What

Closes the five findings of the automated review on #344 (https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/pull/344#issuecomment-5854352045): the footprint-library pad sets behind the pad check are cached once per process instead of once per resolver, the variant hint prefers the footprint's own family, and the surface the review found untested now has tests, including a loop-level test for the finish guard on the repair budget.

## Why

- [footprints.ts](src/kicad/footprints.ts): `variantCovering` parsed every `.kicad_mod` in a library on each new resolver, and `create` builds a new resolver for every completion check of the schematic stage, so one no-variant pairing in a ~1000-file library cost seconds of I/O per check.
- The hint named the first exact pad cover alphabetically, so a two-pin part on `SOT-23` was told to use `TO-252-2_TabPin1`, a DPAK.
- The finish guard at [loop.ts:670](src/agent/loop.ts#L670) had no loop-level test; the PR body of #344 wrongly said no scripted-provider harness existed, but [pre-touched.test.ts](test/pre-touched.test.ts) has one.
- Nine new branches and error paths from #344 were reached by no test.

## Design

- Pad sets live in a module-level map keyed by the library directory and its mtime (a file added or removed changes the mtime), read once per process per directory state. Missing or unreadable directories and malformed files are skipped, as before.
- Of several fitting variants the one sharing the longest name prefix with the offending footprint wins, alphabetical order breaking ties. The stock USB-C case is unchanged: the same-family `_6P` receptacles share the `USB_C_Receptacle_` prefix.
- The loop-level test drives `runAgentLoop` with a scripted provider and `maxRepairCycles: 1`: it unlocks edits, lays a copper track across the board edge (a `copper_edge_clearance` error), makes a repair that does not help (the one cycle), then removes the track, runs DRC, ERC and drift and calls `finish` in the same reply; the run finishes rather than rolling back. It stubs an empty `KICAD_CONFIG_HOME`, as CI has, so a machine whose Device library differs from the fixture's embedded copies does not fail ERC on `lib_symbol_mismatch`.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behaviour changes: the cache and the ranking are implementation detail under AC-15.34, and the tests cover behaviour #344 already specified. `openspec validate fix-layout-draft-footprints` passes.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1127 pass, 3 fail (pre-existing, see below), 21 skip |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | skip (not run) |

New tests: [repair-finish-guard.test.ts](test/repair-finish-guard.test.ts) (finding 1); in [draft-ir-bom.test.ts](test/draft-ir-bom.test.ts): `exposedPads` with a `-2EP` name, `variantCovering` on a bad id, an unknown library, a library removed from disk and a malformed neighbour, the longest-prefix ranking, the combined missing-pad plus unnamed-pad refusal, and the warning reaching the draft report's notes (findings 3 and 4); in [board-populate.test.ts](test/board-populate.test.ts): a value holding a tab and a newline survives populate escaped and the board loads (finding 3).

Pre-existing failures on this machine, identical on `main` and on the `v0.11.0` tag, passing in CI: `init-check`, `gating-sync`, `stage-completion` (this machine's KiCad symbol libraries differ from the fixture's embedded copies).

### Manual test log (required)

pulls.title: fix(draft): draw op-amp stages the way the handbook does
pulls.body:
## What

The drafting engine now lays op-amp circuits out the way a drafter (and TI's op-amp handbook) draws them. The changes:

- Inverting stages are mirrored so the feedback loop runs over the amplifier.
- Feedback loops clear the supply symbols.
- Test points sit in the signal path, with ground probes in a grid at the right.
- Summing inputs stack on one bus.
- Wires no longer cross or run along pin leads.
- The engine and the checker both use the real title block.

## Why

Every schematic in TI's *Handbook of Operational Amplifier Applications* (SBOA092B, 113 circuits) was drafted with the engine and compared against the book's own drawing. Every netlist was exact, but the drawings misled:

- 160 wires crossed a foreign pin lead, so parts read as shorted.
- 87 supply symbols sat on feedback parts.
- 163 terminals were joined only by labels.
- 15 sheets put content inside the title block.

## Design

All rules are general; none is keyed to a circuit. Everything is in [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts) plus the title-block constant in [legibility.ts](src/kicad/legibility.ts).

- `amplifierFlip`: an amplifier unit is drawn `mirror x` (inverting input on top) when that input is a summing junction, meaning fed back from the unit's own output AND fed a signal from elsewhere. Feedback is inferred only through passive parts (at most three pins, all passive); an analog switch or IC on the inverting input is neither feedback nor an input unless it drives the junction. Returns to a rail and bootstraps do not count as signals, and a unit whose output drives its own '-' input is never turned over, so non-inverting stages and followers keep the symbol's orientation.
- Feedback bridges pass beyond a supply pin's stub, power symbol and name on their side, and the amplifier's cell reserves what the stacked loops need.
- A one-pin `TestPoint` is a probe, not a connector. It ends the run it sits on, and on an IC pin it lies on the pin's row. Rail and ground probes stand in a vertically centred grid at the group's right end.
- Pin leads are routing obstacles in `admit`: a wire meets a lead only at its connection point.
- Fan-in: further independent inputs into one pin lie on stacked rows in reference order, joined by one bus. Internal nodes and feedback chains still hang.
- A straight hang is not blocked by a pin on the side it never reaches, when its net has nothing else to route.
- The title block is KiCad's real 110 x 34 mm corner in both the engine and the checker. The spec (AC-16.50) already names the 110 mm corner. A sheet still overlapping it after re-tiling moves up a paper size, and again while a larger one remains.
- Colliding power and flag glyphs turn along their stub, then over. Dangling wire tails past a junction are trimmed; a free end survives only where it ends on, or tees into, another item. A glyph never turns back toward its own pin or onto a placed body. A loop tap drops the unused stub. Field text takes the least-cluttered slot when none is clear.
- Tighter spacing:
  - no label reserve for a run ending at a terminal;
  - label reach counted past a cell's own shelf;
  - one margin between columns that no signal net joins.

Invariants: the change is confined to deterministic placement and routing (LLM-free, network-free). The sexp parser stays read-only, the draft still writes the sheet through `emit`, and no agent, tool, gating or ledger code is touched.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | not run separately (typecheck covers the same tsc project) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 1131 passed, 21 skipped (80 files) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on provider env vars | n/a: no LLM path changed |

The byte-pinned goldens changed intentionally and were regenerated after an old/new visual comparison of each:

- **buck:** BOOT no longer crosses L1's lead.
- **npn-switch:** the MCU box is out of the title block and SW is wired.
- **ldo, usb-atmega-node, Tier C:** shifted clear of the real title block, or a power glyph turned along its stub.

The reference PNGs were re-rendered at their original size. New tests:

- [draft-opamp.test.ts](test/draft-opamp.test.ts), with five hermetic TI-handbook stages plus a switched-gain variant in `test/fixtures/draft-opamp/`: inverting, integrator and summer are mirrored while follower, non-inverting and switched-gain (analog switch across the feedback resistor) are not; each drafts ERC-clean with no legibility errors; the summer's inputs stack R1 < R2 < R3 in one column with each terminal on its row; rail probes stand at the right.
- [legibility.test.ts](test/legibility.test.ts): the full 110 x 34 mm title block is reserved on A5 (fails with the old clamp).

Beyond these, coverage comes from the golden corpus, the reference boards and the handbook sweep below. After the review fixes, all 113 handbook circuits are ERC-clean (stock: 3 with violations) with no dangling wire ends.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `draft` (deterministic drafting, no agent run).
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
# every TI handbook circuit (113), drafted per engine build, netlist exported and compared, ERC, legibility, render
$ npx tsx src/cli.ts --repo <circuit-dir> draft schematic      (x113)
drafted 113/113, netlist exact 113/113, legibility errors 0, out-of-frame 0, title-block overlap 0
before (main before #317's final commits) -> after: wires across a foreign pin lead 160 -> 0,
supply symbol on a part 87 -> 2, label-only terminals 163 -> 11, circuits with any geometric defect 100 -> ~20;
110 circuits better, 0 worse

# holdout, never tuned against
$ npm run refboards -- --update                                 4 boards drafted, ERC clean, legibility clean
$ npx tsx scripts/draft-real-designs.ts cm5_minima complex_hierarchy ecc83 interf_u multichannel \
    pic_programmer royalblue54L_feather "sonde xilinx" tiny_tapeout
8 drafted with 0 pins lost/gained; sonde xilinx refused (merged net), as before this change
legibility errors 38 -> 21, wires across a foreign pin lead 31 -> 1, out-of-frame 3 -> 0, 5 better / 0 worse
Klon Centaur (69 parts), balanced-input crossover, 4 reference boards: 4 better / 0 worse, ERC unconnected-wire 1 -> 0
```

Known remaining:

- Passive networks with no amplifier to anchor them (meter bridges, twin-T) are still drawn as label-joined columns.
- Two dense passive circuits (p86, p91) gained one label split each.

## Docs

The spec and docs move with the code:

- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md): AC-16.39 now says test points are terminals (inline, rise fallback, rail grid). AC-16.47 adds paper escalation. AC-16.50 says 110 x 34 mm on every paper. New AC-16.73 to AC-16.80 cover inverting stages turned over, feedback clearing the supply, leads as obstacles, fan-in rows, one-sided straight hangs, power glyphs keeping apart, no dangling tails, and spacing counting what is drawn.
- [schematic-drafting.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-drafting.md) and [schematic-legibility.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-legibility.md) follow.

Behaviour note: `check` is now stricter on A4/A5 sheets. The checker used to clamp the title block on small paper; it now reserves the full 110 x 34 mm, so content in that corner that used to pass is flagged out-of-frame.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: N/A, no agent tool list change.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: N/A, no mutation or verification path change.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: the only checker change is the title-block size in `legibility.ts` (no clamp on small paper); no I/O added.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: the parser is untouched; drafting writes a new sheet through the existing emitter as before.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, not touched.
- [x] **Secrets**: N/A, not touched.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md AC-16.39, AC-16.47 and AC-16.50 are updated and AC-16.73 to AC-16.80 are added; `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` passes.

pulls.title: fix: close the post-0.11 review findings in draft, create and the agent loop
pulls.body:
## What

Closes the findings of the post-v0.11.0 review of main: the pad-coverage check no longer refuses KiCad's own symbol/footprint pairs, the placement search no longer spends minutes on large boards, routing progress counts against the repair budget, a batched turn that finishes verified is not rolled back, and an already-populated board gets its DRC on resume. Plus three small fixes: dotted numbering and any case in the Draft quality heading, CRLF before a harness marker, and newline/tab escaping in populate.

## Why

The review of the nine PRs merged since v0.11.0 (#269, #317, #319, #334, #335, #336, #340, #341, #342) found two user-facing regressions and a few gaps. No issues were filed for them; the original issues (#320, #325, #327, #331) are closed by those PRs and stay closed.

- **Pad check (#341)**: every numbered pad without a symbol pin was an error. A scan of all stock symbols with a default footprint found 185 pairs refused only by that rule: the MCP73831 on its DFN-8-1EP (exposed pad 9 the symbol does not name), the FT232RL on SSOP-28 and the PIC families (NC leads the symbol omits), a 2-pin crystal on the 4-pad 3225 footprint. The advice could not be followed because the footprint was already the right one.
- **Placement search (#340)**: every trial is a full draft pass and the 60-pass budget was spent in intent order, so a 160-part board went from 5 s on v0.11.0 to 310 s on main and kept nothing.
- **Repair budget (#335)**: the "unrouted is cosmetic" branch was dead code, because the normaliser lifts `unconnected_items` into `unrouted` and never into the violations, and the test for it passed vacuously. The budget was also checked before `finish` in the same turn, so a batched turn that spent the last cycle, fixed, passed and finished was rolled back.
- **create**: populate returned early on an already-populated board without DRC, so a run killed between the populate write and its DRC resumed onto an unverified board.

## Design

- [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts): a pad the library marks `pad_prop_heatsink` is exempt (868 of the 1000 stock `-1EP` footprints); on a footprint named for an exposed pad, the highest-numbered pad(s) the symbol does not name are the exposed pad ([exposedPads](src/kicad/footprints.ts)); the remaining unnamed pads are refused only when the library ships a variant whose electrical pads are exactly the symbol's pins ([FootprintResolver.variantCovering](src/kicad/footprints.ts), pad sets read once per resolver, only on the mismatch path), and otherwise become a note in the draft report via `validated.warnings`. #325 still refuses, and now names the 6-contact variant.
- [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts): a clean baseline (no overlaps, no crossings) is not searched on boards over 25 parts (small boards keep their wire-length search, so the pinned reference boards are byte-identical); `searchPassBudget` shrinks with part count (60 up to 25 parts, 15 at 100, never under 6, a part-count rule so the kept result is machine-independent); trials go first to parts on crossing nets, intent order breaking ties.
- [handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts): `countRepairCycle` returns early when electrical findings are zero and `unrouted` dropped. [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts): the exhaustion check is skipped when `ctx.finishRequest` is set, since finish is approved only after the checks passed. Verification-gated out is preserved: a failing check still blocks finish exactly as before; only when rollback fires changed.
- [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts): an already-populated board always gets the populate-time DRC. A HEAD comparison was tried first and cannot work: `commitResumedStage` sweeps a managed dirty board into HEAD at pipeline start, unverified. The stop message says the board is left in place in that case, since there is nothing older to restore.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- SPEC.md: AC-15.34 (pad exemptions, variant rule, note), AC-16.70 (clean-baseline skip, budget, ranking), §4 step 5 (unrouted progress).
- `fix-layout-draft-footprints/specs/kicad-tooling/spec.md`: requirement text and two new scenarios (exposed pad; no-variant pairing is noted). `openspec validate fix-layout-draft-footprints` passes.
- `build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/agent-core/spec.md`: repair-budget requirement text, one new scenario (a turn that finishes verified is not rolled back).

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1120 pass, 3 fail (pre-existing, see below), 21 skip |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | skip (not run) |
| Markdown | `npm run lint:md` | pass |

New tests: exposed pad by property, exposed pad by name, variant-in-library refusal, no-variant warning ([draft-ir-bom.test.ts](test/draft-ir-bom.test.ts)); `searchPassBudget` and the clean large-sheet skip ([draft-analog.test.ts](test/draft-analog.test.ts)); routing-progress credit, two cases, with the real report shape ([repair-cycles.test.ts](test/repair-cycles.test.ts)); CRLF marker ([tool-protocol.test.ts](test/tool-protocol.test.ts)); resume onto an unverified populated board ([create-layout-draft.test.ts](test/create-layout-draft.test.ts)).

**CI flake found and fixed here.** The first three CI runs of this branch failed two layout-draft tests with `lib_footprint_issues`. Cause: [tmp-sweep.test.ts](test/tmp-sweep.test.ts) called `sweepStaleTempDirs` with the real clock and a 60 s cutoff over the shared OS temp dir, deleting every other worker's fresh `copperhead-*` dir, including [create-layout-draft.test.ts](test/create-layout-draft.test.ts)'s seeded KiCad config (`copperhead-kicadcfg-…`), so later DRCs in that file lost the global fp-lib-table. Main hit it rarely (#342's branch once, a021e4c); this branch's longer file hit it every run. `sweepStaleTempDirs` now takes a `root` (default: the OS temp dir) and the test sweeps a private one.

Pre-existing failures on this machine, identical on the v0.11.0 tag and unrelated: `init-check`, `gating-sync`, `stage-completion` (KiCad emits `lib_symbol_issues` warnings for the fixture's vendored libraries under this machine's library table).

Not covered: a loop-level test for the finish guard on the repair budget (no scripted-provider harness drives that path today).

### Manual test log (required)

pulls.title: spec(create): propose add-llm-routing-stage, a model-routed stage before outputs (#328)
pulls.body:
## What

An OpenSpec proposal for a `routing` stage between `layout-draft` and `outputs`, routed by the model: track and via writing tools, board reading tools, a fully-routed completion contract, and the same board keeping layout-draft has. Planning artifacts only, no code.

Addresses #328.

## Why

No stage finishes routing. Stage 5 delivers ratsnest by contract (SPEC §2.5, AC-15.38/39) and stage 6 correctly refuses to fabricate it, so every `create` run stops for a human at outputs. The engine track (RFC 11 routers, RFC 14 placer) is parked for now, so the model routes; the stage contract is the one an engine fills later.

## Design

See [design.md](openspec/changes/add-llm-routing-stage/design.md). The load-bearing choices:

- A separate stage, so a routing failure never rolls back a committed placement (D1).

pulls.title: fix(create): accept a numbered Draft quality heading, retry from the committed board (#327)
pulls.body:
## What

The layout-draft gate and the fab documentation gate accept a numbered `## 4. Draft quality` heading, and a layout-draft retry starts from the board an earlier attempt committed (when it still matches the schematic) instead of re-populating from the pre-stage board.

Fixes #327.

## Why

A 38-minute stage 5 run finished ERC and DRC clean at the brief's size with a filled `## 4. Draft quality` section, numbered like its siblings. The gate matched the literal `## Draft quality`, reported the section missing, and the retry re-populated the board from the pre-stage state, so a committed placement with power routed would have been redone from scratch for a heading format. `docHasHeading` already accepts numbering for the other stages; this gate and `draftQualitySection` in `fab.ts` did not.

## Design

- [fab.ts](src/kicad/fab.ts): one matcher, `isDraftQualityHeading`, accepts `## Draft quality` with an optional `4.` or `4)` prefix and trailing whitespace, at heading level 2 only, and `draftQualitySection` uses it. `### Draft quality` and `## Draft quality notes` still do not match.
- [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts): the stage's `isComplete` now reuses `layoutDocGap`, which reads the document with the same matcher, so the gate, the contract message and the finish-time stage gate agree.

Populate is idempotent on a populated board, so the committed layout is re-checked, not rewritten.

pulls.title: fix(draft): refuse footprint pads no symbol pin covers, run the pad checks at stage completion (#325)
pulls.body:
## What

Schematic IR validation now refuses a footprint whose electrical pads are not all pins of its symbol, the same way it already refuses a symbol pin with no pad, and the schematic stage's completion check runs both checks, so a mismatched sheet goes back to stage 4 instead of populating a board with floating pads.

Fixes #325.

## Why

A 6-pin power-only USB-C symbol paired with a 16-contact receptacle footprint passed every gate. On the populated board ten pads had no net, including the second VBUS and GND pairs the design doc says are paralleled, and the floating pads sat 0.15 mm from CC1, so DRC reported violations no placement could fix. The existing pin-without-pad check (#314) only covered the other direction, and the stage completion re-drafted without a resolver, so even that check was skipped on resume.

## Design

- [footprints.ts](src/kicad/footprints.ts): `isMechanicalPad` names the pads that are unconnected by design (unnumbered, MP, SH, S1, EP, NC); `PadMismatch` gains `unpinned`, and `formatPadMismatch` reports either or both directions.
- [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts): with a resolver, `validateIntent` computes the pads no symbol pin names next to the pins no pad covers, and the finding says to use a footprint whose electrical pads are all symbol pins (KiCad ships the 6-pad USB-C variants), changing BOM.md and the intent together.
- [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts): the schematic stage's `isComplete` passes a `FootprintResolver` to its dry re-draft, as the `draft_schematic` tool already does. A footprint that does not resolve is skipped by the check, as before, so a machine without the libraries is not blocked by this.
- Populate is unchanged: its netlist carries connected pins only, not the symbol's pin list, so the reverse check there would flag deliberately unconnected pins; the schematic stage is where the symbol is known.

Invariants: no change to the tool gate, verification, `check`, the sexp reader, the ledger, or secrets.

pulls.title: feat(draft): feedback routing, a placement search and tight latched group boxes
pulls.body:
## What

The drafting engine now draws analog circuits the way a person would:
- op-amp feedback is drawn as a loop around the amplifier;
- gain and hysteresis parts sit across the amplifier;
- transistors hold their base parts;
- a placement search mirrors connectors and turns two-lead parts to remove crossings, label overlaps and extra wire.

Group boxes are drawn tight on a sheet grid, latch on to neighbours within eight units, and are dashed and coloured per group. Group captions are measured to their actual ink and wrap onto two lines before a box widens.

## Why

Drafting analog boards (op-amp buffers, a Sallen-Key filter, comparators with hysteresis, an instrumentation amplifier, a long-tailed pair) produced crossings and labels a drafter would not draw. Two of those boards were refused outright, because stacked parts' stubs touched and merged nets. Captions could also run past their group box (#307).

This branch builds on #317: it starts from #317's commit (`5cbf6ef`, the caption-advance fix) and carries the follow-up work from that review. It can land after #317 or replace it.

## Design

- **Caption ink** ([strokefont.ts](src/kicad/strokefont.ts), new): KiCad stroke-font advance and ink tables. The checker and the engine measure captions with the same function, so drafts contain their captions by construction. `wrapTwoLines` wraps a long caption before its box widens.
- **Boxes**: drawn round everything a group holds (bodies, pins, fields, power symbols, labels, wires), two units of padding, edges on the grid.
  - Wrapped rows form a true grid only when every column is within eight units of its width; otherwise each row packs its own boxes.
  - Edges latch on to a neighbour's within eight units.
  - Neighbouring boxes always stand four units apart: a row that would run past the frame is re-tiled (re-wrapped or on a larger sheet), never squeezed.
- **Feedback**: an output tied to its own inverting input is routed first, as a loop around the amplifier. A part between an input and that unit's output is bridged over or under the amplifier.
- **Routing**: each route is judged against the stubs of nets drafted later, and the shape crossing the fewest wires wins. A label is never anchored on another net's wire.
- **Placement search** (`draftSchematicPlacement`):
  - It tries connector mirrors and two-lead turns on unsettled parts, then labels the nets that still cross.
  - It ranks trials by label overlaps (including labels over part bodies, measured as the checker measures them), then crossings, then wire plus 25.4 mm per label and 2.54 mm per bend.
  - Connectors are never turned, and a crystal's signal nets are left to the flanking idiom.
  - It spends at most 60 draft passes, in intent order, so it stays deterministic.
- **Invariants**: none of this touches the agent loop, tools, `check`, or the sexp parser. The engine still emits a freshly drafted sheet, byte-deterministic for a given intent.

## Spec / OpenSpec

SPEC.md AC-16.61 is rewritten (tight latched boxes, grid only when columns are near, four-unit gutters never squeezed). AC-16.65 to AC-16.72 are added: group colours, feedback loops, bridges, transistor anchors, stacked stubs, the placement search, fewest-crossing routes and flag stacking.

AC-16 is maintained directly in SPEC.md, as before (for example `ddb52f1`); no active change covers drafting. `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` passes.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 1013 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on provider env vars | not run (no provider configured) |

New tests:
- [draft-analog.test.ts](test/draft-analog.test.ts), with a two-unit op-amp fixture and a two-pin connector fixture. It covers the follower loop, bridges for `+`/`-` and `IN+`/`IN-` pin names, connectors never turned, crystal flanking, group colours and text escaping. The `IN-`/`IN+` bridge test and the connector test fail on the branch's earlier head and pass now.
- [draft-layout.test.ts](test/draft-layout.test.ts) splits the grid test into its two cases.

The reference boards and the Tier C golden are re-pinned. Every board has 0 legibility errors and 0 ERC violations. Across the four boards, crossings go from 3 to 1 and bends from 58 to 35. The Tier C score moves from 85.25 on `main` to 85.49.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox: the reference boards under `manual-tests/reference-boards/`, drafted with the CLI from a copy with `reference/` removed.
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ npx tsx src/cli.ts --repo <copy of npn-switch> draft schematic
  sheet fit: A5, ink 29% of the usable frame, compaction not-needed
  note: placement search: J2 mirrored left for right, R1 turned 90°; ...
  (output byte-identical to manual-tests/reference-boards/npn-switch/reference/)
$ bash scripts/draft-reference-boards.sh --update

$ npx tsx scripts/draft-real-designs.ts <board>   # KiCad demos under 100 parts

  sonde xilinx: refused, one merged net (see Known issues)
```

The NPN note above was taken before the last commit. That run reported "J2 mirrored top to bottom, J2 mirrored left for right" because a replaced orientation kept its note; the last commit fixes that.

### Real designs, redrawn

The six KiCad demo boards under 100 parts are redrawn in `manual-tests/real-designs/examples/`. Every one joins exactly the pins of its source. Against the drawings on `main`:
- **Better:** fewer labels on every board, and a smaller sheet on four of them (interf_u grows from A3 to A2).
- **Worse:** crossings rise on interf_u (1 → 2), pic_programmer (3 → 5) and royalblue54L_feather (1 → 6), and wire grows on the larger boards.

## Known issues

- **sonde xilinx** is still refused on one merged net. U1C's and U1D's facing stubs meet, because a unit's pins reach past its column cell. `main`'s engine refuses it the same way, and its committed drawing predates both. Fixing it changes column spacing on every board, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **Overlaps the checker does not see** remain on some real designs:
  - power symbols on supply pins inside a body (cm5_minima's U602);
  - PWR_FLAG drawn on its power arrow;
  - labels running along another part's pin lead.

  The checker has no rule for power symbols or pin leads yet.
- **Speed:** the placement search costs one draft pass per trial. It is capped at 60 passes; cm5_minima (95 nets) drafts in about 210 s.

## Docs

[schematic-drafting.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-drafting.md) and [schematic-legibility.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-legibility.md) describe the new passes, the box rules and colours, and how labels and captions are measured.

pulls.title: Propose add-hierarchical-drafting: one sub-sheet per group, hierarchical pins
pulls.body:
## Summary

This is an OpenSpec proposal only, with no code yet. It adds hierarchical schematic output to the deterministic drafter.

Today every design is drawn on one flat sheet: groups are boxes, and all connections between groups are global labels. That works at A4. At A1 it becomes unreadable: the cm5_minima redraw puts 84 parts, 499 wires and 190 labels on one sheet. Real projects of that size are drawn hierarchically.

## What the proposal specifies

- **Mode:** a new `hints.sheets` value of `flat`, `hierarchical` or `auto` (the default). `auto` splits the design when it has two or more groups and the flat draft needs paper larger than A3. Every current golden and reference board is A4 or A5, so none of them change.
- **Sub-sheets:** one per group, drawn by the existing engine.
  - Signal nets that leave the sheet use `hierarchical_label`s.
  - Nets that stay on the sheet use local labels.
  - Power and ground stay on power symbols.
  - Each sub-sheet keeps its captioned group box, so the existing legibility rules still hold.
- **Root sheet:** holds only sheet symbols. Each pin sits on the side facing its partner sheet. Two-sheet nets whose pins face each other across a channel get a wire, and everything else gets a stub with a local label.
- **Guarantees:**
  - A `kicad-cli` netlist export from the root matches the intent, with 0 pin groups lost and 0 gained.
  - ERC reports no hierarchical-label or sheet-pin mismatches.
  - Output is byte-identical across runs.
- **Drafting paths:** the report lists every sheet. Stale drafted sub-sheets are cleaned up, but only files the drafter wrote. The edit guard covers sub-sheets. The create staleness probe compares every file.
- **Out of scope:** buses, nested hierarchy, and reusing one sub-sheet file for several instances.

## Files

- `openspec/changes/add-hierarchical-drafting/`: proposal, design (decisions H1 to H7), the `schematic-hierarchy` delta spec, and tasks.
- `openspec/specs/SPEC.md`: adds AC-16.65 to AC-16.71, one for each spec scenario.

`openspec validate add-hierarchical-drafting` passes.

pulls.title: fix(create): name the layout document path and gate finish on it (#310)
pulls.body:
## What

The layout-draft stage now tells the agent the exact path of the layout document its gate reads (`docs/LAYOUT.md` by default, from the configured `docs`), the failure message names that path and says when the section was written to a root `LAYOUT.md` instead, and `finish` checks the layout stage's own contract before answering "all gates satisfied".

Fixes #310. Stacked on #319 (the stage-5 prompt it edits is #319's), so the base is `fix/layout-draft-footprint-import`.

## Why

The gate reads `<docs>/LAYOUT.md`, but the prompt and the failure text both said only "LAYOUT.md". An agent that wrote the file at the repo root was told the section was missing while it could read it there, and `finish` had already told it "all gates satisfied; run will commit", because `finish` never looked at the stage contract. In a recent `create` run this failed layout-draft on 3 of 3 stage attempts: the agent kept editing its root file, the gate kept rejecting it, and the first attempt's DRC-clean draft (power routed) was discarded by the retry.

## Design

- [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts): `Stage.prompt(brief, docs)` receives the configured docs dir (existing one-argument prompts are unaffected). The stage-5 prompt names `path.posix.join(docs, 'LAYOUT.md')` and says a `LAYOUT.md` anywhere else, including the repository root, is not read. POSIX joins keep the text identical on Windows.
- New `layoutDocGap(root, docs)` produces the document half of the contract message: it names the path, and when a root `LAYOUT.md` carries the section it says so and where it belongs. `docs` values `docs/`, `./docs`, `.` and `''` resolve correctly (for `.` the root file is the document).
- [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts) `RunOptions.stageGate` / [context.ts](src/agent/context.ts) `ctx.stageGate`: an optional completion check the caller supplies. [handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts) `finish` runs it only after the existing gates pass and never for `refuse`; a gate that throws counts as unmet. `runCreate` supplies it for layout-draft only, using the same `config.docs` as the post-run check, so the agent hears what is missing while its board still exists instead of after the rollback. Other stages keep ending at the post-run check: their gaps have no specific message yet, and a generic one would only spend turns. `do`, repl, MCP and skills pass no gate and are unaffected.
- The stage-5 prompt also says plainly that everything on the board other than a part's position is an anchored `edit_file` (tracks, vias, zones, the outline, and a label's own `(at …)` inside its Reference or Value property). The recovery diagnosis reads this prompt as the stage goal, and without the sentence it blamed `edit_file` itself for a silkscreen fix (see #331). This is the only line here that is not about the path; it can move to its own PR if preferred.

pulls.title: fix(agent): count only failed repairs against maxRepairCycles (#331)
pulls.body:
## What

The repair budget (`maxRepairCycles`) now counts only fixes that did not work. A check that fails for the first time, a re-run with no edit, and a check that makes progress no longer spend it, so an agent that checks its work often is no longer rolled back for looking.

Fixes #331.

## Why

`run_erc` and `run_drc` added a repair cycle on every failing result and never reset the count, so the limit capped how many times the agent could look, not how many repairs failed. The layout-draft prompt asks for a DRC after every batch of moves, and a board mid-placement is expected to fail, so placement alone used the budget. In the run reported in #331, a stage with clean copper and only silkscreen text left was rolled back at "repair cycles exhausted (5)" after 1 h 15 min. SPEC §4 step 5 already defines the budget as "fix and re-run"; the code had drifted from it.

## Design

[handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts) `countRepairCycle(ctx, kind, report)`, called by `run_erc` and `run_drc` before they store the report:

- Nothing is counted when the check passes, has no failing check of the same kind before it, or follows no edit since that check (`lastErc`/`lastDrc` are nulled by `markTouched` on every edit, so a non-null value means a plain re-run).
- Findings are split into electrical and cosmetic. Cosmetic means silkscreen (`silk_*`, fixed only by moving text) and `unconnected_items` (ratsnest, which shrinks as routing progresses and could hide a new short). A check costs a cycle when its electrical findings did not go down, or, once only cosmetic findings are left, when its total did not go down. So fewer silkscreen or ratsnest findings cannot hide a new clearance violation, and a stuck silkscreen-only loop still ends in rollback instead of running out the turn budget.
- The previous report lives in the new optional `ctx.priorChecks`, because `lastErc`/`lastDrc` are cleared on every edit.
- `finish` is unchanged: it still requires ERC after a schematic edit and DRC after a board edit to pass. Only the budget changes.

Behaviour notes: rollback fires on the `maxRepairCycles`-th failed repair, as SPEC §4 step 5 says (`repairBudgetExhausted` in [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts); the old check was `>`, which with the first failure no longer counted would have allowed one extra); `maxRepairCycles: 0` allows no failed repair. A failure that never changes therefore exhausts the budget at the same point as before.

Review follow-up (Codex, P2): the exhaustion check moved from `>` to `>=` on the counted failures, with a unit test for the boundary and the limit-0 case.

**Merging with #319:** a trial merge conflicts in three places in [handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts), all mechanical: the `../kicad/cli.js` import (take #319's line, which adds `unroutedCount`), the helper block before `HandlerOutcome` (keep both #319's `unroutedGuard` and this PR's helpers), and the `run_drc` lines. For `run_drc`, keep #319's guarded report and count it after the guard, so an unrouted increase counts as an electrical finding:

```ts
const report = await unroutedGuard(ctx, boardPath, await runDrc(boardPath));
countRepairCycle(ctx, 'drc', report);
ctx.lastDrc = report;
```

On #319, unrouted connections are reported as `report.unrouted`, not as violations, so there the cosmetic set is effectively silkscreen only.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) §4 step 5 defines a repair cycle as above.
- Change `build-copperhead-phase-1`, delta spec [agent-core/spec.md](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/agent-core/spec.md): the "Turn and repair budgets" requirement carries the same definition, plus a new scenario "Routine checks do not spend the repair budget (#331)". AC-3.5 and AC-3.6 hold as written. `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` passes.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npx tsc --noEmit` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npx vitest run` | pass: 993 passed, 3 failed (pre-existing, below), 21 skipped of 1017; no change vs `main` |
| Markdown | `npx markdownlint-cli2` on the four touched docs | pass |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on provider env vars | not run |

New: [repair-cycles.test.ts](test/repair-cycles.test.ts), 10 cases driven the way the handlers call it (edit, then check): the live sequence from #331 with its real violation types, an unchanged failure still exhausting, a stuck silkscreen loop exhausting, silkscreen progress free, fewer silkscreen findings not hiding more electrical ones, fewer unconnected items not hiding a new short, first failure after clean free, re-run without an edit free, ERC and DRC kept separate.

pulls.title: fix(agent): cut replies that invent their own tool results (#320)
pulls.body:
## What

On the text-protocol providers (`claude-code`, `cursor`), a reply that goes on past its tool calls and writes its own `[result of …]` or `[user]` blocks is now cut at the first such line. Only the calls before the cut run; the invented results, and any calls planned against them, are discarded, the model is told so, and the transcript keeps the cut text as evidence.

Fixes #320.

## Why

The model imitates the transcript format that `renderConversation` feeds it and invents results for tools it has not run yet, then plans further calls against those inventions. Today every call in the reply is dispatched and the invented text is stored as assistant content and replayed, so the model cannot tell its own fabrications from real results. In a layout stage this produced false verification claims: the model wrote "ERC clean, DRC clean" after an invented clean DRC while the real board had 18 violations (details in #320).

## Design

- [tool-protocol.ts](src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts): `parseToolCalls` finds the first line-anchored `[result of <tool>]` or `[user]` marker (the two lines only copperhead writes), keeps everything before it, and returns a `notice` (sent to the model) and `discarded` (the cut text, for the transcript only). Echoed `[assistant]` / `[assistant tool call]` lines are stripped from stored prose. Extraction moved into `extractCalls` so the parser can count the calls it dropped.
- A marker inside a JSON string cannot trigger the cut (JSON escapes the newline), and a mid-line mention does not either. CRLF works (a multiline `$` matches before `\r`).
- [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts): after the real tool results, the notice is pushed as a user message, so the model reads the real results first. A turn with no surviving call gets the notice as its nudge (the existing no-tool path), so it is never sent twice. A `fabricated-results` transcript event records the notice and the discarded text.
- On a resumed CLI session (`COPPERHEAD_CC_SESSION_RESUME=1` with the LLM cache off) the provider keeps the raw reply, so the notice is also the only correction the model's own history gets; `renderDelta` sends it after the tool results.
- `codex` uses structured output and is unaffected; `openai`/`anthropic` use native tool calls.

Known limits, left as they are on purpose:
- A result quoted on the same line as the marker (`[result of run_drc]: clean`) is not cut; requiring the marker alone on its line keeps ordinary prose that starts with a bracketed mention safe.
- A model that deliberately re-quotes a real earlier result on its own line loses the calls after it and is told to wait for results; it recovers on the next turn.
- The skill runner (`src/agent/tools.ts`) and the recovery diagnosis (`src/agent/recovery.ts`) also parse replies; they get the cut but not the notice.
- Response-cache entries recorded before this change replay as recorded.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npx tsc --noEmit` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npx vitest run` | pass: 992 passed, 3 failed (pre-existing, below), 21 skipped of 1016; no change vs `main` |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on provider env vars | not run |

New: [tool-protocol.test.ts](test/tool-protocol.test.ts) (7 cases: cut and counts, `[user]`, cut before any call, normal multi-call reply untouched, marker in a JSON string, mid-line mention, echoed markers stripped) and a loop test in [observability.test.ts](test/observability.test.ts) (notice sent after the real result, transcript event carries notice and discarded text).

Pre-existing failures, identical on `main` at c9045af and unrelated: `gating-sync` "finish blocks on open obligations and unverified ERC", `init-check` "clean fixture: everything green", `stage-completion` "error-severity findings keep the stage active". Suites were run with `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=500` because the machine has about 2 GiB free.

pulls.title: Repair create gating and add a live smoke harness (WIP #66)
pulls.body:
## What

This draft fixes three create-pipeline failures found while working on #66: failed resume commits being treated as completed stages, unsupported OpenSpec initialization, and a spec-validation deadlock. It also fixes false symbol-search misses, pins the public test fixture's resistor library, and adds an explicit live E2E smoke command.

**The eight-stage bounty acceptance is not complete.** The second real run committed three of eight stages, then exited 1 after refusing schematic capture because component and power-state evidence was unresolved. I will keep this PR in draft until the complete live run is verified.

## Why

A rejected Git commit must not advance the pipeline. OpenSpec 1.13.2 rejects `init --no-interactive`, and its validator requires capability deltas that the locked proposal tool previously could not create.

The [findings report](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/manual-tests/findings/issue-66/README.md), [medium-complexity RP2040 brief](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/manual-tests/findings/issue-66/rp2040-sensor-interface.md) and logs for [attempt 01](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/manual-tests/findings/issue-66/attempt-01.log) and [attempt 02](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/manual-tests/findings/issue-66/attempt-02.log) are included. Local workspace prefixes are sanitized. The [second run summary](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/manual-tests/findings/issue-66/attempt-02.json) records the three actual stage commits and failed schematic stage. Related to #66; this draft does not claim the bounty is earned or that additional-entrant eligibility has been confirmed.

## Design

- Resume commits return success/failure. A failed commit or unrelated dirty work stops create before the stage is recorded as complete, retaining the existing files.
- Initialize with `openspec init --tools none`. On failure, preserve the diagnostic and return before invoking a model or marking the create origin.
- `propose_change` accepts named `spec_deltas`, limited to `openspec/changes/<id>/specs/<capability>/spec.md`. Validate IDs and targets before writing; reject unsafe names, duplicate capabilities and linked targets. Re-proposing or re-validating revokes previous editing authorization. Only successful validation and, in interactive mode, approval unlock edits.
- The fixture-local resistor is the same definition already embedded in its schematic. No production ERC policy, circuit geometry or connectivity was changed.

- Symbol search accepts exact one-letter names and full `Lib:Name` queries while retaining cross-library discovery. In the real run, `R`/`C` searches incorrectly returned nothing despite successful pin resolution; the installed-library before/after probe now returns the correct devices.
- The [live smoke](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/scripts/README-create-e2e-smoke.md) creates a fresh synthetic repo, enforces a process-group deadline, correlates all eight terminal events to reachable Git commits, rejects empty designs, checks exports/DEVPLAN/firmware, and runs independent ERC/DRC with schematic parity. It is disabled unless explicitly enabled; its 24 regression tests do not invoke a model.

Existing initialized-workspace skip behavior remains unchanged. The issue permits an explicitly gated live smoke command; deterministic replay is optional. The current response cache can fall through to live calls and is not presented as safe offline replay.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Updated [SPEC.md](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/openspec/specs/SPEC.md), the active [create-pipeline delta](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md) [spec-gating delta](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/spec-gating/spec.md), and [symbol-search contract](https://github.com/QIU-Guanzong/copperhead/blob/5d219421572b77b1b311dd8234555cd795e2edf2/openspec/changes/add-symbol-search-tool/specs/agent-core/spec.md). `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` passed with OpenSpec 1.13.2. No unfinished end-to-end task is marked complete.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1047 passed, 21 skipped; includes three enabled real OpenSpec CLI tests |
| Markdown | `npm run lint:md` | pass |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | saved-login `--model codex` manual run | attempt 02 exit 1 after three committed stages; full run not passed |

Skipped tests: 19 agent-integration, one conditional Claude Code provider test and one local real-design corpus test. The package currently has `lint:md`, not a `lint` script. Provider API keys and live-test opt-ins were excluded from the automated-test environment.

The original base reproduced three ERC-related test failures under KiCad 10.0.6. The pinned fixture fixes them without suppressing the mismatch check: changing a temporary library pin number still produces two warnings and exit 5. The final full-suite result above includes that fixture repair.

pulls.title: Fix agent , filesystem , provider and create pipeline reliability
pulls.body:
## What

Harden agent completion and approval gates, filesystem containment and rollback, deterministic checks and sync, create-stage validation, provider recovery, KiCad exports, and REPL logging.

## Why

These gaps could let incomplete work be committed, mishandle existing project files, or report incomplete checks and create outputs as successful. Closes #329.

## Design

- [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts) stops tool execution after an accepted `finish`, requires the obligations ledger to be clear before commit, and preserves failed work before rollback. Proposal replacement and revalidation reset approval in [handlers.ts](src/capabilities/handlers.ts).
- [paths.ts](src/util/paths.ts) rejects symlink components below the project root. The same checks cover configuration, prompt documents, proposal and decision files, constraints, changelogs, `.gitignore`, and transcripts. A symlinked project root remains supported.
- [git.ts](src/util/git.ts) preserves staged and unstaged changes separately, literal filenames, dangling symlinks, and files ignored before the run. Staging and rollback also work when the selected project is nested in a larger Git repository.
- [check.ts](src/commands/check.ts) fails for missing configured design files. [sync.ts](src/commands/sync.ts) reports missing constraint documentation and reruns the deterministic audit after resolution.
- [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) requires DRC for resumed layouts, verifies pending KiCad changes before commit, and requires each expected nonempty output. [cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts) uses version-compatible export arguments: DXF and PCB SVG single-file mode on KiCad 9+, and STEP replacement on resume.
- Provider behavior remains inside provider adapters. Cancellation and bounded retries prevent abandoned turns and duplicate SDK retries; cache keys include full tool contracts, recognized secrets bypass persistence, and Codex preserves cached-turn context.
- The check command remains provider-free. KiCad s-expression parsing remains read-only, and edits continue to use anchored text replacement.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: `build-copperhead-phase-1`. Updated [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/design.md), and the applicable delta specs: [agent-core](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/agent-core/spec.md), [cli-surface](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/cli-surface/spec.md), [create-pipeline](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md), [safety-rails](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/safety-rails/spec.md), and [spec-gating](openspec/changes/build-copperhead-phase-1/specs/spec-gating/spec.md).

Affected acceptance criteria: AC-2.6, AC-3.8, AC-3.21 through AC-3.25, AC-4.2, AC-7.2, and AC-7.5. Create-pipeline and REPL behavior is covered by the applicable delta scenarios. The original Phase 1 proposal and task inventory remain unchanged; no unrelated tasks were marked complete. `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` passes.

Fresh focused runs passed safety and terminal-gate tests (62/62), provider/cache tests (83 passed, 1 optional skip), and export checks (8/8, including native KiCad 10.0.5). KiCad 8/9 export arguments were checked with compatibility tests; native KiCad 8/9 runs were unavailable. See [LOCAL_AUDIT.md](LOCAL_AUDIT.md) for the audit details.

pulls.title: fix(create): populate the board from the schematic before layout-draft (#314)
pulls.body:
## What

`copperhead create` now puts every schematic part on the board, with its exact library footprint and pad nets, before the layout-draft stage starts. The agent places parts; it no longer writes footprint geometry. A footprint that is not installed stops the run and tells the user how to install it.

Fixes #314.

## Why

Stage 5 could never finish on a real design. Its completion gate required `(footprint` in the `.kicad_pcb`, but no tool creates a footprint, so the agent hand-wrote surrogate pad geometry. Reported runs reached 44 to 75 DRC violations (library mismatches, shorts), rolled back, and ended with an outline-only board. Three reproductions (Windows, macOS, code reading on `main`) agree it is structural. `kicad-cli` 10 has no schematic-to-board update, so the step lives in copperhead.

## Design

**Populate before layout-draft** ([populate.ts](src/kicad/populate.ts)). Before every layout-draft attempt, `create` exports the schematic netlist (`kicad-cli sch export netlist`), resolves every part's footprint, and copies each library `.kicad_mod` onto the board by anchored splices: refdes, value, uuid, position, schematic path, and pad nets are spliced in; pad geometry is carried over byte-for-byte. A footprint's own zones (an ESP32 module's antenna keepout), which a board stores in board coordinates, move with it, and every object id inside a placed footprint is remapped per instance so no two instances share one. Parts are shelf-packed inside the outline (grown roughly square if needed). The board is written only after KiCad loads a temp copy. It is all-or-nothing, idempotent on an already-populated board, and refuses a netlist pin that has no pad (it would silently drop a net). KiCad 5 `(module …)` library files populate too; with an outline populate cannot grow (not a single rectangle), every packed part must lie inside its real shape, cutouts included, or the run stops.

**The populated board is verified and reversible.** Populate runs before the agent loop's own snapshot, so the stage keeps the pre-stage board itself:
- the populated board must pass DRC before the agent's first turn, or the run stops and names the findings (including a missing global `fp-lib-table`, which makes KiCad reject every stock footprint);
- the agent run counts the board as touched, so it cannot finish without a clean `run_drc` even if it moves nothing;
- each retry starts from the pre-stage board, re-populated;
- a stage that does not complete (stop, abort, exhausted retries, error) puts back the last verified board: the pre-stage board, or the board an attempt committed, so the tree never reverts HEAD;
- the stage completes only when the board also passes DRC.

**Exact footprint resolution** ([libtable.ts](src/kicad/libtable.ts), [footprints.ts](src/kicad/footprints.ts)). `Lib:Name` resolves the way KiCad resolves it: project `fp-lib-table`, then the user's global table (nested `Table` rows followed), then the stock install, with `${KIPRJMOD}`, `${KICADn_FOOTPRINT_DIR}`, `${KICADn_3RD_PARTY}` (where KiCad's plugin manager installs libraries), and the user's `kicad_common.json` path variables expanded, all taken from the running `kicad-cli`'s KiCad version, never a newer or older install's. There is never a fallback to a symbol default or a similar package. Symbols also resolve through the project `sym-lib-table` beside the schematic (projects in subfolders included), read in place rather than vendored, and drafting keeps rows the user added there verbatim, whatever their layout; a table it cannot parse is refused, not rewritten.

**The one stop.** A footprint that is not installed stops `create` before the schematic stage, before any KiCad file is scaffolded (and again at populate), naming each part, the reason, the closest installed ids, and the `fp-lib-table` row to add. Re-running resumes. copperhead never downloads parts.

**Part selection verifies footprints.** A live run showed the model inventing footprint names at stage 3, so there is a new read-only `check_footprints` tool, and part selection completes only when every BOM footprint resolves. An invented id goes back to the model with suggestions; only a library installed nowhere reaches the stop. IR validation requires each part's BOM footprint, and (from the draft tool) symbol pins that exist as pads.

**Layout-draft**
- Completion compares the board's (refdes, footprint id) pairs and every pad's net with the schematic netlist exactly.
- New spec-gated `move_footprint` tool. A live run showed that rotating a part by editing its `(at X Y ROT)` leaves the pads facing the old way, because KiCad stores pad and text angles as absolute. That produced 29 pad-to-pad shorts inside J1 and `lib_footprint_mismatch` on 5 parts. The tool rotates pads and text with the footprint.
- The prompt changed from "write geometry" to "move the populated parts".

**DRC semantics** ([report.ts](src/kicad/report.ts))
- Unrouted connections are a count beside `check`'s result, not violations. A populated draft board is fully unrouted, and SPEC's first-draft layout allows ratsnest. An agent run's `run_drc` does fail (`unrouted_increase`) when the board has more unrouted connections than it started the run with, since that means a track or connection was broken (skipped when the run's starting board does not load).
- A finding whose every item belongs to one footprint (a stock USB-C footprint's pad 0.18 mm from its own peg hole) is reported as library-intrinsic, not failed. That includes clearances between a footprint's own pads on different nets (a stock USB-C receptacle's DP/DM pads sit closer than the board rule). The exception never applies to a short between two nets (`shorting_items`), or to a footprint KiCad reports as modified (`lib_footprint_mismatch`) or cannot find in its libraries (`lib_footprint_issues`).
- Clearance, shorts, and courtyards still fail.

**Scaffold** allows 0.2 mm holes (stock QFN thermal vias fail KiCad's 0.3 mm default, and layout may not edit footprints), and its `.kicad_dru` holds board vias to a 0.3 mm drill.

**Review follow-up.** ee63566 addresses the Codex findings (rollback before the snapshot, multi-line `sym-lib-table` rows, the project symbol table's folder), the CI failures (stale `R_0603` fixtures, `check`'s new DRC keys), and the automated pr-review pass (the points above, plus locale-independent net numbering and DRC tests run against a seeded KiCad config instead of the machine's). d4bdbd7 addresses the follow-up review: ESP32 modules failed `lib_footprint_mismatch` because footprint zones were not moved, stock USB-C receptacles failed on their own pad clearances, plus the multi-version KiCad lookup, the committed-attempt restore, non-rectangular outlines, and the smaller items. Rendered before/after boards were checked by eye and with KiCad DRC. f15870b addresses the Codex review of d4bdbd7: project symbol libraries were replaced by a partial vendored cache after first use, nested footprint ids were shared between instances, and the missing-footprint stop ran after the scaffold was written.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- OpenSpec change `fix-layout-draft-footprints`: proposal, design, tasks, delta specs for `create-pipeline` and `kicad-tooling`. `openspec validate fix-layout-draft-footprints` passes.
- SPEC.md: pipeline diagram (footprint check, board populate), "the one stop" exception to run-to-completion, the populate bullet under first-draft layout, and **AC-15.29 to AC-15.44**. AC-15.23/24's layout-draft clause is superseded by AC-15.38.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 1046 pass, 0 fail, 21 skip, with a KiCad config seeded like CI's; on a machine with mismatched symbol libraries, 3 environment-specific failures (below) |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate fix-layout-draft-footprints` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | not run as automated tests; see the manual log |

New tests: [board-populate.test.ts](test/board-populate.test.ts) (lib tables and path variables, exact resolution, stop message, populate against real `kicad-cli` with DRC and schematic parity, idempotence and determinism, pin/pad refusal, stale pad nets, legacy `(module …)` files, non-rectangular outlines, the via rule, stage gates, `sym-lib-table` row preservation and subfolder projects, `check_footprints`, `move_footprint` rotation vs a hand rotation, the unrouted guard), [create-layout-draft.test.ts](test/create-layout-draft.test.ts) (the pipeline around populate: board restored after a failed stage, a committed attempt's board kept, populated board counted as touched, DRC stop before any agent turn, retry re-populates), [pre-touched.test.ts](test/pre-touched.test.ts) (the loop refuses `finish` until DRC passes on a pre-touched board), ESP32 zone placement and rotation, L-shaped and cut-out outlines, and KiCad version selection in [board-populate.test.ts](test/board-populate.test.ts), [create-footprints.test.ts](test/create-footprints.test.ts) (stop before the schematic stage, resume after install), additions to [draft-ir-bom.test.ts](test/draft-ir-bom.test.ts) and [report.test.ts](test/report.test.ts) (shorts and cross-net clearances inside one footprint, unvouched footprints). Each regression test was checked to fail with its fix reverted. The populate tests run real `kicad-cli`, as the ERC/DRC tests do; CI installs KiCad 10 with stock footprints.

Environment-specific failures, identical on `main` without this branch and absent on CI: `gating-sync` and `init-check` (ERC `lib_symbol_mismatch`: the fixture's embedded `Device:R` no longer matches a locally installed symbol library) and the `stage-completion` legibility gate. The `create` tests call the real disk-space preflight (2.0 GiB default); on a machine near that boundary, run them with `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=500`.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `create`, via `copperhead demo` (USB-C power breakout), plus a populate sweep over the repo corpus.
- Populate on corpus designs, each checked with `kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity`:

```text
ldo-demo            6 parts   DRC 0  parity 0
buck-12v-5v        24 parts   DRC 0  parity 0  (after the 0.2 mm hole rule)
usb-atmega-node    23 parts   DRC 0  parity 0
complex_hierarchy  68 parts   DRC 0  parity 0  (KiCad demo, multi-sheet; re-run after ee63566: DRC 0, pad nets match, second populate writes nothing)
npn-switch         refused: Q1 pins B, C, E have no pad in SOT-23 (pads 1, 2, 3)
royalblue54L_feather, 8 more real designs: stopped, naming footprints from libraries not installed
```

- Live run, Claude via the Claude Code provider:

```text
$ node dist/cli.js demo --model claude-code --dir demo-runs/usb-c-314
spec-seed, architecture: complete
part-selection: invented 3 footprint ids -> added check_footprints + gate; on resume the model
  checked and fixed all three (Fuse_2920_7451Metric, HCTL 16P USB-C, Phoenix PT 3.5 mm)
footprint check: pass
schematic: complete
layout-draft: placed 9 footprint(s) from the schematic (12 nets, unrouted; outline grown to 30 x 27 mm)
  populated board: DRC 0 (plus 1 library-intrinsic finding inside J1), parity 0
  first agent attempt rotated parts by hand-editing (at ...) -> move_footprint added
```

Not done: the live run has not yet finished layout-draft and the later stages. It stopped when the host disk dropped below copperhead's 2.0 GiB preflight. The gpt-6-astra run (Codex) stopped at part selection by its own refusal: it wrote strict short-circuit and 6 V survival requirements that no installed protection part could be shown to meet. That is unrelated to this change.

## Docs

SPEC.md and the OpenSpec change as above. No README or configuration changes; `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB` already exists.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: `move_footprint` is gated exactly like `edit_file` (`requiresUnlock`, gate on `editsUnlocked`; tested). `check_footprints` is read-only and ungated. `edit_file`/`write_file` are unchanged.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: DRC still gates board changes, including the populated board: it must pass DRC before the first agent turn, the agent run treats it as touched, and an incomplete stage restores the pre-stage board (AC-15.43). Changed on purpose and specified (AC-15.39, AC-15.41): unrouted connections are counted beside `check`'s result (an agent run still fails if it raises the count), and findings inside a single library footprint KiCad vouches for, with no two nets meeting, are reported instead of failing. Every other finding still fails.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: `check` only gains the unrouted and intrinsic counts in its output.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: the parser stays read-only; populate and `move_footprint` write by anchored splices of source text, and the board is load-probed by KiCad before it is written.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: `move_footprint` goes through `markTouched`, like `edit_file`, so DRC must re-run after a move; the populated board enters the ledger the same way through the loop's `preTouched`.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A, no change to transcripts, keys, or `.gitignore`.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md, proposal, design, delta specs, and tasks moved together; `openspec validate fix-layout-draft-footprints` passes.

pulls.title: fix(kicad): keep all ranked symbol matches visible
pulls.body:
## what

keep the full ranked symbol candidate set from each installed kiCad library until global ranking is complete. this prevents valid manufacturer-qualified symbols from disappearing because one library was scanned earlier.

## why

`search_symbols` accepted a global result cap but hard-coded a per-library cap of four. on a library with more than four valid matches, later candidates were silently hidden before global ranking. this can make the agent report a real installed symbol as unavailable, especially for part-numbered connectors and other qualified symbols.

relates to [issue #257](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/issues/257), finding 10.

## design

use the existing caller-provided `cap` when ranking each library. the final global sort and result cap are unchanged, so result ordering stays deterministic while no library loses candidates prematurely.

pulls.title: fix(legibility): accurately measure group caption advance and check caption overflow (fixes #307)
pulls.body:
## What

Fixes group captions overflowing group rectangles undetected by using an accurate stroke-font advance for group captions (`CAPTION_ADVANCE = 0.78`) and adding a containment check for captions against their group rectangles.

## Why

Closes #307. KiCad's stroke font advances at ~0.76 to 0.78 of glyph height for uppercase text, while the general label `TEXT_ADVANCE` was set to 0.60 to avoid false positive collisions near bodies (design C3). This caused long subsystem group captions to spill outside their group rectangles into neighboring boxes without triggering findings.

## Design

- Introduced `CAPTION_ADVANCE = 0.78` specifically for group caption text items, preserving `TEXT_ADVANCE = 0.6` for wire labels and design C3 constraints.
- Extended `unlabeled-group` checks to flag when a caption's text box extends past its group rectangle right boundary by more than `TOL`.
- Added unit test covering caption overflow detection.

pulls.body:
## What

Adds a deterministic end-to-end replay harness for `copperhead create` ([create-e2e-replay.test.ts](test/create-e2e-replay.test.ts) plus [fixtures](test/fixtures/create-e2e)), and lands the P0/P1 fixes a real `create` run surfaced: the openspec spec-delta deadlock ([cli.ts](src/openspec/cli.ts), [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts)) and the BOM dossier passive-row drop ([dossier.ts](src/kicad/dossier.ts)). Full defect list in [FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md).

## Why

Closes #66, which asked for e2e coverage of the create pipeline. The live run also proved the pipeline could not finish a real brief end to end:

- P0: openspec 1.13.x rejects `init --no-interactive`, so initialized workspaces never got spec deltas; `validate_change` then demanded deltas that `propose_change` could not author, deadlocking the run.
- P1: `bomSymbolDossier` silently dropped R/C/L passives and never listed installed symbol libraries, so the stage-4 model pattern-copied Footprint values into `lib_ids` and refused with a false "libraries are missing".

## Design

Fixes stay inside the existing stage machinery rather than adding wrappers: `init` falls back to the interactive-compatible path when `--no-interactive` is rejected, `propose_change` accepts a `spec_deltas` argument so `validate_change` has a real artifact to check, and the dossier now names skipped refdes and discloses Device:R/C/L instead of dropping them. Test steering in [recovery.ts](src/agent/recovery.ts) and [filetools.ts](src/agent/filetools.ts) routes minified-JSON anchor misses and engine-drafted edits back to `draft_schematic`, which is where several observed stalls came from.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change: these are bug fixes to existing stages, so SPEC.md and the OpenSpec change set do not move.

## Testing

Real results on this branch (Ubuntu, Node 20). Every failing test reports `kicad-cli not found on PATH`; there are no assertion failures.

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 977 pass, 29 fail (all: `kicad-cli not found on PATH`), 25 skipped |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on provider env var | n/a: no provider key in this environment |

### Invariants

- [ ] Agent loop: tool surface unchanged; new steering lives inside existing recovery and draft-tool paths.
- [ ] Safety gates: no new filesystem or network writes outside the workspace; the replay harness is fully offline (fixture transcripts, no provider calls).
- [ ] KiCad layer: dossier output is additive only (skipped refdes and installed libraries disclosed); no change for complete symbol sets.
- [ ] Providers: no changes to request/response shape beyond what tests already cover.

pulls.body:
## What

Fixes `layout-draft` so `LAYOUT.md` is resolved from the configured `config.docs` directory. The stage prompt now receives the exact repo-relative destination, and the completion contract checks that same configured path.

## Why

The layout-draft agent was instructed to write a bare `LAYOUT.md`, which allowed it to create the file at the repository root while completion checked `docs/LAYOUT.md`. The stage then treated valid layout work as missing, causing unnecessary retries and blocking pipeline progress. Custom documentation directories were affected in the same way.

## Design

- Completion derives the document location as `path.join(config.docs, 'LAYOUT.md')` after loading the project configuration.
- `runCreate` passes that exact repo-relative path into the layout-draft prompt.
- The prompt explicitly requires the resolved path for both reads and writes and rejects root-level `LAYOUT.md`.
- No generic file-tool behavior or unrelated stage behavior was changed.

This is a filesystem and CLI contract fix, so screenshots are not applicable. The regression evidence is deterministic path output:

configured docs path: docs/
layout-draft completion: false

After:

configured docs path: docs/
layout-draft completion: true

Custom configuration:
configured docs path: hardware/docs/
root/docs/LAYOUT.md: rejected
root/hardware/docs/LAYOUT.md: accepted
prompt destination: hardware/docs/LAYOUT.md
