pulls.title: Finish linear-regulator DC operating-point checks in `check` (closes #308)
pulls.body:
## What

Adds `copperhead check --spice` for declared three-terminal linear regulators. The check runs a bounded local ngspice DC operating-point simulation and reports the measured output voltage against the declared target and tolerance in text and `--json`.

## Why

Copperhead could already verify ERC, DRC, drift, and constraints, but it could not verify whether a declared regulator output actually reached its required voltage. A regulator could pass every existing check while still producing the wrong voltage on the board. This adds a read-only, offline electrical operating-point check for the first supported circuit type, closing that gap.

## Design

- Reuses the existing schematic connectivity reader, Simulation block parser, and constraint registry — no duplicate parsing was introduced.
- Supports linear-regulator DC operating-point checks only for this first slice.
- Reports explicit failures for missing ngspice, missing or unusable models, non-convergence, timeouts, and missing measurements — none of these silently pass.
- Reports `not_checked` when a regulator has no declared voltage constraint, rather than a false pass.
- Runs ngspice only as a bounded local subprocess.
- Does not access the network, invoke a provider, modify project files, modify the Git index, or add any mutation tool.
- Transient analysis, other circuit types, arbitrary topologies, and generalized deck generation are intentionally deferred. The scope boundary is documented in `openspec/changes/add-spice-verification-gate/` and the CLI documentation.

## Testing

### Automated test status

This branch recorded 981 passed, 27 failed, 22 skipped. The failures are existing Windows newline/path assertions, pre-existing safety-behavior differences, and parallel-load timeouts across unrelated draft, gating, MCP, REPL, check, and registry tests — not new deterministic failures introduced by this change. Five full-suite reruns showed the same load-sensitive failures varying between 21 and 25 failed tests; the new `regulator-op` CLI test passed in all five reruns.

### Manual test log (required)

pulls.title: test(mcp): make the concurrent-init busy test deterministic
pulls.body:
## What

Makes `rejects a concurrent mutating call with a typed busy error` in [test/mcp-server.test.ts](test/mcp-server.test.ts) deterministic. Test-only: no production code changes.

## Why

The test fails intermittently on `main` and has turned CI red on unrelated PRs: #298 ([run](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/actions/runs/34763632865)) and `fix/296-locked-write-file-silent-drop` ([run](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/actions/runs/34583101130), green on rerun). Locally it failed in 5 of 16 runs on unmodified `main`.

## Design

**Root cause.** The test fires two `copperhead_init` calls together and expects exactly one to be refused as busy, but nothing guarantees the calls overlap. The handler awaits `requireKicad()`, a `kicad-cli` subprocess probe, before it calls `locks.tryAcquire` ([server.ts](src/mcp/server.ts)), and `init` itself is quick. When one call's probe is slow, the other call acquires the lock, writes the docs and releases it before the slow call arrives. Envelopes logged from failing runs show exactly that: `[{ ok: true, "init wrote 0 file(s)" }, { ok: true, "init wrote 8 file(s)" }]`, so the calls ran one after the other.

**The lock is sound.** `RepoLocks.tryAcquire` is a synchronous check-and-set, so two calls can never both hold it. Nothing in the server changes.

**Fix.** The test spies on `RepoLocks.prototype.release` and holds every release until both calls have answered, then applies them. Whichever call acquires first keeps the lock for as long as the other can still reach `tryAcquire`, so exactly one call is refused whatever the probe timing. The test still drives two real concurrent calls through the real server and handler. It also asserts that only the holder releases (the refused call returns before it takes the lock) and that a follow-up `copperhead_init` succeeds once the held release is applied, so a handler that never releases is caught as well. The spy is restored in a `finally`.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | **938 passed, 0 failed, 21 skipped** (66 files passed, 2 skipped) |

| Mutation | Failure |
| --- | --- |
| Lock check removed (`if (!locks.tryAcquire(...))` never refuses) | `one of two concurrent mutating calls must be refused as busy: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` |

pulls.title: fix(agent): time out turns on inactivity, not total length
pulls.body:
## What

Provider turns are no longer killed just for running past 10 minutes. `turnTimeoutMs` (still 10 minutes) now measures how long a turn goes without any progress, and a new `turnMaxMs` (default 60 minutes) caps a turn that keeps producing output. The claude-code provider now reports progress while it streams, so a long turn that keeps producing output completes. A second commit fixes the Codex provider's teardown, which left a retried turn without its conversation history. The branch also carries the two `test/mcp-server.test.ts` commits from #299 (already merged to `main`), cherry-picked here so CI stays green; they merge cleanly because the file is identical on both sides.

## Why

A turn had a fixed 10-minute deadline, and a timed-out turn was resent unchanged. A turn that legitimately needs longer (a large claude-code capture turn) was killed at 10, 20, 30 and 40 minutes, then the run failed as `provider-error` and rolled back. In `create`, the stage diagnosis saw only "provider-error" and its prompt called timeouts transient, so it retried the stage, which changed every response-cache key and hit the same wall again (worst case over two hours per stage). The heartbeat could not tell slow from hung: claude-code emitted nothing until its reply was complete.

## Design

- **Watchdog** ([recovery.ts](src/agent/recovery.ts)): `withWatchdog(fn, { idleMs, maxMs, onTimeout })` hands `fn` an `activity()` callback that restarts the idle deadline. `maxMs` is a hard cap that activity does not extend, with two rules: it only trips once `fn` has reported progress (progress that first arrives after the cap came due trips it at once), and it is never shorter than `idleMs`. `TurnTimeoutError` carries `kind: 'idle' | 'max'`. `withTimeout` is a thin wrapper over it, so its other callers behave as before. The timer rejects before running `onTimeout`, so a provider whose `close()` rejects its call synchronously still surfaces `TurnTimeoutError`.
- **Compatibility**: a turn that reports no progress (openai, anthropic, vertex, cursor, codex) never restarts the deadline and is never capped, so it gets exactly the old whole-turn `turnTimeoutMs` deadline, including "no deadline" when `turnTimeoutMs <= 0` (`turnMaxMs` then defaults to disabled). A streaming turn's cap is at least `turnTimeoutMs`. No turn that finished in time before times out now, and a hung call is still caught within `turnTimeoutMs`.
- **Agent loop and skill sub-run** ([loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts), [tools.ts](src/agent/tools.ts)): every `onStream` call counts as activity. An idle timeout aborts and retries up to `MAX_TURN_TIMEOUTS`, as before. A turn stopped at the cap fails once, without a resend, with a reason saying it is too large rather than hung. `turn-timeout` and `skill-turn-timeout` transcript events now record `kind`.
- **claude-code** ([claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts)): sets `includePartialMessages: true`. Every `stream_event` is progress, and text deltas feed the heartbeat's character count. The reply is still read from the complete `assistant` message; a live probe confirmed the SDK sends both.
- **create** ([create.ts](src/commands/create.ts)): the stage failure string now carries the run's own reason, because the diagnosis transcript excerpt holds only assistant text and tool results. The diagnosis prompt says a capped turn needs its work split into smaller edits, not a plain retry.
- **Config** ([config.ts](src/config.ts)): new `turnMaxMs`, default `3600000`, `<= 0` disables it, and it defaults to disabled when `turnTimeoutMs` is disabled. `turnTimeoutMs` keeps its `600000` default.
- **Codex** ([codex.ts](src/agent/providers/codex.ts)): `close()` dropped the thread but did not abort `thread.run` and kept `messageCursor`. The watchdog's retry therefore opened a fresh thread and sent it only the latest delta (no system prompt, request or history) while the orphaned `codex exec` kept running. It now passes an `AbortSignal` and aborts it on close, resets the cursor so the fresh thread gets the full conversation, discards any turn that began before the last `close()`, and forgets its working directory before deleting it, so a turn retried while that deletion runs gets a fresh directory.

An automated `pr-review` pass found one medium and four low findings (the cap rules, the simulation's fake clock, the Codex directory race, spec text, and two untested paths). All are addressed in the last commit; see the review comments on this PR.

Not in this PR: codex, cursor and the API providers still report no progress, so a long turn there keeps the whole-turn deadline. The OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs still retry an abandoned request in the background, because those providers have no `close()`.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) §4.5 gains a bullet for the provider turn watchdog (inactivity deadline, streaming progress, the cap and its no-retry failure), and the nested-skill bullet names both limits. §5 documents `turnTimeoutMs`, `turnMaxMs` and `heartbeatMs` with their defaults.
- The active `formalize-tool-registry` change's scenario "Nested provider recovery is bounded" ([spec.md](openspec/changes/formalize-tool-registry/specs/tool-registry/spec.md)) now reads: no response or streamed progress for `turnTimeoutMs`, or still running at `turnMaxMs`, with a turn stopped at the cap not retried. `openspec validate formalize-tool-registry` passes.
- No acceptance criterion changes.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | **967 passed, 0 failed, 21 skipped** (68 files passed, 2 skipped) |
| Spec | `openspec validate formalize-tool-registry` | valid |
| Markdown lint | `markdownlint-cli2` on the two edited spec files | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | not run (see the live probe and manual run below) |

Runs used an isolated `KICAD_CONFIG_HOME` holding only `fp-lib-table`, matching CI. Measured diff coverage at the reviewed head was 96.0% (145 of 151 changed executable src lines); the two uncovered paths now have tests.

### New tests

**Simulated turns longer than 10 minutes** ([test/long-turn.test.ts](test/long-turn.test.ts)). Runs the real `runAgentLoop` and the real `ClaudeCodeProvider` at the shipped defaults (10-minute inactivity limit, 60-minute cap). Only the Agent SDK's `query` is faked: a stand-in `claude` subprocess that emits stream events on a schedule and rejects on abort like the real SDK. Vitest fake timers (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Date`) advance in 250 ms steps, and only while the fake subprocess is waiting on its schedule, so an hour of simulated time runs in about half a second and git, the transcript and the provider's scratch cwd do real I/O without spending simulated time. Abort times are measured from the renderer's `turnStart`, which the loop calls synchronously right before it arms the watchdog, so they are exact.

| Scenario | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| Shipped defaults | `turnTimeoutMs` is 10 minutes, `turnMaxMs` is 60 minutes |
| A 25-minute turn streaming a chunk every 30 s | one subprocess call, no abort, run duration of at least 25 minutes, no retry or timeout lines, and a heartbeat at 20m00s showing streamed output |
| A turn silent for 11 minutes | aborted exactly 600000 ms after the turn started, then retried once (`retrying (1/3)`) |
| A turn still streaming at 70 minutes | aborted exactly 3600000 ms after the turn started, one call only, `provider-error` with "too large, not hung" |

Against the unmodified code, the 25-minute and 70-minute scenarios fail with 4 subprocess calls instead of 1 (killed at 10 minutes and resent three times), and the defaults check fails because `turnMaxMs` does not exist. The silent-turn scenario passes on both, as intended. Robustness check for the clock driver: with 30000 spins of simulated real I/O inserted before the first stream event, the previous driver (which advanced on every spin) failed the 25-minute scenario with 4 calls; the current driver passes.

**Watchdog unit tests** ([test/recovery.test.ts](test/recovery.test.ts)): activity keeps a call alive past `idleMs`; a call with no activity gets `idleMs` as a plain deadline; the idle deadline fires once progress stops; the cap fires however much activity arrives; a call that reports no progress is never capped (`idleMs` 200 with `maxMs` 100 times out as `idle` at 200 ms; with `idleMs` 0 a silent call is not capped); progress that arrives after the cap came due trips it; a streaming call's cap is never below `idleMs`; both limits disable at `<= 0`; and the timeout still wins when `onTimeout` rejects the call synchronously.

**Config** ([test/watchdog-config.test.ts](test/watchdog-config.test.ts)): defaults of 600000 and 3600000; `turnTimeoutMs` of 0 or below turns the default cap off; an explicit `turnMaxMs` is kept; raising only `turnTimeoutMs` keeps the default cap.

**Agent loop** ([test/observability.test.ts](test/observability.test.ts)), with 50 to 300 ms limits: a streaming turn outlives `turnTimeoutMs` on one call; a silent turn is still aborted and retried; a turn at `turnMaxMs` fails without a resend; a turn that stays silent through every retry is called 4 times and fails as `provider-error` with "timed out 4×".

**Skill sub-run** ([test/tool-registry.test.ts](test/tool-registry.test.ts)): a streaming skill turn outlives `turnTimeoutMs`; a skill turn at `turnMaxMs` fails once without a retry. This test caught the watchdog rejecting after `onTimeout` instead of before.

**create** ([test/create-resilience.test.ts](test/create-resilience.test.ts)): a stage whose run fails as `provider-error` hands the diagnosis `the run ended as "failure" (provider-error): <reason>`; with the reason removed from the failure string, the test fails.

**claude-code** ([test/claude-code-provider.test.ts](test/claude-code-provider.test.ts)): `includePartialMessages` is set, every `stream_event` reports progress (thinking and block boundaries with an unchanged count, text deltas growing it), and the reply still comes from the complete message.

**Codex** ([test/codex-provider.test.ts](test/codex-provider.test.ts)): `close()` aborts the in-flight `thread.run` signal, and the retry opens a fresh thread whose first prompt carries the system prompt, the request and the latest message; a turn that settles after `close()` is discarded and cannot move the fresh thread's cursor; a turn retried while `close()` is still deleting the old directory gets a fresh directory that exists afterwards.

**MCP busy test** ([test/mcp-server.test.ts](test/mcp-server.test.ts), from #299): deterministic concurrent-init busy test; see #299 for details.

Against the unmodified code, the claude-code, Codex and agent-loop streaming tests fail (5 failures) and the silent-turn retry test passes.

**Live SDK probe**: one `query()` through the saved claude-code login with `includePartialMessages: true` returned 6 `stream_event` messages (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, `text_delta`, `content_block_stop`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`) plus the complete `assistant` message. The first event arrived about 18 s after the call.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `edit`
- Commands run and outcome: `do` with `--model claude-code`, with `.copperhead/config.json` set to `turnTimeoutMs: 30000` (a 30 s inactivity limit, so a real turn can exceed it), `heartbeatMs: 10000` and `maxTurns: 8`; `turnMaxMs` at its default.

```text
$ ./manual-tests/setup.sh edit
$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit init
(docs created; exits 1 on the fixture's existing legibility error "unlabeled-group", unrelated to this PR)
$ git -C manual-tests/runs/edit add -A && git -C manual-tests/runs/edit commit --no-verify -m "scaffold docs"
(--no-verify: the sandbox pre-commit hook runs check, which fails on the same fixture finding)
$ # set turnTimeoutMs 30000, heartbeatMs 10000, maxTurns 8 in .copperhead/config.json, commit with --no-verify
$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit do --model claude-code "Rename the EN net to CHIP_EN and propagate the change everywhere"
...
[turn 4/8 · 6 in / 2.0k out]
  … still working — 10s elapsed (no output yet)
  … still working — 20s elapsed (no output yet)
  … still working — 30s elapsed, ~493 chars streamed
...
  [finish] all gates satisfied; run will commit
committed ed61634294 (5 file(s))
done · ERC clean · committed ed61634294 · 2m15s · 16 in / 6.5k out
```

From the run's transcript: per-turn durations of 29.2, 8.5, 23.8, **38.3**, 4.4, 3.1, 10.7 and 10.2 s; zero `turn-timeout` events; `run-end` exit path `done`. Turn 4 ran 38.3 s, past the 30 s `turnTimeoutMs`, and completed because it kept streaming; the old whole-turn deadline would have aborted and resent it at 30 s. Turn 1 streamed nothing for at least its first 20 s (subprocess start plus time to first token), which is why the default inactivity limit stays at 10 minutes.

The run predates the review fixes. Those change behavior only for a turn that reports no progress (never capped), a cap below `turnTimeoutMs` (raised to it), `turnTimeoutMs <= 0` (no default cap), and Codex `close()` ordering; none of them applies to this streaming claude-code run with a 30 s limit and the default 60-minute cap.

## Docs

[SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) §4.5 and §5 now document the watchdog and `turnTimeoutMs`, `turnMaxMs` and `heartbeatMs`. Doc comments for `turnTimeoutMs`, `turnMaxMs`, `ChatOpts.onStream`, `withWatchdog` and the Codex teardown. The README and the docs site do not list these keys today, so no user-facing docs page changed.

pulls.title: fix(agent): reject withheld tool calls visibly instead of dropping si…
pulls.body: ## What Fixes a silent-drop bug where a locked `write_file` call in a batched text-protocol reply (claude-code/cursor) was discarded without feedback, causing the agent to `finish` and commit an empty spec-seed stage (0 files) while believing the write had succeeded. ## Why `create --brief` on claude-code/cursor was failing stage 1 (spec-seed) without ever writing `docs/SPEC.md`. The root cause: `parseToolCalls` silently dropped any call to a tool not present in the turn's starting catalog (e.g. `write_file` before `validate_change` unlocked it), with no error and no feedback to the model. The model proceeded to `finish`, the pipeline committed an empty stage, the stage-contract check failed afterward, and the retry hit the same silent drop in a loop. Closes #296. ## Design Implements **Option 1** from the issue discussion (reject visibly, don't drop silently) rather than Option 2 (offering all tools and gating at dispatch time). This preserves the structural edit-lock invariant: `write_file`/`edit_file` remain **structurally absent** from the turn's tool catalog until `validate_change` unlocks them (gated by omission, not by a live dispatch check). Key decisions: - `classifyToolCall` (replacing `toToolCall`) now distinguishes three outcomes instead of collapsing "off-catalog" and "not a tool call at all" into the same `null`: `accepted`, `withheld`, or `null` (genuine parse failure or non-tool prose). This is what makes silent-drop detection possible in mixed batches, not just tool-less turns. - `parseToolCalls` returns a `withheld: WithheldCall[]` array alongside `toolCalls`, carrying `{ name, args, reason }` for every call the model attempted but that wasn't in this turn's catalog. - The loop surfaces a tool-result message back to the model for each withheld call, so it knows to retry next turn instead of silently believing the write happened. - If a turn requests `finish` while any call in that same turn was withheld, `finish` is intercepted (not dispatched-then-undone) and `ctx.finishRequest` is cleared, with a message telling the model to resolve the withheld calls first. This avoids relying on undoing any finish side effects after the fact. - Added `finishGuard?: () => Promise` to `RunOptions`, run before commit logic. `create.ts` wires this to the stage-completion contract, so an incomplete stage (e.g. no filled Budgets section) is rejected with a specific reason before commit, not diagnosed after. - Directory-creation gaps (`appendChangelog`, `record_decision`) fixed with `mkdir({ recursive: true })` so a missing `docs/` no longer produces ENOENT on a brief-only repo. - `.copperhead/runs/` and `.env` added to `GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES` in `git.ts` to stop run transcripts and secrets from being committed into the target repo. > **Note for reviewers:** the fix for `.copperhead/runs/` and `.env` was applied via `GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES` (a `git add` pathspec exclusion), not via `ensureIgnored`/`.gitignore` directly. Please confirm this actually satisfies the Secrets invariant below, which specifically names `.gitignore`. If `GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES` doesn't ultimately feed `.gitignore`, these paths could still show up as untracked/stageable in the target repo even if `commitAll` itself skips them. ## Spec / OpenSpec No spec-level behavior change beyond making the existing `SPEC.md` §1.3 structural-lock guarantee actually hold under batched text-protocol replies (it was previously undermined by the silent-drop bug, not changed). No delta specs required. `openspec validate` not applicable to this change. ## Testing ### Automated test status | Check | Command | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | ✅ Pass (0 errors) | | Build | `npm run build` | ✅ Pass (compile + postbuild chmod succeeded) | | Unit + offline | `npx vitest run test/withheld-tool-calls.test.ts` | ✅ Pass (4/4 tests, 7.07s) | | Full suite | `npm test` | pending: report full-suite run before merge | | Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `` | n/a — not run | New test file: `test/withheld-tool-calls.test.ts`, covering: - `parseToolCalls` populates `withheld` for off-catalog tools in mixed batches (not just tool-less turns). - A batched reply with a withheld call blocks `finish`, emits a tool-result to the model, and succeeds when the call is legitimately retried on the next turn. - `finishGuard` rejects a premature finish and the loop continues rather than committing. - `record_decision` creates its target directory recursively when missing. No pre-existing failures known to be related to this change. ### Manual test log (required) - Sandbox variant used: `create` - Commands run and outcome: ```text $ node repro-brief.mjs # scripted repro from issue #296, run against this branch >> turn 1: write_file advertised=false parsed=[read_file,search] nudge=none >> turn 2: write_file advertised=false parsed=[propose_change,validate_change,check_drift] withheld=[write_file] nudge= >> turn 2: finish withheld, model informed, no commit >> turn 3: write_file retried, dispatched successfully (edits unlocked from turn 2's validate_change) >> turn 3: finish accepted, stage contract satisfied outcome: success | commit: | filesTouched: [docs/SPEC.md] docs/SPEC.md exists: true ``` before fix after fix ## Docs No README/config changes required. Recommend a `CHANGELOG.md` entry noting the silent-drop fix and the new `finishGuard` stage-contract precondition, since this affects observable pipeline behavior (an extra retry turn may now occur where a stage previously committed empty). --- ## Invariant checklist - [x] **Spec-gated in**: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text). Preserved; this PR does not add locked tools to the catalog, it only reports on calls that were correctly excluded. - [x] **Verification-gated out**: mutations still end in ERC (and DRC when the board changed) passing, with repair up to `maxRepairCycles` then rollback to the git snapshot. Unaffected by this change. - [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: nothing reachable from `src/commands/check` touches a provider, an API key, or the network. Unaffected; changes are scoped to `agent/`, `capabilities/handlers.ts`, and `util/git.ts`. - [x] **No sexp serialization**: the `src/kicad/` parser stays read-only; KiCad files are edited only via anchored exact-match text replace (no round-tripping). Unaffected. - [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: post-tool-call hooks keep feeding the ledger, and commit keeps refusing while obligations are open. Needs reviewer confirmation: withheld calls never dispatch, so no obligation is opened for them by design; confirm this doesn't mask any obligation-tracking regression for the calls that do dispatch in the same batch. - [ ] **Secrets**: transcripts and summaries redact `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` at write time; keys live only in env vars; `.gitignore` keeps `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/`. See caution note in Design: implemented via `GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES`, not confirmed to update `.gitignore` directly. Needs reviewer verification. - [x] **Spec coherence**: if spec-level behavior changed, SPEC.md and the change artifacts (`proposal.md`, `design.md`, delta specs, `tasks.md`) moved together and `openspec validate ` passes. N/A, no spec-level behavior changed.

pulls.title: Implement Phase 1/2 part research with credential-free JLCSearch
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR adds **live parts search from a Markdown file**:

```bash
copperhead parts check parts.md
```

The file can contain part numbers, names, or short descriptions in tables, lists, or prose. Copperhead searches the configured supplier and shows exact matches or up to **three candidates per part**.

The default supplier is public JLCSearch. No AI model or supplier API key is needed for this command.

Closes #246.

## Try it

Enable research in `.copperhead/config.json`:

```json
{
  "research": { "enabled": true }
}
```

Then create `parts.md`:

```md
# Prototype parts

- MPN: 0603WAF1001T5E qty: 10
- 10k resistor 0603
- ESP32 module
- LCSC: C21190

Use NE555P for the timer.
```

Run from the repository root:

```bash
copperhead parts check parts.md
```

Or try the included `examples/parts-check.md`. Tables with `MPN`, `Part number`, `LCSC`, `Name`, `Part`, `Component`, `Description`, or `Value` columns also work. Reference, quantity, and package columns are optional.

## Reading the results

- **Available:** An exact match has enough stock and is not marked EOL/obsolete. Missing lifecycle or datasheet information adds a review note; the part still counts as available.
- **Choose a part:** A name or description returned suggestions. Up to three distinct candidates are shown. Check their specifications, put the chosen MPN or LCSC number in the file, and run again.
- **Not available:** An exact match has zero/insufficient stock or is EOL/obsolete.
- **Not found:** The supplier returned no matching part. This does not mean it is out of stock everywhere.

Results show the searched text, source line, stock, quantity-aware unit price, package, description, and supplier link when supplied. Missing currency is labelled explicitly. Long descriptions are shortened in the terminal and retained in the Markdown/JSON output.

Explicit MPN/part-number/LCSC fields require an exact match. Candidates are suggestions, not verified substitutes or automatic selections. Candidate searches and metadata warnings exit zero with review notes; missing matches, unavailable exact parts, and provider errors exit non-zero.

For saved or structured results:

```bash
copperhead parts check parts.md --output parts-report.md
copperhead parts check parts.md --json
```

Markdown extraction uses deterministic rules. Complex prose may need to be rewritten as short part lines. Code, comments, and explicitly excluded sections are skipped. Repeated mentions are deduplicated; distinct references keep their own quantities. Each run accepts up to 50 queries and reuses identical supplier lookups.

## Other features in this PR

- Opt-in agent research tools: JLCSearch part search, optional Nexar, optional Brave web search, and allowlisted datasheet fetching.
- Once a validated OpenSpec change unlocks edits, agent part selection can record an exact MPN in `BOM.md` and a matching sourcing snapshot in `.copperhead/constraints.json`.
- Offline sourcing checks, including `copperhead check --strict-sourcing`.
- Research requests use HTTPS, allowed hosts, checked redirects, size limits, timeouts, transcripts, and secret redaction.

The standalone parts check writes only its ignored transcript and an explicitly requested report. It does not update BOM or sourcing snapshots. Regular `check` / `verify` stays deterministic and network-free.

## Verification

- 43 focused research tests passed, including Markdown extraction, exact matching, candidate limits, per-reference quantities, result counts, and request reuse.
- Typecheck, CLI build, and OpenSpec validation passed.
- Live JLCSearch run of the included example passed: three exact matches and two queries with three candidates each.
- Full suite outside the sandbox: **1020 passed, 9 failed, 21 skipped**. The remaining failures match the earlier KiCad fixture/path expectations and two REPL timeouts; they are outside the parts-search changes.
- Live LLM tests were not run; this command makes no model calls.

pulls.title: build(nix): add flake packaging
pulls.body:
## What

Adds a pinned Nix flake for running copperhead and entering a complete development environment. The package includes Node.js, git, OpenSpec, and KiCad on Linux, while macOS continues to use the separately installed KiCad application.

## Why

Nix users currently need to install and align each runtime dependency manually. A flake makes the CLI and contributor toolchain reproducible while retaining the existing npm and bootstrap installation paths.

## Design

Build logic lives in [`pkgs/copperhead.nix`](pkgs/copperhead.nix) as a reusable `buildNpmPackage` derivation. [`flake.nix`](flake.nix) only pins inputs, wires the overlay, and exposes package, check, and development-shell outputs.

The installed command wraps its PATH with git and OpenSpec. Linux also receives the pinned KiCad package. KiCad is excluded from the macOS closure because the pinned nixpkgs package is marked broken there, and copperhead already resolves the standard KiCad application path on macOS.

Supported outputs are x86-64 Linux, ARM64 Linux, and Apple Silicon macOS.

## Testing

pulls.title: fix(create): import installed footprints and address live pipeline blockers
pulls.body:
## What

Add installed-footprint search and placement so `copperhead create` can build a board from actual KiCad land patterns. Also fix blockers found during the real end-to-end run: selected-part review markers, Codex cancellation, generated power-symbol verification and shared-temp test cleanup.

Draft work toward #66, developed with AI assistance. The original input reached four committed stages. A new clean run with sourced component references has reached four committed stages, including a clean schematic ERC. The full eight-stage run and recorded end-to-end replay remain incomplete; this is not a bounty completion claim.

## Why

The part-selection prompt required a marker that its completion predicate rejected (related: #133). A live timeout logged an abort while the old Codex subprocess remained alive alongside its retry. KiCad 10.0.6 also reported two symbol-library mismatch warnings in the bundled fixture (related: #94).

## Design

`populate_board` is structurally unavailable before proposal validation. It resolves schematic references, installed footprint geometry and pad nets before an atomic write, preserves existing geometry, and opens ERC/DRC obligations. Missing assignments and existing references fail explicitly. `search_footprints` discovers up to 50 installed IDs without claiming package compatibility. Rotation updates pad/text angles according to KiCad semantics. No autorouter or relaxed DRC is introduced.

The verifier recognizes engine-owned synthetic power-symbol semantics without pretending they match installed libraries. Altered entries retain the ordinary verification path. Temp-sweep tests now use private roots, avoiding deletion of a concurrently running provider directory.

`COPPERHEAD_LLM_CACHE_ONLY=1` serves exact cache hits without constructing a live provider; misses fail and the create supervisor cannot fall back to live diagnosis. The complete recorded replay fixture is still pending.


Part selection uses the canonical BOM parser, accepts concrete MPNs with or without the review marker, and rejects placeholders. New selections are still instructed to carry the marker; passing this stage does not establish datasheet verification.

Each Codex SDK request receives an AbortSignal. Closing the provider detaches the old lifecycle synchronously, resets the transcript cursor, aborts captured requests, waits for them to settle, and removes only their owned scratch directory. Late results cannot send correction prompts to a replacement thread. Tests cover cancellation, cleanup, full-transcript retries and stale malformed responses.

A project-local symbol table points to the matching Device library already present in the repository. No ERC warning or verification gate is suppressed.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Updated the central SPEC and changes `fix-part-selection-review-flags`, `add-codex-cli-provider`, `fix-generated-power-symbol-verification`, `add-cache-only-replay` and `add-installed-footprint-placement`. Strict OpenSpec validation passed. The changes preserve the structural edit gate, verification and rollback, and the deterministic check path.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass, including current gate/export and provider correction changes |
| Unit + offline | `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` | pass, 974 passed, 23 skipped (including unrecorded E2E harness) |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass on changed specification files; full Markdown lint previously passed |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | default integration suite | skip; live CLI evidence below is separate |
| Watchdog process-group probe | `COPPERHEAD_E2E_WATCHDOG_TEST=1 npx vitest run test/create-pipeline-replay.test.ts` | pass; real descendant terminated |
| Eight-stage record/replay | opt-in harness committed | no recorded fixture yet; incomplete |

The repository has no `npm run lint` script; `lint:md` is its available lint command. One earlier full-suite run hit an unrelated MCP concurrent-init timing failure; the targeted MCP retest passed 29/29 and the subsequent full suite passed.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `create`.
- Tooling: macOS, Node 22.21.1, KiCad 10.0.6, local OpenSpec, saved-login Codex with Sol medium.
- Isolated KiCad library tables and versioned library paths were configured.

```text
node dist/cli.js --repo manual-tests/runs/create create \
  --brief examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md --model codex:gpt-5.6-sol
spec-seed committed 7404e57ee4
architecture committed 0bc48c48a2
part-selection committed 4fff238d96
schematic committed a1da71118d, ERC clean
initial process exited 1 at layout-draft after identifying missing footprint import
resumed: eight footprints imported; layout-draft failed after five repair cycles
failed stage rolled back; no fifth-stage commit
```

A separate real SDK cancellation check started a Codex subprocess, closed the provider, and verified request rejection, process exit and scratch-directory removal. The pinned fixture's real ERC reported zero violations. The schematic stage passed real ERC. A separate manual sandbox imported seven actual installed footprints at both 0 and 90 degrees: KiCad loaded them with zero library mismatches. Its deliberately unrouted board still has 18 unconnected items and four USB hole-clearance findings. No full-board DRC success is claimed. In an earlier layout attempt the model suppressed DRC categories in project settings; three footprint mismatches still failed the gate, and the stage rolled back. This attempt is recorded as a failure, not clean-board evidence. Project edits now reject added verification exclusions, new non-error severities, and reductions of existing clearances/severities before writing; unchanged bootstrap ignores remain allowed. This guard covers project JSON and does not claim to cover every KiCad rule representation. A later attempt refused to proceed because the replacement connector's 3 A rating was not established in its available input. The new `usb-c-breakout-verified-parts.md` brief preserves the original brief byte-for-byte and appends GCT specification/drawing references. The clean run using this brief has committed spec-seed, architecture, part selection and schematic; layout stopped on malformed Codex tool arguments after its last DRC reported 35 violations. The incomplete work was stashed and the sandbox restored. It uses 100 turns, 20 repair cycles and no stage retry. No generated design artifact was manually changed to pass verification. A fresh native export produced all six jobs without failure and a valid receipt. Mutating a Gerber or the source BOM invalidated it. That live run used the previous build, so its four completed stages are not evidence of these new runtime gates. The post-change suite had 974 passes, 23 skips and one intermittent MCP concurrency failure; all 29 MCP tests passed on isolated rerun. Build passed. The resume mechanism committed that checkpoint as 7561787ee9 and correctly kept layout active.

pulls.title: docs(site): make the GitBook theme hold up on a phone
pulls.body:
## What Makes the docs site readable on a narrow column. Tables stop being content-sized scrolling blocks and become labelled cards below 34rem of column width, inline code stops breaking mid-token, long lines in code blocks wrap instead of being cut off, and a code block nested two lists deep gets its width back. Follow-up to #271. ## Why #271 restyled the site after GitBook's clean theme, but only the wide case was checked. On a phone, and on a tablet with the sidebar open, five things broke: - Starlight renders a table as a content-sized scrolling block, which left a ragged right edge next to full-width code blocks. Worse, the binding constraint is the content column, not the viewport: with the sidebar open the column is about 500px, and a four-column table was crushed into one-word ribbons. - Inline code broke mid-token, so `--json` split at the hyphen and `kicad-cli` at its own. - Long lines in code blocks were cut off rather than wrapped. Sample briefs and prompts are prose-shaped, so the tail simply vanished. - A code block nested two lists deep was squeezed to about two thirds of the column. - Two cosmetic leftovers: the first [JumpLink.astro](docs/src/components/JumpLink.astro) sat flush against its heading, because Starlight's content-spacing rule skips `` siblings, and the Steps guide line ran on past the last step, connecting to nothing. ## Design [rehype-table-labels.mjs](docs/src/plugins/rehype-table-labels.mjs) is a build-time pass over the content HTML, wired in through `markdown.rehypePlugins` in [astro.config.mjs](docs/astro.config.mjs). It does two things: - wraps each `` in `.table-wrap`, so the table itself can be a real full-width table while the wrapper owns horizontal overflow, and stamps every body cell with `data-label=""`; - marks a short single-token inline code span `nowrap`, and splits a multi-word span into per-token ``, so a break can only land on a space. Tokens over 30 characters are left free to wrap. An `inPre` guard keeps the pass out of code blocks entirely. In [custom.css](docs/src/styles/custom.css), `.sl-markdown-content` becomes a size container, so the table rules key off the width the table actually has rather than the viewport. Below 34rem of column width each row becomes a labelled card; the header row is clipped out of the flow but stays in the DOM for assistive tech. Headings that were a bare path (`.copperhead/config.json`) now name the file and give the path in the prose, so a heading is not the widest thing on the page. That changes their generated slugs, so each renamed heading keeps an explicit `` carrying its pre-rename slug (`#copperheadconfigjson` and friends) and links published against the old headings still land on their section. ## Spec / OpenSpec n/a, docs-only and presentational. No spec-level behavior changes, so SPEC.md and the change artifacts correctly stay put. ## Testing ### Automated test status | Check | Command | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass | | Build | `npm run build` (in `docs/`) | pass, clean at 17 pages | | Unit + offline | `npm test` | 923 pass / 21 skip / 15 fail locally. It pins the table wrapping and labelling (including a row wider than its header, and a table with no header row), the nowrap split, the over-long-token case, and that nothing inside a `
` is touched.

pulls.title: fix(mcp): make per-repo mutating-call lock acquisition atomic
pulls.body:
## What
Fixes a race condition in the MCP server where two near-simultaneous mutating tool calls (`copperhead_init`, `copperhead_do`, `copperhead_sync` with `resolve=true`) against the same repo could both proceed instead of one being correctly refused as busy.

## Why
The per-repo mutating-call lock (`locks.tryAcquire(repoRoot)`) was called after one or more `await` points inside each handler (`await requireKicad()`, `await resolveModelOrFail()`). This left an async gap: both concurrent calls could suspend during preflight and reach the lock check before either had acquired it, or the first call could finish and release the lock before the second call even checked it. Either way, both calls got admitted, violating the documented per-repo serialization spec and defeating the purpose of the lock (protecting a repo from concurrent mutating runs stepping on each other).

## Design
- **Root cause**: non-atomic check-then-set. The lock check (`locks.tryAcquire`) happened after async work, not at the synchronous entry of the handler, so two calls racing on the same event-loop tick (or close enough) could both slip past.
- **Fix**: moved `locks.tryAcquire(repoRoot)` to the very first synchronous line of each mutating handler in [server.ts](src/mcp/server.ts), before any `await`. The existing busy-error response (`unavailable`, "another copperhead run is in progress for this repo; retry shortly") is unchanged. All prior handler logic (`requireKicad()`, `resolveModelOrFail()`, the actual run) now executes inside the existing `try` block, with `locks.release(repoRoot)` still in `finally`.
- **Scope**: touches only lock-acquisition ordering in `copperhead_init`, `copperhead_do`, and `copperhead_sync`. No change to the lock implementation itself (`locks.tryAcquire`/`release` stay as-is, already a synchronous Map/Set-based check-and-set), no change to read-only tools (`copperhead_check`, `copperhead_doctor`), no change to any other package (`ir`, `engine`, `commands`, other tools). The diff is 48 insertions / 49 deletions in a single file, mostly a 2-space indentation shift from wrapping existing await calls one level deeper inside the `try` block.
- **Independent of #276 / PR #281**: confirmed via `git diff main feature/pattern-bom-expansion -- src/mcp/ test/mcp-server.test.ts` showing 0 changed lines before this fix; this bug is pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to the pattern-BOM-expansion work.

## Testing
### Automated test status
| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | ✅ Pass (0 errors) |
| Build | `npm run build` | ✅ Pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | ✅ Pass (902/947 on this Windows dev machine; all 24 failures verified pre-existing/environment-specific, see below — no failures attributable to this change) |
| Targeted race test | `npx vitest run test/mcp-server.test.ts -t "rejects a concurrent mutating call with a typed busy error"` | ✅ Pass 20/20 consecutive runs |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a — no provider-facing code touched |

**Pre-existing/environment failures (verified, not introduced by this PR):** on this Windows machine, both `main` and this branch show the same class of failures: 60s timeouts on `kicad-cli` subprocess spawns under parallel Vitest workers (`init-check`, `create-preflight`, `draft-*`, `tool-registry`, etc.), Windows-specific assertion mismatches (CRLF vs `\n`, `chmod 000` not restricting access on NTFS, Windows home-path formatting, Windows NTSTATUS exit codes instead of POSIX), and one test (`draft-hardening`) that fails only under full-suite CPU saturation but passes 32/32 in isolation. None of these touch `src/mcp/server.ts` locking logic. This PR's CI run (Linux) is the authoritative signal for merge, since none of the above Windows-specific causes apply there.

The one test this PR directly fixes — `rejects a concurrent mutating call with a typed busy error` — fails on `main` and passes reliably (20/20) on this branch.

### Manual test log (required)
- Sandbox variant used: n/a
- Reason: this is an internal MCP server concurrency fix with no change to CLI-facing behavior, the agent loop, or KiCad file handling. Exercised instead via the automated concurrency test above, run 20 times consecutively to rule out a lucky pass.
```text
$ for i in $(seq 1 20); do npx vitest run test/mcp-server.test.ts -t "rejects a concurrent mutating call with a typed busy error"; done
20 passed (20)

$ git diff main --stat

```

## Docs
No user-facing docs changes. This is an internal correctness fix to MCP tool-call serialization; the documented spec behavior ("mutating tools are serialized per repo") is unchanged, this PR just makes the implementation actually satisfy it.

---

pulls.title: Feature/pattern bom expansion
pulls.body:
> **Draft note:** This branch is based on top of `feature/circuit-pattern-library` (#279),
> which is still pending merge into main. The diff below will include #279's commits
> until it merges; that is expected and will clean up automatically once #279 lands
> and this branch is rebased onto main. Depends on #274 (static pattern library) landing
> first — no dependency on #277 or #278.

Closes #276

## What
Lets Stage 3 (part-selection) reference a named circuit pattern instead of enumerating every part by hand. The AI may now respond with `use pattern: <pattern-name>` for common sub-circuits, and that expands into standard BOM rows tagged `from pattern: <name>` in the Rationale column for traceability.

## Why
Today the AI re-derives the same handful of parts (regulator + decoupling caps, USB-C connector + CC pull-downs + bulk cap) from first principles on every design, with no memory of "the way this is always done." This causes avoidable BOM mistakes that only surface later at the schematic/ERC stage, and gives reviewers no way to tell a standard block apart from a flat, undifferentiated parts list. Refs #276.

## Design
- **Pure expansion helper**: [expandToBom.ts](src/kicad/patterns/expandToBom.ts) exports `expandPatternToBomRows()`, `expandPatternToBom()`, and `resolvePatternsInBomText()`. These read pattern JSON from `src/kicad/patterns/*.json` (added in #274) and return/insert plain BOM rows; none of them write files directly.
- **Traceable rows, not a new format**: expanded rows use the exact same 5-column `| Refdes | Value | Footprint | MPN | Rationale |` shape as hand-written rows, with `from pattern: <name>` in Rationale and a `| Pattern: <name> | source: ... |` header line, per the before/after example in #276. Stage 4 and everything downstream sees ordinary BOM rows, indistinguishable from manual entries.
- **Stage 3 only**: the prompt and resolution logic changes are scoped to Stage 3 in [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) (`isComplete` / `runCreate`). Manual enumeration remains the default and stays fully supported; pattern use is opt-in per design need.
- **No schema or engine changes**: [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts) and [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts) are untouched. This does not wire pattern-awareness into `schematic.intent.json` — that remains a separate, deferred proposal.
- **Alternatives considered** (per #276's issue body): expanding patterns directly inside `ir.ts`/`schematic.intent.json` was rejected as a bigger, riskier change to the validated Intent schema; a human-only `--use-pattern <name>` CLI flag was considered but doesn't solve the actual problem of the AI re-deriving parts every run, and is left as a possible future addition.

## Spec / OpenSpec
Adds a new OpenSpec change: `add-pattern-bom-reference` (see [proposal.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-bom-reference/proposal.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-bom-reference/design.md), [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-bom-reference/tasks.md), and the delta spec at `specs/pattern-bom-reference/spec.md`). This is gated because it changes Stage 3 agent behavior (per the spec-gated-edits rule), even though no new destructive write tool is introduced — it only changes what content flows into the existing BOM.md write path. `openspec validate add-pattern-bom-reference` passes.

## Testing
### Automated test status

| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | ✅ Pass (0 errors) |
| Build | `npm run build` | ✅ Pass |

| Pattern validation | `npm run validate:patterns` | ✅ Pass (3/3 patterns) |
| OpenSpec validation (new) | `openspec validate add-pattern-bom-reference` | ✅ Pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a — no provider-facing prompt content changed beyond the Stage 3 text itself, no new LLM calls added |

New tests: [pattern-bom-expansion.test.ts](test/pattern-bom-expansion.test.ts) covers expansion of all three existing patterns (`voltage-regulator-ams1117`, `usb-c-power-input`, `crystal-oscillator`) into correct BOM rows, unknown-pattern error handling, `parseBomTable` compatibility (regression check against existing BOM consumers such as `drift.ts` and `export.js`), and in-place `use pattern:` text resolution via `resolvePatternsInBomText`.

Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: none observed.

### Manual test log (required)

pulls.title: Feature/pattern expansion ir
pulls.body:
> **Draft note:** Issue #277 recommends this land only after #276 and #278 are in. Filing as a draft to keep the work visible and unblock review discussion, but not requesting merge until sequencing is confirmed with maintainers. This branch is currently based on top of `feature/circuit-pattern-library` (#279), which is still pending merge into main. The diff below will include #279's commits until it merges; that is expected and will clean up automatically once #279 lands and this branch is rebased onto main.

## What
Adds [patternExpand.ts](src/kicad/draft/patternExpand.ts), a pure helper function that loads a named circuit pattern from `src/kicad/patterns/*.json` and expands it into a `{ parts: IntentPart[], nets: IntentNet[] }` block with renumbered reference designators and rewritten net endpoint pins, for manual merging into `schematic.intent.json`.

## Why
Even after part-selection can reference a named pattern (#276), the drafting engine never learns that a set of parts came from a known-good pattern, so the AI still has to manually re-derive every `REF.PIN` net endpoint for a pattern's internal wiring at the schematic stage, even though that wiring is already fully known from `src/kicad/patterns/*.json`. This reintroduces exactly the wiring-mistake risk that patterns are meant to remove. Refs #277.

## Design
This implements only the "expansion-only" variant discussed in #277, which the issue itself flags as the safer MVP compared to the full metadata-tracking version.

- **Pure function, no file I/O beyond loading the pattern**: `expandPatternRef(patternName, options)` reads the requested pattern definition and returns `{ parts, nets }`. It does not read or write `schematic.intent.json`, and the caller is responsible for merging the result into their own intent.
- **No schema changes**: does not add a `patternRefs?` field to `SchematicIntent` in [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts), and does not change `validateIntent()`'s required shape or logic in any way.
- **No engine changes**: [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts) is untouched. Layout-level pattern-awareness (grouping expanded instances visually) is explicitly deferred to #278.
- **No pipeline wiring**: [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) is untouched. Automatically calling this helper during Stage 4 is out of scope for this PR.
- **Ref and pin renumbering**: remaps each component reference (e.g. `U1` -> `REG1_U1`) using the given ref prefix and instance id, and rewrites every corresponding net pin connection (e.g. `U1.3` -> `REG1_U1.3`) so the expanded output is structurally indistinguishable from hand-written parts and nets.
- **Out of scope, deferred to future issues**: the `patternRefs` metadata field on `SchematicIntent`, structural cross-checking of pattern instances in `validateIntent()`, and layout-engine grouping hints. These are intentionally left out per the descope decision in #277, and should only be attempted after this expansion-only helper has been used in practice.

## Spec / OpenSpec
This adds a new OpenSpec change: `add-pattern-expansion-helper` (see [proposal.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-expansion-helper/proposal.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-expansion-helper/design.md), [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-pattern-expansion-helper/tasks.md), and the delta spec at `specs/pattern-expansion/spec.md`). The proposal documents the problem, the descoped expansion-only solution, and explicitly lists what is out of scope (the `patternRefs` field, `validateIntent()` cross-checks, and engine.ts layout hints) so a future issue can pick those up separately. `openspec validate add-pattern-expansion-helper` passes.

## Testing
### Automated test status
| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | ✅ Pass (0 errors) |
| Build | `npm run build` | ✅ Pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | ✅ Pass (no existing tests affected) |
| Pattern expansion (new) | `npx vitest run test/pattern-expand.test.ts` | ✅ Pass (7/7 tests) |
| Pattern validation | `npm run validate:patterns` | ✅ Pass (3/3 patterns) |
| OpenSpec validation (new) | `openspec validate add-pattern-expansion-helper` | ✅ Pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a — no LLM-facing code changed |

New tests: [pattern-expand.test.ts](test/pattern-expand.test.ts) covers expansion of all three existing patterns (`voltage-regulator-ams1117`, `usb-c-power-input`, `crystal-oscillator`), ref-prefix and instance-id renumbering, verification that expanded output passes the existing `validateIntent()` unchanged when merged into a minimal `SchematicIntent`, and error handling for unknown pattern names.

Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: none observed.

### Manual test log (required)
- Sandbox variant used: n/a
- Reason: this PR does not change CLI behavior, the agent loop, providers, or runtime KiCad generation. `expandPatternRef` is a standalone pure function not yet wired into `create`/`edit`/`check`, so there is no CLI-level flow to exercise manually. Verified instead via the automated suite above:
```text
$ npx vitest run test/pattern-expand.test.ts
```

pulls.title: feat(kicad): add static circuit pattern library (voltage-regulator, u…
pulls.body:
## What
Adds a static, read-only pattern library of three known-good circuit blocks (AMS1117 linear voltage regulator, USB-C power input sink, crystal oscillator) as JSON files under `src/kicad/patterns/`, along with a JSON schema, a standalone validation script, and `docs/patterns.md`.

## Why
During the schematic step, the AI currently has to re-derive every common sub-circuit (regulator, USB-C input, crystal osc) from scratch, pin by pin. This leads to avoidable ERC failures and retries (wrong pull-up rail, missing decoupling cap, miswired USB signal pins), burning both time and compute. There is currently no reusable, named source of known-good multi-part circuit blocks that the AI or a human reviewer could reference. Closes #274.

## Design
This is intentionally a small, purely additive first step, not the Phase 4 "template corpus (tscircuit-style idiom matching)" mentioned in `ROADMAP.md`.

- Pattern files use the same shape already accepted by `SchematicIntent` (`IntentPart` / `IntentNet` from [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts)), so no new concepts are introduced, just static data expressed in an existing shape.
- `src/kicad/patterns/pattern.schema.json` formally defines that shape (`name`, `description`, `parts[]`, `nets[]`) so pattern files can be validated independently of the drafting pipeline.
- `scripts/validate-patterns.ts` loads every pattern file, validates it against the schema, and checks referential integrity (every `REF.pin` in `nets[].pins` must resolve to a `ref` declared in that same file's `parts[]`). It is wired in via `npm run validate:patterns` and does not touch any existing script.
- Pattern values (part refs, decoupling caps, pull-down resistor values, load cap values) were based on the existing multi-part sub-circuits already visible in `manual-tests/real-designs/examples` (the regulator stage in `cm5_minima`, the crystal block in `ecc83`), not invented from scratch.
- Nothing in [ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts), [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts), part-selection, or any prompt/validator is modified. The patterns are not consumed anywhere yet; consuming them from part-selection or the schematic drafting step is explicitly left as a separate, future proposal, per the discussion in #274.

### Invariants
- **Spec-gated edits**: no effect. Only new static data files and docs are added; no new write tools, commands, or agent capabilities are introduced.
- **Verification-gated mutations**: no effect. Nothing in this PR touches `schematic.intent.json` generation, the drafting engine, or triggers ERC/DRC, since the pattern files aren't consumed by any pipeline stage yet. A follow-up proposal (patterns → Intent expansion, or patterns → part-selection) will need to address both invariants explicitly; that is out of scope here.

## Spec / OpenSpec
No spec-level behavior changes. This is data + docs only, so no OpenSpec proposal, `SPEC.md` update, or delta spec is required. `openspec validate` is unaffected.

## Testing

| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a — no LLM-facing code changed |

New tests: none added as unit tests; validation is covered by the new `validate:patterns` script itself, which asserts schema conformance and referential integrity for every pattern file and fails the build otherwise.

Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: none observed.

- Reason: this PR does not change CLI behavior, the agent loop, providers, or runtime KiCad generation. It only adds static reference JSON, a schema, docs, and an offline validation script that is not wired into `create`/`edit`/`check`. Verified instead via:

pulls.title: feat(mcp): serve the gated pipeline to MCP hosts over stdio
pulls.body:
## What

Adds `copperhead mcp`, a stdio MCP server exposing the gated pipeline to any MCP host as five opaque, outcome-level tools: `copperhead_check`, `copperhead_do`, `copperhead_sync`, `copperhead_init`, and `copperhead_doctor`. Closes #40.

## Why

Hosts already point coding agents at KiCad repos through generic file tools, so a host agent can rewrite a `.kicad_sch` with no spec gate, no verification, and no rollback. copperhead's invariants only protected people whose entry point is the CLI — a shrinking share of how people work. This makes the gated pipeline the thing the host calls.

## Design

**Opacity is the security boundary.** The server exposes outcomes, not operations: no file-edit tool, no raw-KiCad tool, no partial-loop tool. Each tool dispatches into the existing entry points ([runCheck](src/commands/check.ts), [runAgentLoop](src/agent/loop.ts), [syncVerify / syncResolve](src/commands/sync.ts), [runInit](src/memory/scaffold.ts), [runDoctor](src/commands/doctor.ts)), so dirty-tree refusal, path sandbox, budgets and rollback are inherited by construction. `--allow-dirty` is deliberately not exposed: a tool input that switches a safety rail off is a rail a host can bypass.

**Experimental on purpose (D7).** A `0.` protocol major, announced on startup, no registry listing until the stabilization criteria in the proposal are met. A stable tool schema is a contract with hosts we cannot migrate, on a CLI that shipped four minor versions in six weeks. A test asserts the `0.`, so stabilizing is a deliberate edit rather than a drift. This is also why the change does **not** block on the run-protocol handshake (#258): an unstable surface makes no promise to reconcile against. Adopting `capabilities --json` is written down as the stabilization trigger instead.

**Shared envelope, separate catalog (D9).** Results are built with `seal()` and errors carry the shared `ToolErrorKind` values, so redaction is inherited rather than reimplemented. But the five tools are deliberately **absent** from the agent capability catalog: a `CatalogEntry` is gated on `RunContext` and therefore callable by the loop, so registering `copperhead_do` there would make the gated pipeline reachable from inside the pipeline — a recursion hazard and a hole straight through the spec gate. A test asserts they resolve to nothing in the registry.

**`doctor` as the fifth tool (D10).** LLM-free, network-free, mutates nothing, so it widens the surface without widening what the surface can *do*. It earns its place because "is this host configured correctly" is the largest predictable support cost of shipping an MCP server. It deliberately skips the `kicad-cli` preflight every other tool performs — gating a diagnostic on the thing it diagnoses would fail exactly when it is needed.

Behaviour worth calling out:

- A rollback is a successful tool call whose result says `rolled_back`, not a protocol error (D6).
- `copperhead_do` runs non-interactively with no confirm callback and no budget-extension prompt: there is no human on this transport, so the loop must fail rather than block.
- Progress streams as MCP progress notifications. All logs go to stderr; stdout carries only JSON-RPC.
- `copperhead_do` and `copperhead_sync --resolve` refuse with a typed `unavailable` naming the missing variable when no model resolves.
- Mutating tools are serialized per repo with a typed busy error; `check` and `doctor` run concurrently.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change `add-mcp-server`, re-specced before implementation: `openspec validate add-mcp-server` passes, 23/25 tasks checked off. The 2 open tasks are the explicitly deferred stabilization items (adopt the handshake; submit registry listings). Two incoherences in the prior spec were fixed rather than implemented around — it promised `fab`/`strict` inputs on `copperhead_check` that `check` cannot accept, and it assumed no tool registry existed when #246 Phase 0 has since landed.

## Testing

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass (186 files) |
| Full suite | `npm test` | **918 passed, 0 failed, 21 skipped** |
| Spec | `openspec validate add-mcp-server` | valid |

24 new tests across three files: tool surface and opacity, a surface audit that fails if a tool starts accepting a filesystem path, catalog absence, redaction of a key reaching a result, `check`/`doctor` parity with the direct entry points, keyless degradation, per-repo serialization, run-status mapping, a **real-stdio handshake** proving stdout carries only JSON-RPC, and a **broken-`kicad-cli` case** proving `doctor` answers where `check` correctly refuses with `unavailable`.

[test/entry-point-parity.test.ts](test/entry-point-parity.test.ts) pins `check`/`sync`/`init` entry-point results byte-identical to their `--json` CLI output, so the server and the CLI cannot silently drift.

> Note for reviewers: three suites (`init-check`, `stage-completion`, `gating-sync`) fail on a dev box whose user-level KiCad `sym-lib-table` exists, which CI does not have. Runs above used an isolated `KICAD_CONFIG_HOME`.

## Docs

[README.md](README.md) gets an MCP section; [integrations/README.md](integrations/README.md) covers host configuration (Claude Code, generic stdio), the Codex gap, and the stabilization criteria. The companion skill is [integrations/claude-code/copperhead/SKILL.md](integrations/claude-code/copperhead/SKILL.md) — note it is prompt-level guidance and explicitly *not* a substitute for the server's structural opacity.

## Dependency

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30.0`. It was already vendored as a peer dependency of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, so the lockfile change is one line.

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: the MCP surface exposes no file-edit tool, so the agent tool list and its spec gate are untouched and cannot be reached around; a surface-audit test enforces it.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: `copperhead_do` runs the unchanged loop; a failure returns `rolled_back` after repair and restores the git snapshot.
- [x] **`check` / `verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: `copperhead_check` dispatches `runCheck` with no provider and no key; a test runs it with no credential.
- [ ] **No sexp serialization**: n/a (the KiCad parser is untouched).
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: n/a (the loop and commit hooks are untouched).
- [x] **Secrets**: keys are read only from env vars, are never a tool input, and every result goes through `seal()`; tests assert a key in a result and in `doctor`'s report comes back redacted.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: the delta specs, design decisions and `tasks.md` moved with the code; `openspec validate` passes.

pulls.title: fix(agent): close skill-run providers and stop reporting unverifiable as failure
pulls.body:
## What

Six follow-up fixes to the two-tier tool catalog merged in #255 (`26d9b51`): one medium (a provider handle `copperhead skill run` never closed) and five low. No new features; `check`, `create` stages, and spec-gated edits are unchanged.

## Why

These are the findings from the [second automated review pass](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/pull/255#issuecomment-5560861628) on #255. They were non-blocking, so #255 merged without them; the patch could not be pushed to the contributor's fork branch, so it lands here instead.

## Design

**`skill run` now owns its provider's lifecycle.** `providerForSkillRun` built a provider and the command exited without closing it. `close()` is what removes the saved-login backend's `mkdtemp` working directory and aborts its subprocess — `runAgentLoop` does it in a `finally` for exactly that reason (the I8 disk-fill mode; see the comment on `close()` in [claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts)), and `skill run` had no agent loop to inherit it from. `sweepStaleTempDirs` only runs from `create`, so the directories accumulated until some later `create` happened to reclaim them, age-gated at 2h.

New [`runSkillCli`](src/commands/skill.ts) brackets the run — including the unknown-skill throw path, so a provider that was already built is not leaked — and warns rather than losing the result when `close()` itself throws. [cli.ts](src/cli.ts) carries an exit code out instead of calling `process.exit` inside the `try`, since `process.exit` skips pending `finally` blocks.

**`verify_symbols` stops reporting unverifiable as failure.** It returned `ok: false` for any non-empty findings array, but `no-library` is the *unverifiable* bucket — counted into `skipped`, excluded from `mismatches`, and documented on `verifySchematicSymbols` as "never treated as a mismatch". On a machine without the referenced libraries it printed `0 issue(s) to reconcile` under a failure glyph: the mirror of the false-green glyph #255 fixed. Now reports from the mismatch count.

Also:

- The surviving conformance assertion (`if (s.ownGate(ctx)) expect(conj).toBe(true)`) became a latent false positive once `ownGate` stopped being rebound to the conjunction — it would fail the first legitimate mutation skill someone adds, even though `registry.list` correctly omits it. Now asserts the property that matters: present in `registry.list(ctx)` ⇒ every declared tool's gate open.
- The availability test's singleton `gate` swap is bracketed so no assertion can leak it.
- The two hardcoded turn-timeout budgets become one shared `MAX_TURN_TIMEOUTS` in [recovery.ts](src/agent/recovery.ts).
- Dead `isRetryableToolKind` dropped; the dispatch 429/exception test still pins the real retry policy. `protocolVersion` **stays** — `specs/tool-registry/spec.md` requires the registry to expose it.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Change: `formalize-tool-registry` (`openspec validate formalize-tool-registry` passes). `cli-surface` gains the provider-release guarantee for `skill run`; `tool-registry` gains an "unverifiable is not failure" scenario; `tasks.md` gains §9.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (892 pass, 0 fail, 21 skip) |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate formalize-tool-registry` | valid |

Three new regression tests: provider closed on both the failing and the unknown-skill throw path; a provider whose `close` throws still yields the run result; `verify_symbols` stays `ok` when every finding is `no-library`.

Note on the suite: a bare `npm test` on a machine with a user-level KiCad `sym-lib-table` shows 3 environmental failures (`init-check`, `stage-completion`, `gating-sync`) from `lib_symbol_mismatch` ERC warnings on the open-key fixture. Run with an isolated `KICAD_CONFIG_HOME` containing only `10.0/fp-lib-table` to reproduce CI, where the suite is fully green.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `edit` (temp copy of `test/fixtures/open-key`, then `init`)
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node --import tsx src/cli.ts --repo <sandbox> skill list
· generate-report  Read-only report of the current design: ERC, DRC (if a board exists), drift, nets, and an optional SVG path. Does not edit files.
exit 0
$ ls -a <sandbox>/.copperhead
(no .copperhead)          # skill list still creates no run directory

$ node --import tsx src/cli.ts --repo <sandbox> skill run banana
exit 1 (no stack trace)

$ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u COPPERHEAD_MODEL \
    node --import tsx src/cli.ts --repo <sandbox> skill run generate-report
no model configured: ... skill run needs OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or --model for a saved-login provider (codex, claude-code, cursor).
exit 1 (no stack trace)
```

## Docs

No user-facing doc change: `skill list` / `skill run` are documented in README.md as of #255, and their behavior is unchanged apart from releasing the provider.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text). Untouched by this PR.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: mutations still end in ERC (and DRC when the board changed) passing, with repair up to `maxRepairCycles` then rollback. Untouched; `verify_symbols` is a diagnostic and its `ok` does not gate `finish`.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: `src/commands/check.ts` and its import graph are untouched; the module-graph guard still passes.
- [N/A] **No sexp serialization**: the `src/kicad/` parser and edit path are untouched.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: post-tool-call hooks keep feeding the ledger and commit keeps refusing while obligations are open. Untouched.
- [x] **Secrets**: redaction at transcript write time and at envelope construction unchanged; `.gitignore` keeps `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/`.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: the `formalize-tool-registry` delta specs and `tasks.md` move with the code and `openspec validate` passes.

pulls.title: docs(site): restyle the docs after GitBook's clean theme
pulls.body:
## What

Restyles docs.copperhead.sh after GitBook's "clean" theme (the look of docs.quilter.ai): a neutral near-black palette with the copper accent, a floating rounded sidebar with per-page icons and a tinted active pill, a wide header search box with a "Get started" button, a section eyebrow and lead paragraph above each page, and a landing page rebuilt as a "Welcome" doc page with "Jump right in" rows and "Keep exploring" card groups. Still Astro Starlight, so search, edit links, last-updated stamps, and the llms.txt plugin are unchanged.

## Why

The stock Starlight look (blue accent, splash hero, boxed sidebar) reads as a template. The docs are the first thing most people open, and the GitBook clean layout is a proven docs pattern: denser navigation, a narrow readable column, quiet borders instead of shadows, and a landing page that routes readers instead of pitching them.

## Design

Everything lives in `docs/`; no runtime code changes.

- [custom.css](docs/src/styles/custom.css) holds the palette, type scale, and layout. It is deliberately unlayered so it overrides Starlight's own cascade layers without `!important`. Starlight names its gray scale from the dark palette, so `--sl-color-white` is the strongest text colour and `--sl-color-black` the page background in both modes; the file documents this.
- Component overrides in [docs/src/components/](docs/src/components/): [Header.astro](docs/src/components/Header.astro), [Sidebar.astro](docs/src/components/Sidebar.astro) plus [SidebarSublist.astro](docs/src/components/SidebarSublist.astro), [PageTitle.astro](docs/src/components/PageTitle.astro), and [ThemeSelect.astro](docs/src/components/ThemeSelect.astro). The sidebar keeps Starlight's persister and restore points so open/closed state and scroll position survive navigation. The theme toggle writes the same `starlight-theme` storage key Starlight's inline provider reads, so there is no flash on load.
- Per-page sidebar icons are set in [astro.config.mjs](docs/astro.config.mjs) via `attrs: { 'data-icon': '<starlight icon>' }` and rendered by the sublist override.
- [JumpLink.astro](docs/src/components/JumpLink.astro), [DocCard.astro](docs/src/components/DocCard.astro), and [DocCards.astro](docs/src/components/DocCards.astro) are the landing-page building blocks used by [index.mdx](docs/src/content/docs/index.mdx).
