pulls.title: Reuse schematic parse in check/draft and parallelize ERC/DRC/openspec
pulls.body:
## What

This PR cuts redundant schematic parsing in `copperhead check` and the `draft_schematic` agent tool: one parse per check run, one legibility pass before scoring, and ERC/DRC/openspec running in parallel when configured. Behavior, exit codes, and tool contracts are unchanged.

## Why

Closes [#229](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/issues/229).

Each `check` was reloading and re-parsing the same `.kicad_sch` roughly 5–6 times via independent calls to [`loadSheets()`](src/kicad/sexp.ts). `draft_schematic` ran legibility and geometry twice (once directly, again inside `scoreSchematic`). ERC, DRC, and openspec ran sequentially despite being independent subprocess work.

## Design

**Single-load schematic session** ([`sexp.ts`](src/kicad/sexp.ts)): `loadSchematic()` returns parsed sheets plus power symbols. Sync helpers derive data without re-reading the file:

- `symbolsFromLoaded` (drift, empty-sheet warning)
- `geometryFromLoaded` (legibility, score)
- `pinNetsFromLoaded` (drift PINOUT, constraints)

Public APIs (`listSymbols`, `pinNets`, `readSheetGeometry`) stay as thin async wrappers so existing callers are unchanged.

**Check orchestration** ([`check.ts`](src/commands/check.ts)):

1. `Promise.all` for ERC, DRC, and openspec (when each is configured).
2. One `loadSchematic()` for drift, legibility, score, and forbidden-pin constraints.
3. Log order preserved: parallel results are emitted in ERC → DRC → openspec order after `Promise.all` resolves.

**Legibility + score reuse** ([`legibility.ts`](src/kicad/legibility.ts), [`score.ts`](src/kicad/score.ts), [`tools.ts`](src/agent/tools.ts)):

- `checkLegibilityWithGeometry()` returns `{ report, sheets }`.
- `checkLegibilityFromGeometry()` runs the checker on geometry already in memory.
- `scoreSchematic` and `draft_schematic` call `scoreFromGeometry(sheets, report)` instead of re-reading and re-checking.

**Drift** ([`drift.ts`](src/memory/drift.ts)): optional `LoadedSchematic` parameter on `checkDrift`; `emptySchematicWarning` accepts pre-loaded symbols.

**Small maintainability fixes** (same PR, no behavior change):

- [`openai.ts`](src/agent/providers/openai.ts): lazy-reuse OpenAI client across turns.
- [`tools.ts`](src/agent/tools.ts): `edit_file` / `write_file` descriptions match next-turn unlock policy.
- [`ledger.ts`](src/agent/ledger.ts): remove unused `decision-log` obligation and `onDecision` (`record_decision` already appends synchronously).
- [`constraints.ts`](src/memory/constraints.ts): `Set` for forbidden-pin lookup.

**Invariants preserved**: no sexp serialization; `check` module still does not import providers; spec-gating and verification-gating unchanged; ledger hooks and finish/commit gates unchanged; only tool description text and internal parse reuse changed.

## Spec / OpenSpec

n/a: internal performance refactor and dead-code cleanup. No spec-level behavior change; SPEC.md and OpenSpec artifacts not modified.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| --- | --- | --- |

| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | partial: 767 pass / 5 fail (see note) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | skip (not required for this change) |

**Targeted regression (this PR):** `npx vitest run test/ledger.test.ts test/legibility.test.ts test/sexp.test.ts test/draft-tools.test.ts` — **42/42 pass**.

**Known failures unrelated to this PR:** `init-check` (clean fixture ERC), `gating-sync` (finish after ERC), and `stage-completion` (schematic legibility gate) fail on this machine with KiCad `lib_symbol_mismatch` ERC warnings. The same tests fail on unmodified code (`git stash` baseline), so these are environmental KiCad CLI/version issues, not caused by parse reuse.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): n/a (performance refactor; no new CLI surface)

pulls.title: fix(sync): report a configured schematic that is missing from disk
pulls.body:
## What

`copperhead sync` no longer reports a clean run when `config.schematic` names a file that is not on disk. It reports the missing schematic and exits 2.

## Why

Closes #188. This is the `sync` half; #191 is the `check` half and is already approved. Splitting them because the fix is a different shape in each command, per the review discussion on #191.

Drift and the forbidden-pin constraint check are both gated on the schematic existing, written out twice in [sync.ts](src/commands/sync.ts). When the file is absent the two skip together and nothing else notices, so the command reports clean having verified nothing.

Reproduced on `a2471b3`, with an init-ed repo whose `schematic` points at a path that does not exist:

```text
$ copperhead --repo <sandbox> sync --dry-run
sync: no inconsistencies
exit=0
```

The contrast with `check` on the same repo state (with #191 applied) is the reason this is worth fixing rather than leaving to the exit code of the other command:

```text
check -> exit 1, "schematic configured at hardware/board.kicad_sch but the file is missing"
sync  -> exit 0, "sync: no inconsistencies"
```

## Design

The missing schematic goes into `violations[]`, not `resolvable[]`.

That is the load-bearing decision here, so the reasoning: [cli.ts](src/cli.ts) hands every resolvable item to `syncResolve`, which runs the agent loop against them. A schematic that is not on disk is not something an agent should try to write its way out of, and asking it to would be inviting it to invent one. Restoring the file or correcting the path is a human decision, which is exactly what `violations[]` already means in this command (AC-7.3, "never auto-resolved"). It also produces the right exit code for free, since violations exit 2 before the resolve phase is reached.

`SyncViolationItem['kind']` widens from the single `'requirement-violation'` to a union with `'schematic-missing'`, so the two can be told apart by a caller reading `--json`. The `formatSyncReport` heading is unchanged: "not auto-resolved; human decision needed" is accurate for this case too.

The two guards are resolved once into `schematicUsable`, the same consolidation #191 does in `check.ts`.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. AC-7.3 is preserved and this leans on it: the new item is a violation precisely so it is never auto-resolved.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | targeted, see below | 6 new pass, no regressions |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a |

New: [sync-missing-schematic.test.ts](test/sync-missing-schematic.test.ts), 6 tests, all pass here.

On the parent commit 4 of the 6 fail. The other 2 are the negative controls (no schematic configured, and schematic present), which correctly pass on both sides:

```text
× reports it, where it previously found nothing at all      -> expected [] to have a length of 1
× says the checks did not run, not that nothing was wrong   -> expected 'sync: no inconsistencies' not to be 'sync: no inconsistencies'
× is a violation, not a resolvable item                     -> expected 0 to be greater than 0
× behaves the same when the file is deleted after config    -> expected [] to have a length of 1
✓ stays silent when no schematic is configured
✓ stays silent when the configured schematic is present
```

Regressions: `gating-sync.test.ts` is the only existing suite that exercises `syncVerify`. Ran it on this branch and on the parent and diffed the failing-test lists: 1 failure each, identical, pre-existing in this environment.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox: fixture schematic copied into a fresh git repo, `copperhead init` run, then `.copperhead/config.json` pointed at a path that does not exist.

**Disclosure:** KiCad is not installed on this machine, so `COPPERHEAD_KICAD_CLI` points at a stub that answers `version`, purely to get past preflight. It is never invoked in these runs, because every schematic-reading step is skipped by the condition under test.

```text
$ copperhead --repo /tmp/ch-sync188 sync --dry-run
1 REQUIREMENT VIOLATION(S) (not auto-resolved; human decision needed):
- schematic configured at hardware/board.kicad_sch but the file is missing, so drift and constraint checks did not run
    governed by: .copperhead/config.json
exit=2
```

Control, restoring the file at the configured path and changing nothing else:

```text
$ cp fixture.kicad_sch hardware/board.kicad_sch
$ copperhead --repo /tmp/ch-sync188 sync --dry-run
sync: no inconsistencies
exit=0
```

## Docs

None. The behavior is a report line and an exit code, both shown above. Happy to add the `schematic-missing` kind to the configuration reference if you want the `--json` shape written up.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] N/A **Spec-gated in**: agent tool list untouched.
- [ ] N/A **Verification-gated out**: no mutation or repair path touched. `syncResolve` is unchanged.
- [ ] N/A **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free**: `check.ts` untouched in this PR (that is #191).
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: `src/kicad/` untouched. `pinNets` stays read-only and now takes the already-resolved path.
- [ ] N/A **Sync-obligations ledger**: not touched. This is `commands/sync.ts`, not the agent ledger.
- [ ] N/A **Secrets**: no transcript, summary, or env path touched. The new line contains only a config-relative path.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: no spec-level behavior change; AC-7.3 is relied on rather than modified.

  * Missing schematics are excluded from automatic resolution, including after a configured file is deleted.
  * Sync reports distinguish missing schematics from other requirement violations and explain deferred resolution items.

pulls.title: fix(agent): remove the unreachable decision-log obligation
pulls.body:
## What

Removes `decision-log`, an obligation kind that could never be opened, and adds a structural test so the same shape cannot come back.

## Why

Closes #181.

`decision-log` appeared in exactly three places, none of them a call site:

```
src/agent/ledger.ts:12    | 'decision-log'      <- the type union
src/agent/ledger.ts:87    onDecision(summary)   <- the only producer
src/agent/ledger.ts:88    this.add('decision-log', summary, 'decision');
```

`onDecision` had no callers in `src/` or in the tests, and there was no `clear('decision-log', ...)` anywhere either. Confirmed on `a2471b3` before touching anything:

```
$ grep -rn "decision-log\|onDecision" src/ test/ docs/ *.md
src/agent/ledger.ts:12:  | 'decision-log'
src/agent/ledger.ts:87:  onDecision(summary: string): void {
src/agent/ledger.ts:88:    this.add('decision-log', summary, 'decision');
```

## Design

Removing rather than wiring, matching #177 / #179 for `constraint-dual-write`. Decisions are already recorded: `record_decision` appends to DECISIONS.md and pushes to `ctx.decisions`, so nothing is lost by dropping the kind. Whether a design-editing run *must* record a decision is a policy question, and it should not arrive as a side effect of deleting dead code. Happy to send the wiring instead if you would rather have that invariant.

**Why wiring it naively would have been worse than leaving it.** `changelog` is the working analogue and it needs three pieces:

```
ledger.ts:49   this.add('changelog', ...)                              opened by a hook
loop.ts:712    ctx.ledger.clear('changelog')                            cleared by the commit path
tools.ts:805   openObligations.filter((o) => o.kind !== 'changelog')    excluded from blocking
```

`decision-log` had only the first. Calling `onDecision()` from `record_decision` without the other two would open an obligation nothing could satisfy, and `finish` refuses while any obligation is open, so the run could never complete.

## The test

That trap is the reason this PR adds [ledger-obligations-satisfiable.test.ts](test/ledger-obligations-satisfiable.test.ts) rather than just deleting six lines. It asserts two things over the source:

1. every kind that some `.add(...)` can open is either cleared somewhere or excluded from the blocking set
2. every kind declared in the union has a producer

The first is the one that matters, and it fails on the parent commit naming the exact kind:

```
× every obligation kind that can be opened can also be closed
  → openable but never cleared or excluded: decision-log
```

After this change, the opened set and the cleared set match exactly:

```
added:   affects-revisit changelog constraint-dual-write drc drift erc legibility
cleared: affects-revisit changelog constraint-dual-write drc drift erc legibility
```

It is written in the same style as the existing AC-2.1 module-graph scan, since the property is structural and a scenario test would only find it by stumbling onto the exact hook.

**Coordination note:** #179 removes `constraint-dual-write` from the same union in the same file, so whichever of these lands second will conflict on those adjacent lines. The resolution is trivial (both are pure deletions from the union) and the new test stays correct either way: it reads the union at runtime rather than hardcoding the members. Happy to rebase on top of #179 whenever it lands, or to hold this until it does.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. Nothing could open this obligation, so no run behaves differently.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | targeted, see below | 2 new pass, 9 pre-existing failures unchanged |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a |

New: [ledger-obligations-satisfiable.test.ts](test/ledger-obligations-satisfiable.test.ts), 2 tests, both pass here. Test 1 fails on the parent commit.

Ran every suite that touches the ledger (`budget-efficiency`, `cli-surface`, `create-hardening`, `dossier`, `draft-tools`, `gating-sync`, `ledger`, `legibility`, `safety`) on this branch and on the parent, and diffed the failing-test lists:

```
my branch: 9 failures
parent:    9 failures
diff:      identical
```

Those 9 are pre-existing in this environment (no `kicad-cli` on PATH, plus the known Windows path cases in `cli-surface` and `safety`), and none of them are in `ledger.test.ts`.

### Manual test log (required)

n/a, and deliberately so: this removes a code path that had no callers, so there is no CLI behavior to exercise. The change is proven by the structural test above rather than by a run. `npm run build` passes, which is what confirms nothing referenced the removed method.

## Docs

None. `decision-log` was not mentioned in any doc, only in the three source lines above.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] N/A **Spec-gated in**: agent tool list untouched.
- [ ] N/A **Verification-gated out**: no mutation or repair path touched.
- [ ] N/A **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free**: `src/commands/check` does not reach the ledger.
- [ ] N/A **No sexp serialization**: `src/kicad/` untouched.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: this is the ledger. The hooks that actually fire (`onKicadEdit`, `onDocEdit`, `onConstraintChange`, `onLegibilityResult`) are unchanged, `commit` still refuses while obligations are open, and the new test pins that every openable kind stays closeable.
- [ ] N/A **Secrets**: no transcript, summary, or env path touched.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: no spec-level behavior change, so no SPEC.md or change artifacts move.

pulls.title: Drawing quality: labels inside the frame, text collisions cleared, sheets compacted, passive banks (#220 phases 1, 2, 4 and #233)
pulls.body:
## What

The drawing-quality work from #220 phases 1, 2 and 4, plus the packing levers from #233: edge-facing label text stays inside the frame, the residual text-collision family is cleared by guarded fallbacks, a mostly-empty sheet reflows onto a smaller one, and passive banks chain on one trunk. Plus one connectivity fix the corpus sweep surfaced along the way: the router now treats netless pins as connection points.

Full-corpus error findings, before (branch point e8f9fc0) and after: stickhub 1 to 0 on A2 instead of A1, interf_u 13 to 0 on A3 instead of A1, complex_hierarchy 5 to 0 on A2 instead of A1, cm5_minima 20 to 1, royalblue54L_feather 3 to 1. Every drafted board round-trips exactly.

## Why

#219 measured all three drafting real boards at composite 40, capped by error-severity legibility findings the IR has no lever over. #220 phase 1 closes the out-of-frame half; phase 2 targets the text-collision family (#210's slot-selection half landed earlier in #211); phase 4 is the packing half, where a sheet two sizes above the human's is the finding. #233 folds in the density levers that make those smaller sheets hold. The jetson fix closes a silently-wrong case: a drafted sheet whose netlist differs from the source, which is the one outcome the engine bars.

## Design

Nine commits, each independently verifiable in [engine.ts](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts):

- **Frame fit counts label text** (003e631): the band budget reserves each group's facing-label extents, and the final centering shift clamps against the true extent with label boxes included. Both are no-ops when the sheet has slack, so unbanded layouts do not move.
- **Three text fallbacks** (1569d97), each firing only when the existing passes leave text colliding, so clean boards stay byte-identical:
  - a power-value sweep runs LAST, after labels are final, and moves the one text item with no electrical meaning with the finished sheet as its obstacle set
  - label rides gain a shorten rung (a facing pair in a tight channel can only separate by retreating) and a deeper budget (4 to 8 units, enough to clear the routing channel under a connector)
  - a vertical stub may flip its text to the other side when a parallel trunk blocks every rung; the flip explicitly re-checks the same-point merge case its non-overlapping box would otherwise hide
  - a wired-net label may sit at any interior grid point of its own run, walked along the run's SEGMENTS so a candidate always lies on a wire of its own net
- **Examples refreshed** (8b6499e): the committed side-by-side drafts, regenerated from the runs below.
- **Netless pins guard their point** (489fa53): `touchesForeign` skipped pins the intent names no net for; jetson-agx-thor-baseboard put a wired net's L-corner exactly on such a pin and shipped a merged net past every gate. Pre-existing on this branch, exposed once banding (de5aa02) made the board draft at all. Stricter only; no current board routes through one.
- **Compaction** (3ae5aeb), the packing half of #220 phase 4: two structural causes put drafts on paper sizes above the human's. A layer depth whose parts stack into one full-height column, and a paper pass that accepted the first sheet the natural ribbon fit without asking how much of it was used. Now a too-tall depth splits into side-by-side columns (the vertical analog of banding), and when the natural fit uses less than the checker's 50% utilization floor the paper pass retries smaller sheets, smallest first, with both budgets. Cells never shrink, so density per cell is untouched; only the arrangement changes. Utilization is measured by INK, not bounding box, so an L-shaped layout does not read as full.
- **Remaining frame overhangs** (5ce9ad0): the corpus sweep at the compacted sizes found power VALUE text sliding past its group rect, so the final clamp measures it too.
- **Review fixes** (b322e71): a wired-net label could anchor on no wire at all, because the interior-point fallback walked the run's anchor-sorted POINTS as though the sort had preserved their pairing. Three corpus nets shipped that way, each anchored off every wire of its own run, which leaves the net carrying whatever name KiCad invents rather than the one the IR gave it; the record now carries the run's segments and the walk steps along those. The supply-name fallback is narrowed so an underscore joins a voltage suffix only, keeping measurement nodes named after their supply (`VBUS_DET`, `VCC_SENSE`) as signals. `classifyNet` reports the basis that decided each class, and 1b11551 marks that basis in the report only where it asserts a POWER class from a name, which is the one classification no pin attests. The bank's merge-safety vetoes and the interior walk, which no test reached, are extracted as pure predicates and tested directly.
- **Passive banks and supply names** (ce72222, #233): decap-row parts adjacent on the same power net chain on ONE trunk, a stub per pin with horizontal joins and a single power symbol at the first end, every stub and trunk segment vetoed by the body-crossing, touches-foreign and foreign-stub-line checks so a bank never buys density with a merged net. The decoupling reduction becomes structural (a two-pin part between a rail and ground) rather than a `Device:C` name test, and a supply-named net whose pins are all `passive` classifies as power from its name, which is how stickhub's 80-pin GND stops drafting as 80 labels.

KiCad layer only: the parser stays read-only, the emitted sheet stays a function of the IR alone, and every mechanism is deterministic.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Two engine contracts in [deterministic-schematic-drafting](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-drafting-engine/spec.md) changed with ce72222; b322e71 moves their delta specs to match, and `openspec validate deterministic-schematic-drafting` passes.

- **Deterministic power-net recognition** stated the rule as electrical type or IR declaration only. It now states the three-input precedence (declaration, then pin type, then name), the name shapes and why they are narrow in one direction, and the per-net basis the report must carry so a name-inferred class is distinguishable from an attested one. Two scenarios added: a passive-only supply recognized by name, and a measurement node named after a supply that stays a signal.

## What

Implements the OpenSpec change `add-unresolvable-parts-checkpoint` (all 17 tasks): `create --interactive` now pauses at schematic-stage entry when a BOM part matches no installed symbol (re-check / continue / stop, with nearest-installed candidates), a new `unresolvableParts: 'agent' | 'stop'` config knob gives unattended runs a fail-fast option, and `create`/`demo` finally forward a real TTY confirm callback so the advertised spec-approval gate prompts instead of silently auto-approving.

## Why

Implements the planning artifacts from #222, closing #206: the stage-4 dossier already computes the absence set deterministically before the first agent turn, but its only consumer was the agent, which spent ~12 turns on the lemondrop brief negotiating substitutes a human picks in seconds. This PR is stacked on `worktree-issue-206-human-parts` so it shows only the implementation diff; it should merge after #222.

## Design

Follows the change's [design.md](openspec/changes/add-unresolvable-parts-checkpoint/design.md) decisions D1 to D7:

- **Resolution split from rendering** ([dossier.ts](src/kicad/dossier.ts)): `resolveBomSymbols` returns structured per-part records (resolved / absent / unreadable, plus errored / not-searched / overflow sets and empty-with-reason degrades); `renderDossier` assembles the block. A test proves the composition is byte-identical to the old `bomSymbolDossier`, including under a tight `maxChars`, and the existing render assertions pass unmodified (D2's regression net).
- **The gate** ([parts-gate.ts](src/commands/parts-gate.ts)): fires once per schematic-stage entry, after the resume check, before the attempt loop (D1). It consumes the same classifier the dossier renders from, so the I15 no-false-absence guard carries over: it stops only on a successful resolution with a non-empty genuine absence set; every degrade path (no readable library, timeout, error, missing BOM) proceeds with a warning in both modes (D5). Precedence: interactive pause beats `'stop'` beats `'agent'`; cancel maps to stop (D3, D4). With no prompt and the default `'agent'` policy it short-circuits without resolving anything, so default stage-4 entry is byte-identical to today (no scan, no warning); a test asserts zero scans on that path.
- **Suggestions, not matches** ([symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts)): `nearestInstalledSymbols` qualifies by bounded edit distance or shared family-stem prefix and allows the digit siblings `oneEditFamilyVariant` refuses (D7). Called only from the gate.
- **Stop report** (D6): a stdout block plus best-effort `.copperhead/runs/unresolved-parts.json` (absent parts with candidates, never-checked buckets, the exact resume command), a separate file rather than a mutation of `report.json`'s stable schema, then the canonical failure exit (resume point, cost table, run report, `ok: false`).
- **Confirm plumbing** ([cli.ts](src/cli.ts), [demo.ts](src/commands/demo.ts)): `confirm: confirmTty` and the checkpoint prompt are spread only under `--interactive` AND an attended TTY; off-TTY no callback is forwarded, since `confirmTty` reads stdin without checking TTY and would silently answer "N".

pulls.body:
## What

Adds the OpenSpec change `hierarchical-schematics`: planning artifacts only, no code. It proposes emitting one child sheet per SUBSYSTEMS.md group plus an auto-generated top sheet, and turning stage 4 into a per-sheet draft/validate/repair loop.

## Why

Closes the planning gap for #207. On a 160-part flat sheet (lemondrop), stage 4 spends most of its iteration on symptoms of "everything on one sheet": paper-size escalation, ~40k-token whole-sheet iteration context, whole-sheet blast radius on a late regression (R6/I16), and router pressure from foreign stub columns (#204 class). Past ~200 parts a flat sheet also stops being human-reviewable. The hierarchy is already in the data: every IR part names a `group`, and the engine already computes the in-group versus cross-group net split, so child sheets and sheet pins are derivable with no new model-authored input.

## Design

Decisions H1-H7 in [design.md](openspec/changes/hierarchical-schematics/design.md). Load-bearing ones:

- H1: the partition is the IR's existing `group` field; the only IR addition is a `hints.hierarchy` override.
- H2: hierarchical is a mode behind a configured part-count threshold; flat stays the byte-identical default below it, proven by unchanged flat goldens.
- H3/H4: cross-group nets become hierarchical labels on child sheets and sheet pins on a derived, component-free top sheet.
- H5: UUIDv5 semantic paths gain a sheet qualifier, so untouched sheets stay byte-stable across re-drafts and per-sheet diffs are meaningful.
- H6: stage 4 iterates one sheet at a time; each clean sheet is separately committable, which is the structural fix for the R6/I16 lost-work problem.

pulls.title: test(draft): run the engine against real designs via their KiCad netlists
pulls.body:
## What

Points the drafting engine at real KiCad designs instead of fixtures. Adds an opt-in sweep, [draft-real-corpus.test.ts](test/draft-real-corpus.test.ts), and the netlist reader it runs on, [netlist.ts](test/support/netlist.ts). Tests only, no production source changes, default `npm test` unchanged.

## Why

Every existing draft suite feeds the engine intents we wrote. That makes them good regression tests and poor discovery tests: an intent written to exercise the engine tends to stay inside what the engine already does. Real designs do not. They bring multi-unit opamps, project-local symbol libraries, hierarchies eight sheets deep, and net counts in the hundreds.

This is the corpus half of what [#141](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/issues/141) asks for, applied to drafting rather than layout.

## Design

**Input is the netlist export, not the schematic.** `kicad-cli sch export netlist` makes KiCad flatten the hierarchy, resolve the buses, and name every net before we see it, including the ones the designer never named (`Net-(D15-1)`). Reading the `.kicad_sch` directly would mean re-deriving connectivity, and unnamed nets are the majority on a real board: `interf_u` has 303 of 373 pins on nets with no label. The export is an s-expression, so [sexp.ts](src/kicad/sexp.ts) reads it and no new parser enters the tree.

`libsource` supplies the lib_id and `sheetpath` supplies the group, so the IR extraction is deterministic with no LLM in the loop.

**The contract is not "every board drafts".** Most real boards legitimately will not: the engine refuses multi-unit symbols by design, because a symbol's units share symbol-space pin coordinates and drafting one would silently merge nets. Asserting that every board drafts would just encode the wrong goal.

The contract is the weaker, more important one: draft faithfully or refuse legibly, never silently wrong. Per project, drafting either succeeds or returns findings and never throws; when it succeeds the drawn netlist must partition pins exactly as the source did; when it refuses every finding must carry an attributable detail.

**Comparison is by pin partition, not net name.** What must survive drafting is which pins end up joined to which. Comparing names would also churn against KiCad's auto-naming, which numbers unnamed nets from the first pin it meets and so shifts whenever placement does.

**Nothing is vendored, and the sweep is opt-in.** Gated on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CORPUS=1`, skipped when the corpus is absent, `COPPERHEAD_CORPUS_DIR` to point it elsewhere. The projects are not committed because the interesting ones carry licences a permissive repo cannot redistribute: the one board that currently round-trips clean, stickhub, is CC BY-NC-SA (NonCommercial). Reading them from a local KiCad install redistributes nothing. Of the corpus, only jetson-agx-thor-baseboard and tiny_tapeout (Apache-2.0) and royalblue54L_feather (CERN-OHL-P) would be vendorable, and all three currently refuse, so a vendored tier would start as a known-limitation ledger rather than a suite.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change: tests only, no production source touched.

## Testing

pulls.title: fix(kicad): verify vendored symbols, refuse IR power parts, survive a stale symbol-dir override
pulls.body:
## What

Closes #212.

Fixes the three defects in it: `verify_symbols` no longer misreports the engine's own power symbols, an IR power-port part is refused instead of silently dropped, and a stale `KICAD*_SYMBOL_DIR` no longer disables symbol search entirely.

## Why

All three were found by the post-merge review of #160/#202 and reproduced here against committed fixtures, no live LLM.

**1. Engine-owned power symbols reported as `wrong-library`.** [verifySchematicSymbols](src/kicad/symlib.ts) resolved lib_ids against installed directories only, so the engine's generated `copperhead_power:*` symbols never resolved and the cross-library fallback fuzzy-matched them to whatever stock name looked close:

```
checked=5 skipped=1 findings=4
  [wrong-library] copperhead_power:3V3       -> "use Converter_DCDC:JTD1524S3V3 or Diode:BZV55B3V3 ... instead"
  [wrong-library] copperhead_power:GND       -> "use power:GND or Device:Crystal_GND2 instead"
  [wrong-library] copperhead_power:PWR_FLAG  -> "use power:PWR_FLAG instead"
  [no-library]    copperhead_power:VIN       -> "not installed on this machine; cannot verify its pins"
```

Four confident findings out of six parts, none of them reachable: the IR exposes no lever for power-symbol lib_ids and `edit_file` is refused on a drafted sheet, so stage 4 was handed issues with no legal resolution. That is the deadlock shape of #163.

**2. IR power parts accepted, then dropped.** [validateIntent](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts) accepted a power-port part and the engine filtered it out of every placement path, so it was never placed, never given an endpoint, absent from its own group's member list, and missing from `notes`, while the draft still returned `ok: true`. A model that writes `power:GND` had no signal at all and would keep doing it.

**3. Stale env override disabled search.** [symbolSearchDirs](src/kicad/symlib.ts) tested exclusivity on whether an override was **set**, while its output collects only directories that **exist**. A variable left by an uninstalled or relocated KiCad made those diverge and returned an empty search path. That is not "search nothing", it is "every symbol is absent": `search_symbols`, `symbol_pins`, the dossier, and the recovery fact-check all degrade at once, and stage 3 substitutes parts that never needed substituting.

## Design

**Ordering is the load-bearing decision in defect 1.** A project's `sym-lib-cache/` is discovered by walking up from the schematic (`vendoredCacheDirs`) and appended **after** the installed directories, never before. This function exists to catch a `lib_symbols` entry whose pins have drifted from the real part, so resolving against the cache the entry was copied from would compare a file with itself and report clean forever. Appending means a stock lib_id still verifies against the stock library while a lib_id no installed directory provides falls through to the vendored copy. A test pins this directly: a tampered `Device:R` pin is still caught as `pin-mismatch` in the same pass where the power symbols verify clean.

I took the "teach it about the cache" option over "skip the `copperhead_power` namespace", per the issue's reasoning: it also makes verification work for any library a project vendors, not only the namespace the engine owns today.

`SYM_CACHE_DIR` moved to [symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts) as canonical and is re-exported from [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts), because symlib cannot import the drafting layer without a cycle. No call sites changed.

For defect 2 the part is recorded in `symbols` **before** the refusal is added, so the group and BOM cross-checks below take their existing `isPower` skips and the model gets one finding about one mistake instead of three unrelated-looking ones.

The only invariant this engages is spec coherence, handled in the section below. It changes advisory reporting and IR validation only: no new tool, no change to the gate ordering, no schematic serialization.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Defect 2 is a spec-level change, corrected after review: an earlier version of this description claimed it was not.

The drafting-engine delta spec enumerates exactly which inputs IR validation refuses and named the multi-unit refusal explicitly. The power-port refusal added here belongs in that enumeration, and the spec's "non-power part" phrasing (in the IR shape, the validation list, and the ungrouped-part scenario) presumed power parts may appear in the IR and are merely exempt from grouping, which stopped being true.

Moved together:

- `openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-drafting-engine/spec.md`: the power-port refusal added to the validation enumeration with its rationale, a new `Scenario: Power-port part is rejected`, and the two "non-power part" clauses reworded.
- `openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/tasks.md`: 6.2 reworded to match, 6.2a added for the refusal.
- `openspec/specs/SPEC.md`: unchanged, and deliberately so. It does not describe `schematic.intent.json` or IR validation at all (zero references), so the delta spec is the only artifact that governs this behavior.

`openspec validate deterministic-schematic-drafting` passes: `Change 'deterministic-schematic-drafting' is valid`.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass, 0 new failures (see note) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a, no provider path touched | n/a |

New tests: 14. Five on the stale-override fallback (all-stale, partially-stale where the surviving override still wins, and an override naming a regular file rather than a directory), four on vendored-cache verification (discovery by walking up, clean verification, the non-vacuity guard, and an unvendored/uninstalled lib_id still reported), and one on the power-part refusal beside its sibling multi-unit case. Four more were added after review: the project-root anchor (a foreign cache above a project is not adopted), the maxDepth bound, a `.git` file as a worktree carries it, and an assertion on the reworded no-symbol diagnostic so it cannot silently regress.

**Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR.** This branch was developed on Windows, where 20 tests fail on `main` before any change here: CRLF normalization (the repo has no `.gitattributes`, so committed `.kicad_sch` files check out CRLF while the emitter writes LF) plus a few platform assumptions in the tests themselves. I compared failure sets **by name** before and after rather than counting, so the "0 new failures" claim is independent of that baseline. Those 20 are not addressed here. CI is Linux-only and is green on this PR.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: the committed reference boards under `manual-tests/reference-boards/`, driven through the same entry points the tools use.

Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node -e "verifySchematicSymbols('manual-tests/reference-boards/<board>/reference/<board>.kicad_sch')"
before:  ldo-demo  checked=5 skipped=1 findings=4   (the four bogus findings quoted above)
after:   ldo-demo         checked=9  skipped=0 findings=0
         buck-12v-5v      checked=12 skipped=0 findings=0
         npn-switch       checked=10 skipped=0 findings=0
         usb-atmega-node  checked=17 skipped=0 findings=0

$ node -e "draftSchematic(ldo-demo intent + {ref:PG1, libId:'power:GND'} on the GND net)"
before:  ok = true | PG1 in sheet? false | notes: [] | PG1 absent from its group's members
after:   ok = false | findings = 1
         PG1: "power:GND" is a power-port symbol, which the drafting engine supplies itself. ...

$ node -e "symbolSearchDirs({ KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR: 'C:/definitely/not/here' })"
before:  []
after:   ["C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/share/kicad/symbols"]
$ node -e "symbolSearchDirs({ KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR: <a real isolated dir> })"
after:   [<that dir>]     (exclusivity preserved)
```

Non-vacuity checked by hand as well as in a test: tampering a `Device:LED` pin name in a copy of the reference sheet still reports `pin-mismatch` after the change.

Retention in defect 2 checked by mutation: replacing `symbols.set(p.ref, sym)` with a non-power-only version makes the new test fail with `expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`, confirming the assertion guards the property rather than passing incidentally.

## Docs

None needed. The changes are internal to the symbol layer and the IR validator; no CLI surface, configuration key, or environment variable changed. Behavior is documented in code comments naming #212 at each site.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] **Spec-gated in**: N/A. No change to the tool list or the unlock gate.
- [ ] **Verification-gated out**: N/A. No change to ERC/DRC sequencing, repair cycles, or rollback.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: preserved. The touched modules are pure filesystem reads; no provider, key, or network access added. `vendoredCacheDirs` does bounded `stat` calls only.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: preserved. The parser stays read-only; this PR reads `lib_symbols` and never writes a KiCad file.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A. Not touched.
- [x] **Secrets**: preserved. No new logging, transcript output, or environment reads beyond the existing `KICAD*_SYMBOL_DIR` names.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: the power-port refusal is recorded in the drafting-engine delta spec (validation enumeration, a new scenario, and the reworded "non-power part" clauses) and in `tasks.md` 6.2/6.2a. `openspec validate deterministic-schematic-drafting` passes. `SPEC.md` does not describe the IR, so it correctly does not move.

## Review feedback addressed

CodeRabbit raised three items, all valid and all fixed in the second commit:

- **Major**: `access()` also succeeds on a regular file, so an override naming a file counted as resolved and suppressed the fallback while satisfying no lookup. Now `stat().isDirectory()`, with a regression test.
- **Minor**: the `no-symbol` diagnostic still said "the installed library", which names the wrong file to fix once a vendored library can be the match. Now "installed or vendored symbol library".
- **Nitpick**: the power-part test did not pass `docsDir`, so the BOM and group paths never ran and the "exactly one finding" assertion would have held even without the retention. Real `SUBSYSTEMS.md` and `BOM.md` fixtures added and `docsDir` passed; the mutation check above confirms the assertion now bites.

An automated pr-review pass then raised three more, all valid and all fixed in the third commit:

- **Medium, spec coherence**: the power-port refusal was absent from the delta spec's validation enumeration (which names the sibling multi-unit refusal explicitly), and this description claimed no spec-level change. Spec, scenario, and tasks updated; description corrected above; `openspec validate` passes.
- **Low**: `vendoredCacheDirs` ascended six levels with no project anchor, so a board nested under a directory holding a `sym-lib-cache` adopted that foreign copy, which could let verification borrow another project's evidence and report clean. The walk now stops at the project root (`.git` or `.copperhead`), inclusive; `.git` is matched by existence because a linked worktree stores it as a file. Confirmed by mutation: removing the anchor makes the new test fail with `expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`. The same cause had made an existing test depend on what else lived in the temp tree, fixed by giving its fixture a `.copperhead` marker.
- **Low**: the reworded `no-symbol` diagnostic was asserted by no test, so the inaccurate wording could have come back green. Now asserted, alongside cases for the `maxDepth` bound and the `.git`-as-a-file case.

pulls.title: test(draft): exercise the drafting engine as a component, off the disk path
pulls.body:
## What

Adds a component-level test suite for the schematic drafting engine: [draft-engine-component.test.ts](test/draft-engine-component.test.ts) (35 tests, 71ms) and the harness it runs on, [draft-harness.ts](test/support/draft-harness.ts). Tests only, no production source changes.

## Why

Every existing draft suite reaches the engine through the whole stack: a temp repo, an intent file on disk, a vendored symbol cache, sometimes ERC. Each one opens with the same mkdtemp/cp/rm block (roughly 15 copies across the draft tests), and a failure can come from anywhere in that stack rather than from the geometry under test.

The second gap is coverage shape. [draft-engine.test.ts](test/draft-engine.test.ts), [golden-corpus.test.ts](test/golden-corpus.test.ts), and [draft-reference-boards.test.ts](test/draft-reference-boards.test.ts) each pin a named board to named bytes, which catches regressions on the boards they name. What they cannot say is whether a contract holds for a board nobody wrote a fixture for.

## Design

**The seam.** `draftSchematicPlacement` ([engine.ts:301](src/kicad/draft/engine.ts#L301)) is already pure: `ValidatedIntent` in, placement model out, no filesystem, no clock, no random. What kept it off a component test was `SymbolSource`, which every existing suite feeds through a repo on disk. Under `vendor: false` ([symsource.ts:349](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts#L349)) resolution never writes, so the harness points it at a repo root that deliberately does not exist: the vendored-cache probe is an `existsSync` that simply misses and falls through to the fixture libraries. `place()` and `emitText()` therefore touch no directory the tests own.

One process-wide `SymbolSource` is shared across the file. Resolution is a pure read under `vendor: false` and the instance caches per lib_id, so the four fixture libraries are parsed once for the whole suite rather than once per test.

**Connectivity is read back, not re-derived.** `drawnNets()` is the single helper that writes. It materializes a sheet to a temp file so the production `pinNets` parser reads connectivity back. A test that re-implemented the netlister would only ever agree with itself.

**Point identity is the emitted coordinate.** The placement model carries raw floats: a pin lands at 48.260000000000005 where its neighbour is at 48.26. Both go through `knum` on the way out, so KiCad sees one coordinate and joins them. `pointKey()` compares the way the emitter writes, the same identity the merged-net guard uses and for the same reason. Comparing model floats directly reports a miss that the sheet does not have.

**Organised across boards, not down one.** Five intents (divider, decoupling row, two-MCU link, series RC chain, minimal) crossed with six contracts asserted on all of them:

1. the drawn netlist equals the declared netlist, pin for pin
2. `report.mergedNets` is empty: no two nets share a point
3. every declared part placed exactly once, carrying its value
4. every connected pin on the 1.27 grid
5. every no-connect marker on the pin it belongs to
6. determinism: two placements of one intent are deep-equal

A change that satisfies the reference board by special-casing it fails here on the sibling that was not special-cased.

Two things surfaced while writing this, both worth knowing and neither a bug: a net needs at least two endpoints, so a genuinely single-part board is not expressible (the `minimal` fixture is one part plus its decoupling cap), and `ValidatedIntent.symbols` is keyed by refdes rather than lib_id ([ir.ts:204](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts#L204)).

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change: this adds tests against existing engine contracts and touches no production source. SPEC.md and the change artifacts stay as they are.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (805 passed, 20 skipped, 57 files) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | n/a (not configured locally; this PR adds no LLM-touching test) |

New tests: 35 in [draft-engine-component.test.ts](test/draft-engine-component.test.ts). No changed or deleted tests. No known pre-existing failures.

`npm test` was run with `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=100`: the disk preflight default trips on this machine for environmental reasons unrelated to the change.

### Manual test log (required)

The change touches no CLI surface, agent loop, provider, or KiCad-layer source, so there is nothing new to exercise by hand at the CLI. What is worth recording instead is the check that the new contracts are not vacuous: the engine was mutated twice, the suite run against each mutation, and the engine restored byte-identical to HEAD afterwards (`git diff src/` empty).

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): n/a, tests-only change
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ sed -i 's/^const STUB = 2;$/const STUB = 2.5;/' src/kicad/draft/engine.ts
$ npx vitest run test/draft-engine-component.test.ts
  x 'seriesChain' > lands every connected pin on the 1.27 grid
  Tests  1 failed | 34 passed (35)
  -> off-grid stub length caught by the grid contract

$ # restored, then: stub labels nudged 1.27mm off their anchor (engine.ts:1259)
$ npx vitest run test/draft-engine-component.test.ts
  x 'divider'  > draws exactly the declared netlist, pin for pin
  x 'twoMcu'   > draws exactly the declared netlist, pin for pin

  AssertionError: expected Map{ 'J1.1' => 'VCC', ...(11) } to deeply equal ...
  -   "R1.1" => "SIG_IN",     +   "R1.1" => null,
  -   "R1.2" => "DIV",        +   "R1.2" => null,
  -   "R2.1" => "DIV",        +   "R2.1" => null,

$ git diff --stat src/kicad/draft/engine.ts
```

Partial fix for #210 (harness I23).

## Why

pulls.title: fix(draft): labelled stubs avoid foreign contact; name wire merges for what they are
pulls.body:
Closes the third face of #204 (harness I22), found live by lemondrop attempt-06.

## Why

A cap-to-ground drop (`BUCK_SS`: U1.9 → C9.1, with C9.2 on GND) places the cap below the pin's stub axis. After #205, the wired route through the neighbouring power-pin row is correctly vetoed — but the labelled fallback then draws the cap's 2-unit stub unconditionally, and its endpoint lands exactly on that power pin's stub interior: the same KiCad endpoint-on-interior join, one pass further down. The agent burned two stage-attempts on it, partly because the finding was rendered with the label-co-location message ("share a label position... both labels were immovable"), which describes a different fault and steered the diagnosis wrong.

## What

1. The trunk veto's foreign-contact check is extracted into a shared `touchesForeign()`, and the labelled-stub fallback uses it: a stub whose endpoint would rest on a foreign wire or connection point grows one grid unit at a time (bounded at +2) until the endpoint clears — the stub's interior then crosses the foreign wire mid-segment, which does not connect. If no length clears, the plain stub is emitted and the merged-net gate refuses loudly rather than shipping the contact.
2. Merged-net findings carry `via: 'labels' | 'wires'` and wire-contact merges get their own message naming the mechanism, so agents (and humans) stop diagnosing routing faults as label-placement faults.
3. Drops the `COPPERHEAD_DEBUG_VETO` instrumentation that slipped into #205.

pulls.title: fix(draft): never route through a foreign connection point; gate wire-level net merges
pulls.body:
Closes #204 (harness I22).

## What

Router foreign-contact avoidance, net-aware chain clearance with a bounded lift, and a wire-level merged-net gate; goldens regenerated from the fixed engine.

## Why

The trunk-and-branch router could route a local net's trunk down a column of neighbouring stub ends: its first candidate is the median stub-end x, which for a net with pins on one symbol side IS the stub/label column, and its only veto was wire-through-body. KiCad joins a wire endpoint resting on another wire's interior, so the geometry silently merged nets, and ERC demotes `multiple_net_names` to a warning. The lemondrop attempt-05 run shipped its crystal drive shorted onto TOUCH_IRQ this way and the stage-4 agent disproved four intent-level repair hypotheses before correctly refusing to certify.

Three layers, so the class dies rather than the instance:

1. **Router avoidance**: candidates are rejected on contact with any foreign connection point (pin, predicted stub end, or already-emitted foreign wire). Falls through candidates to the labelled fallback, which cannot merge.
2. **Chain-pass hardening**: `axisClear` also rejects a horizontal foreign stub segment crossing the axis exactly at a connection row of a different net (net-aware; `ownEps` is too coarse for this case), and chain drops retry with a bounded lift instead of parking a lead on an occupied row.
3. **Gate**: `findWireContactMerges` detects cross-net wire contact (endpoint-on-interior, shared endpoints, label anchored on a foreign wire) and feeds the existing merged-net refusal, so no future pass can ship such geometry silently.

## The goldens contained the defect

- `tierC-board.kicad_sch` had **DIV shorted to GND** at R2.2's stub end (its "clean" ERC was `lib_symbol_issues` noise, connectivity never really evaluated).
- The pull-up idiom fixture tied the pulled SIG node to VCC through U1.1's power stub crossing R1's bottom lead row.

pulls.title: feat(kicad): pin dossier at stage-4 entry, symbol_pins tool, stage-3 drawability check
pulls.body:
Closes #201. Targets `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting`.

**Stacking note:** this branch is the full symbol-discovery lineage rebased onto the cross-library resolution base: it carries #186's merge (`fd1a14c`, `6e3442b` — currently local-only on the base branch, so they appear in this diff until the base is pushed) and the rebased #198 commits (`761e001`, `5f08bc4`). Merging this makes PR #198's branch redundant. The new work is the last two commits.

## What

1. **Pin dossier at stage-4 entry** — every BOM part resolved against the installed libraries before the schematic agent's first turn, injected into the stage prompt: top lib_id, real pin table (number=name/type), MULTI-UNIT flag, alternative candidates, explicit NO-INSTALLED-SYMBOL lines. Recomputed per stage attempt; size-capped with named overflow; degrades to no block on any error, and yields **no** dossier when no library is readable — "could not check" must never render as "checked and absent".
2. **`symbol_pins` tool** — pins + unit count for a lib_id, following `extends`; misses answer with in-library closest names and cross-library matches; warns on multi-unit symbols (the drafting engine refuses them).
3. **Stage 3 is instructed to confirm drawability, not just existence** — the prompt directs a `symbol_pins` single-unit check before a BOM row commits (prompt strength only: the stage completion gate is unchanged, as the delta spec states), closing the `SN74LVC2G17` → `PESD5V0L4UG` exists-but-refused trap that burned a stage-attempt.
4. **Rebase reconciliation** (`ef194d7`) — with #186's `found-elsewhere` outcome in the union type, two #198-era callers (`symbolAvailabilityFacts`, `symbol_pins`) rendered a *located* part as "not installed"; both now report the located lib_ids. The #186 Windows-discovery tests also asserted against only fixture dirs and failed on any machine with a real KiCad install; assertions now filter to the fixture root.

Merge-resolution choices, for review: one shared library lister (`listInstalledLibraries`) replaces `allLibraryFiles`; same-file candidates use the shared ranked `closestSymbolNames` (sub-unit filtered, no single-letter garbage) inside #186's evidence ordering (same-file first, cross-library only when the file offers nothing, fuzzy weaker than exact); `findSymbolAcrossLibraries` keeps its edit-distance guard (`SHT40`→`SHT4x` catchable, `TPS22860`≠`TPS22810`).

## Why

Measured on the lemondrop harness runs (#201): the best stage-4 run to date spent ~15 of 19 turns (~10 of 15 minutes) paging raw `.kicad_sym` geometry to recover pin names, and an earlier attempt probed drafts with deliberately bogus pins to make the validator echo the real pin lists. pulls.title: chore(pr-review): run reviews in an isolated git worktree
pulls.body:
## What

`/pr-review` no longer touches the checkout you are working in. It parks the PR head in a throwaway detached `git worktree` under `$TMPDIR`, runs the diff reading, the suite, and coverage there, and removes it when the report is posted. `gh pr checkout` is gone from the skill.

## Why

The skill's step 1 ran `gh pr checkout <n>`, which moves HEAD in the user's own tree. Reviewing a PR is read-only work, but that command is not: it can refuse over uncommitted changes, it strands the user on someone else's branch when the review ends, and if the review is running in the background it can swap the tree out from under an unrelated edit in progress. A worktree gives the review its own working directory over the same object store, so the main checkout is never entered.

## Design

New helper [worktree.mjs](.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs) with `setup` / `path` / `cleanup` / `cleanup --all`, plus [worktree.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/references/worktree.md) for the details. Load-bearing decisions:

- **Fetch into a private ref**: `+refs/pull/<n>/head:refs/pr-review/<n>`. That ref form resolves for fork PRs too, and the private namespace means no branch the user has (or could check out) is ever moved.
- **Detached worktree**: a worktree cannot check out a branch already checked out elsewhere, and detaching sidesteps that case entirely. Path is `$TMPDIR/pr-review-worktrees/<repo>-<hash-of-main-path>/pr-<n>`, so two clones of the same repo do not collide.
- **The directory name avoids the `copperhead-` prefix**, and this is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: `sweepStaleTempDirs` in [tmp.ts](src/util/tmp.ts) recursively removes `$TMPDIR/copperhead-*` past a staleness cutoff, and [tmp-sweep.test.ts](test/tmp-sweep.test.ts) exercises it against the real temp dir with a 60s cutoff. The first prototype used `copperhead-pr-review/` and the suite deleted the review worktree mid-run, which took the run's own results with it (see the manual log below).
- **Dependencies**: `node_modules` is symlinked from the main checkout, so the suite runs with no install and nothing is ever written into it. When the PR changes `package-lock.json`, `setup` says so and `--install` gives the worktree a real `npm ci`, because otherwise the suite result describes the wrong dependency set.
- **Re-runnable**: an existing worktree at the PR head is reused, a clean one behind the head is fast-forwarded, and one with local modifications is left alone with a note rather than silently discarded.
- **`.env` and other untracked files deliberately do not carry over.** Secrets stay in the main checkout, and the review path (the offline suite, `check`/`verify`) is contractually key-free.

[metrics.mjs](.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/metrics.mjs) gains `--dir <path>` so the whole measurement (git reads, vitest, coverage) happens in the worktree, and its head detection now compares commits instead of branch names: a detached worktree at the PR head was previously reported as "head branch not checked out", which silently downgraded the report to diff-only. It also states the directory and commit it measured, so a report can show its own isolation. Two smaller fixes in the `--base-tests` path: the `node_modules` symlink is guarded on existence, and the symlink is unlinked before the temp worktree is deleted so the removal cannot recurse into the main checkout's `node_modules`.

[SKILL.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) gets a "working-tree isolation" rule that names the forbidden commands (`gh pr checkout`, `git checkout` / `switch` / `stash` / `reset`), a step 0 that creates the worktree, a step 7 that tears it down, and the rule that the skill's own scripts are always run from the main checkout so a PR editing `.claude/skills/pr-review/` cannot review itself with its own modified tooling. Findings still quote repo-relative paths, never worktree paths.

The `gh pr checkout` line inside [fix-prompt.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/references/fix-prompt.md) stays: that block runs in the PR author's own tree, where checking the branch out is the point.

## Spec / OpenSpec

n/a: tooling under `.claude/`, no change to product behavior, `src/`, or any acceptance criterion.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | n/a (no `src/` or `test/` change) |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (no `src/` or `test/` change) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass, run through the new path: 577 passed / 20 skipped / 0 failed |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass (0 issues across the skill's 5 markdown files) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a |

No new automated tests: the repo's vitest suite covers `src/`, and the skill's scripts (including the existing `metrics.mjs`) have no test harness. The scripts were exercised by hand against a real PR instead, logged below.

### Manual test log (required)

Exercised against PR #193 with the main checkout sitting dirty on `chore/pr-review-worktree` throughout. `git status` in the main checkout was identical before and after every command.

```text
$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs setup 193
pr: #193 fix-doctor-openspec-check -> main (fork)
head: cabf483ecc299817b287b16280ee171824bb168b
note: node_modules symlinked from the main checkout (read-only use; nothing is installed into it)
main checkout untouched: /home/animesh/.../copperhead stays on its current branch
worktree: /tmp/pr-review-worktrees/copperhead-9b96eb38/pr-193
(3.2s, fork PR resolved via refs/pull/193/head)

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs setup 193   # idempotence
note: reused the existing review worktree (already at the PR head)

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs path 999    # missing worktree
no review worktree for PR #999 (run: worktree.mjs setup 999)     # exit 1

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/metrics.mjs 193 --dir /tmp/pr-review-worktrees/.../pr-193
lines: +34 / -2 (net 32) across 2 files  ·  src +34/-2, ...
tests: +0 test lines; suite not measured -> 577/20/0 (pass/skip/fail, base -> head)
diff coverage: 44% of changed executable src lines exercised (11/25, measured via vitest v8);
  uncovered: src/commands/doctor.ts:113-126
ci: 4 pass / 0 fail / 0 pending
measured in: /tmp/pr-review-worktrees/.../pr-193 (review worktree; the user's checkout was not entered)
(suite and coverage ran in the worktree; the head was correctly detected as checked out,
 which is the case the old branch-name comparison got wrong)

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/metrics.mjs 193 --dir <wt> --base-tests
tests: +0 test lines; suite 577/20/0 -> 577/20/0 (pass/skip/fail, base -> head)
(base suite ran in its own temp worktree off the merge base, no tree switched)

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs setup 193 --install
note: ran npm ci in the worktree (its own node_modules, isolated from the main checkout)
$ (cd <wt> && npx vitest run test/tmp-sweep.test.ts)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # vitest resolves against the worktree's own install

$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs cleanup 193
removed: /tmp/pr-review-worktrees/copperhead-9b96eb38/pr-193
deleted refs: refs/pr-review/193
$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs cleanup 193   # idempotent
removed: nothing (no review worktree for PR #193)
$ node .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/worktree.mjs cleanup --all
deleted refs: refs/pr-review/74, refs/pr-review/120, ... (9 stale refs the old metrics.mjs left behind)
$ git worktree list
/home/animesh/.../copperhead  <sha> [chore/pr-review-worktree]    # only the main tree left
```

Failure mode found and fixed during this manual run: with the first naming scheme (`$TMPDIR/copperhead-pr-review/...`), `test/tmp-sweep.test.ts` swept the review worktree's contents while the suite was running inside it. The visible damage was a wrong result rather than an error: the suite reported 331 passed / 52 failed instead of 577 / 0, and the base-suite step then failed because git could no longer resolve the emptied worktree. Renaming the base directory out of the `copperhead-` prefix fixes it, and the rerun above is clean.

## Docs

`references/worktree.md` (new), `references/metrics.md` (running instructions, head-detection note, manual fallback), `SKILL.md` (isolation rule, steps 0 and 7, version 2.2). No user-facing product docs affected.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: N/A, no change to the agent tool list.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: N/A, no change to the mutation path.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: N/A, `src/` untouched.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: N/A, `src/kicad/` untouched.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, no change to hooks or commit gating.
- [x] **Secrets**: no key is read or written; the worktree deliberately does not carry `.env` over from the main checkout, and it lives outside the repo so nothing it holds can be committed.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: N/A, no spec-level behavior changed.

pulls.title: fix(kicad): rank symbol candidates usefully, add cross-library search_symbols, fact-check availability refusals
pulls.body:
Fixes #195, #196, #197. Targets `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting` (#160), since [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts) only exists on that branch.

## What

Symbol discovery becomes navigable and refusals about missing symbols become checkable:

1. Near-miss candidate lists are ranked and separator-insensitive, so a failed probe points at the real symbol instead of at `C, D, R`.
2. A new `search_symbols` tool searches every installed library, and stage 3 must run it on every active part before the BOM commits.
3. Before the recovery supervisor judges a failed stage, every lib_id named in the failure is re-probed against the installed libraries and the results are injected as ground truth.

## Why

One harness run produced all three defects: `create` driven end to end on a granular-synth brief (`copperhead-test-harness/run-logs/2026-08-07T17-52-03/attempt-01/`), where stage 4 refused claiming the machine's symbol library is "reduced" and the recovery supervisor aborted on that claim. The machine had the full 222 library stock set installed. Four of the six refused subsystem blocks were installed under names or libraries the agent could not discover, and the refusal's "verified absent" list was contradicted by the validator's own candidate output earlier in the same run.

The three issues are the three links in that chain: bad candidates (#195) hide the real symbol, no cross-library search (#196) makes a wrong nickname look like a missing part, and an unchecked refusal (#197) turns that into an abort.

### 1. Candidate ranking, [symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts) (#195)

Both resolvers printed near-miss lists with two failure modes, seen verbatim in the run:

- `"Device:Rotary_Encoder" does not exist, closest: C, D, R`. The reverse-substring test let single-letter generics match any long query, while `RotaryEncoder_Switch` sat one underscore away, unmatched.
- `closest: TLV320AIC23BPW, TLV320AIC23BPW_0_1, TLV320AIC23BPW_1_1, ...`. Sub-unit children diluted 5 of 8 slots.

`closestSymbolNames` now matches case- and separator-insensitively (`microSD_Card` finds `Micro_SD_Card`), excludes sub-unit children, requires a name to carry at least 3 significant characters before it may match inside the query, and ranks exact, then prefix, then contains, then contained. One shared implementation replaces the two divergent copies in [symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts) and [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts).

### 2. `search_symbols` and the stage-3 requirement, [tools.ts](src/agent/tools.ts) + [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) (#196)

Three of the last four harness briefs died in stage 4 on parts committed at stage 3 with no installed symbol: the first existence check ran three committed stages too late, after the pin map was doc truth. `search_symbols` searches every installed library and returns ranked `Lib:Name` lib_ids, exact matches first. The stage-3 prompt now requires probing every active part with it before the BOM commits, and states the invariant: stage 4 draws only from installed symbols.

This complements #186 (resolver-level cross-library fallback). That fixes the probe's error path; this gives the agent a discovery primitive before anything commits.

### 3. Refusal fact-checking, [recovery.ts](src/agent/recovery.ts) (#197)

`symbolAvailabilityFacts` extracts every lib_id named in the failure text and transcript excerpt (capped at 8, file:line refs and engine-generated power symbols filtered out), re-probes each against the installed libraries, and injects the results into the diagnosis prompt as ground truth, with an instruction that an agent's claim of an absent symbol is not evidence. It costs no LLM turn and never throws: a probe error degrades to reporting what it could.

In the recorded run, the fabricated "Audio and Isolator libraries entirely absent" claim would have arrived alongside `Audio:TLV320AIC23BPW: RESOLVES on this machine (28 pins)`, turning an environmental abort into a retry with the correct lib_ids in the guidance.

## Design

- The candidate ranker is pure and synchronous, so both resolvers and the cross-library search share one ordering, and the sub-unit filter is a name-shape test (`_<unit>_<style>`) rather than a parse: [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts) scrapes names with a regex and has no symbol tree to consult at that point.
- `search_symbols` is `requiresUnlock: false`. It is read-only over the machine's libraries and writes nothing, so it does not touch the spec gate.
- The fact block is deterministic and provider-free. It runs before `diagnoseStageFailure` and is passed in as data, so the supervisor's judgment is the only LLM step and the facts it judges from cannot be hallucinated.
- No KiCad file is written or serialized anywhere in this change: all three paths read `.kicad_sym` text.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No delta spec is updated by this PR, and the invariant checkbox below is left unchecked for a reviewer's call rather than claimed. The judgment: the `deterministic-schematic-drafting` agent-core delta enumerates tool-list additions (it has a paragraph for `check_legibility`), so `search_symbols` arguably belongs there as a sibling sentence. Happy to add it in this PR if a reviewer agrees. The candidate ranking and the refusal fact check are behavior-preserving quality fixes to existing paths and do not read as spec-level.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass, `copperhead --version` prints 0.9.0 |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass, 728 passed / 20 skipped (53 files) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip, not configured in this environment (19 of the 20 skips) |

New tests in [symlib.test.ts](test/symlib.test.ts) use the run's real strings as fixtures: the `C, D, R` case, the sub-unit dilution case, the `TPS61165DBV` in `Driver_LED` wrong-nickname case, and a fact check of the recorded refusal's exact claims (one false, one wrong-library).

One pre-existing expectation was updated: `R` is no longer suggested for `Device:R_Nonexistent`, which was the garbage-match behavior under fix. That test now asserts the opposite, and a new sibling test covers the legitimate near-miss (`Device:R_Smal` still suggests `R_Small`). No unrelated pre-existing failures.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: none. All three changed paths are deterministic and provider-free, so they were exercised directly against this machine's real installed libraries rather than through a sandbox run: KiCad 10.0.4, Node v24.18.0, 222 libraries in `/usr/share/kicad/symbols`. The live stage-3 prompt change is the one part not re-run here; its evidence is the recorded harness run cited above.

`search_symbols` through its real tool handler, including the three wrong-nickname parts from the run and a genuine miss:

```text
$ search_symbols TPS61165DBV
installed symbols matching "TPS61165DBV":
  - Driver_LED:TPS61165DBV

$ search_symbols AudioJack3
installed symbols matching "AudioJack3":
  - Connector_Audio:AudioJack3
  - Connector_Audio:AudioJack3_Ground
  - Connector_Audio:AudioJack3_Switch
  - Connector_Audio:AudioJack3_SwitchT

$ search_symbols TLV320AIC23BPW
installed symbols matching "TLV320AIC23BPW":
  - Audio:TLV320AIC23BPW

$ search_symbols NotAPartAnywhere123
no installed symbol matches "NotAPartAnywhere123" (searched every library in:
/usr/share/kicad/symbols). The part is not capturable on this machine as named,
choose a part whose symbol exists, or a same-family variant that does.
```

The candidate list for the exact lib_id that produced `closest: C, D, R`, now resolved against the real `Device` library:

```text
$ resolveLibrarySymbol("Device:Rotary_Encoder")
{"status":"no-symbol","candidates":["RotaryEncoder","RotaryEncoder_Switch","RotaryEncoder_Switch_MP"]}
```

`symbolAvailabilityFacts` on the recorded refusal's own text, including its `create.ts:311` reference to confirm file:line refs are not probed:

```text
$ symbolAvailabilityFacts("Stage 4 refused: this machine has a reduced symbol library.
  The Audio and Isolator libraries are entirely absent; Audio:TLV320AIC23BPW and
  Isolator:PC817 could not be found, and Device:Rotary_Encoder does not exist (create.ts:311).")

- Audio:TLV320AIC23BPW: RESOLVES on this machine (28 pins)
- Isolator:PC817: RESOLVES on this machine (4 pins)
- Device:Rotary_Encoder: not in that library (closest in that library: RotaryEncoder,
  RotaryEncoder_Switch, RotaryEncoder_Switch_MP); installed as: Device:RotaryEncoder,
  Device:RotaryEncoder_Switch, Device:RotaryEncoder_Switch_MP
```

That is the block the supervisor would have judged the abort against: both "entirely absent" libraries resolve, and the third claim is a real miss with the correct name attached.

## Docs

None. No README, configuration reference, or CHANGELOG entry is affected: the change adds one agent tool and tightens two internal code paths.

Note for reviewers: this conflicts lightly with #186 in [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts) and [symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts), since both touch the candidate path. Whichever lands second rebases the candidate call onto the shared `closestSymbolNames`.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: unchanged. `search_symbols` is read-only and registered with `requiresUnlock: false`; `edit_file`/`write_file` gating is untouched.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: unchanged. No mutation path, repair cycle, or rollback is touched.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: unchanged. Nothing reachable from [check.ts](src/commands/check.ts) is modified; the new code lives in the agent tool list, the recovery supervisor, and `symlib`, and reads only local library files.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: all three paths read `.kicad_sym` text and never write or round-trip a KiCad file.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: unchanged. No hook, obligation, or commit gate is touched.
- [x] **Secrets**: unchanged. No new transcript writer or environment read; the fact block contains only lib_ids and pin counts.
- [ ] **Spec coherence**: see the Spec / OpenSpec section. No delta spec updated; reviewer's call whether the `search_symbols` tool addition needs a line in the `deterministic-schematic-drafting` agent-core delta.

pulls.title: refactor(tool-protocol): update protocol to support multiple JSON object replies and clarify usage instructions
pulls.body:
## What

CLI providers (`claude-code`, `cursor`) may now emit one or more JSON tool calls in a single reply. The text tool protocol no longer contradicts the workflow's batching guidance, so independent reads and similar calls can share one turn.

## Why

Closes #192.

pulls.title: fix(doctor): catch a missing openspec CLI before spec-seed burns real tokens on it
pulls.body:
## What

`copperhead doctor` now checks whether the `openspec` CLI is present on PATH, alongside its existing node/kicad-cli/git/provider checks.

## Why

Closes #190.

`doctor` previously reported `ready` even when `openspec` was completely missing. The failure only surfaced later, inside the `spec-seed` stage, when `validate_change` tried to shell out to `openspec` and failed, after real turns and tokens were already spent. Confirmed this cost roughly 70 minutes and 54.7k output tokens across two real runs before the root cause was clear.

## Design

Adds `openspecCheck`, following the exact same pattern as `kicadCheck` and `gitCheck`: a `DoctorDeps.openspecVersion` probe, wired into `defaultDeps()`, added to the `checks` array in `runDoctor` right after `gitCheck`.

One additional Windows-specific bug found and fixed while testing: `openspec` installed via `npm install -g` (the standard install path the check's own hint recommends) resolves to an `.cmd` shim on Windows, not a real `.exe`. Node's `execFile` cannot run `.cmd` files directly without `shell: true`, so the naive probe (matching `gitVersion`'s exact pattern) false-negatived even when `openspec` was genuinely installed and working from a real shell. Using `shell: true` with an args array also triggers Node's `DEP0190` deprecation warning, so the command is folded into a single string with an empty args array instead, avoiding both issues.

Does not touch spec-gating, verification-gating, or any mutation path; this is a read-only diagnostic addition, same category as the existing checks.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | not run (no test file added for this check yet) |

```text
$ node dist/cli.js doctor

               pipeline need it.

$ npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec
$ node dist/cli.js doctor

```

Both states confirmed directly: fail when genuinely absent, pass with the correct version string once installed. Also confirmed the Windows `.cmd` shim fix specifically, the naive `execFile` probe false-failed even with `openspec` installed and working from a real shell, until `shell: true` (folded into a single command string to avoid the `DEP0190` warning) was added.
