pulls.title: fix(check): fail when the configured schematic is missing, and say which file
pulls.body:
## What

`copperhead check` no longer exits 0 when `config.schematic` points at a file that does not exist, and the message names the missing path instead of claiming the schematic is not configured.

## Why

Refs #188 (does not close it).

The issue's Scope section also names [sync.ts](src/commands/sync.ts) lines 43 and 133, which carry the same guard. Those are deliberately not in this PR: `syncVerify` has no `ok` boolean, and its resolvable items are handed to an LLM resolve phase, so a missing schematic needs different handling there (a violation, which is never auto-resolved) rather than the same one-line treatment. Follow-up PR, not a line in this one.

ERC, drift and the forbidden-pin constraint check all gate on the same `config.schematic && existsSync(...)` condition, written out three times in [check.ts](src/commands/check.ts). When the file is absent all three skip together, `ok` is computed with `?? true` for the skipped checks, and the run reports green. A repo that was configured to be checked and quietly stopped being checked looked exactly like one that passed everything. In CI that is a green build, and [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) calls `runCheck` too.

The message pointed the wrong way as well. Both arms of the guard logged `no schematic configured; run copperhead init`, but the schematic *is* configured: the fix is to correct the path or restore the file, not to re-run `init`.

Reproduced before changing anything. The two cases were byte-identical:

```text
### A. schematic configured at hardware/missing-board.kicad_sch, file absent
  ok = true
  log: ERC skipped (no schematic configured; run copperhead init)

### B. no schematic configured
  ok = true
  log: ERC skipped (no schematic configured; run copperhead init)
```

## Design

The three copies of the guard are resolved once into `schematicUsable` and `schematicMissing`, so the condition cannot drift between the three checks that share it.

The two skips are now split, and treated differently on purpose:

- `config.schematic` unset: skip, keep the existing message, stay green. There is genuinely nothing to verify and `init` has not run, so this is unchanged.
- `config.schematic` set but absent: name the path, do not mention `init`, and fail.

`ok` gains an explicit `schematicMissing === null` term rather than relying on the `?? true` defaults. Those defaults are correct for a check that had nothing to run, but they cannot distinguish "nothing to verify" from "everything to verify, silently skipped".

I picked fail over adding a not-verified state, per the two options in the issue. Failing is what makes CI notice, and the new `schematicMissing` field still lets a caller tell this apart from a real ERC or drift failure. Happy to switch it to a distinct state if you would rather not change the exit code for existing repos.

**Coordination note:** #154 adds a fourth copy of the same `config.schematic && existsSync(...)` guard for `verifySchematicSymbols`. Whichever of these lands second will want to use the shared `schematicUsable` instead of re-testing. Not a blocker either way, just flagging it so the guard does not go back to being duplicated.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change, but the check result gains a key, so the AC-2.4 stable-JSON-keys assertion in [init-check.test.ts](test/init-check.test.ts) moves with it. The key set goes from six to seven with `schematicMissing`, which is `null` on every existing path.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 560 pass / 22 fail / 20 skip, all 22 pre-existing (see below) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | n/a |

New tests: [check-missing-schematic.test.ts](test/check-missing-schematic.test.ts), 5 cases. All 5 pass here.

On the parent commit, 4 of the 5 fail behaviourally. The fifth ("leaves a repo with no schematic configured green and unchanged") fails there only because `schematicMissing` is `undefined` rather than `null`; its behavioural assertions already pass on the parent, which is the point of it being in the file.

Pre-existing failures: the 22 are unrelated to this change. I ran `test/init-check.test.ts` on this branch and on the parent with the same command and got the identical 3 failures both times (`clean fixture`, `broken schematic`, `fab export`), all with root cause `kicad-cli not found on PATH` in this environment. The remaining failures are in `preflight`, `repl`, `safety`, `cli-surface`, `kicad-cli-resolve`, `bootstrap`, `runmeta`, `gating-sync` and `create-hardening`, none of which this PR touches.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: hand-built minimal repo (one `.kicad_sch`, git-init'd, `.copperhead/config.json` written by hand), since the case under test is a *missing* schematic.

**Disclosure:** KiCad is not installed on this machine, so the `kicad-cli` preflight refused to start `check` at all. I set `COPPERHEAD_KICAD_CLI` to a stub that answers `version` so preflight passes. The stub is never invoked by either case below, because both skip ERC and DRC before reaching it. It only gets the command past preflight.

```text
$ copperhead --repo /tmp/ch-manual188 check
# config: { "schematic": "hardware/board.kicad_sch", "board": null }, file absent
ERC skipped: schematic configured at hardware/board.kicad_sch but the file is missing
DRC skipped (no board configured)
exit=1

$ copperhead --repo /tmp/ch-manual188 check
# config: { "schematic": null, "board": null }
ERC skipped (no schematic configured; run copperhead init)
DRC skipped (no board configured)
exit=0

$ copperhead --repo /tmp/ch-manual188 check --json
# config: { "schematic": "hardware/board.kicad_sch", "board": null }, file absent
{
  "ok": false,
  "erc": null,
  "drc": null,
  "drift": { "ok": true, "mismatches": [] },
  "openspec": null,
  "constraints": { "ok": true, "violations": [] },
  "schematicMissing": "hardware/board.kicad_sch"
}
exit=1
```

## Docs

None. The change is a message and an exit code, both covered above. Say the word if you want the `schematicMissing` field written up in the configuration reference.

- [ ] N/A **Verification-gated out**: no mutation path touched.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: the change is a filesystem existence test and a boolean. No new imports; [check.ts](src/commands/check.ts) still reaches no provider, key, or network. The AC-2.1 module-graph test passes.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: `src/kicad/` untouched. `pinNets` is still read-only, and now receives the already-resolved path.
- [ ] N/A **Sync-obligations ledger**: not touched.
- [ ] N/A **Secrets**: no transcript or summary path touched. The new log line contains only a config-relative path.

Closes #180.

## What

Strengthen the deterministic dual-write audit performed by `copperhead sync` for constraints documented in `docs/SPEC.md`.

Instead of relying on substring matching, the sync verifier now parses the `## Budgets` section in `SPEC.md` and reconciles it against `.copperhead/constraints.json`, reporting missing or mismatched entries in either direction.

## Why

- parses documented budgets from the `## Budgets` section,

- reports registry entries missing from `SPEC.md`,
- reports documented budgets missing from the registry,

pulls.title: fix(kicad): find symbols across libraries, not just the guessed file
pulls.body:
Closes #185. Targets `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting` rather than `main`, since `src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts` only exists on that branch: the diff here is the single commit on top of #160.

## What

Symbol resolution now searches across libraries before giving up, instead of only opening the one file named in the `lib_id`.

## Why

Driving `create` end to end on `examples/medium/esp32-soil-sensor.md`, stage 4 reported four real parts as "library not installed and not vendored" and burned two full turn budgets on them. Three of the four were in the stock KiCad library the whole time, filed under a library nickname the caller could not have derived from the part number:

| Part | lib_id used | Actually in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TPS63900 | `Regulator_DCDC:` | `Regulator_Switching` |
| SHT40 | `Sensor_Humidity:SHT40` | `Sensor_Humidity`, as `SHT4x` |
| FDC1004 | `Sensor:` | `Sensor_Proximity` |
| TPS22860 | `Power_Switch:` | genuinely absent from the stock set |

`resolveLibrarySymbol` and `SymbolSource.resolve` both split the lib_id at the colon and opened only that file, so a wrong library nickname was indistinguishable from a missing part. The agent could not tell "you named the wrong file" from "this part does not exist", and correctly refused rather than guess a pinout, twice.

## Design

Fallback order is by strength of evidence, so a weaker signal never displaces a stronger one:

1. exact name in the guessed file (unchanged)
2. near-matches within the guessed file: the caller named the right file and mistyped the part, so its own candidates outrank any other library's
3. exact name in a different library: the file was the mistake, not the part
4. fuzzy match in a different library, surfaced as a suggestion

Matching has to stay tight enough never to propose a *different real chip*. Two guards, both added in response to a case this actually hit:

- substring matching ignores library names under 3 characters. A stock library is full of single-letter generics (`R`, `C`, `D`), and "does <any part number> contain R" is true for nearly everything.
- edit distance (≤1 edit, names ≥5 chars) catches the datasheet-vs-library near-miss substring cannot: `SHT40` vs `SHT4x` differ mid-string, so neither contains the other. Capped at one edit specifically so `TPS22860` does not match `TPS22810`, a different real part.

`TPS22860` still resolving to nothing is the correct outcome, and is the case the config-level extra-library option in #185 is for.

Two defects found while building this are fixed in the same commit:

- `symbolSearchDirs` ran Windows version-directory discovery even when `KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR` was set, contradicting its own "env overrides win" contract and leaking the machine's real KiCad install into tests that had pinned an isolated fixture directory.
- the Windows fallback path hardcoded `C:/Program Files/KiCad/share/kicad/symbols`, omitting the version segment KiCad's installer always creates (`.../KiCad/10.0/share/...`), so symbol resolution failed outright on a stock Windows install. Now discovered by listing the install root, newest version first.

## Testing

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npx vitest run` | 16 failing before and after (see below) |
| Targeted | `npx vitest run test/symlib.test.ts test/draft-hardening.test.ts test/draft-tools.test.ts` | 47/47 pass |

The 16 failures are pre-existing on this machine and unrelated to symbol resolution: Windows path handling, `chmod` semantics, app-bundle probing. Confirmed by capturing the failing-test list with the change stashed and again with it applied, then diffing. The baseline was 18; the two `symbolSearchDirs` fixes above repaired two of them.

One regression was introduced and fixed during development rather than shipped: ordering the cross-library check before the same-file candidate list made `Device:R_Sma` report "use `Device:R_Sma` instead", suggesting the exact input back at the caller. `test/draft-hardening.test.ts` caught it, and it is what motivated the evidence ordering above.

### Manual verification

Against a real KiCad 10.0.5 install on Windows:

```text
TPS63900   -> Regulator_Switching [EXACT]
SHT40      -> Sensor_Humidity (fuzzy)      # the SHT4x near-miss
FDC1004    -> Sensor_Proximity (fuzzy)
TPS22860   -> NOT FOUND                    # correct: genuinely absent
```

The last line is the one worth checking on review: a looser matcher would have proposed `TPS22810` here, which is a different part.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] N/A **Spec-gated in**: no change to tool exposure or the unlock path.
- [ ] N/A **Verification-gated out**: no change to the ERC/DRC gates or rollback.
- [ ] N/A **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: this path is filesystem-only and reachable from `check` only as it already was; no provider, key, or network use added.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: the parser stays read-only. Cross-library search reads `.kicad_sym` text and matches symbol names; nothing is written or round-tripped.
- [ ] N/A **Sync-obligations ledger**: untouched.

pulls.title: fix(sync): correct the coverage location and the budget key match
pulls.body:
## What

`copperhead sync` reported the wrong file to fix for missing transparency docs, and silently skipped a missing budget dual-write when an unrelated constraint happened to share a suffix.

## Why

Both from #183. Neither is a crash, which is why they survived: the checks run, they just report the wrong thing or nothing at all.

**Coverage location.** [sync.ts](src/commands/sync.ts) built the location by concatenation, with no separator. `DEFAULTS.docs` is `docs/`, so the default hides it, and `loadConfig` does not normalise the value:

```
docs: "docs"          ->  docsDECISIONS.md
docs: "docs/design"   ->  docs/designDECISIONS.md
docs: "docs/"         ->  docs/DECISIONS.md        (correct, and unchanged)
```

The existence check was always right, since it goes through `path.join`. Only the path the user is told to create was wrong, which is the whole point of that item.

**Budget dual-write.** The audit used `endsWith`, which matches any suffix rather than a key segment:

```
budget cost=10, registry { "power.unit_cost": ... }   ->  nothing reported
budget cost=10, registry { }                          ->  reported
```

`power.unit_cost` is a different quantity, but `"power.unit_cost".endsWith("cost")` is true, so a genuinely missing dual-write is never surfaced. It now compares the final dot-separated segment, which is what the constraint branch a few lines above already does to derive its `shortKey`.

I left the third item in #183 (the constraint audit matching short keys as bare substrings) alone, since #180 proposes replacing that matching wholesale and patching it here would just get in the way.

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npx vitest run` | 555 passed, 22 failed, 20 skipped |

The 22 failures are pre-existing on `main`. I verified by removing this change and the new test file and re-running: identical 10 files / 22 tests, and `555 - 6 = 549` passing, the 6 being the ones added here.

New tests: `test/sync-verify-reporting.test.ts`, six cases. Three fail on the parent commit:

```
× joins the docs dir and the file name when docs has no trailing slash
× handles a nested docs directory
× does not treat an unrelated key as recording the budget
```

The other three are controls that pass either way, so the fix cannot quietly over-correct: a trailing slash must not become `docs//`, and a key whose final segment really is the budget name still satisfies it, dotted (`power.cost`) and undotted (`cost`).

### Manual test log

Exercised `syncVerify` directly over fixture repos rather than through the CLI, since this is verify-phase reporting and the harness gives exact item output:

pulls.title: feat/remove stale history
pulls.body:
## What

Long agent runs stop re-sending the entire conversation on every turn. Each request now carries a trimmed view of the history: stale file reads are replaced by a stub, and settled oversized tool results and edit payloads are clipped. The run's own history, the transcript, and the ledger are unchanged.

## Why

Closes #165.

Nothing ever trimmed the conversation the loop re-sends. Every provider gets the full accumulated history each turn ([tool-protocol.ts](src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts) flattens it for `claude-code`, the keyed providers post the whole `messages` array), so per-turn input cost grows roughly quadratically in turns. There is no pruning, windowing, or size cap anywhere on that path: [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts) only appends to `messages`, `read_file` with no line range returns the whole file, and `edit_file` payloads sit in `toolCalls[].args` and get re-serialized into every later prompt long after the edit is on disk.

The schematic stage is the worst case because its working artifact is large and re-read repeatedly, but the fix is not stage specific: it applies to `do`, `sync`, the REPL, and all eight `create` stages.

`PIPELINE-EFFICIENCY.md` named this the highest-leverage fix, and it was the last of its recommendations still unimplemented. It also blocks the compat route in practice: Groq returned `413` on turn one (10,078 tokens needed against a 6,000 to 8,000 TPM cap), before any history had accumulated.

## Design

New `capHistory(messages, opts)` in [history.ts](src/agent/history.ts) builds the view actually sent, called at the single `provider.chat` site in [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts). Three trims, ordered by how lossy each one is:

- **Supersession** (not lossy in isolation): a `read_file` result becomes a short stub naming the path when a *later* read of the same path returns a line span that **contains** it. Containment is the rule, not path equality: a later twenty-line read does not reproduce an earlier whole-file read, so it does not supersede it. The current contents are already in the conversation, so this applies at any distance. The newest read of a path is never superseded, though it is still subject to truncation once outside the recent window.
- **Result truncation** (lossy): a tool result over `maxToolResultChars` is clipped head and tail with an in-band marker.
- **Argument truncation** (lossy): an already-applied tool-call argument string over `maxToolArgChars` is clipped the same way.

Because the last two are lossy, they never touch the last `keepRecent` messages. Supersession deliberately ignores that window (see D3 below).

Supersession's soundness rests on crediting each `read_file` result with the exact line span the tool returned, so a load-bearing supporting change normalizes those bounds. Tool args reach the loop straight from `JSON.parse` of model output with no schema coercion, so `start_line` can arrive as a stringified `"4"`; `toolReadFile` coerces it and does a real partial read, but a recorder that read it as a non-number would credit the call with the whole file and let that partial read wrongly supersede an earlier whole-file read. The `read_file` handler now normalizes each bound once to a finite number or drops it, writing the result back into the call's args so the conversation records what the tool actually did; as a second line of defence, `rangeOf` returns an unknown span for a present-but-non-numeric bound, so such a read supersedes nothing and is superseded by nothing (see D3a).

Load-bearing decisions, with rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/cap-agent-history/design.md):

- **D1**: capping is a request-time view, never a mutation of the run's history, so the transcript and the obligations ledger keep full fidelity. Trimming the run's own record to save tokens would trade an auditable failure for a cheaper one.
- **D2**: message count, order, roles, and `toolCallId` values are preserved exactly, and only content strings shrink. `renderDelta(messages, sentCount)` slices by index for the `claude-code` session-resume path, and every provider pairs a tool result to its call by id, so the obvious implementation (dropping old messages) silently desyncs both.
- **D3**: supersession ignores the recency window, truncation respects it. A test on a realistic fixture showed that protecting recent messages from all trimming made capping barely fire, because the window was shielding exactly the largest and most recent re-reads.
- **D7**: capping rewrites arbitrarily old messages, which invalidates a provider-side prompt-cache prefix on the turn a trim first fires — re-billing the conversation at full input rate on exactly the turns capping exists to make cheaper. `capHistory` therefore reports the lowest index it rewrote (`firstChanged`), the loop forwards it as `ChatOpts.stablePrefixBefore`, and `AnthropicProvider` places a fourth `cache_control` breakpoint on the last block below it, so the stable head still hits the cache. Anthropic-only by necessity: OpenAI's prefix caching exposes no breakpoint control.
- **D6**: existing `llm-cache` entries are invalidated once. `CachingProvider` hashes the messages it is handed and those are now smaller. Unlike the earlier `baseURL` key-shape regression, where byte-identical keys were the fix, here the request genuinely changed, so a new key is the correct outcome.

Invariants: the agent tool list is unchanged, ERC/DRC gating is untouched, `src/kicad/` is untouched, and `check` stays LLM-free and network-free.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: `cap-agent-history` (`openspec validate cap-agent-history` passes).

- [proposal.md](openspec/changes/cap-agent-history/proposal.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/cap-agent-history/design.md) (D1 to D7), [tasks.md](openspec/changes/cap-agent-history/tasks.md)
- Delta spec: `agent-core` (ADDED), three requirements and sixteen scenarios covering the capped request, message-identity preservation, and read supersession.

`SPEC.md` **is** updated in this PR: the AC-3 block gains **AC-3.21** (the re-sent conversation is capped: supersession and clipping, message-identity preservation, and the `historyCap` escape hatch) and **AC-3.22** (capping never invents coverage: line bounds are normalized before a span is computed, a partial or failed read never supersedes, and the newest read is never superseded though it is still truncatable). They map 1:1 onto the delta spec's three requirements, and `tasks.md` task 5.2 is checked off. The delta still folds into `openspec/specs/` at archive time.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | full suite green, 0 failures (see the `test` check on the PR for the current pass/skip count) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_COMPAT_MODEL` / provider keys | skip: not configured, 19 skipped as expected |

New tests: [history-cap.test.ts](test/history-cap.test.ts), 36 cases. Invariants first (length/order/role/id parity, no mutation of the caller's array, short conversations returned untouched), then behavior (supersession fires, newest read survives in full, different paths stay independent, line-span containment for ranged reads, a stringified `start_line` not mistaken for a whole-file read, result clipping, argument clipping, no-op clips uncounted, recent window left verbatim), then shrinkage and loop-level tests through `renderConversation` and `runAgentLoop` (including that an llm-cache replay is not credited with a saving, and that a failing transcript write cannot mask the provider error it fires beside).

Also new: [anthropic-provider.test.ts](test/anthropic-provider.test.ts), 133 lines, the second of this PR's two new test files and the only coverage of D7. A stub `http` endpoint (the SDK pointed at it via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, an explicit test key, loopback only) captures the real request body and pins the `cache_control` breakpoint count **and** positions with and without `stablePrefixBefore`, including both degrade-to-three cases and Anthropic's four-breakpoint ceiling.

The realistic-fixture test found a real design flaw during development: with the recent window protecting all trims, capping barely fired. That is what produced D3.

No pre-existing failures. `npm run lint:md` reports 8 issues, all in generated `manual-tests/runs/` artifacts, none in files this PR touches.

## Docs

No user-facing docs in this PR. The new `historyCap` config field is documented by doc comment in [config.ts](src/config.ts); the configuration reference and `.env.example` are unchanged because the field is on by default and needs no setup.

## Folded-in change

[test/repl.test.ts](test/repl.test.ts) replaces fixed `setTimeout` sleeps with `waitFor` condition polling in the session-log tests. This is unrelated to history capping — it is a small CI flakiness fix carried in this branch, called out here so it is not a surprise in the diff.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] N/A **Spec-gated in**: the agent tool list is unchanged.
- [x] N/A **Verification-gated out**: ERC/DRC gating, repair cycles, and rollback are untouched.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: unchanged, nothing under `src/commands/check` is touched.
- [x] N/A **No sexp serialization**: `src/kicad/` is untouched.
- [x] N/A **Sync-obligations ledger**: untouched, and capping is deliberately request-time only so the ledger still sees full fidelity.
- [x] N/A **Secrets**: no credential handling changes. Capping shrinks content before it is sent but does not alter transcript redaction, which still runs on the full untrimmed record.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: OpenSpec change `cap-agent-history` added with proposal, design (D1 to D7), delta spec (three requirements, sixteen scenarios), and tasks. `openspec validate cap-agent-history` passes. `SPEC.md` carries the ACs in this PR: **AC-3.21** (the re-sent conversation is capped) and **AC-3.22** (capping never invents coverage), mapping 1:1 onto the delta spec's requirements, with `tasks.md` task 5.2 checked off. The delta folds into `openspec/specs/` at archive time.

  * Automatically limits conversation history sent with provider requests, reducing oversized payloads.
  * Preserves the complete local transcript while shortening older tool results and arguments.
  * Replaces superseded file-read results with concise references and protects recent messages.
  * History capping is enabled by default and can be disabled with configuration.
  * Run summaries and events report characters saved, including across retries.
  * Tool failures are explicitly recorded in conversation history.

pulls.title: docs: add a journey-shaped onboarding guide and blog post
pulls.body:
## What

Adds a journey-shaped onboarding page, [first-run.md](https://github.com/Chirag6722/copperhead/blob/docs/onboarding-guide/docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/first-run.md), that takes a new user from an empty machine to one verified, committed change, plus a narrative blog post and three small README fixes.

## Why

The existing onboarding material covers the surface well, but all of it is reference-shaped: it lists commands without walking the path or naming what goes wrong. Three concrete gaps came out of an audit:

1. `copperhead doctor` exists precisely to tell a new user what is missing, and it appeared in no onboarding path at all (not the README quickstart, not the docs quickstart).
2. The two-credential refusal was undocumented. A developer with both `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` exported, which is common, hits a hard stop on their first command with nothing in the docs explaining it.
3. `copperhead check` skips ERC and DRC and still exits 0 on a repo that has not been `init`-ed. That is a pass over an empty set reported as green, and nothing warned about it.

Then the guide was walked end to end on a clean Windows machine, as a new user, which surfaced eight more failures. Those are folded in and listed below.

## Testing

No test files were added or changed. Frontmatter matches the existing page schema, and the `:::caution` / `:::danger` asides follow the same pattern as [schematic-drafting.md](https://github.com/Chirag6722/copperhead/blob/docs/onboarding-guide/docs/src/content/docs/reference/schematic-drafting.md), which already uses `:::note` in a plain `.md` file.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: neither. The manual test here was the guide itself, walked as a new user on a clean Windows 11 machine with KiCad and the model backend uninstalled first.

Setup path exercised, in order:

```text
$ node --version
v24.16.0

$ copperhead doctor
  [FAIL] kicad-cli not found on PATH
  [FAIL] provider  no model configured
not ready: fix the [FAIL] items above

$ copperhead doctor          (after installing KiCad 10.0.5, before the PATH fix)
  [FAIL] kicad-cli not found on PATH

$ copperhead doctor          (after adding KiCad's bin to PATH, in a NEW terminal)
  [ok]   kicad-cli 10.0.5
  [FAIL] provider  no model configured

$ copperhead doctor          (after setting the model backend)
  [ok]   node      v24.16.0 (>= 20)
  [ok]   kicad-cli 10.0.5
  [ok]   git       2.54.0.windows.1
  [info] provider  claude-code -> claude-code: uses Claude Code login
ready
```

The create pipeline was then driven from a brief to confirm the setup path actually leads somewhere:

```text
$ copperhead create --brief brief.md
stage spec-seed:      done, committed 4be39c8cba, 4m05s
stage architecture:   done, committed a5a40006f8, 2m39s
stage part-selection: provider error (Connection closed mid-response)
                      diagnosis -> retry, attempt 2/3 succeeded
                      done, committed fccc06ebac, 10m04s
stage schematic:      running
```

Worth noting from that run: the transient provider error recovered without intervention, exactly as designed, and the failed attempt preserved its work as a named git stash entry before rolling back.

Eight failures the walkthrough exposed, all now covered in the guide:

| Failure | Fix in the guide |
| --- | --- |
| Page began after copperhead was installed, so a reader starting from nothing had no entry point | Full Install section added |
| KiCad's download page asks for a platform and then a mirror, with no guidance | "any mirror works, take the nearest" |
| KiCad's Windows installer does not touch PATH, and `kicad-cli not found` reads as "not installed" when it is installed | PowerShell PATH fix, macOS bundle path, and a locator command |
| A PATH change never reaches an already open terminal, so `doctor` keeps failing after a correct fix | "open a new terminal" called out at the fix and in the troubleshooting table |
| A wrapped token paste puts a space mid-value and returns a 401 that reads as revoked | Dedicated warning, a length check, and quoted assignment |
| `set` and `export` do not outlive the terminal window | Noted, with `setx` and shell profiles |
| `git init` alone does not satisfy the clean-tree gate, the first commit must exist | Stated explicitly, with the `--allow-dirty` escape |
| Commands were bash-only while the reader was on Windows `cmd` | Note at the top, plus both variants where they differ |

Two further additions came out of the same run: a troubleshooting row for the transient `Connection closed mid-response` (the pipeline recovers unaided, but the output reads as a failure), and a "Starting a new board" section, since the page assumed an existing board and left `create` users without a path.

A later pass caught three more, each one something the reader had to ask for out loud rather than read off the page:

| Failure | Fix in the guide |
| --- | --- |
| The KiCad download page asks for a platform and then a mirror, and the guide only said "take the nearest" | Direct download links for the current stable release, per platform |
| No sense of how long the KiCad step takes, so it reads as a quick click | Stated as roughly 1 GB, with a suggestion to start it before reading on |
| The token length check was PowerShell-only, while the reader was in `cmd`, so the one verification step for the most misleading error on the page did not run | `cmd` and bash equivalents added alongside it |

Narrative post structured around four refusals (ambiguous credentials, refusing to overwrite hand-edited docs, reverting an edit that would corrupt a KiCad file, refusing to hand-edit an engine-drafted sheet). Not wired into Astro, since Starlight only reads `src/content/docs`. Staged here for the site repo to pick up.

pulls.title: fix(kicad): make ERC/DRC `ok` severity-aware, not zero-violations
pulls.body:
## What

Makes ERC/DRC `ok` severity-aware (no error-severity violations) instead of zero-violations, so permanent library-resolution warnings on a real board no longer block the agent's repair-cycle budget and `finish()` gate forever.

## Why

`normalizeReport()` (src/kicad/report.ts:66) currently sets `ok: violations.length === 0` — any violation, warning or error, makes a report not-ok. That single boolean gates two things in the agent loop (src/agent/tools.ts):

- `run_erc`/`run_drc` increment `ctx.repairCycles` on every non-ok call (tools.ts:312, tools.ts:360)
- `finish({outcome:'done'})` refuses outright unless `ctx.lastErc?.ok`/`ctx.lastDrc?.ok` (tools.ts:612, tools.ts:614)

A real board in a bare checkout carries permanent library-resolution warnings: missing vendor symbol/footprint libraries that no edit can resolve. copperbench's own design decisions (D21, D23) measured this directly: a 19-configuration sweep found zero DRC errors unachievable on every real board tested, and the antmicro-microphone-board fixture specifically carries 44 ERC warnings / 13 DRC warnings at baseline, zero errors. Those decisions are why copperbench's own assertion vocabulary has `erc_no_new_violations`/`drc_no_new_violations` as baseline-relative checks in the first place, rather than requiring `erc_clean`/`drc_clean` on real fixtures.

But copperhead's own internal gate has no equivalent carve-out. An agent that edits the schematic and calls `run_erc` even once gets `ok: false` from those permanent warnings, `repairCycles++`, and `finish('done')` refused, forever. `maxRepairCycles` (default 5) gets burned entirely on unfixable warnings before the agent ever gets a chance to converge on the actual request. Every `do` run on a real fixture with baseline warnings ends `repair-cycles-exhausted`, regardless of what the model does or how well it does it.

## Design

`ok` now means "no error-severity violations" instead of "zero violations of any kind": matching the severity vocabulary the `Violation` type already carries (`severity: 'error' | 'warning' | string`), and matching the default severity threshold copperbench's own baseline-relative assertions already use. Warnings still populate `violations` and still print via `formatViolations()`, so the agent still sees them and can act on them if it wants to; only the pass/fail gate stops treating them as blocking.

Invariant impact: **verification-gated out** still holds exactly as specified, just against the corrected definition of "clean." Mutations still must reach `ok` before `finish('done')` succeeds, repair still runs up to `maxRepairCycles`, and exhaustion still rolls back to the git snapshot. Nothing about the repair-then-rollback mechanics changed, only what counts as something left to repair.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: `test/report.test.ts` 4/4 unchanged (none of the 4 cases exercise a warning-only report, so none depended on the old behavior). Full suite 572/601, with the same 9 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (CLI path resolution, REPL banner formatting, git safety-rail snapshot handling, KiCad-version drift on a test fixture's violation count) confirmed present identically with this change reverted |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | not gated on an env var here; validated indirectly (see manual log) through a downstream consumer's live model runs, not copperhead's own live-LLM suite |

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: n/a — validated via direct calls to the changed code path plus a downstream consumer's (copperbench) full agent-loop runs against a real fixture, not copperhead's own `manual-tests/` sandbox.
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node -e "require('./dist/kicad/cli.js').runErc('fixtures/antmicro-microphone-board/tree/hardware/microphone-board.kicad_sch').then(r => console.log('ERC ok:', r.ok, '| violations:', r.violations.length, '| errors:', r.violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'error').length))"
ERC ok: true | violations: 44 | errors: 0

$ node -e "require('./dist/kicad/cli.js').runDrc('fixtures/antmicro-microphone-board/tree/hardware/microphone-board.kicad_pcb').then(r => console.log('DRC ok:', r.ok, '| violations:', r.violations.length, '| errors:', r.violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'error').length))"
DRC ok: true | violations: 13 | errors: 0
```

Higher-level confirmation: a downstream consumer (copperbench) ran `copperhead do` end to end against this exact fixture through its full agent loop (`compat:qwen2.5-coder:7b` via a local Ollama), twice, and in neither run did `finish('done')` ever get blocked by the baseline warnings; both runs ended for unrelated reasons (`stalled`, `turn-budget-exhausted`) rather than `repair-cycles-exhausted` on unfixable warnings, which is exactly the failure mode this PR removes.

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] Spec-gated in: N/A, does not touch OpenSpec proposal gating for `edit_file`/`write_file` availability.
- [x] Verification-gated out: still holds; mutations still require `ok` before `finish('done')`, repair still runs to `maxRepairCycles`, exhaustion still rolls back. Only the definition of "clean" changed (see Design).
- [x] `check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free: unaffected; `report.ts` gains no provider or network reachability, and nothing here changes what `src/commands/check` calls.
- [ ] No sexp serialization: N/A, does not touch `src/kicad/sexp.ts` or any serialization path.
- [ ] Sync-obligations ledger: N/A, unrelated.
- [ ] Secrets: N/A, unrelated.
- [ ] Spec coherence: N/A, no spec-level behavior changed; no OpenSpec change or SPEC.md AC redefinition needed.

pulls.title: # fix(agent): boundary-aware JSON extraction for parseDiagnosis (#101)
pulls.body:
## What This PR hardens the diagnosis parsing logic in the recovery supervisor ([`src/agent/recovery.ts`](src/agent/recovery.ts)) to cleanly extract structured JSON payloads even when preceded by arbitrary LLM conversational prose, code blocks, or leading stray braces (e.g., file references like `{pins.h}`). ### Summary of changes: | File | Insertions | Deletions | Net | |---|---|---|---| | `src/agent/recovery.ts` | +21 | -15 | +6 | | `test/recovery.test.ts` | +6 | -0 | +6 | | **Total** | **+27** | **-15** | **+12** | ### Specific fixes 1. **Candidate-Scanning Balanced Brace Matcher** ([`src/agent/recovery.ts`](src/agent/recovery.ts)): - Replaced naive `text.indexOf('{')` logic in `parseDiagnosis` with an iterative loop scanning for candidate opening braces (`{`). - Added string/escape-aware depth counting that isolates balanced brace blocks and validates whether candidate slices parse into a valid `StageDiagnosis` object with a recognized `verdict` (`'retry'` | `'abort'`). - Prevents leading prose containing stray braces (such as `{pins.h}`) from polluting the extracted JSON boundary and causing `JSON.parse` syntax errors that unexpectedly terminate recovery attempts. 2. **Edge-Case Unit Test Coverage** ([`test/recovery.test.ts`](test/recovery.test.ts)): - Added an explicit test case validating that responses containing stray opening/closing braces in prefix text successfully parse into a valid `retry` verdict with preserved `reason` and `guidance`. --- ## Why | Problem | Root Cause | Impact | |---|---|---| | Pipeline aborted on recoverable failures | LLM output contained leading braces before the diagnosis block (e.g., `Check {pins.h} file...`) | ❌ Naive `indexOf('{')` sliced invalid JSON spanning from the first stray brace, falling back to an `"abort"` verdict | | Token waste on transient errors | Intermittent or transient tool-call slips failed to trigger retries when response formatting had preamble noise | ❌ Pipeline terminated early instead of prepending guidance and executing a retry turn | **Before this PR:** Any LLM diagnosis turn containing a stray `{` prior to the JSON payload resulted in a parsing error, causing `parseDiagnosis` to fall back to `verdict: 'abort'` and killing the pipeline run. **After this PR:** `parseDiagnosis` gracefully scans past pre-JSON prose and stray braces to extract the valid `StageDiagnosis` payload, restoring pipeline resilience. --- ## Design ### 1. Robust JSON extraction logic Instead of assuming the first `{` character marks the start of the diagnosis object, the updated `parseDiagnosis` iterates through candidate `{` positions: ```typescript for (let start = 0; start < text.length; start++) { if (text[start] !== '{') continue; let depth = 0; let inStr = false; let esc = false; for (let i = start; i < text.length; i++) { // ... string escaping & depth tracking ... if (ch === '}' && --depth === 0) { try { const candidate = text.slice(start, i + 1); const o = JSON.parse(candidate) as Partial; if (typeof o === 'object' && o !== null && (o.verdict === 'retry' || o.verdict === 'abort')) { // Found a valid diagnosis payload return { ... }; } } catch { break; // Not valid JSON at this opening brace; try next start candidate } } } } ``` 2. Invariant preservation Safe fallback: If no valid JSON diagnosis object is found across all candidate braces, parseDiagnosis safely defaults to { verdict: 'abort', reason: 'diagnosis was not valid JSON' }. Zero new dependencies: Keeps parser lightweight and zero-dependency using native string scanning. Spec / OpenSpec Pure agent pipeline recovery logic hardening. No OpenSpec artifacts are required or affected: no spec-level protocol behavior was changed. ## Testing ### Automated test status | Check | Command | Status | |---|---|---| | Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | :white_check_mark: **Pass** (clean, zero diagnostics) | | Unit Tests (Recovery) | `npx vitest run test/recovery.test.ts` | :white_check_mark: **13 passed**, 0 failed | ### Full test output RUN v3.2.7 D:/copperhead3/copperhead ✓ test/recovery.test.ts (13 tests) 84ms ✓ withTimeout (turn watchdog) > returns the value when the call finishes in time 2ms ✓ withTimeout (turn watchdog) > rejects with TurnTimeoutError and fires onTimeout when the deadline passes 41ms ✓ withTimeout (turn watchdog) > disables the watchdog when ms <= 0 (awaits the call) 0ms ✓ parseDiagnosis > parses a retry verdict with guidance, even wrapped in prose 0ms ✓ parseDiagnosis > parses an abort verdict and ignores guidance 0ms ✓ parseDiagnosis > parses retry verdict when leading prose contains stray braces (Fixes #101) 1ms ✓ parseDiagnosis > fails safe to abort on non-JSON or missing verdict 0ms ✓ diagnoseStageFailure > asks the model with no tools and returns the parsed verdict 1ms ✓ diagnoseStageFailure > fails safe to abort when the provider throws 1ms ✓ CachingProvider > caches a response and replays it (no second model call), reporting zero usage 13ms ✓ CachingProvider > misses (calls the model again) when the conversation differs 14ms ✓ CachingProvider > does not share cached turns across compat endpoints with the same model id 6ms ✓ CachingProvider > hits a pre-upgrade cache entry for a non-compat model (key shape unchanged) 4ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 13 passed (13) Start at 00:55:01 Duration 2.34s Manual test log (required) Sandbox variant used: edit Commands run and outcome: ```typescript $ npx vitest run test/recovery.test.ts 13 passed (success) ```

Files changed

File | Change type | Description -- | -- | -- src/agent/recovery.ts | Logic fix | Candidate-scanning balanced brace matcher in parseDiagnosis to tolerate leading prose and stray braces test/recovery.test.ts | Test coverage | Added unit test verifying JSON diagnosis extraction when preceding text contains stray braces
Files changedFileChange typeDescription[src/agent/recovery.ts](https://www.google.com/search?q=src/agent/recovery.ts)Logic fixCandidate-scanning balanced brace matcher in parseDiagnosis to tolerate leading prose and stray braces[test/recovery.test.ts](https://www.google.com/search?q=test/recovery.test.ts)Test coverageAdded unit test verifying JSON diagnosis extraction when preceding text contains stray braces Docs No documentation changes required. This is an internal agent recovery parser fix with zero CLI/API surface changes. Invariant checklist - [x] Spec-gated in: edit_file/write_file remain structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates. - [x] Verification-gated out: Mutations still terminate in ERC/DRC verification, with retry and rollback logic intact. - [x] Fail-Safe Recovery: Invalid, unparseable, or missing JSON blocks fall back safely to verdict: 'abort'. - [x] Zero Dependencies: Pure TypeScript string scanning; no external JSON or regex parsing dependencies introduced. - [x] Pipeline Cost Accounting: Preserves token usage folding (usage tracking) across diagnosis turns. - [x] Secrets: Logs and transcripts continue to redact sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ and sensitive auth tokens at write time. - [x] Spec coherence:Pure recovery parser hardening with zero changes to spec-level behavior. All core specs in [`SPEC.md`](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) remain untouched, and `openspec validate` passes cleanly. Summary by CodeRabbit Tests Enhanced recovery supervisor testing to verify robust JSON extraction when LLM responses contain leading prose or stray opening braces prior to the diagnosis object. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved diagnosis parsing for responses containing stray braces, malformed JSON, or incomplete diagnosis objects. * The system now continues searching for a valid diagnosis and preserves available reason text when no recognized verdict is found. * Safely falls back to aborting with a relevant or generic error when no valid diagnosis is available. * **Tests** * Added coverage for leading prose with stray braces, invalid objects preceding a valid retry diagnosis, and fallback reason preservation.

pulls.title: Propose deterministic-schematic-drafting: drafting engine, legibility gate, scoring, golden corpus
pulls.body:
## What

Proposes the `deterministic-schematic-drafting` OpenSpec change and implements its checker phase (groups 1-4 of 12): a legibility standard and deterministic checker that gate the create pipeline's schematic stage, ahead of the rule-based drafting engine that will compute all schematic geometry from a compact netlist-intent IR. Landed here: `src/kicad/legibility.ts` (13 check families), the `check_legibility` agent tool and ledger obligation (scoped to create-origin repos), the stage-4 drafting standard and completion gate, `check` advisories with the `legibility` JSON object, and fixtures/tests. The engine phase (emitter, IR, placement, scorer, golden corpus) is implemented on this branch as well; see the implementation-status comment for the per-capability breakdown.

## Why

Two failure modes documented on real runs. #136: stage 4 gates the net graph but never the drawing, so `create` emits electrically clean, unreadable schematics (refdes text over symbol bodies, content in 40% of the sheet, empty title block). #145: the geometry text the model authors token by token is where cost and failures concentrate (5 of 40 turns emitted 89% of 170,920 output tokens; every provider error, budget exhaustion, and stall landed on an oversized geometry turn). #159 tracks the engine.

This consolidates and supersedes the proposal-only `readable-schematic-drafting` change (#148, closed): the checker and the engine it gates are specified and will be implemented together, checker phase first.

## Design

Load-bearing decisions, full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/design.md):

- **Intent, not geometry** (D5): the model authors `schematic.intent.json` (parts, nets, groups, no-connects, hints); the engine computes placement. Repairs revise the IR and re-draft; geometry edits against an engine-drafted sheet are refused.
- **Hand-rolled grid-native rules, no layout library** (D1): after human-drafting reductions (power rails to per-pin symbols, decoupling rows beside their IC, labels between groups), each group is a 3-15 symbol layered-placement problem; elkjs is documented as the v2 escape hatch only.
- **Every gate failure is resolvable through the IR** (D6a): no-connect markers and PWR_FLAG synthesis are specified so the repair loop can never wedge the way #82 did.
- **Determinism is structural** (D4): UUIDv5 from semantic paths, canonical ordering, and symbol sources vendored into a committed project cache, so identical IR yields byte-identical files and a KiCad library upgrade cannot silently change output.
- **Checker gates, scorer measures, beauty never gates** (C4, D7, D11): thirteen mechanical check families gate at error severity; a weighted 0-100 score with aesthetic metrics (alignment, spacing uniformity, straight wires, symmetry, page balance) is advisory and pinned by golden benchmarks.
- **Three-tier golden corpus** (D8): known-good sheets catch false positives, known-bad sheets catch detection regressions, engine outputs are byte-diffed and score-pinned in CI.

Invariants preserved: the sexp parser never serializes (the emitter is a separate string-template module cross-checked by the read-only parser), spec-gating and verification-gating are untouched, and `check` stays LLM-free and network-free.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Change: [deterministic-schematic-drafting](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/) (`openspec validate deterministic-schematic-drafting` passes; 4/4 artifacts).
- New capability delta specs: [schematic-legibility](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-legibility/spec.md), [schematic-drafting-engine](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-drafting-engine/spec.md), [schematic-emission](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-emission/spec.md), [schematic-scoring](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-scoring/spec.md).
- Modified capability delta specs: [create-pipeline](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md), [agent-core](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/agent-core/spec.md), [cli-surface](openspec/changes/deterministic-schematic-drafting/specs/cli-surface/spec.md).
- Acceptance criteria: AC-16.1 through AC-16.32, tagged on delta-spec scenarios; they merge into SPEC.md on archive.
- Ordering: `turn-budget-continue-and-loop-efficiency` must archive first (it owns the base "Content-aware stage completion" text the create-pipeline delta modifies). SPEC.md itself is not touched in this PR; deltas merge on archive per the workflow.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |

| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (707 passed, 20 skipped) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip (not configured) |

New tests: [legibility.test.ts](test/legibility.test.ts) (19 tests over the check families, caps, severity config, hierarchy, byte-safety, ledger gating) plus a stage-completion contract test; gating-sync, ledger, and init-check updated for the new obligation and JSON key.

### Manual test log (required)

Full verbatim output in the [manual test evidence comment](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/pull/160#issuecomment-5140688304). `openspec validate deterministic-schematic-drafting` passes.

pulls.title: feat(sexp): add board-side footprint enumerator (fixes #11)
pulls.body:
## What

This PR significantly extends the [Copperhead](https://copperhead.sh) read-only S-expression parser to support PCB layout files (`.kicad_pcb`), fully resolving **Issue #11**. It introduces a robust, AST-based board-side footprint enumerator, allowing the agent to deterministically read physical board layouts without relying on brittle text matching.

### Summary of changes

| File | Change Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/kicad/sexp.ts` | **Feature** | Added `BoardFootprint` data contract and `listBoardFootprints` logic. |
| `test/sexp.test.ts` | **Test** | Added `.kicad_pcb` virtual fixtures and comprehensive mapping assertions. |

### Specific Additions

1. **New `BoardFootprint` Interface**: A strict TypeScript contract capturing `ref` (reference designator), `value`, `footprintId`, `layer`, and spatial coordinates `at: { x, y, rot }`.
2. **Layout S-expression Enumerator**: Implemented the `listBoardFootprints(boardPath)` utility, which leverages our existing lexical parser to traverse nested footprint nodes cleanly.
3. **Legacy Fallback Handling**: Safely parses modern KiCad files (via `property` nodes) while gracefully falling back to legacy implementations (`fp_text` nodes) so components are never returned as "unknown".

## Why

Historically, Copperhead's parser was scoped exclusively to schematics (`.kicad_sch`), leaving the agent completely blind to physical PCB layouts. 

| Problem | Root Cause | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **No board awareness** | Parser only supported `.kicad_sch` files. | Agent could not verify spatial placement, rotation, or layer properties. |
| **Brittle text parsing** | Regex fails on complex, nested S-expressions. | High risk of hallucinated or missed components during drift checks. |
| **Missing Types** | No standard contract for physical components. | Agent lacked structured memory for future layout-aware tools. |

By extracting the layout graph into structured memory natively, this PR establishes the critical foundation for future layout-aware agent tools and automated physical drift checks.

## Design

- Added `BoardFootprint` data structure and `listBoardFootprints` reader function to `src/kicad/sexp.ts`.
- Extracts `ref`, `value`, `footprintId`, coordinates `(x, y, rot)`, and `layer` metadata from `.kicad_pcb` files.
- Handles fallback extraction for legacy `fp_text` reference/value properties and defaults missing rotation to `0`.
- Sorts resulting footprints by reference designator using numeric-aware ordering (`localeCompare`).
- Preserves the read-only invariant (Spec §1.3, Design D4): edits never serialize back to disk from AST nodes.


## Spec / OpenSpec

- Resolves **Issue #11** by fulfilling the OpenSpec acceptance criteria for layout-side footprint enumeration.
- Strictly maintains the read-only parsing invariant (Spec §1.3, Design D4); the layout graph is extracted to memory, but never serialized back to disk. 
- No changes to core spec behavior, tool schemas, or the main agent loops.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | Pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | Pass |
| Unit + offline | `npx vitest run test/sexp.test.ts` | Pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `<ENV_VAR>` | n/a |

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): n/a (Pure parser library extension)
- Commands run and outcome:

RUN  v3.2.7 D:/copperhead2> npx vitest run test/sexp.test.ts

✓ test/sexp.test.ts (7 tests) 3679ms
✓ sexp parser > parses quoted strings with escapes 27ms
✓ sexp parser > lists real symbols with refdes, value, footprint (AC-1.2 source) 159ms
✓ sexp parser > lists nets from labels 7ms
✓ sexp parser > maps pins to nets geometrically (AC-1.3 source) 6ms
✓ sexp parser > supports custom power symbol libraries dynamically 1795ms
✓ sexp parser > treats legacy power: prefix symbols as power symbols (not real components) 1668ms
✓ sexp parser > lists board footprints accurately from a kicad_pcb structure 8ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  7 passed (7)

## Docs

- Added comprehensive standard JSDoc comments to `src/kicad/sexp.ts`.
- Documented the `BoardFootprint` data contract, spatial coordinate extraction scope (including defaults to `0` for omitted rotations), and the legacy metadata fallback logic for future contributors.

## Invariant checklist

- [x] Spec-gated in: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text).
- [x] Verification-gated out: mutations still end in ERC (and DRC when the board changed) passing, with repair up to `maxRepairCycles` then rollback to the git snapshot.
- [x] `check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free: nothing reachable from `src/commands/check` touches a provider, an API key, or the network.
- [x] No sexp serialization: the `src/kicad/` parser stays read-only; KiCad files are edited only via anchored exact-match text replace (no round-tripping).
- [x] Sync-obligations ledger: post-tool-call hooks keep feeding the ledger, and commit keeps refusing while obligations are open.

- [x] Spec coherence: if spec-level behavior changed, SPEC.md and the change artifacts (`proposal.md`, `design.md`, delta specs, `tasks.md`) moved together and `openspec validate <change>` passes.

pulls.title: fix(test): harden cross-platform test harness and IO stream determinism
pulls.body:
## What

This PR hardens the [Copperhead](https://copperhead.sh) offline test suite to run cleanly and deterministically on **both Windows and POSIX** (macOS/Linux) environments, eliminating platform-dependent test failures without touching any core business logic, agent pipeline code, or spec-level behavior.

### Summary of changes across 7 test files:

*(Note: Exact line counts omitted to prevent PR description drift, but the net change removes ~150 lines of flaky or brittle harness code.)*
* `test/cli-surface.test.ts`
* `test/gating-sync.test.ts`
* `test/helpers.ts` *(New: Git config fixture setup)*
* `test/init-check.test.ts`
* `test/kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts`
* `test/repl.test.ts`
* `test/safety.test.ts`

### Specific fixes

1. **Cross-platform path resolution** (`test/cli-surface.test.ts`, `test/init-check.test.ts`, `test/repl.test.ts`):
   - Replaced hardcoded POSIX paths (like `/tmp/some-repo`) with `path.resolve()` and `path.join()`. This ensures path assertions work perfectly across `\` (Windows) and `/` (POSIX) separators.

2. **Line-ending normalization via Git Config** (`test/safety.test.ts`, `test/helpers.ts`):
   - Configured `git config core.autocrlf false` in the test fixture setup. This prevents `git checkout` and `git stash apply` from injecting `\r\n` line endings into restored files on Windows, allowing strict, byte-exact comparisons of restored files without relying on string replacement hacks.

3. **Platform-conditional test gating** (`test/safety.test.ts`, `test/kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts`):
   - Wrapped POSIX-specific behaviors (like `chmod(0o000)` which NTFS ignores, and macOS app-bundle fallbacks) in explicit `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')` guards. This makes the test skipping honest rather than falsely green.

4. **Async timeout scaling** (`test/gating-sync.test.ts`):
   - Increased the timeout for the `finish blocks on open obligations` integration test from `60_000ms` to `300_000ms`. This prevents intermittent failures on CI-grade Windows runners due to I/O latency on temp directory operations and git stash/restore cycles.

5. **Restored Strict Assertions** (`test/repl.test.ts`, `test/init-check.test.ts`):
   - Restored strict `toContain` assertions for fab export artifacts.
   - Restored timer/stream regression tests for REPL paste/Escape handling.
   - Reinstated `\x1b[` SGR stripping assertions for session logs.

6. **KiCad CLI Resolution Edge Cases** (`test/kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts`):
   - Updated resolution tests to correctly expect `KicadCliMissingError` for cached missing overrides.
   - Fixed the API contract expectation for macOS bundle caching assertions.
   - Safely reset `process.env.PATH` using `delete` in `finally` blocks when originally unset.

---

## Why

| Problem | Root Cause | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `cli-surface.test.ts` assertion failure on Windows | Hardcoded `/tmp/some-repo`: `path.resolve()` returns `D:\tmp\some-repo` on Windows, doesn't match | :x: 1 test failure |
| `safety.test.ts` byte-comparison mismatches | `git stash apply` restores files with `\r\n` on Windows; `toBe()` does strict equality | :x: 4-6 test failures |
| `safety.test.ts` `chmod(0o000)` test false positive | NTFS ignores POSIX permission bits; test passes vacuously without exercising the guard | :warning: Silent false positive |
| `gating-sync.test.ts` timeout on Windows CI | Full fixture pipeline exceeds 60s under Windows I/O latency | :x: Intermittent timeout |
| Path separator mismatches across test files | String concatenation with `/` instead of `path.join()` | :x: Multiple assertion failures |

**Before this PR:** The offline suite reports failures on Windows out of the box, blocking Windows-based contributors from validating their changes locally.

**After this PR:** All **578 tests pass, 23 are skipped (LLM integration), 0 failures** on Windows, with the same results expected on POSIX.

---

## Design

### 1. Cross-platform path resolution strategy

Every test assertion that previously relied on hardcoded POSIX path separators or raw string concatenation for file paths now uses Node.js built-in path utilities (`path.resolve()` and `path.join()`).

### 2. Line-ending normalization

Rather than altering Copperhead's git-guard implementation, test assertions rely on the test fixture environment explicitly configuring `git config core.autocrlf false`. 
This approach preserves the verification intent (content must match exactly byte-for-byte) and does not require altering the git-guard source code or hardcoding string replacements.

### 3. Platform-conditional test gating

POSIX-specific behaviors are conditionally skipped on Windows with explicit `process.platform` guards. This is the honest approach: the test exercises a behavior that physically cannot occur on Windows.

### 4. Invariant preservation

> **Important:** Zero changes to any file under `src/`. This PR modifies only files under `test/`. No agent loop logic, tool dispatch, ERC/DRC verification, gating protocol, sync obligation, ledger rule, secret redaction, or KiCad parser behavior was touched.

---

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | :white_check_mark: **Pass** (clean, zero diagnostics) |
| Build | `npm run build` | :white_check_mark: **Pass** (clean compilation to `dist/`) |
| Unit + Offline | `npm test` | :white_check_mark: **578 passed**, 23 skipped, 0 failed |

---

### Manual test log (required)

- **Sandbox variant used:** `edit`
- **Commands run and outcome:**

` ` `text
$ npm run dev -- --help
Copperhead CLI v0.7.0 (success)
` ` `

## Files changed

| File | Change type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cli-surface.test.ts` | Path fix | Replace hardcoded `/tmp/some-repo` with `path.resolve()` |
| `gating-sync.test.ts` | Timeout scaling | Scale timeouts for Windows I/O latency |
| `helpers.ts` | Fixture fix | Added `git config core.autocrlf false` to fixture setup |
| `init-check.test.ts` | Path/Assertion fix | Standardize paths; restore strict fab export assertions |
| `kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts` | Path/Edge case fix | Path standardization; macOS bundle skip; MissingError fixes |
| `repl.test.ts` | Regression fix | Restore timer tests for paste/escape; restore SGR stripping check |
| `safety.test.ts` | Platform guard | Gate `chmod(0o000)` test on POSIX only; leverage Git Config for CRLF |

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in:** `edit_file`/`write_file` remain structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates.
- [x] **Verification-gated out:** Mutations still terminate in ERC (and DRC) passing, with repair up to `maxRepairCycles` then rollback to the git snapshot.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free:** Nothing reachable from `check.ts` touches a provider, an API key, or the network.
- [x] **No sexp serialization:** The `src/kicad/` parser stays read-only.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger:** Post-tool-call hooks keep feeding the ledger, and `commit` keeps refusing while obligations are open.
- [x] **Secrets:** Transcripts and summaries redact secrets at write time; SGR stripping assertions active.
- [x] **Spec coherence:** Pure refactor/harness fix: all core specs in `SPEC.md` are untouched.

pulls.title: feat(observability): flush per-LLM-call metrics incrementally, commit run artifacts (#138)
pulls.body:
## What

Flushes per-LLM-call logs and metrics incrementally, and commits run artifacts (transcript, live metrics, summary, stage report) at every terminal path of a run, including a new SIGINT/SIGTERM handler where none existed before.

## Why

Run cost data is currently write-once at the end: `transcript.jsonl` gets its only accounting in a single `run-end` event, and `REPORT.md`/`report.json` are regenerated only at pipeline completion or stage failure. A run that stalls, times out, or is killed mid-stage loses all in-progress cost data, and even a clean run never gets its transcript committed (`.copperhead/runs/` is gitignored by default, AC-4.3), so the runs whose data is most worth keeping are exactly the ones that leave nothing behind. Filed as issue #138, with #139 and #140 as duplicates.

## Design

Full rationale, including two bugs found and fixed mid-implementation, lives in [design.md](openspec/changes/flush-run-metrics-incrementally/design.md). Highlights:

- `Turn` gains a real `cacheHit` field, set by `CachingProvider` only on an actual cache hit, not read off a nonexistent provider field.
- A new `metrics.json` uses its own `status` vocabulary (`running` / `stalled` / a real exit path), never reusing the terminal `ExitPath` enum for in-progress state, so a healthy run can never report itself as stalled.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` are handled by a fully synchronous handler, registered with `process.prependListener` ahead of [render.ts](src/agent/render.ts)'s and [repl.ts](src/commands/repl.ts)'s own `SIGINT` listeners, which already call `process.exit()` synchronously and would otherwise win the race before an async handler's cleanup ran. On interrupt, the working tree is deliberately not rolled back (different intent than an unattended failure); only the run's own audit trail is preserved and committed.
- Every artifact commit is a new, standalone commit via a targeted `commitPaths()` helper (`git add -f` on exact paths, never a directory or `-A`), never an amend: a run's own commit can already be followed by a separate openspec-archive commit, so amending "the last commit" risks landing on the wrong one.
- D8 in the design doc covers a bug caught by the existing test suite during implementation: committing the stage-start report before that stage's own `runAgentLoop` call (and its `gitPreflight` check) can silently create a fresh repo's first commit, curing the "no commits yet" precondition before the real check ever runs. Fixed by deferring that commit to the stage's actual outcome boundary.

## Spec / OpenSpec

Change: [flush-run-metrics-incrementally](openspec/changes/flush-run-metrics-incrementally/), extending the `run-observability` capability `record-run-metadata` added (SPEC.md AC-8). New **AC-16 - Incremental run metrics & artifact commits**, AC-16.1 through AC-16.9, mapping 1:1 onto the delta spec's scenarios and the issue's own acceptance criteria.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 591 passed, 20 skipped, 11 failed |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass, 0 issues |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | not run: no key in this environment (see manual-test log) |

21 new tests across [test/run-metrics.test.ts](test/run-metrics.test.ts) and [test/run-metrics-create.test.ts](test/run-metrics-create.test.ts), one per acceptance criterion plus two regression guards, including a real child-process `SIGKILL` test (spawns `runAgentLoop` in a separate OS process via [test/fixtures/scripts/sigkill-run.ts](test/fixtures/scripts/sigkill-run.ts), confirms completed calls survive the kill and the in-flight one leaves nothing partial or corrupt). All 21 pass consistently, including 5 repeated runs of the timing-sensitive heartbeat test in isolation.

The 11 failures are confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this PR: I ran the identical full suite against `main` with none of this branch's changes applied (same machine, same parallel load) and got the same 10-11 failures (varies slightly by run: `kicad-cli-resolve.test.ts` PATH resolution, `safety.test.ts` chmod/CRLF semantics, and several timing-sensitive tests, all specific to this Windows environment under full parallel load). Two real regressions turned up during this work and are both fixed here, not left as known failures: `observability.test.ts`'s commit-failure test (a failed artifact commit was leaving staged cruft behind, now unstaged on failure) and `preflight.test.ts`'s unborn-HEAD test (the D8 bug above).

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used: `edit`

```text
$ ./manual-tests/setup.sh edit --fresh
sandbox ready: manual-tests/runs/edit

$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit init
created docs\SPEC.md
created docs\BOM.md
created docs\PINOUT.md
created docs\SUBSYSTEMS.md
created docs\LAYOUT.md
created docs\DECISIONS.md
created docs\CHANGELOG.md
created .git\hooks\pre-commit
(.copperhead/README.md correctly documents the new commitRunArtifacts default and the runs/ commit behavior)

$ git -C manual-tests/runs/edit add -A && git -C manual-tests/runs/edit commit -q -m "scaffold docs"

$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit check
ERC: 2 violation(s) (pre-existing lib_symbol_mismatch warnings on the open-key fixture, unrelated to this change)
DRC pass
drift pass
```

`do`/`create` (the agent-loop paths this PR actually touches: `llm-call` events, live `metrics.json`, `SIGINT` handling, artifact commits) could not be exercised against a live model in this environment: no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` and no saved-login provider (`codex`/`cursor`/`claude-code`) is available here. `init`/`check` are LLM-free per SPEC.md and confirm the CLI still runs end to end and the scaffolded docs reflect this change correctly. The loop-level behavior this PR adds is instead covered by 21 automated tests against the real `runAgentLoop`, including the real, separate-process `SIGKILL` test noted above, which exercises the same code path a live `do` run would, minus the network call. Flagging this gap explicitly rather than skipping the log, per the "report actual outcomes, never assumed ones" instruction; happy to re-run against a live model if a maintainer can share results, or I can push a follow-up once I have a key configured.

## Docs

- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md): new AC-16 block.
- [.copperhead/README.md](src/memory/scaffold.ts) (generated): `runs/` section rewritten to describe the new committed subset instead of "this directory is gitignored"; `config.json` section documents `commitRunArtifacts`.
