pulls.title: feat(kicad): score layout quality against constraints and real boards
pulls.body:
## What

`layout-draft` gets a measurement it cannot be talked out of. A new read-only `.kicad_pcb` reader, a deterministic layout scorer, a `layout_metrics` tool, and a generated `## Draft quality` section in `docs/LAYOUT.md`. The scorer is validated by a mutation suite that runs in CI and by the KiCad demo corpus that ships on the machine.

## Why

Addresses #141 (the measurement half; the placer and router are deferred, see [Design](#design)).

Stage 5's only check is `run_drc`, and DRC is a legality test. The current empty 30x20 mm scaffold passes it trivially, so **a board with nothing on it scores identically to a finished one**. A DRC-clean board can still have a bypass cap 20 mm from the pin it decouples, a return path with no copper behind it, and a sensor pointed at the load connector: every one of those is named by a key already in `.copperhead/constraints.json`, and none is a DRC rule. So the pipeline's acceptance criterion for layout was "the model says it's fine", which is what the stage prompt's "unlabeled non-optimal is not acceptable" clause was trying and failing to compensate for.

That is not a safe thing to rely on. Run `2026-07-29T19-54-42-021Z` refused the layout stage claiming 14 unconnected items in a turn where `run_erc` had returned "ERC: clean".

## Design

Three new modules, all read-only, all pure Node. Full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/design.md) decisions D9 to D11.

**[pcb.ts](src/kicad/pcb.ts)**: footprints, pads with absolute positions, courtyards from `F.CrtYd`/`B.CrtYd`, segments, vias, zones with filled area, and the Edge.Cuts extents. Both net encodings resolve to a name: KiCad 8/9 writes `(net 3 "GND")` on pads and bare `(net 3)` elsewhere against a top-level table, KiCad 10 writes `(net "GND")` everywhere. The footprint rotation sense was picked by measurement, not from memory: `x' = x·cos + y·sin`, `y' = -x·sin + y·cos` lands measurably more pads on real track endpoints than its mirror on every demo checked (`pic_programmer` 139 vs 120, `multichannel_mixer` 328 vs 287, `video` 1297 vs 1256).

**[layout-metrics.ts](src/kicad/layout-metrics.ts)** (D9): `computeLayoutMetrics(board, constraints)` is a pure function of the parsed board plus the registry. It consults neither the agent, nor the schematic, nor `kicad-cli`, precisely because of the refusal above: the scorer must not be able to be told anything. Purity is also what makes the demo corpus a valid calibration set.

- **Connectivity** is union-find over 1 µm-quantized points: a segment unions its endpoints per layer, a via unions across the layers it spans, a pad snaps to any track endpoint within `max(padExtent/2, 0.05 mm)`, and a zone on a net unions every pad on that net. Deliberately approximate and deliberately over-crediting, so it never flags a good board on connectivity it cannot see. The mutation that deletes the pour is what keeps that honest.
- **Hard rows** exist only when a constraint key matches by suffix (`*trace_width_mm`, `*board_outline_mm`, `*keepout`, `*mounting_hole_clearance_mm`, `*decoupling_distance_mm`, `*copper_area_mm2`). Every row names its key, bound, measured value and `pass` / `fail` / `n/a`. An unanswerable row is `n/a` with a reason and is excluded from the score, never counted as a pass. An empty registry gives an empty table, never invented rows.
- **The score** is 40 routed nets, 20 hard constraints, 12 courtyard clearance, 12 on-board placement, 8 density, 8 routing directness. Placement terms are **zeroed, not awarded**, when nothing is placed, so an empty board cannot bank points for the overlaps it does not have. That puts empty (20) below placed-but-unrouted (44) below routed (93.4).

**[layout-report.ts](src/kicad/layout-report.ts)** (D11): `## Draft quality` is generated and regenerated in place after the layout stage's completion contract is met and on every later resume. Everything below the notes marker survives, and a section that predates the marker has its whole body treated as notes, so the model's judgement is never destroyed.

**Deferred, with reasons.** The generation half of #141 is not here, and the blocker is dependency-shaped rather than effort-shaped: `sync_pcb_from_sch` needs the `pcbnew` Python bindings because `kicad-cli` 10.0.4 has no netlist-into-board import; the `placement.yaml` solver is blocked behind that import (nothing to place until the footprints exist); freerouting needs a JVM. None of those is a Copperhead dependency and none is present in CI. Scoring lands first because it is how the placer will be judged: without it, a placer change that quietly makes layouts worse looks exactly like a DRC-clean board nobody looks at. Also deferred: the per-stage place/route checkpointing (that belongs with the checkpoint work) and per-run corpus percentiles in `REPORT.md` (the baseline file exists for it).

**Invariants.** The s-expression layer stays read-only and nothing serializes a board, including the mutation suite, which uses anchored exact-match text replaces and asserts the fixture on disk is unchanged when it finishes. `layout_metrics` reads and reports, so it sits in the unlocked tier next to `run_erc`/`run_drc`. Nothing new is reachable from `check`.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change [`score-layout-quality`](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/): [proposal.md](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/proposal.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/design.md), [tasks.md](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/tasks.md), delta spec [layout-quality/spec.md](openspec/changes/score-layout-quality/specs/layout-quality/spec.md).

`layout-quality` is a **new capability**. `openspec validate score-layout-quality` passes and all four artifacts are complete. SPEC.md is untouched on purpose: the tool-table and stage-5 entries merge on archive (task 6.1), following the `add-fab-release-gate` precedent.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (clean) |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass (clean) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 617 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed (48 files, 1 skipped) |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass: 0 issues in 132 files |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip (not configured; 20 skipped tests are these) |

New tests, 40 in total across six files:

- [layout-pcb.test.ts](test/layout-pcb.test.ts): both net encodings, identical geometry from both, footprint rotation, courtyards and outline, the empty open-key scaffold, the reference board, non-board rejection.
- [layout-metrics.test.ts](test/layout-metrics.test.ts): unrouted nets named, empty < placed-only < routed, the pour credited and then not, hard rows tracing to their key, an empty registry giving no rows, `n/a` rows, and the rendering plus the upsert preserving prose.
- [layout-mutation.test.ts](test/layout-mutation.test.ts): the four degradations, each asserting *which* metric moved and not only that the score fell.
- [layout-tool.test.ts](test/layout-tool.test.ts): available without an edit unlock, "does not apply yet" without a board, the full report, and a degradation on disk showing up in the very next call.
- [layout-draft-quality.test.ts](test/layout-draft-quality.test.ts): the create-pipeline regeneration hook.
- [layout-corpus.test.ts](test/layout-corpus.test.ts): guarded by `existsSync('/usr/share/kicad/demos')`, so it skips on a machine without the demos rather than failing. CI installs KiCad, so it runs there too.

No pre-existing failures; the suite was green before and after.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: hand-built `create`-shaped repo (board at `hardware/board.kicad_pcb`, a six-key `.copperhead/constraints.json`, a model-written `docs/LAYOUT.md`), plus the installed KiCad demos.

**1. The `layout_metrics` tool, from the locked tool list, against the built `dist/`:**

```text
$ node -e "…dispatchTool(ctx, 'layout_metrics', {})…"   # ctx.editsUnlocked = false
edit tools unlocked? false
layout_metrics present in the locked tool list? true
---
layout score: 93.4/100 for hardware/board.kicad_pcb
  Routed nets: 40/40 (4/4 multi-pad nets joined in copper)
  Hard constraints: 20/20 (6/6 constraint rows pass)
  Courtyard clearance: 12/12 (0 overlapping courtyard pair(s))
  On-board placement: 12/12 (0/8 footprint(s) outside the outline)
  Placement density: 1.72/8 (7.5% of the outline covered by courtyards)
  Routing directness: 7.67/8 (42.68 mm ideal vs 44.5 mm routed)
hard constraints:
  [pass] mech.board_outline_mm, Board outline: expected <= 60 x 40 mm, measured 60 x 40 mm
  [pass] mech.load_trace_width_mm, Narrowest current-carrying track: expected >= 1.5 mm, measured 1.5 mm (4 segment(s) on power nets)
  [pass] mech.mounting_hole_clearance_mm, Mounting hole copper clearance: expected >= 1.5 mm, measured 9.447 mm (nearest copper to any of 2 mounting hole(s))
  [pass] power.decoupling_distance_mm, Decoupling pad-to-pin distance: expected <= 5 mm, measured 4.23 mm (worst of 2 bypass cap(s): C1 to U1.1)
  [pass] sense.optical_feedback_keepout, Keepout separation J1 to R1: expected >= 20 mm, measured 30.648 mm (centroid to centroid)
  [pass] thermal.copper_area_mm2, Copper area on GND: expected >= 500 mm2, measured 2212.13 mm2 (tracks, pads, vias and filled zones on that net)
soft metrics:
  footprints=8 routed=4/4 track=44.5mm segments=8 vias=1 zones=1 courtyardOverlaps=0 offBoard=0 boardArea=2400mm2 density=7.5%
  unrouted nets: none
```

**2. Draft-quality regeneration, then a degradation on disk, then regeneration again:**

```text
$ node -e "…refreshDraftQuality(opts, 'layout-draft')…"
stage layout-draft: regenerated "## Draft quality" in docs/LAYOUT.md: score 93.4/100, 4/4 nets routed, 0 hard constraint(s) failing

$ sed -i 's/(width 1\.5)/(width 0.25)/g' hardware/board.kicad_pcb
$ node -e "…refreshDraftQuality(opts, 'layout-draft')…"
stage layout-draft: regenerated "## Draft quality" in docs/LAYOUT.md: score 90.1/100, 4/4 nets routed, 1 hard constraint(s) failing

$ grep -nE 'Layout score|load_trace_width|copperhead:notes|First pass' docs/LAYOUT.md
7:**Layout score: 90.1 / 100**
23:| `mech.load_trace_width_mm` | Narrowest current-carrying track (4 segment(s) on power nets) | >= 1.5 mm | 0.25 mm | fail |
46:<!-- copperhead:notes, everything below this line is preserved when the block above is regenerated -->

```

The model's sentence survived both regenerations; the computed block followed the board.

**3. Mutation numbers, measured on the committed reference board:**

| Board | Score | Routed | Hard rows failing |
| --- | ---: | :---: | --- |
| original | 93.4 | 4/4 | (none) |
| decoupling caps moved 15 mm | 79.8 | 3/4 | `power.decoupling_distance_mm` |
| power net narrowed to 0.25 mm | 90.1 | 4/4 | `mech.load_trace_width_mm` |
| placements shuffled in the outline | 49.1 | 1/4 | `power.decoupling_distance_mm`, `sense.optical_feedback_keepout` |
| ground zone deleted | 80.1 | 3/4 | `thermal.copper_area_mm2` |

Narrowing the power net moves nothing geometrically, so it is visible only through the hard table: that is the case that forces the hard term into the score at all.

**4. The labeled pair, scored by hand:**

pulls.title: feat(agent): quantize stage work and measure turn-cost concentration
pulls.body:
## What

A create-pipeline stage now works in small verified quanta instead of a few enormous emissions, and the run report says how concentrated its spend actually was. Concretely: KiCad edits are size-capped and verification-gated at the tool layer, a clean ERC or DRC checkpoint-commits the verified work and moves the rollback target onto it, stages get token and wall budgets with their own exit paths, and `report.json` / `REPORT.md` / `summary.md` carry per-turn concentration and edit-pressure figures.

## Why

Closes #145.

Across 14 runs in this repo, 112 minutes of wall time produced a schematic and no board, and the spend was not spread across the pipeline. In the 65m46s schematic run, 5 of 40 turns emitted 89% of the run's 170,920 output tokens (median turn: 177, largest: 43,629), and every observed failure landed on an oversized turn: `provider-error` mid-response, `turn-budget-exhausted`, and a 10-minute single-turn stall that cleared the 600 s watchdog with 18 seconds to spare.

Two things were wrong and they compound:

1. **The concentration was invisible.** One wall/turn/token figure per stage cannot tell a stage with one 43k-token turn from a stage with forty even ones. `top5TurnShare` would have read 0.89 at turn five; the wall total only read at minute 66.
2. **The quantum was a suggestion.** The stage-4 prompt says "work ONE part at a time". The measured run made 51 `edit_file` calls against 6 `run_erc` calls, with a single 17,884-character block among them. Nothing committed until the stage ended, so a mid-response provider error cost the whole stage rather than one part.

## Design

Full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/quantize-stage-work/design.md); the load-bearing points:

**D1, measurement is a pure function over `perTurn`.** [turn-metrics.ts](src/agent/turn-metrics.ts) takes the rows the loop already records and returns nearest-rank `p50TurnOut` / `p95TurnOut`, `maxTurnOut`, `top5TurnShare` and `slowestTurnMs`. Being pure and transcript-shaped means `readRunTurnCost` scores a run directory recorded before any of this existed, which is how the issue's own figures are reproduced as a unit test rather than asserted. Degenerate cases are defined: an empty run is zeroed, and the observed 40-turn zero-output cache replay is 0% concentrated, not `NaN`. `perTurn` gains `ms`, additively, so old transcripts stay readable and simply report `slowestTurnMs: null`.

**D2, the quantum is enforced in [tools.ts](src/agent/tools.ts), on KiCad files only.** Both gates refuse before anything is written, so a refused call leaves the file byte-identical. The byte cap defaults to **8192, not the 4 kB the issue suggests**: one canonical `lib_symbols` entry for a wide connector legitimately exceeds 4 kB, and a cap that makes a correct atomic edit impossible converts a batching problem into a deadlock. 8 kB still refuses every oversized edit the issue measured (17.9 kB, and the four over 11 kB). The verify gate counts unverified edits per file kind and resets on `run_erc` / `run_drc` **whether or not the check passed**: the edit that fixes a violation is the very edit a pass-only reset would refuse, so repair would deadlock at the first violation. Docs are not capped, because SPEC.md and BOM.md are legitimately written in one pass and capping them would break the three doc stages for no measured benefit.

**D3, checkpoints commit a subset, then re-snapshot.** A new `commitPaths()` in [git.ts](src/util/git.ts) stages only `ctx.filesTouched`. Every create stage runs with `--allow-dirty`, so `git add -A` here would sweep the operator's unrelated working changes into a copperhead commit each time a unit verified. After each checkpoint the loop takes a fresh `snapshot()` and uses it for any later `restore()`, which is the whole mechanism: the existing snapshot machinery already captures the remaining dirty tracked state and untracked files. Checkpoints are prefixed distinctly from stage commits so history stays greppable, and a checkpoint failure is a warning, never a run failure.

**D4, spend budgets get their own exit paths.** `stageBudgets` is a new config map rather than a reinterpretation of `budgets`, which already means design budgets (sleep current) and is rendered verbatim into the system prompt: overloading one map would make a hardware limit and a token limit indistinguishable. `maxTokensOut` and `maxWallMs` are checked before a turn is bought and fail on `token-budget-exhausted` / `wall-budget-exhausted`, deliberately distinct from `turn-budget-exhausted` because more turns is the wrong answer to a stage that burned its tokens. `maxTurnOut` is different in kind: exceeding it means the unit was too big, so it injects a split-the-unit message and the run continues, rather than throwing away a turn already paid for.

**D5, stage progress is computed, not remembered.** [stage-progress.ts](src/commands/stage-progress.ts) compares BOM refdes against schematic symbols (and schematic symbols against board footprints, reading both the KiCad 7+ and older reference encodings), recomputed before every attempt. A stored cursor goes stale the moment a rollback moves the tree, and a stale cursor is worse than none.

**Deferred: sub-stage decomposition of `schematic` and `layout-draft`.** The issue asks for `symbols` / `connectivity` / `annotation` and `import` / `placement` / `route-power` / `route-signal` / `document`. A sub-stage is only real if its completion contract can be evaluated deterministically, and today's contracts cannot tell "symbols placed" from "symbols wired": both states have symbols, both can be drift-clean, and both can pass ERC on a sheet whose pins are flagged no-connect. Splitting on a contract that cannot distinguish them produces stages reporting complete while the work they name has not happened, which is exactly the failure the content-aware contracts were added to stop. The routing sub-stages need the connectivity model #141 is building; a second, weaker one here would leave two disagreeing definitions in the tree. What motivated the split was resumability, and checkpoint commits plus the computed progress line deliver that at finer granularity than a sub-stage would.

**Invariants.** Nothing here weakens a gate. The edit tools stay structurally absent until the proposal validates; the two new gates sit inside `edit_file` and only ever refuse. Verification-gated-out is strengthened, not relaxed: a checkpoint only ever follows a clean check, and a failure still rolls back (to the last verified point instead of to the start of the run, which is the intended trade and is logged both when a checkpoint is taken and when a rollback lands on one). No sexp serialization: the progress computation and the footprint count are read-only. `check` imports nothing new.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: [quantize-stage-work](openspec/changes/quantize-stage-work/). `openspec validate quantize-stage-work` passes.

- Delta specs: [agent-core](openspec/changes/quantize-stage-work/specs/agent-core/spec.md), [run-observability](openspec/changes/quantize-stage-work/specs/run-observability/spec.md), [create-pipeline](openspec/changes/quantize-stage-work/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md).
- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) moved with it: the config example and prose in section 5, the spend-budget line in section 4.5, the two new exit paths in AC-8.5, and a new **AC-16.1 through AC-16.9** block for this change.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (44 files, 614 tests, 20 skipped, 1 file skipped) |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass (134 files, 0 issues) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip (not configured; the 19 tests in `agent-integration.test.ts` did not run) |

New tests, all offline:

- [test/turn-metrics.test.ts](test/turn-metrics.test.ts): the issue's exact 40-value array reproduces p50 177, max 43,629 and a top-5 share of 0.89; empty input zeroed; a zero-output run is 0%, not `NaN`; slowest turn from `ms`; edit-pressure arithmetic and cross-attempt folding; a historical-style transcript fixture ([test/fixtures/runs/](test/fixtures/runs/)) scored by `readRunTurnCost`.
- [test/quantize-stage-work.test.ts](test/quantize-stage-work.test.ts): an oversized KiCad edit is refused naming cap, size, setting and symbol count with the file byte-identical; a 20 kB docs edit is accepted; `maxEditBytes: 0` disables; a second unverified schematic edit is refused; `edit` then `run_erc` then `edit` passes; a **failing** `run_erc` still resets the counter and the repair edit lands; `maxUnverifiedEdits: 0` disables; a checkpoint commit lands with the right prefix, survives a later failure and does not sweep an unrelated dirty file; dry runs and `checkpointCommits: false` never checkpoint; `token-budget-exhausted` and `wall-budget-exhausted`; the `maxTurnOut` nudge reaches the model and the run still succeeds; `run-end` and `summary.md` carry the new figures on a failing run; the progress line names the missing refdes for both stages.
- [test/create-cost-report.test.ts](test/create-cost-report.test.ts): `report.json` and `REPORT.md` carry the concentration columns, resumed stages report `null` rather than a zeroed (and therefore falsely reassuring) concentration, `stageBudgets` reaches the stage run and junk entries are dropped, and the schematic prompt carries the progress line.

Three existing test files ([gating-sync](test/gating-sync.test.ts), [create-hardening](test/create-hardening.test.ts), [budget-efficiency](test/budget-efficiency.test.ts)) build a `RunContext` by hand and now spread `freshEditCounters()`; no test assertion was weakened and no default was loosened to make the suite pass. No pre-existing failures.

### Manual test log (required)

pulls.title: fix(create): escalate the turn budget after a turn-starved stage attempt
pulls.body:
## What

A `copperhead create` stage that runs out of turns now gets more turns on its next attempt (40, then 60, then 90 on the default budget) instead of being retried at the budget that just proved insufficient. `create` also gains `--max-turns <n>`, the `schematic` and `layout-draft` stages get larger built-in defaults, and the attended "continue?" prompt now survives a piped or redirected stdout.

## Why

Closes #135.

`stageTurns` was read once per stage, outside the attempt loop, and handed unchanged to every attempt. With the default `maxStageRetries: 2` the schematic stage could run three times at 40 turns, roll back three times, and end no closer than it started. The recovery supervisor could not compensate: it saw the failure only as the prose string `the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted)`, so it could not tell turn starvation from a bad edit, and its verdicts were limited to `retry` and `abort`.

Two contributing factors from the issue are fixed here too: `create` had no `--max-turns` (so the only way to give a stage a realistic budget was hand-editing `.copperhead/config.json`), and the attended continue prompt from #15 required both stdin and stdout to be TTYs, which silently removed the escape hatch from every `| tee run.log` run.

## Design

Full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/design.md).

**D1: escalate on the exit path, not on the supervisor's opinion.** `turn-budget-exhausted` is already a machine-readable field on `RunResult`, so the escalation is deterministic arithmetic in [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts): the per-attempt loop remembers the budget it ran under and, when the attempt exited `turn-budget-exhausted`, gives the next attempt `previous + budgetExtraTurns({ maxTurns: previous })` turns. That reuses the increment the attended prompt already offers, so attended and unattended runs escalate identically. The supervisor still runs and still decides retry vs abort, but it is now told the structured cause (`exitPath: <value>`) and the budget already scheduled, with an explicit note that the budget alone is not a reason to abort. A third verdict (`retry-with-more-turns`) was rejected: it would put a deterministic arithmetic decision behind a model call that fails safe to `abort`, which is the failure the issue describes.

**D2: four-level budget resolution, config still wins per stage.** `resolveStageMaxTurns` in [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) resolves `stageMaxTurns[stage]` > `--max-turns` > `DEFAULT_STAGE_MAX_TURNS[stage]` > `config.maxTurns`. The flag sits *under* the per-stage config entry because #135 defines it as "the per-stage cap that `stageMaxTurns` still overrides per stage"; the flag's help text says so. `DEFAULT_STAGE_MAX_TURNS` is `{ schematic: 100, 'layout-draft': 80 }`, the numbers [manual-tests/setup.sh](manual-tests/setup.sh) has been setting for create sandboxes (with a comment saying 40 is inadequate), promoted from a test-only workaround into the product default. The resolver returns a concrete number for every stage rather than leaving it undefined, because escalation needs a budget to escalate from; the visible consequence is that `create` now always passes `maxTurns` to `runAgentLoop`, with the same value the loop would have defaulted to for an untuned stage.

**D3: the prompt needs a TTY to ask on, not one to print to.** `budgetContinuePrompt` moves from [cli.ts](src/cli.ts) (which parses argv at import time, so it cannot be imported in a test) to [cli-args.ts](src/util/cli-args.ts), gates on `stdin.isTTY` alone, and writes to stderr when stdout is not a TTY. `confirmTty` moves with it and takes output and input streams as parameters. Streams are injectable, which is what lets the piped case be driven with real `PassThrough` streams in a unit test.

**Invariants.** Nothing here touches the agent loop's gates: the edit tools stay spec-gated, verification still gates a mutation out, and the rollback path is unchanged. A stage attempt that fails still rolls back exactly as before, it just gets a bigger budget next time. `check`'s module graph is untouched.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: [escalate-stage-turn-budget](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/) with [proposal.md](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/proposal.md), [design.md](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/design.md), [tasks.md](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/tasks.md), and two delta specs: [create-pipeline](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md) (escalation, structured exit path, built-in per-stage budgets) and [cli-surface](openspec/changes/escalate-stage-turn-budget/specs/cli-surface/spec.md) (`create --max-turns`, modified attended budget prompt).

[SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md) moved with it: `create --max-turns` in the CLI surface (§3), the four-level budget precedence in the config section (§5), and a new **AC-16.1 through AC-16.6** covering escalation, the unchanged non-budget paths, the structured supervisor input, the give-up remedy, precedence, and the piped-stdout prompt.

`openspec validate escalate-stage-turn-budget` passes; all four artifacts are complete.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (clean) |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass (clean) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 600 passed, 20 skipped, 42 files passed / 1 skipped |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass: 0 issues in 133 files |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip (not configured; `test/agent-integration.test.ts` is the 19 of the 20 skips) |

New tests: [test/create-budget-escalation.test.ts](test/create-budget-escalation.test.ts) (13 tests: the 40 to 60 to 90 sequence, each raise logged, no escalation on `provider-error`, the give-up line naming `--max-turns` and `stageMaxTurns` and its absence for non-budget failures, `exitPath`/`nextAttemptMaxTurns` reaching the supervisor, and the full precedence chain including config beating `--max-turns` and the schematic stage getting its built-in 100 through a real run). Added to [test/recovery.test.ts](test/recovery.test.ts) (the supervisor prompt carries `exitPath: turn-budget-exhausted` and the next budget; both lines absent when not supplied) and [test/cli-surface.test.ts](test/cli-surface.test.ts) (`budgetContinuePrompt` with a TTY stdin and non-TTY stdout asks on stderr and grants 20 turns on `y`; asks on stdout when both are TTYs; undefined with no stdin TTY; `create --help` advertises `--max-turns` and a bad value refuses to start).

Changed test: [test/create-stage-turns.test.ts](test/create-stage-turns.test.ts) asserted `architecture.maxTurns === undefined`; the pipeline now resolves the global default explicitly (40) because escalation needs a base to measure from, so the assertion moved to `40`. Same effective budget, now stated rather than implied.

No pre-existing failures were observed; the suite was green before and after.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): none. A live `create` run needs a provider credential, which this environment does not have, so the escalation was exercised as a scripted run against the real exported code plus the real pipeline log path. The flag itself was exercised through the real CLI entry point.
- Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ npx tsx src/cli.ts create --help

Mode A: full pipeline from a product brief to the output package

Options:
  --brief <file>   product brief (markdown)
  --model <model>  codex | cursor | gpt-5 | claude | claude-code | compat:<id>
                   (or a provider-specific model id)
  --max-turns <n>  turn budget per stage (a stageMaxTurns config entry still
                   wins for that stage)
  --interactive    re-enable the human gates (spec approval, pre-export)
  -h, --help       display help for command

$ npx tsx src/cli.ts create --brief nope.md --max-turns 5oops
--max-turns must be a positive integer, got "5oops"
exit=1
```

Scripted exercise of the resolver, the escalation arithmetic, the supervisor prompt, and the piped continue prompt, all against the real exported functions (throwaway script, not committed):

```text
$ npx tsx escalation-demo.ts
built-in per-stage defaults: {"schematic":100,"layout-draft":80}
precedence  config{schematic:55} + --max-turns 120 -> 55
precedence  --max-turns 120, no config entry      -> 120
precedence  nothing set, schematic                -> 100
precedence  nothing set, spec-seed                -> 40
escalation over three turn-starved attempts: 40 -> 60 -> 90
--- supervisor prompt ---
Stage: schematic
Stage goal: (stage prompt elided)
Failure: the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted)
exitPath: turn-budget-exhausted
The next attempt has already been granted a larger turn budget of 150 turns, so the budget alone is not a reason to abort.
This was attempt 1 of 3.
...
--- end prompt ---
prompt offered with a piped stdout? true
[stderr] Turn budget exhausted (40 turns, 12.3k in / 6.8k out, 1 file(s) touched, 1 open obligation(s)). Continue with 20 more turns? [y/N]
extra turns granted on "y": 20
prompt offered with no stdin TTY? false
```

The pipeline's own stage output over three turn-starved attempts, from a scripted `runCreate` (mocked `runAgentLoop` returning `turn-budget-exhausted`, mocked supervisor returning `retry`):

```text
stage spec-seed: running
stage spec-seed: the attempt ran out of turns; raising the next attempt's budget 40 → 60
stage spec-seed: the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted); asking the model whether to retry…
stage spec-seed: diagnosis → retry — transient
stage spec-seed: running (attempt 2/3)
stage spec-seed: the attempt ran out of turns; raising the next attempt's budget 60 → 90
stage spec-seed: the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted); asking the model whether to retry…
stage spec-seed: diagnosis → retry — transient
stage spec-seed: running (attempt 3/3)
stage spec-seed: the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted); exhausted 2 auto-retry(ies). Stopping for a human.
stage spec-seed: every attempt ran out of turns (last budget 90): this stage needs a larger budget, not another attempt. Re-run with `--max-turns <n>` or set "stageMaxTurns": {"spec-seed": <n>} in .copperhead/config.json.
```

Not exercised live: an actual model-backed `create` run hitting a real 40-turn wall. That needs a provider credential and roughly an hour of wall time, so it is n/a here.

## Docs

- [docs/reference/cli.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli.md): `--max-turns` in the `create` option table, plus a "Turn budgets" section covering the precedence chain and the escalation behaviour.
- [docs/reference/configuration.md](docs/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md): `stageMaxTurns` row, noting it outranks `create --max-turns`.
- [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md): CLI surface, config precedence, AC-16.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: N/A for the mechanism, and unchanged: the tool list is built in `src/agent/loop.ts`/`tools.ts` and this PR does not touch it.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: unchanged. A failed stage attempt still rolls back to the snapshot; only the next attempt's turn budget differs.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: unchanged. The new code lives in `create`, `recovery`, and `util/cli-args` (which imports only `node:path`, `node:readline/promises`, and a type from the loop).
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: N/A, no KiCad file handling touched.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, untouched.
- [x] **Secrets**: N/A, untouched. No new value is written to a transcript or summary.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: SPEC.md and all four change artifacts moved together; `openspec validate escalate-stage-turn-budget` passes.

pulls.title: feat: Incremental run metrics and partial run preservation
pulls.body:
## What

Implements live run metrics and partial run preservation to ensure cost accounting is visible and data is not lost when a run is aborted or fails midway. Also ensures that `REPORT.md` is updated and snapshot at stage boundaries, and caching wrapper correctly attributes cache hits to the run metrics.

## Why

Fixes #138 and #140 (Incremental run metrics). Closes #139 (duplicate of #137) as `copperhead create` already prompts via `budgetContinuePrompt()` upon budget exhaustion natively.

## Design

- `CachingProvider` adds `cacheHit: true` onto the `Turn` object so that telemetry tracking picks it up and sums it correctly in the final report.
- `src/agent/loop.ts` now emits an `llm-call` event after each turn and maintains a live `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json` via atomic temp file replacement.

pulls.title: Propose readable-schematic-drafting: gate schematic legibility in the create pipeline
pulls.body:
## What

Adds the OpenSpec planning artifacts for `readable-schematic-drafting`: a drafting standard for generated schematics plus a deterministic legibility checker that gates the create pipeline's schematic stage. Planning only, no implementation in this PR.

## Why

Implements the plan for #136, which stays open until the implementation lands (this PR carries planning artifacts only, so no closing keyword). Stage 4's completion contract ([create.ts:155-178](src/commands/create.ts#L155-L178)) requires symbols present, BOM/PINOUT drift-clean, and ERC-clean. All three are statements about the net graph. Nothing in the pipeline says anything about the drawing, so readability is unconstrained output.

The entire geometric guidance in the stage 4 prompt ([create.ts:180](src/commands/create.ts#L180)) is one clause about the 1.27mm grid, and its stated reason is connectivity, not legibility. A recent `create` run produced an electrically clean A4 sheet with refdes and value text drawn over symbol bodies and wires (four labels inside one 10mm box), net labels rotated 90 degrees where a horizontal label had room, all content packed into roughly 40% of the sheet, no signal-flow discipline, ragged power and ground flags, and an empty title block.

This is not cosmetic. The schematic is the primary human review surface for everything the agent claims to have designed, and SPEC.md §3 states the pipeline's end product is "reviewable as a whole". A sheet an engineer will not read makes that guarantee formally satisfied and practically void.

## Design

The change mirrors the [symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts) precedent: read-only checker module, agent tool that reports divergences, prompt obligation to reconcile, stage-completion condition. `verify_symbols` exists because ERC checks the graph but not the parts. The same argument applies one level up: ERC checks the graph but not the drawing.

Load-bearing decisions, full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/design.md):

- **D1: checker, not auto-placer.** An auto-placer would have to emit geometry from code, breaking the invariant that the parser never serializes and KiCad files change only through anchored text replaces. A checker keeps authorship with the agent and adds the missing feedback signal. Kept as a possible successor.
- **D2: groups are plain `(rectangle)` plus `(text)`, not KiCad's native `(group)`.** Native groups are an editor selection aid that draws nothing on a plot, so they would produce none of the captioned boxes that make a sheet readable in an SVG or PDF export. Membership becomes geometric containment, which makes a symbol moved out of its box detectable.
- **D3/D4: conservative geometry.** Symbol body boxes come from `lib_symbols` graphics transformed by `at`/rotation/mirror, excluding pin name and number text so dense MCU symbols are not self-colliding. Text extents use a per-character advance ratio tuned below the true average, so the checker misses marginal collisions rather than inventing them. A false positive costs repair turns and can make the stage contract unsatisfiable; a false negative leaves one tight label on an otherwise organized sheet.
- **D5: nine gating families, four advisory.** Gating: `symbol-overlap`, `text-collision`, `off-grid`, `out-of-frame`, `ungrouped-symbol`, `unlabeled-group`, `group-overlap`, `wire-through-symbol`, `empty-title-block`, each with an unambiguous answer and a single resolving move. Advisory: `low-utilization`, `crowding`, `label-orientation`, `cross-group-wire`, each resting on a threshold. Gating on a threshold invites the repair loop to thrash against a number instead of fixing a defect.
- **D7: `check` reports, `create` gates.** The checker satisfies `check`'s contract but its findings never affect the exit code, because existing repos hold hand-drawn schematics that would light up and `check` is documented CI and pre-commit safe. The binding gate lives where copperhead authored the sheet.
- **D10: off-grid findings reported first.** A model repairing a collision by nudging a symbol can silently break connectivity, since an off-grid pin does not connect.

Coordination note for reviewers: #133 item B.1 proposes a `symbol-verification` obligation kind, and [specs/agent-core/spec.md](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/agent-core/spec.md) here proposes a legibility obligation in the same ledger ([ledger.ts:6-13](src/agent/ledger.ts#L6-L13)). Those two should be shaped together rather than landing as two inconsistent entries.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: `readable-schematic-drafting`. `openspec validate readable-schematic-drafting` passes, 4/4 artifacts complete.

Delta specs:

| Capability | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [schematic-legibility](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/schematic-legibility/spec.md) | New. Drafting standard (group boxes, block partitioning, label-driven inter-block nets, page sizing, title block), check families and severities, finding format and bounded output, config, hierarchy walk |
| [create-pipeline](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/create-pipeline/spec.md) | ADDED: stage 4 states the drafting standard and reconciles findings. MODIFIED: "Content-aware stage completion" gains zero error-severity findings |
| [agent-core](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/agent-core/spec.md) | ADDED: `check_legibility` tool; error findings feed the obligations ledger so `finish` refuses |
| [cli-surface](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/cli-surface/spec.md) | ADDED: `check` prints advisories with the exit code unaffected; `legibility` key in `--json` |

Affected acceptance criteria: the MODIFIED requirement carries the existing AC-15.23 and AC-15.24 scenarios forward unchanged and adds two new ones (illegible sheet does not complete the stage, advisories do not block). New AC-15.x criteria for the drafting standard and the stage gate land in SPEC.md on archive, per [tasks.md](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/tasks.md) 7.2.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (581 passed, 20 skipped, 41 files passed / 1 skipped) |
| OpenSpec validation | `openspec validate readable-schematic-drafting` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | not run | n/a, no provider or loop code touched |

No new or changed tests: this PR adds only markdown planning artifacts under `openspec/changes/`. The suite was run to confirm the branch is clean against `main`, not because this diff could affect it. No pre-existing failures observed.

### Manual test log (required)

n/a. The diff is OpenSpec planning artifacts only, with no runtime behavior to exercise. The implementation PR that follows will carry the manual log against the `create` sandbox, including before and after SVG renders of the fixture schematic.

## Docs

None in this PR. README coverage of the drafting standard and the gate is tracked as [tasks.md](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/tasks.md) 7.1, and the SPEC.md acceptance criteria as 7.2, both landing with the implementation.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] **Spec-gated in**: N/A, no change to tool-list gating.
- [ ] **Verification-gated out**: N/A in this diff. The proposal extends the invariant with a third deterministic checker on the same repair-then-rollback pattern; nothing is implemented here.
- [ ] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: N/A in this diff. Specified as preserved: the checker is a local read-only parse with no provider, key, or network access ([cli-surface delta](openspec/changes/readable-schematic-drafting/specs/cli-surface/spec.md), determinism scenario).
- [ ] **No sexp serialization**: N/A in this diff. Specified as preserved and load-bearing: D1 rejects the auto-placer alternative specifically because it would require writing geometry from code.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A in this diff. The proposal adds a legibility obligation to the existing ledger rather than a parallel path; see the coordination note with #133 above.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A, no transcript, summary, or config-writing code touched.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: `proposal.md`, `design.md`, four delta specs, and `tasks.md` moved together and `openspec validate readable-schematic-drafting` passes. SPEC.md acceptance criteria land on archive per tasks 7.2, which is the point in the workflow where delta specs merge into `openspec/specs/`.

pulls.title: feat(observability): stream turns to the terminal, and record raw traffic and console output per run
pulls.body:
> **Stacked on #132.** Base is `feat/smooth-onboarding-gates`, because `src/agent/loop.ts` and `openspec/specs/SPEC.md` carry both changes. Review #132 first; once it merges I will retarget this to `main` and GitHub will rebase it. The diff shown here is this change only.

## What

Turns now stream to the terminal while they are being generated, on every provider that can stream, and each run writes two new files beside its transcript: `raw.log` (verbatim provider traffic) and `console.log` (everything the run printed).

## Why

Two gaps, both reported as "the logs are not written live".

**Turns arrived in one block.** The OpenAI and Anthropic providers issued one-shot requests, so nothing reached the terminal until a turn finished. On a create-pipeline stage that is minutes of `[turn 4/40]`, a `thinking` status, and a heartbeat that always said "no output yet", because the only streaming signal the loop had (`onStream`, a character count) was fed exclusively by the CLI-backed providers. The loop was already wired for streaming; nothing was feeding it.

**Nothing recorded the raw traffic or the console.** `transcript.jsonl` records what the loop understood: parsed text, parsed tool calls. When a provider returns something the loop mis-parses, the evidence needed to tell a copperhead bug from a provider bug was never written down. And a `do` or `create` run left no record of its own output at all, since only the shell mirrors its session.

## Design

Full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/stream-turns-and-raw-logs/design.md) (D1 to D9). The load-bearing ones:

**`onText` is separate from `onStream` (D1).** A provider that can report progress but not content implements one and not the other, and the heartbeat only ever needed a length. Widening `onStream` would have forced every caller to handle content it does not use.

**The loop line-buffers; the renderer is untouched (D2).** The interactive renderer's invariant is that only complete lines go above the pinned status line. Buffering deltas in the loop and calling the existing `log()` per completed line keeps that invariant, adds no renderer method every implementor would have to write, and hands the console mirror well-formed lines for free. The partial line is flushed in the turn's `finally`, so an aborted or timed-out turn still shows what arrived.

**A streamed turn is not reprinted (D3).** This is the single most visible way the feature could go wrong, every turn doubled, so it is asserted directly rather than left to review.

**`stream_options: {include_usage: true}` is mandatory on the OpenAI path (D5).** Without it a streamed response carries no usage and every turn reports zero tokens, silently breaking the turn budget, the cost table, and AC-8.1. It is the one part of this change where a wrong default is invisible rather than loud, so it has its own wire-contract assertion.

**A streaming refusal downgrades once per provider instance, not per turn (D4).** Compat endpoints are OpenAI-shaped but not OpenAI, and some reject `stream_options` outright. Retrying that turn without streaming turns a hard failure into a formatting difference, and latching means an endpoint that said no is asked exactly once. The match is narrow (a 4xx whose message mentions `stream`) so a genuine 400 still surfaces.

**`raw.log` is JSONL with a per-entry kind and provider (D6).** Runs can fail over between providers mid-flight, so attribution has to be per entry rather than per file.

**Both writers are append-and-forget, serialized, and never throw (D7).** A turn must not wait on a disk write, two concurrent writers must not interleave a half-written line, and a logging failure must not be the thing that fails a run. `runAgentLoop` settles both in its `finally`, so the files are complete before the caller reads them. Caps rather than rotation (D8): 256 KB per entry, 64 MB per file, so a pathological run degrades its own log instead of the disk, and a run's evidence stays in one file.

**The mirror tees the renderer and skips transient output (D9).** `teeRenderer` copies durable lines (logs, turn markers, tool results, heartbeats, the outcome) with ANSI stripped. The status line and its redraws are not mirrored: in a file they would be thousands of copies of the same line.

Invariants preserved: token totals, transcript event shapes, `summary.md`, exit paths, and the redaction guarantee are unchanged, and `check` stays LLM-free and network-free. `raw.log` contains full prompts by design, which is why redaction runs on every write and why `.copperhead/runs/` is gitignored from the first commit (AC-4.3).

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: `stream-turns-and-raw-logs` (`openspec validate stream-turns-and-raw-logs` passes).

Delta spec: `run-observability` (modified).

Acceptance criteria added or extended:

- **AC-8.10 (redaction holds)** extended to `raw.log` and `console.log`.
- **AC-8.11 (turns stream)** assistant text reaches the terminal while the turn is generating and appears exactly once; a provider that cannot stream produces the same output at the end; an endpoint that refuses a streamed request is retried once without streaming, recorded in `raw.log` rather than surfaced as a failure; token accounting is identical on both paths.
- **AC-8.12 (verbatim traffic)** every run writes `raw.log`, one JSON object per line, live, with API payloads for the API providers and CLI messages for the saved-login providers; an unserializable or oversized payload is truncated or noted, never dropped silently or raised.
- **AC-8.13 (console mirror)** every run writes `console.log` live, containing every durable line with ANSI stripped; the status line and in-place redraws are not mirrored.

SPEC.md section 7 also notes that `raw.log`'s redaction is load-bearing rather than incidental, since it records payloads exactly as they crossed the wire.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 603 passed, 20 skipped, 44 files |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass: 0 issues in 138 files |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate stream-turns-and-raw-logs` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | skip: none configured. The API-provider streaming contract is covered by the offline stub servers below; the `claude-code` path was exercised live, see the manual log. |

New or changed tests:

- `test/rawlog.test.ts` (new): JSONL shape and per-entry attribution, redaction, an unserializable payload, truncation at both caps, ANSI stripping, plus an end-to-end run asserting both files land beside the transcript, that the loop passes both callbacks, and that a streamed turn prints exactly once (and a non-streaming provider's turn also prints exactly once).
- `test/openai-provider.test.ts`: the stub servers now answer SSE; the wire-contract test asserts `stream` and `stream_options.include_usage` are actually sent, and a new test drives the non-streaming fallback and its latching.
- `test/openai-compat.test.ts`, `test/budget-efficiency.test.ts`, `test/helpers.ts`: updated for the streamed path.
- The Anthropic prompt-caching test now drives the stream helper and asserts the deltas reach `onText`.

Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: none. The base branch is green (595 passed) and this branch is green (603 passed).

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: **edit** (a copy of the `open-key` fixture). Driven through a real PTY with `--model claude-code`, a full `do`-equivalent run to completion.

**Both files are written, live, beside the transcript:**

```text
$ ls -la .copperhead/runs/2026-07-29T17-43-58-291Z/
console.log        6435
raw.log           63994
summary.md         3034
transcript.jsonl  16143
```

**`raw.log` is JSONL with per-entry attribution (AC-8.12):**

```text
$ head -1 .copperhead/runs/*/raw.log
{"ts":"2026-07-29T17:43:59.541Z","kind":"sdk-message","data":{"type":"system","subtype":"init", ...}}

$ python3 -c "count kinds"
{'sdk-message': 53}
```

53 entries for a 9-turn run, one per CLI message, each carrying its own `kind`.

**`console.log` holds durable lines only, ANSI stripped (AC-8.13):**

```text
$ head -3 .copperhead/runs/*/console.log
copperhead v0.9.0 · kicad-cli 10.0.4 · node v24.18.0
repl · model claude-code (claude-code, via flag) · turns <=40 · main@df90d13 clean
[turn 1/40 · 0 in / 0 out]

$ grep -c "working —\|thinking" .copperhead/runs/*/console.log
0                       # D9: the status line is not mirrored
```

**D3, a turn is not printed twice:**

```text
$ grep -c 'rename net KEY_DAH' .copperhead/runs/*/console.log
0                       # no duplicated turn text anywhere in the mirror
# each assistant turn appears exactly once, at its own [turn N/40] marker
```

**Redaction holds on both new surfaces (AC-8.10):**


pulls.title: feat(onboarding): prepare git in create, offer a way through the dirty gate, stop refusing over copperhead's own artifacts
pulls.body:
## What

Three onboarding gates met a new user with a refusal where copperhead could have acted.

1. `create` prepares git instead of refusing over it: `git init`, the baseline `.gitignore`, a repo-local identity fallback, and the initial commit that stage rollbacks snapshot against.
2. The brief can be given as literal text or as a file, positionally or via `--brief`: `copperhead create "a USB-C powered ESP32 sensor board"` now works in an empty directory.
3. An attended run that meets the dirty-tree gate is offered the fixes the refusal message already described (commit, stash, run anyway, cancel) instead of being sent away to run git by hand.

It also fixes #131: the dirty-tree gate counted copperhead's own audit trail as the user's uncommitted work, so the interactive shell refused to run over its own session log.

## Why

A first-time user's first command was a refusal. `create` in a fresh directory demanded `git init` plus a commit before it would do anything, even though the pipeline's own commits give them that history anyway. `--brief` was a required option, so there was no one-liner. And the dirty-tree gate could only describe the three ways out, never take one.

Issue #131 is the sharpest case. The shell opens its session log at `.copperhead/runs/repl-<ts>.log` before the first turn ([repl.ts](src/commands/repl.ts)). In a repository the user initialized by hand there is no `.gitignore` entry for it, so `git status` reports `?? .copperhead/` and the gate refuses. The repository was clean a second earlier, and all three suggested fixes miss: committing writes transcripts into project history, stashing is undone by the next launch, and `--allow-dirty` disables the protection for the user's real work too.

## Design

**Git preparation is scoped to `create` only.** [`ensureGitReady`](src/util/git.ts) never touches a repository that already has commits beyond committing the brief and an idempotent `.gitignore` top-up. `do`, `sync`, and the shell keep the strict `gitPreflight`: those edit a repo the user already owns, where an implicit initial commit would be a surprise. The brief is committed via a pathspec commit ([`commitPaths`](src/util/git.ts)) so the user's other dirty or staged paths are not swept in, and so a stage rollback's `git clean -fd` cannot delete the file the printed resume command points at.

**The dirty-tree menu never weakens the unattended path.** [`resolveDirtyTree`](src/util/dirty.ts) applies the user's choice and reports whether the run continues under `--allow-dirty`. A cancel, a thrown prompt, and a dismissed prompt all read as cancel, and every unattended run (no TTY, or `--json`) has no chooser at all, so it refuses exactly as before. The prompt is raised before the run's snapshot is taken, and in the shell it is raised before the turn starts, because the shell's key reader is paused for the duration of a turn.

**#131 is fixed by path, not by consulting `.gitignore`.** `.copperhead/runs/` is excluded from the dirty computation directly, so the gate behaves identically before and after the ignore entry lands. The exclusion costs nothing: `restore()` already copies the audit trail across a rollback rather than resetting it with the tree, so it was never work the gate was protecting. `.copperhead/runs/` also joins `GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES`, so every copperhead commit tops the ignore entry up and the transcripts never reach project history (AC-4.3).

`isDirty` and `uncommittedCount` now derive from `dirtyFiles`, so the gate, the file list it prints, and `/git` cannot disagree.

**Two defects found while testing that fix, both fixed here.**

`git()` trims the whole `git status --porcelain` payload, but porcelain encodes index and worktree state in two leading columns and an unstaged modification is `" M path"`. The trim ate that column on the first line only, so the prompt offered to commit `EADME.md`, and any path matched against the list (including the new exclusion) was off by a character. `dirtyFiles` now trims trailing newlines only. It also passes `-uall`, because `git status` collapses a wholly-untracked `.copperhead/` into a single entry that no per-file filter can see inside.

The two session-log tests in [repl.test.ts](test/repl.test.ts) sequenced input with a fixed 30ms sleep. A request turn now resolves the dirty gate first, which shells out to git, so `/quit` could win that race and the turn never ran: 2 of 5 full-suite runs failed on this branch before the fix. They now wait on the turn starting rather than on a clock.

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change: `smooth-onboarding-gates` (`openspec validate smooth-onboarding-gates` passes).

Delta specs: `cli-surface`, `create-pipeline`, `safety-rails`.

Acceptance criteria touched:

- **AC-3.8 (dirty tree)** extended: attended resolution, and "uncommitted changes" now means the user's, so a repository whose only uncommitted path is `.copperhead/runs/` counts as clean.
- **AC-4.3** notes that the baseline ignore file is written before the initial commit of the repository `create` initializes, and that every copperhead commit tops the entry up.

SPEC.md moved with the change: section 2.5 (inputs), section 3 (command list), section 7 (both gates plus the new own-artifacts rule), AC-3.8 and AC-4.3.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass: 595 passed, 20 skipped, 43 files (3 consecutive clean full-suite runs) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | skip: none configured in this environment. Covered by the manual log below, run against a real model. |

New or changed tests:

- `test/create-setup.test.ts` (new): non-git directory, unborn HEAD, empty directory, existing-history repo (only the brief is committed, the user's unrelated file is not), `ensureGitReady` idempotence, and brief materialization.
- `test/dirty-tree.test.ts` (new): each choice's effect on tree and history, a thrown prompt reading as cancel, a clean tree never asking, the repo and unborn-HEAD gates never prompting, the file-list cap, in-loop coverage, and the porcelain-column regression (` M`, `??`, staged rename).
- `test/preflight.test.ts`: the two obsolete `create` refusal cases removed (`create` no longer refuses over them); a new case asserting a hand-initialized repo with a written session log passes the gate while the user's own file still refuses and is the only path named.
- `test/repl.test.ts`: the two session-log tests wait on the turn instead of a fixed sleep.

Known pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: none. `main` is green (572 passed) and this branch is green (595 passed).

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: **edit** (a copy of the `open-key` fixture, plus purpose-built repositories for the git-state gates). Driven through a real PTY so the interactive shell runs as a user meets it, with `--model claude-code`.

**Issue #131, the reported repro:**

```text
$ mkdir board && cd board && printf '# Brief\n' > brief.md
$ git init && git add -A && git commit -m "initial commit"
$ git status --porcelain
                                        # clean
$ copperhead --model claude-code
# shell opens, writes .copperhead/runs/repl-<ts>.log
$ git status --porcelain
?? .copperhead/
# at the prompt: "add a test resistor"
BEFORE: working tree is dirty; copperhead refuses to run on uncommitted changes by default
AFTER:  repl · model claude-code (claude-code, via flag) · turns <=40 · main@e0e2cbc clean
```

**Dirty-tree menu, every branch** (repository with `README.md` modified and `mywork.txt` untracked):

```text
commit      -> committed 2 file(s) as 841f4c5; a rollback now returns here
               git log: chore: save work in progress before a copperhead run; tree clean
stash       -> stashed 2 file(s); restore them with git stash pop; tree clean
run anyway  -> running on the dirty tree; run starts main@073fa98 dirty(2); nothing committed or stashed
cancel      -> the standard refusal with its three fixes, tree untouched, session continues
Esc         -> same as cancel
--allow-dirty -> no prompt at all; run starts main@df90d13 dirty(1)
--json do   -> refuses with no prompt (unattended)
```

The file list before and after the porcelain fix:

```text
BEFORE:   EADME.md
          mywork.txt
AFTER:    README.md
          mywork.txt
```

**Startup gates:**

```text
non-git directory -> not a git repository; copperhead requires git for snapshots and rollback (session continues)
unborn HEAD       -> repository has no commits; copperhead requires at least one commit (session continues)
```

**Full agent run, verification chain intact** (`open-key` fixture, `--model claude-code`):

```text
$ copperhead --model claude-code
> rename net KEY_DAH to KEY_DASH everywhere
  > propose_change   proposal written to openspec/changes/rename-key-dah-to-key-dash/
  v validate_change  validation passed; edit tools are now unlocked
  > edit_file        edited hardware/open-key.kicad_sch (2 occurrence(s) replaced)
  > edit_file        edited docs/PINOUT.md
  v run_erc          ERC: clean
  v check_drift      drift: clean
  > record_decision  decision recorded
  > finish           all gates satisfied; run will commit
committed a5639e77c6 (3 file(s))
done · ERC clean · committed a5639e77c6 · 1m09s · 18 in / 2.8k out

> /check
ERC ok  DRC ok  drift ok
check: all green
```

Edit tools stayed absent until `validate_change` returned, and the run committed only after ERC and drift passed.

**AC-4.3 top-up, in a repository with no `.gitignore` at all:**

```text
$ ls -a | grep gitignore        # none
$ git status --porcelain        # clean
$ copperhead --model claude-code
> rename net EN to ENABLE everywhere
committed c13307251e (3 file(s))

$ cat .gitignore
.copperhead/runs/
.history/
$ git ls-files | grep copperhead/runs
                                # nothing: transcripts stayed out of history
```

**Secret redaction (AC-4.1), live:** a request containing `sk-`, `Bearer`, and `ghp_` tokens landed in the session log as `[REDACTED]`, and a recursive grep of the whole repository directory found no live secret.

**Rest of the shell surface, exercised and correct:** `/help /version /config /git /status /parts /nets /bom /drift /constraints /runs /last /examples /sync /openspec /model /clear /check`, unknown `/nope`, empty Enter, the `/` filter menu, Tab completion, PgUp and PgDn, single ctrl+c clearing a half-typed line, ctrl+c twice quitting, ctrl+d quitting, and a bracketed multi-line paste arriving as one request. In a repository with no KiCad project every read-only command degrades with an actionable message.

## Docs

- `README.md`: the empty-directory one-liner in the quick start.
- `docs/reference/cli.md`: both brief forms, a git-setup section covering what `create` does and why `do` and `sync` differ, and the uncommitted-changes table under `do`.
- `docs/workflows/create-from-brief.md`: the one-liner section, and the manual `git init && git commit --allow-empty` step dropped.
- `openspec/specs/SPEC.md`: sections 2.5, 3, 7, AC-3.8, AC-4.3.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: `edit_file`/`write_file` stay structurally absent from the agent tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates (gated by omission, not prompt text). Unchanged by this PR, and confirmed live in the manual log: the edit tools appeared only after `validate_change` returned.

pulls.title: fix(create): strengthen stage isComplete contracts to prevent false-positive resume (#23)
pulls.body:
## What

Strengthens all 6 shallow `isComplete` probes in [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) so that blank scaffold files, empty directories, and `copperhead init`-generated templates no longer falsely satisfy a stage completion contract, causing the pipeline to silently skip stages.

## Why

Addresses #23. Three independent failure modes compound:

1. `copperhead init` writes SPEC.md with a `## Budgets` heading (placeholder comment only) -- `spec-seed` saw the heading and skipped, leaving zero real budgets recorded.
2. `copperhead init` writes SUBSYSTEMS.md with auto-generated `## Sheet X` headings -- `architecture` skipped with no prose written.
3. `copperhead init` writes BOM.md with `UNVERIFIED` MPNs -- `part-selection` skipped with no real parts chosen.
4. A failed export run leaves an empty `outputs/` dir -- `outputs` skipped before any Gerbers existed.
5. An empty `firmware/` dir -- `firmware` skipped before any source files existed.
6. A blank `DEVPLAN.md` -- `devplan` skipped with no real content.

The consequence observed in the issue: pipeline advanced straight to `outputs`, which refused for a missing `.kicad_pcb`.

Note: `schematic` and `layout-draft` already had robust checks from a prior fix and are unchanged.

## Design

Each probe now checks the stage contract, not just artifact existence:

- **spec-seed**: `## Budgets` heading + at least one non-comment, non-blank content line in the section (a filled section vs. an empty placeholder).
- **architecture**: file exists + at least one heading + at least one non-heading prose line.
- **part-selection**: BOM table exists + at least one row whose MPN column is not `UNVERIFIED` (the exact placeholder `bomTable()` in scaffold.ts emits).
- **outputs**: at least one Gerber file (`.gbr`/`.gtl`/`.gbl`/`.gbs`/`.gbo`/`.gbp`/`.gbd`) inside `outputs/`.
- **firmware**: at least one source file (`.c`/`.h`/`.cpp`/`.py`/`.rs`/`.ino`) inside `firmware/`.
- **devplan**: file exists + at least one heading + at least one non-heading content line.

A new `dirHasFiles()` helper recursively walks a directory for files matching an extension list (used by `outputs` and `firmware`).

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (0 errors) |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (no CLI/packaging change) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (all offline tests pass; kicad-cli failures are pre-existing on this machine) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | skipped (no key) |

New tests: [stage-completion.test.ts](test/stage-completion.test.ts) -- 24 unit tests covering false-positive (scaffold/blank/empty) and true-positive (real content) cases for all 6 stages.

Updated: [create-stage-turns.test.ts](test/create-stage-turns.test.ts) -- mock now emits content satisfying the new contracts (real budget line, prose subsystem, non-UNVERIFIED MPN).

### Manual test log (required)

n/a -- this PR changes only `isComplete` inference logic (no CLI behavior, no agent loop, no provider, no KiCad layer). All observable behavior is exercised by the new unit tests.

## Docs

No README or SPEC changes required -- `isComplete` is an internal resume heuristic, not a user-facing contract.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: no change to the agent tool list; `edit_file`/`write_file` gating is untouched.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: no change to ERC/DRC gating; `schematic` and `layout-draft` probes (which call `runErc`) are untouched.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: this PR touches only `src/commands/create.ts`; no import from a provider or SDK is added.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: no change to `src/kicad/`; file reads are plain `readFile` on docs/dirs.
- [x] **Sync-obligations ledger**: untouched.
- [x] **Secrets**: no new surfaces; no transcript or summary paths changed.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: no spec-level behavior changed; `isComplete` is implementation detail.

## What

The `/pr-review` skill now ends every report with a **Fix prompt**: one copy-pasteable block that restates all surviving findings, the repo invariants, and the verification commands, so the PR author can paste it straight into the coding agent of their choice and have the findings fixed in one pass.

## Why

Today a review comment is written for a human to read and then re-explain to an agent. The findings already carry everything an agent needs (claim, `file:line`, failure scenario, fix), but they are spread through prose with cross-references like "as noted above", so handing them off means re-summarizing and losing detail. Emitting the handoff block as part of the report removes that step.

## Design

Skill-only change, no runtime code.

- [SKILL.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md#L45): the Output contract gains the fix prompt as the report's last section, in-session and in the posted PR comment. It is emitted whenever at least one finding survived verification (including a nits-only report), skipped with a one-line note on a clean report, and required to agree with the findings list above it: same findings, same severities, same order, wording carried over rather than re-summarized.
- [references/fix-prompt.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/references/fix-prompt.md): new reference with the rules and the template. Rules: self-contained (the receiving agent has never seen the review or the repo), a single four-backtick fence (two blocks means two pastes and a lost half), copy-safe plain text (no markdown links, no `@`-mentions or `#123` refs that would fire GitHub notifications when the comment posts), severity-ordered with low findings marked optional, faithful to the verified findings, and scope-bounded (no opportunistic refactors or dependency bumps).
- The template carries the six SPEC.md invariants and the test-determinism rule inline, plus `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` / `npm test`, and tells the agent to report a failure rather than route around it (no deleted assertions, no `.skip`, no loosened thresholds).
- [references/review-checklist.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/references/review-checklist.md): the finding format now notes that its four fields are what the fix prompt is built from, so findings must stand alone.

Version metadata bumped to 2.1.

## Spec / OpenSpec

n/a: tooling only. No spec-level behavior changes, so SPEC.md and the active change artifacts are untouched.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | n/a (no TypeScript changed) |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (no TypeScript changed) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | n/a (no source or test files changed) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | n/a |

No new or changed tests: the diff is three markdown files under [.claude/skills/pr-review/](.claude/skills/pr-review/), which the suite does not cover.

### Manual test log (required)

n/a with reason: this changes only skill instructions, which have no runtime entry point to exercise. Verification is that the next `/pr-review` run emits the section; reviewers can read the template in [references/fix-prompt.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/references/fix-prompt.md) and judge whether a block built from it would be self-contained for a fresh agent.

## Docs

The skill's own reference set is the documentation here. No README or configuration reference mentions `/pr-review`, so nothing else needed updating.

pulls.title: fix(docs): read markdown tables that omit the outer pipes
pulls.body:
## What

`check` now reads PINOUT.md and BOM.md tables that are written without the outer pipes. Before this, a table like `Refdes | Pin | Net` parsed as zero rows, so the drift gate silently checked nothing.

## Why

GitHub-flavored markdown makes the leading and trailing pipes optional. Both of these render as the same table, and both are things a person or the agent may write:

```markdown
| Refdes | Pin | Net |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 | 1 | 3V3 |
```

```markdown
Refdes | Pin | Net
--- | --- | ---
U1 | 1 | 3V3
```

`parseCanonicalTables` skipped any line that did not start with `|`, so the second form produced no tables at all. Everything downstream funnels through that one function (`parsePinoutRows`, `parseBomTable`, `pinoutColumnReport`, `parseCanonicalRows`), which gives two failure modes from the same gap:

**PINOUT.md silently passes.** I put deliberately wrong data in the fixture's PINOUT.md, written without outer pipes, and `check` was happy:

```text
$ copperhead --repo manual-tests/runs/edit check
DRC ✓
drift ✓
```

The doc it just approved claimed `U1:1` is on `COMPLETELY_WRONG_NET` (it is on `3V3`), `U1:2` is on `ALSO_WRONG` (it is on `EN`), plus a pin `U1:99` and a part `R9` that do not exist. `pinoutColumnReport` also reports `hasTable: false` for that doc, so the existing "no Net column" warning cannot fire either: there is nothing to warn about, as far as it can tell.

**BOM.md reports false drift.** The mirror case, with a correct BOM written the same way:

```text
drift: BOM.md claims "R1 absent" but actual is "R1 (10k) in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "R2 absent" but actual is "R2 (1k) in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "U1 absent" but actual is "U1 (ESP32-S3-MINI) in schematic"
```

Every part is listed right there in the file. This is the failure the `parseCanonicalRows` docstring already warns about, where the agent gets pushed to degrade good docs to appease the gate.

Worth noting: a table in that form passes this repo's own markdownlint config with zero issues, so nothing else in the toolchain flags the doc as malformed.

## Design

Three small changes in [bom-table.ts](src/memory/bom-table.ts), all inside `parseCanonicalTables`:

1. A line joins a table when it contains a pipe, instead of when it starts with one.
2. `splitRow` strips one optional leading and one optional trailing pipe before splitting, so both forms yield the same cells.
3. The header is the row directly above the separator row, falling back to the first row when a table has no separator.

Point 3 is what keeps 1 safe. Accepting any pipe-bearing line means a prose line like ``Nets are named `A | B` in the legend.`` sitting directly above a table would otherwise become the group's first row and hide the real header. Anchoring on the separator fixes that case too, which was already broken before this change.

I left `parseMarkdownTables` alone. It is the lenient flat helper and only `bom-export` uses it, so I kept the blast radius on the canonical path that the drift gate actually reads.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. This restores AC-2.3 drift detection for docs the parser was silently skipping, and does not alter the fixed-column contract from design D9.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass for this change (481 passed; see note) |
| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | n/a | not exercised, this path is LLM-free |

Six tests added to `test/bom-table.test.ts` under `optional outer pipes (GitHub-flavored markdown)`: pin rows, column report, BOM rows, both forms agreeing, the prose-with-a-pipe case, and a pipe-free document. Four of the six fail on `main` and pass here. The other two are regression guards that pass both ways.

Note on the full run: I am on Windows, where 9 tests fail on `main` before my change (POSIX path assumptions, CRLF, `chmod 0o000` being a no-op, and `kicad-cli` timeouts). I checked `gating-sync` and `init-check` specifically because they touch drift, and both fail identically with my change stashed, so they are pre-existing here and not caused by this. #94, #76 and #80 are already working on that Windows surface.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: `edit`, via `./manual-tests/setup.sh edit`, with `kicad-cli` 10.0.5 on PATH.

```text
$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit init
created docs\PINOUT.md ... created .git\hooks\pre-commit

# baseline, scaffolded docs (outer pipes)
$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit check
DRC ✓
drift ✓

# PINOUT.md rewritten WITHOUT outer pipes, data deliberately wrong
# before this change:
drift ✓                      <- the bug

# after this change:
drift: PINOUT.md claims "U1:1 net COMPLETELY_WRONG_NET" but actual is "U1:1 net 3V3"
drift: PINOUT.md claims "U1:2 net ALSO_WRONG" but actual is "U1:2 net EN"
drift: PINOUT.md claims "U1:99 exists" but actual is "U1:99 not in schematic"
drift: PINOUT.md claims "R9:1 exists" but actual is "R9:1 not in schematic"

# both docs WITHOUT outer pipes, data correct
$ npm run dev -- --repo manual-tests/runs/edit check
DRC ✓
drift ✓
```

The control matters here: the same wrong data with outer pipes was always caught. The only variable is the pipes.

## Docs

None needed. This makes the parser accept a form the docs already imply is fine, and no documented contract changes.

---

## Invariant checklist

- [ ] **Spec-gated in**: N/A, this does not touch the agent tool list.
- [ ] **Verification-gated out**: N/A, no change to the mutation or repair path.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: the change is pure string parsing in `src/memory/`, no provider, key, or network access added.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: `src/kicad/` untouched.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, ledger and commit gating unchanged.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A, no transcript or summary paths touched.
- [x] **Spec coherence**: no spec-level behavior change, so SPEC.md and the change artifacts stay as they are.

  * Ignores pipe-like content inside fenced code blocks and improves canonical table recognition; prevents prose pipes from interrupting parsing.
