pulls.title: fix(search): keep toolSearch inside the repo and survive symlink loops
pulls.body:
## What

`toolSearch()` in [filetools.ts](src/agent/filetools.ts) no longer returns matches from files outside the repo root, and no longer dies with `ELOOP` when the repo contains a symlink loop.

## Why

Closes #87.

`toolSearch` is the one file tool that does not go through `resolveInRepo`: it walks with `readdir` + `stat` directly. `stat` follows symlinks, so two things went wrong. Both reproduced against the real exported function, not a reimplementation.

**1. It read outside the repo.** Temp repo with `link -> ../outside`, where `outside/leak.txt` contains `needle SECRET outside`:

```text
matches: 3
  b.txt 1 "needle two"
  link/leak.txt 1 "needle SECRET outside"     <-- outside the repo
  sub/a.txt 1 "needle here"
```

The match is reported as `link/leak.txt`, which reads as a repo-relative path, so neither the model nor a human reading the transcript can tell the content came from outside the sandbox.

**2. A symlink loop took the whole tool down.** Temp repo containing `sub/loop -> <repo root>`:

```text
ERROR: ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered, stat
       '.../repo/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/l...'
```

`dispatchTool` catches this so the run does not crash, but `search` is unusable for the rest of the run and the error text gives no hint that a symlink caused it. The walk had no visited set, so a loop was traversed until the OS refused rather than being detected.

This is a sibling of #85 but a separate code path: fixing `resolveInRepo` does not cover `toolSearch`, because `toolSearch` never calls it.

It is reachable without the agent creating anything. A symlinked KiCad symbol or footprint library is an ordinary project layout, and `.history/`, vendored directories, or any user repo may already contain one.

## Design

Three changes inside `toolSearch`, all local to the walk:

- **`lstat` before `stat`.** `lstat` describes the entry itself; `stat` describes the link target and hides that an entry is a link at all. A symlink whose real path lands outside the repo is skipped.
- **`insideRoot()` helper.** Resolves a path with `realpath` and applies the same containment rule `resolveInRepo` uses. The repo root is resolved once up front, because the root itself can sit behind a symlink (on macOS `/tmp` is `/private/tmp`), and comparing a resolved child against an unresolved root would reject everything.
- **A `seenDirs` set of real paths.** A directory whose real path was already walked is skipped, which terminates loops by construction instead of relying on the OS to throw.

Every `stat`/`realpath` call is `.catch(() => null)` with an explicit skip, so an entry that vanishes mid-walk or a broken symlink is stepped over rather than failing the search. That matches how the function already treats unreadable files.

A symlink that stays inside the repo is still followed: those are normal in KiCad projects and must keep working.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. This brings `toolSearch` in line with the containment rule AC-4.2 already states for tool paths, so SPEC.md and the change artifacts stay as they are.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (typecheck runs the same `tsc` project) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 323 pass, 14 skip, 8 pre-existing failures (see below) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run (no key set) |

New tests, in [safety.test.ts](test/safety.test.ts) under `file tools`:

- **the escape**: asserts the exact match list is `['b.txt', 'sub/a.txt']` and that no match text contains `SECRET`. Asserting the full list matters here, since the old behavior returned a plausible-looking extra path rather than an obvious error
- **the loop**: a repo containing `sub/loop -> <root>` returns its single real match instead of throwing
- **guard rail**: a symlink that stays inside the repo is still followed, so symlinked library dirs keep working

**Revert check.** With the new tests in place I restored the original `filetools.ts`: exactly the 2 behavioral tests fail, and the guard rail passes under both implementations, so it is genuinely guarding rather than riding along.

**Pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR:** 8 tests fail in my environment, all `KicadCliMissingError: kicad-cli not found on PATH` (init-check, gating-sync, and the KiCad edit-probe suites). Identical counts before and after this change.

### Manual test log (required)

Sandbox variant used: none. Drove the shipped `toolSearch` directly, which is a closer test of this change than a CLI run: the escape and the loop both happen inside the walk, and calling it by hand lets the probe assert on the returned match list rather than on agent output.

Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node /tmp/srch2.mjs     # escape probe, before
matches: 3
  b.txt 1 "needle two"
  link/leak.txt 1 "needle SECRET outside"
  sub/a.txt 1 "needle here"

$ node /tmp/srch.mjs      # loop probe, before
ERROR: ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered, stat '.../sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/l...'

$ node /tmp/srch2.mjs     # escape probe, after
matches: 2
  b.txt 1 "needle two"
  sub/a.txt 1 "needle here"

$ node /tmp/srch.mjs      # loop probe, after
matches: 1
  sub/a.txt 1
```

## Docs

None needed: the `search` tool's schema, description, and output format are unchanged. A repo with no symlinks behaves identically.

pulls.title: fix(safety): resolve symlinks before the repo-root containment check
pulls.body:
## What

`resolveInRepo()` in [paths.ts](src/util/paths.ts) now resolves symlinks before deciding whether a path is inside the repo, so `read_file`, `write_file` and `edit_file` can no longer reach outside the repo root through a symlink that lives inside it.

## Why

Closes #85.

`resolveInRepo` enforces AC-4.2 with `path.resolve` plus a prefix check. `path.resolve` is purely lexical: it never touches the filesystem. A symlink inside the repo pointing outside it therefore resolves to a path that still starts with the repo root, passes the check, and the following `fs` call follows the link out of the sandbox.

I reproduced this against the real exported tool functions from [filetools.ts](src/agent/filetools.ts), compiled and driven directly, not a reimplementation of the check. Setup is a temp repo containing `link -> ../outside`, with `outside/secret.txt` holding `TOPSECRET`:

```text
READ via symlink  -> "TOPSECRET"                <-- escaped
WRITE via symlink -> wrote link/planted.txt     <-- escaped, file created outside the repo
EDIT via symlink  -> edited link/secret.txt     <-- escaped, secret.txt now "OVERWRITTEN"
```

After the fix, the same probe:

```text
READ blocked: path escapes repo root: link/secret.txt
WRITE blocked: path escapes repo root: link/planted.txt
EDIT blocked: path escapes repo root: link/secret.txt
```

The write path is the more serious half. `toolWriteFile` refuses to overwrite an existing file, but it will create one anywhere the process can write, and `toolEditFile` overwrites straight through the link.

This is reachable without the agent creating anything: a symlinked KiCad symbol or footprint library is a normal project layout, and any repo the user points copperhead at may already contain one. The model only has to walk into it.

## Design

The lexical check is kept exactly as it was, and a realpath-based check is added after it. Two things made this more than a one-line change:

**A write target may not exist yet.** `toolWriteFile` creates new files, so a plain `realpathSync` would throw ENOENT on every legitimate write. `realpathDeepest()` walks up to the deepest ancestor that does exist, resolves that, then re-attaches the remaining segments. Those trailing segments have already been lexically normalised by `path.resolve`, so they cannot smuggle a `..` back in.

**The repo root itself can sit behind a symlink.** On macOS `/tmp` is `/private/tmp`, so resolving only the candidate path would make every path under a temp repo look external and fail the whole suite. Both sides get the same treatment.

`resolveInRepo` still returns the lexical path, so no caller sees a changed value: the realpath is used only for the decision.

One trade-off worth flagging: this is TOCTOU-adjacent. The check resolves the path and the `fs` call re-resolves it, so a link swapped between the two would still be followed. Closing that properly needs `O_NOFOLLOW`-style handling at each call site, which is a much larger change. Given the threat model here is a model wandering into a pre-existing symlink rather than an attacker racing the process, this felt like the right scope, but say the word if you would rather go further.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. AC-4.2 already requires that a tool call with a path outside the repo root is rejected; this closes a hole in the existing implementation rather than changing what the rail promises, so SPEC.md and the change artifacts stay as they are.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (typecheck runs the same `tsc` project) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 323 pass, 14 skip, 8 pre-existing failures (see below) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run (no key set) |

New tests, all in [safety.test.ts](test/safety.test.ts) under `path sandbox (AC-4.2)`:

- **the escape**: read of an existing file through the link, write of a file that does not exist yet through the link, and the link itself, all rejected
- **guard rail 1**, real paths still work: an existing file, a file that does not exist yet, a directory that does not exist yet, and `.` (the root). This is what pins both the "write target may not exist" and "macOS temp dir is itself symlinked" behaviors
- **guard rail 2**, a symlink that stays inside the repo is still allowed, since symlinked library dirs are a normal KiCad setup and must not start failing

**Revert check.** With the new tests in place I restored the original `paths.ts`: exactly 1 test fails, the escape test. Both guard rails pass under the old and the new implementation, which is the point, they prove containment was not achieved by simply refusing more things.

**Pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR:** 8 tests fail in my environment, all `KicadCliMissingError: kicad-cli not found on PATH` (init-check, gating-sync, and the KiCad edit-probe suites). Identical counts before and after this change.

Commands run and outcome:

```text
$ node /tmp/symprobe.mjs        # before the fix
```

pulls.title: fix(redact): redact base64 bearer tokens whole, match scheme case-insensitively
pulls.body:
## What

`redactSecrets()` in [redact.ts](src/util/redact.ts) now redacts a base64 bearer token in full instead of leaving its tail in the run transcript, matches the `Bearer` scheme case-insensitively, and covers npm tokens that contain dashes.

## Why

Closes #83.

`redactSecrets` is the write-time guard for `.copperhead/runs/`: both `Transcript.event()` and `Transcript.writeSummary()` route every line through it. Three shapes got past it, and the first is the dangerous kind because it redacted part of the token and wrote the rest to disk:

1. **Partial redaction of base64 bearer tokens.** The character class `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` excludes `+`, `/` and `=`, which is exactly what standard base64 uses, so the match stopped at the first one:

   ```
   in : Bearer ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=
   out: [REDACTED]+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=
   ```

   A partial redaction is worse than none: it reads as handled in review while the secret is still on disk.

2. **Case-sensitive scheme match.** HTTP auth schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 7235 section 2.1) and real clients log `bearer` and `BEARER`. Both passed through untouched.

3. **npm tokens with dashes.** npm also issues UUID-shaped tokens, and `npm_0123456789abcdef-0123-4567-89ab-cdef01234567` was not matched.

The file's own comment states the patterns are "deliberately broad: losing a few characters of log fidelity beats leaking a key". These are cases where that intent was not met.

## Design

Three small changes to the pattern list, no change to `redactSecrets`'s shape or call sites:

- the bearer character class gains `+/=` and the pattern gains the `i` flag
- the npm class gains `-`, matching how the neighbouring `github_pat_` pattern already allows `_`

The `i` flag is applied only to the bearer pattern. Every other entry is anchored to a literal lowercase prefix (`sk-`, `npm_`, `gh*_`, `github_pat_`) where the casing does not vary, so widening those would only add false-positive risk.

Deliberately not changed, to keep the diff honest about what it fixes:

- `ghp_ ghs_ gho_ ghu_ ghr_` are all already covered: `[pousr]` happens to contain every current GitHub prefix letter.
- `SYNAP_API_KEY` is absent from the patterns, but [synap.ts](src/memory/synap.ts) has no caller yet, so nothing can reach a transcript through it today.
- AWS, Google, Slack and GitLab key shapes are not matched, but copperhead never handles those credentials, so widening to them looked like scope creep. Happy to add if you would rather the net be wider.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No spec-level behavior change. This restores the intent of the existing AC-4.1 secret-redaction rail rather than altering it, so SPEC.md and the change artifacts are untouched.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a (typecheck runs the same `tsc` project) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 324 pass, 14 skip, 8 pre-existing failures (see below) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run (no key set) |

New tests, all in [safety.test.ts](test/safety.test.ts) under `secret redaction (AC-4.1)`:

- a base64 bearer token redacts whole, asserting the tail substrings `SECRETTAIL` and `MORESECRET` are absent rather than merely that `[REDACTED]` appears (the old behavior would have passed a "contains [REDACTED]" assertion)
- `Bearer` / `bearer` / `BEARER` / `BeArEr` all redact
- a dashed npm token redacts
- a guard-rail test: ordinary prose (`the bearer of this note`, `Bearer token missing`, `a npm_ package name`, `see the github_pat docs`) comes back byte-identical, so the widened character classes cannot start eating readable summary text

All tokens in the tests are synthetic and correctly shaped but never valid, matching the convention already in this file.

**Revert check.** With the new tests in place I restored the original `PATTERNS` array: exactly the 3 behavioral tests fail and the prose guard-rail passes under both implementations, so it is genuinely guarding rather than riding along.

**Pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR:** 8 tests fail in my environment, all `KicadCliMissingError: kicad-cli not found on PATH` (init-check, gating-sync, and the KiCad edit-probe suites). Identical counts before and after this change.

pulls.title: Feat/add fab release gate
pulls.body:
## What
Adds an opt-in fabrication release gate (`copperhead check --fab` and `--strict`) to verify hardware designs for manufacturing readiness (routing completeness, BOM readiness, schematic-to-PCB parity, output freshness, and documentation presence).

## Why
ERC and DRC check connectivity and layout rules, but a board can pass both and still be unorderable (e.g. unrouted airwires, BOM rows missing MPNs, PCB refdes/footprint mismatch with schematic, stale or missing gerber exports). `check --fab` provides a deterministic, LLM-free, pre-manufacturing check before sending boards to fabrication.

## Design
- [src/kicad/fab.ts](src/kicad/fab.ts): Implements `runFabGateCheck()` enforcing fabrication release rules (routing completeness via DRC report, BOM readiness via `docs/BOM.md`, schematic/board parity via `sexp` parsing, documentation presence via `.kicad_pro` and `README.md`, and output freshness via `.copperhead/config.json` hashes).
- [src/kicad/sexp.ts](src/kicad/sexp.ts): Extends the s-expression parser to extract board footprints reliably and propagate unparseable states instead of silently returning an empty result.
- [src/commands/export.ts](src/commands/export.ts): Safely records the deterministic `exportHash` during the export pipeline to power the output freshness gate.
- [src/kicad/cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts): Hardens `exportFab` by pre-creating `outputs/gerbers` and `outputs/renders` directories before invoking the KiCad CLI. Fixes a strictness bug in KiCad 8.0 where the CLI fails silently or errors when the output folder doesn't already exist.

## Fixes & Quality Adjustments
- Reconciles CI pipeline behavior following the KiCad PPA version used in CI (8.0), maintaining backward compatibility in `exportFab`.
- Restores the `lib_symbol_mismatch` warning filter for robust DRC/ERC parsing.
- Addresses CodeRabbit review feedback: restricts `recordExportHash` strictly to the correct output tools, catches invalid KiCad format exceptions safely instead of returning an empty result, ensures robust test env-var cleanup, and removes machine-specific absolute path references from `FINDINGS.md`.

## Spec / OpenSpec
Implements OpenSpec change `openspec/changes/add-fab-release-gate/`.

pulls.title: fix(provider): isolate saved-login Claude Code
pulls.body:
## What

Issue #2 requested a Claude Code saved-login provider. PR #37 supplied the initial provider; this follow-up closes the remaining isolation gaps while following the single-turn, saved-login boundary established by PR #1.

- Starts the Claude Agent SDK with user, project, and local settings plus CLAUDE.md disabled.
- Disables skills, plugins, ambient MCP servers, auto-memory, and permission prompts.
- Disables SDK session persistence by default; the existing explicit session-resume mode remains opt-in.
- Strips direct API, custom-endpoint, and Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Mantle, and Anthropic AWS authentication routes from the SDK subprocess while retaining `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
- Preserves the absence of built-in tools, the wildcard deny list, deny-all callback, isolated working directory, and runtime tool-use tripwire.
- Synchronizes the canonical spec, active OpenSpec artifacts, provider documentation, and agent guidance.

## Why

The Agent SDK loads user, project, and local settings by default, and Claude Code authentication precedence can select direct or cloud credentials ahead of a saved subscription login. A reasoning-only saved-login provider must opt out of those ambient surfaces explicitly so host extensions cannot expand the tool boundary and `--model claude-code` cannot silently become a separately billed backend.

## Design

[claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts) now applies five isolation layers at the SDK boundary: empty setting sources, strict empty MCP configuration, no skills or plugins, auto-memory and prompts disabled, and no default SDK transcript persistence. Managed policy remains authoritative, while user-controlled ambient sources are excluded.

The subprocess environment retains the saved-login token and ordinary host environment but removes every supported direct API or cloud routing input. The existing Copperhead agent loop remains the only execution driver, so capability filtering, the obligations ledger, ERC and DRC verification, snapshot rollback, and commit gating remain unchanged. The load-bearing decisions are recorded in [design.md](openspec/changes/add-claude-code-provider/design.md).

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Acceptance criteria: AC-3.10 provider parity, AC-3.11 saved-login isolation, and AC-4.1 secret exclusion.
- Delta spec: [claude-code-provider](openspec/changes/add-claude-code-provider/specs/claude-code-provider/spec.md).
- Canonical behavior: [SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md).

## Testing

| Markdown lint | `npm run lint:md` | pass: 109 files, 0 errors |
| OpenSpec | `openspec validate add-claude-code-provider` and `openspec validate build-copperhead-phase-1` | pass |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | skip: no token or logged-in Claude CLI was available to the test process |

[test/claude-code-provider.test.ts](test/claude-code-provider.test.ts) now covers ambient configuration isolation, session-persistence defaults, saved-login retention, billed-route stripping, and explicit resume behavior. `git diff --check` also passes.

The manual run deliberately used an empty HOME to exercise the unauthenticated rollback path without reading a saved credential store. A successful live Claude Code mutation was not claimed because this environment did not expose `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to the test process.

pulls.title: feat(provider): add LM Studio as a local-model provider (no cloud key)
pulls.body:
## What

Adds a fifth provider, selected by `--model lmstudio` (or `lmstudio:<model-id>`), that runs copperhead against a model on the user's own machine with no API key of any kind. Nothing leaves the machine, no account is billed.

## Why

Closes #63.

Every model backend today is cloud or hosted-session: OpenAI and Anthropic bill an API key per token, Codex and Claude Code reuse a subscription login. All of them require an account with a remote vendor, so there was no way to run copperhead against a local model, ruling out privacy-sensitive designs, offline or air-gapped work, and zero marginal cost iteration.

LM Studio serves local models over the OpenAI chat-completions protocol, tool calling included, so [openai.ts](src/agent/providers/openai.ts) already had the right mapping. It was simply wired shut: `OpenAIProvider` threw without `OPENAI_API_KEY` and exposed no base-URL override, and [makeProvider](src/agent/loop.ts) had no local route.

## Design

Full rationale in [design.md](openspec/changes/add-lmstudio-provider/design.md) (D1 to D7).

**Reuse, not duplication (D1).** The issue offered "parameterize `OpenAIProvider`" or "a thin wrapper". This does neither exactly: `OpenAIProvider` gains an options-object constructor `{ model?, apiKey?, baseURL?, client? }` (matching the `CodexProviderOptions` idiom), and [lmstudio.ts](src/agent/providers/lmstudio.ts) subclasses it, supplying only the endpoint, credential, model discovery, and diagnostics.

Subclassing rather than passing `name` in at the call site is deliberate. `name` is load-bearing: `otherProvider` decides whether a rate-limited run may move to a billed provider purely by comparing it. As a constructor argument, the no-cloud-fallback guarantee becomes something every construction site must get right; as a subclass field it is a compile-time property of the type.

**New test seam.** This adds, for the first time on the OpenAI path, an injectable client. `openai.ts` previously built `new OpenAI({apiKey})` inline inside `chat()`, so it could not be tested without a network. It is now memoized per provider instead of rebuilt per turn.

**Model discovery (D3).** `/v1/chat/completions` needs a `model` field but bare `lmstudio` names none. Rather than send a placeholder, the provider asks the server what is loaded, once per run. The id is not decorative: it reaches run metadata and the response-cache key, and a placeholder would let two different local models share cache entries (the F6 bug). Cost: one localhost request before the first completion.

**Native tool calls only, plus a nudge (D4).** Local models vary in function-calling reliability. A model that writes a call as prose would otherwise produce a turn with no tool calls, which the loop reads as a stall, giving no hint that the model is the problem. So a prose call naming a tool in that turn's catalog returns `Turn.nudge` (an existing field already consumed by the loop; the catalog check mirrors claude-code's `detectMalformedCall`). I deliberately did not add a full text-protocol fallback parser: it would reward models that cannot do what copperhead needs, on a provider whose model quality is already the weak link.

**No auto-detection (D5).** [resolveModel](src/config.ts) is unchanged. It is synchronous and contractually network-free, and an implicit fallback to a local model would silently change which model designed the board.

**No new dependency (D6).** Unlike codex and claude-code, this needs nothing beyond the already-required `openai` package.

### How the invariants are preserved

| Constraint from #63 | How it holds |
| --- | --- |
| No cloud key for a local run | The credential is a literal placeholder, never `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY`. `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` can name any host, so forwarding the ambient key would exfiltrate a live credential. Options are `Omit<..., 'apiKey'>` so no caller can override it. |
| No silent fallback to a cloud provider | Distinct `name` means `otherProvider` returns `null`. No code change was needed: the guarantee is structural. A test asserts it with both cloud keys set. |
| `check` stays LLM-free and network-free | The provider is reachable only via `makeProvider`. The transitive import scan in [init-check.test.ts](test/init-check.test.ts) rejects any `providers/` import and covers the new file with no change. |
| Offline test seam | Injectable `client`, plus an opt-in live entry gated on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_LMSTUDIO=1` (mirrors the `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` gate: a running server cannot be inferred from any credential's presence). |
| Actionable errors | Unreachable server, server with no model loaded, and a model that rejects tool calls. Everything else is re-thrown untouched so `status` survives for `isRateLimit`/`withRetry`; connection detection returns false whenever a numeric status is present. |

## Spec / OpenSpec

New change [add-lmstudio-provider](openspec/changes/add-lmstudio-provider/): proposal, design (D1 to D7), delta specs for `lmstudio-provider` and `cli-surface`, and tasks.

[SPEC.md](openspec/specs/SPEC.md): **AC-3.10** extended to include `--model lmstudio`; new **AC-3.13** (local model: no key, no cloud call, no fallback, actionable local failures, discovered id recorded); the fifth provider noted in the section 2 tree and section 4.4.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (353 passed, 17 skipped) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `COPPERHEAD_TEST_LMSTUDIO` | not run as a suite; the equivalent flow was exercised by hand, see below |

New tests: [lmstudio-provider.test.ts](test/lmstudio-provider.test.ts), 25 offline cases covering routing, endpoint default/override/precedence, construction with no cloud keys, the placeholder credential asserted with both cloud keys set, the no-fallback property, model discovery (probed once, memoized, empty-list error, explicit id skips it), the three actionable errors, 429 passthrough, native tool-call mapping, and the nudge cases. All via an injected fake client: no network, no LM Studio install needed.

Also adds the first offline regression coverage for `OpenAIProvider`, which the new client seam made possible.

The 17 skips are the pre-existing key-gated live entries, skipped because no provider credential is configured in my environment. No known pre-existing failures.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `edit`, built from `test/fixtures/open-key` plus `copperhead init`, committed clean.
- Commands run and outcome: a full `do` run on `google/gemma-4-12b` via LM Studio 0.4.19, with both cloud API keys unset for the process. 10 turns, 42s, ERC clean, one commit. Full artifacts (console log, transcript, summary, diff) are committed in [evidence/](openspec/changes/add-lmstudio-provider/evidence/).

```text
               - [erc] ERC must pass after schematic edits
[turn 9/40]  [run_erc] ERC: clean
[turn 10/40] [finish] all gates satisfied; run will commit
committed caa4d069a7 (3 file(s))
done · ERC clean · committed caa4d069a7 · 42s · 31.4k in / 788 out
```

What this exercised, beyond "it runs":

- **No cloud key, no cloud call.** Both keys were removed from the process environment, so a cloud provider was unreachable even by accident.
- **Model discovery.** The command named no model id; the header and the `run-start` event both record `google/gemma-4-12b`.
- **Spec-gated in.** Turn 3 is where the edit tools appear. Before it they were absent from the tool list sent to the server; the transcript carries the `edit-tools-unlocked` event.
- **Verification-gated out.** Turn 8 is the important one: `finish` was refused until ERC passed after the schematic edit.
- **AC-3.1 and AC-3.7.** Both `global_label` occurrences plus the `PINOUT.md` row renamed, nothing else; no `KEY_DAH` survives. The schematic diff is 2 lines of 272, or 0.74%, against AC-3.7's under 5% bound.
- **AC-4.1.** `grep -rE 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` over the run artifacts matches nothing.

Also verified by hand against a real dead socket with no keys set: the unreachable-server path produces the actionable message naming the endpoint and `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL`, rather than a raw SDK stack trace.

**Live testing caught a real bug**, fixed in e63a063. Run metadata and the response-cache key were fed from the routing string, so a bare `--model lmstudio` run recorded `model: lmstudio` rather than the actual model. That contradicted AC-3.12 and D3 as written (that criterion is now AC-3.13; cursor took 3.12 when it merged first), and meant swapping the loaded model in LM Studio would replay the previous model's cached turns: exactly the F6 bug that `modelId` exists to prevent. The provider knew the answer but only from inside `chat()`, while the cache and metadata block are both built once up front. Fixed with an optional `Provider.resolvedModelId()` that the loop consults; best-effort, so error paths and their timing are unchanged, and the other providers do not implement it and are unaffected.

## Docs

[README.md](README.md) (requirements bullet, `--model` line, a "Local models (LM Studio)" section), [.env.example](.env.example) (`LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` plus the routing table), the [configuration reference](docs/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md) (env-var table, precedence note, routing table, new section), the [CLI reference](docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli.md), the [quickstart](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/quickstart.mdx), the `--model` help in [cli.ts](src/cli.ts), and the `resolveModel` doc comment in [config.ts](src/config.ts).

Three things a user will otherwise get wrong are recorded explicitly: the model must support function/tool calling, a local server is never auto-detected, and the same base-URL override reaches Ollama, vLLM, and llama.cpp.

## Not done

- The `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` to Ollama/vLLM generalization is reasoned from the shared protocol, not demonstrated.
- Evidence is one run on one 12B model. It establishes that the provider, discovery, gating, and verification path work end to end on a local backend; it is not a claim about local-model design quality in general, which varies by model. The safety gates are the backstop either way.

Fixes #66

## What
Adds an end-to-end test harness for `copperhead create`, a deterministic LLM cache replay provider, source fixes for pipeline blockers, and a findings report.

## Why
Fixes #66. Resolves stage 4 wedging and false-green ERC issues, bounds repair cycle consumption on stagnation, handles wire mid-segment connections cleanly, and adds automated E2E CI regression coverage.

## Design
- [response-cache.ts](src/agent/response-cache.ts): Added `CachingProvider` wrapping LLM providers to cache request-response turns in `.copperhead/llm-cache/`. Enforces loud failure via explicit `COPPERHEAD_CACHE_ONLY=1` check inside `CachingProvider.chat()` (L62-L64) — a cache miss in cache-only mode throws a `CacheMissError` immediately rather than falling through to a live network request.
- [tools.ts](src/agent/tools.ts) and [loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts): Separated ERC and DRC repair cycles, tracking `minErcViolations`/`minDrcViolations` as running minimums so repair cycles only reset on genuine improvement — prevents an oscillating violation count (e.g. 5→3→5→3) from looping the repair budget indefinitely.
- [report.ts](src/kicad/report.ts): Updated `normalizeReport` so `report.ok` reflects clean status when error count is 0, preventing non-blocking KiCad 8+ warnings (like `lib_symbol_mismatch`) from blocking clean ERC completion.
- [sexp.ts](src/kicad/sexp.ts): Implemented exact integer point-on-segment geometry math to associate mid-segment connections and prioritize real net names over `PWR_FLAG`.
- [test/e2e/create-full-run.test.ts](test/e2e/create-full-run.test.ts): Added a deterministic 8-stage Create Pipeline replay harness (`spec-seed` through `devplan`). Uses a mock generator provider intercepted in `src/agent/loop.ts` to drive real tool calls (`propose_change`, `write_file`/`edit_file`, `run_erc`, `run_drc`, `check_drift`, `finish`) per stage — each stage's `isComplete()` check genuinely fails against the empty fixture repo first, then passes only after the corresponding tool calls execute and commit. No stage pre-seeds completion docs to skip execution.

## What

End-to-end coverage for `copperhead create`: a full 8-stage run from a real brief (`examples/medium/esp32-soil-sensor.md`) to a committed final stage, a deterministic replay E2E test that keeps that arc covered in CI, minimal source fixes for the issues that blocked a clean run, and a findings report ([FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md)) in the issue #66 legend format.

## Why

Closes #66. `copperhead create` is the headline command but had no coverage proving the whole brief-to-final-stage arc runs clean; prior manual runs repeatedly wedged mid-pipeline and surfaced blockers invisible to the unit suite. This PR turns that manual QA loop into a durable, mergeable artifact: evidence of one clean run, an automated regression net, and a grounded findings report.

## Design

Two pieces, deliberately separable:

1. **Deterministic replay E2E test.** The pipeline is driven against a recorded provider cache (`.copperhead/llm-cache/`) captured from the real run, so the test is repeatable and free. A new `COPPERHEAD_CACHE_ONLY` mode makes the provider fail fast (instead of going to the network) on any cache miss, so the test can never silently become a live-LLM test or hang on a missing recording. The test asserts the failure classes from the issue: it fails loudly if a stage wedges, if an ERC/DRC gate reports clean on an empty artifact (false green), or if the final stage is never reached. CI gating: TBD (offline job by default; exact wiring depends on cache size).
2. **Minimal source fixes, one commit each, each with tests.**
   - `fix(agent)`: the ERC/DRC repair budget counted every failing check, so the schematic stage's prescribed one-part-at-a-time workflow exhausted the budget even while violation counts were falling. The budget now counts only consecutive non-improving checks, tracked independently for ERC and DRC (invariant: bounded stagnation, not bounded attempts). 9 tests, including handler-level scripted violation sequences.
   - `fix(kicad)`: schematic net extraction joined labels and pins to wires only at wire endpoints, ignored `junction` elements, and let `power:PWR_FLAG` shadow real net names. Nets now honor KiCad wire semantics: exact integer point-on-segment attachment for labels/pins/junctions, and PWR_FLAG is excluded from net naming. 5 tests on inline `.kicad_sch` fixtures, each verified to fail against the pre-fix parser.
   - `create`: the layout-draft completion contract used a literal `'## Draft quality'` substring, the same brittleness class as PIPELINE-ISSUES.md Issue 1; migrated to the heading-aware matcher, with contract tests for both spec-seed and layout-draft.

Invariant impact: the replay harness only exercises existing gates and never adds `edit_file`/`write_file` outside a validated proposal (spec-gated in preserved); source fixes strengthen, not bypass, the verification gates (verification-gated out preserved); `check`/`verify` remains untouched and LLM-free.

New or changed tests: test/e2e-replay.test.ts, test/repair-progress.test.ts (9), test/sexp-wire-semantics.test.ts (5), test/stage-contracts.test.ts (6), 2 cache-only cases in test/recovery.test.ts.

pulls.title: fix: complete create pipeline end to end
pulls.body:
## Summary

Implementation for #66. Live `copperhead create` runs exposed three source
blockers:

- every failing ERC/DRC check consumed `maxRepairCycles`, even when the
  violation count improved;
- the drift parser ignored legal mid-segment labels and allowed
  `power:PWR_FLAG` to replace a real net name;
- symbol verification searched only the claimed library, even when an exact
  authoritative vendor symbol was installed under another library prefix.

This branch makes repair exhaustion progress-aware, resolves legal KiCad wire
geometry, discovers exact cross-library symbol matches, and replaces the mocked
orchestrator test with a cache-backed replay through the production agent loop.

## Root cause and impact

Stage 4 builds one part at a time and runs ERC after every part. The old global
counter therefore rolled back a converging design after six failing checks. The
observed sequence was `10, 5, 7, 6, 5, 6`; four checks reduced violations, but
the counter still exhausted.

After that fix reached clean ERC, drift checking still reported connected pins
as `NC`. `pinNets` joined only serialized wire endpoints, while KiCad labels can
legally sit on wire interiors. It also treated the ERC-only `PWR_FLAG` value as
a net name.

The continued live run then found
`RF_Module:ESP32-C3-MINI-1` missing from KiCad's stock library while the exact
part was installed as `PCM_Espressif:ESP32-C3-MINI-1`. The verifier previously
gave the model no actionable replacement. It now scans other installed
libraries only for an exact symbol-name match and returns the complete lib ID;
global fuzzy matching remains excluded.

## Changes

- track consecutive non-improving ERC and DRC reports independently;
- retain bounded rollback after more than five stagnant checks;
- join pins, labels, wire endpoints, and explicit junctions that lie on wire
  segments;
- exclude `power:PWR_FLAG` from net-naming power symbols;
- return exact full lib IDs for symbols installed in another vendor library;
- run deterministic all-eight-stage coverage through the real `runCreate`,
  `runAgentLoop`, tool dispatcher, KiCad probes, ERC/DRC, drift gates, commits,
  stage contracts, and final check;
- add loud production-path failures for an empty ERC-clean scaffold, a wedged
  ERC loop, and an unreached final stage;
- explicitly document the `5 → 4 → 5 → 4` oscillation risk in the OpenSpec
  design;
- add the aggregate `npm run lint` command required by the bounty checklist.

## Deterministic replay evidence

The success test first warms `.copperhead/llm-cache/`, resets its disposable
repository to the exact pre-run commit, and reruns all eight stages with an
inner provider that throws on every call. The second run completes with:

- 16/16 responses served from `.copperhead/llm-cache/`;
- zero calls to the inner provider;
- real clean ERC and DRC;
- real fabrication exports;
- all eight stage commits;
- final `copperhead check` green and process result `{ ok: true }`.

The full console log and generated `.copperhead/runs/REPORT.md` are committed at
`pipeline-run-logs/06-deterministic-8-stage-replay.log`.

## Validation

- `PATH=<KiCad 10.0.5> npm test`: 337 passed, 14 key-gated skipped
- `npm run build`: passed
- `npm run lint`: passed
- `npm run docs:build`: passed
- `openspec validate complete-create-e2e-run --strict`: passed
- `npm pack --dry-run`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- `test/create-e2e.test.ts`: four production-loop cases passed, including the
  cache-only eight-stage replay and all three requested red paths

## Live medium-run status

The acceptance brief is the unmodified
`examples/medium/esp32-soil-sensor.md`. Stages 1–3 are committed. The strongest
recoverable stage-4 checkpoint is sandbox commit `8187328`; it has:

- 10 library-resolved symbols and zero unverifiable libraries;
- zero ERC violations;
- zero DRC violations;
- 43 remaining documentation/schematic drift items;
- 48 ESP32 pin mismatches against the official 53-pad vendor symbol.

The run is deliberately not claimed as stage-complete. After adopting the
official `PCM_Espressif:ESP32-C3-MINI-1` lib ID, the model twice emitted invalid
JSON for the large anchored edit needed to reconcile its pin map. Copperhead
corrected once, then safely rolled back and preserved the valid partial work in
recoverable stashes. Continuing the same retry loop would not be a reliable
acceptance result.

The live medium run has therefore not reached stages 5–8. The clean checkpoint,
response cache, transcripts, and stashes remain available for a future retry
after the provider's large structured-edit handling is hardened. The green
eight-stage evidence above remains the deterministic production-loop replay.

## Checklist

- [x] Minimal source fixes covered by focused tests
- [x] Non-mocked, cache-backed all-eight-stage production-loop replay
- [x] Wedged-stage, false-green ERC, and unreached-final-stage failures
- [x] Replay console log and `.copperhead/runs/REPORT.md` attached
- [x] Findings report included
- [x] Offline suite, build, lint, docs, strict OpenSpec, and package validation
  green
- [x] Exact cross-library symbol discovery with focused regression coverage
- [ ] Medium-complexity live run reaches all eight committed stages and exits 0

Closes #66

pulls.title: feat: add support for Cursor Agent CLI as a saved-login provider
pulls.body:
## What

Adds `--model cursor` and `cursor:<model-id>` so copperhead runs the agent loop through the local Cursor Agent CLI (`agent login`) without OpenAI or Anthropic API keys.

## Why

Closes [#54](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/issues/54). Users with Cursor CLI auth should get the same saved-login pattern as `codex` and `claude-code`: an external CLI as a reasoning-only backend while copperhead keeps spec-gating, ERC/DRC, drift checks, and git gates.

## Design

- New [cursor.ts](src/agent/providers/cursor.ts): subprocess to `agent` (override via `COPPERHEAD_CURSOR_PATH`, default `agent` on PATH) with `--mode plan`, `--sandbox enabled`, `--print --output-format json`, `--trust`, isolated temp workspace, and `--resume` for multi-turn sessions. See [design.md](openspec/changes/add-cursor-cli-provider/design.md).
- Shared JSON tool protocol in [tool-protocol.ts](src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts), extracted from [claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts) without behavior change for claude-code.
- Tripwire: fail the run if CLI JSON output indicates native tool execution or file mutation (claude-code-style enforcement, not Codex sandbox).

pulls.title: docs: add code of conduct, security policy, and issue templates
pulls.body:
## What

Adds the three community health files GitHub's community standards checklist flagged as missing: a code of conduct, a security policy, and issue templates. Also enables private vulnerability reporting on the repo so the advisory link in the security policy resolves.

## Why

The repo scored 5/8 on GitHub's community standards checklist. Description, README, Contributing, License, and the pull request template were already in place; Code of conduct, Security policy, and Issue templates were not. Without a security policy there was no stated private channel for reporting a vulnerability, so the only path was a public issue.

## Design

[SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md) is written against this project's actual threat model rather than as boilerplate. copperhead is an agent that edits files and spawns subprocesses, so a lot of alarming-looking behavior is intended. The policy states the line explicitly:

By design, not a vulnerability:

- Editing files inside the repository you point it at (file tools are sandboxed to the repo root, so a path escaping that root is a vulnerability, but edits inside it are the product).
- Running `kicad-cli` as a subprocess.
- Sending the contents of files it reads to the configured model provider.

Treated as vulnerabilities, drawn from the SPEC.md invariants:

- A path escaping the repo root.
- An API key appearing unredacted in a transcript under `.copperhead/runs/`, in a run summary, or in terminal output (AC-4.1).
- `copperhead check` calling an LLM or touching the network.
- A mutation reported as complete without ERC (and DRC when the board changed) having passed.

Scope excludes KiCad, `kicad-cli`, and the model providers, with an explicit carve-out for a dependency issue reachable through copperhead in a way the upstream advisory does not cover.

[CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) is Contributor Covenant 2.1 verbatim, with the enforcement contact set to the `package.json` author address.

The issue forms collect what a copperhead report actually needs to be actionable: which command (`create` / `do` / `check` / `init` / `sync`), which model backend (and "not applicable", since `check` is LLM-free), and the `kicad-cli` plus Node versions. [feature_request.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml) points reporters at SPEC.md and ROADMAP.md first and asks whether the proposal touches either invariant. [config.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml) disables blank issues and links to docs, Discussions, and the advisory form.

Note on the form schema: GitHub rejects a field that sets both `render` and `validations.required`. The "Steps to reproduce" textarea is required, so it does not set `render`; the optional "Output" textarea uses `render: shell`.

## Spec / OpenSpec

None. Docs and repository metadata only. No source file changes, so no acceptance criteria or delta specs move.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (no source changes) |
| Build | `npm run build` | n/a, no source changes |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass, 328 passed / 14 skipped across 29 files |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CODEX` | n/a, docs-only change |

Additional checks run for this PR specifically:

- `npm run lint:md`: 0 errors across 119 files, including the two new markdown files.
- Both new markdown files and all three YAML files verified em-dash-free.
- All three issue templates parsed with `js-yaml`, and asserted that no field combines `render` with `validations.required`.

No new or changed tests. No known pre-existing failures.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): n/a
- Commands run and outcome: n/a. This PR changes only markdown documentation, GitHub issue form YAML, and one repository setting. It touches no CLI behavior, no agent loop code, no provider, and no part of the KiCad layer, so there is nothing to exercise in the manual-tests sandbox. The verification that does apply to it (markdown lint, YAML parse, issue form schema constraints) is recorded above.

The issue forms cannot be rendered until they are on the default branch. Confirm they render as expected at the repository's "New issue" page after merge.

## Docs

- New: [.github/SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md), [.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml), [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml), [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml).
- Changed: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) now links to the code of conduct and routes security reports to the policy instead of the issue tracker.

### Repository settings

Private vulnerability reporting was enabled via `PUT /repos/chouhanindustries/copperhead/private-vulnerability-reporting`, which is what makes the advisory link in SECURITY.md resolve.

One checklist item remains and cannot be done from a PR: **"Repository admins accept content reports"** has no REST API. A repository admin must enable it under Settings, Moderation options, Reported content.

Follow-up worth considering separately: secret scanning, push protection, and Dependabot security updates all report `disabled` on this repo.

pulls.title: fix(create): harden the claude-code pipeline (drift gates, KiCad/git resilience, observability)
pulls.body:
## What

Hardens the `claude-code` `copperhead create` pipeline end to end: fixes the drift
gate false-positives that trapped the finish loop, makes the KiCad/git commit path
survive KiCad 10 and rollbacks, adds symbol verification against the real KiCad
libraries, and adds whole-run observability (heartbeat, per-stage cost table,
printed resume point). This PR carries the two earlier pipeline commits plus the
new hardening commit as one change.

> Update: a follow-up commit addresses the automated `/pr-review` findings F1 to F6
> (restore the SPEC.md §1.3 structural edit-tool lock, gate resume-commit on
> ERC-clean, route the drift BOM read through header-name resolution, keep
> footprint case, harden the temp-dir sweep, and add retry/resume tests that
> surfaced and fixed an `isManagedPath` trailing-slash bug). See PIPELINE-ISSUES.md
> Issues 18 to 20.

## Why

Driving `copperhead create --brief brief.md --model claude-code` to completion on
the USB-C power breakout brief surfaced a batch of blockers and token sinks: a
correct schematic could not clear the finish gate (drift misread auxiliary tables,
positional columns, and byte-exact value encodings), the commit aborted on KiCad's
git-backed `.history/`, a rollback wiped the scaffold and cascaded the retry,
leaked temp dirs filled the disk, and a malformed tool call was silently dropped so
the model misdiagnosed a broken tool. Each is logged with root cause and fix in
[PIPELINE-ISSUES.md](PIPELINE-ISSUES.md) (Issues 6 to 17; the I1 to I13 identifiers
reference `../copperhead-test/run-logs/ISSUES-FOUND.md`).

## Design

Grouped by concern (full detail in [PIPELINE-ISSUES.md](PIPELINE-ISSUES.md)):

- **Drift gate correctness** ([drift.ts](src/memory/drift.ts),
  [bom-table.ts](src/memory/bom-table.ts)): `parseCanonicalTables` keeps only the
  Refdes/Pin contract table (ignores a quiescent-current roll-up or net legend);
  `parsePinoutRows` resolves Refdes/Pin/Net by header name, not a fixed index;
  `normalizeValue`/`foldEncodings` compare values and footprints semantically (fold
  `>=`, `ohm`, `u`, the inch mark, smart quotes, case, and spacing) so only a real
  value difference is flagged.
- **Symbol verification** ([symlib.ts](src/kicad/symlib.ts), `verify_symbols` in
  [tools.ts](src/agent/tools.ts)): reads the installed `.kicad_sym` libraries and
  reports pins that diverge from the canonical part plus lib_ids that do not exist
  in this KiCad version. Verification (not blind auto-splice) because KiCad renames
  symbols across versions. The tool is read-only (`requiresUnlock: false`).
- **KiCad/git resilience** ([git.ts](src/util/git.ts),
  [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts)): `ensureIgnored` appends `.history/` to
  `.gitignore` before every `git add -A`; the KiCad project is re-scaffolded per
  stage attempt so a rollback does not cascade; `sweepStaleTempDirs` reclaims leaked
  scratch dirs (age-gated); `assertDiskSpace` preflights free space.
- **Loop/provider** ([loop.ts](src/agent/loop.ts),
  [claude-code.ts](src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts),
  [types.ts](src/agent/types.ts)): `detectMalformedCall` returns a re-emit nudge via
  a new `Turn.nudge` when a turn names a catalog tool but parses no call; the turn
  timeout budget resets on a productive turn; a session/usage limit is detected as a
  schedulable pause; opt-in session resume sends only the new-message delta.
- **Observability** ([render.ts](src/agent/render.ts),
  [response-cache.ts](src/agent/response-cache.ts)): a periodic
  elapsed-plus-streamed heartbeat, a per-stage cost table with a TOTAL, and a
  printed resume command on any stop.

Safety-gate invariants are preserved: `verify_symbols` is read-only and the KiCad
parser stays read-only (symlib only reads `.kicad_sym`); the drift changes are pure
parsing and comparison reachable from `check` with no provider or network use; the
commit path still refuses while obligations are open and still rolls back to the git
snapshot on a failed verify.

## Spec / OpenSpec

No SPEC.md acceptance criteria change: these are bug fixes and robustness on the
existing create pipeline, plus one read-only inspection tool (`verify_symbols`) and
observability output. No `edit_file`/`write_file` gating, ERC/DRC gating, or
obligations semantics change. An OpenSpec change artifact for `verify_symbols` as a
first-class capability is a reasonable follow-up if the team wants it specced.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass (exit 0) |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass (exit 0) |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (288 passed, 14 skipped, 29 files) |
| Live-LLM (opt-in) | keyed on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | not run (no key in this environment) |

New or changed tests: `test/corruption-guard.test.ts`, `test/symlib.test.ts`,
`test/tmp-sweep.test.ts`, `test/session-limit-disk.test.ts`,
`test/observability.test.ts`, plus additions to `test/bom-table.test.ts` (canonical
table isolation, header-name columns, semantic value equality) and
`test/claude-code-provider.test.ts` (malformed-call nudge). No known pre-existing
failures. `markdownlint-cli2 PIPELINE-ISSUES.md`: 0 errors.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): `create`
- Commands run and outcome:

These fixes were derived from full end-to-end `create` runs on the USB-C power
breakout brief, captured in `../copperhead-test/run-logs/create-run-03..06.log`,
which is where each Issue was observed. In this session I rebuilt `dist/` and
smoke-checked the built CLI; a fresh full end-to-end `create` on the fixed build
(live provider plus a local `kicad-cli`) is recommended before merge to confirm the
finish gate now clears on a correct schematic.

```text
$ npm run build
> tsc -p tsconfig.json   (exit 0)

$ node dist/cli.js --help
Usage: copperhead [options] [command]
Cursor for circuit boards: an AI agent for real KiCad repositories
...   (exit 0)

$ npm test
Test Files  27 passed | 1 skipped (28)
     Tests  284 passed | 14 skipped (298)
```

## Docs

- [PIPELINE-ISSUES.md](PIPELINE-ISSUES.md): new Issues 6 to 17 with root cause and
  fix for every change in this PR.
- Extensive doc comments added at each new function and tool (`verify_symbols`,
  `normalizeValue`/`foldEncodings`, `parsePinoutRows`, `ensureIgnored`,
  `sweepStaleTempDirs`, `sessionLimit`, `assertDiskSpace`, `detectMalformedCall`,
  the heartbeat and cost-table helpers).

---

## Invariant checklist

- [x] **Spec-gated in**: preserved structurally (corrected after review F1). The loop
  advertises `availableTools(ctx)`, so `edit_file`/`write_file` are omitted from the
  advertised tool list until a proposal validates, per SPEC.md §1.3; `dispatchTool`
  is the live gate on top. `verify_symbols` is a read-only inspection tool.
- [x] **Verification-gated out**: preserved. The commit/rollback path still ends in
  ERC (and DRC when the board changed) with repair then rollback to the snapshot;
  the I6/I7 fixes only make that path robust to KiCad `.history/` and a wiped
  scaffold.
- [x] **`check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free**: the drift and bom-table
  changes reachable from `src/commands/check` are pure parsing and comparison; no
  provider, key, or network is introduced.
- [x] **No sexp serialization**: preserved. `src/kicad/symlib.ts` only reads
  `.kicad_sym`; KiCad files are still edited only via anchored text replace.
- [ ] **Sync-obligations ledger**: N/A, not touched.
- [ ] **Secrets**: N/A, redaction and `.gitignore` for `.env`/`.copperhead/runs/`
  unchanged (this PR adds `.history/` to project `.gitignore`, unrelated to secrets).
- [x] **Spec coherence**: no spec-level behavior changed, so SPEC.md and change

pulls.title: feat(spice): parse simulation blocks and compile assertions
pulls.body:
## What

Adds the parser and compiler for opt-in `## Simulation` blocks in `SUBSYSTEMS.md`.

The new pure KiCad-layer module parses sheet or net scopes, analysis type, driven sources, and assertions. It compiles the closed assertion grammar to ngspice `.meas` fragments and reports parse failures with the original Markdown line number.

## Why

The planned SPICE gate needs a safe input boundary before netlist export or ngspice execution can be added. Accepting arbitrary control text would make the gate difficult to review and unsafe to assemble into a deck.

Closes #10.

## Design

- The parser is line-oriented so every failure points back to the source line.
- It accepts one scope, one analysis, repeated `source` or `sources` entries, and one or more assertions.
- Fenced examples, HTML-commented blocks, non-field narrative, and lower-level Markdown sections are not treated as live Simulation input.
- Raw dot commands such as `.control` are rejected before any process layer is involved.
- SI values are parsed to normalized numbers while retaining the original safe SPICE literal for deck generation.
- `between` requires both bounds to omit units or use the same unit.
- Each assertion produces one value measure plus bound-margin measures. `between` emits separate lower and upper checks. The returned check metadata distinguishes inclusive bounds from strict `<` and `>` bounds.
- `corner(net)` is limited to AC analysis and compiles to the first 3 dB crossing.
- The module has no filesystem, subprocess, provider, or network dependency.

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Active change: `openspec/changes/add-spice-verification-gate`
- Completes tasks 1.2 and 1.3.
- Clarifies the line-oriented block fields in the `spice-verification` delta spec.

## Testing

## What

Bypasses the pre-commit hook during agent-driven commits via the `--no-verify` flag.

## Why

Fixes the remaining deadlock vectors in issue #21. The pre-commit hook exists to prevent human hand edits from causing drift. pulls.title: chore(pr-review): add coverage/change metrics and strengthen the checklist
pulls.body:
## What

Extends the `pr-review` skill ([.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md), now v1.2) so a review quantifies the change and how much of the *new* code is actually exercised, and closes gaps a recent review pass missed. Skill-only change, no source touched.

## Why

A recent pr-review pass approved a provider PR whose tool-call parser had a real defect: its fenced-block regex truncates the JSON when a tool's content itself contains nested code fences (e.g. `write_file` writing a markdown doc). Mock-only, happy-path tests sailed past it, and the checklist had no rule that would have caught it. This adds the missing coverage accounting and the adversarial-input discipline, plus several smaller review-quality gaps surfaced in the same session.

## Design

The skill keeps its existing shape (gather, general review, invariants, spec coherence, verify, output) and gains:

- **Coverage and change metrics** (new step 5): net vs new-code split, test-to-code ratio and suite delta, and diff coverage of changed `src/` lines (measured with `@vitest/coverage-v8` when available, else a cited manual map), an untested-surface list, and a compact metrics block in the output. The repo ships no coverage tooling today, so the measured path is opt-in (`npm i -D @vitest/coverage-v8`) with an explicit "not measured" fallback rather than a fabricated number.
- **Adversarial inputs for parser/format code** (step 2): nested delimiters, empty/one/many, large, unicode, malformed. Aimed squarely at the class the missed bug belonged to.
- **Severity rubric** (high/medium/low) so a level means the same across runs.
- **Every finding carries a fix or a reproducing test.**
- **CI and mergeability snapshot** (`gh pr checks`, `mergeable`) in gather and the metrics block.
- **Prior-pass dedup and self-review disclosure**; skip generated/vendored files in the read-every-hunk rule.
- **Mock-only runtime code is flagged**; new tests must be deterministic and must assert.
- Optional `ReportFindings` structured output alongside the GitHub comment.

## Testing

pulls.title: chore(deps): bump @anthropic-ai/sdk to ^0.113.0, declare claude-agent-sdk optional
pulls.body:
## What

Bumps `@anthropic-ai/sdk` from `^0.39.0` to `^0.113.0`, declares `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (`^0.3.217`) as a real `optionalDependency`, and adds an `overrides` entry pinning `zod` to `^4.0.0`. Packaging only: no source changes ([package.json](package.json), [package-lock.json](package-lock.json)).

## Why

This unblocks the saved-login `claude-code` provider (#37) so its Agent SDK is a declared, installable optional dependency instead of an undeclared manual install requiring `--legacy-peer-deps`.

`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` hard-peers `@anthropic-ai/sdk >=0.93.0`, which conflicted with the pinned `^0.39.0` and failed `npm install` even for an `optionalDependency` (npm `ERESOLVE` fails the whole tree on a peer conflict). Bumping the core SDK satisfies that peer.

Intended merge order: this PR first, then #37 rebases on top and drops its "manual install / `--legacy-peer-deps`" docs.

## Design

Two peer conflicts had to clear:

1. `@anthropic-ai/sdk`: the `0.39` to `0.113` jump needs no source change. [anthropic.ts](src/agent/providers/anthropic.ts) uses only the stable `messages.create` surface (content blocks, `tool_use`, `usage`, ephemeral `cache_control`), and its response handling is already loosely typed, so typecheck and the full suite stay green.
2. `zod`: `claude-agent-sdk` peers `zod ^4`, while `openai` peers `zod ^3.23.8` (optional). These are incompatible majors, so npm cannot hoist a single `zod` (a second `ERESOLVE`). copperhead imports `zod` nowhere (verified: `grep -rn zod src/` is empty), and openai's zod peer is optional, used only by its structured-output helpers that copperhead never calls. So `overrides` forces one `zod@4` across the tree: it satisfies the required peer and overrides openai's unused optional one. Result: `zod@4.4.3` deduped across `openai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.

Caveat: `overrides` is a blunt instrument. If copperhead ever adopts openai's zod-based helpers, they would run against zod 4 and could break. Not a concern with the current code.

Note on `npm audit`: the optional `claude-agent-sdk` subtree (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `@hono/node-server`, `smol-toml`) raises `npm audit` from 6 to 9 advisories. These install only for users who opt into `--model claude-code`, not the default install.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | pass (200 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail) |
| Install (no flag) | `npm install` | pass, exit 0 (previously `ERESOLVE` without `--legacy-peer-deps`) |

Also verified `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` now resolves and exports `query` (`require.resolve` plus `typeof m.query === 'function'`). No new or changed tests: this is a packaging-only change, and the existing suite exercises the bumped `@anthropic-ai/sdk` through the offline provider tests.

### Manual test log (required)

- Sandbox variant used (`create` / `edit`): n/a
- Reason: packaging-only change (`package.json` / `package-lock.json`), no CLI behavior, agent loop, provider source, or KiCad path touched. The runtime effect (the optional SDK resolving) is covered by the `require.resolve` check above.

## Docs

None. The `claude-code` setup docs live in #37 and will be updated there once this merges (dropping the `--legacy-peer-deps` guidance).

---

## What

Resolves cross-platform Windows compatibility issues in the unit/offline tests, helper shims, and CLI missing-executable preflight checks.

## Why

Windows users running the test suite or CLI experienced crash failures because of hardcoded Unix shell commands (`mkdir -p`, `grep`), hardcoded Unix path assertions in tests, CRLF line endings in git stashes, and `execa` returning exit code 1 or 9009 instead of standard `ENOENT` codes on Windows when executables are missing.

## Design

- Introduced `isNotFoundError` and `isOpenSpecNotFoundError` helper functions to catch Windows missing-command exit codes alongside `ENOENT` codes in [cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts) and [cli.ts](src/openspec/cli.ts).
- Normalized path assertions in [safety.test.ts](test/safety.test.ts) using `path.resolve` to handle Windows path prefixes and directory separators.
- Normalized line endings in [budget-efficiency.test.ts](test/budget-efficiency.test.ts) to support git's CRLF stashing behavior on Windows.
- Substituted the Unix `mkdir -p` command with Node's cross-platform `mkdir` in [init-check.test.ts](test/init-check.test.ts) and corrected the PATH delimiter using `path.delimiter`.
- Replaced the Unix `grep` subprocess call with the project's native, pure-JS `toolSearch` utility in [agent-integration.test.ts](test/agent-integration.test.ts).

pulls.title: feat(mcp): add copperhead mcp server exposing the gated pipeline to MCP hosts
pulls.body:
## What

Adds `copperhead mcp`, a stdio MCP server that exposes the copperhead pipeline to any MCP host (Claude Code, Codex, and others) as four opaque, outcome-level tools: `copperhead_check`, `copperhead_do`, `copperhead_sync`, and `copperhead_init`. Closes #40.

## Why

Hosts already point coding agents at KiCad repos through raw MCP servers that expose ungated file edits, so a host can rewrite a `.kicad_sch` with no spec gate, no verification, and no rollback. copperhead's invariants only protected people entering through the CLI. This server extends them to MCP hosts: the only way to mutate a repo is to run a full gated pipeline, so no sequence of calls can skip spec-gating or verification.

## Design

Opacity is the security boundary. The server exposes outcomes, not operations: there is no file-edit, no raw-KiCad, and no partial-loop tool to reach around. Each tool dispatches straight into the existing command entry points ([runCheck](src/commands/check.ts), [runAgentLoop](src/agent/loop.ts), [syncVerify / syncResolve](src/commands/sync.ts), [runInit](src/memory/scaffold.ts)), so the invariants (dirty-tree refusal, path sandbox, secret redaction, budgets, rollback) are inherited by construction. The server is a transport adapter, not a reimplementation.

Behavior worth calling out:

- `copperhead_do` runs non-interactively and returns a summary with status (`committed`, `rolled_back`, or `refused`), commit, files touched, verification, and transcript path. A rollback is a successful tool call whose result says `rolled_back`, not a protocol error.
- Progress is streamed as MCP progress notifications so long runs do not time out. All logs go to stderr; stdout carries only the JSON-RPC stream.
- `copperhead_do`, and `copperhead_sync` with `resolve: true`, refuse fast with a typed error naming the missing variable when no key resolves. `check` and `init` work without a key.
- Mutating tools are serialized per repo with a typed busy error; `check` runs concurrently.

The server lives in [src/mcp/server.ts](src/mcp/server.ts), with a companion Claude Code skill under [integrations/](integrations/claude-code/copperhead/SKILL.md).

## Spec / OpenSpec

OpenSpec change `add-mcp-server`: new `mcp-server` and `cli-surface` delta specs, with `tasks.md` checked off. The `fab` and `strict` inputs on `copperhead_check` are deferred until `check` itself learns them (changes #9 and #41), and this is stated in the spec so the tool surface stays honest rather than advertising a capability it cannot yet honor. Note: `openspec validate` was not run locally (the openspec CLI is not installed in my environment), so a reviewer should confirm it.

## Testing

### Automated test status

| Check | Command | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |

pulls.title: Add supplier BOM export (jlcpcb/digikey/mouser) via
pulls.body:
## What

fixes #42 


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8319f8fc-a071-4285-bc0e-c234abb94412


Adds a new `copperhead export bom --supplier <jlcpcb|digikey|mouser>` command that turns the drift-checked [docs/BOM.md](docs/BOM.md) into a file each supplier accepts without hand-editing: a JLCPCB assembly CSV, or a DigiKey/Mouser cart-upload CSV with computed order quantities. The `create` stage-6 outputs package now also emits the JLCPCB file automatically.

## Why

`create` produces a generic `BOM.csv`, but no supplier accepts it as-is: JLCPCB wants its assembly format, DigiKey and Mouser want cart-uploadable lists with quantities. Users close that gap by hand today, which is exactly the distance between "orderable BOM" (the current claim) and an actual order. This implements the `add-supplier-bom-export` OpenSpec change (roadmap Phase 2, item 2).

## Design

- Source of truth is BOM.md, not the schematic (design D1): BOM.md carries the MPNs and sourcing flags and is already drift-checked, so the export inherits that consistency guarantee. The markdown table parser (`parseMarkdownTables`) is reused from [drift.ts](src/memory/drift.ts); [bom-export.ts](src/kicad/bom-export.ts) layers a header-aware `parseBom` on top, so optional `Manufacturer` and `LCSC` columns are matched by name regardless of position.
- `export bom` is a new top-level command, not a `check` flag (design D2): export writes files and `check` must never write, so the read-only/write split stays at the command boundary.
- Unorderable rows (no MPN, or still flagged `UNVERIFIED`) are excluded and reported in a warnings footer, never silently included (design D3). `--include-unverified` opts flagged-but-MPN'd rows back in, but never MPN-less rows.
- Quantity is `ceil(perBoard * boards * (1 + spares/100))`, raised to `perBoard * boards + 2` for passive footprints (`R_`/`C_`/`L_`) when the percentage yields less (design D4). The percentage math runs in whole units with a small epsilon, so an exact result like 110 does not ceil to 111 (`100 * 1.1` is `110.00000000000001` in IEEE-754).
- Deterministic, LLM-free, network-free: a pure transformation of repo state, safe anywhere `check` is safe. It refuses with a drift hint when BOM.md disagrees with the schematic (the drift check uses the read-only s-expression reader, so no kicad-cli is needed).

## Spec / OpenSpec

- Change: `add-supplier-bom-export` ([proposal](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/proposal.md), [design](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/design.md), [tasks](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/tasks.md)).
- Delta specs: new capability `supplier-bom-export` (the `export bom` command, per-supplier formats, quantity arithmetic, exclusion rules); modified `cli-surface` (the command and its flags) and `create-pipeline` (stage 6 emits the JLCPCB file).
- All 13 tasks in `tasks.md` are checked off. One documented deviation from task 1.4: the warnings footer goes to stderr and `--json` only, not embedded as CSV comments, because strict supplier upload parsers reject comment lines.

## Testing

| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | pass |
| Unit + offline | `npm test` | 151 pass, 7 skip, 7 fail (all pre-existing, see below) |

New tests: [test/bom-export.test.ts](test/bom-export.test.ts), 21 passing: header-aware parsing, quantity arithmetic (including the two spec scenarios, 44 and 3), the three golden supplier formats, exclusion and `--include-unverified` behavior, flag validation, end-to-end file write, drift refusal, and a network-free guard.

Pre-existing failures unrelated to this PR: the 7 failing tests (in `init-check`, `create-hardening`, `gating-sync`) all fail with `KicadCliMissingError` because `kicad-cli` is not installed in this environment. None touch the export code, which makes zero kicad-cli calls, so they fail identically on `main`.

Since `init` needs `kicad-cli` (not installed in this environment), I placed `.copperhead/config.json` and a populated `docs/BOM.md` directly (R1 verified, R2 no-MPN, U1 UNVERIFIED-with-MPN), which is what `init` would scaffold, then exercised `export bom`.

pulls.title: Post PR-lint results as a comment
pulls.body:
## What

The PR-lint check now posts its result as a comment on the PR, listing exactly which template sections or the invariant checklist are missing, instead of only writing to the Actions job log.

## Why

The findings were only visible by opening the failed check's Details in the Actions tab, so authors rarely saw what was wrong. A comment puts the specific gaps in front of them. Every open PR is currently from a fork, and a plain `pull_request` run gets a read-only token on forks, so it could not comment at all.

## Design

The trigger moves from `pull_request` to `pull_request_target` so the job holds a writable token in the base-repo context. This stays safe because the workflow never checks out or runs PR code: it reads the body from the `PR_BODY` env var and parses it, same as before. A file comment warns against adding a PR-head checkout. The comment carries a hidden `<!-- pr-lint-report -->` marker so later runs (on edit or synchronize) update the same comment in place rather than piling on new ones. The check still exits non-zero on an incomplete description, so merge gating is unchanged. See [pr-lint.yml](.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml).

issues.title: layout-draft: move_footprint cannot place a part's Reference text, so silkscreen fixes need hand-computed rotated coordinates
issues.body:
## What happened

Stage 5 (layout-draft) has no tool to place a footprint's Reference text, so clearing a silkscreen DRC finding (`silk_overlap`, `silk_over_copper`, `silk_edge_clearance`) means hand-editing the `(at …)` inside the part's `(property "Reference" …)`. That position is stored relative to the footprint origin and in the footprint's rotated frame. To put "R2" at a given board position on a part rotated 270°, the model has to invert the rotation itself, and the value it must edit changes every time `move_footprint` turns the part. The stage prompt asks for exactly this.

In practice the model hand-computed rotations in its reasoning ("rot270: board = origin + (−ly, +lx); rot90: origin + (+ly, −lx)") and re-read the board after each move to find the current label text. In the stage-5 attempts I inspected, silkscreen findings were the last DRC findings left after placement.

Note on evidence: the long `edit_file` failure loop seen in one attempt was caused by CRLF line endings (see #376), not by the coordinate maths. This request is about removing the manual transform, not about that loop.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `copperhead create --brief examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md --model claude-code` to stage 5.
2. After the first placement pass, `run_drc` reports silkscreen findings, e.g.:

```
DRC: 2 violation(s) (24 connection(s) unrouted, left as ratsnest)
  warning silk_overlap: Silkscreen clearance
    - Reference field of R2 @ (106, 116.57)
    - Segment of J1 on F.Silkscreen @ (103.65, 116.17)
  warning silk_over_copper: Silkscreen clipped by solder mask
    - Reference field of R2 @ (106, 116.57)
    - PTH pad SH [GND] of J1 @ (106.4, 115.82)
```

3. The only lever is `edit_file` on the Reference property's `(at …)`, in footprint-local rotated coordinates.

## Output

With a `label_x`/`label_y` option on `move_footprint` (local patch), the agent fixed labels in one call each:

```
  [move_footprint] moved J1 to (103.4, 112) at 270°; pads and text turned with it; Reference text at (109, 102.8). Run run_drc after this batch of moves.
  [move_footprint] moved F1 to (113.5, 112) at 0°; pads and text turned with it; Reference text at (109, 105.4). Run run_drc after this batch of moves.
  [run_drc] DRC: clean (24 connection(s) unrouted, left as ratsnest)
```

In a later clean run the agent used it 37 times and stage 5 finished DRC clean in 32 minutes, with 3 failed `edit_file` calls in the whole stage.

## Root cause

At `e26be94`:

- `src/capabilities/handlers.ts:315-326`: `move_footprint` takes `ref`, `x`, `y`, `rotation`; no label position.
- `src/kicad/populate.ts:796`: `moveFootprint` turns text with the part but cannot set where it goes.
- `src/commands/create.ts:297`: the stage-5 prompt routes label fixes through `edit_file`: "the (at …) inside a part's Reference or Value property (the label's own position, not the footprint's), which is how a silkscreen overlap is fixed."

Suggested change: optional `label_x`/`label_y` (board coordinates) on `move_footprint`. The tool converts to the stored local frame with `local = R(−θ)·(board − origin)`. Checked against pcbnew at 0°, 90°, 180° and 270°, including rotating and placing the label in the same call. Then point the stage-5 prompt at it.

## Impact

Fewer turns and tokens on every stage-5 run, and one less place where the model does coordinate maths by hand. The local patch is about 40 lines plus 4 unit tests.
