issues.title: create: layout-draft writes LAYOUT.md outside the configured docs directory
issues.body:
## Problem

During a fresh `copperhead create` run, the `layout-draft` stage expected the draft-quality document at the configured docs path:

```text
docs/LAYOUT.md
```

However, the stage agent repeatedly attempted to read and write:

```text
LAYOUT.md
```

at the repository root.

## Reproduction

1. Start `copperhead create --brief examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md` in a fresh repository.
2. Reach stage 5 (`layout-draft`).
3. Observe the agent reading:

```text
read_file error: ENOENT .../demo-runs/full-pipeline-20260916/LAYOUT.md
```

4. Observe the agent writing `LAYOUT.md` at the repository root.
5. The stage completion contract checks `docs/LAYOUT.md`, so the stage cannot recognize the generated document.

## Expected behavior

The stage prompt, file tools, and completion contract should all resolve the layout document through the configured `docs` directory. With the default configuration, the only expected path should be `docs/LAYOUT.md`.

## Impact

The agent can produce a valid layout handoff document that Copperhead does not recognize. This causes unnecessary retries and can prevent the pipeline from advancing even after the PCB and DRC gates pass.

## Suggested fix

- Include the fully resolved layout-document path in the stage prompt and tool context.
- Require the agent to write `path.join(config.docs, 'LAYOUT.md')`.
- Add a regression test using both `docs/` and a custom docs directory.

Before creating any PR for this issue, please reproduce it first.

issues.title: Finish SPICE verification: DC operating-point checks in `check`
issues.body:
### The problem

Copperhead currently verifies designs through ERC, DRC, and document drift checks — all of which confirm the schematic is internally consistent. None of them confirm the circuit actually behaves correctly. A regulator can pass ERC/DRC with the wrong feedback resistor values and still output the wrong voltage, and nothing in check will catch it.

The repo already has a SPICE netlist parser and assertion-related helpers, but there is no execution path: nothing runs a simulation, and nothing is wired into the check command or the agent's verification gate. So today, behavioral correctness is verified manually, if at all — after the design has already passed automated review.

### Proposed behavior

Add SPICE-based DC operating-point verification to check, scoped to circuits with declared output constraints (starting with linear regulator outputs).

copperhead check --spice

Expected output:

SPICE verification

U3 (regulator)
  Circuit: linear regulator, VIN=5V, VOUT target=3.3V ±5%
  Simulation: converged
  Result: VOUT = 3.28V — within tolerance

U7 (regulator)
  Circuit: linear regulator, VIN=12V, VOUT target=3.3V ±5%
  Simulation: converged
  Result: VOUT = 4.1V — OUT OF TOLERANCE

2 circuits checked, 1 passed, 1 failed

And with --json for CI/MCP consumers, matching the existing output convention used by other check subchecks.

The command should:

Translate the relevant schematic subsection into a SPICE netlist using the existing parser output.
Run the simulation via a local ngspice invocation (subprocess, no network).
Extract the resulting operating point and compare it against the constraint already declared for that net/component.
Report pass/fail per circuit, with the simulated value and the declared tolerance — and report clearly (not as a pass) when a circuit has no usable model or the simulation fails to converge.

Scope for v1: DC operating-point analysis only, for circuits copperhead can already recognize as regulators from existing constraint metadata. Transient analysis, arbitrary topologies, and full behavioral verification are explicitly out of scope for this proposal.

### Alternatives you considered

Manual review only (status quo) — works today but doesn't scale, and defeats the purpose of automated verification gates that the rest of the tool already relies on.
A full general-purpose SPICE deck builder for arbitrary circuits — considered and set aside for v1; without a bounded circuit vocabulary, model coverage and assertion design become open-ended and risk shipping something that silently mis-simulates unsupported topologies.
Symbolic/analytical checks instead of simulation (e.g. resistor-divider math for a regulator's feedback network) — simpler to implement, but doesn't generalize past the simplest cases and duplicates what a simulator already does correctly.

### Effect on the invariants

No effect on either invariant.

Spec-gated in: unaffected — this adds a new read-only check, not a write tool. No new mutation capability is introduced.
Verification-gated out: this proposal strengthens this invariant rather than touching it — it adds SPICE as an additional pass/fail gate alongside existing ERC/DRC, so finish/mutation flows have one more offline check they can be required to pass.

The command runs locally via subprocess (ngspice), makes no network calls, and does not access or modify any files outside the existing check output convention.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: legibility: TEXT_ADVANCE 0.6 under-measures stroke text by ~22%, so group captions overflow their boxes undetected
issues.body:
## What happened

`TEXT_ADVANCE` in `src/kicad/legibility.ts:79` is `0.6`, but KiCad's stroke font advances at roughly `0.76` of the glyph height. Every text box the legibility checker computes is therefore about 22% narrower than what KiCad actually draws.

The comment on `textBounds` at line 185 calls this a "conservative text box". It is optimistic, not conservative, and it under-measures in the direction that produces false negatives.

## Measured on a real sheet

From a `copperhead create` run (stage 4, ERC clean, legibility reported score 89.91 with **0 error-severity findings**). Estimated width is `len * TEXT_ADVANCE * height` with height 3.5mm. Rendered width is measured from the `<g class="stroked-text">` path extents in the `kicad-cli sch export svg` output:

| caption | chars | estimated | rendered | under by | implied advance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `B. Input bypass` | 15 | 31.50 | **40.00** | 21% | 0.762 |
| `C. PTC` | 6 | 12.60 | **16.17** | 22% | 0.770 |
| `E. Outputs` | 10 | 21.00 | **26.00** | 19% | 0.743 |
| `F. Mechanical` | 13 | 27.30 | **35.17** | 22% | 0.773 |

## Consequence: group captions escape their own boxes

Group box geometry from the same sheet, with captions placed at `box_start + 2.0mm`:

| group | box x-range | caption rendered x-range | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | 100.08 to **135.89** | 103.37 to **143.37** | 7.48mm outside its box, drawn inside group C's box |
| F | 248.16 to **264.16** | 251.45 to **286.62** | 22.46mm outside its box, close to the frame edge |

Group B's caption is physically rendered inside group C's rectangle, having crossed the full 5.08mm gutter. On the render, `B. Input bypass` and `C. PTC` read as one run of text. They do not strictly overlap (0.73mm apart), which is exactly why the `text-collision` check at line 526 does not fire: with the 0.6 advance the checker believes B's caption ends at 133.58, comfortably clear.

So the checker reports a clean sheet while the captions are visibly wrong.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Draft any sheet whose group captions are long relative to their group box.
2. `copperhead score` / the legibility gate reports 0 error-severity findings.
3. `kicad-cli sch export svg` and measure the `stroked-text` path extents against the group `rectangle` bounds.

## Suggested fix

Two parts, either of which helps on its own:

1. Raise `TEXT_ADVANCE` to about `0.78`. That makes the box genuinely conservative and lets the existing `text-collision` logic do its job. Worth re-running the golden corpus afterwards, since some currently-passing sheets may start reporting real findings.
2. Add a containment check: a group caption should be flagged when its text box is not inside its own group rectangle. `group-overlap` and `unlabeled-group` already exist as error-severity kinds, so a `caption-overflow` sibling would fit the existing model. The engine could also shrink the caption or widen the box when the two do not fit.

## Environment

- copperhead 0.11.0 at `b24de54`
- Windows 11, Node v22.17.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4

issues.title: create: locked write_file is silently absent, so the agent confabulates successful writes
issues.body:
## What happened

During a `copperhead create` run on `examples/simple/usb-c-breakout.md`, stage 1 (spec-seed) spent six turns and roughly 31k output tokens writing eight documents (`docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `openspec/project.md`, and five capability specs). None of them reached disk.

The agent only discovered this at turn 7, when it happened to search the filesystem:

> The docs never actually landed on disk, only the proposal exists. Rewriting all of them now.

It then rewrote everything and the stage completed normally, but at double the necessary cost.

## Why it happens

This is invariant 1 behaving as designed. In `src/capabilities/index.ts:41`:

```ts
gate: def.requiresUnlock ? (ctx) => ctx.editsUnlocked : () => true,
```

`write_file` is structurally absent from the tool list until `validate_change` passes. The agent called it before validating, so nothing ran.

The problem is that an absent tool produces no feedback. The model got no error, assumed the writes succeeded, and confabulated plausible results for six turns.

The two message formats make the confabulation easy to spot after the fact:

```
# turn 2, fabricated by the model (this string appears nowhere in src/)
[result of write_file]
Wrote docs/SPEC.md (6577 bytes).

# turn 8, the real implementation at src/agent/filetools.ts:35
[write_file] wrote docs/SPEC.md
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. `export COPPERHEAD_MODEL=claude-code`
2. `npx tsx src/cli.ts --plain demo --model claude-code --dir demo-runs/scratch`
3. Watch stage 1. The `write_file` calls that precede `validate_change` report success and write nothing.

## Suggested fix

Keep the enforcement, add the feedback. Rather than removing the tool from the list, register it with a handler that refuses:

```
write_file is locked until an OpenSpec proposal validates. Call validate_change first.
```

The safety property is unchanged (nothing is written before validation), but the agent self-corrects at turn 2 instead of turn 7. Stage 1 is the cheapest of the eight stages, so the same trap costs proportionally more later in the pipeline.

## Environment

- copperhead 0.11.0 at `b24de54`
- Windows 11, Node v22.17.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4
- `--model claude-code`

issues.title: Add an electrical change review command
issues.body:
### The problem

Copperhead's current dry-run output is essentially a raw Git diff. KiCad files are large S-expressions, so it's hard to see the actual electrical impact of a proposed change — a reviewer often has to manually re-read the schematic to figure out which components, pins, and nets actually changed.

This is especially a problem for AI-generated edits: a change can pass ERC/DRC cleanly while still altering an important connection, a component value, or a power path. Passing the automated checks isn't the same as confirming the change is what was intended.

### Proposed behavior

Add a deterministic, read-only command:

copperhead diff --base HEAD~1

It would produce a human-readable electrical summary, for example:

Electrical changes since HEAD~1

Components:
  + R8 10k → GPIO_PULLUP
  ~ U1 footprint changed
  - C4 removed

Connections:
  + U1.GPIO14 connected to KEY_DASH
  - U1.GPIO14 disconnected from KEY_DAH
  ! GND and POWER_IN appear to be merged

Nets:
  Renamed: KEY_DAH → KEY_DASH
  Added: STATUS_LED
  Removed: DEBUG_UART

Affected constraints:
  - pins.strapping
  - power.sleep_current_uA

ERC: passed
DRC: not run (board unchanged)


The command would also support --json for CI and MCP consumers. Comparisons run against normalized schematic/netlist data, so formatting-only changes (reference renumbering, whitespace, symbol repositioning) never show up as electrical changes.

### Alternatives you considered

Reviewing the raw git diff — technically available today, but the KiCad S-expression format makes it impractical to read.
Relying only on ERC/DRC — these catch rule violations, but don't explain what the change was or why it was made.
Exporting and diffing full netlists manually — useful as a building block internally, but too heavyweight for routine project review.

### Effect on the invariants

None. The feature is read-only, deterministic, offline, and never unlocks or performs file edits. If wired into do --dry-run, it should run after the existing spec-gated proposal step and before proposed changes are reverted. ERC/DRC requirements are unchanged.

### Before submitting

issues.title: Skill commands drop compatible-provider settings in providerForSkillRun

create --brief on claude-code/cursor commits an empty spec-seed stage: a locked write_file in a batched reply is silently dropped
issues.body:
## What happened

`copperhead create --brief brief.md` in a repo that holds only a brief fails at stage 1 (spec-seed). The run reports `finish: all gates satisfied`, then `changelog append failed (ENOENT … docs/CHANGELOG.md)`, and commits **0 files**. No `docs/SPEC.md` is ever written. The stage-contract check then fails, the stage is retried, and the retry fails the same way until the pipeline stops for a human.

A user reported this by email (to hello@copperhead.sh), on a local install at 0.10.0 and again after downgrading to 0.9.0, and saw the same failure on the hosted site (for their own brief and for the example prompt "An ESP32-C6 room sensor. SHT41 for temperature and humidity, USB-C for power and flashing, a single status LED…"). Their local log, with their path replaced by `<repo>`:

```shell
Now run check_drift (nothing to drift at this stage — no schematic yet) and finish:
  ▸ read_file  error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read '<repo>'
  ▸ read_file  error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<repo>/docs/SPEC.md'
  ▸ search  no matches
  ▸ search  brief.md:1: # BirdBox internals
  ...
  ▸ read_file  error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<repo>/docs'
  ▸ propose_change  proposal written to openspec/changes/spec-seed/ — now call validate_change
  ✓ validate_change  validation passed; edit tools are now unlocked
  ✓ check_drift  no schematic configured; drift vacuously clean
  ▸ finish  all gates satisfied; run will commit
warning: changelog append failed (ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<repo>/docs/CHANGELOG.md'); committing the verified design without a changelog entry
committed 701a78804a (0 file(s))
```

The `docs/` error is a symptom, not the bug: `write_file` creates parent directories ([filetools.ts#L33](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/filetools.ts#L33)), so `docs/` is missing only because **the agent's `write_file` never ran**.

## Root cause: a locked `write_file` in a batched reply is silently dropped

This affects the text-protocol providers, `claude-code` and `cursor`.

1. Each turn, the loop offers only the unlocked tools ([loop.ts#L484](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/loop.ts#L484)). Before `validate_change`, `write_file` is not in the catalog.
2. The system prompt tells the model to batch independent calls in one reply ([prompts.ts#L27](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/prompts.ts#L27)), so it replies with `propose_change` → `validate_change` → `write_file docs/SPEC.md` → `check_drift` → `finish`. (The text protocol still says "EXACTLY ONE JSON object", [tool-protocol.ts#L9](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts#L9), but the parser accepts several; see #192.)
3. `parseToolCalls` keeps only names that were in the catalog at the start of the turn ([tool-protocol.ts#L231](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts#L231); catalog built at [claude-code.ts#L150](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/claude-code.ts#L150) / [cursor.ts#L80](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/cursor.ts#L80)). The `write_file` block becomes prose.
4. The "not in this turn's tool catalog" message added in b888f42 ([tool-protocol.ts#L108](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts#L108)) is only produced when **zero** calls parsed ([tool-protocol.ts#L169](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts#L169)), and the loop only reads `nudge` on a tool-less turn ([loop.ts#L587](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/loop.ts#L587)). In a mixed reply the drop is silent.
5. The four surviving calls dispatch ([loop.ts#L593](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/loop.ts#L593)). `validate_change` unlocks edits, but the write is already gone. Nothing was touched, so no obligations are open, `check_drift` is vacuously clean ([handlers.ts#L560](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/capabilities/handlers.ts#L560)), and `finish` accepts "done" ([handlers.ts#L730](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/capabilities/handlers.ts#L730)).
6. At commit, `appendChangelog` ([loop.ts#L172](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/loop.ts#L172)) writes into `docs/`, which does not exist. `create` never runs `init` ([create.ts#L776](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/commands/create.ts#L776) only runs `openspecInit`). The warning fires and the run commits 0 files.
7. `runCreate` then finds the stage incomplete ([create.ts#L908](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/commands/create.ts#L908)), diagnoses, and retries. The retry sends the same batch and fails the same way.

### How it regressed

- ac1a081 (2026-07-23) fixed exactly this ("edit unlocked+used in one turn was silently dropped") by offering every tool each turn and letting `dispatchTool` enforce the unlock live.
- 460bab2 (2026-07-24, pr-review F1) went back to offering only `availableTools(ctx)`, to keep the SPEC §1.3 structural lock, reasoning that it "traded the spec's structural guarantee for one saved turn". The trade was not one turn: the text-protocol parser filters against that catalog, so the silent drop returned.
- 460bab2 is in **every release since v0.7.0** (v0.6.0 does not have it), which is why 0.9.0 fails too.

The same log can also come from a native-API model that simply skipped the write. The parser drop reproduces it deterministically, and fixes 3–5 below cover both paths.

## Steps to reproduce

This is offline and deterministic: no API key or model. It runs the real `runAgentLoop` on a brief-only git repo, using a scripted provider that sends its replies through the real `parseToolCalls` with the real per-turn catalog, exactly as `claude-code.ts` / `cursor.ts` do.

1. `npm ci && npm run build` (needs `git` and the `openspec` CLI on PATH)
2. Save the script below as `repro-brief.mjs` in the repo root
3. `node repro-brief.mjs`

````js
// Run from the copperhead repo root after `npm run build` (needs git and the openspec CLI on PATH).
import { mkdtemp, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import path from 'node:path';
import os from 'node:os';

const dist = (p) => import(pathToFileURL(path.resolve('dist', p)).href);
const { runAgentLoop } = await dist('agent/loop.js');
const { parseToolCalls } = await dist('agent/providers/tool-protocol.js');
const { openspecInit } = await dist('openspec/cli.js');

// A brief-only repo, exactly as `copperhead create --brief brief.md` sees it at stage 1.
const repo = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'ch-brief-'));
const sh = (c) => execSync(c, { cwd: repo, stdio: 'pipe' }).toString();
sh('git init -q && git config user.email repro@example.com && git config user.name repro');
await writeFile(path.join(repo, 'brief.md'), '# BirdBox internals\n\nESP32-C6 room sensor, SHT41, USB-C, one status LED. Two layers, 50x50 mm.\n');
sh('git add brief.md && git commit -qm brief');
await openspecInit(repo); // runCreate does this before stage 1

// Scripted text-protocol replies, parsed by the REAL parser against the REAL per-turn catalog.
// Turn 2 is the one-reply batch the workflow prompt invites.
const call = (tool, args) => '```json\n' + JSON.stringify({ tool, args }) + '\n```';
const replies = [
  [call('read_file', { path: 'docs/SPEC.md' }), call('search', { pattern: 'BirdBox' })].join('\n'),
  [
    call('propose_change', { id: 'spec-seed', why: 'seed requirements', what_changes: '- docs/SPEC.md', tasks: '- [ ] write docs/SPEC.md' }),
    call('validate_change', {}),
    call('write_file', { path: 'docs/SPEC.md', content: '# BirdBox\n\n## Budgets\n\n- board: 50x50 mm (ASSUMED)\n' }),
    call('check_drift', {}),
    call('finish', { outcome: 'done', summary: 'SPEC.md seeded' }),
  ].join('\n'),
];
let turn = 0;
let seq = 0;
const provider = {
  name: 'claude-code',
  async chat(_messages, tools) {
    const catalog = new Set(tools.map((t) => t.name));
    const parsed = parseToolCalls(replies[Math.min(turn++, replies.length - 1)], () => `cc-${++seq}`, catalog);
    console.log(`>> turn ${turn}: write_file advertised=${catalog.has('write_file')} parsed=[${parsed.toolCalls.map((c) => c.name)}] nudge=${parsed.nudge ?? 'none'}`);
    return { text: parsed.text, toolCalls: parsed.toolCalls, usage: { inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 }, nudge: parsed.nudge };
  },
};

const res = await runAgentLoop({
  repoRoot: repo,
  model: 'claude-code',
  request: 'create pipeline stage: spec-seed',
  stagePrompt: 'Stage 1: write docs/SPEC.md',
  allowDirty: true,
  provider,
  log: (l) => console.log(l),
});
console.log('\noutcome:', res.outcome, '| commit:', res.commit?.slice(0, 10), '| filesTouched:', res.filesTouched);
console.log('docs/SPEC.md exists:', existsSync(path.join(repo, 'docs', 'SPEC.md')));
console.log(sh('git show --stat --format=%s HEAD'));
````

## Output

This is from a build of `main` @ ef5a129 (the same result on v0.10.0). It matches the reported log line for line.

````shell
>> turn 1: write_file advertised=false parsed=[read_file,search] nudge=none
  [read_file] error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/ch-brief-4fjyhF/docs/SPEC.md'
  [search] brief.md:1: # BirdBox internals
[turn 2/40 · 0 in / 0 out]
>> turn 2: write_file advertised=false parsed=[propose_change,validate_change,check_drift,finish] nudge=none
```json
{"tool":"write_file","args":{"path":"docs/SPEC.md","content":"# BirdBox\n\n## Budgets\n\n- board: 50x50 mm (ASSUMED)\n"}}
  [propose_change] proposal written to openspec/changes/spec-seed/ — now call validate_change
  [validate_change] validation passed; edit tools are now unlocked
  [check_drift] no schematic configured; drift vacuously clean
  [finish] all gates satisfied; run will commit
warning: changelog append failed (ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/ch-brief-4fjyhF/docs/CHANGELOG.md'); committing the verified design without a changelog entry
committed f10fba0553 (0 file(s))
done · ERC not run · committed f10fba0553 · 0s · 0 in / 0 out
outcome: success | commit: f10fba0553 | filesTouched: []
docs/SPEC.md exists: false
copperhead: create pipeline stage: spec-seed
 .copperhead/runs/2026-09-11T05-40-21-426Z/transcript.jsonl | 11 +++++++++++
 .gitignore                                                 |  1 +
 openspec/changes/spec-seed/proposal.md                     | 11 +++++++++++
 openspec/changes/spec-seed/tasks.md                        |  3 +++
 4 files changed, 26 insertions(+)
````

`parsed=[propose_change,validate_change,check_drift,finish] nudge=none`: the `write_file` block is echoed as prose and never runs. Note also that the run transcript is **committed** (see issue C below).

## Related defects found along the way (all providers)

- **A. `finish` never checks the stage's output.** A create stage can commit "done" with zero work, and the contract is only checked after the commit ([create.ts#L908](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/commands/create.ts#L908)), costing a diagnosis and a retry. This overlaps #169 (finding 3) and #166.
- **B. Writes into `docs/` assume the directory exists.** `appendChangelog` ([loop.ts#L172](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/loop.ts#L172)) and `record_decision` ([handlers.ts#L722](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/capabilities/handlers.ts#L722), `appendFile`) never create it. On a brief-only repo, a `record_decision` before the first doc write fails with the same ENOENT.
- **C. Run transcripts get committed on a brief-only repo (AC-4.3).** The only `.gitignore` entry maintained for the target repo is `.history/` ([git.ts#L19](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/util/git.ts#L19)). Nothing adds `.copperhead/runs/` or `.env` (only `demo.ts` writes one, for its own demo dir), so the spec-seed commit includes `.copperhead/runs/<ts>/transcript.jsonl`. #131 notes that `create` "bootstraps `.gitignore` itself"; on current main it does not for these entries.

## Suggested fix

1. **Stop dropping calls silently in mixed replies** (tool-protocol.ts + loop.ts). Have `parseToolCalls` return the calls it withheld even when others parsed, and have the loop answer each one in order with a tool result such as `No call ran: "write_file" is not in this turn's tool catalog. Edit tools unlock after validate_change; call it again next turn.` This keeps 460bab2's structural lock: the tool is still neither offered nor dispatched.
2. **Refuse `finish` from a turn in which any call was withheld**, e.g. `cannot finish yet: 1 call in this reply did not run (write_file)`. That costs the model one turn, and a verification-looking finish can no longer ride on a write that never happened.
3. **Make the stage contract a finish precondition in `create`.** Pass `stage.isComplete` into `runAgentLoop` (a `finishGuard` hook, say), so that `finish done` returns "stage contract not met: docs/SPEC.md has no filled Budgets section" while the model still has turns left, instead of committing an empty stage and paying for a diagnosis and retry (A).
4. **`mkdir(docsDir, { recursive: true })`** in `appendChangelog` and `record_decision` (B).
5. **Ensure `.copperhead/runs/` and `.env` are in the target repo's `.gitignore`** before the first create commit, e.g. extend what `ensureIgnored` maintains on the create path (C).
6. **Resolve the protocol/prompt conflict together with #192.** "EXACTLY ONE JSON object" ([tool-protocol.ts#L9](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/providers/tool-protocol.ts#L9)) vs "issue them together in a single reply" ([prompts.ts#L27](https://github.com/copperheadhq/copperhead/blob/ef5a129f13b35e67b98216ea2f09aa7739ce6798/src/agent/prompts.ts#L27)). #192 proposes allowing multi-call replies with locked names still not dispatched. Without fixes 1–2, that makes this bug more likely, so its "rejection of locked names" test should assert a *visible* rejection.
7. **Regression test.** The suite is green because `test/create-resilience.test.ts` mocks `runAgentLoop` entirely and `test/gating-sync.test.ts` calls `dispatchTool` directly; nothing sends a mixed text-protocol reply through the loop. Turn the repro above into an offline loop-level test asserting that the withheld call gets a tool result, `finish` is refused that turn, and no commit is made with 0 files.

An alternative to 1–2 is ac1a081's approach: parse against every known tool name and let `dispatchTool`'s live `availableTools(ctx)` check decide, so a propose → validate → write batch works in one reply. It is simpler, but it reopens the structural-lock decision F1 settled, so it is a maintainer call.

**Workaround until fixed:** `--model claude`, `gpt-5`, or `codex` avoid the silent drop. Native tool calling dispatches in order with a live unlock check, and codex's structured-output enum plus correction turn rejects unknown names visibly. This has not been verified with a live run, and those backends are still exposed to A–C.

## Details

- **Command:** `create`
- **Model backend:** Claude Code saved login (`claude-code`); `cursor` shares the code path. The reporter's backend is unconfirmed, and the hosted site's provider is not visible from this repo.
- **copperhead version:** reported on 0.10.0 and 0.9.0; present since v0.7.0; reproduced on `main` @ ef5a129
- **Environment:** reproduced on Linux, node v24.14.0, kicad-cli 10.0.6; reporter on macOS

issues.title: Make the layout engine pattern-aware: keep pattern-instance parts visually grouped
issues.body:
### The problem

Once a schematic.intent.json can carry pattern provenance via patternRefs (see 
#<issue-number-of-intent-expansion-issue>), the drafting engine still has no idea 
that a given set of parts belongs to one coherent circuit block. Today it only 
groups parts by the free-text `group` field on IntentPart (SUBSYSTEMS.md heading), 
via the existing group-box logic in engine.ts (L616-L636, L1193-L1200).

This means a pattern instance — e.g. a voltage-regulator-ams1117 pattern's U1/C1/C2 
— gets placed exactly like any other loose collection of same-subsystem parts. It 
can end up:
- Split across the width of a large subsystem group instead of drawn as the tight, 
  textbook-standard footprint a regulator stage normally has (IC with input cap on 
  one side, output cap on the other).
- Ordered by whatever the AI happened to list the parts in, rather than in the 
  pattern's own canonical internal layout.
- Visually indistinguishable from a group of unrelated parts that merely share a 
  subsystem label, even though the pattern file already encodes a known-good, 
  human-reviewed spatial relationship between its parts.

The four existing geometric idioms (decoupling rows, crystal flanking, drop chains, 
subsystem group boxing) are all narrow and part-type-driven — none of them currently 
key off "these N parts are one pattern instance."

### Proposed behavior

Extend the existing subsystem-group-boxing pass in engine.ts to additionally 
recognize patternRefs entries as a finer-grained sub-grouping *inside* their 
subsystem box, and apply each pattern's own internal layout hint rather than 
generic group placement.

Concretely:

1. Each pattern file (src/kicad/patterns/*.json) gains an optional `layoutHint` 
   block describing the pattern's canonical internal arrangement, e.g.:

   "layoutHint": {
     "anchor": "U1",
     "relative": [
       { "ref": "C1", "side": "left",  "offset": 1 },
       { "ref": "C2", "side": "right", "offset": 1 }
     ]
   }

2. In engine.ts, when a schematic.intent.json includes patternRefs, the layout pass 
   (right before the existing group-box logic runs) reads each pattern's layoutHint 
   and places that instance's parts relative to its anchor FIRST, using the same 
   grid-alignment primitives the engine already uses for decoupling rows / drop 
   chains — no new placement math, just reusing existing helpers with a different 
   input source.

3. The existing subsystem group-box drawing (engine.ts L616-L636) then draws its 
   box around the whole subsystem as today; pattern instances inside it are simply 
   pre-arranged in their canonical shape rather than left to default ordering. 
   Optionally, a lighter inner outline/label per pattern instance (e.g. a dashed 
   sub-box captioned with the pattern name) can be added, reusing the box-drawing 
   helper the group-box logic already has.

4. If a design's parts+nets structurally match a pattern but carry no patternRefs 
   (e.g. hand-written schematic.intent.json, never touched Stage 3 patterns), 
   behavior is completely unchanged — this only activates when patternRefs is 
   present, so it's opt-in and backward compatible with every existing test fixture.

CLI-wise:
$ copperhead create --stage schematic
...
Applying pattern layout hint for "voltage-regulator-ams1117" (U1,C1,C2) ... done
Drawing subsystem group box "power" ... done

### Alternatives you considered

- Building a brand-new, general-purpose "pattern layout engine" separate from the 
  existing idiom functions: rejected — the four existing idioms already solve the 
  exact placement primitives (rows, flanking, drop chains) that most patterns will 
  need internally; reusing them keeps this additive instead of parallel systems.
- Skipping layoutHint entirely and just relying on part *order* in the pattern file 
  to imply placement: rejected — order-based inference is fragile and would silently 
  break if a pattern file's part order changes for unrelated reasons (e.g. adding a 
  new optional part).
- Drawing a hard visual box around every pattern instance by default: considered, 
  but rejected as the default — could get visually noisy for designs with many small 
  patterns inside one subsystem; making the inner outline optional/toggleable is safer.

### Effect on the invariants

Minimal effect on either invariant.

- Spec-gated edits: this only changes internal layout/placement logic inside the 
  drafting engine (engine.ts) and adds an optional field to pattern JSON files 
  (which are static data, not part of the validated SchematicIntent schema). No new 
  write tool or agent capability is introduced beyond what pattern expansion (see 
  #<intent-expansion-issue>) already requires gating.
- Verification-gated mutations: no effect. This changes WHERE parts are placed on 
  the sheet, not WHAT parts or nets exist — ERC is electrically identical before and 
  after this change, since positions don't affect connectivity. DRC (if the board 
  changed) is unaffected since this proposal is schematic-only, not layout/PCB.

Depends on #<pattern-library-issue> (patterns exist) and #<intent-expansion-issue> 
(patternRefs exists) landing first — this is the final, lowest-risk step in the 
overall pattern-awareness effort and can reasonably be descoped to "no inner outline, 
placement only" if reviewers want an even smaller first cut.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Add optional pattern-expansion support to SchematicIntent (ir.ts + engine.ts)
issues.body:
### The problem

Even after part-selection can reference a named pattern (see #<issue-number-of-
part-selection-issue>), by the time BOM rows reach Stage 4, they get flattened back 
into individual, unrelated IntentPart/IntentNet entries in schematic.intent.json. 
The drafting engine (src/kicad/draft/engine.ts) never learns that a given AMS1117 + 
2 caps, or a given USB-C connector + CC pull-downs, actually came from one known-good 
pattern.

This means:
- The AI still has to manually re-derive every REF.PIN net endpoint for a pattern's 
  internal wiring at the schematic stage, even though that wiring is already fully 
  known from src/kicad/patterns/*.json — reintroducing exactly the wiring-mistake 
  risk that patterns are meant to remove.
- validateIntent() in ir.ts (L157) has no way to cross-check a set of parts+nets 
  against the pattern they supposedly came from, so a pattern's internal wiring 
  invariants (e.g. "output cap must sit between VOUT and GND") aren't reusable at 
  validation time.
- Downstream, the layout engine (engine.ts L845-L1250) has no signal that a group 
  of parts is "one pattern instance" versus an arbitrary handful of unrelated parts 
  that merely share a subsystem group.

This is explicitly the highest-risk part of the overall pattern-library effort, 
because SchematicIntent is a validated, load-bearing schema consumed by the 
drafting engine, sexp emission, and existing tests (test/draft-idioms.test.ts, 
test/draft-engine.test.ts, etc.).

### Proposed behavior

Add pattern expansion as a strictly additive, backward-compatible pre-processing 
step — not a change to the core schema's required shape.

1. ir.ts: add ONE new optional field to SchematicIntent, not to IntentPart/IntentNet:

   SchematicIntent {
     version: number,
     parts: IntentPart[],
     nets: IntentNet[],
     noConnect?: string[],
     hints?: {...},
     patternRefs?: { patternName: string, instanceId: string, refPrefix: string }[]
   }

   patternRefs is purely informational metadata: "these refs came from this pattern, 
   with this instance id." It does NOT replace parts/nets — every part and net must 
   still be fully present and valid exactly as today. validateIntent() continues to 
   require fully-resolved REF.PIN endpoints; it additionally (optionally) cross-checks 
   that if patternRefs is present, the referenced parts/nets structurally match the 
   named pattern's shape from src/kicad/patterns/*.json (part count, net topology).

2. A new, separate expansion helper (e.g. src/kicad/draft/patternExpand.ts) that CAN 
   take a bare patternRefs entry with just a patternName + instanceId + a ref prefix 
   (e.g. "U2") and mechanically generate the full parts+nets block by copying the 
   pattern file and renumbering refs. This runs BEFORE validateIntent(), as an 
   opt-in expansion pass — if a caller wants to write patternRefs only and skip 
   hand-writing parts/nets for that block, they can; if they still write it out by 
   hand (today's behavior), nothing changes.

3. engine.ts: no required change. As a strictly optional enhancement, when 
   patternRefs is present, the engine MAY use it as an additional hint for the 
   existing subsystem-group-boxing logic (engine.ts L616-L636) to box a pattern 
   instance together, same rendering path as today, just a better default grouping.

CLI-wise:
$ copperhead create --stage schematic
...
Expanding pattern reference "voltage-regulator-ams1117" as U1-U3 ... done (3 parts, 3 nets)
Validating schematic.intent.json ... ERC-equivalent structural check passed

### Alternatives you considered

- Making patternRefs replace parts/nets entirely (true macro expansion baked into 
  the schema): rejected — this would mean validateIntent() and the engine need to 
  understand macro expansion as a first-class concept, which is a much larger and 
  riskier change to a schema that many existing tests and the sexp emitter depend on.
- Doing expansion entirely outside ir.ts, as a pre-Stage-4 script that just writes 
  a fully-expanded schematic.intent.json: considered, and is honestly the safer MVP 
  — patternRefs metadata could be added later purely for traceability. Filing this 
  as the "full" version so reviewers can decide whether to descope to the pre- 
  processing-only variant.
- Changing IntentPart to add a `patternInstance?: string` tag per-part instead of a 
  top-level patternRefs array: considered, but rejected because it scatters pattern 
  membership across many part records instead of one clear list, making it harder 
  to validate structurally.

### Effect on the invariants

Touches both invariants — flagging explicitly since this is the highest-risk piece.

- Spec-gated edits: this changes ir.ts (schema) and adds a new expansion helper 
  that writes to schematic.intent.json. Per the "edits are spec-gated in" rule, 
  this absolutely needs an OpenSpec proposal before any write tool exposes pattern 
  expansion — this GitHub issue is the pre-proposal discussion, not the proposal 
  itself.
- Verification-gated mutations: expanded output still must pass ERC (and DRC if 
  layout changed) exactly as any hand-written schematic.intent.json does today — 
  no new bypass is introduced. The proposed structural cross-check in validateIntent() 
  is an *additional* check, not a replacement for ERC/DRC; a pattern instance that 
  expands to bad wiring will still fail the existing verification gate.

Given the risk, recommend this lands only after #<pattern-library-issue> and 
#<part-selection-issue> are both in, and ideally starts with expansion-only 
(no patternRefs field, no schema change) before this metadata-tracking version 
is attempted.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Allow part-selection to reference a named pattern instead of enumerating every part
issues.body:
### The problem

Today, Stage 3 (part-selection) forces the AI to enumerate every single component 
as an individual BOM.md row (| Refdes | Value | Footprint | MPN | Rationale |), even 
for extremely common, well-understood sub-circuits like a linear voltage regulator 
stage or a USB-C power input. This means:

- The AI re-derives the same handful of parts (regulator + 2 caps, or a USB-C 
  connector + CC pull-downs + bulk cap) from first principles on every single design, 
  with no memory of "the way this is always done."
- Small BOM mistakes (missing a decoupling cap, wrong cap value, wrong connector 
  pinout) surface only later, at the schematic/ERC stage, causing avoidable retries.
- There's no way for a human reviewing docs/BOM.md to tell "this is a standard 
  regulator block" at a glance — every design reads as a flat, undifferentiated 
  parts list.

This builds directly on the static pattern library proposed in #<issue-number-of-
pattern-library-issue> (src/kicad/patterns/*.json). Without named patterns to 
reference, this proposal has nothing to point at — that issue should land first.

### Proposed behavior

Extend Stage 3 (src/commands/create.ts L167-L189) so the AI-facing prompt can 
reference a pattern by name from src/kicad/patterns/, and have that expand into 
its constituent BOM rows automatically, tagged so the origin is traceable.

Example BOM.md entry, before:
| U1 | AMS1117-3.3 | SOT-223 | AMS1117-3.3   | Linear regulator |
| C1 | 10uF        | 0603    | GRM188...     | Input decoupling |
| C2 | 10uF        | 0603    | GRM188...     | Output decoupling |

Example BOM.md entry, after (pattern-referenced):
| Pattern: voltage-regulator-ams1117 | source: src/kicad/patterns/voltage-regulator-ams1117.json |
| U1 | AMS1117-3.3 | SOT-223 | AMS1117-3.3 | from pattern |
| C1 | 10uF        | 0603    | GRM188...   | from pattern |
| C2 | 10uF        | 0603    | GRM188...   | from pattern |

CLI-wise:
$ copperhead create --stage part-selection
...
Resolved pattern "voltage-regulator-ams1117" -> 3 parts added to BOM.md
Resolved pattern "usb-c-power-input" -> 5 parts added to BOM.md

Concretely this needs:
1. A small lookup/expansion helper that reads src/kicad/patterns/*.json and turns 
   a pattern name into a list of BOM rows (pure function, no engine change).
2. A prompt change telling the AI it MAY say "use pattern: <name>" instead of 
   listing parts by hand, when a design need matches one of the available patterns.
3. BOM.md rows expanded from a pattern get a "from pattern: <name>" note in the 
   Rationale column so a reviewer can always trace back to the source template.

This does NOT yet touch the schematic Intent stage — the expanded BOM rows still 
flow into Stage 4 exactly as individual parts, same as today. Wiring pattern 
awareness into schematic.intent.json is a separate follow-up.

### Alternatives you considered

- Expanding patterns directly inside ir.ts/schematic.intent.json instead of at 
  BOM.md time: rejected for this proposal because it's a bigger, riskier change 
  to the validated Intent schema; doing it at the BOM stage first is a smaller, 
  reversible step and BOM.md is already free-form Markdown, not schema-validated.
- Leaving part-selection as fully manual and only adding patterns at the layout 
  stage: rejected because the AI still repeats the same wiring mistakes upstream 
  in the BOM if it never gets to "shortcut" via a known-good block.
- A CLI flag like `--use-pattern <name>` for humans only, with no AI involvement: 
  considered as a smaller v0, but doesn't address the actual problem (the AI 
  re-deriving parts every run) — could be a nice-to-have addition on top later.

### Effect on the invariants

Touches the spec-gated invariant, minimal effect on the verification-gated one.

- Spec-gated edits: this changes the Stage 3 prompt/behavior in src/commands/create.ts 
  and adds a new (read-only) pattern-lookup helper. No new destructive write tool is 
  introduced — it only changes what gets written into BOM.md, using the same file- 
  writing path that already exists for part-selection. An OpenSpec proposal should 
  still gate this, per the "edits are spec-gated in" rule, since it changes agent 
  behavior at Stage 3.
- Verification-gated mutations: no effect. Stage 4 (schematic.intent.json generation) 
  and the ERC/DRC gates are unchanged — expanded BOM rows are indistinguishable from 
  hand-written ones by the time they reach the schematic step, so nothing new needs 
  verifying at that boundary.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: PCB layout loop: where the intelligence is missing, and how to add it (B5 model-in-the-loop trial, knowledge base)
issues.body:
## Summary

The closed layout loop (`copperhead pcb layout`, RFC 11 §12) runs unattended and reports faithfully, but it has almost no capacity to *reason* about a board. B4 (`bench/reports/B4-2026-09-07.md`) showed the repair cycles never turned a PARTIAL into a PASS. A first trial with a model in the repair planner (Claude Opus via `claude-code:claude-opus-5`, same engines and budgets as B4) changed nothing: the model picks the same routing-only actions the deterministic policy picks, and on one cycle picked an action the policy would never take. This issue records how placement and routing work today, where the intelligence is and is not, the trial's findings, and a proposed path.

## How placement and routing work today (branch `feat/pcb-layout-framework`)

Copperhead never places or routes anything itself (RFC 11: wrap engines, never build a placer or router).

**Placement** (`src/pcb/engines/place.ts`), a staged plan when intent exists:
1. locked parts stay; a mechanical stage pins parts an `edge`/`fixed` constraint fixes outright (`legalize.ts`)
2. `placer-anchors`: each functional block's anchor to its signal-flow region centroid, then locked (blocks derived deterministically from `SUBSYSTEMS.md` and the schematic intent, `src/pcb/intent/blocks.ts`)
3. `placer-attach` / `placer-layout-reuse`: `relative.attached` parts beside their target pin, approved reference blocks copied by rigid transform; targets locked; blocks hanging over the outline shifted back inside
4. bulk: wrapped optimisers in preference order (kicad-tools force-directed, pyplacer simulated annealing, kicad-tools evolutionary, `placer-fixed` control, harness-only `placer-reference`); the loop runs them in ensemble mode
5. legalize (keepouts, block separation, edge clearance), rip up invalidated copper, materialize, verify against the placement gates, routability probe (short Freerouting run), rank under a scoring profile

**Routing** (`src/pcb/engines/route.ts`, plan in `plan.ts`): refuses a board that fails pre-flight or placement gates, then a staged plan: power/ground first at class width with pours preserved, critical nets next, bulk at 1.5x clearance, then bulk at the rule for what is still owed. Routers: Freerouting (DSN/SES, out of process), kicad-tools `kct route`, harness-only grid A*. Each stage carries the earlier stages' copper; candidates come from the last stage that produced copper.

**Closed loop** (`src/pcb/agent/orchestrate.ts`): cycle 0 places then routes with the whole budget; up to three repair cycles each take one action from a fixed catalog (`repair/catalog.ts`): continue-routing, change-net-priority, select-router, tune-router, rip-up-nets, move-group, rotate-component, resize-region, use-ranked-candidate, request-user-action. A worse cycle is rolled back to the best board. The user's file is written only with `--apply` on PASS or PARTIAL; evidence lands in `docs/LAYOUT.md` and the run directory.

## Where the intelligence is, and is not

- **Geometry is heuristic.** Simulated annealing over wirelength, force-directed/evolutionary search, push-and-shove and grid A* routing. No engine knows what the circuit is.
- **Judgment is hand-written rules.** The staged plans, legalizers, scoring profile, and the "cheapest untried plausible action" repair policy encode good defaults but do not reason about a specific board. The deterministic policy never offers `move-group`/`rotate-component` for owed connections.
- **The model enters in two validated slots only:** the intent compiler (`src/pcb/agent/intent/compiler.ts`, steps 1 and 3: part roles, datasheet-derived rules) and the repair planner (`src/pcb/agent/repair/planner.ts`, one tool-less JSON turn per cycle). Neither slot had run under measurement before today.
- **What is genuinely strong is the harness:** snapshot isolation, gates no candidate bypasses, zero selection regret across B0–B4, budget accounting, best-board rollback, evidence `check` can re-verify with no engine.

## B5 trial: Opus in the repair planner (2026-09-07, in progress)

Setup: `layoutBoard` with `provider = makeProvider('claude-code:claude-opus-5')`, placers pyplacer + fixed, routers Freerouting + kicad-tools, `maxRepairCycles 3`, no apply; boards that stayed PARTIAL at B4. Run dir: `bench/var/runs/B5-model-opus/` (script in the session scratchpad; a bench `--model` flag does not exist yet, see below).

| board | budget | cycle 0 | model actions | final | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decoupling-qfn` | 300 s | PARTIAL 67 %, 2 owed | continue-routing → tune-router → select-router(**router-freerouting**) | PARTIAL 67 % in 79 s | never proposed moving the capacitor; 221 s unused because the cycle cap, not the budget, ended the run |
| `congestion` | 300 s | PARTIAL 95 %, 2 owed (cycle 0 took ~150 s) | continue-routing → tune-router (ended at 5 %, rolled back) | PARTIAL 95 % in 305 s, budget exhausted after cycle 2 | same as B4 |
| `AnalogThermometer` (PCBench, placement kept) | 600 s | running | | | will be added in a comment |

Findings:

1. **The model reproduces the deterministic policy.** With only error counts, eight sample findings, the budget, and the catalog text in the prompt, Opus picks the same routing-only sequence. Its reasons are coherent but it has no information that would justify a placement action.
2. **Prompt gap: the planner does not say which router produced the current board.** On `decoupling-qfn` cycle 3 the model chose `select-router` with `router-freerouting`, the engine that had produced every cycle, believing it was "the other registered engine". The validator only checks the id is registered. One wasted cycle the policy would not take.
3. **Cycle cap vs budget.** `maxRepairCycles 3` ended `decoupling-qfn` with 221 of 300 s unused. The budget is meant to be time, not retry count (RFC 11 §12.4); the cap should be a safety valve, not the usual stop.
4. **The bench cannot run the model path.** `src/bench/runner.ts` passes `provider: null`; there is no `--model` on `copperbench run`. The trial needed an ad-hoc script.

## Proposal (ranked by value per effort)

1. **Give the planner the board.** For each owed connection: the two pads, owners, distance, courtyards between them, block membership; plus the per-block spread table already computed for the evidence, the ranking, the current router, and the board SVG for vision-capable providers. Let the model propose `move-group`/`rotate-component` with concrete vectors; the catalog, validation, budget check, and gates stay as they are. Add "current router" to the prompt and reject `select-router` to the router in use.
2. **Model-guided search per cycle.** The model proposes 2–4 candidate moves; materialize each, run the existing routability probe on all in parallel, route the best fully. Uses the ensemble runner as is.
3. **A deterministic placement action for owed connections** (the catalog entry B4 named): for each owed pair, take the smaller movable part, try three rotations, the nearest free slot toward the other pad, and the bottom side when the profile allows; probe each; keep the best. Makes the no-model loop useful and gives the model turn a stronger fallback.
4. **A model placer behind the plugin contract**, harness-only at first, benched against pyplacer on intent-rich blocks (decoupling networks, crystals). This is the §8.3 question deferred to B3: does intent change whether copperhead needs its own placer.
5. **Learned engine selection** over board features from the B0–B4 run records (algorithm portfolio instead of a fixed preference order).
6. **A layout knowledge base, split into what compiles and what guides.** Prompted by kistack's PCB skill (https://github.com/American-Embedded/kistack/blob/main/skills/pcb/SKILL.md, human-written, no license declared so nothing copied verbatim). Its advice (decoupling caps placed for minimum loop area and trace length, horizontal connectors at edges, alignment, render-and-look, then DRC) is mostly expressible in copperhead's constraint language already (`layout.relative.attached`, `layout.mechanical.edge`, separation). Proposed shape:
   - a machine-readable rulebook keyed on part role and package under `src/pcb/knowledge/`, applied by the intent compiler's deterministic steps and cited in `intent-report.md` (same pattern as the physics compiler for track widths); every rule must be one the checkers verify
   - short, versioned prompt sections for the three model slots (role classification taxonomy; what a citable datasheet rule looks like; a repair diagnosis guide: "two owed connections under a QFN means the cap moves, not another routing pass"; "only switch to a router that has not produced the current board")
   - render-and-look adopted as item 1 above (the loop already writes `board.svg` with findings marked)
   - overlaps with #274 (static pattern library) and #246 (skills stream); the rulebook should be the layout half of the pattern library
7. **`copperbench run --model`** and a B5 track: the PARTIAL boards from B4 with and without a provider, success = PARTIAL→PASS conversions with selection regret still zero. Nothing above should ship without this measurement.

## Caution

Four of the eight PCBench PARTIALs at B4 (`rufs_smart_psu`, `hp_led_switch`, `beehive`, `piezo_amplifier`) end with every candidate carrying shorts or clearance errors. It is not verified whether those are router limits or fidelity losses in the DSN export and netclass mapping. If the latter, no planner change helps; check before asking the model to reason about them.

## References

- RFC 11 (copperhead-rfcs), `openspec/changes/add-pcb-layout-framework/` (design, implementation spec, tasks 7.x)
- `bench/reports/B4-2026-09-07.md`
- related: #252 (engine boundary), #274 (pattern library), #246 (skills stream), #257 (golden-board eval)

issues.title: Add a static pattern library for common circuit blocks (voltage regulator, USB-C input, crystal osc)
issues.body:
### The problem

During the schematic step, the AI has to invent every circuit block from scratch, one 
pin at a time, even for extremely common sub-circuits like a linear voltage regulator, 
a USB-C power input stage, or a crystal oscillator with load caps. This leads to 
avoidable mistakes (wrong pull-up rail, missing decoupling cap, miswired USB signal 
pins) that get caught by ERC and force retries, burning both time and compute cost.

The engine already has narrow, hardcoded geometric heuristics for parts of this 
(decoupling rows, crystal cap flanking, drop chains — see engine.ts L806-L1191), but 
there's no reusable, named source of *known-good* multi-part circuit blocks that the 
AI or a human could reference instead of re-deriving the wiring every time.

ROADMAP.md (Phase 4) mentions a future "template corpus (tscircuit-style idiom 
matching)" as a possible successor once the hand-rolled rule engine runs out of road — 
this proposal is not that. It's a much smaller, purely additive first step.

### Proposed behavior

Add a new directory, e.g. `src/kicad/patterns/`, containing static JSON files that 
describe known-good circuit blocks as plain parts + nets — the same shape already 
accepted by SchematicIntent (IntentPart / IntentNet), nothing new to parse.

Example: src/kicad/patterns/voltage-regulator-ams1117.json
{
  "name": "voltage-regulator-ams1117",
  "description": "AMS1117 linear regulator with input/output decoupling caps",
  "parts": [
    { "ref": "U1", "libId": "Regulator_Linear:AMS1117-3.3", "value": "AMS1117-3.3", "group": "power" },
    { "ref": "C1", "libId": "Device:C", "value": "10uF", "group": "power" },
    { "ref": "C2", "libId": "Device:C", "value": "10uF", "group": "power" }
  ],
  "nets": [
    { "name": "VIN", "pins": ["U1.VIN", "C1.1"], "kind": "power" },
    { "name": "VOUT", "pins": ["U1.VOUT", "C2.1"], "kind": "power" },
    { "name": "GND", "pins": ["U1.GND", "C1.2", "C2.2"], "kind": "ground" }
  ]
}

This is intentionally NOT wired into part-selection, the Intent schema, or the 
drafting engine in this proposal. It is a read-only reference corpus. No existing 
command, prompt, or validator changes.

CLI-wise, nothing changes yet — this is just data living in the repo, seeded from 
the multi-part sub-circuits already visible in manual-tests/real-designs/examples 
(e.g. the regulator stage in cm5_minima, the crystal block in ecc83).

A short docs/patterns.md would list what's available and note that consuming these 
patterns (from part-selection or the schematic step) is a separate, future proposal.

### Alternatives you considered

- Waiting for the full Phase 4 "template corpus" from ROADMAP.md: rejected for now 
  because that's scoped as a much larger successor system (idiom matching + engine 
  integration), and there's no cheap way to validate the idea of a pattern corpus 
  without first having any patterns to look at.
- Embedding pattern data directly as extra fields in ir.ts: rejected because it 
  would touch the validated Intent schema before any consumer of that data exists, 
  which is unnecessary risk for a documentation/data-only step.
- Doing nothing and relying on the AI to keep re-deriving these sub-circuits: current 
  behavior, and the source of the mis-wiring/retry cost described above.

### Effect on the invariants

No effect on either invariant.

- Spec-gated edits: this only adds new static data files (src/kicad/patterns/*.json) 
  and a docs page. No new write tools, commands, or agent capabilities are introduced.
- Verification-gated mutations: nothing in this proposal touches schematic.intent.json 
  generation, the drafting engine, or triggers ERC/DRC. The pattern files are not 
  consumed by any pipeline stage yet, so there is nothing new to verify.

A follow-up proposal (patterns → Intent expansion, or patterns → part-selection) 
would need to address both invariants explicitly; that is out of scope here.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Add copperhead export firmware + copperhead check --firmware: pinout drift gate between schematic and firmware headers
issues.body:
### The problem

In embedded hardware projects, MCU pin assignments are defined in the schematic (e.g. PA5 → LED_STATUS),
but the same mapping is manually duplicated and maintained in firmware code (pinout.h, pins.rs, etc.).

When a pin gets reassigned during a schematic or layout revision (e.g. PA5 to PA6), the firmware
header is often not updated in lockstep. The result is a non-functional peripheral, or in worse
cases, a damaged GPIO from driving the wrong pin. This class of bug is typically only caught during
bench bring-up — late, and at real cost.

Copperhead already enforces "drift is a build failure" for docs, BOM, and KiCad files
(via verify_symbols, check), but firmware code sits outside that guarantee. There is currently
no automated way to verify that a schematic and its corresponding firmware header stay in sync.

### Proposed behavior

1. 1. Export command — generate a firmware header from the schematic's pin/net mapping:

   $ copperhead export firmware --target c --out firmware/inc/pinout.h

   Expected output (pinout.h):
   // Auto-generated from schematic. Do not edit manually.
   #define PIN_LED_STATUS   PA5
   #define PIN_UART_TX      PA9
   #define PIN_UART_RX      PA10

2. Drift gate — verify the committed header against the schematic:

   $ copperhead check --firmware

   Expected output (on mismatch):
   ✗ Firmware drift detected
     PIN_LED_STATUS: schematic=PA5, firmware/inc/pinout.h=PA6
   1 mismatch found. Run `copperhead export firmware` to resync.
   exit code: 1

   Expected output (in sync):
   ✓ Firmware pinout in sync (3 pins checked)
   exit code: 0

MVP scope: `--target c` (header file) only. Rust, Zephyr, and Arduino targets could follow as
separate, later proposals.

### Alternatives you considered

- Maintaining a manual PINOUT.md and relying on code review: already possible today, but it does
  not enforce anything — drift still happens through human error.
- Parsing the schematic from the firmware side (reverse direction): rejected, since under
  Copperhead's invariants the schematic is the source of truth and firmware should be derived
  from it, not the other way around.
- Fuzzy/naming-convention-based matching (auto-mapping schematic net names to firmware macro
  names): deferred for now, since it introduces non-determinism. The MVP will use explicit,
  config-based mapping instead (e.g. a naming convention declared in `.copperhead/config.json`).

### Effect on the invariants

- Spec-gated (write tools absent until an OpenSpec proposal validates): Applies. `export firmware`
  is a new write path and will not exist until this proposal is validated.
- Verification-gated (nothing done until ERC/DRC passes): No direct effect, since this only reads
  from the schematic and does not mutate the board. `export firmware` itself will be a
  deterministic, LLM-free, network-free operation (schematic S-expression parsing + template
  generation), making it safe for CI and pre-commit hooks.
- `check --firmware` is also purely deterministic: no network or LLM calls, just a comparison
  between the schematic-derived mapping and the committed header file.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: toolSearch fails glob matching and leaks subdirectories on Windows due to unnormalized path separators
issues.body:
### What happened

In `src/agent/filetools.ts`, `toolSearch` uses `path.relative(repoRoot, abs)` to evaluate candidate files against the regex produced by `globToRegex(glob)`. On Windows, `path.relative()` produces backslashes (`\`) such as `docs\BOM.md` or `src\commands\check.ts`.

However, `globToRegex()` constructs regular expressions with POSIX forward slashes (`/`), e.g., converting `docs/*.md` to `/^docs\/[^\/]*\.md$/`.

This causes two bugs on Windows:
1. **Directory-scoped globs fail to match**: When the agent calls `search` with a glob like `docs/*.md`, `hardware/*.kicad_sch`, or `src/**/*.ts`, 0 results are returned because `docs\` never matches `docs/`.
2. **Root-scoped globs leak into subdirectories**: A glob like `*.md` compiles to `/^[^\/]*\.md$/`. Because `\` is not `/`, `[^\/]*` matches `docs\BOM`, erroneously returning matches across all nested folders instead of only the repository root.

**Expected:**
- `docs/*.md` matches files in `docs/` on Windows just like on Linux/macOS.
- `*.md` only matches files at the root level and does not match files inside subdirectories on Windows.

**Actual:**
- `docs/*.md` returns 0 results on Windows.
- `*.md` matches files in all subdirectories on Windows.
he compiled regex.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a Windows machine, create a repository with files in subdirectories (e.g. `docs/SPEC.md` and `README.md`).
2. Call `toolSearch(repoRoot, 'pattern', 'docs/*.md')`.
3. Notice that 0 matches are returned despite matching text in `docs/SPEC.md`.
4. Call `toolSearch(repoRoot, 'pattern', '*.md')`.
5. Notice that `docs/SPEC.md` is returned despite being in a subdirectory.


### Output

```shell
// In src/agent/filetools.ts:139
const rel = path.relative(repoRoot, abs); // Returns "docs\\SPEC.md" on Windows
const globRe = globToRegex("docs/*.md");  // Returns /^docs\/[^\/]*\.md$/

globRe.test(rel); // returns false because "\" != "/"
```

### Which command

other or not command-specific

### Model backend

Not applicable

### copperhead version

0.10.0 

### Node, KiCad, and OS

Node: v24.16.0 KiCad: kicad-cli 8.x / 9.x OS: Windows 11 (win32 x64)

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I removed API keys and other secrets from everything I pasted.

issues.title: Run protocol stream: version the CLI/consumer boundary with a handshake, an event stream, and a result document
issues.body:
## Summary

This stream owns the **wire between the CLI and any non-interactive consumer**: how a consumer discovers what the installed CLI can do, how a run reports what it is doing while it runs, and how it states what it did when it finished.

It owns the **transport, not the semantics**. Nothing here changes what a stage does, what a tool returns, when a run is retried, or where an artifact is stored. It fixes the form those facts take on the way out.

The other four streams each assume this wire exists. #251 needs an exit status that carries a retry class and progress events a lease can trust; #250 needs artifact records carrying the producing tool call; #249 wants its cost numbers emitted "as structured transcript events so hosted runs can aggregate them without scraping the CLI table"; #246 needs its tool-result envelope to survive the trip. Each assumes it, none owns it, and today a consumer reconstructs all of it by tailing a human audit trail and matching regexes against `--plain` output.

## Boundary rule

- **In scope:** capability discovery and protocol versioning, the machine event stream and its envelope, the result document, the form (not the policy) of exit classification, typed findings, and conformance fixtures.
- **Out of scope:** retry policy, leases, cancellation policy (#251); artifact storage, workspace lifecycle, payload limits (#250); caching and model routing (#249); the tool registry and the contents of its envelope (#246); anything that changes circuit-design behaviour.
- Structural invariants are untouched: edit tools stay absent from the tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates, and `check` / `verify` stays LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1).
- **No clause of this protocol may name a hosted platform.** Every field has to be meaningful to someone running `copperhead do --event-stream run.ndjson` in their own CI with no account. That rule is what keeps this an open-core capability rather than cloud plumbing living in the CLI, and it is testable: the conformance fixtures in Phase 4 are generated on a bench.

## Current state (baseline on `main`)

**1. There is no way to ask the CLI what it supports.** `doctor --json` reports host health (`DoctorReport { ok, checks }`, [doctor.ts:38](src/commands/doctor.ts#L38)) and is the right shape for a human, not for a negotiation. A consumer pins a version in a Dockerfile and hopes. The copperhead-cloud runner image pins `copperhead@0.9.0` while `0.10.0` is published, and nothing on either side detects the gap.

**2. The transcript is an audit trail being used as an API.** `Transcript.event()` ([transcript.ts:86](src/agent/transcript.ts#L86)) appends `{ts, type, data}` to `.copperhead/runs/<ISO timestamp>/transcript.jsonl`, one directory per run **and per stage attempt**. A consumer discovers those directories by polling, reads them by byte offset, and infers ordering from the timestamp names. 21 `transcript.event()` call sites across `loop.ts` and `tools.ts` emit 18 distinct types; the cloud consumer maps 4 of them. `run-refused`, `restore-failed`, `provider-failover`, `session-limit`, `turn-timeout`, `budget-extended`, `work-preserved` and `run-committed` all arrive as untyped rows, so a refusal is not a first-class run state anywhere downstream.

**3. Nothing carries a sequence number.** Ordering is per-file byte order. A consumer cannot detect loss, cannot dedupe a redelivery, and cannot assert forward progress, which is the signal #251 wants a lease renewal gated on.

**4. Instrumentation is post-hoc.** `tool` is written after the call returns ([loop.ts:594](src/agent/loop.ts#L594)) and `assistant` after the turn completes ([loop.ts:568](src/agent/loop.ts#L568)), so a consumer cannot show what is running and any duration it displays is invented. `onStream` exists in `ChatOpts` ([types.ts:44](src/agent/types.ts#L44)) and is honoured only by `cursor.ts` and `claude-code.ts`. `openai.ts`, which is also the `compat:` route every hosted run uses, never passes `stream: true` and never calls it.

**5. `run-start` already carries the facts a consumer needs, and none of them are a contract.** `RunMeta` ([runmeta.ts](src/agent/runmeta.ts)) holds `versions.copperhead`, `versions.kicadCli`, `runId`, `brief.sha256`, `command`, `model` and `provider`, rendered onto three human surfaces. A consumer reading it today is reading an implementation detail that is free to move.

**6. The machine result is thin, late, and clobbered.** `do` returns `RunResult` ([loop.ts:71](src/agent/loop.ts#L71)) under the global `--json`; `create` returns `{ ok, completed }` ([create.ts:744](src/commands/create.ts#L744)). The richer report is written once, at the end, to `.copperhead/runs/report.json` ([create.ts:736](src/commands/create.ts#L736)), a fixed run-independent path the next run overwrites.

**7. Findings exist only as prose.** `check --plain` prints `ERC: 30 violation(s)` and indented detail; there is no structured form. Every consumer that wants counts parses them with regexes, which means an output tweak silently changes a verdict about somebody's board.

**8. Exit codes carry no class.** Diagnosed in #251 current-state 4. The policy is theirs; the shape it takes on the wire is this stream's.

## Scope and deliverables

### Phase 0: the handshake (blocking)

Nothing else here is safe to depend on until a consumer can tell what it is talking to.

- [ ] `copperhead capabilities --json`: `{ protocol: "copperhead-run/1", cli, commands, features, tools: { kicadCli, git, openspec, node } }`. Runs no model, touches no repository, makes no network call.
- [ ] A protocol version constant with a documented compatibility rule: major means breaking, minor means additive, consumers pin a major and refuse an unknown one before doing work.
- [ ] A SPEC.md section for the protocol, and a structural test asserting the declared `features` list matches what is actually registered, so the handshake cannot drift from the implementation.

### Phase 1: the event stream

- [ ] `--event-stream <path>` (and `fd:N`): NDJSON, append-only, opened before the first unit of work. A path by default, because a file survives a crash, cannot deadlock on backpressure when nobody reads, and behaves the same on every filesystem.
- [ ] Envelope: `{ v, seq, ts, tRelMs, type, id?, parentId?, stage?, turn?, data }`, with `seq` monotonic from 1.
- [ ] Vocabulary mapped from the 18 types already emitted, plus four that are new: turn lifecycle, model request and response with the input split, `finding`, `artifact`. A `notice` type carries everything else, so a new signal never requires a consumer release.
- [ ] `tool.started` before the call rather than only `tool.finished` after it, so durations stop being invented.
- [ ] **Unknown-tolerance is mandatory on the consumer and stated in the spec:** an unrecognised `type` or field is ignored, never an error.
- [ ] Redaction at write time as today (AC-4.1); truncation to the limits #250 sets, not to a second set invented here.

### Phase 2: the result document

- [ ] `--result <path>`, written per run beside the transcript and flushed incrementally, superseding the clobbered shared `report.json`.
- [ ] Fields: protocol and versions, `runId`, command, outcome, exit path, retry class, stats (turns, repair cycles, tokens split fresh / cacheRead / cacheWrite, duration), stages with the last completed one, a `resumeSafe` flag, commits, files touched, artifacts, findings summary.
- [ ] `create` honours the global `--json` the way `do` already does.
- [ ] Deliberate overlap with #251 Phase 0: that issue decides what these fields mean for retry policy, this one fixes their shape and their location.

### Phase 3: typed findings

- [ ] `finding` events from `check` and the verification gate: `{ source: erc | drc | drift | legibility | openspec | constraint, severity, code, message, location, detail }`, emitted alongside the human output rather than replacing it.
- [ ] `check --json` returns the same set, so nothing has to parse `--plain` to count violations.
- [ ] Explicitly not a change to what `check` concludes (#247 owns that), only to how it says it.

### Phase 4: conformance

- [ ] A validator and golden `.ndjson` fixtures shipped in the npm package, so a consumer's tests read them from the installed CLI and a change that breaks the wire fails here first, in this repo.
- [ ] A test proving an unknown event type in a fixture is ignored by the reference reader.
- [ ] Deprecations travel in band: a `notice` at level `warn` with a code, at least one minor before removal.

## Delegated, not duplicated

| This stream carries it | That stream decides it |
| --- | --- |
| exit status, retry class, run identity, cancellation events | #251 Phase 0 (taxonomy, `--run-id`, `SIGTERM` with a grace deadline) |
| artifact events and their provenance fields; payload caps | #250 Phase 0 and 1 (the record, the limits, the spill) |
| `usage` split three ways on turn and model events | #249 Phase 0 (splitting `Turn.usage` at the providers) |
| the tool payload on the wire | #246 Phase 0 (`ToolResult` envelope, typed errors, view hints) |

## Acceptance

- A consumer can determine, **before** starting a run, whether the installed CLI speaks its protocol major, and refuse without doing work.
- A run driven with `--event-stream` and `--result` is fully reportable with no directory discovery, no regex over human output, and no inference from an exit code.
- Adding an event type does not require a consumer release, proven by a test rather than by intent.
- Every feature here is demonstrable with `copperhead do --event-stream run.ndjson` on a bench with no account, and the fixtures are generated that way.
- `test/gating-sync.test.ts` and the `test/init-check.test.ts` module-graph guard stay green and are extended, never weakened.

## Related

- #251 orchestration: consumes this wire and owns the retry, lease and cancellation semantics it carries.
- #250 files and artifacts: owns the artifact record this stream transports and the payload limits it obeys.
- #249 performance and token cost: its Phase 0 asks for exactly these cost events.
- #246 tool framework: its envelope and view hints are what `tool.finished` should carry.
- #247 hybrid board review: decides what a finding means; this stream decides how one is written down.
- #254, #243, #241 and #256 are each a small instance of the same gap: a condition recorded where no consumer can read it, or a fact folded away before it reaches one.

issues.title: Eval: `copperhead do` on a golden board (HackRF One) — 9 findings, 4 blocking before the agent gets a turn
issues.body:
## Context

First end-to-end exercise of `copperhead do` against a real third-party KiCad
project rather than the test fixture, to find out what breaks when the tool is
pointed at a repo it did not create.

**Target:** [HackRF One](https://github.com/greatscottgadgets/hackrf) @ `e5d1593` —
the canonical open-source USB-only SDR. Hierarchical project (root +
`baseband`/`frontend`/`mcu`), 420 BOM rows, full PCB, zero Ethernet content at
baseline.

**Request under test:** add a gigabit Ethernet interface (USB2→GbE bridge,
MagJack, rails, straps, USB tap-in), schematic only, no PCB changes.

**Environment:** copperhead 0.10.0 (`feat/vertex-ai-provider`), kicad-cli 10.0.6,
node v24.14.0, provider `claude-code`.

The headline result is that **four separate defects had to be worked around
before the agent got a single turn.** Those are the findings below.

---

## Reproducing

```bash
mkdir -p /workspaces/ch-eval/logs && cd /workspaces/ch-eval

# 1. Golden board, isolated into its own git repo
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse \
  https://github.com/greatscottgadgets/hackrf.git hackrf
git -C hackrf sparse-checkout set hardware/hackrf-one
mkdir hackrf-test && cp -r hackrf/hardware/hackrf-one/. hackrf-test/
cd hackrf-test && rm -rf PlasticCase_CAD acrylic_case
git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "HackRF One as published upstream"

# 2. WORKAROUND for finding 3 — silence legacy-import rule families, else the
#    verification gate fails on 936 pre-existing violations the agent never caused
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
p = json.load(open('hackrf-one.kicad_pro'))
sch = ['footprint_link_issues','lib_symbol_issues','endpoint_off_grid',
       'lib_symbol_mismatch','same_local_global_label']
brd = ['text_height','lib_footprint_issues','starved_thermal','text_thickness',
       'silk_edge_clearance','footprint_type_mismatch','padstack',
       'nonmirrored_text_on_back_layer','lib_footprint_mismatch']
rs = p.setdefault('erc', {}).setdefault('rule_severities', {})
for t in sch: rs[t] = 'ignore'
rs = p.setdefault('board', {}).setdefault('design_settings', {}).setdefault('rule_severities', {})
for t in brd: rs[t] = 'ignore'
json.dump(p, open('hackrf-one.kicad_pro','w'), indent=2)
PY
git add -A && git commit -qm "silence legacy-import ERC/DRC families"

# 3. Scaffold. NOTE: requires the finding-1 fix, otherwise init selects
#    baseband.kicad_sch (a sub-sheet) and everything downstream is wrong.
copperhead init --no-hooks --plain
grep '"schematic"' .copperhead/config.json   # must be hackrf-one.kicad_sch

# 4. WORKAROUND for findings 5 + 6 — init scaffolds no .gitignore, and the
#    .kicad_prl that kicad-cli drops during `check` then blocks `do`
printf '.env\n.copperhead/runs/\n*.kicad_prl\n*-backups/\nfp-info-cache\n' > .gitignore
git add -A && git commit -qm "gitignore secrets, transcripts, KiCad local files"

# 5. Baseline must read ERC ✓ DRC ✓ drift ✓ before the run means anything
copperhead check --plain | grep -E '^(ERC|DRC|drift)'

# 6. The run
copperhead do --model claude-code --plain "Add a gigabit Ethernet network \
interface to this HackRF One design. The board currently exposes only USB. Pick \
```
