```bash
a realistic architecture for this MCU (the LPC4320 has no Ethernet MAC, so a USB \
2.0 to gigabit Ethernet bridge controller like a Realtek RTL8153B or Microchip \
LAN7800 is the sensible route), and add at schematic level: the bridge \
controller, an RJ45 jack with integrated magnetics (MagJack), the required \
supply rails and decoupling, reset/strap/clock circuitry, and the USB connection \
into the existing design. Do not modify the PCB layout. Record part choices and \
rationale in the design docs."
```

---

## Findings

### 1. `init` picks the wrong root schematic on hierarchical projects — fix in hand, uncommitted

`findKicadFiles` in `src/memory/scaffold.ts` took the first `.kicad_sch` in
directory-walk order. HackRF has four sheets and `baseband.kicad_sch` sorts
first, so copperhead treated a sub-sheet as the entire design.

Silent and destructive downstream: ERC ran on that sheet standalone and reported
**183 errors** that are pure artifacts of the isolation (power pins fed by the
parent read as undriven, hierarchical labels read as isolated), and docs were
scaffolded from one sheet, so `check` reported hundreds of false drift
mismatches — *"BOM.md claims C1 absent but actual is C1 (33pF) in schematic"*.

Blocks pointing copperhead at essentially any real board, since real boards are
hierarchical.

**Fix applied locally:** prefer the sheet named after the adjacent
`.kicad_pro`/`.kicad_pcb` (KiCad's own convention), else the sheet no other
sheet references via `Sheetfile`. `init` then selects `hackrf-one.kicad_sch`
first try. No new test failures.

### 2. `init --force` silently reverts a hand-corrected root

`src/memory/scaffold.ts:184` assigns `config.schematic` unconditionally on every
run, so a hand-set root is discarded without warning and there is no way to pin
it. This is what made finding 1 impossible to route around — the only escape
was patching compiled output in `dist/`.

### 3. Verification gates count pre-existing violations — no severity filter, no baseline

`src/kicad/report.ts:66` sets `ok = violations.length === 0`;
`src/kicad/cli.ts:160` passes no severity filter to `kicad-cli`;
`src/kicad/report.ts:35` defaults a missing severity to `error`.

HackRF's untouched baseline under KiCad 10 is **489 ERC violations** (all
warnings) and **447 DRC violations** (426 warning / 21 error) — entirely
legacy-import noise: symbol and footprint libraries that ship outside the repo,
off-grid endpoints, starved thermal reliefs, silkscreen text metrics.

So `do` fails verification on its first check for violations the agent never
caused, burns all five repair cycles chasing them, and rolls back. The gate
measures the 2014 toolchain, not the edit.

Suggested fix: baseline-relative gating — did *this edit* add violations? — or
at minimum a severity threshold.

### 4. The legibility score is computed from truncated counts

`src/kicad/legibility.ts:338` applies a per-family-per-sheet cap of 10 and builds
`counts.error` from the kept list rather than the raw one; `src/kicad/score.ts:295`
scores off that capped count.

On HackRF the header reported **81 errors** while the suppression notes revealed
roughly **380 further findings** — the number driving the score understates
reality by ~5×, and a board with 81 errors scores identically to one with 500.

Separately the score was **40/100** against a "known-good floor" of 85 on a real,
shipped, professionally drawn board, largely because HackRF uses no group
rectangles so every symbol trips `ungrouped-symbol`. It correctly does not gate
here (`src/agent/loop.ts:262` gates only engine-authored repos), but the metric
says little about human-drawn schematics.

### 5. `init` violates AC-4.3 on existing repos

On the init-on-existing-repo path **no `.gitignore` is created at all**, while
the `.copperhead/README.md` it scaffolds asserts of the runs directory: *"This
directory is gitignored."* Only `demo` and `create` scaffold one.

So on any existing repo `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/` are **not** ignored,
against AC-4.3's requirement that both be ignored from the first commit. Run
transcripts are precisely the artifact most likely to carry sensitive design
detail.

### 6. A `check` run leaves the tree dirty and blocks the next `do`

`kicad-cli` writes `<project>.kicad_prl` (KiCad's machine-local project settings)
as a side effect of ERC/DRC. Nothing ignores it on the `init` path, so running
`copperhead check` makes the next `copperhead do` refuse:

```
working tree is dirty; copperhead refuses to run on uncommitted changes by default
```

The rail behaved correctly and its error text is genuinely good. The problem is
that copperhead's own read-only, CI-safe command creates the condition that
blocks its main command.

### 7. A missing sub-sheet reference throws a bare ENOENT

`src/kicad/sexp.ts:122` reads referenced sub-sheets with a raw `readFile`, so a
broken `Sheetfile` reference surfaces as
`ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../mcu.kicad_sch'` with nothing
naming the parent that referenced it. Minor, but this is exactly the
malformed-real-repo case the tool exists to handle.

### 8. Three pre-existing test failures under kicad-cli 10

Verified against unmodified source (stash, rebuild, rerun), so unrelated to the
finding-1 fix:

- `test/init-check.test.ts` — "clean fixture: everything green (AC-2.1)"
- `test/gating-sync.test.ts` — "finish blocks on open obligations and unverified ERC"
- `test/stage-completion.test.ts` — "error-severity findings keep the stage active"

`CLAUDE.md` states the offline suite is green; it is **3 failed / 842 passed**
here. The failing case is "clean fixture: everything green", same root cause as
finding 3 — newer kicad-cli reports more, and nothing filters by severity.

### 9. No symbol-authoring tool bounds the "add a subsystem" use case

Observed live during the run. The agent has `search_symbols`, `symbol_pins` and
`verify_symbols` for *finding* parts, but no tool for *authoring* one. It probed
`LAN7800`, `RTL8153`, `AX88179`, `LAN9500` and `Ethernet` — none has a symbol in
stock KiCad libraries (`RJ45` and `USB3300` do).

No USB-to-gigabit-Ethernet bridge ships in stock KiCad libs, so any realistic
new-subsystem request hits this wall. Remaining routes are hand-writing a
`.kicad_sym` via `write_file` (HackRF has precedent — it carries its own
`74AUP2G58GU.kicad_sym`), substituting a generic symbol and accepting a wrong
part, or refusing. Worth an explicit decision about which is intended.

---

## Current state

- **Findings 2–9 are open.** Finding 1 has a fix in the working tree
  (`src/memory/scaffold.ts`), uncommitted, no new test failures.
- **The agent run is in flight** — turn 6/40 at time of writing, still in its
  verification phase, no edits proposed yet. It has confirmed the LPC4320's
  second USB port (`USB1_DP`/`USB1_DM`, pins 89/90 on U23) is present and
  unconnected, which is the correct architectural hook on this board, and is
  checking the power budget. Outcome will be added as a comment.
- Two earlier attempts were lost to Codespace stop/start (`/tmp` wiped,
  `/workspaces` intact, uptime reset, `oom_kill 0`, 11 GB free) — idle
  suspension of the dev container, unrelated to copperhead. Test assets and
  logs now live on `/workspaces` so they survive; the run process cannot.

## Suggested priority

Findings **1, 3 and 5** are the ones that make copperhead unusable or unsafe on
a real repo: wrong design root, a gate that fails on someone else's legacy
warnings, and secrets plus transcripts left untracked. 2 and 6 are small fixes
that remove the sharp edges around them.

issues.title: Layout stops at a deterministic grid: pick the placement/routing engine boundary (DSN/SES vs circuit-json) and adopt an external router
issues.body:
### The problem

The board half of `create` now has a deterministic front end and nothing behind it.

`src/kicad/board.ts` (in flight on `test/real-netlist-corpus`) closes #227: before every attempt of stage 5, `ensureBoardPopulated` exports the schematic's netlist with `kicad-cli sch export netlist --format kicadsexpr`, resolves each part to an installed footprint, shelf-packs the footprints inside an Edge.Cuts rectangle sized to fit, assigns pad nets, and verifies the board loads and passes DRC. The agent no longer refuses for lack of readable pad geometry.

```
schematic.intent.json
     |  draft engine + emit.ts
.kicad_sch
     |  kicad-cli sch export netlist (kicadsexpr)
netlist (parts, nets, Footprint fields)
     |  resolveFootprint: schematic field > symbol default > generic table > ki_fp_filters
     |  shelfPack (area-descending, 1.5 mm gaps)
     |  instantiateFootprint (text surgery on the library .kicad_mod)
.kicad_pcb   all on F.Cu, pads carry nets, zero tracks, zero vias
     |  kicad-cli pcb drc  ->  clean, N unrouted
stage 5 agent: nudges (at X Y) lines, writes LAYOUT.md "## Draft quality"
     |
stage 6: gerbers, drill, DXF, STEP, BOM.csv
```

Two gaps follow from that picture:

**Placement is a grid, not a layout.** `shelfPack` orders by footprint area and packs left to right. It knows nothing about connectivity, so a decoupling cap can land on the far side of the board from its IC. The stage prompt asks the agent to fix this by editing `(at X Y)` lines a few parts at a time with `run_drc` between batches, and explicitly offers the grid as a fallback when that fails. On any real part count that fallback is what ships.

**Routing does not exist and no gate asks for it.** `normalizeReport` deliberately keeps `unconnected_items` in a separate `unrouted` bucket that never counts against `ok`, which is right for a draft. But `grep -rn "unrouted" src/` returns only `check.ts` and the stage-5 prompt: the fab release gate in `src/kicad/fab.ts` and `copperhead export` never look at it. A board with zero copper passes stage 6 and produces gerbers. Related: #228.

So the question this issue is for: **what is the engine boundary, and which engines go behind it.**

### Findings on the integration boundary

Three candidate interchange points, checked against KiCad 10.0.4 on a stock Ubuntu install.

**1. Specctra DSN / SES. Available, but not through `kicad-cli`.**

`kicad-cli pcb export` in 10.0.4 offers `3dpdf, brep, drill, dxf, gencad, gerbers, glb, hpgl, ipc2581, ipcd356, odb, pdf, ply, pos, ps, stats, step, stl, stpz, svg, u3d, vrml, xao`. There is no `specctra` and no `dsn`. `kicad-cli pcb import` accepts `pads, altium, eagle, cadstar, fabmaster, pcad, solidworks`, not SES. The headless CLI cannot speak the interchange format that every autorouter speaks.

The SWIG `pcbnew` module can, and it works without a GUI. Verified on a board this pipeline produced:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages python3 -c "import pcbnew; print([m for m in dir(pcbnew) if 'pecctra' in m])"
['ExportSpecctraDSN', 'ImportSpecctraSES']
```

Driving `populateBoard` on the open-key fixture and exporting the result: 2 placed footprints, 8 nets, then a 2508-byte `.dsn` carrying 2 `(place ...)` records and the net list. Round trip confirmed, no X server, no running KiCad.

The cost is a Python dependency in a TypeScript CLI, and `pcbnew.py` is not on the default `sys.path` (it needs `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages` on this install, elsewhere on macOS and Windows). It also writes wxWidgets assertion noise to stderr on import.

**2. circuit-json.** #231 already proposes it as a second draft backend for the schematic. The tscircuit autorouter reads unrouted traces from circuit-json and writes routed traces back, so extending #231 to the PCB layer would give the routing boundary and the viewer boundary the same format. Coordinate conventions are the same care point #231 already names.

**3. KiCad IPC API (`kicad-python` / `kipy`).** Rejected. In KiCad 9 and 10 the IPC API only talks to a running KiCad GUI with the API server enabled in preferences. It cannot manipulate design files headlessly. That disqualifies it for a CI-safe CLI, though it stays the right answer for the Phase 3 "chat panel inside KiCad" item in SPEC.md section 8.

### Findings on the engines

**Routing has real options.**

- [**Freerouting**](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting): open source, the reference DSN/SES autorouter. Headless from the command line (`java -jar freerouting.jar -de board.dsn -do board.ses`), plus a public API in beta at `api.freerouting.app/v1`, plus a native MCP server with an offline local-executable mode. A refactor is targeted at v2.4 around the end of August 2026. Needs a JRE (25 for the current jar). The natural default: local, offline, no account, licence-compatible.
- [**tscircuit-autorouter**](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter) and `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter`: MIT, TypeScript, runs in node. No JVM, no subprocess, no interchange file, same language as this repo. Contingent on #231 landing the circuit-json layer.
- [**DeepPCB**](https://deeppcb.ai/deeppcb-kicad-plugin-ai-pcb-routing/) (InstaDeep): cloud RL router, DSN in and SES out, KiCad plugin, free tier. Cloud-only, so it can never sit in `check`'s path without breaking the network-free contract (AC-2.1).
- [**Quilter**](https://www.quilter.ai/blog/the-2026-guide-to-autonomous-pcb-design-quilter-vs-deeppcb-vs-flux-ai): commercial, but self-hostable on Kubernetes including air-gapped, which is the only paid option that could ever run inside a network-free gate.

**Placement has almost nothing.** This is the finding that should shape scope.

KiCad's own `AUTOPLACE_TOOL` is GUI-only with no CLI surface. Coloquinte gets cited as the open-source analytical placer, but it is a VLSI standard-cell placer in the Coriolis toolchain, not a PCB footprint placer. What exists for PCBs is thin and unproductionized: [pyplacer](https://github.com/ajokela/pyplacer) (simulated annealing over `.kicad_pcb`, minimizing wirelength, overlap, congestion), [kicad-parts-placer](https://github.com/snhobbs/kicad-parts-placer) (deterministic, centroid-file driven, aimed at keeping a fixed form factor), NeurPCB (GNN plus RL, research-grade). [atopile](https://github.com/atopile/atopile) solves the adjacent problem instead: module-level layout reuse, so an imported `rp2040` module carries its known-good placement with it.

Conclusion: there is no third-party placer worth depending on. `shelfPack` is closer to the state of the art than it looks, and the near-term win is our own constraint-driven placement pass (connectors to edges, decoupling to its IC's power pins, crystal near its oscillator pins, group boxes from SUBSYSTEMS.md as placement regions) using connectivity we already parse in `parseNetlist`. `kicad-parts-placer`'s centroid-file interface is the useful idea to steal: a centroid table is a far better placement language for the agent than `(at X Y)` edits scattered through a board file.

### Proposed behavior

**An engine adapter layer, not a router.** Two interfaces in `src/kicad/`, each with a deterministic in-repo default and room for external adapters:

```ts
interface PlacementEngine {
  place(board: BoardModel, netlist: Netlist, constraints: PlacementConstraints): Promise<Placement>;
}
interface RoutingEngine {
  route(board: BoardModel, rules: DesignRules): Promise<RoutedBoard>;
}
```

`shelfPack` becomes the first `PlacementEngine`; a connectivity-aware placer becomes the second. Freerouting becomes the first `RoutingEngine`.

**Write the DSN bridge in TypeScript rather than taking the Python dependency.** DSN is another s-expression format, this repo already has a read-only s-expression parser and already emits KiCad text deterministically, and `board.ts` already does exactly this kind of text surgery. Emitting DSN from our own placement model keeps the toolchain single-language and CI-portable, and SES import is a small parse of wire and via records appended back into the board as text insertions, which is the same anchored-insert pattern `instantiateFootprint` uses. The SWIG path stays useful as the differential test oracle: export both ways and diff, so our emitter is checked against KiCad's own.

**Keep the invariants intact.**

- *Spec-gated in*: a router writes copper, but through a deterministic tool like `draft_schematic`, not through `edit_file`. `edit_file` stays refused on engine-authored regions.
- *Verification-gated out*: every SES import is followed by `run_drc`, and a router returning a DRC-failing board rolls back to the pre-route state, which the grid guarantees is reachable and clean.
- *`check` stays LLM-free and network-free*: only local engines (Freerouting jar, tscircuit in-process) may ever run inside a gate. Cloud routers stay opt-in, explicitly configured, and never on `check`'s path.

**Close the routing gate gap independently of any engine.** `fab.ts` should read `CheckReport.unrouted` and refuse a release on a board with unrouted connections, with an explicit override for a deliberately unrouted draft. That is a small change and it is correct whether or not an autorouter ever lands.

**Cross-cutting**: Freerouting's MCP server is a concrete first consumer for the tool-calling and MCP work in #246, and this whole boundary is the PCB-side counterpart to #231's schematic-side one.

### Alternatives considered

- **Ship the grid and call layout a human step.** Defensible for a first draft, and it is honestly what the "## Draft quality" section is for. Rejected as the end state: the product claim is a design a human refines, not a parts bin arranged by area.
- **Depend on `pcbnew` SWIG for the DSN bridge.** Fastest path, verified working. Rejected as the default because it puts a Python runtime, a platform-specific `sys.path`, and stderr noise into a Node CLI's critical path. Kept as the test oracle.
- **Go straight to circuit-json and route with tscircuit.** Single language, no interchange file, no JVM. Blocked on #231, and it routes in a model that then has to be lowered back to KiCad copper, so DSN/SES is the shorter path to a routed `.kicad_pcb` today. Not exclusive: both adapters can exist.
- **Wait for `kicad-cli` to gain Specctra export.** Not on any roadmap found, and the feature has been GUI-and-SWIG-only across several major versions.

issues.title: Jobs and run orchestration stream: leases, retries, cancellation, and reaping for hosted runs
issues.body:
## Summary

This stream owns the run lifecycle from queue to terminal state: `enqueue_run`, `claim_run`, lease acquisition and renewal, `reap_stalled_runs`, retries, cancellation, terminal-state transitions, KEDA scaling and worker concurrency, runner health and heartbeats, and propagation of run status and events to the platform.

It owns **orchestration, not workspace contents**. Its contract ends at invoking the workspace operations defined by **stream 2** and recording the resulting status.

Most of the control plane lives outside this repo. What is tracked here is the half of the contract only the CLI can provide, and today that half does not exist in machine-usable form: there is no failure classification on the exit status, no injectable run identity, no `SIGTERM` path, and no progress signal a lease renewal can be honest about. Every guarantee below (idempotent retry, reliable cancellation, truthful heartbeats, retry-vs-drain decisions) rests on behaviour that only `copperhead create` / `do` can supply.

## Boundary rule

- **In scope:** the run state machine, leasing, retry policy, cancellation, reaping, scaling, worker concurrency, status and event propagation, plus the CLI-side signals the orchestrator consumes (exit-code taxonomy, run-id injection, incremental progress events, `SIGTERM` handling).
- **Out of scope:** workspace contents, cloning, checkout, and everything stream 2 owns. Nothing here changes what a stage does or how a circuit is designed.
- Structural invariants are untouched: edit tools stay absent from the tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates, and `check` / `verify` stays LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1).
- **Cancellation may never produce a state the verification gate would have refused.** A cancelled run either rolls back or leaves committed complete stages behind. It never leaves a half-written `.kicad_sch` that a later resume treats as done.

## Current state (baseline on `main`)

**1. Idempotency is derived from repo state, not from a run record.** `create` detects a completed stage from the repository itself ([src/commands/create.ts:38](src/commands/create.ts#L38)) and skips it, and stage completion includes ERC-clean, not just file presence ([create.ts:204-210](src/commands/create.ts#L204-L210)). Re-invoking the same command is therefore naturally resumable, which is the right foundation for at-least-once delivery. The catch is that it assumes a **single writer**: nothing in the CLI detects a second process working the same workspace, so a duplicate claim or a zombie worker is silent corruption rather than a refused run.

**2. Resume auto-commits a dead worker's leftovers, under a strict gate.** `commitResumedStage()` ([create.ts:487](src/commands/create.ts#L487)) commits an already-complete but uncommitted stage so a later rollback cannot wipe it, but only when *every* dirty path is copperhead-managed ([`isManagedPath`, create.ts:459](src/commands/create.ts#L459)). Good behaviour to build retries on; it needs to be stated as a contract the orchestrator can rely on, and tested against crash-mid-stage rather than session-limit-mid-pipeline.

**3. There is no `SIGTERM` handler anywhere in `src/`.** Only `SIGINT` is handled, by the renderer ([src/agent/render.ts:104](src/agent/render.ts#L104), exit `130`) and the REPL ([src/commands/repl.ts:391](src/commands/repl.ts#L391)). Kubernetes cancels a job with `SIGTERM` and then `SIGKILL` after the grace period, so today a cancelled hosted run is killed mid-turn: no terminal transcript event, no `summary.md`, no rollback, no run report, and whatever the stage had written left in the tree.

**4. Exit codes carry no failure class.** `create` exits `res.ok ? 0 : 1` ([src/cli.ts:420](src/cli.ts#L420)), `do` exits on `outcome === 'failure'` ([cli.ts:306](src/cli.ts#L306)), `sync` uses `2` for violations, Ctrl+C gives `130`. The distinction an orchestrator needs (retryable transient, terminal refusal, budget exhaustion, environmental gap) already exists *inside* the process: the recovery supervisor produces a `retry` / `abort` verdict ([src/agent/recovery.ts:43](src/agent/recovery.ts#L43)) and the run carries an `outcome` plus `exitPath` pair ([create.ts:1032](src/commands/create.ts#L1032)). None of it reaches the exit status, so the orchestrator can only guess retryability.

**5. Run identity is local wall-clock and cannot be injected.** `runId` is the basename of the transcript directory ([src/agent/loop.ts:254](src/agent/loop.ts#L254)), and that directory is an ISO timestamp ([src/agent/transcript.ts:76-79](src/agent/transcript.ts#L76-L79)). There is no way to stamp the platform's run id onto the transcript, so a platform run correlates with its artifacts only by timestamp proximity.

**6. Liveness is stage-granular and stdout-shaped.** Transcript events append per event ([transcript.ts:87](src/agent/transcript.ts#L87)), but per-stage cost and wall data is assembled only at the end, and the machine report is written once, at run end, to a **fixed, run-independent path** `.copperhead/runs/report.json` ([create.ts:855](src/commands/create.ts#L855)), which the next run clobbers. Per #249 there is no instrumentation below stage granularity at all. A lease renewer therefore has nothing to assert except that the process exists, which cannot tell a working run from a hung provider call. `TurnTimeoutError` ([recovery.ts:8](src/agent/recovery.ts#L8)) is the only in-process liveness bound.

**7. Two retry layers already exist, and neither belongs to the orchestrator.** `maxStageRetries` (default 2, diagnosis-guided re-run) and `maxRepairCycles` (verification repair) both sit below any platform-level retry, so budgets multiply unless the layers are made aware of each other. #135 is the existing symptom: a turn-budget-exhausted stage is retried with the same budget and walls three times.

**8. Node-health failures are indistinguishable from run failures.** The dirty-tree gate (#131), the disk preflight (`COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB`, `src/util/preflight.ts`) and a missing `kicad-cli` (#242) all surface as exit `1`. For a worker these are reasons to drain the node, not to fail the run: retrying them on the same node reproduces them exactly.

**9. Run artifacts are gitignored.** `.copperhead/runs/` is excluded from the very first commit (AC-4.3), so transcripts, summaries and reports do **not** travel with the workspace commit. The orchestrator has to collect them from the workspace before teardown, which makes the teardown ordering part of this stream's contract rather than an implementation detail.

## Scope and deliverables

### Phase 0: the CLI-side orchestration contract (blocking, lands in this repo)

Nothing in the later phases is testable while the runner has to infer everything from exit `1`.

- [ ] **Exit-code taxonomy**, documented in SPEC.md and covered by a structural test: success, verification refusal (terminal), budget or turn exhaustion (retryable with a raised budget), provider transient (retryable as-is), environmental or node-health (drain, do not retry here), cancelled. Derive it from the `outcome` / `exitPath` and the recovery verdict that already exist rather than inventing a second classifier.
- [ ] **Injectable run identity:** `--run-id` / `COPPERHEAD_RUN_ID`, used for the transcript directory name and stamped into the run-start event and `summary.md`, so a platform run id maps to its artifacts exactly.
- [ ] **`SIGTERM` handling with a grace deadline:** stop at the next safe point, flush a terminal transcript event and `summary.md`, take the rollback-or-commit branch the verification gate requires, exit with the cancelled code, and hard-exit if the deadline passes. This is the single largest gap: cancellation cannot be made reliable without it.
- [ ] **Machine-readable result for `create`:** honour the global `--json` (`do` already does, [cli.ts:305](src/cli.ts#L305)) with outcome, exit path, per-stage status, last completed stage, and an explicit resume-safe flag.
- [ ] **Per-run report path:** write `report.json` into the run directory alongside the transcript instead of only the shared `.copperhead/runs/report.json`, and flush it incrementally so a killed run still has one (folds with #140 / #138).
- [ ] **Monotonic progress events** on the transcript (sequence number plus stage and turn), so a lease renewal can assert forward progress instead of mere process liveness.
- [ ] **Crash-equivalence test:** on the fixture project, a run killed mid-stage and resumed reaches the same terminal state as an uninterrupted run.

### Phase 1: run state machine and leasing

- [ ] Explicit state machine with the terminal set enumerated: `queued`, `claimed`, `running`, `cancelling`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `expired`. Every transition idempotent and keyed on `(run_id, attempt, from_state)`, so duplicate delivery is a no-op rather than a second attempt.
- [ ] `enqueue_run` idempotent on a caller-supplied key: re-enqueueing an in-flight run returns the existing run, never a second row.
- [ ] `claim_run` as one atomic compare-and-set. Exactly one worker wins. No read-then-write, no advisory-lock-then-update.
- [ ] Lease renewal interval well under expiry, and renewal gated on the Phase 0 progress events, not on the process being up.
- [ ] `reap_stalled_runs` moves an expired lease to retryable or terminal **by failure class**, and is safe against a worker that returns and tries to renew a lease it has lost: fencing token or attempt epoch, checked on every write.
- [ ] Single-writer guarantee per workspace, enforced at the orchestrator and asserted by the runner, so a reaped run's replacement never runs concurrently with a zombie holding the same repo (see current state 1).

### Phase 2: retries and cancellation

- [ ] One retry budget reconciled across all three layers: platform retry, `maxStageRetries`, `maxRepairCycles`. Document the multiplication, and do not retry at the platform level what the stage supervisor already classified as `abort`.
- [ ] Retry only on classes marked retryable. Node-health classes drain or cordon the node instead of burning attempts (current state 8).
- [ ] Cancellation end to end with the database as the single source of truth: DB intent, runner signal, Kubernetes job delete. Cancelling an unclaimed run is a pure DB transition; cancelling a claimed run waits for the runner's graceful path before force deletion.
- [ ] Cancel is idempotent from every state, including after a terminal transition, and races with completion resolve deterministically (first terminal transition wins, the loser is recorded, not overwritten).
- [ ] Artifact collection happens before workspace teardown on **every** exit path including cancellation and reaping (current state 9), and a failed collection never masks the run's real status (#107 is the local analogue).

### Phase 3: scaling, health, and propagation

- [ ] KEDA scaler on the depth of *claimable* runs, not total rows, so cancelled and leased work does not inflate the target.
- [ ] Scale-down never interrupts a leased run: cooldown at or above the maximum run duration, or a lease-aware deactivation.
- [ ] Worker concurrency: one run per workspace, with the per-node limit documented against what actually binds (the `kicad-cli` subprocess, disk from the preflight, memory).
- [ ] Runner heartbeat kept **distinct** from lease renewal: node health and run progress are separate signals and must fail separately.
- [ ] Status and event propagation at least once with a monotonic sequence so consumers dedupe, and terminal status repeated until acknowledged.

### Phase 4: metrics and tests

- [ ] Metrics: queue time, execution time, retry count by class, lease expiry count, cancellation latency (intent to terminal), failure-class distribution, KEDA scale events.
- [ ] Tests, each reproducing the failure it prevents: worker crash mid-stage; duplicate delivery of one run; expired lease with the original worker still alive and still writing; partial completion picked up by a second worker; cancel racing a terminal transition; `SIGTERM` during an in-flight provider call; reap during artifact collection.

## Acceptance

Every item lands with a test, and the concurrency items land with a race test rather than a happy-path unit test. "It should be fine under contention" is not acceptance. Phase 0 items land with the same structural-test discipline the invariants already use: `test/gating-sync.test.ts` and the `check` module-graph guard in `test/init-check.test.ts` stay green and are extended, never weakened.

## Related

- Stream 2 (workspace operations): the boundary this stream calls into and does not cross.
- #249, performance and token-cost stream: this stream consumes those spans (KEDA scale-out, runner startup, queue time) and does not define the model-side ones.
- #131 dirty-tree gate refuses on copperhead's own run log, #135 retry with the same budget, #140 / #138 incremental log and metric flush, #242 `kicad-cli` discovery, #107 failed rollback takes the run report with it.

issues.title: Files, Git, and artifacts stream: run workspaces, writeback for do/create, and durable artifact storage
issues.body:
## Summary

This stream owns the run workspace and everything durable that comes out of it: how a repository arrives on a runner, how work leaves it, and where generated files live once the workspace is gone.

Everything involving the run workspace and its durable outputs belongs here:

- cloning the repository at the pinned SHA
- clone depth and repository hydration
- `GIT_ASKPASS` and short-lived Git credentials
- branch creation and commit generation
- pull-request writeback for `do`
- direct branch push for `create`
- conflict detection and writeback failure handling
- `.copperhead/` on-disk layout
- workspace isolation and cleanup
- disk quotas and hygiene
- event payload size limits and truncation
- artifact creation, upload, retention, and download
- `runs.origin`
- CLI-created and local projects, from Phase 4 of the CLI integration plan

## Boundary with stream 1

The seam is four operations:

```ts
prepareWorkspace(run): Workspace
writeBack(workspace, runMode): WritebackResult
recordArtifact(run, artifact): ArtifactRef
cleanupWorkspace(workspace): void
```

Stream 1 decides **when** these operations occur. Stream 2 owns **how** they work. No run scheduling, queueing, or run-state logic lands in this stream, and no blob paths or Git plumbing leak into stream 1.

The repo's structural invariants are untouched: edit tools stay absent from the tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates, and `check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1). Artifact upload is a post-verification concern; it never becomes a way for a run to be "done" without ERC and DRC.

## Headline gap: artifact storage

Artifact storage was deliberately left beyond the M1 and M3 boundary. Agent runs now exist, but export has nowhere durable to place Gerbers, PDFs, BOMs, renders, reports, and other generated files. The `/artifacts` surface is therefore still only a shell.

The producers already exist locally and all of them terminate on the runner's disk:

- `copperhead export bom` writes `outputs/<supplier>-bom.csv` ([src/commands/export.ts:31](src/commands/export.ts#L31))
- SVG renders from the KiCad wrapper ([src/kicad/cli.ts](src/kicad/cli.ts))
- the redacted JSONL transcript and `summary.md` under `.copperhead/runs/<ts>/` ([src/agent/transcript.ts](src/agent/transcript.ts))
- the per-run report emitted by `create` ([src/commands/create.ts](src/commands/create.ts))

Every one of those is destroyed with the workspace today.

### First major deliverable

- [ ] Azure Blob storage under `{org_id}/...`
- [ ] an artifact metadata table protected by RLS
- [ ] `record_artifact` wired into the runner
- [ ] server-side user-delegation SAS generation
- [ ] SAS minting only after an RLS-filtered artifact lookup, never from a client-supplied blob path
- [ ] retention, content type, size, checksum, and provenance metadata (run id, stage, producing tool call) on every record
- [ ] artifact upload retry and deduplication rules (checksum-addressed, so an idempotent re-upload produces one record)
- [ ] console download support through the platform contract

This also unblocks the activity log's deferred `ArtifactRef` spill for events that exceed the inline payload limit.

## Scope, in order

### Phase 0: the seam (blocking)

- [ ] Freeze the four operation signatures above, with `Workspace`, `WritebackResult`, and `ArtifactRef` as versioned types
- [ ] Define the inline event payload limit and the truncation/spill rule that `ArtifactRef` satisfies

### Phase 1: artifact storage

The checklist above. Nothing downstream (console downloads, activity-log spill, shareable run outputs) is testable until it lands.

### Phase 2: workspace and Git

- [ ] Clone at the pinned SHA, with clone depth and hydration policy chosen per run mode rather than hardcoded
- [ ] `GIT_ASKPASS` with short-lived credentials; the token never lands in the workspace, the environment dump, or a transcript (AC-4.1 redaction applies to writeback logs too)
- [ ] Branch creation and commit generation, reusing the local snapshot/rollback semantics in [src/util/git.ts](src/util/git.ts) rather than inventing a second model
- [ ] Pull-request writeback for `do`; direct branch push for `create`
- [ ] Conflict detection: a moved base is a reported writeback failure with the run marked accordingly, never a silent success
- [ ] `runs.origin` on the hosted record, matching the local `origin?: 'create' | 'init'` config field ([src/config.ts:71](src/config.ts#L71))

### Phase 3: isolation and hygiene

- [ ] Workspace isolation between concurrent runs on one node
- [ ] `cleanupWorkspace` guaranteed on every terminal path, including crash and timeout
- [ ] Disk quotas per run, with a clear failure rather than a full node
- [ ] `.copperhead/` on-disk layout documented as a contract, since it is both agent memory and an artifact source

### Phase 4: CLI-created and local projects

- [ ] The Phase 4 CLI integration path: projects created locally by the CLI, and local projects adopted into the platform, get the same writeback and artifact contract as cloud-cloned repos

## Acceptance

- A `create` run's Gerbers, PDF, BOM, and SVG renders are downloadable from the console after the workspace has been destroyed.
- A user in org A cannot mint a SAS for org B's artifact, proven at the RLS layer, not only in the UI.
- A `do` run opens a PR against the pinned SHA; a base that moved underneath produces a writeback failure with a specific reason.
- Uploading the same artifact twice yields one metadata record.
- No workspace survives its run, and node disk usage returns to baseline after a run storm.
- An activity-log event over the inline limit spills to an `ArtifactRef` and is still readable end to end.

## Out of scope

- Run scheduling, queueing, and the run state machine (stream 1)
- Token economics and wall-clock performance (#249)
- Tool surface and MCP exposure (#246)
- Anything that changes circuit-design behaviour

issues.title: Performance and token-cost stream: prompt caching at the gateway, per-stage model routing, and cost attribution
issues.body:
## Summary

This stream owns two coupled concerns: **token economics** and **wall-clock performance**. They are tracked together because improvements to one usually move the other (caching cuts both cost and latency; a faster model cuts latency but may cost more retries).

The stream may change how much context the model receives, how often it receives it, and which model processes it. It may **not** change the semantic truth of the instructions.

## Boundary rule (non-negotiable)

- **In scope:** context volume, context frequency, caching, transport, model routing, concurrency, instrumentation.
- **Out of scope:** the meaning of any instruction. A prompt edit that alters circuit-design behaviour belongs to **stream 5** and must be evaluated by **stream 8**.
- Structural invariants are untouched: edit tools stay absent from the tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates, and `check`/`verify` stays LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1).
- Every change lands with a before/after measurement. "It feels faster" is not acceptance.

## Current state (baseline on `main`)

### Token economics

1. **A large fixed preamble is resent every turn.** `buildSystemPrompt()` ([src/agent/prompts.ts:30](src/agent/prompts.ts#L30)) inlines *every* `.md` in `docs/` in full plus the entire constraint registry as pretty-printed JSON. The 23 tool schemas in [src/agent/tools.ts:93](src/agent/tools.ts#L93) serialize to 9,069 bytes (~2.3k tokens) and go out on every turn. On the small `usb-c-breakout` demo repo that is docs 10.6 KB + constraints 4.3 KB + rules/workflow ~3 KB + schemas 9.1 KB, roughly 27 KB (~7k tokens) before a single turn of conversation exists. On a 94-part board (#219) the docs half is several times that.
2. **Docs are inlined in alphabetical order, which is the worst possible order for caching.** `CHANGELOG.md` and `DECISIONS.md` are append-only and the most volatile, and they sort *first*, ahead of the stable `SPEC.md`/`SUBSYSTEMS.md`. One recorded decision therefore invalidates the entire rest of the prefix for the next stage.
3. **Conversation grows monotonically within a stage.** [src/agent/loop.ts:339](src/agent/loop.ts#L339) seeds `messages` and thereafter only pushes ([loop.ts:574-605](src/agent/loop.ts#L574-L605)). There is no compaction, truncation, or tool-result summarization. With `maxTurns` defaulting to 40, the last turn of a stage resends everything the previous 39 produced.
4. **Prompt caching exists on exactly one path.** `src/agent/providers/anthropic.ts` sets three ephemeral `cache_control` breakpoints (system prompt, last tool schema, last message). The OpenAI, compat, claude-code, codex and cursor paths set nothing, and the hosted gateway is a plain proxy that adds no caching of its own, so hosted runs get no prefix reuse at all.
5. **Cache accounting is lossy.** [anthropic.ts:100](src/agent/providers/anthropic.ts#L100) folds `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` back into a single `inputTokens`, so nothing downstream can tell a cached token from a fresh one. The `Cache` column in the create cost table ([src/commands/create.ts:685](src/commands/create.ts#L685)) counts only local disk replays from `src/agent/response-cache.ts`, and it is a percentage of *turns*, not of tokens. There is no dollar figure anywhere.
6. **One model for eight stages.** Config exposes a single `model` with per-stage `stageMaxTurns` but no per-stage model (`src/config.ts`). `spec-seed`, `architecture`, `part-selection`, `schematic`, `layout-draft`, `outputs`, `firmware` and `devplan` all run on whatever the run resolved to.
7. **Retries pay full price and are invisible in the totals.** `maxStageRetries` defaults to 2, and a retry re-runs the stage with diagnosis guidance prepended, which changes the input hash and deliberately bypasses the response cache. That is correct behaviour, but a three-attempt stage costs roughly three times a clean one and the cost table does not separate first-attempt spend from retry/repair spend.

### Wall-clock

No instrumentation exists below stage granularity. `create.ts` records `wallMs` per stage and nothing else. There is no breakdown of KiCad image cold start, clone and workspace preparation, gateway latency, model latency, KEDA scale-out, runner startup, or time spent retrying and repairing. Those spans live in the hosted control plane, outside this repo.

## The two largest levers

1. **Prompt caching at the gateway.** The access pattern (a long stable prefix, a small growing tail, many turns per stage) is exactly what prompt caching is designed for, and the gateway currently does nothing with it. Highest value per unit of effort, and it requires no change to prompt semantics.
2. **Stage-specific routing between `copperhead-fast` and `copperhead-deep`**, instead of one model for all eight pipeline stages.

## Scope and deliverables

### Phase 0: measurement first (blocking)

Nothing in the later phases is acceptance-testable without this.

- [ ] Split input tokens into `fresh` / `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite` through `Turn.usage` and every provider that reports them; stop collapsing them in `anthropic.ts`
- [ ] Per-stage attribution: tokens by class, provider cache-hit rate **by token** (not by turn), wall-clock, turns, retries, and dollar cost from a per-model price table
- [ ] Separate first-attempt cost from retry and repair cost in the cost table and `run-report.json`
- [ ] Emit the same numbers as structured transcript events so hosted runs can aggregate them without scraping the CLI table
- [ ] Commit a baseline for a fixed brief and a fixed board, so every later change is a measured diff against it

### Phase 1: prompt caching (largest lever)

- [ ] Gateway-side prompt caching: stop being a plain proxy, hold cache breakpoints across the turns of a stage, and report cache statistics back on the response
- [ ] Extend explicit breakpoints to the OpenAI and compat paths where the provider supports them; document which paths cannot cache and why
- [ ] Reorder the system prompt for prefix stability: rules, workflow, tool schemas, stable docs (`SPEC.md`, `SUBSYSTEMS.md`), then the volatile append-only docs (`DECISIONS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) and the constraint registry last. Same bytes, same meaning, cacheable prefix.
- [ ] Test that asserts the cacheable head is byte-identical across two stages of the same run

### Phase 2: context volume

- [ ] Per-stage context selection: a stage declares the docs it needs instead of receiving every `.md` (`spec-seed` does not need the BOM; `outputs` does not need the brief prose)
- [ ] Render the constraint registry as a compact table rather than pretty-printed JSON, or filter it to the constraints the stage can act on
- [ ] Per-stage tool-list narrowing on top of the existing gating, so a stage advertises only what it can use. `test/gating-sync.test.ts` must stay green: narrowing may only ever *remove* tools, never surface an ungated one.
- [ ] Bound tool-result growth in history: cap or summarize large `read_file` and report payloads once they have been acted on
- [ ] Deduplicate re-reads (overlaps #229, redundant schematic parsing)

### Phase 3: stage-specific model routing

- [ ] `stageModel` config with the same precedence chain as `model` (flag > env > config), defaulting to today's single-model behaviour
- [ ] Route each stage to fast or deep, and record the resolved model per stage in run metadata so a run stays self-describing (AC-8.1)
- [ ] Escalation rule: a stage that fails on fast retries on deep instead of retrying identically
- [ ] Quality gate: routing defaults change only after a stream 8 evaluation. A cheaper stage that lowers design quality is a regression, not a win.

### Phase 4: wall-clock in the hosted path (control-plane repo)

- [ ] Span-level timing: clone and workspace prep, KiCad image pull and cold start, gateway latency, model latency, KEDA scale-out, runner startup, per-stage execution, repair loops
- [ ] Attack cold start: pre-warmed KiCad image, warm pool or minimum replica count, layer and cache tuning
- [ ] Overlap what can be overlapped (workspace prep during scale-out)
- [ ] Publish a per-run timeline alongside the cost report

## Sequencing

Phase 0 gates everything: without token-class and cost attribution there is no way to demonstrate that a caching or routing change helped. Phase 1 is the highest value per unit of effort and touches no prompt semantics. Phases 2 and 3 are independent of each other. Phase 4 runs in parallel in the control-plane repo.

## Acceptance

- Every phase lands with before/after numbers against the Phase 0 baseline, on the same fixed brief
- `npm run typecheck && npm test` green; spec-gating and AC-2.1 regressions untouched
- No semantic change to any prompt in this stream; a diff that changes instruction meaning routes to stream 5
- For any routing or context-trimming change, design quality is unchanged or better per stream 8 evaluation

issues.title: Ingest an existing KiCad project into a normalized design graph: chips, pinout, BOM fields, and real connectivity are lost today
issues.body:
## Summary

When copperhead is pointed at a KiCad project it did not create, it should parse the project into a normalized, versioned design graph: chips and their identity, full pinout with pin types and functions, BOM with the manufacturer data the project already carries, real net connectivity, netclasses, and board facts. That graph is then the single input for analysis (the review pipeline in #247), for drift, and for the create/do loop.

Today the ingestion path exists but is lossy in specific, verifiable ways, and it throws away an authoritative extraction copperhead already runs.

## The problem

### What happens today

`copperhead init` does ingest an existing project. [scaffold.ts:187](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/scaffold.ts#L187) calls `listSymbols` and `pinNets`, then `generateDocs` writes `BOM.md`, `PINOUT.md`, and `SUBSYSTEMS.md` from them. So there is a starting point. The problem is what does not survive the trip.

**1. Every symbol property except Reference, Value, and Footprint is dropped.** `symbolsOf` at [sexp.ts:227](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/sexp.ts#L227) reads exactly three properties into `SchematicSymbol`. MPN, Manufacturer, LCSC, Datasheet, Description, and every user-defined field a real project carries are never read by anything.

**2. `init` then overwrites the manufacturer data it just discarded.** `bomTable` at [scaffold.ts:34](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/scaffold.ts#L34) hardcodes the MPN column:

```js
(s) => `| ${s.ref} | ${s.value} | ${s.footprint} | UNVERIFIED | extracted from schematic by copperhead init |`
```

A project whose schematic already carries verified MPNs gets `UNVERIFIED` written for all of them, and from that point the drift check enforces the degraded copy. This is the most user-visible defect in the list: ingesting a well-maintained project actively loses data.

**3. DNP and excluded parts become orderable BOM rows.** Nothing reads the `dnp` or `exclude_from_bom` flags, so do-not-populate parts land in `BOM.md` and flow into the supplier export in [bom-export.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/bom-export.ts).

**4. "Chips" is a string prefix.** `generateDocs` identifies the parts worth a pinout as `s.ref.startsWith('U')` ([scaffold.ts:51](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/scaffold.ts#L51)). Connectors, regulators addressed as `VR1`, MOSFETs, and crystals are not chips by that rule, and a `U`-prefixed part is not necessarily an IC. The resulting `PINOUT.md` has refdes, pin number, pin name, and net: no pin type, no pin function, no package, no datasheet, no indication of which pins are power, inputs, or bidirectional.

**5. Connectivity is re-derived by hand and is incomplete.** `pinNets` at [sexp.ts:597](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/sexp.ts#L597) builds its own union-find over wire endpoints. It unions `pts[0]` to each other point of a wire, so a wire endpoint landing mid-span of another wire (an ordinary T tap with a junction dot) is not joined. There is no handling of `bus`, `bus_entry`, or bus-vector labels such as `D[0..7]`, no `no_connect`, and the union-find is rebuilt per sheet with no resolution of sheet pins to child hierarchical labels, so cross-sheet nets only merge when the names happen to match. Real hand-drawn boards use all of these. #217 already reports net merging on dense real boards.

**6. The authoritative extraction is already run, and discarded.** [cli.ts:207](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/cli.ts#L207) invokes `kicad-cli sch export netlist` into a temp dir purely as a loadability probe, then deletes the output. `kicad-cli` is already a hard dependency: no run can start without it. The netlist KiCad itself produces is strictly better than the hand-rolled parse, and copperhead is already paying for it.

**7. The board is never ingested.** `init` reads only the schematic. Footprints as placed, netclasses, stackup, layer count, zones, track widths, and clearances are not extracted by anything outside the drafting engine's own bootstrap in [board.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/board.ts).

**8. The one good extractor is dev-only.** `test/support/netlist.ts` has `parseNetlist` and `netlistToIntent`, used by [scripts/draft-real-designs.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/scripts/draft-real-designs.ts) to ingest the KiCad demo corpus. It lives in `test/`, never ships in `dist/`, and it too drops `fields`, `datasheet`, `pintype`, `pinfunction`, `tstamps`, and `units`, because drafting did not need them.

### What the netlist actually carries

Verified on `kicad-cli 10.0.4` against `/usr/share/kicad/demos/pic_programmer`:

```
(libparts (libpart (lib ...) (part "24C16")
  (fields (field (name "Reference") "U") (field (name "Datasheet")) (field (name "Description")))
  (pins (pin (num "1") (name "A0") (type "input"))
        (pin (num "4") (name "GND") (type "power_in")) ...)))

(comp (ref "C1") (value "100µF") (footprint "Capacitor_THT:CP_Axial_...")
  (fields (field (name "Footprint") ...) (field (name "Datasheet")) (field (name "Description")))
  (libsource (lib "pic_programmer") (part "CP") (description ""))
  (property (name "Sheetname") (value "pic_programmer"))
  (property (name "ki_fp_filters") (value "CP* Elko* ..."))
  (sheetpath (names "/") (tstamps "/"))
  (tstamps "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000442a5056")
  (units (unit (name "A") (pins (pin (num "1")) ...))))

(net (code "1") (name "/CLOCK-RB6") (class "Default")
  (node (ref "U1") (pin "6") (pinfunction "...") (pintype "passive")))
```

Every gap in the list above is filled by data in that file:

| Missing today | Available in the export |
| --- | --- |
| MPN, Manufacturer, LCSC, custom fields | `comp > fields > field` (arbitrary names) |
| Datasheet URL | `comp > fields > Datasheet`, `libpart > fields > Datasheet` |
| Part description | `libsource > description`, `libpart > fields > Description` |
| Pin type (power_in, input, bidirectional, ...) | `libpart > pins > pin > type`, and `node > pintype` |
| Pin function on the net | `node > pinfunction` |
| Netclass per net | `net > class` |
| Multi-unit package structure | `comp > units > unit > pins` |
| Stable per-object identity across runs | `comp > tstamps`, `sheetpath > tstamps` |
| Sheet path and file per component | `property Sheetname` / `Sheetfile`, `sheetpath > names` |
| Footprint filters (package sanity) | `property ki_fp_filters` |

Two of those are worth calling out because they unblock other open issues. `units` is the multi-unit package structure that #218 currently refuses designs over. `tstamps` is a stable object identity, which is exactly what #247 Phase 3 needs for finding identities that survive across runs and support baseline comparison.

### The rest of the toolbox is also already installed

`kicad-cli 10.0.4` offers, all deterministic and offline:

- `sch export bom --fields ...` with arbitrary fields plus generated `QUANTITY`, `DNP`, `EXCLUDE_FROM_BOM`, so the DNP defect above is a flag away
- `pcb export stats`: board width/height/area, min track clearance, min track width, min drill diameter, stackup thickness, front and back copper area, component density, pad counts by type, via counts by type. Free deterministic manufacturability inputs
- `pcb export ipcd356`: the netlist as the board sees it, which makes schematic-to-PCB synchronization a real check rather than an assumption
- `pcb export pos`: placement, side, rotation per footprint
- `pcb export ipc2581`: BOM, netlist, and stackup in one structured file

## Proposed behavior

A deterministic, LLM-free, network-free ingestion step that produces one normalized design graph, and every other consumer reads that instead of re-parsing.

```
copperhead ingest                 # write/refresh the design graph
copperhead ingest --json          # emit it to stdout
copperhead init                   # runs ingest, then generates docs from the graph
copperhead check --mode review    # consumes the graph as pipeline step 1 (#247)
```

Written to `.copperhead/design-graph.json`, versioned, with the source file hashes it was derived from so staleness is detectable without re-parsing.

Shape, sketched:

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "generated": { "kicadCli": "10.0.4", "sources": [{ "path": "board.kicad_sch", "sha256": "..." }] },
  "parts": [{
    "ref": "U4", "uuid": "0000...5056", "value": "AP2112K-3.3",
    "libId": "Regulator_Linear:AP2112K-3.3", "footprint": "Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5",
    "class": "ic",                       // ic | passive | connector | power | mechanical
    "sheet": "/power", "sheetFile": "power.kicad_sch",
    "dnp": false, "excludeFromBom": false,
    "fields": { "MPN": "AP2112K-3.3TRG1", "Manufacturer": "Diodes", "LCSC": "C51118" },
    "datasheet": "https://...",
    "units": [{ "name": "A", "pins": ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"] }],
    "pins": [{ "num": "1", "name": "VIN", "type": "power_in", "net": "+5V" }]
  }],
  "nets": [{ "name": "+3V3", "class": "Power", "nodes": [{ "ref": "U4", "pin": "5", "pintype": "power_out" }] }],
  "board": {
    "layers": 2, "stackupThicknessMm": 1.6,
    "minTrackWidthMm": 0.35, "minClearanceMm": 0.5885, "minDrillMm": 0.6,
    "footprints": [{ "ref": "U4", "side": "front", "atMm": [12.4, 30.1], "rotation": 90 }],
    "netclasses": [{ "name": "Power", "trackWidthMm": 0.5 }],
    "zones": [...]
  },
  "sync": { "schematicOnly": ["C21"], "boardOnly": [], "netMismatches": [] }
}
```

Extraction rules:

- **`kicad-cli` export is the source of truth for connectivity, part identity, and BOM fields.** It is already a hard dependency, and KiCad's own netlister resolves buses, hierarchy, and junctions correctly. The hand-rolled union-find in `pinNets` should stop being the primary connectivity path.
- **The s-expression parser stays the source of truth for geometry**, which no export gives: symbol positions, wire routes, text placement. The legibility checker and drafting engine keep using it unchanged.
- **`test/support/netlist.ts` graduates into `src/`**, extended to keep the fields it currently drops, so the corpus tooling and the product share one extractor and cannot drift apart.
- **Nothing is invented.** A part with no MPN in the project is reported as having no MPN, not as `UNVERIFIED` prose. A pin whose net the export does not name is `null`, not guessed.
- **Chip classification is derived, not prefixed.** Pin count, pin types (presence of `power_in` plus `input`/`output`/`bidirectional`), library category, and footprint family classify a part, with the raw evidence kept so the classification is auditable.

### Then analyze it

Once the graph exists, ingestion feeds three consumers:

1. **Deterministic analysis that needs no model.** Power rails enumerated from `power_in`/`power_out` pins and net classes. Pins driving or driven with no source. Unconnected `power_in` pins on ICs. Decoupling presence per supply pin, derived from the graph plus placement distance from `pcb export pos`. Schematic-to-PCB sync from `ipcd356`. Board geometry against a fab profile from `pcb export stats`. These are exactly the Phase 4 rule candidates in #247, and several of them become cheap once the graph carries pin types.
2. **The LLM review pipeline in #247**, which is currently specified to need a normalized graph as step 1. This issue is that step 1.
3. **Doc generation and drift.** `BOM.md` and `PINOUT.md` generated from the graph carry the real MPNs, the real pin types, and the DNP flags, and drift then checks docs against a graph rather than against a second independent parse.

## Effect on the invariants

- **Spec-gated in:** no effect. Ingestion is read-only over KiCad files and writes only `.copperhead/`.
- **Verification-gated out:** no effect, and it must stay that way. The design graph is an input to analysis, never a gate: a graph that fails to extract degrades the consumer, it does not fail the build. `check` in deterministic mode stays LLM-free and network-free; ingestion is both.
- One caution: `.copperhead/design-graph.json` is a derived artifact, so it must never become a second source of truth that can disagree with the KiCad files. Hence the source hashes in the header and a staleness check on read.

## Related

- #247 hybrid board review: this is pipeline step 1, and the analysis consumer
- #229 reduce redundant schematic parsing in check and draft tools: the shared graph is the fix for that duplication
- #218 multi-unit symbols block 7 of 15 real designs: `comp > units` in the export is the structure that is missing
- #217 router merges nets on dense real boards: connectivity from KiCad's own netlister rather than a hand-rolled union-find
- #200, #196 symbol resolution: `libsource` plus `ki_fp_filters` give a real identity to match against
- #182 `check --fab` is never invoked, #180 constraint registry reconciliation, #232 evidence-backed constraints: all read better off a normalized graph
- [openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/tree/main/openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/): BOM.md is currently the sole export input, so it inherits every loss above

## Open questions

1. Does ingestion belong on `init` (implicit), as its own `copperhead ingest` command, or both? A separate command is easier to test and lets #247 call it without a docs side effect.
2. Is `.copperhead/design-graph.json` committed or gitignored? Committed makes review reproducible and diffable in a PR; gitignored avoids a large derived file in history. The source-hash header matters either way.
3. How much board ingestion is in scope for a first pass. `pcb export stats` plus `pos` is cheap; zones, stackup detail, and `ipc2581` are a bigger lift.
4. Graceful degradation when `kicad-cli` cannot export (a project that fails to load): fall back to the s-expression parser with the graph marked partial, or refuse?
5. Do existing repos need a migration for `BOM.md` files whose MPN column was overwritten with `UNVERIFIED` by an earlier `init`?

issues.title: Copperhead Check: hybrid board review (deterministic + LLM + source-verified evidence)
issues.body:
## Summary

Turn `copperhead check` from a single deterministic gate into a three-mode board review: `--mode deterministic` (today's behavior), `--mode review` (LLM-assisted analysis with datasheet and internet research), and `--mode hybrid` (deterministic first, LLM review for the gaps). Every finding declares how it was produced (`DETERMINISTIC` / `SOURCE_VERIFIED` / `CROSS_VERIFIED` / `LLM_INFERRED` / `UNVERIFIED`) and carries the evidence that supports it.

The architectural invariant this proposes:

> Copperhead Check may use LLMs to discover risks and the internet to verify them, but every finding must disclose whether it was proven, source-supported, inferred, or left unverified.

This is a stream-sized issue in the shape of #246, not a single PR.

## The problem

### What `check` actually does today (verified against `main`)

[src/commands/check.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/commands/check.ts) runs five deterministic families and ANDs them into one boolean:

| Family | Source | Gating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ERC | `kicad-cli` via [src/kicad/cli.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/cli.ts) | fails the run |
| DRC (+ unrouted count) | `kicad-cli` | fails the run |
| Doc drift | [src/memory/drift.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/drift.ts) | fails the run |
| OpenSpec validation | [src/openspec/cli.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/openspec/cli.ts) | fails the run |
| Constraints | [src/memory/constraints.ts:136](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/constraints.ts#L136) | fails the run |
| Legibility + score | [src/kicad/legibility.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/legibility.ts), [src/kicad/score.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/score.ts) | advisory only, never affects exit code |

Three limits are worth naming precisely, because they set the size of the gap:

1. **Constraint enforcement is one rule wide.** `checkForbiddenPins` is the only mechanical constraint check that runs. Numeric budget keys (`min` / `max` / `value`) are parsed into the registry and then not evaluated by `check` at all: its own comment says "numeric budget keys surfaced for the doc-level checks. Geometry checks are out of scope for Phase 1."
2. **The fab gate is dead code.** [src/kicad/fab.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/fab.ts) has no callers (#182), so routing completeness, BOM readiness, and documentation presence are not part of any `check` invocation.
3. **There is no board-level electrical review of any kind.** Nothing in the tree evaluates supply compatibility, decoupling, regulator passives, pull-ups, logic levels, protection, thermal, or return paths. ERC catches unconnected pins and conflicting drivers; it does not catch a 1 uF output cap on a regulator that documents 4.7 uF minimum. [src/kicad/spice.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/spice.ts) exists but is also uncalled from any command.

So the honest deterministic coverage number for electrical correctness today is close to the 18% the proposal uses as its example, and the tool currently reports pass/fail with no coverage statement at all.

### What already exists that this should reuse, not rebuild

- **Design graph extraction is half built.** [src/kicad/sexp.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/sexp.ts) already yields symbols, nets, pin-to-net mapping, and full sheet geometry (`listSymbols`, `listNets`, `pinNets`, `readSheetGeometry`); [src/kicad/board.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/board.ts) parses the board; [src/kicad/dossier.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/dossier.ts) already resolves BOM parts against installed libraries and renders pin facts as a prompt block; [src/memory/bom-table.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/memory/bom-table.ts) parses the BOM. Pipeline step 1 is mostly a matter of unifying these into one normalized graph, not writing a parser.
- **The source cache is already specified.** [openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/tree/main/openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/) specifies `web_search` / `search_parts` / `fetch_datasheet`, the allowlisted egress boundary, the committed datasheet cache keyed by URL plus retrieval date plus content hash, and the `UNVERIFIED` to `VERIFIED(datasheet)` upgrade path. That change is the retrieval layer this proposal's step 4 needs, and #246 owns shipping it. This issue should consume it, not duplicate it.
- **Evidence-backed constraints are already requested.** #232 asks for citation verification on general constraints (`power.sleep_current_uA <= 25` traced to a cached document and a page). That is the same evidence model this proposal needs for `SOURCE_VERIFIED`.
- **Severity separation has a precedent.** The legibility checker already distinguishes `error` from `advisory` and keeps advisory findings out of the exit code, which is exactly the posture `LLM_INFERRED` findings need on day one.

### The contract this collides with

`check` being LLM-free and network-free is not a habit, it is a written contract in four places:

- SPEC.md AC-2.1: "makes zero LLM calls (assert: no network to api.* hosts)"
- [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): "`check` (alias `verify`) is contractually LLM-free and network-free: CI/pre-commit safe"
- [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) Phase 2: the fab gate is specified as "contractually LLM-free and network-free like the rest of `check`"
- A structural test: [test/init-check.test.ts:159](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/test/init-check.test.ts#L159) transitively scans the `check` module graph and fails if any file matches `providers/|from 'openai'|@anthropic-ai`

`add-part-research-tools` already relaxes the global "no network tools" rail in SPEC.md §7, but it explicitly preserves AC-2.1 ("`check` remains contractually LLM-free and network-free"). This proposal is the first thing that breaks that, so it needs a spec-level decision rather than an implementation detail.

**Recommendation, and the one open decision I would settle before any code:** keep bare `copperhead check` deterministic by default, permanently, and make `--mode review` / `--mode hybrid` explicit opt-ins. The proposal's "review is the default during initial implementation, hybrid once deterministic coverage is sufficient" inverts a contract that pre-commit hooks, CI jobs, and the module-graph test all depend on, and it makes the default path non-reproducible and network-dependent for every existing user. Concretely:

- `runCheck()` stays where it is, keeps its module graph clean, and remains what AC-2.1 asserts against.
- Review lives in a sibling module (`src/review/`) that `src/cli.ts` imports only when `--mode` selects it, so the transitive scan in `test/init-check.test.ts` keeps passing unmodified rather than being weakened.
- AC-2.1 is restated as "`copperhead check` with no mode flag, and `--mode deterministic`, make zero LLM calls and no network requests", and a new AC covers the review modes' disclosure requirements.

If the intent really is for review to become the default later, that should be a separate, explicit spec change with its own CI story, not a side effect of shipping the feature.

## Proposed behavior

### Modes

```
copperhead check                        # deterministic (unchanged, CI-safe)
copperhead check --mode deterministic   # explicit form of the above
copperhead check --mode review          # LLM analysis + research, no deterministic gating
copperhead check --mode hybrid          # deterministic first, LLM review for gaps
```

### Verification hierarchy

Every finding declares its provenance:

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `DETERMINISTIC` | proven by a versioned executable rule |
| `SOURCE_VERIFIED` | supported by an authoritative datasheet, standard, or manufacturer rule |
| `CROSS_VERIFIED` | supported by multiple independent authoritative sources |
| `LLM_INFERRED` | engineering inference from available evidence |
| `UNVERIFIED` | plausible concern without sufficient supporting evidence |

LLM findings are never rendered as deterministic facts, and deterministic results are fixed evidence the model may not reinterpret: a failed DRC cannot be argued into a pass.

Severity and confidence stay separate axes. A potentially catastrophic issue can be a blocker at 62% confidence and must still be surfaced, without being called confirmed:

```
BLOCKER · NEEDS_REVIEW · 62% confidence
Possible violation of isolation clearance near J3.
The required working voltage and pollution degree were not provided.
```

### Review pipeline

1. **Extract the design context.** One normalized graph: hierarchy, components and footprints, pins and nets, power rails, buses and interfaces, placement and routing, zones and stack-up, net classes, ERC and DRC results, BOM, approved requirements, design calculations, existing source references, and the git diff. The model receives structured slices of this graph, not screenshots or raw s-expressions.
2. **Run the deterministic checks first** (everything in the table above, plus the fab gate once #182 is fixed). Results enter the review as fixed evidence.
3. **Plan the review.** The model identifies functional blocks, power domains, interfaces, critical components and nets, likely failure modes, missing engineering inputs, and required datasheets, then prioritizes by severity and confidence. The plan is persisted before research begins so the final report can be audited against it.
4. **Retrieve authoritative evidence** through the `add-part-research-tools` boundary: manufacturer datasheets, official reference designs, app notes, errata, standards, fab and assembly capabilities. Primary sources preferred; distributor summaries, forums, and blogs may help discover a source but never independently verify a critical finding. Each retrieved document is cached with canonical URL, publisher, title, revision, retrieval timestamp, content hash, relevant page or section, extracted claim, and extraction confidence.
5. **Review block by block and across system-level interactions.** Initial high-value areas: component suitability, absolute maximum ratings, recommended operating conditions, supply compatibility, regulator stability and required passives, decoupling topology and placement, power sequencing, reset and boot configuration, oscillators, logic-level compatibility, pull-ups and bus loading, connector protection, ESD and transients, MOSFET operating conditions, current paths, thermal dissipation, switching-regulator loops, analog signal integrity, high-speed routing, return paths, grounding, differential pairs, isolation and clearances, programming and debug, testability, manufacturability, BOM completeness, requirement coverage.

### Finding shape

Claims, evidence, inference, and recommendation are separate fields:

```json
{
  "finding_id": "CHK-0042",
  "title": "Possible regulator stability issue",
  "severity": "error",
  "verification": "SOURCE_VERIFIED",
  "confidence": 0.91,
  "objects": ["U4", "C21"],
  "claim": "The selected output capacitor may not satisfy the regulator's stability requirements.",
  "observed_design": { "capacitance": "1 uF", "part": "C21", "connected_to": "U4.VOUT" },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "source_type": "manufacturer_datasheet",
      "document": "U4 datasheet",
      "revision": "Rev. F",
      "page": 17,
      "content_hash": "sha256:...",
      "supports": "The regulator requires at least 4.7 uF effective output capacitance."
    }
  ],
  "reasoning": "The nominal fitted value is below the documented minimum before accounting for DC-bias derating.",
  "missing_evidence": ["C21 DC-bias curve at the operating voltage"],
  "recommendation": "Select a capacitor whose effective capacitance remains above the documented minimum.",
  "automatically_fixable": false
}
```

**No unsourced numeric thresholds.** Any number used to classify a finding must resolve to the design, a retrieved source, a user-approved requirement, or a versioned deterministic rule. This is the rule that keeps the feature from degrading into confident-sounding model memory, and it is testable: a finding whose classifying number has no resolvable origin is a bug.

### Multi-pass verification

One model response never becomes the report.

- **Pass 1, investigator:** find potential issues and missing evidence.
- **Pass 2, researcher:** retrieve sources for each material claim.
- **Pass 3, critic:** try to disprove each finding by checking component variant, document revision, operating conditions, units, pin mapping, package differences, exceptions stated elsewhere in the datasheet, conflicting authoritative sources, and whether the issue applies to this exact topology.
- **Pass 4, adjudicator:** assign `CONFIRMED`, `LIKELY`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `REJECTED`, or `BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE`.

Rejected hypotheses stay in the audit log and are excluded from the headline issue count.

**Contradiction handling.** When sources disagree, show both claims, identify revisions and variants, lower confidence, and request human review rather than silently picking the convenient answer. A newer document is not automatically authoritative if it describes a different silicon revision or package.

### Coverage reporting

Three separate numbers, never collapsed into one:

```
Deterministic coverage:  18%
Source-backed coverage:  67%
Review coverage:         91%
```

Deterministic coverage means executable validation exists. Source-backed coverage means the relevant review used authoritative evidence. Review coverage means the area or requirement was examined by rules or by the model. High review coverage is not proof of correctness and the report must not present it as such.

### Report

```
Copperhead Check

1 deterministic error
4 source-verified issues
7 likely issues
9 missing inputs
3 hypotheses rejected during verification

Deterministic coverage     18%
Source-backed coverage     67%
Review coverage            91%

Overall result: NEEDS REVIEW
```

Grouped as: confirmed deterministic violations, source-verified issues, likely issues requiring engineering review, missing inputs preventing validation, rejected hypotheses, unreviewed areas, deterministic coverage gaps. Markdown, JSON, HTML, and PR-comment renderings; `--json` keeps stable keys per AC-2.4.

### Security boundary

Network-enabled review needs a controlled research boundary, most of which `add-part-research-tools` already specifies: domain allowlist for manufacturers and approved standards bodies, content-type and download-size limits, no execution of downloaded content, PDF and HTML treated as untrusted input, prompt-injection detection with content isolation, bounded and recorded redirects, secrets excluded from queries and prompts, fetched sources stored separately from instructions, source text prohibited from changing tool permissions, and every request in the audit record.

The research agent may retrieve evidence. It may not edit the board, push git changes, expose repository contents, or fetch arbitrary URLs.

**Repository privacy.** Before any cloud or external-model review: classify project files, send only the required structured context, redact git credentials, tokens, usernames, internal URLs, comments, and unrelated files, support per-organization provider and retention policy, offer self-hosted inference for sensitive designs, and record which project objects went to which provider.

### CI policy

```yaml
check:
  mode: hybrid

  fail_on:
    deterministic: [blocker, error]
    source_verified: [blocker, error]

  require_human_review:
    llm_inferred: [blocker, error]

  research:
    network: true
    allowed_sources: [manufacturer, standards_body, approved_manufacturer_profile]

  coverage:
    minimum_review: 0.85
    minimum_source_backed: 0.60
```

LLM-only findings request review rather than blocking merges, unless an organization explicitly opts into a stricter policy.

### Progressive deterministic conversion

This is the part that makes the feature converge rather than sprawl. Every repeated, well-supported LLM finding is a rule candidate:

```
LLM hypothesis -> source-verified finding -> repeated across boards ->
formalized inputs and applicability -> versioned deterministic rule ->
fault-injection benchmark -> default CI check
```

Rule candidates are stored with frequency, affected board classes, supporting sources, false-positive history, required structured facts, expected implementation complexity, and potential severity. Deterministic coverage then goes up over time as a measured number rather than a claim.

## Delivery plan

- **Phase 1, LLM-assisted reviewer.** Normalized design graph from the existing parsers, ERC and DRC ingestion, functional-block and critical-net identification, schematic and PCB structural review, findings with confidence and exact board locations, Markdown/JSON/HTML/PR reports, human confirmation required for every LLM finding.
- **Phase 2, internet-backed verification.** Rides on `add-part-research-tools` (#246): datasheet and app-note retrieval, official-source prioritization, hashed source cache, page-level citations, investigator/critic/adjudicator passes, contradiction detection, prompt-injection isolation, `SOURCE_VERIFIED` findings. Overlaps #232 for general-constraint citation verification.
- **Phase 3, hybrid CI.** Deterministic checks followed by LLM gap review, stable finding identities across runs, baseline comparison with new/resolved/unchanged, configurable blocking policy, coverage gates, expiring waivers.
- **Phase 4, deterministic rule conversion.** Start where inputs are clear: voltage compatibility, missing pull-ups, decoupling presence, regulator capacitor requirements, trace width, clearance, missing protection components, schematic-to-PCB sync, BOM completeness. Each rule passes seeded-fault tests before promotion. Wiring up [src/kicad/fab.ts](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/kicad/fab.ts) (#182) and evaluating numeric constraint keys are the two cheapest wins here and could land before Phase 1.
- **Phase 5, safe remediation.** Source-backed corrections, annotated renders, OpenSpec fix proposals, human approval, controlled edits, rerun and compare, rollback on regression.
