This is the one phase that touches the existing invariants directly: any edit it makes is spec-gated in and verification-gated out like every other mutation.

## Stream ownership

| Area | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Review tool schemas and model tool access | Stream 4 |
| KiCad graph extraction and deterministic rules | Stream 5 |
| LLM review prompts and electronics semantics | Stream 5 |
| Research tools and source-verification framework | Stream 4 |
| Model cost, caching, and routing | Stream 3 |
| Reports, PR review, and console rendering | Stream 6 |
| Provider contracts and CI compatibility | Stream 7 |
| Accuracy benchmarks and rule promotion gates | Stream 8 |
| Report and source-cache artifact storage | Stream 2 |

## Effect on the invariants

- **Spec-gated in:** unaffected for Phases 1 to 4. Review is read-only: it produces findings, never edits. Phase 5 remediation must go through the existing OpenSpec gate with no new path around it.
- **Verification-gated out:** strengthened in intent, but with a hazard worth stating. "Nothing is done until the tools agree" must not become "nothing is done until the model agrees". Only `DETERMINISTIC` and (by explicit policy) `SOURCE_VERIFIED` findings may gate; `LLM_INFERRED` requests review. The repair loop in the agent must never be handed a non-deterministic finding as a hard gate, or runs become unreproducible.
- **AC-2.1 and [test/init-check.test.ts:159](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/test/init-check.test.ts#L159):** need the restatement described above. The structural guard should be preserved for the deterministic path, not deleted.

## Related

- #246 tool-calling framework and part-research tools: the retrieval layer this depends on
- #232 evidence-backed verification for general constraints: the same evidence model, narrower scope
- #182 `check --fab` documentation gate is never invoked: dead deterministic coverage this should reclaim
- #176 DC power-integrity checks via Ki-PIDA: a Phase 4 rule candidate
- [openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/tree/main/openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/), [add-fab-release-gate](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/tree/main/openspec/changes/add-fab-release-gate/), [add-spice-verification-gate](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/tree/main/openspec/changes/add-spice-verification-gate/)

## Open questions

1. Default mode. Recommendation above is that bare `check` stays deterministic permanently. Needs an explicit decision because the proposal as written says otherwise.
2. Where review lives: a `--mode` flag on `check` versus a separate `copperhead review` command that `check --mode hybrid` composes. A separate module keeps the module-graph guard intact either way, but the command surface is a product decision.
3. How coverage percentages are computed. A coverage number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number. What is the denominator: nets, components, functional blocks, requirements?
4. Which provider runs the review, and whether multi-pass verification requires provider diversity (the critic pass is weakest when the same model that generated a finding is asked to refute it).
5. Cost. Four passes over a normalized graph on a 94-part board is not cheap, and #165 already flags quadratic input growth in the loop. Caching and routing are listed under Stream 3 for a reason.

issues.title: Tool-calling framework + skills stream: formalize tool system, ship part-research tools, expose via MCP
issues.body:
## Summary

This stream owns the tool system as a framework and its outward-facing surfaces. It formalizes copperhead's currently-flat tool registry into a real framework (schema registry, tool-name registry, schema versioning, gating, cross-provider adapters, result envelopes, error/retry semantics, view hints), delivers **part-research tools** as the first payload, and then reuses the same schemas to power the Copperhead MCP server and the Claude Code / Codex skills.

## Non-negotiable invariant

Edit tools (`edit_file`, `write_file`, and the other `requiresUnlock` tools) must remain **absent from the model's tool list until an OpenSpec proposal validates** — enforced through code and structural tests, not prompt wording. This is enforced today in `availableTools()` / `dispatchTool()` in `src/agent/tools.ts` and covered by `test/gating-sync.test.ts`. Every change here keeps that test green and adds a matching structural test on any new surface (registry, envelope path, MCP surface).

`check` / `verify` stays LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1). The `test/init-check.test.ts` module-graph guard is extended, never weakened.

## Current state (baseline)

- Tool system is a flat `TOOLS: ToolDef[]` array with **plain-string results**, working structural spec-gating, and cross-provider adapters in `src/agent/providers/` (native OpenAI/Anthropic; `tool-protocol.ts` for reasoning-only Claude Code / Cursor; structured-JSON for Codex).
- **No** schema-registry abstraction, tool-name registry, schema versioning, structured result envelope, or per-tool view-hint metadata yet.
- `add-part-research-tools` OpenSpec proposal is complete (4/4 artifacts) but 0/47 tasks; no `src/research/` code on `main`.
- `add-mcp-server` OpenSpec proposal exists, unimplemented.

## Scope / Deliverables

### Phase 0 — Framework foundations (incremental)
- [ ] `ToolRegistry` keyed by name (wrap `TOOLS`); `get`/`list(ctx)`/gating metadata
- [ ] Schema versioning: `version` on `ToolSchema` + registry protocol version
- [ ] Structured `ToolResult` envelope (`{ ok, summary, detail?, data?, error?, viewHint? }`) that flattens to today's plain-string for backward compatibility
- [ ] Typed tool-error kinds (`unavailable`/`validation`/`refusal`/`exception`) + unified retry policy with `src/util/retry.ts`
- [ ] View-hint metadata consumed by `render.ts` / `dock-renderer.ts` / `theme.ts` (replace the pass/fail regex heuristic)
- [ ] Cross-provider adapters read the registry and round-trip the envelope; keep off-catalog rejection in `parseToolCalls`
- [ ] Extend `test/gating-sync.test.ts` with registry-level gating assertions + envelope round-trip test

### Phase 1 — Re-ratify `add-part-research-tools` (spec-level)
This replaces the "no network tools" rail (SPEC.md §7), so the proposal must be re-ratified before implementation.
- [ ] `openspec validate add-part-research-tools`
- [ ] Reconcile archive/sync ordering with `build-copperhead-phase-1` (tasks.md 7.4)
- [ ] Update `design.md` for the Phase 0 abstractions (envelopes, key-presence gating idiom)

### Phase 2 — Part-research tools (FIRST DELIVERABLE)
Implements the 47 tasks in `add-part-research-tools/tasks.md`:
- [ ] `src/research/net.ts` allowlisted egress boundary (only module allowed to `fetch`; redirect re-validation, timeout, size cap, per-request transcript network-log)
- [ ] `research` config block in `src/config.ts` (absent = disabled)
- [ ] Generalized secret redaction (`*_KEY`/`*_SECRET`/`*_TOKEN`)
- [ ] `SearchProvider` (Brave) + `PartDataProvider` (Nexar) with fixture tests
- [ ] Committed datasheet cache: `.copperhead/datasheets/<mpn>-<hash8>.pdf` + `index.json` + per-page `.pdf.txt`; size-cap `not-cached`; changed-hash revisit obligations
- [ ] Register `web_search` / `search_parts` / `fetch_datasheet`, **structurally absent** unless `research.enabled` AND keys present
- [ ] `sourcing.<refdes>` snapshots + citation drift check + `check --strict-sourcing` (AC-2.1 preserved: zero network in check)
- [ ] `UNVERIFIED -> VERIFIED(datasheet)` upgrade path in BOM handling
- [ ] Scenario tests 1:1 with delta specs; SPEC.md §7/§4.2/§8 edits; `.env.example` keys

### Phase 3 — Outward-facing MCP exposure (`add-mcp-server`)
- [ ] Refactor `check`/`do`/`sync`/`init` into callable entry points (golden byte-identical `--json` parity tests)
- [ ] `src/mcp/server.ts` stdio server exposing exactly four **opaque** tools (`copperhead_check/do/sync/init`) on the same registry/versioned schemas — no file-edit, no raw-KiCad, no partial-loop tools, no network transport
- [ ] Key detection (typed missing-key errors) + per-repo serialization of mutating tools
- [ ] Surface-audit test: no registered MCP tool can bypass spec/verification gating

### Phase 4 — Claude Code + Codex skills on the same tool frame
- [ ] Companion skill under `integrations/claude-code/` (+ Codex equivalent or documented gap): call copperhead's gated tools, never edit `.kicad_*` directly
- [ ] README MCP/host-config section; submit registry listings

## Sequencing

Phase 0 is the shared substrate. Part-research (Phase 2) is the first deliverable and rides on it. MCP (Phase 3) and skills (Phase 4) reuse the identical registry/schemas so external clients and the gated pipeline share one tool frame.

## Acceptance / verification
- `npm run typecheck && npm test` green after each phase; `npm run build` for CLI/MCP changes; `npm run docs:build` for docs
- Structural gating invariant proven by test on every surface
- `check` remains network-free and LLM-free (AC-2.1 regression passes with research configured)

issues.title: check reports a clean pass when nothing was checked: an empty repository passes a hosted review as "ERC, DRC, and drift all clean"
issues.body:
## What happened

Two hosted `check` runs on app.copperhead.sh both returned a green **Passed** verdict with the summary "ERC, DRC, and drift all clean", on repositories where neither check ran at all.

| Repository | State | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fpv-drone-board` | Created from `copperhead-board-template`; `ecad/` contains only `.gitkeep` | Passed |
| `drone` | Entirely empty repository, zero files | Passed |

The run log is accurate about what happened:

```text
worker copperhead-runner-4c7d6-49mj6:1 claimed run (attempt 1)
cloning Chirag6722/fpv-drone-board at 8f2ce51ad266
copperhead check starting
ERC skipped (no schematic configured; run copperhead init)
DRC skipped (no board configured)
finished: passed (done)
```

The verdict rendered above it is not: it reads "ERC, DRC, and drift all clean." Nothing was checked. The org Overview now reports "Passed 2, 100% of finished runs."

## Root cause

`src/commands/check.ts:126`:

```ts
const ok =
  (erc?.ok ?? true) &&
  (drc?.ok ?? true) &&
  drift.length === 0 &&
  (openspec?.ok ?? true) &&
  constraintViolations.length === 0;
```

`erc` and `drc` are `null` when the check was skipped, so `?? true` counts a skipped check as a passing one. `runCheck` returns `ok: true` having verified nothing, and exits 0.

This is a pass over an empty set reported as a pass over a clean board: the same shape as a test suite reporting success because it collected no tests.

The CLI at least prints the `skipped` lines as its output, so a human running it locally sees them. The hosted surface reduces the result to a green badge plus a summary sentence, which is where it becomes actively misleading. The phrase "ERC, DRC, and drift all clean" does not appear anywhere in the CLI source, so it is composed platform-side from `ok: true`.

## Why it matters

A repository that has never had a design in it will pass every hosted review, forever, and be counted in the org's pass rate. The failure is silent and the surface that would reveal it (the log) is collapsed behind a verdict that contradicts it.

## Suggested direction

Distinguish "checked and clean" from "nothing to check". `CheckResult` already carries enough to tell them apart: `erc` and `drc` are `null` when skipped rather than `{ ok: true }`. Options, in rough order of how much they change:

1. Keep `ok` as-is but add a `checked` count or a `skipped` list to `CheckResult`, and have the hosted verdict refuse to claim cleanliness when nothing ran.
2. Introduce a third verdict state (`passed` / `nothing-to-check` / `failed`) so the distinction survives into the platform contract.
3. Make `ok` false when no check ran at all. This is the strongest, and it would change the CLI's exit code for un-adopted repos, so it needs a call about whether `check` on a docs-only repo should be non-zero in CI.

I have no preference between these; the choice depends on what the platform contract wants to consume.

## Separately, possibly related

`copperhead-board-template` ships `.copperhead/config.json` as:

```json
{
  "docsDir": "docs",
  "ecadDir": "ecad"
}
```

`loadConfig` (`src/config.ts:113-115`) reads `schematic`, `board`, and `docs`. It does not read `docsDir` or `ecadDir`, so both keys are ignored and the defaults apply, which is consistent with the `no schematic configured` line above.

This may be deliberate (a newer platform-side schema the CLI has not adopted yet) rather than a defect, so raising it as a question rather than a claim.

## Reproduction

1. Create a repository from `copperhead-board-template`, or an empty one.
2. Connect it as a project on app.copperhead.sh.
3. Start a Review run.

Verdict is Passed, summary claims ERC, DRC, and drift are clean.

Locally, the same shape reproduces with:

```bash
copperhead check --repo <repo-with-no-schematic>   # prints "ERC skipped", exits 0
```

issues.title: kicad-cli is not discovered from standard Windows KiCad installation paths
issues.body:
### What happened

## Bug Description

On Windows, Copperhead fails to automatically discover `kicad-cli` when KiCad is installed in its standard installation directory but `kicad-cli.exe` has not been added to the system `PATH`.

For example, a standard KiCad installation may place the executable under:

`C:\Program Files\KiCad\<version>\bin\kicad-cli.exe`

In this situation, `resolveKicadCli()` reports that `kicad-cli` is missing instead of falling back to the standard Windows installation location.

## Current Behavior

When `kicad-cli` is not available on `PATH`, the fallback resolution currently does not probe the standard Windows KiCad installation directories.

Additionally, the resulting troubleshooting message contains macOS-specific paths, which is misleading for Windows users.

## Expected Behavior

Copperhead should:

1. Attempt the existing explicit configuration and `PATH` resolution first.
2. If those fail on Windows, probe standard KiCad installation locations for `kicad-cli.exe`.
3. Provide Windows-specific troubleshooting guidance when running on Windows.
4. Preserve the existing macOS/Linux behavior.

## Example

A user with KiCad installed at:

`C:\Program Files\KiCad\10.0\bin\kicad-cli.exe`

should be able to run Copperhead without manually adding `kicad-cli.exe` to `PATH`, provided the standard installation path is detected.

## Additional Context

The repository already contains Windows version-directory discovery logic in `src/kicad/symlib.ts`, but equivalent fallback discovery is currently missing from `src/kicad/cli.ts`.

This issue was identified during a repository-wide audit.

## Proposed Fix

* Add platform-aware Windows fallback discovery for `kicad-cli.exe`.
* Make `KicadCliMissingError` and `KicadCliBadOverrideError` provide platform-appropriate hints.
* Add regression tests covering Windows fallback resolution and platform-specific error messages.
* Document Windows KiCad CLI discovery/configuration in the README.

No new dependencies should be required.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install KiCad 8, 9, or 10 on Windows using the standard installer.
2. Do not add the KiCad `bin` directory containing `kicad-cli.exe` to the system `PATH`.
3. Ensure KiCad is installed in its standard location, for example:
   `C:\Program Files\KiCad\10.0\bin\kicad-cli.exe`
4. Clone and build Copperhead.
5. Run:
   `copperhead doctor`
6. Run a Copperhead command that requires `kicad-cli`, such as:
   `copperhead check`
7. Observe that Copperhead reports `kicad-cli` as missing instead of discovering the executable from the standard Windows KiCad installation directory.
8. Observe that the troubleshooting message may provide a macOS-specific KiCad path instead of Windows-specific guidance.


### Output

```shell
No terminal output attached. The issue is reproducible from the steps above; the relevant behavior is that `kicad-cli` is not discovered from the standard Windows KiCad installation path when it is not available on `PATH`.
```

### Which command

check / verify

### Model backend

Not applicable

### copperhead version

v0.9.0

### Node, KiCad, and OS

Node.js: v24.16.0 KiCad: 10.0.5 OS: Windows 11

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I removed API keys and other secrets from everything I pasted.

issues.title: Stage 3 substitutes or drops parts whose symbol is not installed: fetch the exact symbol from LCSC/EasyEDA by MPN into a project-local library instead (13 parts on h2-flask)
issues.body:
## What happened

Stage 3 (part-selection) can only choose from symbols already installed under `/usr/share/kicad/symbols` (or the exclusive `KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR` override, `src/kicad/symlib.ts:80-99`). When a brief or the stage-2 architecture names a real, orderable part whose symbol is not in the stock KiCad 10.0.4 set, the agent burns turns probing `search_symbols`, then either substitutes a "same-family" part or drops the part to a connector. On the `h2-flask` brief (harness `briefs/h2-flask.md`, session `2026-08-17T01-53-42`, `test/real-netlist-corpus` @ `4998f54`, `claude-code:opus`) **13 named parts** had no installed symbol:

`TLV3691` (comparator), `DRV5032` (Hall), `LIS2DH12`, `TTP223`, `TPS22918`, `FS8205A`, `MPX5700`, `TPS63020`, `2450AT18A100E` (chip antenna), `CUD7GF1B` / `XBT-3535-UV` (UV-C LEDs), `SN74LVC1G08` / `SN74LVC1G11` (present only under the `74LVC1G0x` alias). Stage 3 log excerpt:

```
[search_symbols] no installed symbol matches "TTP223" (searched every library in: /usr/share/kicad/symbols). The part is not capturable on this machine as named — choose a part whose symbol exists, or a same-family variant that does.
[search_symbols] no installed symbol matches "FS8205" ...
[search_symbols] no installed symbol matches "CST816" ...
[search_symbols] no installed symbol matches "2450AT18A100" ...
[search_symbols] no installed symbol matches "DMP2035U" ...
```

Expected: a part that exists at a distributor and has a public symbol should be capturable as named. For a client design the substitution is the wrong default — the customer specified `LIS2DH12`, not "closest installed accelerometer" — and every substitution is a decision a human has to re-review in `docs/BOM.md`.

## Proposal

Add a `fetch_symbol` path (tool for the stage-3 agent, and/or a `copperhead symbols fetch <MPN|LCSC-id>` command) that, when `search_symbols` misses:

1. Resolves the MPN to an LCSC id (JLCPCB parts search API works unauthenticated: `POST https://jlcpcb.com/api/overseas-pcb-order/v1/shoppingCart/smtGood/selectSmtComponentList {"keyword":"<MPN>"}` → `lcscGoodsUrl` carries `C<id>`).
2. Pulls the EasyEDA symbol (and footprint) for that id and converts to `.kicad_sym` — `easyeda2kicad` (pip) already does this: `easyeda2kicad --symbol --lcsc_id C180352 ... --output <proj>_Extra`.
3. Writes it into a project-local library, e.g. `libs/<Project>_Extra.kicad_sym`, and registers the nickname in the project `sym-lib-table` — `src/kicad/draft/draft.ts:105-141` already writes that table for the vendored power lib, so the plumbing exists.
4. Makes the resolver see it: today the env override is exclusive, so a fetched library is invisible unless the caller rebuilds a directory of stock symlinks + extras. `symbolSearchDirs` should append project-local libs to the stock set rather than require the override.
5. Records provenance in the BOM row (source: EasyEDA/LCSC `C<id>`, fetched date) so the human reviewer knows it is a fetched, not curated, symbol.

## Proof of concept (worked)

```
python3 -m venv e2k && e2k/bin/pip install easyeda2kicad
e2k/bin/easyeda2kicad --symbol --lcsc_id C180352 C140921 C110926 C80757 C131941 C2830320 C90152 C15483 C89334 C7666 C22046 C165129 --output ./H2Flask_Extra
kicad-cli sym export svg -o chk H2Flask_Extra.kicad_sym    # all 14 symbols render, pins correct (TLV3691: IN+/IN-/GND/OUT/VCC)
mkdir libs && ln -s /usr/share/kicad/symbols/*.kicad_sym libs/ && cp H2Flask_Extra.kicad_sym libs/
KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR=$PWD/libs node -e "import('./dist/kicad/symlib.js').then(async m=>{const d=await m.symbolSearchDirs();console.log(await m.searchInstalledSymbols('TTP223',d))})"
# => [ 'H2Flask_Extra:TTP223-BA6' ]   (LIS2DH12 => H2Flask_Extra:LIS2DH12TR + Sensor_Motion:LIS2DH ..., stock libs still visible)
```

12 of 13 parts converted automatically; `CUD7GF1B` is not on EasyEDA and was hand-written (2-pin LED) — the tool should fall back to a generic symbol with the MPN in Value and say so, rather than substitute a different part.

## Related

- #218 (multi-unit symbols refused): the same run had to swap `TPS62133` because the stock symbol is 2-unit; a fetched EasyEDA symbol is single-unit, so this path also side-steps that class of refusal.
- #227 (footprints unreachable from the sandbox): `easyeda2kicad --footprint` fetches the matching `.kicad_mod`, so the same mechanism could vendor footprints into a project `.pretty` and partially unblock stage 5.
- #212 mentions a stale `KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR` disabling search; #87 notes tool search follows symlinks — the symlinked merged directory used above should be checked against both.
- `bin/doctor.sh` in the harness gates on "222 symbol libraries"; a project-extras approach must be a superset check, not an exact count.

issues.title: Codex provider: double-encoded tool `arguments` abort the run on trailing content — decision_symbols killed stage 3 on both retries, and the supervisor calls it transient
issues.body:
## What happened

On the Codex provider, a tool call whose `arguments` string carries any trailing
content after its JSON object aborts the entire run as a provider error. Expected:
a malformed tool call is surfaced to the model as a tool-level error it can
re-emit, the way every other bad-input path in the loop behaves. Observed: the
parse throw propagates out of `parseStructuredTurn` and kills the stage.

It is not transient. Stage 3 (part-selection) died on it twice in the same
attempt, at nearly the same offset in the same tool's arguments — once as
`decision_symbols` at position 505, once as `decision-symbols` at position 504.
The retry supervisor diagnosed both as transient and spent a full stage attempt
re-running, so the stage burned 20m46s and 706.3k input tokens before stopping.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `copperhead create --brief brief.md --model codex:gpt-5.6-sol` in a workspace
   whose brief drives a part-heavy BOM (this one selects ~60 parts across a
   24-channel discrete measurement chain, an isolated comms domain and a
   comparator protection block).
2. Stages 1 and 2 complete and commit. Stage 3 runs symbol probes normally —
   `search_symbols` and `symbol_pins` calls parse fine for ~20 turns.
3. The stage's decision-log call emits a long `arguments` string; the run dies
   the moment it is parsed. Two auto-retries hit the same wall.

## Output

```
run failed: provider error: Codex tool call decision_symbols has invalid JSON
arguments: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 505 (line 1 column 506)

run failed: provider error: Codex tool call decision-symbols has invalid JSON
arguments: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 504 (line 1 column 505)

stage part-selection: the run ended as "failure" (provider-error); asking the model whether to retry…
stage part-selection: diagnosis → retry — The attempt ended with a provider error, which is
transient, while the machine-verified probes confirm the checked symbols resolve correctly.
stage part-selection: the run ended as "failure" (provider-error); exhausted 2 auto-retry(ies).
Stopping for a human.

Per-stage cost summary
  Stage             Wall  Turns  Out tok  Cache
  --------------  ------  -----  -------  -----
  spec-seed        4m15s      3    20.7k     0%
  architecture     2m07s      3     9.8k     0%
  part-selection  20m46s     21   323.8k     0%
```

The transcript's last good turn parses cleanly, so the failure is specific to the
one call's `arguments` payload rather than to the envelope:

```json
{"type": "assistant", "data": {"text": "The installed center-tapped-primary symbol is
`Device:Transformer_SP_1S`; I'm confirming its package pin numbers before adopting it for T1.",
"toolCalls": [{"id": "pins-transformer-sp", "name": "symbol_pins",
"args": {"lib_id": "Device:Transformer_SP_1S"}}]}}
{"type": "run-failed", "data": {"reason": "provider error: Codex tool call decision-symbols has
invalid JSON arguments: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 504
(line 1 column 505)", "exitPath": "provider-error"}}
```

## Root cause

Two separate decisions combine into a fatal path.

`turnSchema()` in `src/agent/providers/codex.ts` declares tool arguments as a
*string* rather than an object:

```js
arguments: { type: 'string' },
```

So the model must double-encode: a JSON object serialised into a string, inside a
structured-output envelope. Structured output can validate the envelope but cannot
see inside that string — the one field most likely to be malformed is the only one
the schema cannot constrain. `"Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON"` is
the signature of exactly this: a complete JSON value followed by extra content,
which is what double-encoding invites.

`parseStructuredTurn()` in the same file then parses it strictly and lets the throw
escape:

```js
try {
  args = JSON.parse(call.arguments);
} catch (err) {
  throw new Error(`Codex tool call ${call.id} has invalid JSON arguments: ${(err as Error).message}`);
}
```

That throw becomes a provider error and ends the run. Nothing feeds it back to the
model as a recoverable tool error, and nothing strips trailing content or takes the
first complete JSON value.

Three fixes, cheapest first — happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer:

1. Parse leniently: take the first complete JSON value from `call.arguments` and
   ignore trailing whitespace or content (also handles fenced output).
2. Surface the parse failure to the model as a tool-level error so it can re-emit
   the call, instead of aborting the run.
3. Remove the double-encoding: declare `arguments` as an object in `turnSchema()`
   so structured output validates it directly. Largest change, but it deletes the
   failure class rather than tolerating it.

Worth noting separately: the retry supervisor labelled a deterministic parse defect
"transient" and paid for a full stage re-run on that basis. Whatever happens to the
parse, a provider error that reproduces at the same offset in the same tool's
arguments should not be classified as transient.

## Impact

Blocks the entire `--model codex:*` path at stage 3 of 8. This was the first Codex
attempt in this campaign — the provider does not survive a part-heavy stage. The
Claude Code path on the identical brief, same commit, same machine, reached stage 4
without hitting it, because native tool calls arrive as structured arguments and are
never double-encoded.

Secondary observation from the same run: cache hit rate is 0% across all three
stages on this provider, against 706.3k input tokens in part-selection alone.

Which command: create
Model backend: Codex CLI saved login (ChatGPT), `codex:gpt-5.6-sol`, codex-cli 0.144.6
copperhead version: 0.9.0 (test/real-netlist-corpus @ 4998f54, 21 files dirty)
Node, KiCad, OS: v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4, Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS

issues.title: Stacked passives draw as isolated islands: a 16-cap bank carries 26 power symbols where the human used 2
issues.body:
## What happened

After #224 (frame fit, text collisions, compaction), page size across the corpus floors at roughly 2.5x to 4x the human's total sheet area, with utilization above the 50% floor on most boards. The excess is no longer packing: it is the drawing idiom for stacked passives.

Every capacitor in a decoupling bank draws as an isolated island: its own rail symbol above, its own GND symbol below, no wiring to its neighbours. stickhub's shared VBUS bank is 16 caps that the designer drew hanging off ONE +5V trunk and ONE GND trunk, two power symbols total, with junction dots doing the counting. The engine emits 26 power symbols for the same bank and joins nothing. cm5_minima's top row is 28 such islands; jetson's banks are bigger. Each island is several times the drawn footprint of the human's wired equivalent, which is exactly the residual 2.5x to 4x.

Page-size comparison at #224's head (engine sheet over the human's total sheet area): interf_u 1.0x, ecc83 1.0x, royalblue 1.3x, cm5_minima 2.5x, tiny_tapeout 2.7x, openair-max 2.7x, kit-dev-coldfire 3.2x, stickhub 4.0x, complex_hierarchy 4.0x, multichannel 4.0x, pic_programmer 4.0x, sonde xilinx 4.0x.

## The fix: rail-bank trunks

Caps already placed in a decap row (the `decapOwner` reduction) that sit adjacent, at the same pin height, on the same power net, chain on one trunk:

- one vertical stub per pin (unchanged),
- horizontal trunk segments joining consecutive stub ends (junction dots appear automatically at interior meets),
- ONE power symbol and ONE visible value per run, at the first stub end; the PWR_FLAG stays on the net's first endpoint,
- every stub and trunk segment passes `touchesForeign` and a body-crossing check first; any failure splits the run or falls back to per-cap symbols, so a bank can never buy density with a merged net.

Deterministic in the IR, no LLM, no new config.

## How tscircuit handles the same problem

tscircuit's matchpack layout engine hit the identical failure ("capacitors cluster in a chaotic pile" under the generic packer) and shipped a dedicated partition type: `decoupling_caps` partitions bypass the generic PackSolver2 and get a specialized horizontal-row layout, deterministically sorted, with a configurable gap (SingleInnerPartitionPackingSolver.ts, see the linked change record). Their PMARS pipeline (schematic-match-adapt) is corpus-template match-and-adapt, but the decap insight is the same one: banks are an idiom, not a packing problem. copperhead already has the partition half (`decapOwner` plus the uniform decap row); this issue is the drawing half the row is missing.

References:
- https://algora.io/claims/4DJ5YWWYALjN9VN9 (matchpack: specialized linear layout for decoupling_caps partitions)
- https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-match-adapt (PMARS pipeline)

## Done when

- A bank of N caps emits exactly one rail symbol and one ground symbol (plus flags), N-1 trunk joins per side, junctions at interior meets.
- Corpus sweep: label and power-symbol counts drop measurably on stickhub, cm5_minima, and jetson; every drafted board still round-trips lost=0 gained=0; no new error-severity findings.
- Reference goldens and the offline suite stay green (banks of 2+ same-rail adjacent caps are rare on the reference boards; any golden that changes is regenerated in the same PR).

Part of #220 phase 3 (wiring style). The other phase-3 pieces (anonymous-net series chains, adjacency-first ordering) stay tracked on #220.

## Which command

`npm run realdesigns -- stickhub`, then compare the cap bank region of `render/drawn.png` with the original.

## copperhead version

0.9.0, `fix/drawing-quality-220-phases-1-2` at 5ce9ad0

## Node, KiCad, and OS

Node 24.18.0, KiCad 10.0.4 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), Linux 6.6.6

issues.title: Support evidence-backed verification for general constraints
issues.body:
### The problem

Copperhead already supports general engineering constraints through the constraint registry and the `record_constraint` tool. Each constraint has a `source` field, and system-level constraints such as `power.sleep_current_uA` are already supported.

However, the planned `add-part-research-tools` change introduces datasheet caching, citations, hashes, and citation-drift verification primarily around part/BOM sourcing (`sourcing.<refdes>`).

The evidence-backed specification capability for general engineering constraints is not currently implemented as a standalone capability.

For example:

`power.sleep_current_uA <= 25`

may be supported by a datasheet, application note, or specification document. Today, the `source` identifies where the constraint came from, but there is no implemented mechanism that verifies that the referenced evidence actually exists, matches the cached source, and supports the cited location.

The proposed enhancement is to extend the existing evidence/citation approach so that general constraints can also have their supporting evidence mechanically verified.

### Proposed behavior

Extend or clarify the existing citation-drift verification so that it can validate the `source` attached to general constraints, not only `sourcing.<refdes>` BOM entries.

Conceptually:

Constraint
    ↓
source / citation
    ↓
cached evidence
    ↓
citation verification
    ↓
valid / drift

For example:

power.sleep_current_uA <= 25
    ↓
manufacturer datasheet
    ↓
specific page/section containing the supporting value
    ↓
citation/evidence verification
    ↓
PASS or reported drift

The existing evidence, caching, hashing, citation, and deterministic verification mechanisms from `add-part-research-tools` should be reused rather than introducing a separate evidence system.

This enhancement should not introduce network access into the deterministic `check`/verification path. Verification should operate against locally available evidence/cache artifacts.

### Alternatives you considered

1. Create a separate evidence system for general constraints.

Rejected because Copperhead already has a general `Constraint.source` mechanism and `add-part-research-tools` already defines the evidence, caching, hashing, and citation infrastructure.

2. Keep evidence verification limited to `sourcing.<refdes>` / BOM entries.

Not sufficient because Copperhead already supports system-level constraints such as `power.sleep_current_uA`, which may also require traceable engineering evidence.

3. Generalize the existing citation-drift mechanism to general constraints.

Preferred direction to investigate because it reuses the existing architecture and avoids introducing duplicate evidence/provenance systems.

### Effect on the invariants

This enhancement should preserve Copperhead's existing deterministic verification boundaries.

In particular:

- `check`/verification should remain network-independent.
- External research/network access should remain outside the deterministic verification path.
- Evidence should be validated from locally available cached/committed artifacts.
- Existing constraint propagation and `affects` behavior should remain unchanged.
- Existing BOM/sourceability verification should continue to work unchanged.
- No change to the meaning of an engineering constraint should be introduced.

The enhancement should extend evidence verification without weakening Copperhead's existing deterministic and safety boundaries.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Add circuit-json export as a second draft backend
issues.body:
### The problem

A drafted design's only machine-readable artifact is the emitted `.kicad_sch`. Anything that wants to render or consume the design (a live viewer for Phase 2, netlist tooling, converters) has to parse KiCad s-expression text, which is exactly the lifting work our own read-only parser exists to avoid duplicating. Meanwhile the [tscircuit ecosystem](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json) already has renderers and converters (circuit-to-svg, web viewers, gerber, SPICE) that all speak one format: circuit-json, a flat JSON array of typed elements (`source_*` for the logical netlist, `schematic_*` for placement and wiring geometry) with published TypeScript types and Zod schemas.

### Proposed behavior

Add circuit-json as a second backend to the draft pipeline: same intent IR, same engine, one extra serializer after layout. This is a transpiler-style change, a new codegen target for the existing draft compiler, not a new pipeline.

**Current flow (`copperhead create`):**

```
BOM.md + SUBSYSTEMS.md
        v  agent authors netlist intent
schematic.intent.json      (parts, nets, no-connects: no coordinates)
        v
draft engine               (validates IR, computes all placement + wiring)
        v
emit.ts                    (single backend: deterministic KiCad text)
        v
.kicad_sch  -->  kicad-cli ERC  -->  legibility score  -->  done
```

**Proposed flow (same pipeline, second backend):**

```
schematic.intent.json
        v
draft engine  (same lowered placement model, computed once)
        +-->  emit.ts              -->  .kicad_sch  -->  ERC gate   (unchanged)
        +-->  circuit-json backend -->  outputs/design.circuit.json
                                            v
                            tscircuit ecosystem for free:
                            circuit-to-svg, web viewers (Phase 2),
                            gerber / SPICE / BOM tooling
```

Mapping: `IntentPart` becomes `source_component` (pins become `source_port`), `IntentNet` becomes `source_trace`/`source_net`, `noConnect` carries over, and the engine's computed placement fills the `schematic_*` layer, so the JSON depicts exactly the sheet that was emitted and ERC-checked. Output regenerates deterministically alongside the `.kicad_sch`.

CLI surface: `copperhead export circuit-json`, sitting beside `export bom` with the same contract (deterministic, LLM-free, network-free). Tests validate output against the `circuit-json` package's own Zod schemas.

Care points: coordinate conventions (both use mm, but y-axis direction and rotation conventions differ from KiCad's) and keeping the backend a pure serializer over the placement model.

### Alternatives you considered

- **Lift from `.kicad_sch` instead (parse with sexp.ts, recover nets from wires and labels).** More general: it covers `init`'d projects that have no intent.json. But net recovery from geometry is the hardest part, and for drafted projects it re-derives information the engine already had. Scoped as a follow-up for non-drafted projects, not the v1.
- **Export from intent.json alone (`source_*` layer only).** Trivial, but the IR carries no coordinates by design, so renderers would autolayout their own picture that does not match the sheet copperhead drew, scored, and verified. Rejected as the primary path; may still be useful as a netlist-only mode.
- **Import (circuit-json to KiCad).** A separate frontend with a hard symbol-library-resolution problem; explicitly out of scope here.

### Effect on the invariants

No effect on either. Spec-gated in: the export is a new deterministic command, not an agent write tool. Verification-gated out: the KiCad output and its ERC gate are unchanged; the circuit-json artifact is derived from the same placement model after the existing gates run. The read-only guarantee of sexp.ts is untouched (the v1 never parses KiCad text at all).

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Reduce redundant schematic parsing in check and draft tools
issues.body:
### Problem

On a typical `copperhead check`, the same `.kicad_sch` is loaded and parsed multiple times:

- `checkDrift` → `listSymbols` (+ `pinNets` for PINOUT)
- `emptySchematicWarning` → `listSymbols` again
- `checkLegibility` → `readSheetGeometry`
- `scoreFromGeometry` → `readSheetGeometry` again
- `checkForbiddenPins` → `pinNets` again

Each call goes through private `loadSheets()` in `src/kicad/sexp.ts` with no shared cache (~5–6 full parses per check).

`draft_schematic` is worse: it calls `checkLegibility`, then `scoreSchematic`, which internally calls `readSheetGeometry` + `checkLegibility` again (4 geometry reads + 2 legibility passes).

ERC, DRC, and openspec in `src/commands/check.ts` also run sequentially despite being independent subprocess calls.

### Proposed changes

**`src/kicad/sexp.ts`**
- Export `loadSchematic()` returning parsed sheets + power symbols
- Add sync helpers: `symbolsFromLoaded`, `geometryFromLoaded`, `pinNetsFromLoaded`
- Keep `listSymbols` / `pinNets` / `readSheetGeometry` as thin async wrappers

**`src/commands/check.ts`**
- `Promise.all` for ERC ∥ DRC ∥ openspec
- One `loadSchematic()` for drift, legibility, score, and constraints

**`src/kicad/legibility.ts` + `src/kicad/score.ts` + `src/agent/tools.ts`**
- Add `checkLegibilityWithGeometry()` returning `{ report, sheets }`
- `draft_schematic` / `scoreSchematic`: one legibility pass → `scoreFromGeometry(sheets, report)`

**`src/memory/drift.ts`**
- Optional pre-loaded `LoadedSchematic` param to avoid re-parsing in `checkDrift` / `emptySchematicWarning`

**Small maintainability fixes**
- `openai.ts`: lazy-reuse client across `chat()` calls
- `tools.ts`: fix `edit_file` / `write_file` descriptions (unlock on next turn, not same reply)
- `ledger.ts`: remove unused `decision-log` / `onDecision` (`record_decision` already appends synchronously)
- `constraints.ts`: `Set` for forbidden-pin lookup instead of `Array.includes`

### Expected impact

- ~3–6× less schematic I/O+CPU per `check`
- ~50% less post-draft legibility/geometry work
- Faster `check` wall-clock when ERC + DRC + openspec all run (parallel instead of sum)

### Acceptance criteria

- Same CLI behavior, tool contracts, and exit codes
- `npm run typecheck` passes
- Offline tests green (`ledger`, `legibility`, `sexp`, `draft-tools`)

### Out of scope

God-module splits (`loop.ts`, `tools.ts`, `draft/engine.ts`), prompt doc indexing, spatial indexing for O(n²) legibility/draft geometry, lazy agent import from `cli.ts`.

issues.title: The outputs stage contract demands gerbers/drill/DXF/STEP but the tool surface has no kicad-cli mechanism — only export_svg — so stage 6 is unsatisfiable by construction
issues.body:
## What happened

Stage 6 (outputs) instructs the agent to produce a fabrication package — "gerbers+drill
(JLC profile), DXF and STEP outline, SVG renders (export_svg), and an ordering BOM.csv
… Every export must succeed" — but the agent's tool surface contains no mechanism that
can produce any of it except the SVG renders: there is no shell/command tool and no
kicad-cli wrapper; the only export tool is `export_svg`, which writes renders to
`.copperhead/renders/`, not fab outputs. The contract is unsatisfiable by construction:
a fully placed, routed, DRC-clean board would still fail stage 6 on this tool surface.
Observed as two consecutive stage-6 refusals followed by a supervisor abort on the
first run in our harness campaign to commit stages 1–5.

The agent's handling was correct — it identified the missing mechanism rather than
inventing an error (the failure mode your fact-checked supervision addressed) and
deliberately declined to emit a partial `outputs/` (renders + BOM.csv with fab files
silently absent), reasoning that it would read as a completed release package.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `copperhead create --brief <any brief>` and let it reach stage 6 (or resume a
   workspace with 5 committed stages)
2. Stage 6's prompt demands gerber/drill/DXF/STEP exports; the agent inventories its
   tools and finds only `export_svg`
3. The stage refuses on every attempt; the recovery supervisor confirms the contract is
   unreachable regardless of retry and aborts

## Output

Second stage-6 attempt's refusal (transcript `run-refused`, 23:20:33Z):

```
REFUSED. Two independent blockers, one environmental and one a documented BLOCKING
constraint.

1) No mechanism to run kicad-cli. My tool surface has no shell/command tool; the only
export tool is export_svg (writes .copperhead/renders/). gerbers…
```

Supervisor abort (create.log):

```
stage outputs: diagnosis → abort — … no shell tool exists to invoke kicad-cli for
gerbers/drill/DXF/STEP — so the stage's 'every export must succeed' contract is
unreachable regardless of retry.
stage outputs: recovery supervisor recommends stopping for a human.
```

(The co-occurring "zero footprints/pads/copper" blocker is filed separately — the two
are independent: fixing footprints alone still leaves stage 6 unable to export.)

## Root cause

Contract/tool-surface mismatch (locations on `test/real-netlist-corpus` @ `4998f54`):

- `src/commands/create.ts:269` — the stage-6 prompt: "Export into outputs/:
  gerbers+drill (JLC profile), DXF and STEP outline, SVG renders (export_svg), and an
  ordering BOM.csv generated from BOM.md (refdes, MPN, qty). Every export must
  succeed."
- `src/agent/tools.ts:554` — `export_svg` is the only export-class tool registered;
  nothing in `src/agent/tools.ts` invokes kicad-cli or exposes gerber/drill/DXF/STEP.
  kicad-cli appears in the codebase only in doctor/version/report paths.

## Impact

Terminal for 100% of runs that reach stage 6, on any brief, regardless of board
quality. First observed 2026-08-09 (flip7 brief) because no earlier campaign run got
this far; every future run that clears stage 5 hits it.

Smallest viable fix: a purpose-built `kicad_export` tool (plot profiles for
gerber/drill/DXF/STEP via kicad-cli, exit status and report surfaced to the agent) —
a general shell is not required and, given the sandbox design (#85/#87), probably not
wanted.

Which command: create
Model backend: Claude Code saved login
copperhead version: 0.9.0 (test/real-netlist-corpus @ 4998f54)
Node, KiCad, OS: v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4, Linux (kernel 6.6.6)

issues.title: Stage 5 cannot place any part: footprint libraries are unreachable from the sandbox and no footprint-inspection tool exists — a wrong pad map would pass DRC, and the placement-less "complete" stage poisons resume
issues.body:
## What happened

Stage 5 (layout-draft) cannot place a single component, on any brief, because no
footprint definition is readable from inside the pipeline sandbox and no tool can
inspect one. A `.kicad_pcb` embeds full pad geometry inline — there is no by-reference
footprint form in the board file — so placement requires reading footprint definitions.
None are reachable: the system library (`/usr/share/kicad/footprints`, 10.0.4 full set,
present and readable on the machine) sits outside the sandboxed repo root, the
bootstrap writes no `fp-lib-table`, there is no project-local `.pretty`, and the tool
surface has no footprint counterpart to `symbol_pins`. The stage-5 agent refused
placement on exactly these grounds — correctly: pad maps authored from memory pass DRC
(DRC validates given geometry against itself, not against the real part) and fail at
assembly. The refusal then cascaded: stage 6 found a board with zero
footprints/pads/copper and aborted, ending a run that had committed stages 1–5 — the
furthest any run in our harness campaign has reached.

A compounding defect: the stage-5 completion gate accepted the scaffolding-only commit
(board outline, stackup, keepout — no placement), so `create`'s resume counts stage 5
complete and restarts at outputs, which re-fails on the placement gap the "complete"
stage left behind. The workspace cannot recover through resume; it needs a manual reset
to the schematic commit. (Same shape-not-correctness class as #23 / #133.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `copperhead create --brief brief.md --model claude-code:opus` in a workspace whose
   BOM reaches stage 5 with any nontrivial part count (ours: ~150 parts from a
   Bluetooth-speaker brief; any brief that survives stage 4 will do)
2. Stage 5 has no way to read or verify any footprint: probes for a footprint library
   or `fp-lib-table` find nothing inside the sandbox, and no tool answers pad-geometry
   questions
3. Stage 5 either refuses placement (observed — honest) or invents pad maps that DRC
   cannot falsify (the dangerous alternative); stage 6 then dies on a copper-less board

## Output

From the stage-5 commit message (agent's own record, verified against the board file):

```
WHAT WAS REFUSED AND WHY: no component was placed and no net routed, because a
.kicad_pcb embeds full pad geometry inline (KiCad has no by-reference footprint form
in the board file) and no footprint definition is readable on this machine —
/usr/share/kicad/footprints escapes the repo root, there is no fp-lib-table, no
project-local .pretty, and no footprint-inspection tool (symbol_pins resolves symbols
only). Placing the ~150 BOM parts would mean authoring ~150 pad maps from memory that
no available tool can check. A wrong pad map passes DRC — DRC checks given geometry
against itself, not against the real part — and surfaces at assembly.
```

From the run's final supervisor diagnosis:

```
stage outputs: diagnosis → abort — Two independent hard blockers confirmed by grep and
tool inventory — the board has zero footprints/pads/copper and no shell tool exists to
invoke kicad-cli for gerbers/drill/DXF/STEP — so the stage's 'every export must
succeed' contract is unreachable regardless of retry.
```

Highest-risk pad maps if authoring-from-memory were attempted, from the workspace's
`docs/LAYOUT.md` §2.2: BM83 module (symbol pin numbering skips 52–55), VQFN-32-1EP
(EP thermal-via farm), STQFN-20 at 0.4 mm pitch, PowerPAK SO-8 carrying 13.5 A,
SOT-457.

## Root cause

Capability gap, three pieces (locations on `test/real-netlist-corpus` @ `4998f54`):

- `src/agent/tools.ts` registers `search_symbols` (:346) and `symbol_pins` (:371) for
  the symbol side, and no footprint analog — nothing can list footprint libraries or
  return a footprint's pads.
- The path sandbox roots reads at the repo; the KiCad footprint set lives outside it,
  and neither `init` nor stage-5 bootstrap materializes an `fp-lib-table` or a
  project-local `.pretty` inside the workspace.
- The stage-5 completion gate accepts a board with zero placed footprints as stage
  completion (shallow-check class of #23/#133), which is what poisons resume.

Related but distinct: #8 asks for a board-side footprint enumerator in the s-expression
reader — that reads footprints already on a board; this issue is about reaching library
footprints so placement can happen at all. #141 (deterministic placement) presupposes
exactly the footprint access this issue asks for.

## Impact

Terminal for every run that survives stage 4, independent of brief. Observed on the
first run to do so (flip7 brief, 2026-08-09, stages 1–5 committed, ~150-part ERC-clean
schematic): stage 5 committed scaffolding only, stage 6 aborted, exit 1. Placement is
unreachable for the pipeline as shipped, and resume cannot recover the workspace
afterward.

Smallest viable fix, in order: (a) have bootstrap write a project `fp-lib-table`
pointing at the installed system footprints (path discoverable the same way the symbol
side finds `/usr/share/kicad/symbols`), (b) add a `footprint_pads` tool mirroring
`symbol_pins` (pad numbers, positions, sizes, courtyard), (c) make the stage-5 gate
require ≥1 placed footprint per BOM refdes, or an explicit deferral marker that resume
re-opens.

Which command: create
Model backend: Claude Code saved login
copperhead version: 0.9.0 (test/real-netlist-corpus @ 4998f54)
Node, KiCad, OS: v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4, Linux (kernel 6.6.6)

issues.title: Drawing quality: the golden drawings are wired, dense, and anchored; the drafts are labelled islands. Comparison and phased plan
issues.body:
## What this is

A side-by-side reading of the golden drawings (the schematics humans drew) against what the engine drafts from the same netlists, and a phased plan to close the gap. Produced from `npm run realdesigns` on `test/real-netlist-corpus` at e8f9fc0. Connectivity is already exact on all three drafting boards, so this issue is entirely about the drawing.

This issue is the umbrella record for the comparison and the tracking issue for the pieces that have no home yet: **wiring style (phase 3)** and **the density metrics (phase 6)**. The other phases land against #219, #210, and #207.

## The measured state

All three boards reproduce the source netlist exactly (zero pin groups lost or gained), and all three composite at 40, capped below the known-good floor of 85 by error-severity findings. After de5aa02, stickhub's out-of-frame count fell from 367 to 1; the text-collision family was untouched by design.

| Board | Parts | Nets | Human's paper | Engine's paper | Wires | Labels | Error findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stickhub | 94 | 45 | A3, one sheet | A1 | 267 | 197 | 1 out-of-frame |
| cm5_minima | 84 | 95 | 8 sheets, hierarchical | A0, flat | 452 | 205 | 20 text-collision |
| interf_u | 24 | 110 | A3, one sheet | A1 | 322 | 240 | 13 text-collision |

interf_u is the control case: the same part count as the reference board buck-12v-5v, but 110 nets against 11. The trigger for collapse is routing and label density, not part count.

## The same circuit, twice

The human's drawing of cm5_minima's USB subsystem, one of its eight sheets:

![Human's cm5_minima USB sheet: dense, wired, annotated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/e8f9fc0f35f0f8b5a390589aee91d09a421e0aa4/manual-tests/real-designs/examples/cm5_minima/render/original-CM5_MINIMA_3-USB.png)

The engine's draft of the whole board, flattened onto one A0:

![Engine's cm5_minima draft: banded label islands on a flat A0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/e8f9fc0f35f0f8b5a390589aee91d09a421e0aa4/manual-tests/real-designs/examples/cm5_minima/render/drawn.png)

And the engine's interf_u, 24 parts on A1, the content in one narrow strip with the connectivity carried by 240 labels:

![Engine's interf_u draft: one narrow column on A1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/e8f9fc0f35f0f8b5a390589aee91d09a421e0aa4/manual-tests/real-designs/examples/interf_u/render/drawn.png)

The sharpest side-by-side is stickhub, whose CC BY-NC-SA licence keeps its renders out of the repo and out of this issue; reproduce locally with `npm run realdesigns -- stickhub` and open `manual-tests/runs/real-designs/stickhub/render/{original,drawn}.png`. Its human drawing packs all 94 parts on a dense A3: U1 central, USB connectors down the right edge, LED drivers in a wired column, sixteen VBUS caps chained on one +5V/GND trunk pair under a "Shared VBUS capacitance" note.

## Six things the human does that the engine does not

1. **Wires carry the circuit; labels are reserved for names that mean something.** The human wires anonymous nets and labels only long-haul, deliberately named signals. The engine inverts this: its wire rule (single group, at most 4 endpoints, span under 50.8 mm, `engine.ts:1445`) rarely fires because placement never tries to shorten spans, so connectivity collapses into label pairs like `Net-(D15-1)`. An auto-generated name is a wire the designer never named; printing it twice as text tells the reader nothing.
2. **Passives sit next to the part they serve.** The human draws R7 inline between U1's LED pin and D15, wired through. The engine places the resistor and the diode as separate islands, four labels standing in for two short wires.
3. **Banks share a trunk.** The human's sixteen VBUS caps hang off one +5V trunk and one GND trunk, one power symbol each end, junction dots doing the counting. The engine gives every cap its own power symbol above and its own GND below: 26 power symbols where the human used 2.
4. **Edges mean something.** Connectors face the sheet edge they serve, host entry left, downstream ports right. The engine's connectors go to depth-0 columns inside their group rectangle, wherever the group happens to tile.
5. **The hub part anchors the page.** U1 places centrally and everything radiates from it. The engine's U1 lands wherever its column falls in the band order.
6. **The sheet explains itself.** Notes, boxes around functional clusters, and in interf_u a drawn bus for `PC-DB[0..7]`. The engine emits only the group rectangle and its name.

## The plan

Ordered so the score becomes trustworthy first, then the density lever lands, then structure. Each phase ships separately behind the corpus sweep, whose contract (draft faithfully or refuse legibly) does not change.

**Phase 1: count label extents in the frame fit** (#219). The leftmost column's left-facing label text is not counted in its group rectangle, so it overhangs the frame margin: the one surviving out-of-frame finding on stickhub. The `labelExtents` machinery already widens gaps between groups; apply the same extent to the sheet-side margins and band origins. Done when stickhub reports zero out-of-frame findings.

**Phase 2: retire the text-collision family** (#210). All remaining error findings on cm5_minima (20) and interf_u (13) are colliding text. Fix ref/value slot selection to see wires, foreign bodies, and existing text, then let labels alternate above and below the stub and lengthen the stub as a last resort. Done when all three boards report zero error findings, which uncaps the composite and makes every later phase measurable.

**Phase 3: wiring style, the density lever** (this issue). Three placement-side changes so the conservative wire rule can stay:
- *Anonymous-net chains.* Two-endpoint auto-named nets define series chains (pin to resistor to diode). Place chain members adjacent, in pin order, and wire through, generalising the existing crystal and divider idioms. A chain that cannot be wired is a finding, not a silent label fallback.
- *Rail-bank trunks.* Caps assigned to the same owner and rail chain on one trunk wire with a single power symbol per end, deleting two dozen power symbols per bank.
- *Adjacency before labelling.* Order rows and columns to put parts sharing anonymous nets next to each other, then let the existing span rule decide. The thresholds are fine; today placement never gives them a chance.

Done when anonymous nets are carried by wires, not labels, on all three boards, and stickhub's label count drops from 197 to under 80.

**Phase 4: macro placement** (#219). Connector edge affinity, hub-central anchoring, and height-balanced band packing (shelf best-fit), then re-run the paper fit on the packed extent. Done when each board drafts within one paper size of the human's sheet and content covers at least half the usable frame.

**Phase 5: structure beyond one flat sheet** (#207 for the sheets). Buses for indexed net families (`PC-DB[0..7]`), one child sheet per group so cm5_minima's flat A0 becomes eight readable child sheets the way its designer drew it, and group titles plus bank annotations emitted as sheet text.

**Phase 6: measurement** (this issue). Two advisory metrics join `checkLegibility` so progress is visible between phases: content coverage (drawn bounding box over usable frame area) and labels per part. Neither caps the composite; both print in the corpus sweep. Exit target for the corpus: composite at or above 85 with zero error findings on all three drafting boards, papers within one size of the golden sheets.

## Which command

`npm run realdesigns`, then compare `render/original*.png` and `render/drawn.png` per project under `manual-tests/runs/real-designs/`.

## copperhead version

0.9.0, `test/real-netlist-corpus` at e8f9fc0

## Node, KiCad, and OS

Node 24.18.0, KiCad 10.0.4 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), Linux 6.6.6

issues.title: Layout collapses past reference-board scale: 367 out-of-frame findings on a 94-part board, correct netlist, unreadable sheet
issues.body:
## What happened

The engine draws the right circuit and an unreadable sheet once a board is bigger than the reference corpus. Connectivity is exact; layout is not usable.

Found by drafting real designs (#216) and then looking at the renders next to the originals, which is what `npm run realdesigns` now produces. The automated sweep calls these boards a pass, and by its contract they are: draft faithfully or refuse legibly. Faithfulness is not legibility.

All three real boards that draft come out at composite **40**, capped below the known-good floor of 85, against **85.6 to 92 with zero error findings** for the committed reference boards.

| Board | Parts | Nets | Paper | Netlist | Composite | Error findings (true count) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stickhub | 94 | 45 | A0 | exact | 40 | **367** out-of-frame |
| cm5_minima | 84 | 95 | A0 | exact | 40 | 20 text-collision |
| interf_u | 24 | 110 | A1 | exact | 40 | 13 text-collision |
| buck-12v-5v (reference) | 24 | 11 | A3 | n/a | 85.6 | 0 |
| ldo-demo (reference) | 12 | 8 | A4 | n/a | 92 | 0 |

Note the counts are the true ones, read from `suppressed`. The findings list shows ten per family per sheet because of `familyCap`, so `checkLegibility` reports "10" for all three and the real figure for stickhub is 367.

## The stickhub case, concretely

94 parts, 45 nets, netlist reproduced exactly (zero pin groups lost or gained). The sheet:

- every part strung out in essentially **one horizontal ribbon** across the top, with a few short rows beneath it
- roughly **85% of the A0 sheet empty**
- the engine grew the paper **four sizes past the A3 the designer used**, rather than wrapping into a block
- **367 out-of-frame findings**: content is placed outside the drawing frame, so it would not plot
- almost every connection reduced to a label (`Net-(D15-1)`, `Net-(D16-1)`) rather than a wire

The human's A3 of the same circuit puts U1 as a central block with pin names visible, USB connectors down the right edge, LED drivers in a column, the decoupling bank under a "Shared VBUS capacitance" note, and the ESD caps in a labelled box. It is dense and reviewable.

## Why this was invisible until now

The committed reference boards are 12 to 24 parts, where a single ribbon reads fine and fits. Nothing in the suite exercises layout above that, so shelf-wrap and paper selection have never been tested at scale.

`interf_u` is the interesting counterexample: only 24 parts, the same size as `buck-12v-5v`, but 110 nets against 11. It scores 40 too. So the trigger is routing and label density, not part count alone.

## Steps to reproduce

Needs KiCad 10.x with its demo projects, on the branch from #216.

```bash
git fetch origin test/real-netlist-corpus && git checkout test/real-netlist-corpus
npm run realdesigns -- stickhub
```

Then open, side by side:

```
manual-tests/runs/real-designs/stickhub/render/original.png   the designer's A3
manual-tests/runs/real-designs/stickhub/render/drawn.png      the engine's A0
manual-tests/runs/real-designs/stickhub/REPORT.md             netlist comparison
```

## Output

```text
stickhub: DRAFTED  parts=94 nets=45 paper=A0 lost=0 gained=0

composite=40  cap={"appliedAt":40,"reason":"10 error-severity legibility
  finding(s) cap the composite below the known-good floor (85)"}
shown: out-of-frame/error=10
TRUE:  out-of-frame/error=367   (357 suppressed by familyCap)
```

## Which command

`draft schematic`

## Model backend

n/a, the drafting engine is LLM-free

## copperhead version

0.9.0, `test/real-netlist-corpus` at 251929d

## Node, KiCad, and OS

Node 24.18.0, KiCad 10.0.4 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), Linux 6.6.6

## Notes for whoever picks this up

Three separable pieces, probably in this order:

1. **Out-of-frame placement is the hard failure.** 367 findings on one sheet means the layout is not being clamped to the usable frame at all once content exceeds some size. That is a correctness-adjacent bug, not an aesthetic one: the sheet does not plot. Worth checking whether shelf-wrap computes its row width from the frame or from the content.
2. **Paper selection compensates in the wrong direction.** Growing A3 to A0 to fit a ribbon is the opposite of the fix; the ribbon should wrap and the paper should stay small. `low-utilization` already notices the result (`cm5_minima` reports 0.46, `interf_u` 0.29) but only at advisory severity.
3. **Everything degrades to labels.** With 45 nets over 94 parts, almost nothing is wired. `MAX_WIRED_ENDPOINTS` and `MAX_WIRE_SPAN` are tuned for reference-board scale, and a sheet of pure labels is legal but much harder to read than the original.

Related: #141 asks for a reference-board corpus to score layout quality against, which is what made this measurable.

issues.title: Multi-unit symbols block 7 of 15 real designs: opamps, gate packs, and multi-gang jumpers cannot be drafted
issues.body:
## What happened

The drafting engine refuses multi-unit symbols (opamps, gate packs, multi-gang connectors and jumpers). That refusal is correct as things stand: a symbol's units share symbol-space pin coordinates, so placing one instance would silently merge unrelated nets, and validation refuses before anything is drawn.

What was not quantified until now is the cost. A sweep of 15 real KiCad projects (the KiCad 10.0.4 demos, via #216) shows multi-unit symbols are the single largest blocker to drafting a real design:

| Project | Parts | Nets | Multi-unit parts refused |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| complex_hierarchy | 68 | 50 | 2 (LM358N) |
| ecc83 | 15 | 9 | 1 (ECC83 twin triode) |
| kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 | 160 | 209 | 2 (JUMPER_TRIPLE) |
| multichannel | 114 | 79 | 5 (TL072CD) |
| pic_programmer | 63 | 34 | 1 (74LS125) |
| sonde xilinx | 25 | 26 | 2 (74LS125_1) |
| tiny_tapeout | 150 | 108 | 2 (CARAVEL_TT04_BREAKOUT_REVB) |

**7 of 15 projects, blocked by between 1 and 5 parts each.** In every one of those seven, the multi-unit symbols were the *only* refusal: fix this and those boards would proceed to routing. ecc83 is blocked by a single component.

The shape of the gap is worth noting. These are not exotic parts. A dual opamp, a quad buffer, and a triple jumper are ordinary content on ordinary boards, and a board with one TL072 on it is otherwise entirely within what the engine handles today.

## Steps to reproduce

Needs KiCad 10.x with its demo projects, on the branch from #216.

```bash
git fetch origin test/real-netlist-corpus && git checkout test/real-netlist-corpus
COPPERHEAD_TEST_CORPUS=1 npx vitest run test/draft-real-corpus.test.ts
```

Seven projects report `multi-unit=N` in the summary. The suite passes: a legible refusal is a valid outcome under its contract, so this issue is about the capability gap, not a failing test.

Smallest case is ecc83, one part:

```bash
kicad-cli sch export netlist --output ecc83.net \
  /usr/share/kicad/demos/ecc83/ecc83-pp.kicad_sch
```

then convert with `netlistToIntent` from [test/support/netlist.ts](test/support/netlist.ts) and draft.

## Output

```text
U1: "ecc83-pp:ECC83" is a multi-unit symbol (an opamp or gate pack), which the
drafting engine cannot place yet; use a single-unit part instead

IC1: "multichannel_mixer:TL072CD" is a multi-unit symbol (an opamp or gate pack),
which the drafting engine cannot place yet; use a single-unit part instead

JP101: "kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213:JUMPER_TRIPLE" is a multi-unit symbol (an opamp
or gate pack), which the drafting engine cannot place yet; use a single-unit part instead
```

## Which command

`draft schematic` (via `draftSchematicToText`)

## Model backend

n/a, the drafting engine is LLM-free

## copperhead version

0.9.0, `main` at c208680

## Node, KiCad, and OS

Node 24.18.0, KiCad 10.0.4 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), Linux 6.6.6

## Notes for whoever picks this up

The refusal lives in `validateIntent` ([ir.ts](src/kicad/draft/ir.ts)) off `ResolvedSymbol.multiUnit`, which [symsource.ts](src/kicad/draft/symsource.ts) derives from `maxUnitOf(node) >= 2`.

The blocker is that the IR has no way to say which unit a part is. A part is `{ref, libId, value, group}`, and two halves of a TL072 are both `IC1`, distinguished only by unit number, with pins numbered per-unit. So this is an IR change (a unit field, and pin references scoped to it) plus placement treating units as separately placeable instances that share a reference, plus the emitter writing the right `(unit N)` and per-unit pin uuids.

The pin-coordinate collision that motivated the refusal is real and would need handling directly: units must resolve their pins from the correct unit child rather than the shared symbol space.

Related: #159 (rule-based deterministic drafting) sets the direction this sits inside.

issues.title: Router merges nets on dense real boards (+5V/GND on cm5_minima, /PC-RD//WR_REG on interf_u): refused, so undraftable
issues.body:
## What happened

The trunk-and-branch router produces a merged net on real designs, including a **power rail short**. The merged-net guard catches both cases and refuses to write, so nothing wrong ships, but neither board can be drafted at all.

This is the same class as #204 (closed 2026-08-08). The difference is where it surfaces: in #204 the merge survived into ERC, so the engine shipped a short. Now the guard fires first, which is the improvement working. What remains is that the router cannot route these boards.

The engine's own finding text classifies it:

> This is an engine routing/placement fault, not an intent error; the engine's own avoidance should have prevented it. Reshaping the IR is unlikely to help and should not be attempted more than once, report it against the engine with the intent that produced it.

Two cases, from a 15-project sweep of KiCad 10.0.4's demos. They are the only two boards that got past symbol resolution and multi-unit refusal to reach routing, so this is 2 of 2 boards that actually exercised the router.

**cm5_minima** (84 parts, 95 nets), Raspberry Pi CM5 carrier:

```
nets +5V and GND come into WIRE contact at (631.19, 247.64999999999998)
```

That is a rail-to-rail short. Rails are supposed to be drawn as per-pin power ports and never as spanning wires (AC-16.8), so a +5V wire in contact with a GND wire is surprising on its own.

**interf_u** (24 parts, 110 nets), ISA bus interface:

```
nets /PC-RD and /WR_REG come into WIRE contact at (455.92999999999995, 107.95)
```

Only 24 parts but 110 nets, so it is dense rather than large. Net-to-part ratio around 4.6 against roughly 1.1 for cm5_minima, which suggests the trigger is routing density rather than board size.

## Steps to reproduce

Needs KiCad 10.x installed with its demo projects, on the branch from #216.

```bash
git fetch origin test/real-netlist-corpus && git checkout test/real-netlist-corpus
COPPERHEAD_TEST_CORPUS=1 npx vitest run test/draft-real-corpus.test.ts
```

Both boards appear in the summary as `merged-net=1`. The suite passes: a legible refusal is a valid outcome under its contract, so this issue is about the capability gap the sweep exposes, not a failing test.

To get the intent that produced it, the sweep's `roundTrip` writes `schematic.intent.json` into a temp dir before drafting: point `draftSchematicToText` at a kept directory, or export the netlist by hand:

```bash
kicad-cli sch export netlist --output cm5.net \
  /usr/share/kicad/demos/cm5_minima/CM5_minima.kicad_sch
```

then convert with `netlistToIntent` from [test/support/netlist.ts](test/support/netlist.ts).

## Output

```text
##### cm5_minima parts=84 nets=95
nets +5V and GND come into WIRE contact at (631.19, 247.64999999999998) — a wire
endpoint or label of one rests on the other's wire, which KiCad joins into one net,
so the drawn netlist would not match the intent. This is an engine routing/placement
fault, not an intent error; the engine's own avoidance should have prevented it.

##### interf_u parts=24 nets=110
nets /PC-RD and /WR_REG come into WIRE contact at (455.92999999999995, 107.95) — a wire
endpoint or label of one rests on the other's wire, which KiCad joins into one net,
so the drawn netlist would not match the intent. This is an engine routing/placement
fault, not an intent error; the engine's own avoidance should have prevented it.
```

## Which command

`draft schematic` (via `draftSchematicToText`)

## Model backend

n/a, the drafting engine is LLM-free

## copperhead version

0.9.0, `main` at c208680

## Node, KiCad, and OS

Node 24.18.0, KiCad 10.0.4 (Ubuntu 22.04 build), Linux 6.6.6

## Notes for whoever picks this up

The fallback ladder already exists and works: [draft-engine.test.ts](test/draft-engine.test.ts) documents DIV falling back to per-stub labels precisely because every trunk it tried contacted a foreign connection point. The question is why that fallback does not save these two boards, and whether the +5V/GND case is a different fault from the signal-to-signal one, given rails should not be routed as spanning wires at all.

Worth checking first: whether the contact is between two trunks, or between a trunk and a stub end, since #204's fix targeted the latter.

issues.title: Repo hygiene: 3.3 MB of unreferenced assets, nine unarchived changes, and three subsystems without a home
issues.body:
Audit of the tree at `c208680` (main, 432 tracked files, 9.9 MB). Two separable problems: dead weight that is tracked but unreferenced, and three subsystems that outgrew the directories holding them. Everything below was verified by tracing the import graph and the CI wiring, not inferred from filenames.

This is deliberately one issue so the sequencing stays visible. It can be split per phase if that reviews better.

## Part 1: dead weight

### 1.1 `assets/` is 4.0 MB, 41% of the tracked repo, and 3.3 MB has no automated consumer

| File | Size | Consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copperhead.gif` | 714 KB | `README.md:14`, via an absolute `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL |
| `copperhead-1080p.mp4` | 1.6 MB | only a `#` comment in `scripts/demo-rename-1080p.tape:15` |
| `home-resonance.mp3` | 630 KB | only a `#` comment in `scripts/demo-rename-1080p.tape:10` |
| `copperhead-linkedin.gif` | 534 KB | nothing |
| `copperhead-linkedin.mp4` | 533 KB | nothing |

The two `-1080p` / `home-resonance` references sit inside a commented-out ffmpeg invocation documenting a manual video edit. Nothing executes against them. The two LinkedIn cuts are one-shot social posts.

Caveat worth stating up front: deleting these from HEAD does not shrink `.git`. They are the five largest blobs in history and stay there.

### 1.2 `pipeline-run-logs/` is 368 KB with zero references

Three debug logs plus seven raw JSONL transcripts from Jul 22 runs. No reference in code, docs, tests, or CI. Scanned for `sk-` patterns: clean, so this is dead weight rather than a leak. `.copperhead/runs/` is the gitignored home for this kind of output.

### 1.3 756 KB of regenerable PNGs are committed under `manual-tests/reference-boards/`

`test/draft-reference-boards.test.ts` compares `res.text` against the reference `.kicad_sch`, then runs legibility and ERC. It never reads a PNG. The renders exist for human eyeballing and `npm run refboards` regenerates them.

Keeping them is defensible. Worth a deliberate call either way, because every engine change now produces a four-way binary diff while the actual contract is text.

### 1.4 Nine finished OpenSpec changes are still in `openspec/changes/` (105 files)

Complete and archivable: `add-symbol-pin-dossier`, `add-symbol-search-tool`, `add-claude-code-provider`, `add-openai-compatible-provider`, `add-cursor-cli-provider`, `add-supplier-bom-export`, `add-codex-cli-provider`, `turn-budget-continue-and-loop-efficiency`, `record-run-metadata`. `deterministic-schematic-drafting` is at 62/64 and nearly joins them.

Separately, four changes have barely started (`add-mcp-server` 0/16, `add-part-research-tools` 0/33, `prove-live-acceptance` 0/17, `add-fab-release-gate` 1/16) and currently read as in-flight when they are backlog.

### 1.5 `.claude/commands/opsx/` duplicates `.claude/skills/openspec-*`

Six command files against seven skills, with near-identical instruction bodies. Both register, so `/opsx:apply` and `openspec-apply-change` do the same job from two maintained copies.

## Part 2: three subsystems without a home

### 2.1 `src/kicad/` is a 16-file, ~5,700-line grab bag

Five unrelated concerns in one flat directory:

| Concern | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Verification | `cli.ts`, `report.ts` |
| Parsing | `sexp.ts`, `symlib.ts` |
| Drafting | `draft/` (4), `emit.ts`, `dossier.ts` |
| Quality assessment | `legibility.ts`, `score.ts` |
| Export and output | `bom-export.ts`, `fab.ts`, `spice.ts`, `bootstrap.ts` |

Two concrete misplacements:

- **`emit.ts` belongs inside `draft/`.** Its only importers are `draft/draft.ts`, `draft/engine.ts`, `draft/symsource.ts`, and `test/draft-engine.test.ts`. Nothing outside the draft subsystem touches it.
- **`draft/draft.ts` stutters.** Sitting next to `draft/engine.ts`, two files both claim to be the drafting entry point. It is the orchestrator over `engine` + `ir` + `symsource`, so `draft/index.ts` or `draft/pipeline.ts` says that.

`legibility.ts` and `score.ts` are genuinely shared (`agent/tools.ts`, `cli.ts`, `commands/check.ts`, `commands/create.ts`) and belong where they are. `dossier.ts` is used only by `commands/create.ts`, so it is a create-stage concern rather than a general KiCad one.

Not a naming issue, but noted while here: `draft/engine.ts` is 1,637 lines, more than double the next-largest file in the repo.

### 2.2 The terminal UI layer is split across three directories, none of them a UI directory

Nine modules, roughly 1,500 lines:

- `src/agent/`: `theme` (91), `box` (99), `animate` (90), `logo` (23), `render` (238), `dock-renderer` (181)
- `src/util/`: `dock` (161), `live-prompt` (595), `select` (192)
- `src/layout/`: the design docs for this layer, in a directory containing no code

The dependency runs both ways, so neither directory owns it: `util/live-prompt.ts` and `util/select.ts` import `../agent/theme.js`, while `agent/dock-renderer.ts` imports `../util/dock.js`.

`CLAUDE.md` describes `src/agent/` as the provider-agnostic agent loop. Six of its modules are a terminal renderer.

Proposed: `src/tui/` absorbs all nine plus the two layout docs, and `src/layout/` disappears.

### 2.3 BOM logic spans three directories, and the draft engine made it worse

- `src/memory/bom-table.ts` (336) is a generic markdown-table parser serving BOM.md and PINOUT.md. Not memory, and the `bom-` prefix undersells it.
- `src/kicad/bom-export.ts` (321) takes BOM.md as its sole input and never reads a KiCad file, yet lives under `src/kicad/`.
- `src/commands/export.ts` (117) does not say export what.

`src/kicad/draft/ir.ts` now reaches two levels out of the KiCad tree into `memory/` for `parseBomTable`.

Proposed: `src/util/markdown-table.ts` for the parser, `src/bom/export.ts` for the transform, `commands/export-bom.ts` for the command.

## Part 3: naming

### 3.1 Three files named `cli.ts`, three meanings

`src/cli.ts` is the commander entry (472 lines), `src/kicad/cli.ts` wraps the `kicad-cli` binary, `src/openspec/cli.ts` wraps the `openspec` binary. The latter two are deliberately the same pattern, which is good design and bad naming: three identical editor tabs. Rename to `kicad-cli.ts` and `openspec-cli.ts`, matching the binary each shells to.

### 3.2 `test/` is 56 flat files under five naming schemes

The draft work added a 13-file cluster using four conventions at once:

- prefixed: `draft-engine`, `draft-hardening`, `draft-idioms`, `draft-ir-bom`, `draft-layout`, `draft-tools`, `draft-reference-boards`
- module-mirroring: `legibility`, `score`, `dossier`
- behavior-named: `golden-corpus`, `net-merge-guard`
- suffixed, breaking its own family: `cli-draft`

`create-hardening.test.ts` now has a sibling `draft-hardening.test.ts`, so "hardening" is an established convention that conveys nothing: `create-hardening` actually holds KiCad edit-probe validation and drift bootstrap exemption, neither specific to create. There is no rule for where a new engine test goes. `toolcall-extra.test.ts` (65 lines) is unparseable until opened; it tests a field literally named `extra`.
