Doesn't touch the "not an autorouter" line either — this only reads and reports on power delivery, it never proposes or makes a placement or routing change on its own.

### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: spec-seed behavior analysis: both invariants are ceremonial at stage 1, and the stage's load-bearing output (constraints.json) is enforced by nothing
issues.body:
## Summary

A close read of the spec-seed stage as implemented on main @ c72b2da: the gate ([create.ts#L78-L103](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L78-L103)), the unlock choreography, the constraint machinery, and how the stage's outputs reach later stages. This is the behavior-analysis companion to the pipeline-wide audit in #166, zoomed into stage 1.

Verdict in one sentence: **stage 1's two core invariants are both ceremonial at this point in the pipeline, the spec-gate has nothing to gate against yet and the completion gate checks the wrong artifact, while the stage's actual load-bearing output, `constraints.json`, is enforced by nothing.**

## Findings

### 1. The spec-gate is self-referential at stage 1, and its enforcement quietly degrades by environment

`propose_change` writes whatever prose the model supplies ([tools.ts#L172-L185](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L172-L185)). `validate_change` then picks its validation path by checking for the literal file `openspec/config.yaml` ([tools.ts#L198](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L198)):

- workspace present: the OpenSpec CLI validates format
- workspace absent: "validation" is `existsSync(proposal.md) && existsSync(tasks.md)` ([tools.ts#L205-L207](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L205-L207))

`runCreate` discards `openspecInit`'s result ([create.ts#L665](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L665)): if the `openspec` CLI is not on PATH, init fails silently, no workspace exists, and the unlock becomes "the model wrote two plan-shaped files".

So invariant 1 at stage 1 spans three behaviors selected by environment details the operator never sees: format check (workspace present, OpenSpec 1.6), rubber stamp (missing CLI or workspace), permanent lockout (OpenSpec 1.7+ workspace, #142). Deeper than the bug: at stage 1 there are no specs yet for a proposal to be gated against, so the spec-gate's protective value genuinely begins at stage 2, but the code runs the full ceremony (including a per-stage change archive) and buys nothing at seed time.

### 2. The gate verifies the pull channel and ignores the push channel

Stage 1 produces two artifacts, and they reach downstream stages by different mechanisms:

- `docs/SPEC.md` is **pull**: a later stage's agent sees it only if it chooses to `read_file` it.
- `.copperhead/constraints.json` is **push**: every subsequent run loads it ([loop.ts#L318](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/loop.ts#L318)) and injects it verbatim into the system prompt as hard constraints ([prompts.ts#L41-L43](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/prompts.ts#L41-L43)); it also drives `reopenDeferredAffects`, which re-opens revisit obligations when the schematic/BOM later come into existence.

The registry is the mechanism by which stage 1's budgets actually govern stages 2 through 8. Yet:

- the gate reads only SPEC.md text and never opens the registry, and
- the ledger obligation meant to force the dual write is born dead: `record_constraint` opens `constraint-dual-write` and unconditionally clears the same obligation on the next line ([tools.ts#L478-L479](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L478-L479)), and `onConstraintChange` has no other caller. The "commit refuses while the dual-write obligation is open" enforcement can never fire.

Net: the artifact that is automatically enforced downstream is completely unchecked; the artifact that is checked requires downstream cooperation to matter. An agent that writes prose budgets and never calls `record_constraint` passes the stage with an empty registry, which silently disarms budget refusal (AC-3.4) for the rest of the pipeline.

### 3. The gate is an existence proof with three specific defects

1. It anchors on the **first** heading anywhere in the file whose text contains the word "budget(s)": a doc with `## Cost budget notes` above `## Budgets` is parsed at the wrong section.
2. The content bar is one non-blank, non-comment line: `TBD` passes, a stray table separator passes.
3. The section slice ends at the next heading of **any** depth, so budgets organized under `###` subsections read as empty (the I17 false negative; the fix exists as wip commit `5f94875` on `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting`, unmerged).

Mechanics of a post-run false negative are worse than a wasted retry: the run already committed inside `runAgentLoop` (all rollback paths live inside the loop; `runCreate` has none), then the completion-contract recheck ([create.ts#L761](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L761)) declares "no usable artifact was produced", diagnosis fires, retries re-run against an already-good repo, and the pipeline can halt for a human with a healthy committed SPEC.md in git. The operator sees a failure; the repo contains success.

### 4. The stage prompt and the tool contract disagree about the write path

The prompt says "write docs/SPEC.md". `write_file` refuses to overwrite anything ([tools.ts#L281](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L281)). On an `init`-ed repo docs/SPEC.md already exists (scaffold at [scaffold.ts#L54](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/memory/scaffold.ts#L54)), so the literal instruction is impossible: the agent burns a turn discovering the refusal, then must anchored-edit around the scaffold's HTML comments. On a fresh repo `write_file` works. Two divergent first moves, neither mentioned in the prompt.

### 5. Interactive "spec approval" approves intent, not output

The human gate in `validate_change` ([tools.ts#L211-L213](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/agent/tools.ts#L211-L213)) fires before SPEC.md exists: the human approves the model's plan to write a spec. No human ever reviews the budgets the model actually wrote, in either mode. Given finding 2, the one thing `--interactive` should surface, "here are the budgets I extracted from your brief, machine form and prose form", is shown to no one.

### 6. The brief decouples from the repo the moment stage 1 commits

The brief is hashed into run metadata only ([create.ts#L646](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L646)); it is never committed, and no gate ties SPEC.md back to it. Edit the brief after stage 1 and the pipeline continues against the old SPEC.md; the only trace is a different sha256 in transcript metadata. The requirements' source document is the one thing allowed to drift freely.

## Suggested order of fixes (by leverage)

- [ ] **Enforce the registry (finding 2)**: gate requires `constraints.json` non-empty and every registry key traceable to a Budgets line (cheap symmetry check, drift-style); fix or remove the born-dead dual-write obligation
- [ ] **Make unlock degradation loud (finding 1)**: fail `create` when `openspecInit` fails; log which validation mode `validate_change` is using; fix #142's two one-liners
- [ ] **Harden the gate (finding 3)**: merge the I17 fix from `5f94875`; anchor on a Budgets heading rather than any budget-containing heading; raise the content bar to at least one budget-shaped line
- [ ] **Prompt/UX corrections (findings 4, 5, 6)**: tell the agent the scaffold may exist and edit_file is the path; move or add the interactive review to after SPEC.md is written; commit the brief (or its hash) into the repo so divergence is detectable

None of this needs new machinery: every fix is a stricter `isComplete`, an un-swallowed error, or a moved `clear()`.

Related: #166 (pipeline-wide audit), #142 (OpenSpec 1.7+ lockout), #133 (gates verify shape), #23 (shallow existence checks), #21 (pre-commit hook vs docs-lead-schematic ordering), #66 (end-to-end bounty; I17 numbering comes from its findings report).

issues.title: Remove the Synap cross-run memory integration
issues.body:
## What

Remove the optional Synap cross-run memory integration (`@maximem/synap-js-sdk`): the `src/memory/synap.ts` module, its recall/record hooks in the agent loop, the `SYNAP_*` environment variables, and the related docs.

## Why

The integration adds an optional third-party dependency and a Python bridge subprocess for a feature that is off by default and unused. Removing it simplifies the agent loop (no memory lifecycle to own, no shutdown needed for a clean CLI exit) and drops a network side channel; in-repo docs and constraints remain the agent's only memory, which is already the documented source of truth.

## Scope

- Delete `src/memory/synap.ts` and `test/synap.test.ts`
- Remove the recall-into-system-prompt and record-on-finish hooks from `src/agent/loop.ts`
- Drop `@maximem/synap-js-sdk` from `optionalDependencies`
- Remove `SYNAP_API_KEY` / `SYNAP_USER_ID` / `SYNAP_CUSTOMER_ID` from `.env.example` and the configuration reference, including the "Cross-run memory" docs section

issues.title: Pipeline audit: verification strength is placed inversely to blast radius across the eight create stages
issues.body:
## Summary

A stage-by-stage audit of the `create` pipeline (brief.md in, gerbers out) against what each stage promises. The finding in one sentence: **verification strength is placed inversely to blast radius**. The middle of the pipeline (stage 4) has the strongest gate and is getting stronger, while the ends, stage 1 which defines what "correct" means for everything downstream, and stage 6 which is where money gets spent, have existence checks only. Meanwhile the loop machinery under all eight stages has failure modes that waste retries and kill recoverable runs.

There is still no proven clean end-to-end run on record (#66). The best-documented attempt (#163) died at stage 4/8 after 3h11m and 956k output tokens.

The brokenness comes in three flavors, and they need different fixes:

1. **Gates that verify shape, not correctness** (#133): 5 of 8 stages check only that a file exists with plausible content.
2. **Concrete bugs** with issue numbers, several with fixes stranded unmerged on `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting`.
3. **Run economics**: token growth and retry behavior that make every stage fragile regardless of its gate.

All `create.ts` references below are against main @ c72b2da.

## Stage-by-stage

### Stage 1: spec-seed

- **Gate false-negative bug**: the Budgets-section extractor slices from the heading to the next heading of any level ([create.ts#L95](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L95)). Budgets organized under `###` subsections read as empty, so a complete stage re-runs. The fix (I17, `5f94875`) is unmerged on the drafting branch.
- **The machine-readable half is unenforced**: the prompt demands every budget also go through `record_constraint`, but the gate never opens the constraint registry. An empty `constraints.json` passes, silently disarming budget refusal (AC-3.4) downstream.
- **OpenSpec seeding is broken on OpenSpec 1.7+** (#142): `propose_change` omits `.openspec.yaml` and validation lacks `--type change`.
- Nothing checks ASSUMED flags were applied, or budgets against the brief. The stage with the largest blast radius has the least verification relative to it.

### Stage 2: architecture

- **Weakest gate in the pipeline**: one `##` heading plus one prose line surviving boilerplate filters. No check that subsystems cover the brief, carry reasoning, or reference SPEC.md budgets.
- The boilerplate filters are regexes guessing at LLM output and each has needed patching (latest: `fad3bb3`, refdes-bullet regex swallowed `- 5V:` bullets).

### Stage 3: part-selection

- **The gate is satisfied by one row**: a 60-part BOM with one real MPN and 59 placeholders passes.
- **Every MPN is guesswork by construction**: no network tools, so "datasheet-verifiable justification" means the model remembers a datasheet. #47 asks for catalog lookup; `add-part-research-tools` is the structural fix and is essentially not started.
- **This stage poisons stage 4**: nothing constrains the BOM Value column format, yet the drafting engine pins symbol values to it by exact string equality (root cause of #163).
- Doc-as-database parsing is fragile: the last six commits on main are all BOM.md table-parsing fixes.

### Stage 4: schematic

Strongest gate (symbols + drift-clean + ERC), still the stage where real runs die:

- **Proven deadlock** (#163): the BOM value cross-check and the legibility gate contradict each other, and `edit_file` is refused on drafted sheets, so the agent has no legal move. Any brief with descriptive BOM values hits it.
- **ERC gates the graph, not the drawing** (#136): electrically clean, unreadable schematics pass. The drafting branch (18 commits, unmerged) exists to fix this and introduced #163 in the process.
- **`verify_symbols` is advisory** (#133): hallucinated pin sets that pass ERC are prompt-discouraged, not gated.
- **Worst-hit by loop economics**: cost concentrates in a handful of giant turns, each a single point of failure (#145), and quadratic history growth (#165) taxes the longest stage hardest.

### Stage 5: layout-draft

- **The gate never runs DRC**: the prompt requires `run_drc` on every routed net, but `isComplete` checks only footprints-exist plus the `## Draft quality` marker ([create.ts#L184-L195](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/c72b2da/src/commands/create.ts#L184-L195)). A DRC-failing board advances, and on resume is skipped as already complete.
- Placement and routing are LLM-sampled coordinates with no deterministic engine and no quality scoring (#141). The honesty section is checked as a string marker, not for content.

### Stage 6: outputs

- **The gate is "any `.gbr` file exists"**: no freshness check, so gerbers exported from an earlier board revision satisfy the gate forever. `add-fab-release-gate` (routing completeness, BOM readiness, sch/pcb parity, content-hash freshness) is the designed fix, 1 of 16 tasks done.
- **The ordering BOM orders phantom parts** (#99): supporting tables in BOM.md, including header rows, become order lines.
- STEP, DXF, SVG, and BOM.csv are all requested and none are gated.

### Stage 7: firmware

- **The gate accepts any source file**: `pins.h`, the stated point of the stage, is not required.
- **The one existing cross-check is vacuous** (#105): sync's pins.h check substring-matches PINOUT.md, so any word anywhere satisfies any `#define`. It can never fail.
- "Build must pass if toolchain available" is never checked by anything.

### Stage 8: devplan

- Gate is heading + one content line. Pure existence, but the least broken relative to its stakes: it is prose for a human, and a human will read it.

## Cross-cutting machinery (breaks any stage)

- #135: a turn-budget-exhausted stage retries with the same budget, walling up to three times in a row.
- #101: `parseDiagnosis` reads a retry verdict as abort when a brace precedes the JSON, killing recoverable runs.
- #165: the loop re-sends the whole conversation every turn, so input cost grows quadratically.
- #131: the dirty-tree gate refuses to run over copperhead's own `.copperhead/runs/` logs.
- #107: a failed rollback takes the run report with it.
- #103: init silently skips the pre-commit hook when one exists, so the commit gate is off without saying so.
- #89: `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=""` silently disables the disk preflight.
- I18 (unmerged, `e71b1fd`): providers can silently withhold tools instead of surfacing the dropped call.

## Critical path to one clean run (#66)

The gate-hardening above makes runs honest, not successful. The narrower path to a first clean brief-to-gerbers run:

- [ ] Merge the drafting branch's I17 and I18 fixes (`5f94875`, `e71b1fd`, currently wip-flagged)
- [ ] Resolve the #163 deadlock: it is a contract bug, either the value cross-check needs a legibility escape hatch or stage 3 needs a constrained Value column
- [ ] Fix #135 and #101 so recovery stops eating retries
- [ ] Then harden the ends: layout gate runs DRC, outputs gate checks freshness (`add-fab-release-gate`), firmware gate requires `pins.h`, spec gate requires a non-empty constraint registry

Related tracking: #133 (gate correctness), #66 (end-to-end bounty), #163 (stage 4 deadlock), #145 / #165 (economics).

issues.title: The agent loop re-sends the entire conversation every turn, so input cost grows quadratically — nothing caps or prunes history
issues.body:
## The problem

Nothing ever trims the conversation the agent loop re-sends. Every provider gets the full accumulated history on every turn — `claude-code` flattens it with `renderConversation` (`tool-protocol.ts`), and the keyed providers post the whole `messages` array — so per-turn input cost grows roughly quadratically in turns.

There is no pruning, no windowing, and no size cap anywhere on that path:

- `src/agent/loop.ts` appends to `messages` and never removes or shortens anything (`messages.push` at the assistant, tool-result, and nudge sites).
- `read_file` with no line range returns the **entire** file (`tools.ts`), and that result stays in history verbatim for the rest of the run.
- `edit_file` payloads live in `toolCalls[].args` and are re-serialized into every later prompt, long after the edit is on disk.

The schematic stage is where this bites hardest, because it is the one stage whose working artifact is large and re-read repeatedly: a `.kicad_sch` is tens of kB, the model re-reads it between anchored edits, and every stale copy plus every already-applied edit payload is re-billed on every subsequent turn.

### Evidence

`PIPELINE-EFFICIENCY.md` (from the end-to-end `claude-code` debugging run) already identified this as the single highest-leverage fix, and it is the only recommendation from that document still unimplemented:

> **Stop re-sending the whole conversation every turn (biggest token win).** … Cost grows ~quadratically in turns — part-selection's 40k output tokens over 10 turns is mostly re-billed history.

The measured baselines in `pipeline-run-logs/`:

| stage | turns | out tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| part-selection | 10 | 40.5k |
| schematic | 8+ | 48k+ |

It also blocks the compat route in practice. From the manual test log in #123: **Groq returned `413` on turn one** — 10,078 tokens needed against a 6,000–8,000 TPM cap — before any history had accumulated at all. Small local Ollama models stall on context length for the same reason.

### This is a different axis from #145, and they interact badly

#145 measures **output** tokens and finds cost concentrated in a handful of giant turns; its fix is to quantize stages into many small verified steps.

This issue is about **input** tokens from re-sent history. The two are complementary, but note the interaction: **quantizing without capping makes this worse.** Splitting one large turn into ten small ones multiplies the number of times the full history is re-sent. #145's own data shows the shape already — one schematic run used **54 turns**, each re-sending everything accumulated before it. Landing #145 first, alone, would raise total input cost.

## Proposed behavior

Send the provider a capped *view* of the conversation, while the run's own history stays whole.

Trims ordered by how lossy each one is:

- **Supersede a stale file read.** When a `read_file` result is followed later in the same conversation by another read of the same path, replace the earlier one with a short stub naming the path. Not lossy — the current contents are already in front of the model — so it can apply at any distance. The newest read of a path is always sent in full.
- **Truncate settled oversized content.** Clip tool results and already-applied tool-call argument strings head-and-tail, with an in-band marker stating how much was removed and how to recover it. This *is* lossy, so it must never touch recent messages.

Two properties this has to hold to be safe in front of any provider:

1. **The transcript and ledger keep full fidelity.** Capping is request-time only. Shrinking the run's own record to save tokens would trade an auditable failure for a cheaper one.
2. **Message count, order, roles, and `toolCallId`s are preserved exactly** — only content strings shrink. `renderDelta(messages, sentCount)` slices by index for the `claude-code` session-resume path, and every provider pairs a tool result to its call by id; dropping or reordering messages silently desyncs both. The obvious implementation ("drop old messages") is unsafe for exactly this reason.

Behind a config flag (default on) so an exact-prompt reproduction is still possible.

## Alternatives considered

- **Turn on `claude-code` session resume instead.** It already exists but is gated behind `COPPERHEAD_CC_SESSION_RESUME=1` *and* is mutually exclusive with `llmCache`, which defaults on — so the second-biggest saving is off by default. Worth doing, but it is provider-specific: it does nothing for the OpenAI/compat path, which is exactly where the TPM ceilings bite.
- **Prompt caching on the compat path.** The Anthropic provider sets three `cache_control` breakpoints; the OpenAI/compat provider sets none. Also worth doing, and also narrower — caching reduces the *price* of re-sent history but not its size, so it does not help a hard context or TPM limit.
- **Drop old messages entirely.** Simplest, and unsafe — see the index/id invariant above.

## Effect on the invariants

- **Spec-gated in** — unaffected; the tool list is unchanged.
- **Verification-gated out** — unaffected; ERC/DRC gating is untouched.
- **`check` stays LLM-free and network-free** — unaffected.
- **Transcripts** — deliberately unaffected, per the property above.
- **One-time LLM-cache invalidation** is unavoidable: `CachingProvider` hashes the messages it is handed, and those messages become smaller. Unlike the earlier `baseURL` key-shape regression — where keeping keys byte-identical was the fix — here the request genuinely changed, so a new key is the *correct* outcome; replaying the old one would serve a response generated from a different prompt. Cost is one re-paid run plus orphaned files, since the cache has no eviction.

issues.title: Stage 4 deadlock: the BOM value cross-check freezes the only lever that can clear the legibility gate
issues.body:
## Summary

Stage 4 (`schematic`) can be **unsatisfiable**. Two gates that are each reasonable in isolation contradict each other, and the agent has no legal move that satisfies both:

- [`src/kicad/draft/ir.ts:210`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/3bc7d6d/src/kicad/draft/ir.ts#L210) pins the IR's part value to `docs/BOM.md` by **exact string equality**.
- [`src/commands/create.ts:311`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/3bc7d6d/src/commands/create.ts#L311) fails the stage while any error-severity legibility finding remains — and `edit_file` is refused on a drafted sheet, so the IR is the agent's only lever.

When stage 3 writes a *description* into BOM.md's Value column — which it does routinely — the engine renders that string as the symbol's Value field, it collides with neighbouring symbols, and the only fix (shortening it) is rejected by the BOM cross-check.

The run stalls at 4/8 and burns all three stage attempts. This is a design bug in the drafting contract, not a flaky run: any brief whose BOM carries descriptive values hits it.

## Reproduction

```
copperhead create --brief brief.md --model claude-code
```

Brief: an RF game joystick (61 parts, 53 nets, 8 subsystems). copperhead 0.9.0, branch `feat/deterministic-schematic-drafting` @ `0d23858` (+5 uncommitted files — the binary under test exists in no commit), node v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4.

Result: stages 1–3 committed, stage 4 exhausted 3/3 attempts, **exit 1**, 3h11m, 144 turns, 956.3k output tokens.

## The deadlock, concretely

`BT1`'s value in the stage-3 BOM is:

```
| BT1 | 1S Li-Po cell, 500 mAh, bare leads | Connector_JST:JST_PH_S2B-PH-K_1x02_P2.00mm_Horizontal | ...
```

34 characters rendered as the Value field next to a battery symbol overruns into Q4 → error-severity legibility finding → `create.ts:311` refuses the stage.

Putting `500mAh Li-Po` in the IR instead fails first, at `ir.ts:210`:

```js
else if (bomValue !== p.value) add(`${p.ref} value "${p.value}" differs from BOM.md's "${bomValue}"`)
```

Six parts are stuck this way: BT1, C3, Q2, Q3/R7, R14/U3, D1. Representative BOM values:

| Ref | BOM.md Value (= what gets drawn) |
| --- | --- |
| BT1 | `1S Li-Po cell, 500 mAh, bare leads` |
| Q2 | ``P-MOSFET, `BAT_SENSE_EN` divider gate`` |
| Q3 | `N-MOSFET, gate level-shifter for Q2` |
| R14 | `TS bias network, value set at capture` |

## Why this is the mechanism, not a guess

Three independent confirmations from the run:

1. **Controlled comparison inside the run.** The agent also shortened net names it had invented itself (`BAT_SENSE_GATE`, `BAT_SENSE_DIV`) — those aren't in BOM.md, so nothing blocked the edit, and *those exact findings cleared*. Same sheet, same collision class; the only difference was whether the string was BOM-pinned.
2. **Independent rediscovery.** Attempt 1 reached the same diagnosis unprompted, 2.5 hours before attempt 3: *"The remaining errors are text overlaps driven by my very long Value strings (e.g. \"NTC thermistor, 10 kΩ, B = 3380 K\" spilling onto RT1)."*
3. **The other levers provably don't move it.** Paper A2 → A1 → A0 changed framing only (placement is on a fixed internal grid); two different group assignments for the battery-sense chain changed nothing. Six draft iterations in attempt 3, 28 across the run.

## Suggested fix

**Separate the oracle from the rendering.** Cross-check the IR against a canonical value, but render an abbreviated Value on the sheet (first comma-delimited clause, or a length cap with the full text preserved in a Description field). This fixes it without changing the stage-3 contract or any existing BOM.md.

Alternatives considered:

- Relax `ir.ts:210` to compare a normalised form — narrower, but leaves the sheet rendering long strings.
- Have stage 3 emit `Value` and `Description` as separate BOM.md columns — structurally cleanest, and it's what the stage-4 agent proposed on its own, but it changes the stage-3 contract and every existing BOM.md.

Worth a regression test either way: a BOM.md with a prose Value must either draft legibly or fail with a message naming the real cause. **Today's failure message points at legibility findings and never mentions BOM.md** — it cost this run most of stage 4 to work that out, twice, independently.

## Related

- #159 — the deterministic drafting engine this exercises.
- #136 — the legibility gate whose error-severity findings are the blocking half of the deadlock.
- Found while working #66 (end-to-end `create` bounty run).

## Two other findings from the same run

Filed here for traceability; happy to split into separate issues if preferred.

**A. The engine can emit a netlist that merges distinct nets.** Attempt 1 refused on two *real* ERC defects:

```
Both ISET and NTC are attached to the same items; ISET will be used in the netlist
Both KB and KG are attached to the same items; KB will be used in the netlist
```

The first merges U3.4 (charge-current program) with U3.6 (TS thermistor input) on a BQ24040 — if built, charge current is no longer set by R3 and the 0–45 °C charge inhibit the brief requires does not work. Two `multiple_net_names` warnings were still present at the end of attempt 3. The IR declares these as distinct nets; the engine computes the coordinates, and labels for adjacent pins land close enough that KiCad resolves them to one net. **This is more dangerous than the deadlock** — the deadlock stalls loudly, this one silently produces a wrong board that a run clearing the deadlock would carry into layout and Gerbers. Suggest failing the draft when two distinct net labels resolve to the same coordinate, rather than leaving it to an ERC warning.

**B. Unresolved symbols become connector placeholders, silently.** Only `Connector`, `Connector_Generic`, `Device`, `Power_Protection`, `RF_Module` and `Switch` resolved on this machine. U2 (TPS7A0233), U3 (BQ24040), U4 (S-8261) and Q4 (FS8205A) were captured as `Conn_01x05`/`01x10`/`01x08` with real package pin numbers preserved; D2 became `Conn_01x06` because `Power_Protection:TPD4E05U06DQA` is a **derived symbol the engine rejects**. Netlist and footprints are correct, but those five symbols carry no pin names or electrical types, so ERC cannot type-check them — an ERC pass on this sheet is a partial signal. Suggest making placeholder substitution an error-severity finding requiring explicit acknowledgement, and supporting derived/extended symbols in `symsource.ts`.

## Evidence

Full attempt log, per-attempt transcripts, git status/stash/log snapshots and the run report are preserved. Attempt breakdown:

| Attempt | Run dir | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `18-24-36-752Z` | refused — 2 real ERC netlist defects (finding A) |
| 2 | `19-40-21-478Z` | failed — turn budget exhausted at 40 turns, 24 files unverified, work stashed |
| 3 | `20-35-14-518Z` | refused — 10 error-severity legibility findings after 6 draft iterations |

Two notes for anyone reading the logs:

- At one point the agent's prose reads *"Clean sheet: no legibility findings, score 91"* immediately below tool output reading `cap: 40 — 3 error-severity legibility finding(s)`. The agent's claim is wrong and the machine gate correctly refused to advance — but the two are concatenated onto one line in the log without a separating newline, so anything parsing these logs will mis-attribute it. **No clean sheet was produced at any point** on the full 61-part netlist.
- No workspace artifact was hand-edited to satisfy a gate. The agent self-reported adding an expansion table to `docs/BOM.md` during attempt 3; `restore()` reverted it, and `docs/BOM.md` is byte-identical to its committed form. Verified.

issues.title: Idea: mine kicad-tools for s-expression round-trip parsing and KiCad format edge cases
issues.body:
Hi — we build [kicad-tools](https://github.com/rjwalters/kicad-tools) (MIT), a Python toolkit for programmatic KiCad work: s-expression parsing/editing, autorouting, DRC/ERC/LVS, and fab export, driven by a `kct` CLI. We just filed an issue on our side to mine copperhead for workflow ideas (rjwalters/kicad-tools#4520), and it occurred to us the exchange could go both ways.

**Suggestion:** point one of your agents at the kicad-tools repo to harvest our s-expression and KiCad-file-format work. Since you're hand-rolling a TS parser and editing `.kicad_sch`/`.kicad_pcb` directly,  our accumulated edge cases might save you real time. Everything is MIT, so porting logic or test cases into an Apache-2.0 project is no problem.

Things likely worth mining:

- **Round-trip, format-preserving s-expression parser** (`src/kicad_tools/sexp/` — `parser.py`, `builders.py`). Preserving KiCad's exact formatting on rewrite matters a lot for clean git diffs, and there are non-obvious cases (quoting, float formatting, KiCad's own normalizations) baked into it and its test suite.
- **Higher-level editors** over the raw tree: `src/kicad_tools/pcb/` (board editor, footprints, zones, outline) and `src/kicad_tools/schematic/` (symbol generation, models, grid rules) — useful as a map of which fields agents actually need to touch and which are landmines.
- **Writer quirks we hit in production** that a fresh implementation will hit too — e.g. pad-angle serialization for rotated footprints silently corrupting gerbers (our #3902). Our issue tracker doubles as a catalog of KiCad-format gotchas.
- **A hard-won verification lesson:** an internal DRC alone is not sufficient — we now mandate a `kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones` cross-gate, because stale zone fills and sub-micron clearance marginals slip past otherwise. Since your `check` already shells out to `kicad-cli`, making `--refill-zones` unconditional is a cheap robustness win.
- **Machine-readable surface:** if it's ever useful to delegate rather than reimplement, `kct` exposes routing, DRC/LVS, and export as CLI commands an agent can shell out to, same as you do with `kicad-cli`.

No coordination needed on our end — this is just a pointer. Happy to answer questions about any of the modules above.

issues.title: Feature Request: Rule-based deterministic schematic drafting: compute placement and routing from the netlist instead of sampling it
issues.body:
### The problem

Every coordinate in a generated `.kicad_sch` is text the model authored token by token through `edit_file`. There is no placement logic anywhere: the scaffold hands the agent a blank A4 page (`emptySchematic()` in `src/kicad/bootstrap.ts`), and the only geometric guidance in the codebase is one prompt sentence about the 1.27mm grid. The result is what #136 documents: electrically clean sheets that read badly, with placement that drifts run to run because it is sampled, not computed.

The `readable-schematic-drafting` change (branch `feat/readable-schematic-drafting`) adds a deterministic legibility *checker* and gates stage 4 on it, but authorship stays with the model. That means legibility is achieved through a draft-check-repair loop: the model places, the checker objects, the model nudges, and each repair turn costs budget and risks new defects (an off-grid nudge silently breaks connectivity, which is why the checker orders grid findings first). The checker tells us when a sheet is bad; nothing makes a sheet good by construction.

**Token cost is a first-order motivation, not a side benefit.** The per-run data in #145 shows the schematic stage is where the spend concentrates: in the 65m46s schematic run, 5 of 40 turns emitted 89% of the run's 170,920 output tokens (largest turn 43,629; median 177), and every observed failure mode (`provider-error` mid-response, `turn-budget-exhausted`, a 10-minute stall) happened on an oversized turn. Those giant turns are geometry emission: `(symbol …)` instances, `(wire …)` runs, and coordinates are the overwhelming bulk of the s-expression text the model authors, and the legibility repair loop multiplies them, since every nudge re-emits the placement text it touches. A deterministic drafting engine moves that entire token class out of the LLM: the model emits compact netlist intent (roughly, a connection list plus group assignments), and the engine expands it to geometry for free. This attacks the same pathology #145 addresses by quantizing turns, but removes the tokens instead of slicing them smaller: the two are complementary.

### Proposed behavior

A rule-based, deterministic drafting engine for the schematic stage: given the netlist, BOM.md, and SUBSYSTEMS.md, compute symbol placement (and ideally wire routing) from rules rather than sampling it from the model.

Sketch of the rule set, deliberately aligned with the 13 check families in `docs/reference/schematic-legibility.md` so the output is legible by construction:

- Partition symbols into groups from SUBSYSTEMS.md/BOM.md, one captioned rectangle per group, matching D2's geometric-containment convention.
- Place groups on the sheet left to right along signal flow (sources left, loads right), sized from summed symbol body boxes plus clearance, meeting the utilization and no-overlap families.
- Place symbols inside their group on the 1.27mm grid with minimum body-box pitch, Reference/Value text slots computed to never collide.
- Route wires on-grid with a simple orthogonal router, falling back to net labels beyond the max-wire-length threshold; labels horizontal wherever horizontal fits.
- Fill the title block from the project config.

Determinism is the point: the same netlist always produces the same sheet, diffs between runs become meaningful, and the legibility gate becomes a regression check on the engine instead of a repair-loop objective for the model. The model still decides *what* to connect; the engine decides *where* it sits.

Expected pipeline shape: stage 4 splits into "model authors the netlist intent" and "engine drafts the geometry", with the existing checker and ERC gating the combined output. A `copperhead draft` (or a stage-internal step) that is deterministic and network-free, like `check`.

### Alternatives you considered

- The current plan of record, checker plus prompt conventions: lands first and stays valuable as the acceptance gate, but it optimizes via repair turns and cannot make output deterministic.
- Pre-drawing empty captioned group boxes from SUBSYSTEMS.md in the scaffold (the open question in the change's design.md): a useful intermediate step, "fill the boxes" instead of "organize the sheet", and probably the first milestone of this issue.
- Full-blown auto-layout from an external EDA tool: rejected, adds a heavyweight dependency and gives up control over the conventions the checker encodes.

### Effect on the invariants

This is the issue's real design question. The repo invariant is that the sexp parser never serializes and KiCad files change only through anchored exact-match replaces; design D1 of `readable-schematic-drafting` rejected an auto-placer for exactly that reason, but kept it "as a successor once the checker has pinned down what good means in machine-checkable terms". That successor is this issue. Options to resolve the tension, in rough order of preference:

1. The engine emits s-expression *text* through the same anchored-edit path the model uses (a template emitter, not a parser round-trip), keeping "parser never serializes" literally true.
2. A scoped exception: a dedicated geometry emitter module is allowed to serialize the elements it owns (symbols placement, wires, group rectangles), while the parser stays read-only.

Verification-gating is unaffected: engine output still has to pass ERC and the legibility checker like any other mutation. Spec-gating is unaffected: the engine runs inside the already-unlocked stage.

Depends on: #136 / the `readable-schematic-drafting` change landing first, since its checker defines the machine-checkable target the engine is built against. Related: #141 is the same idea for the PCB layout stage, this issue is its schematic-stage counterpart; #145 documents the token-concentration pathology this issue removes at the source.

issues.title: Feature Request: Quantize the schematic and layout stages — the cost is concentrated in a handful of giant turns, and every one of them is a single point of failure
issues.body:
## Summary

Across 14 runs in this repo, **112 minutes of wall time** produced a schematic and no board. The cost is not spread across the pipeline — it is concentrated in a few enormous turns inside two stages, `schematic` and `layout-draft`, and those turns are exactly the ones that die.

In the 65m46s schematic run, **5 of 40 turns emitted 89% of the run's 170,920 output tokens** (median turn: 177 tokens; largest: 43,629). Every observed failure mode in this repo — `provider-error` mid-response, `turn-budget-exhausted`, and a 10-minute single-turn stall — happened on an oversized turn.

Request: measure per-turn cost concentration, and restructure `schematic` and `layout-draft` so work advances in small verified quanta (one part, one subsystem, one net at a time), each checked and committed, instead of one large emission that must succeed whole or be lost whole.

## Problem

### 1. Where the time and tokens actually go

Every `run-end` event in `.copperhead/runs/`:

| Run | Stage | Wall | Turns | Out tokens | Largest turn | Exit |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `2026-07-29T18-02-20-554Z` | schematic | **65m46s** | 40 | **170,920** | **43,629** | `turn-budget-exhausted` |
| `2026-07-29T17-34-57-685Z` | architecture | 10m07s | 13 | 41,909 | 22,086 | done |
| `2026-07-29T17-45-04-449Z` | part-selection | 10m02s | **2** | 49,163 | **48,599** | done |
| `2026-07-29T17-55-29-356Z` | part-selection | 6m51s | 9 | 29,865 | 16,079 | done |
| `2026-07-29T17-20-13-820Z` | create | 6m21s | 2 | 28,663 | **28,517** | `provider-error` |
| `2026-07-29T17-29-57-342Z` | spec-seed | 5m00s | 14 | 21,316 | 5,104 | done |
| `2026-07-29T19-17-45-761Z` | schematic | 3m31s | 54 | 9,575 | 2,832 | done |
| `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z` | layout-draft | 2m03s | 3 | 135 | 53 | `provider-error` |
| `2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z` | schematic | 1m15s | 40 | 0 | 0 | `turn-budget-exhausted` |
| `2026-07-29T19-21-18-717Z` | layout-draft | 1m26s | 2 | 6,215 | 6,159 | `refused` |
| 4 × `layout-draft` | layout-draft | ~1s each | 2 | 0 | 0 | `refused` |

**Two stages account for the overwhelming majority of the spend**, and `layout-draft` has produced nothing at all (see #141).

### 2. The distribution inside a stage is pathological, not merely skewed

Per-turn output for the 65-minute schematic run:

```
63, 254, 43629, 17777, 28830, 32243, 2530, 898, 481, 1986, 29672, 1268, 909, 1388,
2324, 177, 293, 142, 128, 135, 177, 167, 201, 82, 82, 82, 89, 82, 82, 85, 81, 82,
89, 82, 86, 951, 2554, 23, 23, 693
```

- median turn: **177** tokens
- top 5 turns: 43,629 / 32,243 / 29,672 / 28,830 / 17,777 → **89% of the run**
- the run then spent its last ~20 turns emitting 23–90 tokens each and hit the 40-turn wall

This is a bimodal workload wearing one budget. The stage exhausted its **turn** budget while 89% of its **token** cost sat in 5 turns — meaning the resource being rationed is not the resource being consumed. A 43,629-token turn and an 82-token turn each cost exactly "1 turn."

### 3. The stage's own protocol is being ignored, and nothing enforces it

The stage-4 prompt is explicit:

> "Work ONE part at a time, not in large blocks: add a symbol (its lib_symbols entry if new, then its placement), run `run_erc`, fix any violation, then move to the next part — small incremental edits keep a geometry or grid slip local instead of forcing a full-block rewrite."

Actual tool calls in that run:

| Tool | Calls |
| --- | ---: |
| `edit_file` | **51** |
| `run_erc` | **6** |
| `verify_symbols` | 6 |
| everything else | 9 |

**8.5 edits per verification.** The largest single `edit_file` pushed **17,884 characters** into `board.kicad_sch` in one call; four separate edits exceeded 11,000 characters. The instruction to work incrementally is prose in a prompt with no mechanism behind it, so the model batches — and when a grid slip lands inside a 17.9 kB block, the repair is a full-block rewrite, which is another giant turn.

### 4. Giant turns are where runs die

- `2026-07-29T17-20-13-820Z` — turn 2 emitted 28,517 tokens, then `provider error: ... Server error mid-response`. Work lost to a stash.
- `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z` — `layout-draft` died with `Server error mid-response` on the turn where it was about to emit the whole board.
- `2026-07-29T17-45-04-449Z` — one 48,599-token turn took **10 minutes** of wall clock inside a 600s `turnTimeoutMs`; it cleared the timeout with 18 seconds to spare.
- `2026-07-29T18-02-20-554Z` — 66 minutes, 171k tokens, ended with nothing committed.

Long single responses have a higher chance of being interrupted, and an interrupted monolithic emission loses everything in it. Small turns fail small.

### 5. Retry replays the failure verbatim

After the 66-minute exhaustion, the retry (`2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z`) burned 40 turns and **0 output tokens** in 75 seconds — a full cache replay of the same losing trajectory, hitting the same wall. Caching a deterministic replay of a failed trajectory is cheap but useless; it re-derives the failure instead of decomposing the work. (Related: #135.)

## Proposed Behavior

### A. Measure it first

Cost concentration is currently invisible: `REPORT.md` reports one wall/turn/token figure per stage, so a stage with one 43k-token turn and a stage with 40 evenly-sized turns look identical.

Add to `report.json` / `REPORT.md`, per stage:

- `p50TurnOut`, `p95TurnOut`, `maxTurnOut`
- `top5TurnShare` — fraction of output in the 5 largest turns
- `editBytesPerVerify` — bytes written per `run_erc` / `run_drc` call
- `largestEditBytes`
- wall time of the slowest single turn

Concentration is the leading indicator. **In this repo `top5TurnShare` = 0.89 for the stage that failed, and the metric would have said so at turn 5, not at minute 66.**

(This depends on per-call metrics existing at all — see #140, which is the prerequisite: the numbers in this issue had to be reconstructed from `run-end` events after the fact.)

### B. Quantize the unit of work

**Make the quantum explicit and enforced, not suggested.**

1. **Declare a work unit per stage.** `schematic` → one part (lib_symbol + placement + its wires). `layout-draft` → one placement group, then one net class. `part-selection` → one BOM row group.

2. **Cap the emission per turn.** A soft limit on `edit_file` / `write_file` payload size (e.g. 4 kB), with the tool returning a redirect rather than accepting a 17.9 kB block: *"too large for one edit — split by part; you have added N of M parts."* This is a mechanism, where the prompt is currently only an instruction.

3. **Gate progression on verification.** After each unit, `run_erc` (or `run_drc`) must run before the next unit's edit is accepted. `editBytesPerVerify` becomes a bounded quantity instead of 8.5 edits per check.

4. **Commit per unit, not per stage.** A checkpoint commit (`copperhead: schematic part 12/32 — U1 placed, ERC clean`) after each verified quantum. A provider error then costs one part, not 66 minutes. This is the direct fix for the mid-response deaths: `2026-07-29T17-20-13-820Z` stashed its work; a checkpointed run would have kept 11 of 12 parts.

5. **Resume at unit granularity.** `isComplete` currently answers a yes/no question per stage (`src/commands/create.ts`: "does the board contain `(footprint`?"). Extend it to "which units are done?" so a resumed stage continues from part 12 instead of restarting or being skipped wholesale.

### C. Budget in the right unit

`maxTurns: 100` rations turns while the failure is token- and time-shaped. Add token and wall budgets per stage, and let the pipeline see when a stage is burning budget on a few huge turns:

```json
"budgets": {
  "schematic":    { "maxTokensOut": 120000, "maxWallMs": 2400000, "maxTurnOut": 8000 },
  "layout-draft": { "maxTokensOut":  80000, "maxWallMs": 1800000, "maxTurnOut": 8000 }
}
```

`budgets` already exists in `.copperhead/config.json` and is empty — this gives it a meaning that matches the observed failure mode. When `maxTurnOut` is exceeded, the right response is to *split the unit*, not to abort the stage.

### D. Split the stages themselves

`schematic` and `layout-draft` are each doing several separable jobs that currently share one budget and one all-or-nothing outcome:

- `schematic` → **symbols** (place all parts, `verify_symbols` clean) → **connectivity** (wire them, ERC clean) → **annotation** (PINOUT/BOM drift clean)
- `layout-draft` → **import** (netlist + footprints) → **placement** (DRC clean) → **route-power** (DRC clean) → **route-signal** (DRC clean) → **document**

Each sub-stage gets its own gate, budget, commit, and resume point. This composes with #141, whose deterministic placer/router makes several of these sub-stages non-LLM work entirely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `report.json` and `REPORT.md` carry per-stage `p50TurnOut`, `p95TurnOut`, `maxTurnOut`, `top5TurnShare`, `editBytesPerVerify`, `largestEditBytes`, and slowest-turn wall time.
- [ ] Replaying the existing 14 runs in `.copperhead/runs/` reproduces the concentration figures in this issue (schematic `top5TurnShare` = 0.89, `editBytesPerVerify` ≈ 12.5 kB).
- [ ] A per-turn / per-edit size cap exists and is enforced by the tool layer, not only stated in the prompt.
- [ ] `schematic` cannot make a second `edit_file` to the schematic without an intervening `run_erc`; `layout-draft` likewise with `run_drc`.
- [ ] Checkpoint commits land per verified unit; killing a run mid-stage leaves all previously verified units committed.
- [ ] Resume restarts at the first incomplete unit, not at the start of the stage.
- [ ] Per-stage token and wall budgets are configurable in `.copperhead/config.json` and enforced.
- [ ] Exceeding `maxTurnOut` triggers a split-the-unit retry, not a stage abort.
- [ ] `schematic` and `layout-draft` are decomposed into gated sub-stages with independent completion checks.
- [ ] A re-run of the `schematic` stage on this repo shows `top5TurnShare` < 0.4 and `maxTurnOut` < 8,000.
- [ ] A re-run completes `schematic` within its wall budget without hitting `turn-budget-exhausted`.
- [ ] The response cache does not replay a trajectory that previously ended in `turn-budget-exhausted` without changing the decomposition.

## Implementation Notes

- The per-turn data needed for the metrics already exists in the `run-end` `perTurn` array — it just isn't summarized. Everything in the tables above was computed from the committed transcripts, so the analysis needs no new instrumentation to *start*; #140 is what makes it survive a crash.
- The size cap belongs in the `edit_file` / `write_file` handlers in `src/agent/tools.ts`, where the KiCad-file refusal for `write_file` already lives — the precedent for a tool-level guardrail on file mutation is established.
- Checkpoint commits should be distinguishable from stage commits (`copperhead: create pipeline stage: <name>`) so history stays readable and a squash step is possible.
- Unit-level `isComplete` for `schematic` can count `(symbol` / wired pins against `list_symbols`; for `layout-draft`, count `(footprint` and routed nets against the netlist. Both are cheap parses with `src/kicad/sexp.ts`.
- Worth checking whether the 40-turn tail of 23–90-token turns is the model thrashing on a repair it cannot localize — if so, that is direct evidence for the "small edits keep a slip local" claim and a second argument for the cap.

## Additional Context

The wider pattern across all 14 runs: **112.4 minutes of wall time, 8 stages defined, 4 completed, 0 boards produced.** The two stages that touch KiCad files are where the pipeline both spends its budget and loses its work, and in both cases the mechanism is the same — a large unverified emission that must land perfectly or not at all.

Related:
- #141 — deterministic placement and routing; removes most of `layout-draft`'s LLM emission entirely, which is the same problem attacked from the geometry side.
- #140 — incremental per-call metrics; the prerequisite for measuring any of this while a run is still alive.
- #139 / #137 — `maxTurns` budget behavior; this issue argues the budget's *unit* is also wrong, not just its exhaustion handling.
- #135 — `create` retries a turn-budget-exhausted stage with the same budget; run `2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z` is that bug and this issue's cache-replay observation in one event.

issues.title: fix(agent): propose_change omits .openspec.yaml and openspecValidate lacks --type change for OpenSpec 1.7+
issues.body:
## What

1. In `src/agent/tools.ts`, `propose_change` handler writes `proposal.md` and `tasks.md`, but omits `.openspec.yaml`. Under `@fission-ai/openspec` v1.7.0+, calling `openspec validate` fails with:
   `✗ [ERROR] file: Change must have at least one delta or set skip_specs: true in .openspec.yaml`
2. In `src/openspec/cli.ts`, `openspecValidate(repo, changeId)` runs `openspec validate <changeId>` without `--type change`, which returns `Unknown item '<changeId>'`.

## Why

Because `validate_change` fails, Copperhead's safety invariant keeps `edit_file` / `write_file` structurally locked, causing AI agent runs to stall or refuse execution.

## Proposed Fix

1. Update `propose_change` in `src/agent/tools.ts` to write `.openspec.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   schema: spec-driven
   skip_specs: true
   ```
2. Update `openspecValidate` in `src/openspec/cli.ts`:
   ```ts
   export function openspecValidate(repo: string, changeId?: string): Promise<OpenSpecResult> {
     return openspec(repo, changeId ? ['validate', '--type', 'change', changeId] : ['validate', '--all']);
   }
   ```

issues.title: Feature Request: Deterministic placement and routing for the layout stage, plus a reference-board corpus to score layout quality against
issues.body:
## Summary

Stage 5 (`layout-draft`) asks the LLM to author a board layout by writing raw KiCad s-expressions — 32 footprint placements, 15 nets, trace geometry, a zone, and vias — from memory, with `run_drc` as the only check. That is the wrong division of labor: placement and routing are geometric constraint problems with deterministic solvers, and DRC-clean is not the same as *good*.

Request: move coordinate generation into deterministic tooling (real footprint geometry from the installed libraries, a constraint-driven placer, an actual router), keep the LLM on *intent* (what must be near what, what must be far, what carries current), and build a **layout quality scorer validated against real reference boards** so "is this layout good?" has an answer that is not the model's own opinion.

## Problem

### 1. The stage prompt asks the model to invent coordinates it has no basis for

The stage-5 prompt (copperhead `src/commands/create.ts:186`) reads:

> "Stage 5: first-draft layout. Rule-driven placement written as **real coordinates**: connectors on edges, decoupling at IC pins, ESD at connectors, keepouts honored. Route power and short critical nets; leave the rest as ratsnest. Every routed net must pass `run_drc`."

The tool surface available to the model (`src/agent/tools.ts`) is `read_file`, `search`, `edit_file`, `write_file`, `list_symbols`, `list_nets`, `run_erc`, `run_drc`, `verify_symbols`, `export_svg`, `export_outputs`, `check_drift`. There is **no tool that loads a footprint**, no tool that returns pad coordinates, no tool that reports a courtyard, and no tool that moves a part. So the model must hand-write pad-accurate geometry for `Capacitor_THT:CP_Radial_D6.3mm_P2.50mm`, `Package_TO_SOT_THT:TO-220-3_Vertical`, `Capacitor_SMD:C_0805_2012Metric` etc. from recall — while 155 footprint libraries sit installed at `/usr/share/kicad/footprints` and the `pcbnew` Python API (KiCad 10.0.4) is importable on this machine.

The proposal the model produced for this stage admits the consequence in its own decision list: it records **"placeholder footprint geometry"** as a design decision, and invents 4 placeholder net names because it cannot import a real netlist (`openspec/changes/layout-draft/proposal.md`).

### 2. The stage has not once completed

Four `layout-draft` runs exist and none produced a board:

| Run | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z` | `provider-error` after 6m11s — died mid-response on turn 3, right after `list_nets` |
| `2026-07-29T19-54-42-021Z` | `refused` — model concluded "the upstream schematic does not have a valid netlist, and the repo tooling is returning unreliable file contents" |
| `2026-07-30T03-09-03-447Z` | `refused` — identical refusal, replayed from cache |
| `2026-07-30T03-09-22-134Z` | reached `propose_change` / `validate_change`, then stopped; `tasks.md` still has the write/DRC/LAYOUT.md boxes unticked |

Note the refusal reasoning: `run_erc` returned **"ERC: clean"** in that very same run, and the model still claimed 14 unconnected items and broken nets. It hallucinated a blocker and quit. `board.kicad_pcb` is still the untouched 30×20 mm scaffold with zero footprints.

The single-shot, all-geometry-in-one-`write_file` shape of the task is what makes every failure total: there is no partial layout to resume from, unlike the schematic stage which the prompt explicitly instructs to advance "ONE part at a time."

### 3. `run_drc` cannot tell a good layout from a bad one

`run_drc` (`src/agent/tools.ts:349`) shells out to `kicad-cli pcb drc` and reports violations. That is a legality check, and a weak signal in both directions:

- The current empty scaffold passes DRC trivially — zero footprints, zero nets, zero violations. **A board with nothing on it scores identically to a finished one.**
- A DRC-clean board can still have the LDR staring into the lamp connector, a 2 A return path through a zone stitch instead of copper, C2 20 mm from the pin it decouples, and a MOSFET with no thermal copper. Every one of those is a real defect the `.copperhead/constraints.json` entries already name — `sense.optical_feedback_keepout`, `mech.load_trace_width_mm` (≥1.5 mm), `thermal.junction_rise_C` (≤35 °C "with copper-pour heatsinking only") — and none of them is a DRC rule.

So the pipeline's own acceptance criterion for layout is "the model says it's fine," which is exactly what the stage prompt's "unlabeled non-optimal is not acceptable" clause is trying and failing to compensate for.

## Proposed Behavior

### A. Deterministic geometry: the model states intent, tooling produces coordinates

**1. Import a real netlist and real footprints instead of transcribing them.**
Add a `sync_pcb_from_sch` tool that runs the KiCad netlist import (`pcbnew` Python API, or `kicad-cli sch export netlist` + a small importer) so the board gets its 11 real nets and 32 real footprints — correct pads, courtyards, 3D refs — before any placement happens. This deletes the "placeholder footprint geometry" and "placeholder net names" decisions outright.

**2. Placement as a declarative constraint spec, solved deterministically.**
The model writes a placement *intent* file, not coordinates:

```yaml
# openspec/changes/<id>/placement.yaml
board: { outline: [60, 40], origin: [100, 100] }
place:
  - { ref: J1,   edge: left,   role: supply }
  - { ref: J2,   edge: right,  role: load }
  - { ref: J3,   edge: bottom-left }
  - { ref: C2,   near: U1.8,   max_mm: 2.5 }
  - { ref: C1,   near: Q1.3,   max_mm: 6 }
  - { ref: D1,   near: J1,     max_mm: 8, role: esd }
  - { ref: LDR1, far_from: J2, min_mm: 40, reason: sense.optical_feedback_keepout }
  - { chain: [J1, F1, Q1, C1, D1, J2], order: left-to-right }
keepout:
  - { around: [H1, H2], radius_mm: 3 }
```

A solver turns that into legal coordinates: seed from the constraints, then minimize ratsnest length under hard constraints (courtyard non-overlap, board outline, keepouts, edge assignments) — force-directed relaxation or simulated annealing is more than enough at 32 parts. It cannot emit an overlapping or off-board placement, because those are hard constraints rather than things to remember.

**3. Routing by an actual router.**
`freerouting` runs on this machine (`java` present) via the Specctra round-trip `kicad-cli pcb export specctra` → route → import SES. Power nets get their width from `mech.load_trace_width_mm` as a net class, not as a number the model retypes. If the freerouting dependency is unwanted, a deterministic A*/grid router over the 2-layer board covers the "power and short critical nets" the stage prompt actually asks for.

**4. Incremental, resumable, DRC-gated.**
Placement and routing land in stages (place → DRC → route power → DRC → route signal → DRC), each committed, so a provider error at minute six loses one step instead of the stage. This mirrors the "ONE part at a time" rule that already makes stage 4 reliable.

The LLM keeps the work it is genuinely good at: reading SPEC/SUBSYSTEMS/constraints and deciding *that* the LDR must be far from the lamp, *that* C2 belongs at pin 8, *that* the fuse comes first — and writing the `## Draft quality` prose afterward.

### B. Layout quality scoring: make "good" measurable

Add a `layout_metrics` tool that computes, from the `.kicad_pcb` alone, a scorecard:

**Hard (constraint-traceable, pass/fail — derived from `.copperhead/constraints.json`)**
- min trace width on each current-carrying net vs `mech.load_trace_width_mm`
- board extents vs `mech.board_outline_mm`
- centroid distance LDR1↔J2 vs `sense.optical_feedback_keepout`
- copper-free radius around mounting holes
- decoupling pad-to-pin distance for every bypass cap
- copper area attached to the MOSFET drain/source pad, as the input to the `thermal.junction_rise_C` check

**Soft (comparative, scored)**
- unrouted ratsnest count and total unrouted length
- total trace length, and length per critical net (GATE, CMP_OUT, SENSE)
- via count; vias on high-current nets
- ground return loop area for the load path
- courtyard overlap count (should be 0), placement density, board area utilization
- number of DRC violations by severity

Then wire it in: the `## Draft quality` section of `docs/LAYOUT.md` should be **generated from this scorecard** and only annotated by the model — that turns "unlabeled non-optimal is not acceptable" from an honor-system instruction into a computed artifact.

### C. Validate the scorer against reference boards

A metric nobody has calibrated is just another opinion. Score real boards and check the numbers come out where they should.

**A corpus is already on this machine** — `/usr/share/kicad/demos` ships 17 complete KiCad projects, professionally laid out:

| Project | Footprints | Track segments |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `vme-wren` | 1508 | 24858 |
| `jetson-agx-thor-baseboard` | 1125 | 19835 |
| `tiny_tapeout` | 309 | 2143 |
| `openair-max` | 210 | 1638 |
| `video` | 189 | 7932 |
| `kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213` | 160 | 2935 |
| `cm5_minima` | 112 | 1884 |
| `stickhub` | 94 | 1113 |
| `pic_programmer` | 63 | 370 |
| `ecc83-pp` | 15 | 59 |

**And it ships a free labeled pair.** `multichannel/` contains both `multichannel_mixer.kicad_pcb` (114 footprints, 576 segments, routed) and `multichannel_mixer-unrouted.kicad_pcb` (114 footprints, 140 segments, same design, unrouted). Same netlist, same parts, known-better vs known-worse. **The scorer must rank the routed one higher.** If it doesn't, the scorer is wrong — and that test costs nothing to run.

Beyond the local corpus, worth pulling in (analog/discrete boards in this project's size class, not just dense digital):
- KiCad's own project templates (`/usr/share/kicad/template`)
- Open-hardware KiCad repos with 2-layer through-hole-and-passives boards — Olimex, the KiCad "made with KiCad" list, Bus Pirate, ULX3S, MNT Reform
- The freerouting project's own test boards, for router-quality comparison specifically

**Validation protocol (mutation testing).** Take a good reference board, apply degradations, and require the score to fall monotonically:
- move every decoupling cap 15 mm from its IC → decoupling metric collapses
- narrow the power net to 0.25 mm → hard constraint fails
- shuffle placements at random within the outline (keeping DRC legal) → total trace length and ratsnest metrics blow up
- delete the ground zone → return-loop-area metric spikes

A scorer that doesn't separate the mutants from the original is not measuring layout quality. This is also the regression suite: run it in CI, and a change to the placer that quietly makes layouts worse shows up as a corpus score drop rather than as a DRC-clean board nobody looks at.

**Benchmark our own output.** Score every `layout-draft` result against the corpus percentile and record it in `REPORT.md` alongside cost. "DRC clean, 40th percentile trace efficiency, all 6 hard constraints met" is a stage outcome you can act on. "The model says non-optimal but acceptable" is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A netlist/footprint import tool exists; the board's nets and footprints come from `board.kicad_sch` and the installed KiCad libraries, never from model-authored s-expressions.
- [ ] No placeholder footprint geometry or placeholder net names appear in any committed board.
- [ ] Placement is produced by a solver from a declarative intent spec; the solver cannot emit overlapping courtyards, off-board parts, or keepout violations.
- [ ] Power nets get their width from `mech.load_trace_width_mm` via a net class, not from a literal in a model-written trace.
- [ ] Routing is performed by a router (freerouting round-trip or an internal deterministic router), not by hand-written `(segment ...)` forms.
- [ ] The stage checkpoints and commits after each of place / route-power / route-signal, so a provider error costs one step, not the stage.
- [ ] `layout_metrics` returns the hard-constraint table and the soft-metric scorecard for any `.kicad_pcb`.
- [ ] Every hard metric traces to a key in `.copperhead/constraints.json`.
- [ ] The `## Draft quality` section of `docs/LAYOUT.md` is generated from `layout_metrics` output.
- [ ] The scorer ranks `multichannel_mixer.kicad_pcb` above `multichannel_mixer-unrouted.kicad_pcb`.
- [ ] All 17 `/usr/share/kicad/demos` boards score without crashing, and their scores are recorded as the baseline distribution.
- [ ] Each of the four mutation tests lowers the score of a reference board.
- [ ] The mutation suite runs in CI; a scorer or placer regression fails the build.
- [ ] `layout-draft` completes on this repo: 32 footprints placed, power path routed at ≥1.5 mm, DRC clean, LDR1 ≥40 mm from J2, all hard constraints green.

## Implementation Notes

- Everything needed is already installed here: `kicad-cli` 10.0.4, `pcbnew` 10.0.4 Python bindings, `java` (for freerouting), and 155 footprint libraries under `/usr/share/kicad/footprints`. No new heavy dependency is implied — `src/kicad/` already has `sexp.ts`, `cli.ts`, `fab.ts`, so the parsing and CLI plumbing exist.
- `KICAD_STAGES` in `src/commands/create.ts:263` already gates `layout-draft` on KiCad availability, so the tooling assumption is established.
- Metrics should be computed from the board file, not from the agent's account of it — the refusal in run `2026-07-29T19-54-42-021Z` is a live example of the model reporting board/schematic state that contradicted the tool output in the same turn.
- Keep the scorecard as `report.json`-adjacent structured data, not only prose, so the corpus baseline and per-run scores are diffable.
- The placer is small: 32 parts, 2 layers. Ratsnest-length minimization under hard constraints converges in well under a second; this does not need to be clever to beat hand-written coordinates.
- Worth deciding early: does the placement intent spec live in `openspec/changes/<id>/` (reviewable as part of the change) or in `.copperhead/`? The former makes placement decisions reviewable the same way constraints already are.

## Additional Context

Motivated by the four failed `layout-draft` runs above, and by the observation that stage 4 (schematic) succeeds precisely where stage 5 fails: stage 4 has structured tools (`list_symbols`, `verify_symbols`, `run_erc`) and an explicit incremental protocol, so an error is caught within one part. Stage 5 has one binary check at the end of a single large write.

Related:
- `ISSUE-incremental-llm-call-metrics.md` — the same `layout-draft` provider error that motivated that issue is what makes the single-shot layout write so expensive to lose.
- `ISSUE-implement-maxTurns-prompt.md` — a deterministic placer removes most of the turn budget layout currently consumes.

issues.title: Feature Request: Flush per-LLM-call logs and metrics incrementally, and commit them with every stage commit
issues.body:
## Summary

Copperhead currently emits run metrics **only when a run terminates cleanly**, and regenerates `.copperhead/runs/REPORT.md` / `report.json` **only at the end of a run**. When a run stalls, times out, or dies mid-response, the per-call cost and timing data for the work that *did* happen is either lost or left uncommitted.

Request: record logs and metrics for **each LLM call as it completes**, and include those artifacts in the stage commit Copperhead already makes (`copperhead: create pipeline stage: <name>`), so the data survives a stalled or killed run.

## Problem

Concretely, in this repo:

1. **Per-turn metrics only exist in the terminal `run-end` event.**
   In `transcript.jsonl:9`, the entire cost record for the run arrives in one final event:

   ```json
   {"type":"run-end","data":{"exitPath":"provider-error","turnsUsed":3,"tokensIn":6,"tokensOut":135,
     "perTurn":[{"turn":1,"in":2,"out":53},{"turn":2,"in":2,"out":44},{"turn":3,"in":2,"out":38}],
     "durationMs":122872}}
   ```

   The `assistant` events written during the run (`transcript.jsonl:2`) carry only `text` and `toolCalls` — no tokens, no latency, no cache-hit flag, no model id. If the process is killed or hangs before `run-end`, nothing about per-call cost is recoverable from disk.

2. **`REPORT.md` / `report.json` are end-of-run only.**
   `REPORT.md` says so in its own header: "regenerated at the end of every run." A run that stalls leaves the report describing the *previous* run, silently stale.

3. **The failed run's data was never committed.**
   Run `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z` (layout-draft) failed with `provider error: Claude Code returned an error result: API Error: Server error mid-response`. Its run directory, plus `REPORT.md` and `report.json`, are still untracked in git — while earlier successful runs' directories *are* tracked. So exactly the runs whose data is most worth keeping are the ones that never make it into a commit.

4. **Cache metrics have no per-call provenance.**
   `report.json` reports `cacheHits: 2` / `cacheHitPct: 40` for the stage, but the transcript has no event saying *which* call hit `.copperhead/llm-cache`. Cache behavior can't be debugged after the fact.

Net effect: a 6m11s stage that burned real tokens can leave behind no attributable cost record, and `maxTurns` / `budgets` accounting can't be reconstructed from a partial run.

## Proposed Behavior

### 1. Emit an `llm-call` transcript event per call, at call completion

Append to `transcript.jsonl` immediately after each provider response resolves (and flush/fsync, so a `SIGKILL` a moment later still leaves the line on disk):

```json
{"ts":"2026-07-29T19:46:01.102Z","type":"llm-call","data":{
  "turn": 2,
  "stage": "layout-draft",
  "callId": "cc-2",
  "model": "claude-code",
  "provider": "claude-code",
  "tokensIn": 2,
  "tokensOut": 44,
  "cacheRead": 0,
  "cacheWrite": 0,
  "cacheHit": true,
  "latencyMs": 6127,
  "startedAt": "2026-07-29T19:45:54.975Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-07-29T19:46:01.102Z",
  "stopReason": "tool_use",
  "toolCalls": ["list_symbols"],
  "error": null
}}
```

Failed and retried calls get an event too, with `error` populated — a call that costs input tokens and then errors is still a cost.

### 2. Maintain a live `metrics.json` per run

Write `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json` after every call, containing the running totals currently computed only at `run-end` (`turnsUsed`, `tokensIn/Out`, `perTurn`, cache counters, `durationMs` so far, current stage). Atomic write (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-write can't corrupt it.

### 3. Regenerate the report incrementally, not just at run end

`REPORT.md` / `report.json` should be regenerated at least **at each stage boundary**, marking any in-flight stage as `running` (or `stalled` if the last heartbeat exceeds `heartbeatMs`) rather than omitting it. `run-end` remains the final regeneration, not the only one.

### 4. Include the artifacts in the stage commit

When Copperhead makes its `copperhead: create pipeline stage: <name>` commit, stage and include:

- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/transcript.jsonl`
- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json`
- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/summary.md` (partial is fine — mark `Outcome: in-progress`)
- `.copperhead/runs/REPORT.md` and `report.json`

### 5. Preserve data on abnormal exit

On `turn-timeout`, `provider-error`, `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`, and heartbeat-detected stalls, flush metrics and make a `copperhead: partial run data <runId>` commit (or at minimum leave the files written and print the path), rather than exiting with the run directory untracked. The transcript already has `work-preserved` and `run-failed` event types — this extends the same idea to metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every LLM call appends an `llm-call` event to `transcript.jsonl` before the next call starts, with tokens, latency, model, cache status, and error (if any).
- [ ] `SIGKILL`-ing a run mid-stage leaves per-call metrics for all completed calls on disk.
- [ ] `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json` exists and is current while the run is still in progress.
- [ ] `REPORT.md` / `report.json` are regenerated at each stage boundary and show in-flight stages as `running` / `stalled`.
- [ ] Each stage commit contains that stage's transcript, metrics, summary, and the regenerated report.
- [ ] A run ending in `provider-error` or `turn-timeout` still leaves its data committed (or clearly reported as uncommitted with the path).
- [ ] Totals reconstructed by summing `llm-call` events equal the totals reported in `run-end` for a clean run.
- [ ] Per-call `cacheHit` values sum to the `cacheHits` reported in `report.json`.

## Implementation Notes

- The token data already exists at `run-end` as `perTurn` — this is largely a matter of emitting it at the point of measurement instead of buffering it to the end of the run.
- Writes must be append-and-flush; buffered stdio is the reason a killed process currently loses the tail.
- `metrics.json` should be written atomically (temp + rename) since it is rewritten on every call.
- Adding an event type to `transcript.jsonl` is backward compatible — readers already tolerate mixed types (`run-start`, `assistant`, `tool`, `run-end`, `work-preserved`, …).
- `heartbeatMs` (30000) and `turnTimeoutMs` (600000) in `.copperhead/config.json` give a ready signal for marking a stage `stalled`.
- Consider a config flag (e.g. `metrics.flushPerCall`, default `true`) and/or `commitRunArtifacts` for users who don't want run data in git history.

## Additional Context

Motivated by run `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z`: the `layout-draft` stage ran 6m11s across 5 turns, hit a provider error mid-response, and left its transcript, `REPORT.md`, and `report.json` untracked — with per-call cost visible only because the run happened to reach `run-end`. A hard stall would have left nothing.

Related: #139 — budget-exhaustion behavior depends on the same accounting being trustworthy mid-run.

issues.title: Feature Request: Prompt to extend `maxTurns` or adjust budget when near exhaustion
issues.body:
## Summary

Currently, `copperhead create` exits when it reaches the configured `maxTurns` limit or other run budgets, without offering an in-run prompt to extend the budget or continue with a higher limit.

This feature request is to add a user-facing prompt when Copperhead detects that the current run is about to exhaust `maxTurns` or a similar hard budget, so the user can decide to continue with more turns, increase the budget, or abort gracefully.

## Problem

In non-interactive or terminal-driven runs, Copperhead can reach a configured limit and stop without asking the user to increase `maxTurns` or explicitly continue. This leads to confusion because the run may appear hung or prematurely terminated, and the user does not get a chance to extend the limit before the run exits.

## Proposed Behavior

When a run is approaching `maxTurns` or other hard limits, Copperhead should:

1. Detect that the run is within a configurable threshold of the limit (for example, within 5 turns or 10% of `maxTurns`).
2. If the current session is interactive and a terminal is attached:
   - Prompt the user with a clear choice:
     - Continue with additional turns
     - Increase `maxTurns`
     - Abort the run
3. If the session is non-interactive or the prompt cannot be displayed:
   - Log a clear warning and fail with a distinct exit reason such as `turn-limit-exhausted` or `budget-exhausted`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Copperhead logs a warning when the run reaches the prompting threshold.
- [ ] In interactive mode, Copperhead displays a prompt before exiting due to `maxTurns`.
- [ ] The prompt offers at least these options:
  - `extend` / `continue` with a new `maxTurns`
  - `keep` current limit and abort
  - `cancel` or `quit`
- [ ] If the user chooses to extend, Copperhead resumes the run with the new limit.
- [ ] If the session is non-interactive, Copperhead does not hang; it exits with a clear status and message.
- [ ] The prompt feature is disabled or bypassed for truly autonomous/non-interactive execution modes.

## Implementation Notes

- The prompt should be integrated with the existing CLI runtime, not the agent model itself.
- It may require inspecting the run loop where `turnsUsed` is compared to `maxTurns`.
- The feature should respect `--maxTurns` and any equivalent configuration in `.copperhead/config.json`.
- A fallback environment variable like `COPPERHEAD_PROMPT_ON_BUDGET` could be added for automation control.

## Additional Context

This issue was motivated by a user session where Copperhead reached the turn budget without an interactive prompt, causing uncertainty whether the run was hung or had failed due to budget exhaustion.

If implemented, this would improve the developer experience for CLI-driven Copperhead runs and make budget exhaustion behavior more transparent.
