```json
  "cacheRead": 0,
  "cacheWrite": 0,
  "cacheHit": true,
  "latencyMs": 6127,
  "startedAt": "2026-07-29T19:45:54.975Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-07-29T19:46:01.102Z",
  "stopReason": "tool_use",
  "toolCalls": ["list_symbols"],
  "error": null
}}
```

Failed and retried calls get an event too, with `error` populated — a call that costs input tokens and then errors is still a cost.

### 2. Maintain a live `metrics.json` per run

Write `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json` after every call, containing the running totals currently computed only at `run-end` (`turnsUsed`, `tokensIn/Out`, `perTurn`, cache counters, `durationMs` so far, current stage). Atomic write (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-write can't corrupt it.

### 3. Regenerate the report incrementally, not just at run end

`REPORT.md` / `report.json` should be regenerated at least **at each stage boundary**, marking any in-flight stage as `running` (or `stalled` if the last heartbeat exceeds `heartbeatMs`) rather than omitting it. `run-end` remains the final regeneration, not the only one.

### 4. Include the artifacts in the stage commit

When Copperhead makes its `copperhead: create pipeline stage: <name>` commit, stage and include:

- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/transcript.jsonl`
- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json`
- `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/summary.md` (partial is fine — mark `Outcome: in-progress`)
- `.copperhead/runs/REPORT.md` and `report.json`

### 5. Preserve data on abnormal exit

On `turn-timeout`, `provider-error`, `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`, and heartbeat-detected stalls, flush metrics and make a `copperhead: partial run data <runId>` commit (or at minimum leave the files written and print the path), rather than exiting with the run directory untracked. The transcript already has `work-preserved` and `run-failed` event types — this extends the same idea to metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every LLM call appends an `llm-call` event to `transcript.jsonl` before the next call starts, with tokens, latency, model, cache status, and error (if any).
- [ ] `SIGKILL`-ing a run mid-stage leaves per-call metrics for all completed calls on disk.
- [ ] `.copperhead/runs/<runId>/metrics.json` exists and is current while the run is still in progress.
- [ ] `REPORT.md` / `report.json` are regenerated at each stage boundary and show in-flight stages as `running` / `stalled`.
- [ ] Each stage commit contains that stage's transcript, metrics, summary, and the regenerated report.
- [ ] A run ending in `provider-error` or `turn-timeout` still leaves its data committed (or clearly reported as uncommitted with the path).
- [ ] Totals reconstructed by summing `llm-call` events equal the totals reported in `run-end` for a clean run.
- [ ] Per-call `cacheHit` values sum to the `cacheHits` reported in `report.json`.

## Implementation Notes

- The token data already exists at `run-end` as `perTurn` — this is largely a matter of emitting it at the point of measurement instead of buffering it to the end of the run.
- Writes must be append-and-flush; buffered stdio is the reason a killed process currently loses the tail.
- `metrics.json` should be written atomically (temp + rename) since it is rewritten on every call.
- Adding an event type to `transcript.jsonl` is backward compatible — readers already tolerate mixed types (`run-start`, `assistant`, `tool`, `run-end`, `work-preserved`, …).
- `heartbeatMs` (30000) and `turnTimeoutMs` (600000) in `.copperhead/config.json` give a ready signal for marking a stage `stalled`.
- Consider a config flag (e.g. `metrics.flushPerCall`, default `true`) and/or `commitRunArtifacts` for users who don't want run data in git history.

## Additional Context

Motivated by run `2026-07-29T19-45-49-196Z`: the `layout-draft` stage ran 6m11s across 5 turns, hit a provider error mid-response, and left its transcript, `REPORT.md`, and `report.json` untracked — with per-call cost visible only because the run happened to reach `run-end`. A hard stall would have left nothing.

Related: `ISSUE-implement-maxTurns-prompt.md` — budget-exhaustion behavior depends on the same accounting being trustworthy mid-run.


---

Filed from the demo repo `chouhan-industries/copperhead-demo1`; file references above are paths within that repo.

issues.title: Prompt to extend maxTurns or adjust budget when near exhaustion
issues.body:
# Feature Request: Prompt to extend `maxTurns` or adjust budget when near exhaustion

## Summary

Currently, `copperhead create` exits when it reaches the configured `maxTurns` limit or other run budgets, without offering an in-run prompt to extend the budget or continue with a higher limit.

This feature request is to add a user-facing prompt when Copperhead detects that the current run is about to exhaust `maxTurns` or a similar hard budget, so the user can decide to continue with more turns, increase the budget, or abort gracefully.

## Problem

In non-interactive or terminal-driven runs, Copperhead can reach a configured limit and stop without asking the user to increase `maxTurns` or explicitly continue. This leads to confusion because the run may appear hung or prematurely terminated, and the user does not get a chance to extend the limit before the run exits.

## Proposed Behavior

When a run is approaching `maxTurns` or other hard limits, Copperhead should:

1. Detect that the run is within a configurable threshold of the limit (for example, within 5 turns or 10% of `maxTurns`).
2. If the current session is interactive and a terminal is attached:
   - Prompt the user with a clear choice:
     - Continue with additional turns
     - Increase `maxTurns`
     - Abort the run
3. If the session is non-interactive or the prompt cannot be displayed:
   - Log a clear warning and fail with a distinct exit reason such as `turn-limit-exhausted` or `budget-exhausted`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Copperhead logs a warning when the run reaches the prompting threshold.
- [ ] In interactive mode, Copperhead displays a prompt before exiting due to `maxTurns`.
- [ ] The prompt offers at least these options:
  - `extend` / `continue` with a new `maxTurns`
  - `keep` current limit and abort
  - `cancel` or `quit`
- [ ] If the user chooses to extend, Copperhead resumes the run with the new limit.
- [ ] If the session is non-interactive, Copperhead does not hang; it exits with a clear status and message.
- [ ] The prompt feature is disabled or bypassed for truly autonomous/non-interactive execution modes.

## Implementation Notes

- The prompt should be integrated with the existing CLI runtime, not the agent model itself.
- It may require inspecting the run loop where `turnsUsed` is compared to `maxTurns`.
- The feature should respect `--maxTurns` and any equivalent configuration in `.copperhead/config.json`.
- A fallback environment variable like `COPPERHEAD_PROMPT_ON_BUDGET` could be added for automation control.

## Additional Context

This issue was motivated by a user session where Copperhead reached the turn budget without an interactive prompt, causing uncertainty whether the run was hung or had failed due to budget exhaustion.

If implemented, this would improve the developer experience for CLI-driven Copperhead runs and make budget exhaustion behavior more transparent.

issues.title: Stage 4 gates the net graph but never the drawing: create emits electrically clean, unreadable schematics
issues.body:
### The problem

Stage 4's completion contract (`src/commands/create.ts:155-178`) requires symbols present, BOM/PINOUT drift-clean, and ERC-clean. Every one of those is a statement about the net graph. Nothing in the pipeline says anything about the drawing, so the schematic's readability is unconstrained output, and it shows.

What the stage 4 prompt (`src/commands/create.ts:180`) says about geometry, in full:

> (2) Place every symbol origin and every wire endpoint on the 1.27mm (50mil) grid; an off-grid pin silently fails to connect and costs turns to diagnose.

That is the entire drafting guidance, and its stated reason is connectivity, not legibility. There is no rule about placement, spacing, grouping, flow, page usage, or the title block, and no tool that could check one.

A recent `create` run produced an electrically clean A4 sheet with all of the following:

- Refdes and value text drawn on top of symbol bodies and wires. One roughly 10mm box contained `TP3`, `CMP_OUT`, `R8`, and `100` stacked on each other.
- Net labels rotated 90 degrees (`SENSE`, `+12V`, `GND`, `CMP_OUT`) in places where a horizontal label had room, because label orientation was inherited from the pin and never corrected.
- All content packed into roughly 40% of the sheet: the right 40% and bottom 35% were empty while parts sat at minimum pitch.
- No signal flow discipline. The sense chain, comparator, and gate driver ran diagonally across the sheet, and the spare comparator half sat between two unrelated blocks rather than in a spares corner.
- Power and ground flags at inconsistent heights, so there was no visual rail.
- An empty title block.

This matters more than cosmetics. The schematic is the primary human review surface for everything the agent claims to have designed, and SPEC.md §3 states the create pipeline's end product is "reviewable as a whole". A sheet an engineer will not read is a design they cannot check, which makes the review guarantee formally satisfied and practically void.

Relationship to #133: that issue covers the same stage gates from the electrical side (which stages have deterministic backing, and `verify_symbols` being advisory). It does not cover the drawing. The two do overlap in mechanism: #133's B.1 proposes a `symbol-verification` obligation kind, and the gate proposed here needs a legibility obligation in the same ledger (`src/agent/ledger.ts:6-13`). Those should be designed together so the ledger does not grow two inconsistently shaped verification obligations.

### Proposed behavior

Mirror the `symlib.ts` precedent exactly. `verify_symbols` exists because ERC checks the graph but not the parts, so a fabricated pin set passed every gate while being wrong. The same argument applies one level up: ERC checks the graph but not the drawing.

**A. A drafting standard, stated in the stage 4 prompt.**

Derived from how competent human-authored KiCad sheets are organized:

- One drawn group box per subsystem from SUBSYSTEMS.md: a schematic `(rectangle ...)` with a `(text ...)` caption naming it. Solid stroke for functional blocks, dashed for annotation clusters (decoupling bank, boot/reset, test points).
- Groups tiled without overlap. A large MCU or connector gets its own full-height column.
- Left-to-right signal flow inside a group, power rails toward the top, grounds toward the bottom.
- Symbol pitch that leaves room for both neighbours' refdes and value text.
- Net labels for connections between groups. Long wires crossing the sheet are what labels exist to avoid.
- Spare gates and unused sections in their own annotation group.
- Paper size chosen so the groups fill the frame.
- A populated title block.

**B. A deterministic checker that verifies it.**

New read-only `src/kicad/legibility.ts` over the existing `src/kicad/sexp.ts` parser. It never serializes (SPEC §1.3, phase-1 design D4), makes no network call, and invokes no model. Symbol body boxes come from the instance's `lib_symbols` graphics transformed by `at`/rotation/mirror, excluding pin name and number text. Text extents are approximated from font height with a per-character advance ratio tuned below the true average, so the checker misses marginal collisions rather than inventing them.

Thirteen check families, each with a stable kind and a default severity:

| Gating (error) | Advisory |
| --- | --- |
| `symbol-overlap`, `text-collision`, `off-grid`, `out-of-frame`, `ungrouped-symbol`, `unlabeled-group`, `group-overlap`, `wire-through-symbol`, `empty-title-block` | `low-utilization`, `crowding`, `label-orientation`, `cross-group-wire` |

The split is deliberate: the gating set is exactly the defects with an unambiguous answer and a single move that resolves them. The advisory families each rest on a threshold, and gating on a threshold invites the repair loop to thrash against a number instead of fixing a defect. Thresholds and per-family severity (including `off`) come from an optional `legibility` block in `.copperhead/config.json`.

**C. Wiring.**

1. New `check_legibility` agent tool, shaped like `verify_symbols` (`src/agent/tools.ts:327`): numbered findings carrying kind, severity, sheet, coordinates, refdes, and the concrete fix.
2. Error-severity findings open a ledger obligation, so `finish` refuses while the sheet is illegible. This is the piece that needs to agree with #133 B.1.
3. Stage 4's completion contract gains zero error-severity findings, alongside the existing symbols/drift/ERC conditions.
4. `check` runs the checker and prints findings grouped by severity, with the exit code unaffected at every severity, plus a `legibility` key in `--json`.

Point 4 is intentional. The checker is deterministic and network-free so it satisfies `check`'s contract, but `check` is documented CI and pre-commit safe, and existing repos contain hand-drawn schematics that would light up under these checks. Making it fail would break users on upgrade for a defect class they never opted into. The binding gate belongs in `create`, where copperhead authored the sheet and owns it.

Full specification, including WHEN/THEN scenarios per family and the design rationale, is drafted as the `readable-schematic-drafting` OpenSpec change (proposal, design with decisions D1-D10, four delta specs covering `schematic-legibility`, `create-pipeline`, `agent-core`, `cli-surface`, and a 27-task implementation list).

### Alternatives you considered

**Prompt and conventions only.** Add the drafting standard to the stage 4 prompt and stop there. Cheapest option, and rejected as the sole fix for the same reason `verify_symbols` exists: an unverified instruction regresses the moment sampling goes a different way. It is included here, but as the thing that gets the first draft right, not as the guarantee.

**A deterministic auto-placer.** Compute symbol coordinates from the netlist, rank by signal flow, band by subsystem, and emit geometry from code, taking placement away from the model entirely. Biggest consistency win and rejected for this change on two grounds: it would have to write geometry into `.kicad_sch` from code, breaking the invariant that the parser never serializes and edits happen only as anchored text replaces; and it would have to beat the model on every topology to be worth it. Kept as a plausible successor once the checker has pinned down what "good" means in machine-checkable terms.

**KiCad's native `(group ...)` construct for grouping.** Rejected: native groups are an editor selection aid, a uuid membership list that draws nothing on a plot, so they would produce none of the captioned boxes that make a sheet readable in an SVG or PDF export. Plain rectangles plus text render in the outputs, are easier for the agent to author by anchored edit, and make membership geometric, which has the useful property that a symbol moved out of its box becomes detectable.

**Gating on every family including the thresholds.** Rejected as a convergence risk: `low-utilization` and `crowding` are judgment calls, and a repair loop that cannot satisfy a subjective number burns the turn budget and ends in rollback.

### Effect on the invariants

Spec-gated in: no effect. Nothing about the write-tool gating changes.

Verification-gated out: this extends it. The invariant currently reads "nothing is done until ERC, and DRC when the board changed, passes", and that is true of the net graph and the board. This adds a third deterministic checker on the same pattern, binding at the stage 4 completion contract and at `finish` through the obligations ledger. `check` stays LLM-free and network-free with the checker included, and its exit code is unchanged, so no existing repo starts failing.

issues.title: create retries a turn-budget-exhausted stage with the same budget, so it walls up to three times in a row
issues.body:
## What happened

A `create` stage that fails with `turn-budget-exhausted` is retried with **exactly the same turn budget** that just proved insufficient, so it can burn every auto-retry hitting the same wall.

`stageTurns` is read once per stage at [`src/commands/create.ts:798`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/commands/create.ts#L798), outside the attempt loop, and passed unchanged into every attempt at [`src/commands/create.ts:836`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/commands/create.ts#L836). Nothing escalates it between attempts, so with the default `maxStageRetries: 2` the pipeline can run the schematic stage three times at 40 turns each, roll back three times, and end no closer than it started.

The recovery supervisor cannot compensate either. `diagnose()` ([`create.ts:884`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/commands/create.ts#L884)) is handed the failure only as the prose string `the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted)`, with no structured signal that the cause was budget rather than a bad edit or a failed gate, and its verdicts are limited to `retry` and `abort`. It has no way to say "retry, but with more turns". For every other failure mode an identical retry plus guidance is reasonable; budget exhaustion is the one case where it is knowably futile.

Two contributing factors, arguably separable:

1. **`create` has no `--max-turns` flag.** `do` and `sync` both expose one ([`cli.ts:100`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/cli.ts#L100), [`cli.ts:232`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/cli.ts#L232)); `create` ([`cli.ts:351-385`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/cli.ts#L351-L385)) does not, so the only way to give the schematic stage a realistic budget is to hand-edit `stageMaxTurns` into `.copperhead/config.json` before the run. That the default is too small for this stage is already known internally: [`manual-tests/setup.sh:46-51`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/manual-tests/setup.sh#L46-L51) sets `maxTurns: 100` for create sandboxes, with a comment explaining why. `init`-scaffolded repos get 40.

2. **The attended continue prompt from #15 does not fire on non-TTY output.** `budgetContinuePrompt()` ([`cli.ts:55-59`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/cli.ts#L55-L59)) returns `undefined` unless *both* stdin and stdout are TTYs, so piping or `tee`-ing a long create run silently removes the escape hatch and budget exhaustion goes straight to fail-and-restore.

Expected: a stage that dies of turn starvation either gets more turns on its next attempt, or aborts immediately with "this needs a larger budget" instead of spending two more rollbacks to rediscover the same thing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a repo whose `.copperhead/config.json` carries the default `maxTurns: 40` and no `stageMaxTurns` (i.e. anything scaffolded normally, not via `manual-tests/setup.sh create`).
2. Run `copperhead create --brief <brief.md>` on a brief with more than a handful of parts, with output piped or redirected so the TTY continue prompt is unavailable.
3. Wait for the `schematic` stage to exhaust its 40 turns.
4. Observe: the tree is restored, the supervisor is asked whether to retry, and the retry starts again with the same 40-turn budget.

## Output

```
llm-cache: replayed a cached response (hit #40, no tokens spent)
  > edit_file  edited docs/CHANGELOG.md
run failed: turn budget exhausted (40 turns, 8 files touched but unverified)
working tree restored to pre-run snapshot
failed work preserved: git stash entry "copperhead failed run 2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z" (07caccd7dc); recover with `git stash apply`, discard with `git stash drop`
transcript: .copperhead/runs/2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z/transcript.jsonl
summary: .copperhead/runs/2026-07-29T19-08-45-912Z/summary.md
turn-budget-exhausted . ERC clean . 1m15s . 0 in / 0 out
stage schematic: the run ended as "failure" (turn-budget-exhausted); asking the model whether to retry...
```

Note the `0 in / 0 out`: this particular run replayed all 40 turns from `.copperhead/llm-cache`, which is also worth knowing, a cached failure re-walls for free rather than surfacing as "you have already tried this".

## Which command

create

## Model backend

Not meaningful for this excerpt: the pasted run replayed entirely from the LLM cache. The defect is in pipeline control flow and is backend-independent.

## copperhead version

0.9.0 (commit 0d47855)

## Node, KiCad, and OS

node v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4, Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS

## Suggested fix

- Escalate the budget on this failure mode only: when the previous attempt's `exitPath` is `turn-budget-exhausted`, raise the next attempt's `maxTurns`. Reusing the `budgetExtraTurns` shape (`ceil(original / 2)` per [`cli-args.ts:30-31`](https://github.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/blob/main/src/util/cli-args.ts#L30-L31)) gives 40 to 60 to 90 across three attempts, consistent with what the attended prompt already offers.
- Pass the structured `exitPath` into `diagnose()` so a budget failure can be answered with `abort` and an explicit "this needs a larger budget, not another attempt" reason, rather than the supervisor guessing from prose.
- Optionally add `--max-turns <n>` to `create`, defined as the per-stage cap that `stageMaxTurns` still overrides per stage. This would not have saved the run above, but it removes the config-edit round trip.
- Consider raising the scaffolded default for the `schematic` stage, since the repo already documents 40 as inadequate there.

issues.title: create's stage gates verify shape, not correctness: 5 of 8 stages have no deterministic check, and verify_symbols is advisory
issues.body:
### The problem

`create`'s eight stages are gated by `isComplete` predicates in `src/commands/create.ts:78-235`, and the pipeline re-checks the same predicate after a run reports success (`src/commands/create.ts:861-866`). That correctly catches "the agent produced nothing". It does not catch "the agent produced something wrong", and for five of the eight stages nothing else does either.

What actually verifies each stage today, with the citation for each claim:

| # | Stage | Deterministic verification that runs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | spec-seed | none | doc-only stage; see the two clauses below |
| 2 | architecture | none | same |
| 3 | part-selection | none | same |
| 4 | schematic | ERC, drift, edit-time load probe, `verify_symbols` (advisory) | `tools.ts:300`, `tools.ts:409`, `tools.ts:246-272`, `tools.ts:327` |
| 5 | layout-draft | DRC, via the finish gate because the board was touched | `tools.ts:610-615` |
| 6 | outputs | `export_outputs` reports per-artifact failure, but the gate only requires one `.gbr` to exist | `tools.ts:386`, `create.ts:201-205` |
| 7 | firmware | none | no compile step exists anywhere in the tool list |
| 8 | devplan | none | shape check only |

Two clauses are what make stages 1, 2, 3 and 8 unverified rather than merely lightly verified:

1. A `.md` edit opens a `drift` obligation (`ledger.ts:52-54`), and `check_drift` is the only tool that clears it. But with no schematic configured it clears the obligation and returns `no schematic configured; drift vacuously clean` (`tools.ts:421-425`). Stages 1 to 3 all run before the schematic exists, so the one obligation a doc-only stage opens closes itself without comparing anything. `checkDrift` has a second carve-out for a zero-symbol schematic (`drift.ts:52-58`).
2. `finish` requires ERC and DRC only when a KiCad file was touched (`tools.ts:610-615`). A doc-only stage touches none, so it exits with no deterministic tool having run at all.

Three further gaps, each verifiable against the current tree:

**`verify_symbols` is advisory.** It is the only check that catches an invented pinout on a real-sounding `lib_id`, which ERC cannot see because ERC only checks the file's internal consistency. It cross-checks `lib_symbols` against the `.kicad_sym` libraries installed on the machine (`symlib.ts:189`, findings `no-library | no-symbol | pin-count | pin-mismatch` at `symlib.ts:168`). But its handler opens no obligation, there is no matching `ObligationKind` (`ledger.ts:6-13`), and `finish` cannot block on it. Outside its own definition, `verify_symbols` appears in exactly one place in the repository: the stage 4 prompt string at `create.ts:180`. It is not in `check`, not in `sync`, not in SPEC.md. If the model does not call it, or calls it and ignores the findings, the run still completes and commits.

**Recorded numeric budgets are never evaluated.** `record_constraint` stores `min` and `max` (`tools.ts:470-471`), but `checkForbiddenPins` (`constraints.ts:142`) is the only mechanical check in the registry. A budget like `sleep_current_uA: 25` is injected into the system prompt and honored only by the model choosing to honor it. Recording a budget currently reads as enforcing it.

**Stage 3's gate is satisfiable by deleting a flag.** The gate is "at least one row whose MPN column is not `UNVERIFIED`" (`create.ts:131-148`). `check` is contractually network-free, so nothing confirms the part exists. Removing the honesty flag satisfies the gate.

The net effect is a mismatch between what the pipeline guarantees and what "verification-gated out" is reasonably read to mean. The invariant is true of the schematic and the board. It is not true of the pipeline, and nothing states where the line falls.

### Proposed behavior

**A. Document the real verification surface, per stage.**

Add a stage-by-stage table to SPEC.md's `create` section and to `docs/src/content/docs/workflows/create-from-brief.md` giving, for each stage: the artifact, the gate predicate, the deterministic tool that backs it, and the data source that tool reads. A stage with no deterministic backing is listed as unverified in plain words rather than left to inference. Same table in the run summary vocabulary, so a reader of `summary.md` can tell which of a run's claims were asserted by a tool.

**B. Close the gaps where verifiable local data already exists.**

1. **Gate `verify_symbols`.** Add a `symbol-verification` obligation kind, opened when a schematic edit touches `lib_symbols`, cleared only by a `verify_symbols` run with zero reconcilable findings (`no-library` skips stay warnings, since an uninstalled library is not a design error). Wire the same check into `copperhead check` so it is visible in CI, not only inside an agent run. Data source: the installed `.kicad_sym` libraries, already resolved by `symbolSearchDirs` in `symlib.ts:48`.
2. **Verify footprint identity against the installed footprint libraries.** Symbols get library verification; footprints get none. A `.pretty/*.kicad_mod` counterpart to `symlib.ts` would confirm that a footprint id resolves to a real footprint and that its pad count matches the symbol's pin count. Note this is distinct from `add-fab-release-gate`, which checks footprint *presence* in BOM rows and *parity* between schematic and board; neither asks whether the id names a footprint that exists.
3. **Make budget evaluation explicit.** Where the inputs are in the repo, evaluate a recorded `min`/`max` constraint and report the result. Where they are not, report the constraint as recorded-but-unevaluated rather than letting a recorded budget read as an enforced one.
4. **Stage 6 gates on the export report**, not on one `.gbr` existing. `exportFab` already returns per-artifact `produced` and `failed` (`tools.ts:386-407`); the stage should require the report, and persist it so the gate is reproducible on resume.
5. **Stage 7 records whether a compile happened.** If a vendor toolchain is present, build and record the result; if not, record "not compiled here" as run metadata rather than only as prose the model was asked to write.

Every check added here must name the artifact it read, so a green result is reproducible offline by a human running the same tool.

### Alternatives you considered

- **Leave it to the prompts.** This is the current state. Stage 4's prompt already asks for `verify_symbols` and reconciliation, and it is exactly the kind of instruction that gets dropped under turn pressure. The repository's own design position is that gates beat prompts.
- **Wait for `add-part-research-tools`.** That change grounds MPNs in cached datasheets and is the right fix for stage 3, but it is network-backed and orthogonal to library-identity verification, which is local, offline, and available today. Both are wanted; neither replaces the other.
- **Fold this into `add-fab-release-gate`.** That gate is a pre-fabrication check on a finished repository. This is about per-stage gating while `create` is still running, and about symbol and footprint library identity, which the fab gate does not check. Overlap is limited to the BOM-readiness row and is noted above.

### Effect on the invariants

Strengthens verification-gated-out and does not touch spec-gated-in. It extends "nothing is done until ERC, and DRC when the board changed, passes" toward "and the parts are the parts they claim to be". Every proposed check is LLM-free and network-free, so `check` stays contractually CI-safe and inside its time budget.

Roadmap overlap has been checked: `add-fab-release-gate` (Phase 2 item 1) and `add-part-research-tools` (Phase 2 item 3) cover adjacent ground, and the scope above is what neither covers.

issues.title: Dirty-tree gate refuses to run over copperhead's own .copperhead/runs/ session log
issues.body:
### What happened

In a repository the user set up by hand (`git init`, then a commit), the interactive shell refuses to run on its own session log.

The shell opens a session log at `.copperhead/runs/repl-<ts>.log` before the first turn ([repl.ts:325](src/commands/repl.ts#L325)). A hand-made repository has no `.gitignore` entry for `.copperhead/runs/`, so `git status` now reports `?? .copperhead/`. The dirty-tree gate ([git.ts](src/util/git.ts), `gitPreflight`) counts that as uncommitted work and refuses the run.

The result is a dead end on a repository that was clean a second earlier: copperhead tells you to commit or stash work that is not yours, over a file copperhead itself just wrote. The three suggested fixes all miss, because none of them is the actual problem:

- `git add -A && git commit` commits copperhead's transcripts into project history
- `git stash` stashes them, and the next launch recreates them
- `--allow-dirty` works, but it silently disables the protection for the user's real work too

Expected: copperhead's own audit trail is not the user's uncommitted work, so it should not count toward the dirty-tree gate. `restore()` already carries `.copperhead/runs/` across a rollback rather than resetting it, so excluding it costs nothing.

Affects `do`, `sync`, and the interactive shell. `create` is unaffected: it runs with `allowDirty: true` and bootstraps `.gitignore` itself.

### Steps to reproduce

```
1. mkdir board && cd board
2. printf '# Brief\n\nA simple LED blinker board.\n' > brief.md
3. git init && git add -A && git commit -m "initial commit"
4. copperhead            # or: copperhead do "add a resistor"
5. type any request at the prompt
```

Step 4 creates `.copperhead/`. Step 5 refuses.

### Output

```shell
$ git status --porcelain     # after step 3
$                            # clean

$ copperhead
# ... shell opens, writes .copperhead/runs/repl-<ts>.log

$ git status --porcelain     # copperhead's own file, nothing of the user's
?? .copperhead/

# at the prompt:
working tree is dirty; copperhead refuses to run on uncommitted changes by default

why it failed: a rollback hard-resets to the pre-run snapshot, which would silently destroy your uncommitted work
to fix:
  1. git add -A && git commit — to keep your changes (recommended)
  2. git stash — to set them aside for now
  3. or rerun with --allow-dirty to let copperhead preserve them via "git stash create"
```

### Related: the ignore entry is never topped up

`GIT_ADD_EXCLUDES` in [git.ts](src/util/git.ts) currently holds only `.history/`, so no copperhead commit adds `.copperhead/runs/` to a repository that lacks it. AC-4.3 requires that entry. In a hand-made repository, a run that reaches `commitAll` (`git add -A`) therefore sweeps the transcripts into project history.

### Which command

other or not command-specific (`do`, `sync`, and the interactive shell)

### Model backend

Not applicable: the gate fires before the provider is constructed.

### copperhead version

0.9.0

### Node, KiCad, and OS

node v24.18.0, kicad-cli 10.0.4, Linux 6.6.6 (Pop!_OS)

issues.title: compat:<id> gaps: unclear Gemini/Groq docs, and their API keys aren't redacted
issues.body:
## 1. Docs don't show how to configure Gemini / Groq

The `compat:<id>` model route lists Gemini, Groq, and OpenRouter as supported endpoints, but only OpenRouter has a worked example. Gemini and Groq are named with no base URL, key env var, or model id, so configuring either means guessing three separate values.

Where: `README.md` (`--model` paragraph), `docs/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md` (`## Model selection`), `.env.example` (`OpenAI-compatible endpoint` block).

## 2. Gemini / Groq API keys aren't covered by secret redaction

`PATTERNS` in `src/util/redact.ts` only recognizes `sk-...`-shaped keys (OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter all start `sk-`), `Bearer ...`, and npm/GitHub tokens. It has no pattern for:

- Gemini: `AIzaSy...`
- Groq: `gsk_...`

`redactSecrets()` is the single write-time redaction path for transcripts (`agent/transcript.ts`), REPL logs (`commands/repl.ts`), Synap memory calls (`memory/synap.ts`), and `doctor`'s credential-echo output (`commands/doctor.ts`, `checkCredential`). A Gemini or Groq key that ends up in any of that text is written out in full — most plausibly the same way `doctor.ts`'s own comment already flags for OpenAI keys ("a pasted API key can end up as the model value: `--model sk-...`, a stray `COPPERHEAD_MODEL`").

Note `doctor.ts` already has a narrow, separate mitigation for one specific path — it drops the query string/userinfo before displaying a `baseURL`, since Gemini's native API sometimes carries the key as `?key=...`. That protects only that one display line, not `redactSecrets` itself, which is what every other surface relies on.

### Ask

Add key-shape patterns to `PATTERNS` in `src/util/redact.ts` for Gemini (`AIzaSy` + the usual base64url-ish tail) and Groq (`gsk_` + alphanumeric tail) keys, mirroring how `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` covers OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter today.
