issues.title: Agent install prompt: one pasteable line to install copperhead for a repo
issues.body:
## The problem

Installing copperhead correctly today means reading the README and making several judgment calls by hand: Node >= 20, KiCad >= 8 with `kicad-cli` on PATH, and then picking one of five model backends (saved-login Codex, Cursor Agent CLI, Claude Code, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`), each with its own setup path. `install.sh` covers the deterministic half (prereqs, npm install, `copperhead doctor`) but deliberately does nothing about backend choice, `copperhead init`, or wiring copperhead into a repo the user already has.

Meanwhile most of our users are already sitting in a coding agent. They should not be the ones doing this reconciliation. Greplica solves the same problem with a single pasteable line that points the agent at a prompt file: [`docs/agent-install-prompt.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Autoloops/greplica/refs/heads/main/docs/agent-install-prompt.md).

## Proposed behavior

Ship an agent install prompt so onboarding is one line the user pastes into any coding agent:

```
Install copperhead for this repo using https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chouhanindustries/copperhead/main/agent-install-prompt.md
```

The agent fetches the file and drives the rest: asks a short questionnaire, installs, verifies, and reports back in a few sentences.

### What the prompt file should contain

**1. Preamble.** A summary of what is about to happen, and an explicit instruction to ask the questionnaire *before* running any install command.

**2. Questionnaire** (native multiple-choice UI if the runtime supports it, plain multiple choice otherwise):

- *Q1: Which model backend?* Options: existing Codex CLI login, existing Cursor Agent CLI login, existing Claude Code login, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or "decide later" (copperhead's model picker handles it). The agent detects which logins are already present and marks the detected one as recommended, instead of asking cold.
- *Q2: Is this an existing KiCad repo or a greenfield project?* Existing means `copperhead init` scaffolds `docs/` from the schematic. Greenfield means point the user at `copperhead create --brief` and the [examples/](examples/) briefs.
- *Q3: Install globally via npm, or build from this checkout?* Recommended answer is inferred: build from source when run inside a copperhead checkout, `npm install -g copperhead` otherwise.

**3. Install and verify.** Prefer [`install.sh`](install.sh) when available (it already handles Node, git, `kicad-cli`, and never runs sudo), fall back to `npm install -g copperhead`. Then `copperhead doctor` for the environment and `copperhead check` for the repo. `check` is LLM-free and network-free, so it is a safe first run.

**4. Repo hygiene.** Confirm `.gitignore` covers `.env` and `.copperhead/runs/` (AC-4.3), and add them if it does not.

**5. Safety rules the prompt must state explicitly:**

- Never ask the user to paste an API key into the chat. Keys go in env vars or a `.env` the agent does not read back.
- Do not run `copperhead do` or `copperhead create` as part of installation. Those are mutating and LLM-backed; installation ends at `doctor` and `check`.
- Do not answer any copperhead confirmation prompt on the user's behalf.
- Do not echo full installer output.

**6. Final answer rules.** A few sentences: copperhead is installed, this is the backend it will use, this is what `doctor` and `check` reported, here is the one command to try next. No command dumps, no template filling.

### Where the file lives

Recommendation: `agent-install-prompt.md` at the repo root, so the raw URL stays short enough to paste. `docs/` is an Astro project, so a plain markdown file dropped at `docs/agent-install-prompt.md` would not be served by the docs site anyway. Mirror the content as a docs page under `getting-started/`, with a CI check that fails if the two drift.

Also needed:

- A short "Agent quick start" section at the top of the README `## Install` block, above the manual instructions, following Greplica's framing: most users should not install copperhead by hand.
- The same one-liner on the docs site quickstart.

## Alternatives considered

- **Extend `install.sh` to ask the backend questions interactively.** Rejected: the script is deliberately conservative and non-interactive-friendly, and it cannot detect a Claude Code or Cursor login and reason about which one the user actually wants. The agent can.
- **Leave it to the README.** That is the status quo, and it is exactly the step where a user has to hold five backend options in their head at once.
- **A `copperhead install` subcommand.** Duplicates `install.sh` and `doctor` without solving the judgment calls, and cannot run before copperhead is installed.

## Effect on the invariants

No effect. This is documentation plus a README section, and the prompt file must not instruct an agent to work around either invariant: it stops at `doctor` and `check`, and it never runs a mutating command. The safety rules above are what keep that true, so they belong in the acceptance criteria for this issue, not just in the prose.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `agent-install-prompt.md` exists and its raw URL is pasteable
- [ ] Pasting the one-liner into Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor each produces a working install on a clean machine
- [ ] The prompt asks the questionnaire before running anything
- [ ] The prompt never requests a key in chat and never runs `do` or `create`
- [ ] README and docs quickstart both lead with the one-liner
- [ ] Drift check between the root file and the docs page

issues.title: Panel chat UI: VS Code-style WebView front end for the pcbnew pane (Claude Code panel structure, copperhead skin)
issues.body:
## Summary

Upgrade the pcbnew side panel (#114 Phase B) from the plain wx TextCtrl log to a full chat UI replicating the structure and interaction design of the Claude Code VS Code panel: a WebView-hosted HTML/CSS/JS app in VS Code-dark chrome, wearing copperhead's own identity (dark tile + flat copper + fiducial mark, not Anthropic branding).

Feasibility already verified on a KiCad 10 Linux install: `libwxgtk-webview3.2` present, wxPython 4.2 ships `wx.html2`. Availability still varies across platforms/builds, so the current plain-wx pane remains as the runtime fallback.

## Architecture (3 layers)

**1. `plugins/kicad/copperhead_panel/ui/`: self-contained HTML/CSS/JS chat app** (no frameworks, no network). All visual fidelity lives here:

- Title row: fiducial mark, project name, model chip, connection dot (same grammar as the REPL observability row)
- Transcript: user request bubbles, agent prose, collapsible tool-call cards (`run_erc -> clean`, click to expand), turn separators with token counts, outcome banner (committed / refused / failure) with the reload-prompt callout as a distinct element
- Streaming state: spinner + the REPL's rotating working words (Routing... / Etching...) ported to CSS
- Composer: multiline input pinned at bottom, Enter to send, Shift+Enter newline, disabled with spinner during a run, stop button, slash steering inline
- Theming via CSS variables in one `:root` block (VS Code-dark palette, copperhead copper accent), so the skin is swappable

Developable and reviewable in a plain browser with a fixture transcript; no KiCad needed for the visual work.

**2. `webview_panel.py`: the wx host.** `wx.html2.WebView` filling the existing AUI pane (and a pop-out `wx.Frame` variant via a "pop out" button). Python->JS: `RunScript` with one JSON event per serve message. JS->Python: `AddScriptMessageHandler` where available, custom scheme handler fallback for older wx builds. Feature-probe at pane creation; on failure, the current plain-wx panel is used unchanged. `client.py` and `logic.py` are shared by both UIs, so the existing 29 scenario tests keep covering the decision layer.

**3. Serve protocol v2: structured events.** Flat `log` lines cannot drive tool cards. Additive protocol bump: `turn` (n/max, tokens), `tool` (name, one-line + full result), `text` (assistant prose), `outcome` (exit path, verification, commit, reload note as data). Implemented as a custom `ProgressRenderer` inside `copperhead serve`; the seam exists, no agent-loop changes. Old `log` events stay for the fallback UI and existing consumers.

## Work plan (OpenSpec change `add-panel-chat-ui` when picked up)

1. Serve v2 structured events + tests (shapes, ordering, redaction still applies on the wire)
2. UI app with browser fixture transcript (the bulk of the work)
3. WebView host: bridge both directions, feature probe, fallback wiring; new decisions go into `logic.py` for unit coverage
4. Packaging: `ui/` ships in the PCM zip (build script already walks the plugin dir)
5. Docs: TESTING.md webview column (probe fallback, IME/clipboard, long-run scroll), SPEC.md 2.8 update, browser screenshots in the PR

## Risks

- WebView backend availability across platforms (webkit2gtk / WebView2 / WKWebView); the fallback pane is what keeps the addon shippable everywhere
- JS->Python bridge API differences across wx 4.x; scheme-handler fallback covers it
- Long-transcript DOM growth; virtualize past ~500 entries
- KiCad 11 story unchanged (rides the existing SWIG pane, tracked in #114)

## Branding note

Replicate the interaction structure of the Claude Code VS Code panel; do not use Anthropic's name, marks, or assets. Copperhead visual identity throughout.

Depends on: #114 Phase B (implemented on `feat/kicad-ipc-bridge`).

issues.title: KiCad extension: IPC context bridge + in-KiCad side panel (PCM addon)
issues.body:
## Summary

Integrate the copperhead REPL with a running KiCad instance, similar in spirit to what Claude Code's VS Code extension does for the editor: a launch point inside KiCad, plus live editor context (open documents, current selection) flowing into the agent.

The integration has two halves: KiCad's IPC API (KiCad 9+) gives us a protobuf-over-socket connection to the running editor for live context, and a dockable side panel inside pcbnew gives the agent a home in KiCad's own window rather than a separate terminal. The panel constraint is real: KiCad's IPC plugins run as standalone processes and cannot embed UI, so an in-window pane must be in-process wx UI (the SWIG Python path in KiCad 9/10). The panel therefore hosts a chat UI that drives copperhead headless over a local RPC, instead of embedding the terminal REPL.

## Constraints from KiCad's side

- The IPC API covers the PCB editor only. The schematic editor has no API yet in KiCad 9/10/11 (planned for later). Plotting/export over the API arrived in KiCad 11.
- The legacy SWIG Python bindings are removed in KiCad 11, so the IPC API is the only viable target.
- Official bindings are Python only (kicad-python). A Node client means compiling KiCad's published .proto files (protobufjs) and speaking the envelope protocol directly.
- External clients can also connect to the well-known socket when the user enables the API server in KiCad preferences, so the core bridge works without any plugin installed.

This maps cleanly onto copperhead's invariants: file edits + kicad-cli ERC/DRC remain the source of truth for mutations; the IPC connection adds context in, not edits out.

## Phased plan

**Phase A: context bridge (KiCad 9-11, no packaging needed)**

- `src/kicad/ipc.ts`: Node client for the IPC API (protobufjs over Unix socket / named pipe).
- REPL auto-detects a running KiCad on startup and shows it in the observability row, e.g. `kicad: connected (pcbnew: board.kicad_pcb)`.
- New read-only agent tools: `get_kicad_selection`, `get_open_documents`. Selection is injected into the prompt like ide_selection in the VS Code extension.
- After a verified run that touched the open board, prompt the user to reload in KiCad (or trigger the refresh via the API where supported).
- Degrades gracefully: no running KiCad means the tools are absent/no-op and the REPL behaves exactly as today.

**Phase B: the extension proper (side panel inside KiCad, PCM addon)**

- `plugins/kicad/` in this repo: a wxPython plugin that docks a copperhead pane into the pcbnew window (wx AUI), not a separate terminal window.
- The pane hosts a chat UI (prompt box, streamed responses, run status) and drives a headless copperhead backend (`copperhead serve` or similar) over a local RPC (JSON over stdio or a Unix socket), forwarding `KICAD_API_SOCKET`/token so the backend gets Phase A's context bridge for free.
- CI builds the PCM zip as a release artifact; distributable via the official PCM registry or a self-hosted repository URL.
- Known risk, tracked here: the in-process wx path is the SWIG plugin system, which KiCad removes in v11, and the IPC plugin system has no UI-embedding story yet. Phase B targets KiCad 9/10; for KiCad 11+ we follow upstream (UI embedding over IPC has been discussed) and fall back to launching the terminal REPL from a toolbar action if no in-window option exists by then.

**Phase C: live board edits via IPC commits (deferred)**

- Push board changes through IPC commits so they land in KiCad's undo stack with no reload. Bends the anchored-text-edit invariant and needs its own OpenSpec change plus a story for ERC/DRC gating against unsaved editor state. Blocked until the API's DRC/export surface stabilizes and the schematic API has a release date.

## Repo decision

The addon lives in this repo (`plugins/kicad/`), not a separate one: the shim is tiny, tightly coupled to the CLI contract, and covered by the same OpenSpec workflow. Distribution only needs a zip URL (GitHub release asset). Split later only if the addon grows its own UI, versions independently, or attracts contributors who don't want the copperhead toolchain.

## References

- KiCad IPC API dev docs: https://dev-docs.kicad.org/en/apis-and-binding/ipc-api/
- Add-on developer docs: https://dev-docs.kicad.org/en/apis-and-binding/ipc-api/for-addon-developers/
- kicad-python (official Python bindings): https://pypi.org/project/kicad-python/
- Related: #40 (MCP server exposes the pipeline to MCP hosts; this issue is about KiCad-side integration)

issues.title: Generalize the OpenAI provider: configurable baseURL, model, and key env var for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
issues.body:
### The problem

Copperhead currently supports three providers: direct OpenAI, direct Anthropic, and local saved-login Codex. The OpenAI provider constructs its client with no configurable base URL, and the model is hardcoded to `gpt-5` (`src/agent/providers/openai.ts`). That locks contributors into paid OpenAI or Anthropic credits, even though Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, and Cerebras all expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints with recurring free tiers, and Ollama offers the same interface fully locally. For an open source agent, "bring your own key, pay nothing during development" is a real need, and today the code cannot serve it.

### Proposed behavior

Generalize the existing OpenAI provider instead of adding new provider integrations. One change, five-plus providers:

1. **Configurable OpenAI-compatible provider.** Make `baseURL`, model name, and the API key env var configurable (via `.copperhead` config and/or env). Pointing the existing provider at Groq, OpenRouter, Gemini's OpenAI-compat endpoint, Cerebras, or a local Ollama instance should require zero code changes. This is the 90% of the value at 5% of the effort.
2. **Extend `copperhead doctor`.** Detect whichever compatible provider is configured (key present, endpoint reachable) and warn when the configured provider/tier is one that permits training on prompts (for example Gemini free tier, OpenRouter `:free` models). PCB designs are often proprietary; the diagnosis should surface that risk before a run does.
3. **Document a tested "zero-cost contributor stack".** A docs page describing a currently-working free setup, validated against the live AC-3.x integration tests, rather than encoding a routing cascade or a table of model names in code. Model picks rot in months; docs are the right place for them.

Example:

```bash
COPPERHEAD_PROVIDER=openai-compatible \
COPPERHEAD_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 \
COPPERHEAD_MODEL=qwen-3-coder \
COPPERHEAD_API_KEY_ENV=GROQ_API_KEY \
copperhead do "rename net VCC_3V3 to VDD_3V3"
```

### Alternatives you considered

- **Four separate provider integrations (Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras).** Rejected: all four are OpenAI-compatible, so separate integrations are pure maintenance overhead.
- **Per-task model routing (orchestration vs. editing vs. tool calls) with automatic failover.** Rejected for now: copperhead has a single agent loop, not an orchestrator with distinct call sites, and switching models mid-repair-cycle breaks prompt caching and behavioral consistency. Failover and routing are deferred to a later change; per CLAUDE.md, integrations are Phase 3 and out of scope for `build-copperhead-phase-1`, so this track should be its own OpenSpec change.

### Effect on the invariants

No structural effect: spec-gating and verification-gating are provider-agnostic. One caveat worth testing: weaker free-tier models are worse at byte-exact anchored edits and disciplined tool calls, which means more repair cycles and more rollbacks. That is the verification gate working as designed, but it is why the documented free stack must be validated against the live AC-3.x tests before being recommended.

### Next step

Since this repo is spec-driven, the first concrete action is drafting an OpenSpec proposal for the configurable OpenAI-compatible provider (items 1 and 2, with item 3 as a docs task). Happy to start on that; comment here if you want to pick it up or have opinions on the config surface.

issues.title: a failed rollback takes the run report with it on the refuse and dry-run paths
issues.body:
### Summary

When the rollback throws, two of the three rollback call sites in `runAgentLoop` let the exception escape, which skips `run-end` and `summary.md`. The run leaves no report at exactly the moment a report matters most: the working tree has been left in a partial state and nothing on disk says so.

`fail()` already handles this and says why:

```ts
// The rollback itself can fail (git in a bad state). That must not become
// an unhandled throw that skips run-end and summary.md — the summary is
// most valuable exactly when the tree is left in an unknown state.
```

The **refuse** path (`loop.ts`, `outcome === 'refuse'`) and the **dry-run** path call `restore` bare.

### How the rollback throws

`restore` shells out to git, so it throws on anything git refuses. The reachable case needs no corruption:

`snapshot` records a `git stash create` object when the tree is dirty. Git leaves that object **unreferenced by design** (`stash create` does not store it in the stash reflog), so an ordinary `git gc --prune=now` collects it. A `create` pipeline runs for a long time, and a gc landing in that window is not exotic.

```text
$ git stash create        # what snapshot records
86c98f67c51abbfab6b93c725e8a90c89d545f05
$ git gc --prune=now --quiet
$ git stash apply 86c98f67...
fatal: Could not resolve 86c98f67... to a stash entry     # restore throws here
```

Reproduced directly:

```text
restore THREW: Command failed with exit code 128: git stash apply 86c98f67...
```

### Why each path matters

**Refuse.** A refusal is the run telling the user a budget or constraint blocks the request, and the code right below calls it out as the most valuable thing to record:

```ts
// Refusals are the most valuable thing to remember: they encode a budget
// or constraint that this user's designs keep running into.
await remember({ ... });
```

If `restore` throws first, the `run-refused` event, `run-end`, `summary.md` and that `remember` call are all skipped. The user sees a stack trace and never learns what was refused or why.

**Dry run.** Beyond losing the report, a dry run's entire contract is that it leaves nothing behind. If the revert fails and the throw is swallowed higher up, the last thing written would still claim:

```ts
detail: 'dry run: changes reverted',
```

which is false in exactly the case the user most needs to know about.

### Expected

Both paths should do what `fail()` does: record the failure, keep going, and say so in the summary. The dry-run path additionally should not report "changes reverted" when the revert did not happen.

### Note on an adjacent PR

#34 (`--keep-on-fail`) touches the `fail()` rollback, which is the one path that already handles this. It does not touch the refuse or dry-run call sites, so there is no overlap in the lines involved.

### Verified

Reproduced against `main` at `6dcca30` by running the real loop with a scripted provider and collecting the stash mid-run, rather than by stubbing git:

```text
× refuse path      ExecaError: Command failed with exit code 128: git stash apply 17dd3edf...
× dry-run path     ExecaError: Command failed with exit code 128: git stash apply 055fc9ec...
```

I have a fix with regression coverage and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.title: sync's pins.h check can never fail: it substring-matches PINOUT.md, so any word anywhere satisfies any #define
issues.body:
### Summary

The `pins-h` check in `copperhead sync` compares a generated firmware header against `PINOUT.md` by substring-matching the raw document text. Any word that appears **anywhere** in the file satisfies any `#define`, so a header that has drifted arbitrarily far from the pin table is reported as consistent.

`sync` prints `sync: no inconsistencies` while `firmware/src/pins.h` names pins that do not exist.

### Steps to reproduce

Against the `open-key` fixture, whose `PINOUT.md` `init` generates as:

```markdown
Pin assignment extracted from the schematic. Check strapping/RTC notes before
reassigning pins.

| Refdes | Pin | Name | Net | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | 1 | 3V3 | 3V3 | |
| U1 | 5 | GPIO14 | KEY_DAH | |
```

Write a header naming three pins that the table does not assign:

```c
#define PIN_KEY  5
#define PIN_GPIO 21
#define PIN_3V   8
```

```bash
copperhead sync
```

### Actual

```text
sync: no inconsistencies
```

`KEY` matches inside the net `KEY_DAH`. `GPIO` matches inside `GPIO14`. `3V` matches inside `3V3`. None of the three is a pin.

Prose counts too: the sentence above the table contains "strapping", "RTC" and "pins", so `#define PIN_RTC` would also pass on a doc that never mentions an RTC pin.

### Expected

```text
3 resolvable inconsistency(ies):
- [pins-h] firmware/src/pins.h: claims "defines PIN_KEY" but actual is ...
- [pins-h] firmware/src/pins.h: claims "defines PIN_GPIO" but actual is ...
- [pins-h] firmware/src/pins.h: claims "defines PIN_3V" but actual is ...
```

### Root cause

`src/commands/sync.ts`:

```ts
const pinout = await readFile(path.join(docsDir, 'PINOUT.md'), 'utf8');
for (const m of header.matchAll(/#define\s+PIN_(\w+)\s+(\S+)/g)) {
  if (!pinout.includes(m[1]!)) {
```

`pinout` is the whole file as one string, so the test is "does this substring occur in the document", not "does the pin table assign this name". The module next door already parses the table structurally (`parseCanonicalTables` / `parsePinoutRows` in `src/memory/bom-table.ts`), and the drift checker uses it; this one check does not.

### Why it matters more than a normal false negative

Stage 7 of `copperhead create` generates `pins.h` **from** `PINOUT.md`, and `sync` is the mechanism that says the two still agree. A check that cannot fail is worse than no check: the pipeline reports the invariant as holding.

The direction is also the unlucky one. A false positive would be noisy and get fixed. This is a false negative, so nothing ever draws attention to it.

### Note on the pin numbers

The regex captures the value (`m[2]`) and never uses it. That is defensible and I am not proposing to change it: `PINOUT.md`'s `Pin` column is the **symbol pin number** from KiCad, while a firmware header holds the **MCU GPIO number**. On the fixture, `GPIO14` sits at symbol pin 5, so comparing the numbers would report drift on a correct header. The names are the part that can be checked; the numbers are not comparable without an MCU pin map.

### Verified

Reproduced against `main` at `6dcca30` through the CLI, output above. I have a fix with regression coverage and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.title: init silently skips the pre-commit hook when the repo already has one, so the commit gate is off without saying so
issues.body:
### Summary

`copperhead init` silently does not install the pre-commit hook when the repository already has one. It prints nothing, exits 0, and the user is left believing the commit-time `copperhead check` gate is active when it is not.

Any repository with `husky`, `pre-commit`, `lefthook`, or a hand-written hook hits this, which is a large share of real projects.

### Why the silence is the bug, not the skip

Not clobbering someone else's hook is correct, and I am not proposing to change that. The problem is that the outcome is never reported.

The documentation states the hook is installed, in three places:

- `docs/getting-started/quickstart.mdx`: "It reads the schematic, scaffolds the design docs, writes `.copperhead/config.json`, and **installs a pre-commit hook**."
- `docs/workflows/verify-and-sync.md`: "`init` **installs a pre-commit hook** that runs it, so hand edits that desync the docs, the constraint registry, or the schematic fail at commit time."
- `docs/concepts/docs-as-memory.md`: "you can put it in CI and in a pre-commit hook, and **the hook is installed for you by `init`**."

`init` already treats a comparable collision as worth reporting loudly. A hand-edited doc it will not overwrite prints `REFUSED (hand-edited; use --force)` and **exits 1**. The hook collision, which disables a verification gate rather than skipping one file, prints nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd <a KiCad project with git>
printf '#!/bin/sh\nnpm run lint\n' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
copperhead init
```

### Actual

```text
created docs/SPEC.md
created docs/BOM.md
created docs/PINOUT.md
created docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md
created docs/LAYOUT.md
created docs/DECISIONS.md
created docs/CHANGELOG.md
```

Exit 0. Nothing about the hook. `git commit` now runs `npm run lint` and never runs `copperhead check`.

### Expected

Something that says the gate is off and what to do about it. `--json` should carry it too, since that is the CI-readable surface.

### Root cause

`src/memory/scaffold.ts`:

```ts
if (existsSync(hookPath)) {
  const existing = await readFile(hookPath, 'utf8');
  if (existing.includes(HOOK_MARKER)) return null; // idempotent
  return null; // never clobber a user's own hook
}
```

Both branches return `null`, and the caller only uses a non-null value:

```ts
const hook = await installPreCommitHook(repoRoot);
if (hook) result.created.push(path.relative(repoRoot, hook));
```

So "already ours, nothing to do" and "someone else's hook, gate is off" are indistinguishable to every caller. The same `null` also covers a third case: no `.git/hooks` directory at all.

### Note on test coverage

Every `runInit` call in the test suite passes `installHooks: false`, except the AC-1.1 test which asserts the hook is created on a fresh repo. The collision path has no coverage, which is why this has stayed invisible.

### Verified

Reproduced against `main` at `6dcca30` using the CLI, with the output above. I have a fix with regression coverage for all four outcomes (fresh install, idempotent re-run, foreign hook, no hooks dir) and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.title: parseDiagnosis reads a retry verdict as abort when a brace precedes the JSON, ending the run
issues.body:
### Summary

`parseDiagnosis` scans only the **first** `{` in the diagnosis turn. Two shapes that models actually produce make it read a `retry` verdict as `abort`, which ends the run instead of retrying the stage.

Recovery is supposed to fail safe toward abort when the diagnosis is *ambiguous*. These are not ambiguous: the model returned a well-formed verdict and the parser threw it away.

### Shape 1: an unbalanced brace in the prose ahead of the JSON

```
The stage emitted a literal { in its output.
{"verdict":"retry","reason":"dropped edit","guidance":"apply the edit"}
```

Actual: `{"verdict":"abort","reason":"diagnosis was not valid JSON"}`

The scan starts at the brace in the prose, so depth never returns to zero. The real object is consumed as part of that one never-closing candidate, and the loop ends without ever considering it.

This is easy to hit because the diagnostician is describing a failing pipeline stage, and stage failures frequently *are* about JSON, tool arguments, or s-expressions. The word "brace" is not rare in that context.

### Shape 2: a preamble object with no verdict

```
{"note":"thinking"}
{"verdict":"retry","reason":"real reason"}
```

Actual: `{"verdict":"abort","reason":"no reason given"}`

The first object parses, so the `try` succeeds and the function returns. `o.verdict` is `undefined`, and

```ts
const verdict = o.verdict === 'retry' ? 'retry' : 'abort';
```

turns "this object has no verdict" into "this object says abort". The real verdict is one line below and is never read.

### Why it matters

`create.ts` treats `abort` as terminal:

```ts
if (diagnosis.verdict === 'abort') { ... }   // stage ends, run ends
```

So a parsing slip on a *correct* diagnosis costs the entire run. The prompt in `diagnoseStageFailure` asks for "ONLY a JSON object, no prose", but the whole reason this parser is lenient about surrounding prose (there is already a test named "even wrapped in prose") is that models do not always comply. The leniency just does not extend to these two cases.

### Suggested

Try every brace-balanced object in the text, in order, and accept the first that actually carries a `verdict`. That fixes both shapes with one rule, and it keeps the fail-safe: text with no verdict anywhere still aborts.

It also improves the message. Today shape 2 aborts with `no reason given`, which points at the model. With the fix, an actually-verdictless diagnosis aborts with `diagnosis was not valid JSON`, which points at the real problem.

### Verified

Reproduced against `main` at `6dcca30`; both shapes are covered above with the actual output. I have a fix with regression coverage and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.title: export bom orders parts that are not on the board: a supporting table's rows (and its header row) become order lines
issues.body:
### Summary

`export bom` reads BOM.md as a flat list of pipe-rows, so every markdown table in the file is treated as part of the parts table. A supporting table's rows become parts, and its **header row becomes a part too** — the literal string `MPN` is emitted as a manufacturer part number in the DigiKey/Mouser cart CSV.

This is the same class of bug as I5, which was fixed for the drift gate (`parseCanonicalRows` groups tables and keeps only the Refdes/Pin-headed one). `src/kicad/bom-export.ts` still calls the pre-I5 `parseMarkdownTables`, so the exporter never got the fix.

It matters here more than it did for drift: drift produced a false failure that a human reads. This produces a **file the user uploads to a supplier to buy parts with**.

### Steps to reproduce

A BOM.md in exactly the shape I5 taught the drift gate to accept, a parts table plus a quiescent-current roll-up:

```markdown
# Bill of Materials

| Refdes | Value | Footprint | MPN | Manufacturer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | 5.1k | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | RC0603FR-075K1L | Yageo |
| D1 | Red | LED_SMD:LED_0603_1608Metric | LTST-C191KRKT | Lite-On |

## Quiescent-current roll-up

| Item | Current | Notes | MPN | Manufacturer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LED branch | 0.9 mA | at 5 V | ROLLUP-NOT-A-PART | n/a |
| Total | 0.9 mA | | ROLLUP-NOT-A-PART | n/a |
```

Then `copperhead export bom --supplier digikey`.

### Actual

```
parseBom refdes: [ 'R1', 'D1', 'Item', 'LED branch', 'Total' ]

Manufacturer Part Number,Manufacturer,Quantity,Customer Reference
LTST-C191KRKT,Lite-On,2,D1
MPN,Manufacturer,2,Item                          <- the roll-up's HEADER row
ROLLUP-NOT-A-PART,n/a,3,"LED branch,Total"       <- the roll-up's data rows
RC0603FR-075K1L,Yageo,3,R1
```

Three of the five order lines are not parts on the board.

### Expected

```
Manufacturer Part Number,Manufacturer,Quantity,Customer Reference
LTST-C191KRKT,Lite-On,2,D1
RC0603FR-075K1L,Yageo,3,R1
```

### Root cause

`src/kicad/bom-export.ts`, `parseBom`:

```ts
const tableRows = parseMarkdownTables(md);   // every table in the file, merged
const headerIdx = tableRows.findIndex(...);  // finds the Refdes header
for (const row of tableRows.slice(headerIdx + 1)) { ... }   // ...and never stops
```

`slice(headerIdx + 1)` runs to the end of the document. Nothing marks where the parts table ends, because `parseMarkdownTables` discards the table boundaries.

`src/memory/bom-table.ts`, `parseCanonicalTables` already does the grouping correctly for the drift gate. The exporter cannot call it directly because it recognizes a wider set of header aliases (`Ref`, `Designator`, `Reference`) than `isHeader`'s `refdes|pin` test.

### Notes

- The drift gate runs before the export and passes, because after I5 it correctly ignores the roll-up. So the gate is green and the CSV is still wrong.
- Two open PRs (#79, #91) add new callers of `parseBom`, which would inherit this.

I have a fix with regression coverage and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.title: An empty COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB silently disables the disk preflight (Number('') is 0)
issues.body:
### Summary

The `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB` override in [create.ts](src/commands/create.ts) parses with bare `Number()`, and `Number('')` is `0`, not `NaN`. So an **empty or blank** value sets the threshold to 0 bytes, which silently disables the disk preflight that Issue 16 added:

```ts
const minFreeMb = Number(process.env.COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB);
const minFree = Number.isFinite(minFreeMb) && minFreeMb >= 0 ? minFreeMb * 1024 * 1024 : DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_BYTES;
```

`assertDiskSpace` then returns immediately, because `free >= 0` is always true.

### Actual results

| `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB` | `Number()` | resulting threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unset | `NaN` | 2.0 GiB (correct) |
| `abc` | `NaN` | 2.0 GiB (correct) |
| `500` | `500` | 0.488 GiB (correct) |
| **`` (empty)** | **`0`** | **0 GiB — check disabled** |
| **`" "` (blank)** | **`0`** | **0 GiB — check disabled** |

The failure mode is the one Issue 16 exists to prevent: the run starts on a nearly-full disk and dies partway through with a raw `ENOSPC` from whichever write loses, after doing expensive work. Because the intent of `Number.isFinite(...) && >= 0` is clearly "fall back on a bad value", an empty value reads as a bad value that isn't caught.

### Why an empty value is easy to produce

This repo's own `.env` loader creates exactly that shape. All three of these lines in `.env` set the variable to `''`:

```
COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=
COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=
COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=""
```

A commented-out example that gets uncommented but not filled in, or a CI job with `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB: ${{ vars.SOMETHING_UNSET }}`, lands in the same place. An operator who does this is trying to *keep* the default, and instead turns the guard off.

### Two smaller things in the same expression

- **`0` is accepted as a deliberate value.** That may be intentional (an explicit opt-out), but it is indistinguishable from the empty-value accident above, so there is currently no way to tell "I meant to disable it" from "my env var is empty".
- **`Infinity` falls back to the default** because `Number.isFinite(Infinity)` is `false`. That is arguably the wrong direction: `COPPERHEAD_MIN_FREE_MB=Infinity` reads as "never run", but silently becomes 2 GiB. Minor, and I would not change it without a word from you.

### Expected

An empty or whitespace-only value is treated as unset, i.e. it falls back to `DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_BYTES`, the same as `abc` already does.

### Reproduction

```js
Number('');    // 0     -> threshold becomes 0 bytes, assertDiskSpace returns immediately
Number(' ');   // 0     -> same
Number('abc'); // NaN   -> correctly falls back to 2 GiB
```

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

issues.title: toolSearch bypasses the sandbox: reads through symlinks and dies on a symlink loop
issues.body:
### Summary

`toolSearch()` in [filetools.ts](src/agent/filetools.ts) walks the repo with `readdir` + `stat` and never calls `resolveInRepo`. Two consequences, both reproduced against the real exported function:

1. **It reads outside the repo through a symlink.** `stat` follows links, so a symlinked directory inside the repo is descended into and its contents are returned to the model.
2. **A symlink loop kills the search entirely** with `ELOOP`, so `search` stops working for the whole repo, not just the affected subtree.

This is a sibling of #85 but a genuinely separate code path: `toolSearch` is the one file tool that does not go through `resolveInRepo`, so fixing the sandbox helper does not cover it.

### Reproduction 1: reading outside the repo

Temp repo with `link -> ../outside`, where `outside/leak.txt` contains `needle SECRET outside`:

```
matches: 3
  b.txt 1 "needle two"
  link/leak.txt 1 "needle SECRET outside"     <-- outside the repo
  sub/a.txt 1 "needle here"
```

The match is even reported with a path (`link/leak.txt`) that looks repo-relative, so neither the model nor a human reading the transcript can tell the content came from outside the sandbox.

### Reproduction 2: symlink loop

Temp repo containing `sub/loop -> <repo root>`:

```
ERROR: ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered, stat
       '/tmp/srchprobe/repo/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/loop/sub/l...'
```

`dispatchTool` catches this and hands the model `error: ELOOP: ...`, so the run does not crash — but `search` is unusable for the rest of the run, and the error text gives no hint that a symlink is the cause. Note the walk also has no visited-inode set, so a loop is traversed until the OS refuses rather than being detected.

### Why it's reachable

Same as #85: the agent does not need to create the link. A symlinked KiCad symbol or footprint library is an ordinary project layout, and `.history/`, vendored directories, or any user repo may already contain one.

### Expected

- `toolSearch` does not descend into a directory that resolves outside the repo root, and does not return matches from files outside it.
- A symlink loop does not take the whole `search` tool down.

### Notes on the current walk

Two smaller things in the same function, mentioned for context rather than as separate reports:

- `SKIP_DIRS` is matched on the bare entry name, so it correctly skips `.git` at any depth.
- The `maxMatches` guard is checked before `readdir` and after each entry, so a large repo terminates fine. Only the symlink cases misbehave.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

issues.title: Path sandbox (AC-4.2) is lexical only: a symlink in the repo lets read/write/edit escape the root
issues.body:
### Summary

`resolveInRepo()` in `src/util/paths.ts` enforces AC-4.2 ("a tool call with a path outside the repo root is rejected") using `path.resolve` + a prefix check. `path.resolve` is **purely lexical** — it does not consult the filesystem — so a symlink inside the repo that points outside is resolved to a path that still *starts with* the repo root, passes the check, and the subsequent `fs` call follows the link.

```ts
export function resolveInRepo(repoRoot: string, p: string): string {
  const abs = path.resolve(repoRoot, p);   // lexical only
  const root = path.resolve(repoRoot);
  if (abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + path.sep)) {
    throw new SandboxError(p);
  }
  return abs;
}
```

The comment above it says "All file tools must go through this", and they do — which is why every one of them inherits the gap.

### Reproduction

I ran this against the **real exported tool functions** (compiled `src/agent/filetools.ts`), not a reimplementation. Setup is a temp repo containing `link -> ../outside`, with `outside/secret.txt` holding `TOPSECRET`:

```
READ via symlink  -> "TOPSECRET"                <-- escaped
WRITE via symlink -> wrote link/planted.txt     <-- escaped, file created outside the repo
EDIT via symlink  -> edited link/secret.txt     <-- escaped, secret.txt now "OVERWRITTEN"
```

So all three of `toolReadFile`, `toolWriteFile` and `toolEditFile` operate outside the repo root. The write path is the more serious one: `toolWriteFile` refuses to overwrite an existing file, but it will happily *create* one anywhere the process can write, and `toolEditFile` overwrites through the link.

The lexical cases the existing tests cover all still behave correctly:

```
'../secret/key.txt'            -> BLOCKED
'/etc/passwd'                  -> BLOCKED
'./link/../../secret/key.txt'  -> BLOCKED
'link/key.txt'                 -> ALLOWED   <-- the gap
```

`test/safety.test.ts` covers `../../etc/hosts`-style traversal and the shared-prefix sibling case (`/repo` vs `/repo-evil`), but nothing involving a symlink.

### Why it's reachable

The model chooses these paths. A `.history/` or vendored directory containing a symlink, a KiCad library symlinked into the project (a normal thing to do — shared symbol/footprint libs), or any repo the user points copperhead at that already has one, is enough. The agent doesn't need to create the link, only to walk into it.

### Expected

A path that resolves *through* a symlink to a location outside the repo root is rejected, the same as a lexical `../` escape.

### Suggested approach

Resolve the real path before the containment check, with the caveat that the target of a *write* may not exist yet — so the check needs to fall back to the nearest existing ancestor for new files. Something like: `realpath` the deepest existing prefix of the path, then re-apply the same containment test. Both `repoRoot` and the candidate need `realpath` treatment, or a repo that itself lives under a symlinked path (`/tmp` on macOS is `/private/tmp`) would start failing.

I have a fix along those lines ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

issues.title: redactSecrets leaves the tail of a base64 bearer token in the transcript
issues.body:
### Summary

`redactSecrets()` in `src/util/redact.ts` is the write-time guard for transcripts and summaries (AC-4.1) — `Transcript.event()` and `Transcript.writeSummary()` both run every line through it before it lands in `.copperhead/runs/`. Three gaps let a secret through, and the first one is the bad kind: it redacts **part** of the token and writes the rest to disk.

The file's own comment says the patterns are "deliberately broad: losing a few characters of log fidelity beats leaking a key" — these are cases where that intent isn't met.

### 1. A base64 bearer token is only partially redacted

`/Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{16,}/` doesn't include `+`, `/` or `=`, which are exactly the characters standard base64 uses. The match stops at the first one and the remainder is written verbatim:

```
in : Bearer ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=
out: [REDACTED]+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=
```

The surviving tail is `+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=`. A partial redaction is worse than none — it looks handled in review while the secret is still on disk.

### 2. `Bearer` is matched case-sensitively

HTTP auth schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 7235 §2.1), and real clients and logs emit `bearer` and `BEARER`:

```
'authorization: bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrst'  -> unchanged
'BEARER abcdefghijklmnopqrst'                 -> unchanged
```

Every other pattern in the file is anchored to a literal prefix where case doesn't vary, so this is the only one affected.

### 3. `npm_` tokens with dashes are missed

`/npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}/` excludes `-`, but npm also issues UUID-shaped tokens:

```
npm_0123456789abcdef-0123-4567-89ab-cdef01234567   -> unchanged
```

The `github_pat_` pattern next to it already allows `_`, so allowing `-` here is consistent with the file's existing approach.

### Reproduction

```js
import { redactSecrets } from './src/util/redact.js';

redactSecrets('Bearer ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET=');
// '[REDACTED]+SECRETTAILabcdef/MORESECRET='   ← tail leaks

redactSecrets('authorization: bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrst');
// unchanged

redactSecrets('npm_0123456789abcdef-0123-4567-89ab-cdef01234567');
// unchanged
```

### What I checked and did *not* report

- `ghp_ ghs_ gho_ ghu_ ghr_` are all covered — `[pousr]` happens to include every current GitHub prefix letter. No gap.
- `sk-` (OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter) and JWT-style bearers are correctly redacted.
- `SYNAP_API_KEY` is absent from the patterns, but `src/memory/synap.ts` has no caller yet, so nothing can reach a transcript through it today. Not filing that.
- AWS/Google/Slack/GitLab keys aren't matched either, but copperhead never handles those, so that reads as out of scope rather than a defect.

The existing tests in `test/safety.test.ts` cover the `sk-`, `npm_`, `ghp_` and `github_pat_` cases; none exercise base64, lowercase `bearer`, or dashed npm tokens.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

issues.title: bug: schematic-stage finish gate wedges — resolve_affected can't clear obligations (truncated output + exact-string match)
issues.body:
## What happens

Running `copperhead create` from a brief, the **schematic stage gets stuck at the finish gate** and never advances to layout.

The model finishes the schematic (ERC clean, drift clean, symbols placed), calls `finish`, and gets `cannot finish yet:` because some `affects-revisit` obligations are still open. It tries to close them with `resolve_affected`, the call doesn't clear them, and it loops — re-issuing the same call and burning turns.

From an actual run log (`pipeline-run-logs/03-...log`, turns 5–8):

```
[finish] cannot finish yet:
[finish] cannot finish yet:
... model: "The resolve_affected call didn't register. Let me re-issue it" ...
[finish] cannot finish yet:
```

## Why (two causes)

**1. Multi-line tool results are shown as their first line only.**
`finish` returns a full reason that lists the open obligations (`src/agent/tools.ts`, around the `cannot finish yet:` return), and `resolve_affected` returns a `Match these exactly:` list when an item doesn't match. Both are multi-line, but the output only shows the first line — so neither the operator nor the model sees *which* obligation is still open or what string to match. That's what produces the "didn't register" confusion.

**2. `resolve_affected` matches obligations by exact string.**
It clears an obligation by `` `${constraint_key} affects ${item}` `` (`src/agent/tools.ts`, `resolveOne`). The `item` text has to be reproduced word-for-word from whatever `record_constraint`'s `affects` field stored. A close-but-not-exact `item` doesn't clear anything. On top of that, the full set of open obligations isn't shown up front — in the same run the model closed the 4 it could see, called `finish`, and only then found a 5th (`env.operating_temperature_C`) it was never shown.

Together these make the finish gate wedge instead of telling the model exactly what's left.

## Suggested fix

- Don't truncate multi-line tool results — show the full obligation list.
- Have `finish` list the **complete** set of open obligations, with the exact `item` strings needed to clear each one, so `resolve_affected` can close them in a single batched call.

## Notes

- No existing test covers the obligation-ledger → finish loop (`test/create-hardening.test.ts`, `create-resilience.test.ts`, `create-stage-turns.test.ts` cover other paths). A scripted-provider test that opens affects-obligations, calls `resolve_affected`, then `finish` would repro this without needing kicad-cli or a provider key.
- Possibly related but distinct: #23 (shallow stage-completion checks), #21 (pre-commit deadlock). This one is specifically the finish/obligation loop.
- Found while working on the #66 create end-to-end bounty.
