**2. `resolve_affected` matches obligations by exact string.**
It clears an obligation by `` `${constraint_key} affects ${item}` `` (`src/agent/tools.ts`, `resolveOne`). The `item` text has to be reproduced word-for-word from whatever `record_constraint`'s `affects` field stored. A close-but-not-exact `item` doesn't clear anything. On top of that, the full set of open obligations isn't shown up front — in the same run the model closed the 4 it could see, called `finish`, and only then found a 5th (`env.operating_temperature_C`) it was never shown.

Together these make the finish gate wedge instead of telling the model exactly what's left.

## Suggested fix

- Don't truncate multi-line tool results — show the full obligation list.
- Have `finish` list the **complete** set of open obligations, with the exact `item` strings needed to clear each one, so `resolve_affected` can close them in a single batched call.

## Notes

- No existing test covers the obligation-ledger → finish loop (`test/create-hardening.test.ts`, `create-resilience.test.ts`, `create-stage-turns.test.ts` cover other paths). A scripted-provider test that opens affects-obligations, calls `resolve_affected`, then `finish` would repro this without needing kicad-cli or a provider key.
- Possibly related but distinct: #23 (shallow stage-completion checks), #21 (pre-commit deadlock). This one is specifically the finish/obligation loop.
- Found while working on the #66 create end-to-end bounty.

issues.title: Add optional install.sh bootstrap script for easier first-time setup
issues.body:
### The problem

New users currently need to install KiCad separately and ensure kicad-cli is on PATH before copperhead check can run. That creates friction for first-time contributors, especially on macOS/Linux.



### Proposed behavior

Add an optional install.sh bootstrap script that:

* Checks for Node.js.
* Checks whether kicad-cli is available.
* Detects the OS/package manager when possible.
* Installs copperhead or guides the user through the setup.
* Verifies the final setup with kicad-cli version and a basic copperhead check.

### Why this helps

* Reduces setup friction for new users.
* Gives a one-command onboarding path for macOS/Linux users.
* Keeps the current npm-based workflow intact for advanced users.
* Provides a clearer entry point than asking people to manually piece together prerequisites.

### Suggested scope

* Start with macOS and Linux support.
* Keep it idempotent and conservative.
* Print clear next steps if automatic installation is not possible.
* Avoid silent changes to shell config without user consent.

### Acceptance criteria

* Script detects missing prerequisites and prints actionable guidance.
* Script succeeds on a clean machine where dependencies are available.
* Script exits safely with clear messaging when auto-install is not supported.
* README includes usage instructions and supported platforms.

### Possible follow-up

* Add a copperhead doctor command that checks prerequisites and prints a setup report.

### Alternatives you considered

Workaround was installing based on commands given as part installation failure.

### Effect on the invariants

No effect doesn't touch OpenSpec or do any mutations. 



### Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and the roadmap, and this is not already tracked.

issues.title: Bounty: end-to-end test copperhead create (brief → clean full run) + findings report
issues.body:
> 💰 **BOUNTY — $50 USD**
> Tracked in **#💰・bounties**. Claim by commenting below. **First mergeable PR wins; paid on merge, not on submission.** Claims expire after 2 days without visible progress. Keep fix discussion on this issue, not in the channel.

Discord: https://discord.com/channels/1527265832730628136/1529900631735799828/1530129559868149800

## Summary

`copperhead create` is an **8-stage pipeline** (spec-seed → architecture → part-selection → schematic → layout-draft → outputs → firmware → dev-plan) that turns a natural-language brief into manufacturable KiCad artifacts. Each stage is committed independently, and a full board is built over multiple invocations.

There is rich per-stage instrumentation but **no end-to-end coverage that proves the whole pipeline runs clean from a brief to a committed final stage.** Manual driving of the pipeline has repeatedly wedged mid-run (most recently at stage 4, schematic) and surfaced a string of blockers, defects, and inefficiencies. We want that manual QA loop turned into a durable, mergeable artifact.

This bounty is for **taking `copperhead create` end-to-end on a real brief, landing whatever fixes it takes to reach a clean full run, and adding automated coverage + a findings report so the next regression is caught by CI instead of by hand.**

## Why this is worth a bounty

- The create pipeline is the product's headline command and its **least-tested surface** — unit tests cover pieces, nothing exercises the full brief→final arc.
- Prior manual runs found real, shipping-blocking issues across the pipeline (commit rollback wiping verified work, false-green ERC on empty schematics, drift-checker forcing doc degradation, unbounded temp/`.history/` growth filling the disk, session-limit treated as a hard error). Several are fixed; a regression today would be invisible.
- It's **gnarly and long-horizon** — it needs a KiCad + `kicad-cli` environment, patience across a multi-stage run, and judgment about what's a tool bug vs. an expected model wobble. That's exactly the kind of work that doesn't get picked up on its own.

## Scope — what a winning PR contains

1. **A clean end-to-end run.** Drive `copperhead create --brief <brief> --model <provider>` to a clean, complete run: **all 8 stages committed, process exits 0.** Fix whatever blocks that in the source (not by editing artifacts by hand). Small, well-explained fixes with tests are strongly preferred over large rewrites.
2. **Automated coverage.** Add an end-to-end / integration test (or a scripted smoke harness gated appropriately for CI cost — a deterministic replay against a recorded provider cache is acceptable and encouraged) that runs the pipeline far enough to catch the classes of regression above and **fails loudly** if a stage wedges, an ERC/DRC gate false-greens, or the final stage isn't reached.
3. **A findings report.** A markdown report in the PR listing every **new** issue and recommendation you hit, each grounded in an actual log/transcript/source line (no speculation). Use the existing legend — **BLOCKER / DEFECT / INEFFICIENCY / NOTE** — with `Where / Symptom / Suggested / Status` fields, and the **P0–P3** priority scheme for recommendations. Reference existing issue numbers on a recurrence instead of duplicating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `copperhead create` reaches a clean full 8-stage run on at least one non-trivial brief (a USB-C power breakout or similar), exiting 0 with the final stage committed. Evidence attached (log + `.copperhead/runs/*` summary).
- [ ] New automated coverage exercises the pipeline end-to-end and fails on: a wedged stage, a false-green gate (e.g. ERC "clean" on a zero-symbol schematic), or the final stage not being reached. It runs in CI (or is documented as an explicitly-gated job with a runnable command).
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass; existing behavior is not regressed.
- [ ] Any source fixes are minimal, explained in the PR description (what changed and why), and covered by tests.
- [ ] A findings report is included in the PR, in the format above.

## How to reproduce / get started

```bash
git clone git@github.com:chouhanindustries/copperhead.git
cd copperhead
npm install && npm run build && npm link   # global `copperhead` → dev build
copperhead check                           # verify kicad-cli + provider are wired up

# write a brief.md (a short product prompt), then:
copperhead create --brief brief.md --model <provider>
# re-running resumes past already-committed stages automatically
```

Notes for contributors:
- Confirm the global `copperhead` resolves to your dev build (`readlink -f "$(which copperhead)"` → `.../copperhead/dist/cli.js`); a stale global install will shadow it.
- The pipeline is resumable — completed stages are committed and skipped on re-run.
- Watch disk/temp buildup between attempts (`.history/`, `copperhead-*` tmp dirs) so a rerun doesn't fail for the wrong reason.
- A deterministic replay against the response cache (`.copperhead/llm-cache/`) is the cheapest way to get a repeatable run for the automated test.

## Out of scope

- Cosmetic/doc-only changes (see the good-first-issue #3 for README-quickstart friction — that one is unpaid, for getting your feet wet).
- Provider-specific new features (LM Studio, Cursor CLI, etc. are their own issues).

## Bounty rules (from #💰・bounties)

1. Claim by commenting on this issue. First mergeable PR wins.
2. Paid on merge, not on submission.
3. Claims expire after 2 days without visible progress.
4. Fix discussion happens here, on the issue — not in the channel.

issues.title: Add LM Studio as a local-model provider (OpenAI-compatible, no cloud key)
issues.body:
## Context / problem

copperhead's model backends are all cloud or hosted-session: OpenAI (`gpt-5`), Anthropic (`claude`), Codex (`codex`, saved ChatGPT login), and Claude Code (`claude-code`, saved subscription login). Every one either bills a cloud account or needs a hosted session, so there is no way to run copperhead against a **local** model, for privacy-sensitive designs, offline / air-gapped work, or zero marginal cost.

[LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai) serves local models behind an **OpenAI-compatible** HTTP endpoint (default `http://localhost:1234/v1`), including OpenAI-style function/tool calling for capable models. copperhead already speaks that protocol: `src/agent/providers/openai.ts` does the full chat and tool-call mapping via the `openai` SDK. It is just not reachable today because:

- `OpenAIProvider` hard-requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` (throws if unset) and has **no base-URL override**, so it always hits `api.openai.com`.
- `makeProvider` (`src/agent/loop.ts`) has no local route (`codex` then `claude-code` then `claude` then OpenAI).

## What to build

A local-model provider selected by `--model lmstudio` (and `lmstudio:<model-id>`) that points the OpenAI-compatible client at a local LM Studio server, needing **no cloud API key**. Sketch (open to design):

- Reuse the OpenAI chat/tool-call mapping with a configurable `baseURL` (default `http://localhost:1234/v1`, overridable via `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL`) and a dummy key (LM Studio ignores it; the SDK just needs a non-empty string). Either parameterize `OpenAIProvider` with `{ baseURL, apiKey? }` or add a thin `LMStudioProvider` wrapping it.
- Route `lmstudio` / `lmstudio:<model-id>` in `makeProvider`, where `<model-id>` is the model LM Studio has loaded (for example `lmstudio:qwen2.5-coder-32b`). Use a **distinct provider name** so the rate-limit failover (`otherProvider`) never silently switches a local run to a billed cloud key (mirrors the codex/claude-code no-fallback property).
- Document `lmstudio` and `LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL` in the `--model` routing (`config.ts` `resolveModel`, `.env.example`, the configuration reference, `README.md`).
- Actionable errors when the server is unreachable or the loaded model does not emit tool calls (local models vary in function-calling reliability; a tool-capable model is required, as the OpenAI/Codex paths already assume).

## Constraints / invariants to respect

- **No cloud key** for a local run; keys stay env-only per the secrets rail; endpoint config is env/config, never committed.
- **No silent fallback** to a cloud provider (distinct provider name, so `otherProvider` returns null).
- **`check` and `export bom` stay LLM-free and network-free**: the provider is reachable only via `makeProvider`, never from `src/commands/check` (the static import-scan test in `test/init-check.test.ts` still holds; localhost is not a cloud `api.*` host).
- **Offline test seam**: injectable client (like the other providers) so tests run with no network and no LM Studio install; plus an opt-in live parity entry gated on a reachable local server.

## Definition of done

- `copperhead do "..." --model lmstudio` (LM Studio serving a tool-capable model) runs the normal loop with no `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set.
- Offline provider tests green (routing, base-URL default and override, dummy-key, unreachable-server error, no-fallback); docs updated; `check` / `export bom` still make zero cloud-network calls.
- An OpenSpec change `add-lmstudio-provider` (proposal/design/specs/tasks) plus a SPEC.md AC entry, mirroring `add-claude-code-provider`.

## Notes

No API key needed; a local LM Studio install serving a tool-capable model is required for live runs. This mirrors the codex/claude-code saved-login providers (opt-in, distinct name, no cloud fallback) but for a local endpoint, and the same OpenAI-compatible seam generalizes to other local servers (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp) via the base-URL override.

issues.title: bug: isPowerSymbol hardcoded to 'power:' prefix ignores custom power symbol libraries
issues.body:
### Summary
In `src/kicad/sexp.ts`, the `isPowerSymbol` helper function identifies power symbols (GND, VCC, etc.) by checking if the library ID starts with the default `'power:'` prefix. If a project uses custom power symbol libraries (e.g. `CustomPower:GND` or `power_symbols:VCC`), they are misclassified as regular components.

This causes BOM pollution during `init`/`check` (appending power symbols to `BOM.md`) and breaks connectivity resolution in `pinNets`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. In a KiCad project, add a custom power symbol library (e.g., `CustomPower`) and place a `GND` symbol from it (with lib ID `CustomPower:GND`).
2. Run `copperhead init`.
3. Observe that `CustomPower:GND` is treated as a component and placed into `BOM.md`.

### Root Cause
In `src/kicad/sexp.ts`:
```typescript
const isPowerSymbol = (libId: string): boolean => libId.startsWith('power:');

issues.title: Build an edit-verification dataset: golden 'before' boards + expected outcomes for copperhead do (AC-3.x)
issues.body:
## Context

`copperhead do "<instruction>"` (src/cli.ts:125) is the core edit loop: take an
existing, known-good KiCad project and apply a surgical, verified change to it.
The acceptance criteria that define this product (SPEC.md AC-3.1 ... AC-3.7, the
pitch) are all edits *on an already existing board*:

- AC-3.1 propagating net rename across sheets + docs, surgical diff (< 5% lines).
- AC-3.2 constraint-aware pin choice (RTC-capable, non-strapping on ESP32-S3).
- AC-3.3 add a part with a unique refdes + `UNVERIFIED` BOM row.
- AC-3.4 budget refusal (the money demo): refuse an edit that busts a power budget.
- AC-3.5 repair loop, AC-3.6 rollback, AC-3.7 surgical (file not regenerated).

We cannot exercise any of these repeatably today. `test/fixtures/` has a single
known-good project (`open-key`, one sheet) plus a few canned report JSONs. It is
enough to prove the ERC/DRC plumbing works, but it does not contain the board
*features* each AC-3.x edit needs to reason over: multi-sheet nets, an ESP32-S3
with a documented strapping-pin table, a power budget in SPEC.md, an existing
footprint library to add from. So the strongest claims we make are untested
against real inputs.

This is distinct from #14 (the broken-fixture zoo for `check --fab`): those break
exactly one thing each to make a gate *fail*. This dataset is the opposite: rich,
ERC/DRC-clean *starting* boards plus the expected *outcome* of a specific edit, so
we can assert what `do` produced.

## What to build

A `test/fixtures/edits/` dataset. Each entry is a self-contained "before" KiCad
project that is ERC and DRC clean, carrying the design docs (SPEC.md with budgets,
PINOUT.md, SUBSYSTEMS.md, BOM.md) the corresponding edit must reason over and keep
in sync. Alongside each, a small manifest describes the edit and its expected
outcome so tests can assert against it rather than eyeballing a transcript.

Suggested `manifest.json` per case:

```json
{
  "id": "rename-net-cross-sheet",
  "ac": "AC-3.1",
  "instruction": "rename net KEY_DAH to KEY_DASH",
  "expect": {
    "erc": "clean",
    "commits": 1,
    "filesChanged": ["*.kicad_sch", "docs/PINOUT.md", "docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md"],
    "maxSchLinesChangedPct": 5,
    "mustContain": { "docs/PINOUT.md": "KEY_DASH" },
    "mustNotContain": { "*.kicad_sch": "KEY_DAH" }
  }
}
```

Cases to cover, one clean "before" board each (some can share a board):

1. **`rename-net-cross-sheet` (AC-3.1)**: a net used on 2+ sheets; expected after:
   renamed everywhere, PINOUT/SUBSYSTEMS updated, surgical diff.
2. **`pin-choice-strapping` (AC-3.2)**: an ESP32-S3 design whose SPEC/PINOUT
   documents the strapping pins (GPIO0/3/45/46); a key input currently on a
   non-ideal pin; expected after: moved to an RTC-capable, non-strapping pin.
3. **`add-part-second-led` (AC-3.3)**: a board with one RGB LED and a footprint
   library; expected after: a second LED, unique refdes, new BOM row flagged
   `UNVERIFIED`.
4. **`budget-refusal-pullup` (AC-3.4)**: a low-power design with an explicit
   sleep-current budget in SPEC.md (e.g. 25 µA) that a 100 kΩ pullup would bust;
   expected outcome: **refusal / alternative**, tree unchanged.
5. **`repair-loop` (AC-3.5)**: an edit whose naive form first trips a specific,
   deterministic ERC violation, so the repair loop is exercised.
6. *(optional)* **`rollback` (AC-3.6)**: an instruction crafted to remain broken
   past `maxRepairCycles`; expected: tree byte-identical to before, non-zero exit.

## Definition of done

- Each "before" project lives under `test/fixtures/edits/<id>/`, is ERC clean
  (and DRC clean where a board is present), and carries the docs the edit touches.
- Each entry has a `manifest.json` (id, ac, instruction, expected outcome).
- A short `test/fixtures/edits/README.md` maps each case to its AC and what it proves.
- "Before" boards are minimal but *realistic* for their AC: AC-3.2 must be a real
  ESP32-S3 with a strapping table; AC-3.4 must carry a real budget number in SPEC.md.
- Fixtures are reviewable as text (s-expressions); boards load under `kicad-cli`.

## Notes

- No API key needed to *build* the fixtures. The LLM-driven `do` assertions that
  consume them are provider-gated integration tests (run only when a provider is
  configured), consistent with the rest of the suite.
- Coordinate loosely: fixtures + manifest schema can land first; the harness that
  runs `do` against them and asserts the manifest can follow.
- If unsure an edit trips the intended ERC/DRC state, run `kicad-cli sch erc` /
  `kicad-cli pcb drc` locally and paste the report in the PR.
- Priority mirrors the spec: AC-3.4 > AC-3.2 > AC-3.1. If time is short, ship those
  three "before" boards first.

issues.title: Add Cursor CLI provider (--model cursor)
issues.body:
## Add Cursor CLI provider (`--model cursor`)

### Summary

Add a **Cursor Agent CLI provider** so users can run Copperhead’s agent loop (`do`, `create`, `sync` resolve) using their **local Cursor CLI authentication** (`agent login`), without needing an OpenAI or Anthropic API key.

This mirrors the existing **Codex CLI provider** (`--model codex`), where an external CLI acts as a **reasoning-only backend** and Copperhead remains the sole dispatcher for file edits, KiCad verification, and git commits.

### Motivation

Today, Copperhead supports:

- Direct API providers: `gpt-5` / OpenAI, `claude` / Anthropic (require API keys)
- Local CLI provider: `codex` (uses `codex login` + `@openai/codex-sdk`)

Users who already have **Cursor CLI** set up (`agent` on PATH, authenticated via `agent login`) cannot use that subscription/login for Copperhead runs today. They must obtain separate model API keys even though Cursor Agent is available locally.

**Use case:** run `copperhead do` / `create` with `--model cursor` using existing Cursor CLI auth, same workflow as `--model codex`.

### Proposed solution

Add a new provider namespace:

```bash
copperhead do "rename net KEY_DAH to KEY_DASH" --model cursor
copperhead create --brief brief.md --model cursor
copperhead do "..." --model cursor:composer-2.5   # explicit model override (if supported)
```

**Implementation approach (follow Codex prior art):**

| Area | Reference |
|---|---|
| Provider implementation | `src/agent/providers/codex.ts` |
| Provider routing | `src/agent/loop.ts` → `makeProvider()` |
| Model resolution | `src/config.ts` → `resolveModel()` |
| OpenSpec change template | `openspec/changes/add-codex-cli-provider/` |
| Offline tests | `test/codex-provider.test.ts` |

**Design constraints (non-negotiable):**

1. **Spec-gated in:** `edit_file` / `write_file` stay structurally absent until an OpenSpec proposal validates.
2. **Verification-gated out:** ERC/DRC must pass before success/commit; failures roll back to the git snapshot.
3. **Reasoning-only Cursor:** Cursor must not mutate the target hardware repo directly. All mutations flow through Copperhead’s capability-filtered tools, obligations ledger, and verification gates.
4. **`check` stays LLM-free:** no provider/network imports on the `check` path.
5. **Structured tool calls:** returned tool names must be validated against the current Copperhead tool catalog (same pattern as Codex structured output).

### Authentication

Support at minimum:

- [ ] **Saved login:** `agent login` session (primary UX, analogous to `codex login`)
- [ ] **Explicit key fallback:** `CURSOR_API_KEY` env var / `--api-key` passthrough (optional, confirm in design)

Optional env var for non-standard installs:

- `COPPERHEAD_CURSOR_PATH` — path override when `agent` is not on PATH (mirrors `COPPERHEAD_CODEX_PATH`)

### Scope

**In scope:**

- New `CursorProvider` implementing the existing `Provider` interface
- Route `cursor` and `cursor:<model-id>` in `makeProvider()`
- Update `resolveModel()` so `--model cursor` works without OpenAI/Anthropic keys
- Offline unit tests with mocked CLI/SDK (no network)
- Opt-in live integration test flag (e.g. `COPPERHEAD_TEST_CURSOR=1`), mirroring Codex
- Docs: README, `.env.example`, `openspec/specs/SPEC.md` §4.4
- OpenSpec change: `add-cursor-cli-provider` (proposal, design, delta specs, tasks) before implementation

**Out of scope:**

- Replacing or removing existing providers
- Cursor editing KiCad files or docs directly
- MCP server wrapper (`add-mcp-server` is separate)
- Live viewer / Phase 2 features

### Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `makeProvider('cursor')` returns a Cursor provider without `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- [ ] Cursor thread/session runs read-only / plan-mode; Copperhead alone dispatches mutations
- [ ] Structured tool calls validated against the current tool catalog; invalid calls get one corrective retry (Codex parity)
- [ ] Missing CLI or auth produces an actionable error (e.g. point to `agent login` / `agent status`)
- [ ] `npm test` offline suite stays green; new provider tests added
- [ ] Manual test: `copperhead do` on `manual-tests/runs/edit` sandbox passes with `--model cursor`
- [ ] Provider parity: at least AC-3.1-style rename test passes live with `--model cursor` (opt-in suite)
- [ ] `check` / `verify` behavior unchanged (LLM-free, network-free)

### Open questions

1. **CLI vs SDK:** subprocess to `agent --print --output-format json` vs `@cursor/sdk` — which is preferred for multi-turn structured tool calling?
2. **Model namespace:** is `cursor:<model-id>` the right override syntax (matching `codex:<model-id>`)?
3. **Auth precedence:** saved `agent login` only, or also `CURSOR_API_KEY` when both are present?
4. **Peer dependency:** should `@cursor/sdk` be optional/lazy-loaded like `@openai/codex-sdk`?

issues.title: export bom: add networked verification that ordered parts actually exist (MPN catalog lookup)
issues.body:
## Problem

`copperhead export bom` (added in #45) produces supplier-format CSVs, but nothing verifies that the parts are real. Orderability is gated purely on self-attestation in `BOM.md`:

- `hasMpn` — the MPN cell is not one of a fixed placeholder set (`src/kicad/bom-export.ts:381`)
- `unverified` — the literal token `UNVERIFIED` does not appear in the row (`src/kicad/bom-export.ts:385`)

So "verified" means only that someone deleted the word `UNVERIFIED` and typed something into the MPN column. A typo'd or fabricated MPN like `RC0603FR-9999XYZ` passes both gates and is written into the supplier CSV as an orderable line. A clean export gives false confidence that the parts exist and will ship — but suppliers only validate MPNs at *their* end, post-upload, where a bad line fails or silently drops.

This is by-design for `export bom`: the **network-free invariant** (SPEC.md) structurally forbids catalog lookups from that deterministic path. So real part verification needs to live in a separate, explicitly-networked step.

## Proposal

Add a networked part-verification capability that validates each orderable MPN against real supplier/distributor catalogs before an order is trusted.

Sketch (open to design):

- A new opt-in command, e.g. `copperhead verify-parts` (or `export bom --verify`), that is allowed to hit the network — kept structurally separate from `check`/`export bom` so those stay network-free.
- For each row with an MPN, query a distributor catalog and confirm: the part number resolves to a real part, is active/not obsolete, and (optionally) has stock. Candidate sources: DigiKey Product Search API, Mouser Search API, LCSC/JLCPCB parts API. API keys via env vars only (mirrors the existing secrets invariant; redact at write time).
- Report per row: `RESOLVED` / `NOT FOUND` / `OBSOLETE` / `NO STOCK`, and optionally write the confirmed LCSC part # back into `BOM.md` (behind a flag / drift-obligation).
- Wire the result into the `UNVERIFIED` lifecycle: a part that resolves against a catalog is what should clear the flag, instead of a human just deleting the token.

## Constraints / invariants to respect

- Must NOT be reachable from `src/commands/check` or `export bom` — those remain LLM-free and network-free.
- Secrets: keys in env vars only; redact `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`-style tokens in any transcript/summary.
- Deterministic core stays deterministic; networked verification is an explicit, opt-in overlay.

## Context

- Surfaced during review of #45 (see the "components are real" review thread).
- Roadmap: fits Phase 3 integrations per SPEC.md.

Blocked-by / relates-to: #45

issues.title: Add supplier BOM export: copperhead export bom (JLCPCB/DigiKey/Mouser)
issues.body:
Tracking issue for the **`add-supplier-bom-export`** OpenSpec change. Full spec: [`openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/`](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/) ([proposal](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/proposal.md), [design](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/design.md), [tasks](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/tasks.md), [specs/](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/specs/)).

## Why

`create` stage 6 produces a generic `BOM.csv`, but no supplier accepts it as-is: JLCPCB wants its assembly format, DigiKey and Mouser want cart-uploadable part lists with quantities. Users close that gap by hand today, which is the exact distance between "orderable BOM" (the current claim) and an actual order. Small lift, immediate payoff.

## What ships

- New command `copperhead export bom` with `--supplier <jlcpcb|digikey|mouser>`, `--boards <n>` (default 1), `--spares <percent>` (default 10):
  - **JLCPCB**: assembly-service CSV (Comment, Designator, Footprint, LCSC Part # when known) plus the matching pick-and-place columns note.
  - **DigiKey / Mouser**: cart-upload CSV (MPN, manufacturer, quantity, customer reference); quantity = `ceil(per-board count × boards × (1 + spares))`.
- Source of truth is **BOM.md** (already drift-checked against the schematic), so exports inherit that consistency guarantee.
- Rows flagged `UNVERIFIED` or missing an MPN are listed in a warnings footer and excluded from supplier files unless `--include-unverified` is passed.
- `create` stage 6 additionally emits the JLCPCB file alongside the existing outputs package.

## Invariants that MUST hold

Deterministic, LLM-free, network-free: a pure transformation of repo state, safe anywhere `check` is safe. `check` and the agent loop are untouched; BOM.md remains the human-readable source of truth.

## Impact

New `src/commands/export.ts` and `src/kicad/bom-export.ts` (reuse the BOM.md table parser that already exists in drift checking); create stage 6 gains one call. No new dependencies. Tests: golden-file per supplier format from the fixture BOM, quantity arithmetic units, warnings-footer/exclusion cases. Task breakdown in [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-supplier-bom-export/tasks.md).

Good first issue: self-contained, deterministic, golden-file testable, no LLM or network.

issues.title: Add part-research tools: web/part search + datasheet cache, sourceable as a checked constraint
issues.body:
Tracking issue for the **`add-part-research-tools`** OpenSpec change. Full spec: [`openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/`](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/) ([proposal](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/proposal.md), [design](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/design.md), [tasks](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/tasks.md), [specs/](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/specs/)).

## Why

The agent designs from trained knowledge alone: it cannot look up a datasheet, confirm a part exists, or check availability, so every new part is guesswork flagged `UNVERIFIED` and constraint sources cite datasheets nobody fetched. Grounding part selection in real, current data removes the biggest credibility gap in `create`/`do` output and pulls forward the "sourceable becomes a checked constraint" roadmap item (SPEC.md §8).

## What ships

- New **research tool family**, available to the agent loop in `do`/`create` alongside file/KiCad/memory tools:
  - `web_search`: reference designs, app notes, errata
  - `search_parts`: structured part search (MPN, parametrics, availability, pricing) via a supplier API
  - `fetch_datasheet`: download a datasheet PDF and cache it under `.copperhead/datasheets/`, recorded with URL, retrieval date, and content hash for reproducibility
- **Sourceable becomes a checked constraint**: search results (availability, lifecycle) land in `.copperhead/constraints.json` as cached snapshots with `source`/`retrieved`; `check` validates against the snapshot offline and reports staleness.
- **`UNVERIFIED` upgrade path**: a part confirmed against a cached datasheet is flagged `VERIFIED(datasheet)` with a pointer to the cached file and confirming section. No fetched evidence, stays `UNVERIFIED`. The agent still never invents MPNs.
- Fetched facts are cited (cache path + section), not pasted, so the registry is human-verifiable offline.

## BREAKING spec change to watch

The "no network tools in Phase 1" safety rail (SPEC.md §7) is **replaced** by a scoped network boundary: research tools are the only network surface, restricted to an allowlisted set of hosts, every request logged to the transcript. **`check`/`verify` stay LLM-free and network-free (AC-2.1 unchanged).** This modifies the `safety-rails` capability, so review that delta spec carefully.

## Invariants that MUST hold

- Research tools are read-only: they never mutate repo files outside `.copperhead/datasheets/`.
- Spec-gating of edit tools is unaffected.
- Supplier API keys join the env-var-only rule and the `sk-` redaction family.

## Impact

New `src/research/` (search client, supplier API client, datasheet fetcher/cache); three tool schemas in `src/agent/tools.ts`; transcript writer logs network requests; `check`/drift learns to read cached sourceability snapshots. `.copperhead/config.json` gains a `research` block (enable flag, host allowlist, supplier selection). BOM flag vocab gains `VERIFIED(datasheet)`. Supplier provider chosen in [design.md](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/design.md).

## Note

Depends on / composes with the MCP work only if part research is delivered MCP-backed; as specced it is a native tool family. Task breakdown in [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-part-research-tools/tasks.md).

issues.title: Add MCP server: expose the gated copperhead pipeline to MCP hosts
issues.body:
Tracking issue for the **`add-mcp-server`** OpenSpec change. Full spec: [`openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/`](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/) ([proposal](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/proposal.md), [design](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/design.md), [tasks](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/tasks.md), [specs/](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/specs/)).

## Why

Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, every MCP host) are already pointed at KiCad repos through raw tool servers that expose ungated file edits, so the host can rewrite a `.kicad_sch` with no spec gate, no verification, no rollback. copperhead's invariants only protect users whose entry point is the CLI. A thin MCP wrapper makes the gated pipeline the thing the host agent calls, so the invariants survive the integration.

**Decision (see proposal): this lives in copperhead, not a separate repo.** The MCP layer's value is the gated pipeline, not raw KiCad access; it dispatches into the existing command implementations so all invariants are inherited by construction.

## What ships

- New command `copperhead mcp`: a stdio MCP server exposing only opaque, high-level tools:
  - `copperhead_check` (optional `fab`/`strict` inputs) returns the JSON report
  - `copperhead_do` runs the full gated `do` loop and returns the run summary; the host never drives intermediate steps
  - `copperhead_sync` (verify always; resolve only when `resolve: true`)
  - `copperhead_init` scaffolds docs-memory
- **Structural opacity**: no file-edit, no raw KiCad, no partial-loop tools exposed. Nothing to reach around.
- Companion Claude Code / Codex skill under `integrations/` telling agents to use these tools instead of editing `.kicad_*` directly.

## Invariants that MUST hold (CLAUDE.md, SPEC.md §1.3 / §7)

- Spec-gated in: mutating tools stay structurally absent until a proposal validates.
- Verification-gated out: mutations are not done until ERC (and DRC if the board changed) passes, then repair or rollback.
- Sandbox to repo root; secret redaction (`sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`); keys in env vars only.
- No new network surface: stdio only; LLM calls happen exactly where the CLI already makes them. `copperhead_do` / `sync --resolve` refuse when no API key env var is present.

## Impact

New `src/mcp/server.ts`; `src/commands/` refactored so `check`/`do`/`sync`/`init` expose callable entry points returning structured results. New dep `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. Task breakdown in [tasks.md](openspec/changes/add-mcp-server/tasks.md).

## Open questions

- Transport: stdio only first, or also a local socket for the viewer/plugin later?
- MCP registry submission (a task, not a spec).

issues.title: Require CI + PR lint + review via branch protection on main
issues.body:
## Context

We now have two PR-quality checks in place:

- [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md): pre-fills What/Why/Design/Spec/Testing/Docs plus an invariant checklist.
- [.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml](.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml): fails a PR whose description drops a required section or the checklist.

Both are currently advisory. A failing check is just a red X; nothing blocks merge, and direct pushes to `main` still bypass everything. Branch protection is the missing layer that makes these checks required.

## What to do

Enable branch protection on `main`:

- Require status checks to pass before merge: `test` (CI) and `PR lint`.
- Require the branch to be up to date with `main` before merging.
- Require 1 approving review; dismiss stale approvals on new commits.
- Disallow direct pushes to `main` (all changes via PR).
- Optionally include administrators.

## Why

- Turns `pr-lint` and `ci.yml` from decorative into blocking.
- Guarantees a human (or the pr-review skill) verifies the invariants that the lint cannot check for truth: ERC still runs, secrets redacted, spec-gating intact.
- Stops unreviewed changes reaching `main` and keeps CI running against the real post-merge tree.

## Reference

Enforcement layers and rationale were worked out alongside the template and lint. The pr-review skill (.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) is the review-time checklist that pairs with the required-review setting.

issues.title: Rollback deletes the in-flight run's audit trail (preserveFailedRun stages it, reset --hard removes it), then the summary writer crashes the process
issues.body:
## Summary

When a run fails and rolls back (e.g. maxRepairCycles exhausted), the run's own `.copperhead/runs/<id>/` directory is deleted mid-run, and the process then dies with an unhandled `ENOENT` trying to write `summary.md` into it. The audit trail of the failed run — exactly the evidence `restore()` promises to keep — is destroyed, and the create pipeline exits with a crash instead of a clean stage failure.

Observed in copperhead-test: schematic stage hit 48 ERC violations wiring the board, exhausted 5 repair cycles, rolled back, crashed:

```
  [run_erc] ERC: 48 violation(s)
  [read_file] 1: # Pinout
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../.copperhead/runs/2026-07-21T13-18-28-851Z/summary.md'
```

## Mechanism

Two functions in `src/util/git.ts` interact badly:

1. `preserveFailedRun()` runs first and does `git add -A` — staging the (untracked) in-flight run directory.
2. `restore()` then does `git reset --hard <snap>` followed by `git clean -fd -e .copperhead/runs`. The `-e` exclusion only protects **untracked** files — but step 1 just made the run dir *staged*, and a staged-but-not-in-HEAD path is deleted by `reset --hard` before `clean` ever runs.

So the protection exists, and is defeated by the sibling function one line earlier. Everything else survives (the failed work does land in the named stash), only the audit trail dies — taking the process with it.

## Fix applied locally

- `preserveFailedRun()` now unstages the audit trail before creating the stash: `git add -A` then `git reset -q -- .copperhead/runs`. (An `:(exclude)` pathspec doesn't work: `git add` errors outright when a pathspec touches gitignored paths, and `.copperhead/runs/` is gitignored in some target repos but tracked in others.)
- `Transcript.event()`/`writeSummary()` now `mkdir -p` their directory before writing — losing an event is acceptable; crashing the run to report one is not.
- Suite passes 89/89 (including the AC-15.16 stash-preservation test, which caught a first attempt that used the exclude pathspec).

## Related hardening worth considering

- `restore()` could snapshot-protect `.copperhead/runs` structurally (e.g. move it aside and back) rather than relying on every caller to keep it unstaged.
- The crash surfaced because nothing between the agent loop and the CLI catches transcript-write failures; a failed run should still end as a *reported* failure.

issues.title: Feature: re-run individual pipeline stages on demand, with a stage dependency graph that invalidates and updates downstream work
issues.body:
## Problem

The create pipeline is strictly forward-only: `copperhead create` resumes at the first incomplete stage and there is no way to deliberately re-run one stage. But design iteration is exactly that: the BOM changes after the schematic exists, the spec's budgets tighten after layout, a footprint swap invalidates the outline. Today the options are bad — hand-delete artifacts until the completion probes read "incomplete" (fragile, see #23), or drive everything through free-form `copperhead do` requests that don't know they're redoing a stage.

## Request

### 1. Targeted stage re-run

```
copperhead create --stage part-selection          # re-run one stage
copperhead create --from schematic               # re-run a stage and everything after it
```

The stage runs with its normal stage prompt and gates, but against the *existing* artifacts (revise, don't recreate).

### 2. An explicit stage dependency graph

The pipeline order already implies it; make it data:

```
spec-seed → architecture → part-selection → schematic → layout-draft → outputs
                                              └→ firmware (via PINOUT.md) → devplan
```

Each edge should name *what* flows across it (architecture reads SPEC budgets; schematic reads BOM refdes/values/footprints; firmware reads PINOUT.md; outputs reads the board), so invalidation can be precise rather than "everything after".

### 3. Downstream invalidation + propagation

When a stage is re-run and its outputs actually change, downstream stages that consume the changed artifacts are marked stale and either:

- **auto-update** (default in autonomous mode): each stale stage re-runs in dependency order, scoped to reconciling with the upstream change ("BOM changed R1 10k→4.7k: update schematic value, re-run ERC, refresh PINOUT/outputs"), or
- **report-only** (`--dry-run` / interactive): print the stale set and what changed, let the human pick.

No change in a stage's outputs → downstream stays valid (content-hash the crossing artifacts, in the spirit of init's `generatedHashes`).

## Building blocks already in the codebase

- `record_constraint`/`resolve_affected` + the obligations ledger already implement fine-grained affects-propagation *within* a run — this is the same idea lifted to stage granularity.
- `checkDrift` already detects BOM/PINOUT-vs-schematic disagreement, i.e. a stale schematic edge.
- #23's direction (per-stage contracts, explicit completion records at commit time) gives the natural place to store staleness: a stage completion record can carry the content hashes of its inputs; stale = recorded input hash ≠ current hash. That would replace the shallow repo-state probes and make `--stage` re-runs safe by construction.
- #22's run metadata would record which stage re-ran, why (which upstream hash changed), and what it invalidated.

## Example end-to-end

```
$ copperhead create --stage part-selection
stage part-selection: revising BOM.md (fuse F1 3A→2A per updated budget)
stage part-selection: complete; BOM.md changed (F1)
stale: schematic (BOM edge), outputs (BOM.csv edge); layout-draft unaffected (footprint unchanged)
stage schematic: updating F1 value, re-running ERC... clean
stage outputs: regenerating BOM.csv, gerbers unchanged
pipeline consistent; all checks green
```

issues.title: create's stage-completion inference uses shallow existence checks — blank bootstrap files and init's own doc templates mark stages complete
issues.body:
## Summary

`copperhead create` infers stage completion from repo state (design D10, `src/commands/create.ts`), but several `isComplete` probes are shallow existence checks that false-positive on states where the stage's actual work never happened. Observed consequence in copperhead-test: **the pipeline skipped the schematic and layout-draft stages entirely** — over a schematic with zero symbols — and went straight to outputs, which then refused for a missing `.kicad_pcb`.

Third bug in the bootstrap series: #19 (can't create KiCad files), #21 (drift gates deadlock while docs lead the schematic), and now this — the resume heuristics can't tell "bootstrapped" from "done".

## Observed sequence

1. Worked around #19 by hand-scaffolding a blank `usb-c-power-breakout.kicad_sch` + running `copperhead init`.
2. Re-ran `copperhead create`. Output:
   - `stage schematic: already complete (resuming past it)` — `isComplete` is just `config.schematic` set + file exists; a blank sheet passes.
   - `stage layout-draft: already complete` — `isComplete` checks LAYOUT.md for the literal `## Draft quality` heading, **and init's generated LAYOUT.md template contains exactly that heading** as a placeholder. Running `init` retroactively marks layout-draft complete.
   - `stage outputs: running` → refused: `usb-c-power-breakout.kicad_pcb is missing, so Gerbers/Drill, DXF, STEP, and PCB SVG cannot be exported`.

## The general problem

Two independent flaws compound:

1. **Existence ≠ completion.** File-on-disk (`schematic`) or dir-on-disk (`outputs/` — a partially-failed export run also satisfies it) says nothing about whether the stage's contract was met.
2. **init's templates contain create's completion markers.** `generateDocs` in `src/memory/scaffold.ts` emits SPEC.md with `## Budgets` (spec-seed's marker) and LAYOUT.md with `## Draft quality` (layout-draft's marker). On any init-ed repo, create silently skips those stages. The probes and the templates were written against each other with no shared contract.

## Applied locally (stopgap, in this repo's working tree)

- `schematic.isComplete`: file must exist **and `listSymbols(...) > 0`** — a blank bootstrap sheet no longer counts.
- `layout-draft.isComplete`: additionally requires `config.board` set, the board file present, and at least one `(footprint` on it.
- Full test suite passes (89/89) with both changes.

## Suggested durable fixes

- Make each stage's `isComplete` check the stage's *contract*, not an artifact's existence: spec-seed → budgets recorded in constraints.json; schematic → symbols present + last ERC clean; layout-draft → footprints placed + DRC clean; outputs → expected artifact set present and non-empty; firmware → build marker.
- Alternatively (or additionally): record explicit stage completion in `.copperhead/` state at commit time — the pipeline already commits per stage, so the commit is the natural completion record — and use repo-state probes only as a fallback for repos not built by `create`.
- De-collide init: templates must not contain the literal completion markers, or markers must be something init never emits (e.g. a filled section vs an empty placeholder).

issues.title: Feature: record full run metadata (model, config, versions, git state) at run start — in the transcript, summary, and CLI output
issues.body:
## Problem

A run's context is mostly invisible. Today `run-start` records only three fields (`src/agent/loop.ts:168`):

```ts
await transcript.event('run-start', { request: opts.request, model: opts.model, provider: provider.name });
```

`summary.md` shows request/outcome/change/tokens, and the live CLI output shows nothing about the environment at all — just `stage spec-seed: running`. When triaging a failed or surprising run after the fact (e.g. the schematic-stage refusal in #19, or the drift gate-gaming in #21), you can't answer basic questions from the artifacts alone: which copperhead version ran (repo build vs stale global install)? what turn budget applied? what did the repo look like when the run started? was a schematic even configured?

## Request

Emit a structured metadata block **before the first agent turn**, written to all three surfaces:

1. `run-start` event in `transcript.jsonl` (machine-readable, complete)
2. a `## Environment` section in `summary.md`
3. a one/two-line header in live CLI output (at minimum: version, model/provider, stage, turn budget)

## Suggested metadata

**Tooling & versions**
- copperhead version + install path (catches the stale-global-install problem: running `dist/` from the repo vs `~/.nvm/.../node_modules/copperhead`)
- `kicad-cli` version (ERC/DRC behavior differs across KiCad 8/9/10), openspec CLI version if present
- Node version, OS/platform

**Model & provider**
- model id, provider, and how the model was selected (flag > `COPPERHEAD_MODEL` > config > available-key fallback — the winning source matters when debugging "why did this run on gpt-5?")
- sampling/reasoning params if set; API base URL if overridden

**Run identity & mode**
- run id, ISO timestamp, command (`do`/`create`/`sync`), stage name + position in the create pipeline
- interactive vs autonomous, and whether human gates were auto-approved
- for `create`: brief path + content hash (detects a brief edited mid-pipeline)

**Config snapshot** (resolved, not just the file)
- `schematic`/`board` paths (or null — #19 would have been diagnosable from `schematic: null` in the header alone), `docs` dir, `maxTurns`/stage override, `maxRepairCycles`, budgets verbatim

**Repo state**
- git commit, branch, dirty/clean + count of uncommitted files at run start
- whether the copperhead pre-commit hook is installed (relevant to #21)
- counts of open constraints and prior runs

**Post-run addenda** (same event stream, at finish)
- tokens in/out (already in summary) plus per-stage/per-turn breakdown and estimated cost
- turns used vs budget, repair cycles used vs budget, wall-clock duration
- exit path: done / refuse / turn-budget-exhausted / commit-failed (the `git add -A` failure mode from the .history/ embedded repo surfaced only as a raw exit-128 stack — it should land in summary.md as an outcome)

## Why it pays off

Every debugging session in copperhead-test so far (#19, #21) started by reverse-engineering exactly this information from transcripts, `which copperhead`, and `git status`. Runs are long, non-deterministic, and cost real tokens — a cheap deterministic header makes each one self-describing and comparable across model/config changes.

issues.title: init-installed pre-commit hook deadlocks the create pipeline: repo-wide drift check blocks stage commits while docs legitimately lead the schematic
issues.body:
## Summary

`copperhead init` installs a pre-commit hook that runs `copperhead check`. During `copperhead create`, this hook blocks the pipeline's **own** stage commits: the docs-first stages (part-selection writes BOM.md) legitimately run before the schematic stage populates the sheet, so the repo-wide drift check fails and every stage commit dies with exit 1 until the schematic exists.

Related to #19 (create can't bootstrap a KiCad project) — this was hit immediately after working around #19 by hand-scaffolding a blank schematic and running `copperhead init`.

## Reproduction (observed in copperhead-test, 2026-07-21)

1. `copperhead create` runs spec-seed → architecture → part-selection on a fresh repo. These stages write SPEC.md, SUBSYSTEMS.md, BOM.md. No hook exists yet (no `init` was run), and no schematic is configured, so `check_drift` reports "vacuously clean". All commits succeed.
2. Schematic stage refuses (#19). To unblock: scaffold a blank `usb-c-power-breakout.kicad_pro`/`.kicad_sch` by hand and run `copperhead init` — which sets `config.schematic` **and installs the pre-commit hook**.
3. Re-run `copperhead create`. The spec-seed stage finishes (its run-level ledger is clean — it touched no docs) and tries to commit:

```
Command failed with exit code 1: git commit -m 'copperhead: create pipeline stage: spec-seed...'

ERC ✓
DRC skipped (no board configured)
drift: BOM.md claims "J1 exists" but actual is "J1 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "F1 exists" but actual is "F1 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "D1 exists" but actual is "D1 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "R2, R3 exists" but actual is "R2, R3 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "D2 exists" but actual is "D2 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "R1 exists" but actual is "R1 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "J2 exists" but actual is "J2 not in schematic"
drift: BOM.md claims "J3 exists" but actual is "J3 not in schematic"
constraints ✓
```

The pipeline is now deadlocked: no stage can commit until the schematic contains every BOM refdes, but the schematic stage can only get there through commits.

## Why it happens

Two consistency gates disagree about scope and timing:

- The **run-level** gate (`finish` + obligations ledger in `src/agent/tools.ts`) is *incremental*: a drift obligation opens only when the run edits a doc. A stage that touches nothing finishes clean.
- The **hook-level** gate (`copperhead check` via the hook from `src/memory/scaffold.ts` `installPreCommitHook`) is *global*: it compares all docs against the schematic regardless of what the current run changed.

During `create`, docs are *supposed* to lead the schematic — that's the pipeline order (spec → architecture → parts → schematic). The hook's invariant ("docs and schematic never desync at a commit boundary") is only valid for steady-state `do`/`sync` runs on a complete project, not for the bootstrap sequence.

The comment on `check_drift` in `tools.ts` shows this was already half-solved once: "No schematic yet means there is nothing for the docs to drift against... Returning without clearing deadlocks every docs-only stage of the create pipeline." The same reasoning wasn't extended to a schematic that exists but is still being bootstrapped.

## Suggested fixes (any one unblocks; first two seem most principled)

1. **Pipeline commits bypass the hook**: `create`/`do` commit with `git commit --no-verify` (or `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`). The hook exists to catch *hand* edits; copperhead's own commits already went through the run-level gates, so the hook is redundant-but-stricter for them.
2. **Bootstrap-aware drift**: treat "refdes in BOM but schematic has zero symbols / stage < schematic in the pipeline state" as pending-bootstrap, not drift — mirroring the existing "no schematic configured → vacuously clean" carve-out.
3. **Defer hook installation**: `init` (or the future create-stage scaffolding from #19) installs the hook only once the schematic is non-empty / the create pipeline has passed the schematic stage.

## Workaround

`rm .git/hooks/pre-commit` (or make it `exit 0`), re-run `copperhead create`, reinstall the hook after the schematic stage lands.

issues.title: copperhead create can't bootstrap a KiCad project — schematic stage always refuses on a fresh repo
issues.body:
## Summary

On a fresh repo, `copperhead create` runs the docs-only stages (spec-seed, architecture, part-selection) fine, but the **schematic** stage always ends in a refusal: the agent has no way to bring a KiCad project into existence, and nothing earlier in the pipeline scaffolds one.

Observed in a real run (copperhead-test, run `2026-07-21T11-08-30-594Z`): the agent proposed and validated the `schematic-stage` change, then called `finish(refuse)` with:

> Blocked: the repo has no KiCad project/schematic files and the tools cannot create .kicad_* files. ... Please add a blank KiCad project and top-level schematic.

## Why it's boxed in

- `write_file` hard-refuses KiCad files by design (`src/agent/filetools.ts` — `write_file refuses KiCad files (...); use edit_file with anchors instead`), so the agent can never create a `.kicad_sch`/`.kicad_pro` from scratch.
- `edit_file` needs an existing file to anchor into — nothing to edit.
- `list_symbols` / `list_nets` / `run_erc` all return `no schematic configured` because `config.schematic` is unset.
- `copperhead init` only *discovers* an existing schematic (`src/memory/scaffold.ts`: "no .kicad_sch found ... point copperhead at a KiCad project") — it doesn't scaffold one either.

So the create pipeline assumes a KiCad project pre-exists, but `create` is supposed to bootstrap the whole project. The guardrail (never let the LLM generate a whole `.kicad_sch`) is sound; the gap is that no *deterministic* code path creates the blank project.

## Proposed fix

Have the schematic stage (or `create` itself, before that stage) scaffold a minimal valid blank project deterministically — template-based, not LLM-generated:

- write a blank `<project>.kicad_pro` + `<project>.kicad_sch` (empty top sheet with title block) from templates or via `kicad-cli`
- set `config.schematic` so `list_symbols`/`run_erc`/`edit_file` work from there
- keep the `write_file` KiCad refusal exactly as is — the agent then builds the schematic through anchored `edit_file` calls as designed

Alternative considered: a narrowly-scoped `create_schematic` tool that only writes a fixed blank template (no LLM-provided content), which keeps bootstrapping inside the agent loop.

issues.title: Add --keep-on-fail debug flag: skip rollback/clean of the working tree on failed runs
issues.body:
## Problem

Every failed run is hard-rolled-back: `fail()` (`src/agent/loop.ts:182-184`) calls `restore()` (`src/util/git.ts:45-51`), which runs `git reset --hard <snapshot>` followed by `git clean -fd -e .copperhead/runs`. That `clean -fd` deletes all untracked files the agent wrote (docs/, openspec/, KiCad files).

This is the right default — a failed run means the verification gates never passed, so the tree shouldn't keep unverified edits. But when debugging copperhead itself (or a failing stage), the rollback destroys exactly the evidence you want to inspect: the actual files the agent produced. The transcript records tool calls, but reading a whole design doc out of `transcript.jsonl` is much worse than opening the file. Two recent spec-seed runs failed on turn-budget exhaustion with ~90%-complete spec docs, deleted both times.

## Proposal

Add a `--keep-on-fail` (or `--no-rollback` / `--debug`) flag to `copperhead run` / `copperhead create`:

- On failure, **skip** `restore()` and leave the working tree exactly as the agent left it.
- Print a prominent warning with the snapshot ref and the manual recovery command, e.g.:
  `run failed; tree left dirty for inspection (--keep-on-fail). To roll back: git reset --hard <head> && git clean -fd -e .copperhead/runs`
- Do NOT commit anything — the failure semantics stay the same (no commit, obligations unmet); only the cleanup is skipped.
- Summary.md should record that rollback was skipped.

## Details / edge cases

- The next run's clean-tree check (`src/agent/loop.ts:118`) will refuse a dirty tree, which is good — it forces an explicit decision (`git reset --hard` or `--allow-dirty`) before re-running, so the flag can't silently compound state across runs.
- With `--allow-dirty` + `--keep-on-fail`, the stash-based snapshot (`git stash create`) still exists; the warning should print the stash ref too.
- Complements #15 (which proposes auto-stashing failed work by default): `--keep-on-fail` is the zero-friction debug version — files stay in place, no stash archaeology needed.

issues.title: On turn-budget exhaustion, prompt to continue (with token usage) + agent-loop efficiency fixes
issues.body:
## Context

Two consecutive `copperhead create` (spec-seed) runs on a USB-C breakout brief failed with `turn budget exhausted (40 turns, N files touched but unverified)` and were hard-rolled-back, discarding ~90%-complete spec docs. Combined cost: ~500k input tokens with nothing kept.

Trace analysis (`.copperhead/runs/2026-07-21T10-44-49-392Z/`): 12 `record_constraint` calls opened 33 `affects-revisit` obligations plus a drift obligation. `finish` was refused at turn 25 with 15 turns left; the model then resolved obligations one per turn (every resolution was "no change needed: schematic/layout/BOM not yet created") and ran dry with 20 still open. A zero-waste run of this stage needs ~60 turns — the failure is structural, not model slowness.

## Feature: on turn exhaustion, ask the user instead of rolling back

When `maxTurns` is reached (`src/agent/loop.ts:385`), instead of immediately failing and restoring the snapshot:

1. Print run stats so far: turns used, files touched, open obligations count, and **token usage** (`tokensIn` / `tokensOut` are already tracked in the loop — currently they only surface in summary.md).
2. Prompt: `Turn budget exhausted (40 turns, 247k in / 9.5k out). Continue with N more turns? [y/N]` — on yes, extend the budget and keep the conversation going; on no (or non-TTY), fall back to the current fail-and-restore behavior.
3. Precedent exists: `--interactive` already pauses for approval after proposal validation (`src/cli.ts:103`), so there's a prompt mechanism to reuse. For non-interactive/CI runs the current behavior stays the default.

Related quality-of-life: even when the user declines, consider preserving the failed work via `git stash create` + `git stash store` (or a `copperhead/failed/<run-id>` branch) before `restore()` in `fail()` (`src/agent/loop.ts:182`), so budget-exhaustion failures are recoverable rather than destroyed.

## Optimizations (from the same trace analysis)

1. **Prompt the model to batch tool calls.** The loop executes every tool call in one assistant message within a single turn (`src/agent/loop.ts:251`), and both providers support parallel calls — but nothing in `src/agent/prompts.ts` says so. gpt-5 emitted exactly one call per message for all 40 turns. Add to `WORKFLOW`: "Emit multiple independent tool calls in a single response: all `record_constraint` calls in one message, all `resolve_affected` calls in one message, independent `write_file` calls together." Also add it to the "Only 5 turns remain, converge now" nudge (`src/agent/loop.ts:267`). This alone compresses the failed run's 40 turns to ~10.

2. **Don't open `affects-revisit` obligations for artifacts that don't exist.** 27 of the 34 obligations targeted schematic/layout/BOM when none existed yet (spec-seed stage). In the `record_constraint` handler (`src/agent/tools.ts:377`), skip or auto-defer obligations whose target artifact isn't configured (`ctx.config.schematic` / `ctx.config.board`) or whose doc doesn't exist; re-open deferred obligations when the artifact is later configured, so the reconciliation guarantee is kept.

3. **Array form for `resolve_affected`.** Accept `resolutions: [{constraint_key, item, resolution}]` alongside the single form, so one call can clear the backlog even with models that won't parallelize tool calls.

4. **Prompt caching in the Anthropic provider.** The loop resends the full conversation every turn (quadratic input cost — this is how 9.5k output tokens cost 247k input). OpenAI gets automatic prefix caching; `src/agent/providers/anthropic.ts` sends no `cache_control` at all, so Claude runs pay full price every turn. Add `cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}` breakpoints on the system prompt, the last tool definition, and the final message block per turn — roughly an order of magnitude off input cost on Claude runs.

5. **Smaller dials:**
   - `record_constraint`'s return value should include the running open-obligation count, so the model sees debt accumulating instead of discovering it at `finish`.
   - Make `maxTurns` configurable per stage — spec-seed (docs + bookkeeping) has a very different turn profile from a layout stage.
   - `search` should reject empty patterns with a corrective hint (turn 1 of the failed run was wasted on `pattern: ""`).
   - `run_erc`'s "no schematic configured" response should say ERC isn't applicable yet, so the model doesn't retry it.

## Expected impact

Items 1+2 take the spec-seed stage from ~60 required turns to ~10, comfortably inside the default 40. Item 4 cuts Claude input cost ~10×. The continue-prompt turns the remaining edge cases from "destroy the work" into a user decision, with token usage visible at the decision point.


## Acceptance criteria

Binary criteria, mirrored 1:1 by the delta specs in `openspec/changes/turn-budget-continue-and-loop-efficiency/` and by SPEC.md's new AC-15 block. Each is covered by an offline test in `test/budget-efficiency.test.ts` / `test/create-stage-turns.test.ts`.

**Continue prompt**

- [ ] **AC-15.1** When `maxTurns` is reached in an attended run and the user grants extra turns, the loop continues from the same conversation state, records a `budget-extended` transcript event, and the run can still finish successfully. The prompt can fire again at the next exhaustion.
- [ ] **AC-15.2** Declining at the prompt fails and restores the pre-run snapshot exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC-15.3** Non-interactive/CI runs (no TTY) fail and restore exactly as before this change.
- [ ] **AC-15.4** The decision point shows turns used, files touched, open obligation count, and cumulative token usage in/out, matching what summary.md reports.

**Work preservation**

- [ ] **AC-15.16** Any run failure with touched files leaves a `copperhead failed run <run-id>` git stash entry holding the work (tracked and untracked), while the working tree is still restored byte-identical; the CLI prints the recovery hint.
- [ ] **AC-15.17** A failure that touched nothing creates no stash entry.

**Efficiency**

- [ ] **AC-15.5 / AC-15.6** The system prompt workflow and the 5-turns-remaining nudge both instruct emitting multiple independent tool calls in a single response.
- [ ] **AC-15.7** `record_constraint` with `affects` targeting a schematic/board/doc that does not exist yet opens zero `affects-revisit` obligations; the items are reported as deferred and never block `finish`.
- [ ] **AC-15.8** `affects` items whose artifact exists still open obligations exactly as before.
- [ ] **AC-15.9 / AC-15.10** `resolve_affected` accepts `resolutions: [{constraint_key, item, resolution}, ...]`; entries resolve independently, so one bad entry does not invalidate the rest.
- [ ] **AC-15.11** `record_constraint`'s return value includes the running open-obligation count.
- [ ] **AC-15.12** `run_erc`/`run_drc` without a configured schematic/board say the check is not applicable yet, so the model does not retry.
- [ ] **AC-15.13** `search` with an empty pattern returns a corrective hint with an example instead of a generic missing-argument error.
- [ ] **AC-15.14 / AC-15.15** The Anthropic provider sends exactly three `cache_control: ephemeral` breakpoints (system prompt, last tool definition, last block of the final message) and reports `inputTokens` as uncached + cache-read + cache-creation.
- [ ] **AC-15.18 / AC-15.19** `stageMaxTurns` in `.copperhead/config.json` overrides `maxTurns` for the named create-pipeline stages; stages without an entry, or an absent map, behave exactly as before.

issues.title: Build the broken-fixture zoo for the fab release gate
issues.body:
## Context

The planned `copperhead check --fab` (OpenSpec change `add-fab-release-gate`, task 4.1) needs deliberately broken KiCad fixture variants so every gate check has a failing test. This is an ideal issue for someone fluent in KiCad who does not write TypeScript: each fixture is a small KiCad project committed as text, immediately consumed by tests.

## What to build

Starting from the known-good project in `test/fixtures/`, create minimal variants, each breaking exactly one thing:

1. **Unrouted net**: board with one net left unrouted (DRC reports an unconnected item).
2. **MPN-less BOM row**: BOM.md row with an empty MPN column.
3. **UNVERIFIED row**: complete BOM.md row flagged `UNVERIFIED`.
4. **Refdes mismatch**: component present in the schematic, absent from the board.
5. **Footprint mismatch**: same refdes, different footprint between schematic and board.
6. **Missing `## Draft quality`**: LAYOUT.md without the section.

## Definition of done

- Each variant lives under `test/fixtures/` with a short README line stating what is broken and which gate check should catch it.
- Variants are minimal diffs from the known-good fixture (reviewable as text; KiCad files are s-expressions).
- The known-good fixture itself stays ERC/DRC clean.

## Notes

No API key needed. Coordinate loosely with the gate implementation issues; fixtures can land first and tests will pick them up. If you are unsure a variant triggers the right DRC violation, run `kicad-cli pcb drc` locally and paste the report in the PR.

issues.title: Parse the ## Simulation block and SPICE assertion grammar
issues.body:
## Context

The planned SPICE verification gate (OpenSpec change `add-spice-verification-gate`, tasks 1.2 and 1.3) lets a subsystem opt into behavioral verification via a `## Simulation` block in SUBSYSTEMS.md. The block parser and the assertion-to-`.meas` compiler are pure parsing work, fully unit-testable without ngspice installed. Good fit if you enjoy writing small parsers.

## Spec

The block names: a netlist scope (hierarchical sheet reference or explicit net set), an analysis type (`op`, `dc`, `ac`, `tran`), optional `sources` lines for driven ports, and one or more assertions.

Assertion grammar (closed, nothing else is legal):
- Measurables: `V(<net>)`, `I(<refdes>)`, `corner(<net>)`
- Comparators: `between <a> and <b>`, `< <x>`, `> <x>`
- Numbers with SI suffixes (`25uA`, `3.3`, `10k`)

Raw ngspice `.control` blocks must be rejected with a parse error naming the offending line (reviewability and injection safety are the point of the closed grammar).

## Definition of done (from the delta spec)

- `V(VREF) between 3.25 and 3.35` compiles to a corresponding `.meas` directive with both bounds evaluated.
- A raw `.control` line fails with a parse error naming the line, without any ngspice invocation.
- Unit tests cover every measurable x comparator pair and SI-suffix parsing.

## Notes

Offline, no API key, no ngspice needed for this piece. The wrapper that actually runs ngspice is a separate task; this issue ends at "correct deck fragment out, or precise parse error".

issues.title: Implement the documentation-presence check for the fab release gate
issues.body:
## Context

The planned `copperhead check --fab` (OpenSpec change `add-fab-release-gate`, task 1.5) includes a documentation-presence check: a board is not release-ready if LAYOUT.md lacks a filled `## Draft quality` section, or if a `create`-produced repo is missing DEVPLAN.md. This is probably the smallest real feature in the backlog.

## What to do

1. Implement a check function (suggested home: `src/kicad/fab.ts`, create it if the fab module does not exist yet) that:
   - fails when LAYOUT.md has no `## Draft quality` section or the section is empty,
   - fails when the repo was produced by `create` (detectable from `.copperhead/config.json`) and DEVPLAN.md is absent.
2. Report failures in the drift-report voice: name the file, the claim ("release-ready"), and the actual state (missing section/file).
3. Unit tests with fixture doc variants.

## Definition of done (from the delta spec)

- LAYOUT.md without a `## Draft quality` section produces a violation naming LAYOUT.md and the missing section.
- A complete doc set produces a pass.
- Pure function over file contents, zero network and zero LLM calls (this lives inside the `check` contract).

## Notes

Offline, no API key, no KiCad needed. Good first real feature: small surface, clear spec, existing reporting patterns to imitate.

issues.title: Add a board-side footprint enumerator to the read-only s-expression reader
issues.body:
## Context

`src/kicad/sexp.ts` is a read-only tokenizer/walker over KiCad s-expression files. It currently offers `list_symbols` (schematic side) and `list_nets`. The planned fab release gate (OpenSpec change `add-fab-release-gate`, task 1.3) needs the board side: enumerate footprints from a `.kicad_pcb` so the gate can diff refdes and footprint assignments between schematic and board.

## What to do

1. Add a board-side enumerator to `src/kicad/sexp.ts` returning, per footprint: refdes, footprint library id, and position/side if cheaply available.
2. Follow the existing `list_symbols` pattern: read-only walking, no serialization ever (this parser never writes KiCad files, by design).
3. Unit tests against the fixture board in `test/fixtures/`.

## Definition of done

- Enumerator returns one entry per footprint on the fixture board with correct refdes and footprint ids (spot-check against opening the board in KiCad).
- No write/serialize code paths added.
- Tests cover a footprint without a refdes property (graceful handling, not a crash).

## Notes

Offline, no API key. KiCad installed helps for eyeballing the fixture but is not required to run tests. This is the enabling piece for the schematic-to-PCB match check in the fab gate.

issues.title: Implement order-quantity arithmetic for supplier BOM export
issues.body:
## Context

The planned `copperhead export bom` command (OpenSpec change `add-supplier-bom-export`, task 1.2) computes per-line order quantities from board count and a spares percentage. The rules are fully specified; this issue is a pure function plus tests.

## Spec

- Base: `ceil(perBoardCount x boards x (1 + spares/100))`, with `--boards` defaulting to 1 and `--spares` defaulting to 10.
- Passive minimum: for lines whose footprint has prefix `R_`, `C_`, or `L_`, raise the result to `perBoardCount x boards + 2` when the percentage yields less (losing two 0402s to tweezers is normal).

## Definition of done (from the delta spec, these are the test cases)

- A line with 4 parts per board at `--boards 10 --spares 10` exports quantity 44.
- A passive line with 1 part per board at `--boards 1 --spares 10` exports quantity 3.
- Edge cases covered: zero spares, non-passive single part, fractional ceil results.

## Notes

Implement as a standalone function (suggested home: `src/kicad/bom-export.ts`) with vitest unit tests. Offline, no API key. Depends loosely on the shared BOM parser issue but can be built independently against the typed row shape.

issues.title: Extract the BOM.md table parser from drift.ts into a shared module
issues.body:
## Context

The drift checker in `src/memory/drift.ts` parses BOM.md and PINOUT.md tables to diff docs against the schematic. The planned supplier BOM export (OpenSpec change `add-supplier-bom-export`, task 1.1) needs the same BOM.md parser. Rather than duplicating it, the parser should move to a shared module both consumers import.

## What to do

1. Extract the BOM.md table parsing from `src/memory/drift.ts` into its own module (e.g. `src/memory/bom-table.ts`) with a typed row shape (refdes, value, footprint, MPN, flags).
2. Update `drift.ts` to consume the shared module. Behavior must not change.
3. Move or add unit tests so the parser is tested directly against the fixture BOM, not only through drift tests.

## Definition of done

- All existing drift tests pass unchanged (they are the safety net for this refactor).
- The parser is importable without pulling in drift logic.
- Direct unit tests cover the parser, including a malformed-table case.

## Notes

Pure offline refactor: `npm test` against `test/fixtures/` is the whole dev loop, no API key or KiCad install needed. This unblocks the supplier export work (see the follow-up issues on quantity arithmetic and CSV emitters).

issues.title: Contribute an example design brief (simple, medium, or hard tier)
issues.body:
## Context

`examples/` contains design briefs in `simple/`, `medium/`, and `hard/` tiers that feed `copperhead create --brief`. More briefs mean more coverage of the pipeline and better demos. This is a pure-markdown contribution: no TypeScript, no toolchain.

## What to do

1. Read `examples/README.md` and one existing brief per tier to absorb the format and level of detail (constraints, budgets, unstated-decision traps).
2. Write a brief for a new board. Ideas: a battery sensor node, a small motor driver, an audio preamp, a USB-C power sink. Pick something you actually know.
3. Good briefs include explicit budgets (power, cost, size) and at least one deliberate trap: a constraint that a naive design would violate, so the agent has something to refuse or flag.
4. Open a PR adding the brief to the appropriate tier.

## Definition of done

A new brief merged under `examples/<tier>/`, consistent in format with its neighbors, containing at least one explicit budget and one trap, with a one-line entry in `examples/README.md`.

## Notes

You do not need to run `create` against your brief (that needs an API key); format and content review happens in the PR. Domain knowledge is the contribution here.

issues.title: Walk the README quickstart on a clean machine and report friction
issues.body:
## Context

AC-6.1 in `openspec/specs/SPEC.md` requires the README quickstart to work on a clean machine, and task 11.1 of the `build-copperhead-phase-1` change tracks verifying it. Nobody inside the project can test this properly: we all have working setups. A newcomer's confusion log is the deliverable.

## What to do

1. On a machine (or container/VM) without copperhead installed: clone the repo, then follow the README quickstart exactly as written: `npm i -g .`, `copperhead init`, `copperhead check` on the test fixture.
2. Note every point of friction: missing prerequisites, unclear wording, commands that fail, error messages that don't tell you what to do next.
3. Comment your log here (OS, Node version, KiCad version, what happened). PRs improving the README based on your log are very welcome but not required, the log alone is a real contribution.

## Definition of done

A written walkthrough report from a machine that had never run copperhead, covering clone through a green (or honestly failing) `copperhead check`.

## Notes

No API key needed: `init` and `check` are contractually LLM-free and network-free. This issue is repeatable per OS; reports for Linux, macOS, and WSL are each valuable.

issues.title: Add a saved-login Claude Code provider via the Claude Agent SDK
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #1 adds a saved-login Codex provider: `--model codex` drives the locally installed, ChatGPT-authenticated Codex CLI through the official SDK, so no OpenAI API key is needed. The same pattern should exist for Claude Code users via the **Claude Agent SDK** (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, docs at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk). It drives the locally installed Claude Code and reuses its existing login, so a `--model claude-code` provider would let subscription users run copperhead without an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Proposed design

Mirror the decisions settled in PR #1:

- **Provider seam**: route `claude-code` (and `claude-code:<model-id>`) in `makeProvider`, implement `Provider.chat(messages, tools) -> Turn` on top of the SDK's query surface, and keep an injectable client seam for offline tests, same as `CodexProvider`.
- **Reasoning-only backend**: disable the SDK's built-in file-editing, bash, and web tools; run in an isolated working directory. All mutations flow through copperhead's capability-filtered tools, obligations ledger, ERC/DRC verification, snapshot, and commit gates.
- **Structural tool gating**: this may come out cleaner than the Codex version. Instead of mirroring the gate in a structured-output enum, the Agent SDK supports registering custom in-process tools, so copperhead can expose exactly the tools `availableTools(ctx)` returns each turn. The spec-gated-in invariant stays structural rather than schema-mirrored.
- **Auth stays external**: copperhead never reads, copies, or logs the Claude Code credential; the CLI owns authentication. A missing or unauthenticated install fails through the normal rollback path with an actionable error.
- **No silent fallback** to a paid API provider, matching the Codex provider's behavior.
- **Optional dependency**: lazy `import()` in `makeProvider` rather than a hard install for every user (same packaging question raised on PR #1 for `@openai/codex-sdk`).

## Scope

- OpenSpec change with proposal, design, delta specs, and tasks (same shape as `add-codex-cli-provider`).
- Offline provider tests (routing, tool mapping, gating, malformed output, error status preservation for the shared retry wrapper).
- Opt-in live provider-parity entry in `test/agent-integration.test.ts` (AC-3.10).
- Docs: README, docs site, `.env.example`, configuration reference.

## Blocked on

PR #1 landing first, since this reuses the provider seam, gating approach, and packaging decisions settled there.
